## PR #8760 — config: pin #8755's reachability claim over the population it is about [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-05)

Branch: `work/8755-reachability-pin`

#8755's load-bearing scope claim is that the flat `set` spelling is **unaffected** — an operator at the CLI binds the filter correctly, and the loss reaches a box only through a hierarchical config file, a `load override` or a peer config-sync payload. That claim is what keeps the severity honest: *"an operator types `set` and gets no filter"* would be false.

**It was cited to a pin that does not cover it, and I supplied the citation.** `TestFlatSetMergesWhereHierarchicalDuplicates` is about a repeated **instance statement** under `security policies … policy <p>` merging rather than duplicating — a different container, a different mechanism, and it says nothing about whether an interface unit's packed tail survives the flat spelling.

> Existence is not coverage.

Measured instead, over the population the issue is actually about: **all 23 sites the #8690 register classes `open` survive the flat spelling.** The cell reads that register rather than a hardcoded list, so it shrinks by itself as sites are normalized instead of going stale in the direction that looks like success.

## What I got wrong on the way, because it is the useful part

The first version asserted *"this is the flat tree, not the hierarchical one"*, and a mutation swapping the builder for `NewParser` **escaped**. That mutation was right to escape. Measured, for `interfaces <if> unit <u> family inet filter input f1`:

```
flat `set`            max Keys per node = 2
hierarchical braced   max Keys per node = 2
hierarchical ELIDED   max Keys per node = 5
```

The flat and braced spellings are **structurally equivalent** here — `SetPath` builds the same nested chain the parser does — so swapping one for the other changes nothing, and the distinction I was asserting **does not exist** for this population. The distinction that does exist is *elided vs not-elided*.

So the cell measures that instead, and carries a **per-site positive control**: each surviving site's *elided* twin must compare **equal** under the same comparison. Without it, a comparison broken toward "always different" reports zero losses and reads as a clean result — found by mutation.

## Two guards labelled unfalsifiable rather than dressed up

The `lost` arm fires for nothing (no open site *is* lost under the flat spelling) and the tail-packed guard fires for nothing (no flat tree is tail-packed). Deleting either kills no cell. Both stay, and both say so.

> An inert guard that is labelled costs nothing and stops the next reader trusting it; a deleted one takes its reason with it.

## Validation

`go test ./pkg/config/` passes; `go build ./...` and `gofmt` clean.

**5 mutations:**

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| the per-site elided control never fires | **killed** |
| every site unmeasurable, non-vacuity guard intact | **killed** |
| the flat builder swapped for `NewParser` | escaped — **correctly**; the two spellings are equivalent here, which is what the measurement established and what the first version of this cell denied |
| the loss arm can never fire | escaped; **labelled** |
| the tail-packed guard removed | escaped; **labelled** |

Part of #8755 — no close keyword. This is the reachability half; the per-site packed-tail and disarm checks are lane-8388's arm and are not touched here.

## PR #8762 — config: guard against #8690 scope rules that can never fire [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-05)

Branch: `fix/8690-dead-rule-census`

A pair admitted to `compactNormalizeInScope` only folds when `head` is a schema child of the node reached by keyword `kw`. **A pair with no such position anywhere in the schema matches nothing** — it sits in the switch reading as coverage, passes review, satisfies the register, and normalizes nothing. Refs #8690.

## The hazard is live, and it arrives from a new direction

The census fixture **nests every path segment**, so for `family inet address 10.0.0.1/24` it records `("inet","address")`. The real spelling is one node, and the pass unfolds **outermost-first**, so it asks `("family","inet")` first:

```
admitted ("inet","address") only   folds=0  addresses=[]
admitted BOTH chain links          folds=2  addresses=[10.0.0.1/24]
```

**A scope rule written from the census path for that family normalizes nothing at all**, and every existing check would look satisfied. Not a wildcard container this time — a census fixture whose *nesting* differs from the real spelling, so the pair it records is the last link of a chain whose earlier links it never sees.

**490 admitted pairs, 761 schema positions, 0 unfireable.** The second angle agrees: no site remaining in the inventory has an already-admitted pair anywhere on its chain — which a live rule would have resolved.

**Both were run with positive controls rather than trusted**, because a clean result from an unvalidated instrument is the defect this file exists to catch:

|---|---|
| inject a pair whose head is not a schema child | **reds**, names it |
| admit only the **last** link of the known two-link `family inet address` chain | inventory cross-check **names that exact site** — the scenario the guard is for |

Dropping the wildcard descent makes **20 live pairs look dead**. ## PR #8764 — config: merge a repeated named instance on the tolerant load path [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-05)

Branch: `fix/8752-duplicate-instance-fold`

Closes #8752

A configuration that names the same `policy <p>` twice under one zone pair (or under `global`) did not merge the two statements — it produced two policies with the same name. The strict commit path rejects that (#3473), so the shape only reaches a running system through the paths that exist to accept configurations the operator did not just author: `Store.Load` at boot and `Store.SyncApply` on HA config sync.

On that path the duplicate did not merely sit there. Compiling

```
policy p1 { match { source-address 10.0.0.0/8; destination-address any; application any; } then { permit; } }
policy p1 { then { deny; } }
```

produced the operator's policy plus a spurious match-less second policy carrying `LenientContentDropped` — and that flag is the operative harm. `policies_lower.go` poisons such a rule with the `__unsupported__` sentinel so the Rust integrity preflight rejects the **whole snapshot**: previous-good retained, fresh-boot default-deny. The consequence was not a policy set an operator could read in `show`; it was that the operator's entire configuration did not load.

### The fix

Fold duplicates in place at the first occurrence — append the repeat's children onto the first node, and carry any packed tail (`policy p1 scheduler-name S;`) in as a leaf so a brace-elided repeat lands its statement on the surviving policy rather than on a phantom.

Merging rather than replacing is not an invention: the flat `set` spelling **already merges**, and the measured result is identical.

| | policies | action | criteria | `LenientContentDropped` | warnings |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| hierarchical, before | 2 | permit + deny | split | **TRUE** on the spurious one | 1 |
| hierarchical, after | **1** | deny | intact | **false** | 2 |
| flat `set` (reference) | 1 | deny | intact | false | 1 |

The two spellings converge exactly, differing afterwards by one warning: the hierarchical one additionally reports the duplicate it merged. The terminal action resolves to the later statement's `deny` — what `set` does for the same input — and the existing conflicting-terminal-action gate still reports the disagreement, so the fold never becomes the thing that decides a policy's action.

**Nothing here can make `Store.Load` reject a config that loads today.** The pass only ever removes a duplicate node; a tree with no duplicates is untouched. The strict path is unchanged and still rejects, because there the operator is present and should be told to rename. And the fold **warns**, so a configuration a strict commit refuses does not load silently.

Scope is a **pair list, not a shape**: `policy` under from-zone/to-zone and under `global`. `nat source rule-set` has the same slice-backed duplicating shape and is deliberately **not** folded — it is unmeasured, and a fix aimed at a shape rather than at measured sites is how a narrow defect becomes a wide regression.

### Four instruments were re-derived, not re-pointed

- **`TestTheDuplicatePolicyPoisonsTheSnapshot8752`** named itself the acceptance criterion: *"an implementation that removes the duplicate OBJECT but leaves the flag set has not fixed the thing operators feel."* Now asserted directly, plus that the fold warns and that the action gate still fires. The chain's second half (flag → sentinel → preflight) is untouched and still pinned in `pkg/dataplane/userspace` — the flag was never wrong, the duplicate was.
- **`TestFlatSetMergesWhereHierarchicalDuplicates`** pinned the contrast between the two spellings at `policy`. The fold converges them there, so that sub-test could no longer see the substitution trap it was built to catch. The trap did not go away with the contrast — the fold is scoped to a pair list, so containers outside it still duplicate where `set` merges. The discriminating sub-test **moved to `security nat source rule-set`**, measured to still split, and `policy` kept a convergence assertion that doubles as the regression guard.
- **The #8690 register** classed the two `scheduler-name` sites `wrong-remedy` because normalizing them would restore the schedule onto the spurious duplicate. That premise is gone with the duplicate. Reclassified **`open`**: the harm is fixed *without* the normalizer, but a lone brace-elided statement still drops the schedule the block spelling carries, so a narrower divergence remains and the remedy would now land correctly. The class history is kept — this entry has been wrong three times.
- **The conservation-census annotation** described the harm in the present tense and said "#8752 tracks the fold itself". It now records the measured before and after.

### lane-8526's caution, answered by measurement

A merge fix was expected to make every `dupEffectSplitInstances` entry stale. Measured with a positive control: `validateDuplicateNamedBlockAST` reports the control (`bgp group`, the only such entry) with its split-instances wording on the lenient path and errors on the strict one, and reports **nothing** for a duplicate policy on either path. The container this fold changes is not in that classification at all — it is governed by the #3473 gate — and the one entry that is classified stays true, being outside the fold's pair list. The caution was right in form and has no members.

Each mutant built and ran before its verdict was read.

| M1 packed tail not carried | convergence + scheduler cells |

## PR #8765 — config: guard that sites admission cannot separate share a class [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-05)

Branch: `fix/8690-pair-homogeneity-guard`

## What

Admission to the compact normalizer is decided per **(container, head) pair**; the permanent-exclusion register classifies per **site**. When one site's key set *contains* another's, admitting the first necessarily admits everything the second needs — so the second folds too, and the two cannot carry different verdicts however carefully each was measured.

**The live instance:** `security ike policy <p> proposal-set` and `security ipsec policy <p> proposal-set` both key on `("policy","proposal-set")`, both fold today, and the discriminator (ike/ipsec) sits one level *above* the container — outside the key, genuinely inexpressible at that link. It was handled **by hand** in `ipsec_ike_fold_8690_test.go`, which is what makes this a handled-instance-not-class gap.

Written while every group still agrees, deliberately: a guard landing after a split has to grandfather it, and a day-one exemption is what the next reader trusts. **Born green over all 68 register sites.**

## Attribution is measured, not derived

Three attempts to derive a site's pair from its path each gave a *different* wrong answer — the container path carries the schema arg placeholder where production passes `node.Keys[0]`, and a site's key chain is a property of the **spelling**, not the site.

So the cell asks the pass: swap in a recording predicate, run the real spelling, read back the keys actually consulted. No model left to drift.

That needs one indirection in production — `compactNormalizeInScope` becomes a `var` over an unchanged default, never reassigned outside a test. A throwaway measurement can mutate and revert; a permanent guard cannot. **Flagged explicitly because it is test scaffolding in a shipping file, which is a cost.**

## A measured correction to my own premise

The recorder admits everything, intended so it explores *past* a refusal. Asserting that as a hard control **failed on the real code**: admit-all observes exactly the same 63 keys as the real predicate, because at the census's packing, folding a node exposes no further packed node. **These chains are one link.** lane-8367's multi-link chains were measured on maximally-packed spellings; this fixture set is not that.

So the comparison is over keys consulted *at this packing*, and a pair that looks separable here may share a key at another. Stated rather than assumed — the assumption was wrong and only the control caught it.

## Validation

Three mutants, each asserted to have run and checked for **the branch it should fire**:

| mutant | result |
|---|---|
| flip the inet6 filter-input twin's class → inseparable pair disagrees | **CAUGHT**, via `cannot separate`, naming which site forces which |
| recorder records nothing | **CAUGHT** by the non-vacuity control |
| flip a **separable** site's class (`inner-vlan-id`) | **SURVIVED**, as it must — specific, not merely loud |

An earlier revision had no non-vacuity control, and **a recorder degraded to `return false` SURVIVED while still reporting all 68 sites** — it under-records, yielding fewer subset relations and fewer reds, with an identical-looking count. The guard would have gone quiet exactly as it lost its evidence. That mutation is why the control exists rather than a comment claiming admit-all matters.

Full `pkg/config` green, dataplane canaries green, gofmt clean tree-wide. **No register entry, class, or scope-switch case changed.**

## PR #8766 — config: say which spelling a scope entry closes, and guard it (#8755) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-05)

Branch: `work/8755-register-bound`

The #8690 register lists 23 `open` sites, and **`open` reads as "available work, fully fixable"**. For the 20 under `family inet` / `family inet6` it is not: a scope entry closes **one of four** losing spellings.

Measured through the real pass under the production scope at `769f2f622`:

```
A  family inet { filter { input f4; } }   keeps "f4"   fully braced, correct
B  family inet { filter input f4; }       DROPS        idiomatic elision
C  family inet filter input f4;           DROPS        one-liner
D  family { inet { filter input f4; } }   DROPS
E  family { inet filter input f4; }       DROPS
```

**Only C is reachable by admitting a chain.** B is unreachable *by construction* — and B is the form a hand-written config with several statements in the family block will contain.

```
family inet { filter input f4; }      pairsAsked=[]
family inet filter input f4;          pairsAsked=[family inet | inet filter | filter input]
```

`normalizeCompactNodes` recurses into a braced `Keys=[family inet]` with `schema.children["family"]`, while those children belong to `family inet`. **The schema advances one level where the node advanced two**, so nothing beneath a braced multi-key container is ever consulted. `unit`-level sites are unaffected: there the second token is an instance **arg** consumed by `identity`, not a child keyword.

## What this changes

Every `open` entry now carries a **SPELLING BOUND** note saying which spelling a chain admission closes, and the three `unit`-level sites say explicitly that the gap does not apply to them. Registering 20 sites `open` without that invites a fix covering a quarter of the exposure.

## The guard, not the prose

`TestAChainAdmissionDoesNotCloseTheIdiomaticElision_8755` is green today (both spellings drop) and green after a complete fix (both keep). **It fires on exactly one state: the partial one**, where someone lands a chain admission and the idiomatic elision still drops. That state does not exist yet — which is the point, and it says so rather than pretending to be tested.

`TestEveryOpenEntryCarriesTheSpellingBound_8755` keeps the register honest: an `open` entry without the note reds the suite.

## Validation

`go test ./pkg/config/` passes; `go build ./...` and `gofmt` clean.

**5 mutations:**

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| an `open` entry loses its spelling bound | **killed** |
| the control fixture swapped for a non-binding spelling | **killed**, after the control was made load-bearing |
| the braced control's own assertion blanked | **escaped first time** — see below |
| the partial-fix arm can never fire | escaped; **labelled** (the state it detects does not exist yet) |
| the control's non-vacuity check removed | does not compile |

**The third one is the finding.** The braced control was checked only in its own cell, so it could stop binding without the cell that depends on it noticing — a control asserted in isolation is not a control for anything else. The bound cell now **reads** the control's value and compares against it, so blanking the control reds the cell that relies on it.

**The pass itself is untouched.** The traversal gap is in `compact_normalize_8662.go`, another lane's area; it is reported and bounded here rather than fixed here.

## PR #8767 — config: scope the #8755 spelling-bound guard to its own population [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-05)

Branch: `fix/8755-guard-overbroad`

**Master was red and it was my guard.**

#8766 landed `TestEveryOpenEntryCarriesTheSpellingBound_8755`, which required a `SPELLING BOUND` note from **every** `open` entry in the #8690 register. Minutes later another lane added two `security policies … policy <p> scheduler-name` entries, and the cell reddened on them.

Those sites are not under a braced multi-key container. **The bound says nothing about them, so the guard was demanding a claim that would have been false if written** — and the cheapest way to make such a cell green is to write the note anyway, which is worse than the gap it was protecting.

> A guard written for one population must **select** that population, or it becomes a tax on every lane appending to the same file.

The selector is a proxy and says so: the bound applies to a site whose container passes through a braced **multi-key** node whose second token is a child keyword. In this register that is exactly `family inet` / `family inet6`. `unit <n>` does not qualify — its second token is an instance arg consumed by `identity`, which is why those three sites were already annotated as *not* subject to the gap.

A proxy can stop matching, so the cell now **fails if the selector matches nothing**: a string selector defeated by a register rename would report "no failures" for the same reason it reports nothing at all.

## How I let it through

**I merged #8766 with its post-merge gate red.** The conflict check came back CLEAN/MERGEABLE and I read that as the gate. It is not — that reports mergeability, and the suite result is the gate. I had the suite result in the same command output and merged past it.

## Validation

`go test ./pkg/config/` green at this head (123s, full package); `go build ./...` and `gofmt` clean.

Fixes the red introduced by #8766 — no close keyword.

## PR #8769 — config: inject the scope predicate instead of mutating a global [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-05)

Branch: `fix/8690-scope-injection`

## What

#8765 gave the pass a test seam as a package-level **mutable var**, so a recorder could observe which `(container, head)` keys it consults. The capability is right; the shape was not.

A mutable global is reassignable by anything in the package, a test that forgets its restore leaves admit-all in place for every later test, and it makes `t.Parallel()` near it a data race. The comment asked callers not to reassign it outside a test — **a rule enforced by nothing**, which is the kind that holds until the first person who hasn't read it.

## Instead: pass the predicate

```go
func normalizeCompactStanzas(tree *ConfigTree) int {
    return normalizeCompactStanzasWithScope(tree, compactNormalizeInScope)
}
func normalizeCompactStanzasWithScope(tree *ConfigTree, inScope func(container, head string) bool) int
```

`compactNormalizeInScope` is a plain function again; production has exactly one call site; the recorder is an argument. Same capability, no mutable state, no restore discipline, no race. *(Design: team-lead, reviewing the var form.)*

## The justification comment survives verbatim

A seam without its history gets deleted by the next person tidying. Scope is decided per **pair**; the register classifies per **site**; and every attempt to *derive* that mapping from a site's path has been wrong — the container path carries the schema arg placeholder where production passes `node.Keys[0]`, and a site's key chain is a property of the **spelling**, not the site. **Three separate derivations produced three different wrong answers, across three different lanes.** The comment now says explicitly not to remove the seam as unnecessary without reading why.

## Validation

Behaviour **preserved, not hollowed** — same 63 keys over the same 68 register sites. All three mutants behave exactly as before, each asserted to have run and checked for the branch it should fire:

| mutant | result |
|---|---|
| split an inseparable pair | **CAUGHT** via `cannot separate` |
| recorder records nothing | **CAUGHT** by the non-vacuity control |
| flip a **separable** site's class | **SURVIVED**, as it must |

Zero assignments to `compactNormalizeInScope` anywhere in the tree, confirmed by grep.

Gated at master `0ab895a56`, whole `pkg/config` suite green — the earlier `TestEveryOpenEntryCarriesTheSpellingBound_8755` red was **master's, not this branch's**, and is fixed there. Canaries green, gofmt clean.


**So the remedy would fix a form with no instances in the corpus, while the form with 77 stays unreachable.** That is the difference between *"here is the remedy"* and *"here is why the remedy does not reach the case that occurs"*, and it belongs ahead of any per-site verdict.

Three lanes measured this and got **77 / 104 / 144**, by different corpora and patterns, unanimous on the shape. The cell states its own command so its number is comparable rather than authoritative — the lesson two greens of 72 and 77 taught earlier today.

## PR #8771 — config: say which packing the one-link chain claim is about [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-05)

Branch: `fix/8690-packing-comment`

## What

The pair-homogeneity cell noted that its admit-all recorder observes no key the real predicate does not, explaining it with *"these chains are one link at the census packing"*. True — and it reads as a claim about the **normalizer** when it is a claim about the **fixtures**.

The same content, written the way a config file writes it, cascades:

```
family inet { dhcp lease-time 600; }   touched=0  asked=[]
family inet dhcp lease-time 600;       touched=3  asked=[family inet | inet dhcp | dhcp lease-time]
```

So admit-all **is** load-bearing for a real spelling, and observes nothing extra only in this census. A reader taking the old wording at face value would conclude chains do not cascade — a claim about production drawn from a probe artifact, which is **the exact error this file already records three lanes making today**.

The note now says which packing it is about, and so does the log line, since the log is what a reader sees without opening the file.

The braced form asking for *nothing* (rather than merely fewer keys) is **#8763**, a traversal defect, and is called out as such so the two-line table isn't read as one phenomenon.

## The claim is pinned, but not the bug

A comment asserting a measurement is prose. `TestRealSpellingsCascadeUnlikeTheCensusPacking8690` asserts a one-line spelling consults **more than one key**.

It deliberately does **not** pin the braced form's zero — that is the bug, and asserting it would encode a defect as an expectation and red when #8763 is fixed. What's asserted is the part that survives the fix, with a log branch telling a future reader to drop the pre-fix table once the braced form starts cascading.

## Validation

| mutant | result |
|---|---|
| aim the cell at the non-cascading braced spelling | **CAUGHT** |
| **production**: stop the pass recursing after one link | **CAUGHT** |

The second is the one that matters — the first only proves the assertion reads a real value, the second proves the cell detects the regression it names.

## PR #8774 — config: split a packed tail into statements, per container, opt-in [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-05)

Branch: `fix/8768-packed-tail`

The fold moved a packed tail into **one** child, which is right only when the run holds one statement. A run may hold several, and every statement after the first was swallowed into the first one's Keys and lost. Refs #8768.

```
snmp { trap-group tg1 targets 10.0.0.1 version v2; }
  before -> targets=[10.0.0.1 version v2]  version=""
  after  -> targets=[10.0.0.1]             version="v2"
```

**Both spellings compiled cleanly and produced different configs**, with no error on either path — the #8690 safety property being false on an admitted site. @lane-8526 confirmed the same shape independently. The census cannot see this class at all: it supplies exactly **one leaf per site**, so every "resolved" verdict was taken against a single-statement tail.

## The boundary is answered, not guessed — and my first version guessed

Splitting at "a token that names a sibling keyword" is **actively wrong**: a value may coincide with a sibling keyword, and #4313 makes some tails open-world.

```
then { source-nat pool P persistent-nat permit off; }
```

`off` is a `source-nat` child **and** a value inside a sub-grammar the schema does not model. Name-matching invents a second translation action and **rejects a config that commits today** — `TestOpenWorldTailContainingOffStillCommits_7033` exists for exactly that and caught it.

This version consumes each statement with `consumeNodeKeys` and returns the tail **whole** the moment a token leaves the modelled grammar — borrowing `packedBodyChildren`'s contract rather than inventing one.

## Opt-in per container, because "can split" ≠ "safe to split"

**The NAT `then` family does not opt in.** Its gate depends on the current lowering — it rejects a packed cross-mode contradiction *precisely because* `pool <p> off` lowers to one action and cannot be counted (#7033) — and the cells record that **two earlier attempts to fix that class in the lowering were reverted**. Splitting `source-nat` would be a third.

**A container whose leaves take unmodelled values cannot be split even if it opts in.** `ike policy <p> pre-shared-key ascii-text <v> mode main` is one: `ascii-text` is unmodelled, so the tail returns whole and `mode main` stays swallowed. **That site needs the schema extended before it needs this flag**, and the note says so.

So `snmp trap-group` is the **first and only** container opted in, on the measured differential. Others follow one at a time on the same evidence — the discipline the #8690 scope list arrived at.

## Validation

Full `go test ./pkg/...` green; canaries and tree-wide `gofmt -l` run regardless of diff scope. **The acceptance criterion is the two-spelling differential, not the scope arm** — that arm cannot see this class.

| check | result |
|---|---|
| flag **off** | new cell reds with `targets=[10.0.0.1 version v2] version=""` — the exact swallow |
| flag **on** | packed ≡ braced |
| all #7033 / #7034 / #7014 cells | pass (default off; `source-nat` not opted in) |

The cell's name (`subset`) and its comment promise containment. Over the

guarding, but not chain containment.

packing. Fourth instance of that error today, first one found inside the

the surviving Fatal is the live control.

## PR #8776 — config: pin that compoundKey nodes are exactly the family nodes (#8763) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-05)

Branch: `fix/8763-compoundkey-equivalence`

Two #8763 instruments depend on the equivalence between nodes declaring
`compoundKey: true` and nodes named "family", and neither states it as an
assumption it can check:

  - a fixture builder that renders compound containers as ONE node decides
    which containers those are BY NAME. Its author flagged it as "exact only
    because all seven declarations happen to share that name" -- a heuristic
    wearing an exact answer's clothes.
  - the traversal-defect diagnosis is scoped to compoundKey containers, and
    its population argument ("seven, all named family") is quoted by name.

Measured: the schema declares 7 nodes with compoundKey and 7 named
"family", and they are THE SAME 7 -- the equivalence holds in both
directions, so the name predicate is not a heuristic today. It is exact.

But an eighth declaration of EITHER kind silently invalidates one
instrument or the other, in opposite directions:

  a compoundKey node NOT named "family"  -> the fixture builder renders it
                                            as two levels, measures the shape
                                            the census invents, and reports
                                            clean about a spelling nobody
                                            writes
  a "family" node WITHOUT compoundKey    -> the builder merges a container
                                            the pass traverses correctly and
                                            manufactures a defect that is not
                                            there

Both directions produce a plausible number rather than a failure, which is
why this is a cell and not a note. It costs one schema walk.

The walk enumerates both sets itself rather than trusting the grep that
found them, and carries a degeneracy control: a walk reaching no
compoundKey nodes fails loudly, because an empty set equals any other
empty set and the assertion would otherwise pass vacuously.

Validation: both directions mutation-tested and killed -- renaming a
"family" key reds naming the mismatch, and flipping one compoundKey to
false reds the same way from the other side. `go test ./...` green

## The flag alone could not fix it, and that is the interesting half

#8768's `packedStatements` opt-in splits a packed tail by consuming each statement with `consumeNodeKeys`, stopping the moment a token leaves the modelled grammar. Here it stopped **immediately**:

```go
"pre-shared-key": {desc: "Pre-shared key (ascii-text <key>)", children: nil}   // no args
```

`ascii-text` was outside the modelled grammar, so the tail came back whole.

**Everything except the declaration already knew the shape.** The description says `ascii-text <key>`. `compileIPsec` has always read the value from `p.Keys[2]` — three tokens. The ipsec-vpn sibling already declares `args: 1`.

So `args: 2` is **not a widening** — it states the arity the description, the compiler and the parser already agreed on, and it is what makes the statement boundary computable. With it, `ike policy` opts in and the two spellings compile identically.

## A good failure, tightened rather than left loose

The change moved that leaf out of the #7484 spelling-gate `unreachable` class, and the coverage cell reported it as a failing **instruction**:

```
COVERAGE IMPROVED — TIGHTEN THE RATCHET (this is a good failure):
  [unreachable (leaf changed nothing): 142 -> 141]
```

Ceiling lowered to 141 with the reason recorded. *A ceiling nobody lowers rots into a rubber stamp* — this is the ratchet advancing, not coverage regressing.

## Validation

Full `go test ./pkg/...` green; canaries and tree-wide `gofmt -l` run regardless of diff scope. The acceptance criterion is the **two-spelling differential**, which the scope arm cannot see because the census supplies one leaf per site.

**Two containers now opt in:** `snmp trap-group` and `security ike policy`. NAT `then` still does not and must not — its gate depends on the current lowering, and two earlier attempts to change it were reverted.

## PR #8779 — config: make both spellings of a cross-family DSCP match agree, and say so [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-05)

Branch: `fix/8773-traffic-class-packed`

Closes #8773

Junos spells the DSCP / Traffic-Class field `dscp` in a `family inet` firewall filter and `traffic-class` in `family inet6` — the same six bits in different headers. `compileFilterFrom` handles both in one family-blind switch arm, but the schema declared each under one family only. That is correct Junos, and it made the two ways of writing the same match disagree.

The packed reader resolves its tail **through the schema** (`packedBodyChildren` → `resolveSchemaChild`) and returns the node's children unchanged when the lookup fails. So:

```
family inet { ... from { traffic-class 0; } }   accepted, applied
family inet { ... from traffic-class 0; }       dropped, in silence
```

Both commit cleanly on the strict path. The packed form leaves the term matching on one fewer dimension than written.

### The fix is two halves

Declare each spelling as an alias in the other family so the forms agree, **and** warn at commit naming the Junos spelling for that family. Aligning the spellings alone would have traded a silent drop for a silent acceptance — the same defect wearing the other sign.

**Accept rather than reject** was a deliberate choice with a real alternative. Refusing the cross-family spelling is closer to Junos, and it would also fail commits that succeed on every shipped build, for a configuration that compiles to exactly the matcher the operator intended. The settled answer for that trade here is the one `interface-specific` and the lo0-mirror modifiers already take: accept, and say so at commit. Rejecting is a larger Junos-parity decision and should not ride in on a spelling fix.

The spelling is recorded on the term (`CrossFamilyDSCPSpelling`) rather than re-derived in the validator, because after compilation both criteria land in `term.DSCPs` and the distinction is gone — the same reason `UnknownFrom` and its siblings exist.

### Two expected consequences of adding schema leaves

- **The #4406 golden moves.** The only difference is the new field serializing as `null` on every term of the shipped ha-cluster config; `FirewallFilterTerm` carries no json tags, so any added field moves the baseline. Diffed field-by-field before regenerating, rather than regenerated on the strength of the test name.
- **The #7484 ratchet improves**, 699 → 701 comparable sites, which that cell calls a good failure. Tightened to the measured value.

### How this was originally mis-diagnosed

Recorded because the shape recurs, and because it was my error. It was first reported as *"`traffic-class` is silently lost in the brace-elided spelling, while its siblings are not"*, with a firewall-filter blast radius attached. Every fixture wrapped its case in `family inet` and varied only the **criterion**, so the measurement could not see that the real variable was the **family**. A control that varied the criterion confirmed the wrong reading instead of catching it — and an independent verification inherited the fixture, turning one lane's error into a corroborated one. **A control is independent only along the axes it actually varies.** The cell added here varies both axes and says so in its own comment.

`docs/config-schema.md` gains the general rule, which outlives this instance: adding a schema leaf is a compiler-behaviour change, not only a completion change — if a compiler switch arm names a keyword, the schema must declare it everywhere that arm can run, or the packed spelling of that keyword is quietly inert.

### Validation

Full `go test ./...` green tree-wide at the merged head; `gofmt -l` clean; five mutations killed, each mutant confirmed to build and run first:

| mutation | killed by |
|---|---|
| inet `traffic-class` alias removed | cross-family packed/braced agreement |
| inet6 `dscp` alias removed | same, other family |
| spelling not recorded | advisory assertions |
| advisory unwired | advisory assertions |
| advisory fires on same-family too | the negative control |

The two aliases are mutated **separately** — they are different arms of one fix, and a single mutation would have tested only one. That is the `global`-arm lesson from #8752 applied here.

## PR #8780 — config: hold a packedStatements opt-in to EVERY leaf pair, not the one measured [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-05)

Branch: `fix/8768-optin-guard`

Opting a container into `packedStatements` is a claim that **every** admitted leaf survives the packed spelling. I opted two containers in on the strength of two leaf pairs each — two of nine. Refs #8768.

## The container is the wrong unit, and @lane-8526 established why

The divergence it found under `snmp community` **is not in the fold**: the splitter produces a correct two-statement structure and the `clients` **reader** does not take its value from it, while `authorization` in the same tail does. So survival is a property of each leaf's reader, and a container is safe only if every one of them agrees.

**Multi-ness is not the discriminator**, which is worth recording because it's the obvious wrong answer: `snmp trap-group targets` is multi and fine; `snmp community clients` is multi and diverges.

## What this checks

Packed versus braced for **every ordered pair of admitted leaves** in every opted-in container — **18 pairs across the two, all equal**, so both opt-ins are sound wholesale rather than for the pair each was landed on.

**The fixture registry is asserted against the schema in both directions:**

| condition | result |
|---|---|
| container opts in with no fixtures | **red**, names it |
| fixture set names a container that no longer opts in | **red**, names it |
| container admits a leaf with no fixture statement | **red**, names the leaf |
| no pair compared | **fatal** (degeneracy) |

Without the first, this cell would silently cover only the containers someone remembered to add — the accumulating registry the #8690 buckets exist not to be.

## The fixtures are hand-authored, deliberately

A synthesized value that leaves the modelled grammar makes the splitter return the tail whole, which presents as "no divergence". @lane-8526 measured its own generator doing exactly that and **withheld the table rather than publish it**. The census can't supply them either — one leaf per site is the blindness this whole issue turns on.

## Validation

Full `go test ./pkg/...` green; canaries and tree-wide `gofmt -l` run regardless of diff scope. Mutation-tested both directions with each edit verified before its result was read.

*(One `pkg/daemon` race test flaked under full-suite load on an earlier run; it passes 3/3 on this branch and 3/3 at pristine master, and this diff is a single `pkg/config` test file.)*

## PR #8782 — config: compile snmp community `clients` from the packed spelling [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-05)

Branch: `fix/8778-snmp-clients-failopen`

## The defect

```
set snmp community public authorization read-only clients 10.0.0.0/8   # ONE line  -> clients=[]  ALLOW-ALL
set snmp community public authorization read-only                      # TWO lines -> ENFORCED
set snmp community public clients 10.0.0.0/8
```

**The difference was a line break, and this is a fail-OPEN rather than a lost restriction.** `AllowsSource` documents `len(Clients) == 0` as allow-all (the Junos default), so dropping the allowlist did not narrow it — it **inverted** it. The community answered from every source while the operator's config said otherwise and the commit reported success.

## Two shapes, one defect, different causes

Only measuring the tree showed the second. Flat `set` builds a **chain**, not siblings:

```
community public
  authorization read-only
    clients 10.0.0.0/8        <- CHILD of authorization
```

so a loop over one level of children saw `authorization` and never saw `clients`. The brace-elided hierarchical spelling instead packs every token onto **one node's `Keys`**, where a separate flat-form loop read `authorization` and not `clients`.

**Fixing the Keys loop alone left the flat-set spelling — the one an operator types — still broken.** I assumed one shape, measured, and found two.

The fix walks the chain (descending only through recognised keywords, so a `clients` node's own **value** children are not mistaken for statements) and extends the Keys loop to consume the `clients` run. That run goes to `parseSNMPClients` rather than being parsed inline, so the `restrict` modifier and the #5898 orphan-`restrict` fail-closed path behave identically to the braced spelling instead of being reimplemented beside them.

## The guard asserts the outcome, not an agreement

The obvious cell is *"packed compiles to what braced compiles to"* — and it is **wrong here**: it passes when both spellings are allow-all, which is exactly the regression it would exist to catch. Each spelling is instead asserted to **admit** an address inside the allowlist and **deny** one outside it, which is false of an empty allowlist however the other spelling behaves. *(Constraint: team-lead.)*

Subtests: flat-set one-liner; hierarchical packed; `restrict` under packing; a positive control on the two-line spelling that always worked; and the **second ingestion surface** — `docs/config-schema.md` records that snmp compiles from both `snmp {}` and `system { snmp {} }`, and that a defect has already been reachable from one and not the other, on the spelling our own reference config uses. Both call `compileSNMP` today; the cell asserts that rather than assuming it.

## Validation

Three **production** mutants, each asserted to have run and each caught by exactly the subtest that should catch it:

| mutant | failing subtest |
|---|---|
| drop the chain descent | `flat-set one line` only |
| drop the packed-Keys `clients` case | `hierarchical packed` + `restrict` |
| truncate the clients run | `restrict` only |

0 residual. Full `pkg/config`, `pkg/snmp`, `pkg/api` green; dataplane canaries green; gofmt clean.

Docs updated in the same change — the three spellings, the fail-open explanation, and the guard-shape note that an equality cell is the wrong instrument for an allowlist.

Closes #8778

## PR #8784 — config: opt vpn-monitor into packedStatements, and refuse ambiguous container names [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-05)

Branch: `fix/8768-six-containers`

`security ipsec vpn <v> vpn-monitor destination-ip <ip> source-interface <if>;` collapsed both statements into one node. Opted in, and verified across **every** admitted leaf pair rather than the one it was first reported on. Refs #8768.

## The guard had a flaw, and trying to opt in more containers exposed it

Its fixture registry is keyed by container **name**, and schema names repeat:

```
"proposal"             under ike  AND ipsec
"dead-peer-detection"  under ike gateway AND ipsec
```

If two nodes of one name opt in, the map holds **whichever the walk reached last**, and the leaf enumeration silently describes the wrong container — a guard reporting on a node nobody opted in, while reading as coverage for the one they did.

**So the cell now refuses:** two opted-in nodes sharing a name is a hard failure naming the container. Keying by schema path is the real fix, and is deliberately left until a second node of one name actually needs to opt in — refusing is correct today and doesn't claim a generality it hasn't been tested at.

`ike proposal`, `ipsec proposal` and `dead-peer-detection` all have **ambiguous names**, so opting them in needs the path-keyed registry first. Its measurement that all three are FIXABLE for one leaf pair each stands; what's missing is the machinery to hold them to *every* pair.

## PR #8786 — config: correct the #8768 opt-in guard's stated reason, which cited a retracted mechanism [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-05)

Branch: `fix/8768-guard-rationale`

The guard's assertions were never wrong. **Its explanation of why they matter was** — and it was landed, in the header comment, two error strings, and most urgently in the **failure message a person sees when the cell reds**. Follow-up to #8768 (closed).

## The retracted mechanism

It claimed `snmp community` demonstrated a leaf-level reader ignoring a correctly-split tail. **It does not.** `snmp community` does not fold at all — `("community","authorization")` isn't in the scope list — so there is no split structure and no reader ignoring one. Its lost `clients` is an ordinary drop at an unadmitted site (#8778).

**I measured that myself and reported it as a correction, then did not re-read my own landed rationale against it.** The hollowed-rationale shape, with the later change made by the same person who wrote the claim.

**So no per-leaf reader divergence has ever been demonstrated**, and the 18-of-18 EQUAL this cell measures is entirely consistent with none existing.

## The justification is a priori, and says so

Opting a container in is a claim about **every** admitted leaf, so every pair must be compared for the claim to be tested. That needs no counter-example and doesn't weaken without one. **Weaker footing than "we found one", and the honest one.**

## The failure message mattered most

It told whoever hit it that a leaf's reader does not take its value from the split structure — **a specific diagnosis for a defect nobody has observed**, which is worse than no diagnosis because its specificity is what makes it trusted.

It now states what the cell **measured** (these two spellings disagree, nothing more) and names the likelier causes to *establish* rather than assume: the fold declining to split on a token outside the modelled grammar, or an under-declared arity — the #8777 case.

**"Multi-ness is not the discriminator" is no longer asserted.** Its evidence was `snmp community clients` diverging, which is not a fold divergence, so the evidence is gone even if the claim may still be true.

The retraction is **recorded rather than deleted**: a guard whose stated reason is a phantom still passes review, and the next reader inherits the phantom.

## Validation

Full `go test ./pkg/...` green, **73 packages**; canaries and tree-wide `gofmt -l` run regardless of diff scope. **Verified by forcing a real divergence** that the new message is what appears and the retracted text does not — a failure string is only correct if you have seen it fail.

## PR #8788 — config: declare `next-header` so an IPv6 term's protocol match survives packing [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-05)

Branch: `fix/8781-next-header-packed`

Closes #8781

`from next-header` is the Junos spelling of the protocol match in a `family inet6` firewall filter. `compileFilterFrom` has handled it since #3307 — which added the switch arm precisely because the criterion *"was silently dropped (the term lost its protocol constraint)"* — but the schema never declared it under `from` in either family.

The packed reader resolves its tail **through the schema** (`packedBodyChildren` → `resolveSchemaChild`) and returns the node's children unchanged when the lookup fails. So #3307 fixed the braced half and left the packed half inert:

```
family inet6 { ... from { next-header tcp; } }   Protocols=[tcp]
family inet6 { ... from next-header tcp; }       Protocols=[]
```

Both commit cleanly on the strict path. **A correctly authored IPv6 term, written in the packed spelling, loses its protocol match entirely and therefore matches every protocol** — the failure direction `docs/config-schema.md` already names for this class (*"a filter term whose `from` was dropped matches EVERYTHING"*, #7457). A term meant to accept TCP accepts everything; a term meant to discard TCP discards everything.

### Worse than #8773, and found by censusing it

#8773's dropped criterion was a **cross-family** spelling — a configuration Junos rejects anyway. Here the dropped spelling is **the one Junos tells operators to write**.

It was found by census rather than observation: enumerate the keywords each compiler switch arm handles, and check whether the schema declares each at that path. That is the cheap way to find the rest of a class instead of waiting for a second symptom.

### The fix, both halves

Declare `next-header` under `from` in both families so the packed reader can resolve it, **and** warn at commit for the cross-family spellings. Declaring alone would make the spellings agree silently; warning alone would not stop the drop.

`CrossFamilyDSCPSpelling` becomes `CrossFamilyMatchSpellings` — a second aliased field joined it, and a DSCP-specific name on a list holding protocol spellings is the kind of stale label that later gets reasoned from. The validator's `want` was derived from the **address family**, which was correct while the list held one field and silently wrong the moment it held two: a field-specific answer computed from a field-independent input. It is now a map from each spelling to its own counterpart, listed in both directions so a third aliased field is a visible edit rather than a silent gap.

### Two census results worth recording

- **A candidate is not a finding.** `then next` was also undeclared and measured **clean**: both spellings leave `Action` empty, so they agree — by both being wrong, which is a different defect and not this one.
- **Enumerate the arms from source, not memory.** A hand-written list of the `then` arms included `sample` and `port-mirror`, which are not compiler arms at all, and reported both as defects.

### Gate movements

Both expected, neither a behaviour change. The #4406 golden moves by the field **rename only** — 12 old keys out, 12 new keys in, every value `null`, zero value diffs, checked field-by-field before regenerating. The #7484 ratchet improves 701 → 703, which that cell calls a good failure.

### Validation

Full `go test ./...` green tree-wide at the merged head; `gofmt -l` clean; four mutations killed, each mutant confirmed **both to have applied and to build** before its verdict was read: removing the inet6 declaration (the defect itself), removing the inet alias, not recording the cross-family protocol spelling, and dropping `next-header` from the counterpart map.

The applied-check is new and earned itself immediately — two earlier mutants whose anchors no longer matched after gofmt reformatting were reported as **ESCAPED on a tree that had never been mutated**. A mutation harness that cannot prove its edit landed reports false escapes, which are indistinguishable from real ones.

The registry was keyed by container **name**, and names repeat: `proposal` under both `ike` and `ipsec`, `dead-peer-detection` under both gateways. A name-keyed map doesn't fail on that — it holds whichever node the walk reached last and enumerates the **wrong** container's leaves while reading as coverage for the one someone opted in.

The first path-keyed version listed every container **twice**. Junos `groups` mirrors the whole schema, so each container also has a `groups/*/<path>` address pointing at the identical node. ## PR #8793 — config: traverse into a braced compound-key container, with the 30 measured [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-05)

Branch: `work/8763-traversal`

Part of #8763.

The brace-elision pass never traversed into a braced `family inet { … }`. For a
node with `Keys=[family inet]` it took `kw=Keys[0]="family"` and recursed with
`schema.children["family"]`, while the node's children belong to `family inet`
(`family.children["inet"]`). **The recursion advanced the schema one level where
the node advanced two**, so every lookup beneath a braced compound-key container
missed and the subtree was never visited — not "declined to fold", never asked.

It bites exactly where the second token is a **child keyword**. `unit 0` is
unaffected: there the second token is an instance arg, and `args` is precisely
what `identity` counts. Every `compoundKey` declaration in the schema is named
`family`, which bounds the surface.

## What this activates, measured pair by pair

30 admitted pairs are reachable **only** below a `family`. They folded nothing
before and fold for the first time after — and "the suite stays green" is not a
measurement of them, because a silently dropped value produces a clean commit
either way.

| verdict | n | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| reads-but-inert | 16 | the packed tail is **already** read; the fold changes nothing |
| recovery | 9 | dropped today; the fold delivers exactly the braced result |
| chain-incomplete | 2 | folds and **still** delivers nothing |
| refused either way | 2 | a live gate rejects the value in both spellings |
| reader defect | 1 | nothing reads it in **any** spelling; pre-existing |

**Nothing hazardous**, and the headline is the opposite of what "30 pairs go
live" suggests: the entire firewall-filter match and action surface —
`from source-address`, `destination-port`, `tcp-flags`, `icmp-type`,
`then policer`, `then forwarding-class`, `then routing-instance` — is **already
read** out of the packed tail, so this traversal activates none of it.

The nine real repairs: `flexible-match-range range`, `filter term`, the four
`flow-server` leaves, `output source-address`, `output flow-server`,
`prefix-limit maximum`.

`flexible-match-range range` is worth naming — **same container, same `from`,
opposite answer from the eleven beside it.** A container-level verdict would have
been wrong for it.

## The instrument is three-way, and that is the point

Comparing packed against braced establishes **agreement**, and two spellings agree
whenever both are wrong: a leaf whose reader ignores the value compiles
identically either way, so an agreement check reports success on a leaf that does
nothing. Every case therefore also compiles a **baseline** with the statement
removed.

## PR #8795 — config: read a brace-elided routing instance's packed body [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-05)

Branch: `fix/8787-instance-type-packed`

## The defect

```
routing-instances { ri1 { instance-type forwarding; } }   1 instance
routing-instances { ri1 instance-type forwarding; }       0 instances
routing-instances { ri1 interface ge-0/0/0.0; }           0 instances
```

Not a dropped property — the **entire instance vanished**, on a commit reporting success.

**The harmful direction is `forwarding`.** `InstanceType == "forwarding"` is what makes the daemon **skip** VRF creation, so a dropped value creates a VRF the operator asked *not* to have and moves interfaces into it — a forwarding and isolation change, not a lost label. **Reachable from a loaded or peer-synced config file, not from flat `set`** (which builds a chain and compiled correctly throughout): the boot and HA-sync paths rather than the CLI.

**Cause:** `compileRoutingInstances` skipped `child.IsLeaf`, and a brace-elided instance *is* a leaf.

## Not fixable by the #8690 normalizer

That pass is scoped per `(container, head)` pair, and the pair it asks for this site is **`("ri1", "instance-type")`** — the operator's *instance name*, not a keyword. No scope entry can name it. Measured both ways: admit-all folds the node, the real predicate cannot be made to.

The packed tail is read with the **same keyword set the braced switch handles**, so the two spellings cannot drift. `interface` consumes its whole run — the #3904 note records that reading only the first value stranded the remaining ports outside the instance (a VRF isolation break), and a single-value packed read would have reintroduced exactly that.

## Two separable halves, and mutation shows they do different work

Removing the schema declarations leaves **every compile assertion passing** — the compiler fix carries that alone. What the declarations do is offer the leaves in completion and `?` help: **2 completions before, 4 after**. Pinned by their own cell so the halves can't be confused. #8785 is why I measured rather than assumed: there, declaring a leaf was expected to fix a drop and did not.

The stale rationale is replaced, not left: *"instance-type and interface are NOT listed here → they become leaf nodes"* was true when written and stopped being true when packed-tail resolution landed.

## The guard asserts absolute outcomes

Never `packed == braced` — both spellings producing zero instances agree perfectly, so an equality cell is green on exactly the defect it exists to catch. Controls: braced and flat-`set` both already worked and must keep working; a bare `ri1;` must **not** become an untyped phantom VRF.

| mutant | fails |
|---|---|
| restore the `IsLeaf` skip | both packed subtests, neither control |
| disable the packed-tail read | both packed subtests, neither control |
| drop both schema declarations | **only** the completion cell |
| drop one declaration | that cell alone |

0 residual.

`gateCoverageFloor` 703 → 705: the #7484 ratchet reported *COVERAGE IMPROVED* and named the new floor — two leaves blind to the spelling gate are now compared, which is the declaration half working.

Full `pkg/config` green; `pkg/routing`, `pkg/daemon`, `pkg/frr` green; canaries green; gofmt clean.

## PR #8801 — config: carry the IKE identity through a packed gateway body [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-05)

Branch: `fix/local-identity-arity`

Closes #8796

An IKE gateway whose body is written as a **packed tail** silently loses `local-identity`, and depending on statement order loses the rest of the body with it. All of these commit cleanly on the strict path:

```
braced  gateway gw1 { ... local-identity hostname foo; }   local=hostname/foo ext=ge-0/0/0
packed  gateway gw1 local-identity hostname foo;           local=""/""        ext=""
packed  gateway gw1 local-identity ... external-interface  local=""/""        ext=""
packed  gateway gw1 external-interface ... local-identity  local=""/""        ext=ge-0/0/0
```

An IKE gateway compiled with no local identity does **not** fail closed: strongSwan falls back to the local address, so the tunnel negotiates under a different peer identity than the operator configured — it authenticates as the wrong party or not at all. `remote-identity` has the identical shape and defect.

### Master's fix is incomplete, and this completes it

While this was in flight, master opted the `security ike` gateway into `packedStatements`. That is **one of three decisions**, and alone it changes nothing — measured at master's exact state, all three packed spellings still return `LocalID=""/""`. The security defect is live on master right now behind a change that looks like it addressed it.

| decision | controls | status before this PR |
|---|---|---|
| pair admitted to `compactNormalizeInScope` | **whether** the tail folds | missing |
| `packedStatements` on the container | **how** the folded tail splits | master added it — to one of the two gateway containers |
| `args: 2` on the identity leaves | where each statement **ends** | missing |

Both remaining parts are re-verified load-bearing *on top of* master's change: removing either alone reds the cell. The second gateway container (`security ipsec`) is also opted in — same children, same compiler path, and fixing one of a pair leaves the defect live at a spelling operators reach the same way.

### Declaring the arity alone is inert

Measured byte-identical output. A fix that changed only the arity would have measured as correct on a harness forcing the other two and changed nothing shipped.

The arity hypothesis was **refuted by a control**, not by reasoning: two `args`-declared siblings in one packed tail (`external-interface ge-0/0/0 ike-policy pol1`) also lost the second statement, so a missing arity could not be the whole cause — the tail was building a **chain**, each statement nested under the previous. That control is kept in the cell; it is the only assertion there that catches the chain regressing.

The order-dependence is the diagnostic signature: the **first** leaf decides whether the pass fires, because admission is per `(container, leaf)` pair.

### A coverage trade, recorded rather than absorbed

Declaring `args: 2` moves those four leaves out of the #7484 spelling gate's `args<=1` population; the floor drops to 701. That cell says *"find what stopped compiling rather than lowering this floor"*, so that was done — nothing stopped compiling, four leaves changed declared shape for a correct reason, and the constant now carries the cause. Four spelling-gate verdicts traded for a packed spelling that stops discarding an IKE peer identity.

### Merge resolution

Both conflicts were substantive. The ratchet conflicted (master 705, branch 699) and was resolved by **re-measuring at the merged tree** rather than adjusting arithmetically — measured 701, which happens to equal 705 minus these four leaves; the agreement is the evidence, not the method. Master's #8768 fixture for the container was dropped in favour of this branch's: master's omits `local-identity` and `remote-identity`, so it would have opted the container in and never compared the leaves the opt-in exists for.

## PR #8802 — config: create every zone in a bracketed security-zone group [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-05)

Branch: `fix/8794-zone-group`

## The defect

`security-zone [ trust untrust ] { screen edge; }` created only `trust`. **Not a missing body — the later zone was never created**, because `namedInstances` takes `Keys[1]` and discards `Keys[2:]`. The syntax is affirmatively supported (`formatset_container_bracket_6668`, `wantCommit: true`).

## Severity: measured, and it is NOT the reported fail-open

```
policy naming the lost zone   strict REJECTS, naming it
CONTROL two explicit blocks   strict ACCEPTS      <- the miss is the cause
tolerant path                 accepts + 2 warnings, one naming the zone
grouped body's interfaces     land in the SURVIVING zone, not misattributed
```

The Rust `ScreenVerdict::Pass` path is **real but unreachable here** — `screen/tests.rs` calls it *"the legit Pass case"*, but it needs traffic attributed to the missing zone, and that zone has no interfaces. The report inferred the consequence from the shape; the shape is right, the path is not live.

**The harm is ordering:** commit the group before anything references it, and the loss is silent until a later unrelated commit fails pointing at the *policy* rather than at this statement.

## The HA concern dissolves — measuring is what showed it

The worry was that `ConfigTree.Format` emits bare keys, so a provenance-based fix would desync a primary from its standby. But the lexer strips brackets and both spellings parse to **identical trees**:

```
security-zone [ trust untrust ] { ... }   Keys=[..trust untrust] children=1
security-zone   trust untrust   { ... }   Keys=[..trust untrust] children=1
```

There is no provenance to preserve, so a provenance-only fix is impossible and any fix is structural — and a structural fix has both sides of the `Format` → `SyncApply` boundary fanning out identically. **No version fence needed.** A rolling upgrade still differs, but that is the pre-fix behaviour on the old node and errs toward *fewer* zones — the fail-closed direction.

## The discriminator cannot sweep in a packed tail

A group has surplus keys **and a braced body**; a packed tail has surplus keys and **no children**. Disjoint by the same property that separates them in the #8690 normalizer, whose fold requires `len(Children) == 0`. Scoped to zones deliberately — `namedInstances` is shared, and fanning it out globally is a separate decision with its own evidence.

## Validation

| mutant | fails |
|---|---|
| revert the fan-out | both group subtests, neither control |
| fan out only the first name | both group subtests + discriminator |
| weaken discriminator to `len(Keys) >= 3` | **only** the discriminator subtest |

**The safety subtest was vacuous and mutation found it.** Its first version fed `security-zone trust screen edge;` through a compile — and the weakened-discriminator mutant **survived**, because the #8690 normalizer admits `("security-zone","screen")` and pre-splits that tail before `compileZones` runs, so the input never reached the discriminator. It now calls `zoneGroupInstances8794` directly, the only way to put the bodiless shape in front of it.

Guard asserts **absolute outcomes** — both zones exist and carry the profile — never grouped == longhand, since two spellings each producing one zone agree perfectly.

Full `pkg/config` green, canaries green, gofmt clean.

Closes #8794

Branch: `work/8755-chain`

Part of #8755.

A brace-elided interface unit silently lost its address **or** its firewall filter
binding, on a commit reporting success with **zero warnings**. The filter case is a
fail-open: an operator binds a filter, the commit succeeds, no filter is applied —
and it emits **fewer** warnings than the correct spelling, because nothing is left
to warn about. A quieter commit is the signal an operator reads as healthier.

## Two symptoms, two mechanisms

The issue names both losses together and **they are not one defect.** They need
different numbers of chain links — measured, not inferred from the shared shape:

| spelling | links needed | state before |
|---|---|---|
| `family inet address 10.0.0.1/24;` | **one** | `(inet, address)` unadmitted → pass folded **0** times; the statement stayed one node |
| `family inet filter input f1;` | **two** | `(inet, filter)` **was** admitted → folded **1** time, to `family inet` + `filter input f1`, then stopped: `(filter, input)` was not in |

The filter half is the instructive one: **a scope entry existed, it fired, and it
delivered nothing.** Admission is a chain and only the first link was in. #8763
recorded that as `chain-incomplete` rather than leaving it to be rediscovered,
precisely because an admitted pair reads as coverage.

Had the two been treated as one defect, admitting `(filter, input)` would have
"fixed #8755" while the address half stayed broken with a green suite — **the two
symptoms have no link in common.**

## Four pairs admitted, reach checked against the schema

`inet address`, `inet6 address`, `filter input`, `filter output`.

Both heads exist under other containers, and pair scoping is what keeps them out —
checked by walking `setSchema`, not by asking the inventory (a census of divergent
*sites* answers a different question):

- `filter` is also `firewall family inet filter <name>` (args:1, children
  `{term, interface-specific}`) — **no** `input`/`output` child, so
  `(filter, input)` cannot reach it. Exactly two paths each, both the interface unit.
- `inet` is also under firewall, forwarding-options, protocols bgp and rib-group.
  **None** has an `address` child. `(inet, address)` reaches exactly one path.

A head-only rule would have been wrong for both.

## Three-way measurement, absolute assertions

A packed-vs-braced comparison goes green whenever **both** spellings drop the
value — exactly this defect's shape. So every case also compiles a **baseline**
with the statement removed, and the cell `Fatal`s if the baseline already
satisfies the expectation: that would mean the fixture cannot distinguish a
delivered value from a default.

Closes #8800

`security nat source pool <p> address <a>;` — the brace-elided ("packed") spelling — compiled to a pool with **zero addresses**, while `pool <p> { address <a>; }` compiled correctly.

## Cause

Neither the fold nor an under-declared arity — the two prior causes in this family. **`address` was never declared as a schema child of `pool`.** The compiler has read it since #4521 (multi-value: `Keys[1:]` plus block children), but with no declaration `isBody` is false, so the brace-elision pass was never *asked* about `("pool","address")` and no scope entry could ever have named the site. `pool port-overloading-factor` and `pool routing-instance` were already admitted — `address` was the one missing sibling of an otherwise in-scope container.

The first version of this PR fixed only the **source** pool, and that was a partial fix that read as complete. `compileNATDestination` reads `address` under a **destination** NAT pool too (`parseDNATPoolAddress`, which deliberately walks every token so `address <ip> port <n>` captures both), and that pool declared `children: nil` — the identical defect at the sibling path:

```
packed        addr=""          port=0     strict REJECTS   <- defect
braced-port   addr=10.0.0.5/32 port=8080  strict accepts
packed-port   addr=""          port=0     strict REJECTS   <- defect
```

After declaring it, all four agree and `packed-port` carries both the address and port 8080.

**What hid it is worth stating, because it generalises.** The scope predicate is **pair-keyed**: the `("pool","address")` entry added for the source pool *already* applied to the destination pool. Inspecting the scope list would have shown the pair present and looked correct while this path stayed broken. Only the schema declaration was missing, and only at one of the two containers. Found by asking which other container the same compiler-arm shape appears in — not by a test failing.

So this was a config-file-only defect, which is why it is a small change rather than an urgent one.

Declare `address` in `setSchema` so the pass asks, **and** admit `("pool","address")` in `compactNormalizeInScope` so it says yes. Declaring alone was measured to leave the packed spelling still compiling to zero addresses.

A second symptom of the same missing declaration: completion never offered `address` after `set security nat source pool <p>`.

## PR #8805 — cluster: bound the persistent-NAT lease count before allocating from it [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-05)

Branch: `fix/8792-lease-count-bounds`

Closes #8792

`decodePersistentNatLeasePayload` sized its preallocation from the 4-byte record count taken straight off the wire, and the loop's bounds check sat one line **below** the `make()` it was meant to protect:

```go
count := int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(buf))
out := make([]userspace.IdleLeaseWire, 0, count)   // sized from the wire
for i := 0; i < count; i++ {
    if off+4 > len(buf) { return out, false }      // correct, and unreachable
}
```

A four-byte frame of `ff ff ff ff` asks for 2^32−1 records of 112 bytes — about 448 GiB — before a single length prefix has been read. Each record costs at least its own 4-byte length prefix, so the body holds at most `(len(buf)-4)/4`; a count above that cannot describe the frame under any encoding and is now refused **before** the allocation.

### Refused rather than clamped, unlike the DHCP sibling

That decoder carries this bound under "the #7175 discipline" — which this function's doc comment already cited — but it separates a wrong *count* from lost *data* and tolerates the former, a tolerance its own cell pins. This one's bool means "decoded **completely**", and a full-set push **replaces** the peer set, so installing whatever fit would delete every lease past the point the sender's count went wrong. The divergence is deliberate and now recorded at both ends.

### What this does not claim

Not that it stops a crash. Whether the oversized allocation is fatal is a property of the **host**: `112 × (2^32−1)` stays under the runtime's `maxAlloc` so no `makeslice` panic is inherent, and under `overcommit_memory=1` the mapping can succeed unbacked and the process survives to discard the frame. The invariant repaired here holds everywhere — a count the body cannot physically hold is rejected before the allocation.

Reachability, stated precisely: a supported **unkeyed** control segment, plus a malfunctioning or malicious **legitimate peer** on a keyed one. No Internet-facing exposure was established.

Worth keeping: the receive loop's `defer` only disconnects. It is not a recovery boundary, so wrapping the decoder in `recover()` is not a fix even where the allocation *is* fatal — a Go runtime OOM is a `fatal error`, not a panic.

### The guard measures the allocation, not only the return values

This is the assertion that earned itself. **A bound applied one line too late produces identical return values** — `ok=false`, zero leases — so an outcome-only cell is green on the defect.

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| bound removed (the original defect) | killed |
| bound moved **below** the `make` (outcome identical) | **killed by the allocation budget alone** |
| checked subtraction reverted | **escaped** |

The third is reported rather than fixed: with the count bounded, neither operand can overflow on any reachable input, so the subtraction form is shape hygiene and not part of the repair. The code says so at the line, so it is not later mistaken for load-bearing.

**The cell deliberately does not use `0xFFFFFFFF`.** A guard whose regression mode is to allocate hundreds of gigabytes does not fail — it takes the suite, and possibly the machine, with it. Every count in it is impossible for its buffer while staying trivially small, so a revert reds in milliseconds. The allocation probe uses `1<<20` (~112 MiB if the bound is bypassed): unmistakable against GC noise, survivable anywhere.

### Docs

`docs/sync-protocol.md` gains the rule rather than the instance — a wire-advertised count is untrusted, the bound is `(len(body)-4)/4`, the check must precede the allocation, the two decoders' answers differ deliberately, and a test for this class must assert the invariant rather than a crash.

### Validation

Full `go test ./...` green tree-wide — 72 packages ok, 0 FAIL, **counted** rather than inferred; `gofmt -l` clean; each mutant confirmed to *apply* and to build before its verdict was read.

```
compiler_empty_security_identity.go:57
compiler_tunnel_plaintext_advisory.go:196
```

Before that fix, every path consistently saw one zone. After it:

```
compiler zones      = [trust untrust]
collectZoneNamesAST = [trust]
```

**A zone existed in the compiled config that the zone-ID collision machinery could not see.** A uniform truncation became an internal disagreement.

## One entry point, not five patches

All six sites now share `zoneGroupInstances8794`. The disagreement *is* the argument for a single helper: a sixth caller added later inherits the behaviour instead of re-introducing the split.

The new cell asserts **agreement rather than a count**, so it survives a change in the group's cardinality and fails for *any* enumeration path that regresses to `namedInstances` — not only the five that existed when it was written. Mutation: reverting `zoneid.go` **alone** is caught by it.

## How it was found

The #8794 census carries a positive control requiring `security-zone` to be at-risk **before** the fix and to **vanish after**. It did not vanish — the census still reported five call sites at master.

**A control that only had to fire pre-fix would have passed.** One that must also go quiet afterwards is what caught an incomplete fix in already-landed code.

`Closes #8794` on #8802 was an overclaim: the defect it names was only partly closed, and this completes it.

## PR #8809 — config: the IPv6 forwarding mode was read from a shape nothing produces [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-05)

Branch: `work/8797-inet6-mode`

Part of #8797.

`forwarding-options family inet6 mode <flow-based|packet-based>` compiled to an
empty value **in every spelling an operator can write**. The leaf completes, `?`
help describes it, commit returns success, `show configuration` renders it back —
and `ForwardingOptions.FamilyInet6Mode` stayed `""`.

## It was not unread, which is the part that matters

#8797 recorded this as "declared and accepted with no reader", measured with a
baseline-with-the-statement-removed: `braced == baseline`, and `packet-based ==
flow-based`. **Both observations were right and the diagnosis they suggested was
wrong.**

There *is* a reader. `compileForwardingOptions` descended
`FindChild("family") → FindChild("inet6") → FindChild("mode")` — a **two-level**
lookup. But `family` is declared `compoundKey`, so the parser **and** `SetPath`
both produce **one** node with `Keys=["family","inet6"]`; the address family is
part of the node's key, not a child of it.

| spelling | before |
|---|---|
| `family inet6 { mode packet-based; }` (NewParser) | `""` |
| `family inet6 mode packet-based;` (one-liner) | `""` |
| `set forwarding-options family inet6 mode …` (**what operators type**) | `""` |
| `family { inet6 { mode packet-based; } }` | `"packet-based"` |

The one shape that worked is the split form the #2419 census synthesizes and
nothing else emits. **The leaf looked unread because every spelling that could
reach it missed, and the one that hit is not a spelling.**

This is the **same defect as #8763's traversal bug** — a two-level lookup against
a one-node compound key — in a compiler instead of the normalizer. That class has
now appeared in the normalizer, in a guard's own tree walk, and here. The
`compoundKey` shape is the one people model wrongly.

## Testing

Four hierarchical spellings plus the **flat `set`** form — the one that matters
here: it is what an operator types, it went through the broken path, and a
hierarchical-only test would have reported this fixed while
`set forwarding-options family inet6 mode packet-based` still compiled to `""`.

A baseline leg asserts the field is empty with no statement, so a green cannot be
a default. The **value** is asserted, not just presence: `flow-based` and
`packet-based` must compile to *different* values, since them compiling to the
same thing was half the original symptom.
