## PR #9593 — config: reject an address carrying a prefix and an unimplemented value form (#9524) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-10)

Branch: `fix/9524-address-mixed-substanza`

Closes #9524

## What was wrong

A Junos `address` takes exactly one value form: a prefix, or a `dns-name`, `wildcard-address` or `range-address`. xpf implements only the prefix. An entry carrying **both** compiled to the prefix alone on every config channel, with no warning. The other form was discarded before representability ever saw it.

Measured at `c7a497c5c`, per channel:

| channel | before |
|---|---|
| `config.SchemaValidate` | accepted |
| `config.CompileConfig` | accepted, no warning |
| `configstore.CheckText` | accepted |
| `config.CompileConfigLenient` | accepted, book holds only the prefix |
| `PolicyContentRejectionReasons` | empty |

With a `deny` on the object and `default-policy permit-all`, `policymatch.Match` let 192.0.2.5 (named by the entry's `range-address`) and 10.0.0.1 (named by its `wildcard-address`) fall through to the default. The dropped half narrows the match and never widens it, silently.

## Documented contract

#3261 already taints an address-**set** that mixes a literal member with an unimplemented one ("any unrepresentable member taints the whole name"). The single-address mixed form escaped that rule only because the form was dropped at parse time. This change aligns the single entry with the set doctrine. A sole `dns-name` / `wildcard-address` / `range-address` is valid Junos and keeps its existing handling: #3149 strict reject when referenced, #3261 poison on the tolerant path.

## Change

- `Address.UnimplementedForms` records the form in both parser shapes, and the zone-local fold copies it.
- `validateAddressUnimplementedFormsStrict` rejects a prefix-bearing entry that also carries a form, naming both. The tolerant path downgrades it to a warning (`lenientAddressUnimplementedForms`, #1960 no-brick). The gate skips the synthetic `zone-local/` names, so the error names what the operator wrote.
- `Address.UsableValue()` is `""` for such an entry. The userspace representability resolver and the junos-host deny projection read it, so a referencing policy on the tolerant path fails closed exactly like the sole-form case. `Value` is kept for show surfaces.
- The warn validator names the dropped form.
- **Not changed, on purpose:**
  - `policyMatchAddressBookResolves` is shared with the NAT strict gate, and the new commit gate covers it.
  - Static-NAT prefix-name resolution is a scalar target that already refuses an address with no prefix.
  - For the legacy userspace expansion, a trial switch was unobservable: the #3261 sentinel already replaces a poisoned rule's addresses.

## Validation

- **Cells** in `pkg/config`, `pkg/configstore`, `pkg/dataplane/userspace` and `pkg/policymatch`:
  - strict reject and tolerant warning for all three forms, in both token orders, both parser shapes, and zone-local;
  - `CheckText` rejects and names the entry;
  - the wire sentinel and mirror reason;
  - the simulator reports `ContentRejected` for the range-address host.
- **Accepting controls:** a sole prefix, a sole unreferenced `dns-name`, a prefix with a description, a zone-local sole prefix, and a mixed entry that nothing references (no poison).
- **Go mutation matrix**, 14 cells, scored on `go test -json` `Action=="fail"` against each cell's target names:
  - the unmutated control collected 6/6 with no failures;
  - **13/13 KILLED, 0 SURVIVED, 0 VOID**;
  - every mutation was confirmed applied by occurrence count.

  The mutants sever the recording in both shapes, the zone-local fold, the gate call site, the lenient downgrade and its constructor flag, `UsableValue`, both reader switches and the warn arm. They also over- and under-reach the gate.
- **`make test`** (Go + Rust) at the tested head: 77 Go packages ok, 0 FAIL; Rust 5748 passed, 0 failed.
- **Landing rule:** master moved since the tested base (`c7a497c5c` -> `c71f9d556`), `master_delta ∩ mine` is empty, and no mutated file changed on master.
  - The merged tree was compiled first: `go build ./...` ok; the `go vet ./...` differential shows 0 diagnostics on master, 0 on the merged tree, 0 new; `cargo check --tests --benches` ok.

## PR #9597 — userspace: refuse a policy whose application the tolerant compile changed (#9525) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-10)

Branch: `fix/9525-app-spec-lenient-poison`

Closes #9525

## What was wrong

The application spec, syntax and structure gates reject on commit and `CheckText`, but on the tolerant load / HA peer-sync path (`lenientApplicationSpecs`, #1960 no-brick) they only warn. The documented contract of that downgrade (#2142) is that a leniently loaded bad application "is inert rather than silently mis-matching". It held only for drops the userspace expansion could see: a malformed port, a missing or unresolvable protocol. Every other member installed a well-formed-looking term that matched something else, and `PolicyContentRejectionReasons` stayed empty.

## Measured

Channel: `config.CompileConfigLenient`, followed through the policy wire, `PolicyContentRejectionReasons` and `policymatch.Match`, at `e90b9f714` and `c71f9d556`.

| member | before |
|---|---|
| `destination-port` on icmp / gre / sctp | never matches (a deny never fires; the simulator even permitted sctp/80) |
| `source-port` on icmp / icmpv6 | matched against the sender-chosen ICMP Identifier |
| `icmp-type` / `icmp-code` 999 (direct or term) | dropped, so every type or code matches (a permit widens) |
| icmp field on tcp; code without type | the helper already refuses (#3712), but the mirror certified a verdict |
| dangling `destination-port` / `icmp-type` | widens to every port or type |
| conflicting `destination-port` / `protocol` | last value only (a deny under-covers) |
| direct body mixed with terms (also nested in a set) | direct body discarded (a deny under-covers) |

## Dispositions, every downgraded arm

- **Refused (this PR):** every row above.
- **Already refused, unchanged:** a malformed port (invalid, 0, inverted), a missing protocol, an unresolvable protocol.
- **Still installed, benign:** a bad, dangling or conflicting timeout or `alg`. The match set is unchanged, measured.
- **Deferred to #9595:** `UnknownDirectLeaves`, `UnknownTermLeaves` and `UnknownMembers`.
  - #6524's `TestStrayStatementDoesNotDisarmSiblingLeaves` explicitly decides that a stray statement must not disarm a well-formed application, and it is recorded as `UnknownDirectLeaves`.
  - A mutant that refuses on that record is killed by exactly that cell.

- `config.ApplicationMatchDrops` and `config.ApplicationReferenceMatchDrops` name the drops.
  - The reference walk resolves the way the expansion does and adds `MixedDirectTermApps`.
  - Only match leaves count: `applicationMatchLeaves9525` and `applicationSettingLeaves9525` partition `valueTakingApplicationLeaves`.
- `expandUserspacePolicyApplications` refuses a reference with any drop.
  - The rule lowers to the #3261 `__unsupported__` sentinel, and the helper refuses the whole snapshot (a running node keeps its previous one).
  - The mirror names the application.
- The strict `source-port` text now names the ICMP Identifier instead of claiming non-port protocols present ports of 0.
- The #6766 policymatch verdict cells pinned keep-last *enforcement*.

  - The app-id catalog only stamps flow app ids.

## PR #9598 — userspace-dp: purge a deleted first policy's sessions the daemon sweep must skip (#9526) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-10)

Branch: `fix/9526-first-policy-delete-purge`

Closes #9526

## What was wrong

The commit-time session sweep (`pkg/daemon/daemon_policy_invalidate.go`) clears a deleted policy's sessions by `policy_id`, and it deliberately skips 0. The literal first policy's positional id is 0, but 0 is also what host-local, neighbor-seed, fabric, tunnel and older-HA-peer sessions carry. The skip is right, and it stays. Its rationale said the first policy's sessions "idle out" instead. They don't for a one-way flow: the #8356 re-derivation declines every reverse packet, and reverse traffic keeps the forward half alive (`companion_keeps_alive`). So after the first policy was deleted or renamed, a server push or one-way UDP reply stream kept transiting on a commit that reported success.

## Premise re-measured at current master, as asked

| issue's exit | at `48a5177be` |
|---|---|
| zone-0 decline | **gone** (#9513 re-judges an unzoned interface) |
| GATE 1 reverse decline | present |
| GATE 1b type-constrained ICMP decline | present |
| `companion_keeps_alive` | present |
| anything else clearing the session | none: `DEFAULT_POLICY_SENTINEL_ID` is attribution-only, and the #3395 refresh re-stamps rows but deletes nothing (directory pathspecs + positive controls) |

## Why the fix is in the helper

The Go capture iterates the BPF conntrack map, which carries only the overloaded `policy_id`, and `PolicyCounterIdx` is documented as not on that map. The helper has the discriminator: a session a policy admitted binds that rule's counter handle, which carries its stable id, and the overloaded-zero installs bind none. The default-policy handle has the non-empty id `default-policy`, so the purge keys on the first rule's id, not on "rule vanished".

## Change

- `PolicyState::first_policy_rule_id` returns the one rule at id 0, or `None` when several rules carry 0 (the unassigned all-zero shape M01 tolerates). `has_rule_id` is added alongside.
- `deleted_first_policy_rule_id(old, new)` returns that rule's id when the new snapshot lacks it (deleted or renamed).
- `purge_sessions_bound_to_deleted_first_policy` walks the forward sessions bound to it and tears each down via `delete_terminal_filtered_session`: both halves, NAT release, shared HA maps, `DeleteSynced`, and a close delta that becomes an HA peer delete.
- The worker loop compares before `forwarding = new_forwarding;` and purges after it. The compare is O(rules) per rotation, and the session walk runs only when the first policy vanished.
- The daemon rationale is corrected in both sweep builders. Go behaviour is unchanged.
- Not covered: a MODIFIED first policy keeps its stable id, so policy-rematch still leaves it to the re-derivation. Filed as #9596.

## Validation

- Rust cells (`deleted_first_policy_purge_9526_tests.rs`):
  - the accessors, including all-zero and empty snapshots;
  - the rule choice: delete and rename fire; unchanged, a later deletion, a reorder and an all-zero old snapshot do not;
  - the purge removes both halves of the bound first-policy pair with one close delta, and keeps the second-policy, unbound id-0 and default-policy pairs;
  - the worker-loop wiring, bound on the source because the rotation block has no unit harness: the compare runs before assignment, and the purge sits under its answer and tears down under the new state.
- The daemon cells pinning the id-0 exclusion still pass.
- **Rust mutation matrix:** 13 cells, scored on each named target's `test ... FAILED` line (a build failure, a timeout or nothing collected scores VOID). The unmutated control collected 4/4 and passed. 12/12 mutants KILLED, 0 SURVIVED, 0 VOID, each confirmed applied by occurrence count, and the tree was clean after the run. The mutants sever or skew the loop's compare (severed, reading the new state twice) and its purge (guard severed, keyed on an empty id); drop the duplicate-zero guard; key the first rule on id 1; make has_rule_id always false; make the choice ignore the new snapshot; and break the purge filter (reverse entries included, the rule id ignored, unbound sessions matched, no deletion).
- **`make test`:** (Go + Rust) at bde5fe562: 77 Go packages ok, 0 FAIL; Rust 5785 passed, 0 failed.
- **Landing rule:** master MOVED since the tested base (48a5177be -> d1266ee79) and master_delta ∩ mine is EMPTY, with no mutated file changed on master. The merged tree was compiled in a throwaway worktree first: go build ./... ok; the go vet ./... differential shows 0 diagnostics on master alone, 0 on the merged tree, 0 new; cargo check --tests --benches ok. Merged with --match-head-commit.
- **HA note:** this adds a new caller of the existing HA-aware teardown path (`delete_terminal_filtered_session`), and no session-sync or failover code changed. `make test-failover` was not run in this lane; whether that gate applies is a call for review.

## PR #9599 — config: state where a WireGuard tunnel's zone is enforced in the #5618 advisory [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-10)

Branch: `fix/9251-wg-plaintext-advisory-residual`

## Summary

Since #8274, the #5618 commit advisory had been telling every WireGuard operator
something false: that decapsulated traffic is "NOT evaluated against xpf security
policies", and, for a zoned tunnel, "ASSIGNED A ZONE THAT IS NOT ENFORCED — this
reads as protected and is not". #8274 moved WireGuard transport decap into the
AF_XDP worker, which adjudicates the inner packet under the tunnel's zone.

The advisory now states both halves:

- the zone governs the **dataplane path**;
- it does **not** govern the **kernel path**. On that path, a transport record
  for the steered listen port reaches the helper's control thread through the
  kernel, via ingress the shim does not attach to (#8274's residual) or a
  degraded dataplane (#9594). The thread writes it to `wgN` and the kernel
  forwards it. Other listen ports are dropped there (#9521).
- An unzoned tunnel's transit is **denied** on the dataplane path (#6682). This
  is now pinned through the poll loop.

The renderer's headings and unzoned caveat stop being shared with the #5619 IPsec
advisory; they are protocol-specific since #8274. They become required fields
with no default, so one advisory cannot silently render the other's account.
IPsec output is byte-identical.

Closes #9251

## What changed

- `pkg/config/compiler_wireguard_plaintext_warn.go`: new lead, zoned suffix,
  mechanism, remedy, and WireGuard's own headings and unzoned caveat. The file
  header and function doc describe the post-#8274 dataplane and kernel paths,
  and say why the advisory still names every tunnel: the steered port's only
  derivation reads the typed Config, which does not exist yet in the AST pre-walk.
- `pkg/config/compiler_tunnel_plaintext_advisory.go`: `zonedHeading`,
  `unzonedHeading` and `unzonedCaveat` become required `plaintextAdvisoryWording`
  fields with no default. The contract comment says why they stopped being shared.
- `pkg/config/compiler_ipsec_plaintext_warn.go`: IPsec's headings and caveat
  move here with text unchanged.
- `pkg/config/compiler_prewalk.go`: the #5618 call-site comment.
- Docs: the `userspace-dataplane-gaps.md` WireGuard row and section (renamed
  "Tunnel plaintext adjudication", with a per-path table), and a pointer note in
  the #7167 adjudication.
- #1434 steering selectors (`pkg/config`, `pkg/dataplane/userspace`): the first

## PR #9600 — userspace-dp: run the input filter and PBR verdict before the flowless ICMP-error arms (#9528) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-10)

Branch: `fix/9528-flowless-icmp-error-gates`

Closes #9528

## What was wrong

The flowless poll arm has two ICMP-error exceptions that `continue` with the descriptor consumed: #6472 translates a NAT64 error, and #5690 reverses a same-family embedded-ICMP error. Each ran ahead of a gate below it.

| order at `48a5177be` | site |
|---|---|
| 1 | #6472 NAT64 arm (`continue` on Queued/Dropped) |
| 2 | #7359 interface input filter |
| 3 | #5690 same-family arm (`continue`) |
| 4 | #3291 flowless enforcement, the only `ingress_route_table_override` (PBR) on this path |

Consequences:

- An input `discard` did not drop a NAT64-translated error.
- A `then { routing-instance X; discard; }` term could not drop either arm's error.
- In both cases the term's counter did not advance, so the gap was invisible too.

## Contract

The tree states it three times. #7359 hoisted the filter above the #5690 arm: "a discard term did not drop it, a count term did not advance, and a policer did not meter". #5798 and #6835 made the association-hit arm run the input filter and then PBR, because a matching routing-instance term makes `evaluate_non_pbr_input_filter` return Accept before recording its counter or applying its action. No document exempts either arm.

## Change

Pure code motion inside one block:

- The arm now builds the L3 context, runs the non-PBR input filter, runs the PBR verdict (`Drop` recycles), and only then tries the #6472 and #5690 arms.
- The flowless transit enforcement consumes the same `route_table_override`. Both evaluators are **hoisted, not duplicated**, so every term counts once.
- A non-drop steer is not applied to an error an arm queues, which goes to the quoted session's owner (the association hit's reasoning).
- The afxdp README and the NAT64 row in `docs/feature-coverage.md` now state the order.

## Validation

- Behavioural cells in `tests_embedded_poll_filter.rs`, driven through `poll_binding_process_descriptor` with real frames. Each has a no-filter control in the same harness that must still forward. The meta carries the stamped L3 identity; without it every gate is skipped and the cells would pass vacuously.
  - NAT64 plus an input `discard`: dropped, counted once.
  - NAT64 plus a PBR `discard`: dropped, counted once.
  - #5690 plus a PBR `discard`: dropped, counted once.
  - An accepting term and a PBR steer on both arms: still delivered, counted exactly once.
  - A flowless non-first fragment with a PBR steer: evaluated exactly once.
- The full `tests_embedded_poll_filter` and `poll_descriptor` groups pass: tests_embedded_poll_filter 44 passed, poll_descriptor 174 passed, 0 failed
- **Rust mutation matrix:** 6 cells, run at 185f3ecec (and identically at f4ae5b751 before the fixture fix), scored on each named target's `test ... FAILED` line (a build failure, a timeout or nothing collected scores VOID). The unmutated control collected 5/5 and passed. 5/5 mutants KILLED, 0 SURVIVED, 0 VOID, and the tree was clean after the run. The mutants: the #6472 arm inserted back ahead of the input filter; the #5690 arm inserted back ahead of the PBR verdict; the hoisted PBR Drop ignored; the PBR verdict evaluated twice; the hoisted input-filter deny skipped. The three insertions keep their anchor, so their occurrence count reads 1->1 and the kill proves they applied; the other two were confirmed by count.
- **`make test`:** (Go + Rust) at 185f3ecec: 77 Go packages ok, 0 FAIL; Rust 5786 passed, 0 failed. The first run, at f4ae5b751, was red on the #7689 ratchet (NeighborSnapshot exhaustive literals 27 > 26). The +1 was this change's own new fixture literal, so it was rewritten with ..Default::default() rather than raising the ceiling.
- **Landing rule:** master MOVED since the tested base, twice. It first moved d1266ee79 -> 042effebb (the #9526 merge); that merged tree compiled (go build ./... ok; go vet ./... differential 0 master / 0 merged / 0 new; cargo check --tests --benches ok). Master then moved again to fe86a51c8 (the #9599 merge) before the push, which the pre-push guard caught. The check was re-run against fe86a51c8: master_delta ∩ mine EMPTY, no mutated file changed on master, and the merged tree compiled again with the same results. Merged with --match-head-commit.

## PR #9605 — cluster: bound the DHCP lease decoder before it allocates [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-10)

Branch: `fix/9507-dhcp-lease-decode-bound`

Closes #9507

## What was wrong

The DHCP full-set lease decoder **preallocated the wire count**, clamped only to `len(payload)/4`, before validating a single record. It also accepted zero-length records, which decode to a zero-valued 168-byte lease, so 4 wire bytes bought a retained lease.

- Measured at 1 MiB, one frame allocated **44,056,920 bytes, 42× the frame**. At the 16 MiB frame cap that is about **672 MiB per address family**.
- The junk leases **replaced the standby's peer set**. A cell drove one frame through `handleMessage` and lost a legitimate stored set.

**Reachable before authentication on a cluster with no key.** `handleMessage` decodes after only the per-family sequence admit. The receive loop verifies the auth trailer only when the connection is authenticated, and cluster sync authentication is an optional config leaf. Any host with L3 reach to the fabric listener can deliver the frame.

## The change: validate, then allocate

- **A count above `len/4`** refuses the frame at once. That is the same `(nil, false)` the old clamp-then-loop reached, but without its allocation.
- **Pass 1 allocates nothing.** It walks the records the count names and stops cleanly at the buffer end, which is #7175's tolerance for an over-declared count. It refuses the frame on any of:
  - a record under **36 bytes**;
  - a cut record;
  - an empty address, or one that overruns its record.
- **Pass 2** allocates exactly the validated records.

A refused frame returns `(nil, false)`, so the full-set REPLACE is suppressed and the standby keeps its set, exactly as for a cut record today.

**Why 36.** It is the smallest record that can carry a real lease: the #2239 layout with a one-byte address. #2239 already had every field through the FQDN flags byte, with `uint16` string prefixes, and #5073 later appended `PreferredRemaining`. So a rolling upgrade's oldest record still decodes.

**The bound.** The sender caps nothing, and the receiver's 16 MiB frame cap limits a legitimate set, so a bound derived from bytes cannot refuse a deliverable set. A retained lease now costs at least 40 wire bytes, about **4.2× the frame** plus its string bytes, and an impossible frame **allocates nothing**.

**A first attempt that only preallocated by bytes failed my own ceiling cell**, written before the fix: 4.3× against a 4× limit. The cell was right, which is why the decoder now validates before it allocates.

## Tests (`pkg/cluster/dhcp_lease_decode_bound_9507_test.go`)

| Cell | At base | After |
|---|---|---|
| zero-length ceiling frame: within 4× and malformed | **RED** (42.0×) | green |
| ceiling frame does not replace a stored set | **RED** (set lost) | green |
| a 35-byte record (the floor's boundary) is malformed | **RED** | green |
| an empty-address record is malformed | **RED** | green |
| the oldest #2239-format record still decodes | green | green |
| **a legitimate set filling one 16 MiB frame decodes completely** | green | green |
| minimal valid records stay within 6× | green | green |
| an over-declared count allocates only whole records | — | green |
| an address overrunning its record is malformed | — | green |

The #7175 contract cells (`TestDHCPLeasePayload_TruncatedStream`, `TestDHCPFullSetStillToleratesAnOverDeclaredCount7175`, `TestDHCPFullSetRejectsARecordCutMidStream7175`) and every existing DHCP lease cell stay green. The full `pkg/cluster` package runs 971 tests with 0 failed.

## Validation

**Mutation matrix** (`scripts/mutate-9507.py`, at 099487fff): **9 of 9 KILLED**, none survived, none VOID.
- Go-only, over the whole `pkg/cluster` package per run.
- Every mutant applied by count; every run bounded.
- Verdicts scored from `go test -json` by the killing cell's name. A run that started fewer than 50 tests would have been VOID.

## PR #9606 — userspace-dp: take test ports from an ephemeral source, not fixed numbers [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-10)

Branch: `fix/9549-ephemeral-test-ports`

## Summary

A census found fifteen `userspace-dp` unit tests that bind fixed UDP ports on the WireGuard control-thread path: thirteen at the start, and two more that a merge during review (#9592) added. #9549 named one of them. A second copy of the suite on the same host holds the same ports, and a mutation matrix runs two copies by design. The tests then failed with a bind panic that reads like a WireGuard regression.

Measured on `origin/master` `fe86a51c8`, release test binary, on those fifteen cells only:

| control | result |
| --- | --- |
| nothing else holds the ports | 0 of 15 fail |
| an external process holds the ports | 5 fail |
| 8 concurrent copies, 5 rounds | 40 of 40 copies fail |

The other ten cells passed while their listener could not bind. They had silently stopped exercising a bound listener.

## Change

- `src/test_ports.rs` (new, `cfg(test)`) provides two helpers:
  - `hold_ephemeral_udp_port()` binds `[::]:0` and returns the holders with the port, for a test that needs the port held as a blocker.
  - `reserve_ephemeral_udp_port()` releases the port for the code under test to bind. It never hands the same port out twice in one process, and it panics after 64 attempts rather than hanging.
- The named server cell and the EADDRINUSE tombstone rig hold their port. The other thirteen coordinator cells reserve one. The bind panic now blames the test host, not WireGuard.
- Remaining risk: another process can take a released port in the milliseconds before the WG control thread binds it. That is far rarer than a fixed port, but not zero.
- **The #1866 server cell could not see the rule it pins.** `run_request` serializes the request, and `wg_local_privkey_hex` is `skip_serializing`, so the key never reached the handler and the refresh held no WireGuard endpoint. "No WG thread spawned" passed whichever refresh ran. A new test helper, `run_request_delivering_wg_secrets`, re-inserts the secrets as the Go control plane sends them, and the cell asserts one WG engine (`wg_engine_count_for_test`, `cfg(test)`) before trusting its no-spawn checks. Reverting the handler's disarmed call site, or making the disarmed refresh spawn, now fails the cell; neither did before.
- `a_held_port_is_ephemeral_and_actually_held_9549` also asserts that the returned port is the `[::]` holder's own. An earlier matrix run showed the v4 holder could hide a mismatch on a dual-stack host.
- `docs/engineering-style.md` adds "Ports in tests (#9549)" beside "Time in tests". #9502 is the same class with a different resource (a wall-clock budget in `cmd/xpfd`), and it is linked, not changed here.

## Validation

- **Controls on the fixed tree**: On the final head `47377cf2f` (base `fe86a51c8`): with an external process holding the 17 former fixed ports, 0 cells fail (base: 5). With 8 concurrent copies for 5 rounds, 0 of 40 copies fail (base: 40 of 40). With nothing holding them, all 15 pass, and both new `test_ports` cells pass. Table in `docs/log/9549.md`.
- **Mutation**: 6 of 6 KILLED on `e946ac790` (code-identical to the head `47377cf2f`), none void, each scored by the failing test's name against its own target (table in `docs/log/9549.md`). The named #1866 cell kills Q1 (the disarmed refresh spawning) and Q2 (the handler's disarmed call site severed). The `test_ports` cells kill F1 (a fixed held port), F2 (a returned port the `[::]` holder does not hold), F3 (a repeated reservation) and F4 (a leaked holder). A first run, before the live-cell and identity fixes, had three survivors: Q1, Q2 and F2.
- **`make test`, both legs**: exit 0 on `47377cf2f` (`origin/master` `fe86a51c8` plus this commit). Go: 77 packages ok, no FAIL. Rust: 5,788 passed, 0 failed, across all 11 test binaries. Lands via merge commit with no further rebase: the `origin/master` delta since the tested base `fe86a51c8` shares no files with this change, and whenever master has moved past that base the merged tree must pass `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` (nothing beyond master's own diagnostics) and `cargo check --tests --benches` in `userspace-dp` before the merge.

Closes #9549

## PR #9607 — vrrp: surface a failed becomeMaster rollback as a stale VIP [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-10)

Branch: `fix/9509-becomemaster-rollback-surface`

Closes #9509

## What was wrong

When `becomeMaster` could not actuate its VIP set, its fail-closed arm rolled back the VIPs it had added and **discarded the rollback's error**, then published BACKUP. If that rollback delete also failed, the node advertised **BACKUP while still holding a VIP** the peer was about to own: split ARP/ND ownership, the condition chassis cluster exists to prevent.

## What the node was actually left in

This was measured at base with a fake kernel behind the existing netlink seams:
- VIP 1 adds, VIP 2 fails, and the rollback delete fails.
- `becomeMaster` returns false, the state is `StateBackup`, and BACKUP is published.
- **VIP 1 stays on the interface.**
- `vipRemoveFailures` stays 0, and `vipDiverged` stays false.
- **No delete is ever attempted again**, across seven retry windows after the fault clears.

Nothing else converges it either:
- `ReconcileVIPs` acts only on a MASTER.
- The master-down retry never fires while a healthy peer adverts.
- The daemon's per-tick VIP net is gated to no-RETH VRRP.

## The change: a call, not new machinery

`becomeMaster`'s fail-closed arm captures `rollbackErr`, sets BACKUP, releases `vipMu`, and then calls `surfaceStaleVIP(rollbackErr, "becomeMaster-rollback")`, exactly as `becomeBackup` does. That gives the failure counter, the divergence flag, an Error log, and the bounded, generation-fenced reconcile.
- **Ordering.** The reconcile captures `ownerGen` when it is scheduled, and it takes `vipMu`. Calling it before BACKUP is set makes it fence itself out; mutant V4 proves that.
- **Unconditional.** A clean rollback clears a divergence flag that an earlier, now-superseded reconcile left set.

**The second discard (`reconcileVIP`'s superseded arm) stays log-only, on evidence rather than argument.**
- Every state write goes through `setState`.
- The only transition that can supersede a reconcile holding `vipMu` is `becomeBackup`. It then blocks on `vipMu`, removes **all** configured VIPs, and surfaces that result.
- `TestSupersededReconcileRollbackIsCoveredByBecomeBackup_9509` races a real `becomeBackup` against a real `reconcileVIP` with every delete failing. It is green **at base**.
- That site's rollback error is now logged, and both false comments that justified the discards are replaced.

## Tests (`pkg/vrrp/becomemaster_rollback_9509_test.go`)

| Cell | At base | After |
|---|---|---|
| acceptance: the stranded VIP is surfaced and reconciled away | **RED** (`vipRemoveFailures = 0`) | green |
| permanence: a delete is attempted again | **RED** (no delete ever again) | green |
| a clean rollback clears a stale divergence flag | **RED** | green |
| control: a clean rollback flags nothing | green | green |
| guard: a re-promotion during the retry keeps both VIPs | green | green |
| second-site adjudication (above) | green | green |

The #5082 and #5482 neighbours stay green (13 of 13 in the package run). gofmt and `go vet` are clean.

## Validation

**Mutation matrix** (`scripts/mutate-9509.py`, the whole `pkg/vrrp` package per run, scored by test name): **4 of 4 KILLED**, 0 VOID.

| Mutant | Killed by |

## PR #9610 — userspace-dp: announce a close seen only by a worker replica [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-10)

Branch: `fix/9582-replica-close-announce`

Closes #9582

## What was wrong

A TCP close that only a **worker replica** saw never reached the HA peer. That is typically the server's FIN or RST, arriving on the other interface's RSS queue. Only the installing worker announced close-class transitions: a replica has origin `WorkerLocalImport`, and `emit_close_state_update` returned for every `is_peer_synced()` origin. After a failover, the peer's copy aged on the established window.

## Why "let replicas announce" was not enough

Replicas did not share the installer's `session_id`. The local shared publishes carried `session_id: 0`, so each replica minted its own id. An Update under a replica's id would have two effects:
- **the peer adopts a flipped id**, which breaks #5212 correlation;
- **it defeats the #9412 sender memo.** The memo is keyed by (tuple, SessionID) and drops its record when a different id arrives. The next sweep row, which carries the installer's id because the mirror row is written only on install, would then resend class 0.

## The change

| Where | Change |
|---|---|
| `poll_descriptor` transit ForwardFlow publish, `poll_descriptor` missing-neighbor seed publish, `promote.rs` republish | stamp the installer's stable id (`session_id_for(key)`), so replicas **adopt** it |
| `emit_close_state_update` | a `WorkerLocalImport` replica announces, but only when `session_id_carried_from_another_worker` holds: a non-zero id whose high 16 bits differ from this table's own namespace |
| unchanged, on purpose | peer-import replicas (`SyncImport`) still never announce; the local-delivery helper's 0 feeds only the BPF session map; reverse companions stay 0 by design |

**Bounds kept.**
- Several workers may announce the same class; the memo is monotone per (tuple, id).
- TIME_WAIT needs both FIN bits on ONE worker's entry. A flow split across workers announces CLOSING, which shares TIME_WAIT's 30 s default window.

## Tests

| Cell | At base | After |
|---|---|---|
| `a_close_seen_only_by_a_local_replica_is_announced_with_the_installer_id_9582`: server RST on a replica pair emits one class-3 Update with the installer's id; fixtures check the replica carries the id and records class 3 itself | **RED** (`[]`) | green |
| `a_peer_import_replica_still_announces_nothing_9582` (control) | green | green |
| `a_replica_holding_a_locally_minted_id_stays_silent_9582` (guard) | green | green |
| `only_a_non_zero_id_from_another_namespace_counts_as_carried_9582`: the guard's three branches | — | green |
| `txn_transit_install_publishes_the_installer_session_id_9582`: through the real descriptor | — | green |
| `poll_descriptor_missing_neighbor_seed_publishes_its_session_id_9582` | — | green |
| `promote_republishes_the_session_id_for_replicas_to_adopt_9582`: shared entry **and** queued replica | — | green |

## PR #9612 — userspace-dp: refuse steered WireGuard transit arriving while degraded [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-10)

Branch: `fix/9594-wg-degraded-kernel-path`

## Summary

While the userspace dataplane is **degraded**, the XDP shim passes local-destination traffic to the kernel in every degraded arm: ctrl disabled at helper start, during an RG transition or a reth link cycle; binding missing or not ready; heartbeat missing or stale. All of those checks run before both WireGuard arms, so a transport record for the **steered** listen port reaches that port's control thread through the kernel.

#9521's refusal does not cover it: that decision is chosen at spawn from the listen port alone, and it lets the steered port through on purpose (#8274's uncovered-ingress residual). The thread wrote the plaintext to the wgN TUN, so **inner transit rode the kernel's open forward hook with no zone policy**, during exactly the windows in which the shim drops every other transit packet.

The steered port's thread now applies the shim's own degraded posture to the decapsulated packet, when and only when the record arrived on an ingress the shim adjudicates:

| Ingress (from `IP_PKTINFO`) | Inner addressed to the firewall | Inner transit |
|---|---|---|
| In the shim's `userspace_ingress_ifaces` (a healthy shim would have claimed it, so the dataplane is degraded) | delivered | **dropped**, counted `rx_degraded_transit_drops` |
| Configured interface the shim does not adjudicate (#8274's residual) | delivered | delivered, unchanged |
| Cannot be placed | delivered | dropped (fail closed) |

Locality is the shim's own `is_local_destination`: `userspace_local_v4/v6` minus interface NAT, from the pinned maps Go fills (VRRP VIPs included).

The design and the rejected alternatives were posted on the issue before code: https://github.com/psaab/xpf/issues/9594#issuecomment-5625712795

**The interface-mode SNAT listener is unaffected by construction.** In degraded mode the shim drops it (it is not local), and on the healthy path the worker decapsulates it without ever reaching a control thread.

**The operator is told.** There is a `degraded-transit` receive-drop reason in `show security wireguard detail`, `reason="degraded_transit"` on `xpf_userspace_wg_transport_drops_total`, and the #5618 commit advisory now says degraded-window transit is refused.

Closes #9594

## What changed

- `wg_control/kernel_path.rs` (new): the disposition, ingress classification and locality rule as pure functions, plus the production pinned-map view and a per-tunnel test seam.
- `wg_control/sock.rs`: sets `IP_PKTINFO` / `IPV6_RECVPKTINFO` and parses the cmsg into `WgRecv.ingress_ifindex`. The option is set inside the control loop, so every path that runs the loop exercises it.
- `wg_control/dispatch.rs`: the posture gate, right after #9521's unsteered check.
- `wg_control/mod.rs`, `tunnel_supervision.rs`: the thread receives `ha.runtime_reader()`, and `wg_control_loop` builds the production view. The viewless loop exists only under `cfg(test)`.
- Counter `rx_degraded_transit_drops`, carried through `WgCounters`, the status wire, the Go status field, the `show` reason row and receive total, and the Prometheus reason label.
- The #5618 advisory, `compiler_prewalk.go` and renderer comments; the gaps doc, the interop doc, the coordinator README and the #7167 adjudication note.

## Acceptance

| Check | Control | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `steered_port_kernel_transport_gets_the_degraded_posture_on_covered_ingress_9594` (real loop, IPv4 and IPv6) | uncovered transit delivered; covered host-inbound delivered; the posture was asked about the real loopback ifindex from the pktinfo cmsg | covered transit dropped and counted; unplaceable transit dropped |
| `unsteered_port_is_refused_before_the_degraded_posture_is_consulted_9594` | — | #9521 counts it; the posture is never asked |
| `wg_steered_endpoint_refuses_degraded_transit_end_to_end_9594` (real spawn path, production view) | the same thread delivers the record once it is addressed to the firewall | transit refused and counted |
| `shim_maps_view_places_configured_uncovered_ingress_9594` | a real snapshot's runtime state | covered / uncovered / unplaceable placed correctly |
| `bind_wg_socket_requests_pktinfo_before_any_datagram_9594` | — | the production socket requests pktinfo before the loop runs, so no record is misread as unplaceable at thread spawn |
| Unit cells: disposition, classification, NAT-excluding locality, native-endian v4 key | — | pass |

## PR #9613 — config: refuse unknown app statements that drop a match constraint [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-10)

Branch: `fix/9595-unknown-app-statement`

Closes #9595

## Summary

A misspelled leaf in an application body, such as `destination-poort 22` on `protocol tcp`, is recorded as an unrecognized statement. Strict commit rejects it. On the tolerant path (Store.Load, HA SyncApply, upgrade) it was only a warning, and the application installed as tcp-any, so a policy meant to permit SSH permitted all TCP.

#6524 decided that a stray statement must not disarm an otherwise well-formed application. That decision stands, and `TestStrayStatementDoesNotDisarmSiblingLeaves` stays green. The line is drawn by structure, not keyword similarity. An unrecognized statement is refused in two cases:
- The application is otherwise protocol-wide on a dimension its protocol has (tcp/udp with no port, icmp/icmpv6 with no icmp-type) AND the unrecognized run carries a constraint-shaped token: a port spec (named ports included), a decimal integer or range, or a Junos ICMP type name.
- An application-set's unrecognized member statement names a real application or application-set.

The refusal reaches the helper through the existing #9525 channel: the #3261 `__unsupported__` sentinel and a whole-snapshot refusal, reported by `PolicyContentRejectionReasons` and `show security match-policies`.

Since #9611 (the #9588 pre-flight consults the same refusal mirror), `commit confirmed` also refuses a rollback target carrying this class, with no further edit.

Measured limits (see `docs/log/9595.md`):
- **Left installed:** a constraint lost BESIDE a retained one (`destination-port 80; source-poort 1024`). Structurally it is identical to a numeric stray beside a retained port. That decision is #9603.
- **Refused (deliberate over-reach):** a numeric or named-port stray on a protocol-wide application (`bogus 8080`). Structurally it is identical to a lost port, so it fails closed.

## Channel and plane

Go plane. `CompileConfigLenient` records the unrecognized run (`UnknownDirectTokens`, `UnknownMemberValues`). `config.ApplicationReferenceMatchDrops` feeds `expandUserspacePolicyApplications`, which emits the sentinel.

## Validation

- Cells in pkg/config (refused rows in every parser shape, armed rows with #6524's shape first, the pinned over-reach, token recording, the shape authority), pkg/dataplane/userspace (wire sentinel and mirror reason; #6524 wire unchanged) and pkg/policymatch (verdicts).
- Go mutation matrix: 22 mutants plus control, scored on `go test -json` Action=="fail" against each cell's named targets (a mutation not applied, a build failure, a timeout or no target collected scores VOID). Control 10/10 passed. The first run KILLED 20; two SURVIVED, the subtree-keys and bracket-tail recording arms. A probe found the parser shapes that reach them (`destination-poort { 22; }` and `protocol tcp 22;`), rows were added, and a follow-up KILLED both. Final: 22/22 KILLED, 0 SURVIVED, 0 VOID.
- Before the matrix, each planned mutant was checked against the cells. That added five rows, and one exposed a real miss: a misspelled keyword with a NAMED ICMP type (`icmp-typ echo-request`) installed as icmp-any. The shape now accepts the compiler's ICMP type-name tables.
- Rebased twice, onto fa1843126 and then 81efb7aad, because master changed `docs/userspace-dataplane-gaps.md` in other sections both times. `git range-diff` shows the patch unchanged each time, and no mutated file changed on master, so the matrix stands. After the second rebase, the suites that read that doc and the #9595 cells were re-run (the Rust snat_contract_doc_guard (1 passed) and forwarding_build tests (179 passed, 0 failed); Go doc readers ok; 41 cells, 0 failures).
- `make test` at b12435f28 (rebased onto fa1843126): 77 Go packages ok, 0 FAIL; Rust 5801 passed, 0 failed.

The first parent is verified after merging.

## PR #9614 — cluster: fence the readiness barrier when the sync stream changes connection [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-10)

Branch: `fix/9508-barrier-connection-causal`

Closes #9508

## What was wrong

Session-sync demotion readiness (`WaitForPeerBarrier`) claims the peer processed every delta queued before the barrier. A BarrierAck proves that only for the connection the barrier travelled on, and `barrierAckSeq` is global. `sendLoop` writes each message on whichever fabric connection is active when it is dequeued, so the ordered stream moves between connections in two ways:
- **a partial drop**: fab0 is lost and fab1 remains;
- **no fault at all**: a preferred fab0 connects while fab1 carries the stream.

Frames written on the old connection can still be unprocessed, or be lost with it, while a barrier is ACKed on the new one. Demotion prep then admits a demotion that loses those sessions. Both routes were RED at base on a harness whose connection accepts writes at once, as a TCP socket does. `net.Pipe` cannot model "written but not yet processed".

## The change: a barrier fence (`pkg/cluster/sync_barrier_fence_9508.go`)

- **Arming.** The first ordered-stream write (a `sendLoop` message or a BulkStart) on a different connection bumps a fence epoch under `writeMu`, **before** it writes. No ACK for a frame on the new connection can be observed without the bump.
- **Refusal.** `WaitForPeerBarrier` snapshots the epoch before checking it. It fails a barrier that was pending across a bump, and refuses every barrier while the fence is armed. The daemon already wraps that as `demotion peer barrier failed`, a `RetryablePreFailoverError`.
- **Recovery.** A move releases the pending barrier waiters and starts one single-flight re-prime; every refused barrier re-kicks it. The daemon cannot own this: it restarts its own prime-retry loop after a failed barrier only for an unprimed peer, and a primed peer is the normal case.
- **Discharge.** Only the ACK of a bulk that captured the epoch **before reading its session source** clears the fence.
  - `doBulkSync` captures before `BulkSnapshotSource`.
  - The store walk reads during the window, so it captures at BulkStart.
  - A caller-read snapshot captures nothing.
  - The capture is stored after `pendingBulkAckEpoch` and loaded before it, so an ACK never pairs one bulk's epoch with a newer bulk's capture.

No wire change.

**Not claimed:** a frame from a superseded connection that is still up can reach the peer after the re-prime and be applied after it. That ordering exists without the fence and is unchanged; the docs say so.

## Tests (`pkg/cluster/barrier_connection_causal_9508_test.go`)

| Cell | At base | After |
|---|---|---|
| route 1: a delta lost with a dropped fabric does not let a barrier pass | **RED** | green |
| route 2: a preference flip with no drop does not let a barrier pass | **RED** | green |
| control: single fabric completes | green | green |
| control: dual fabric with no move completes | green | green |
| recovery: a barrier completes again once the fence re-prime is ACKed | n/a | green |
| recovery through the store walk | n/a | green |
| capture order: a bulk whose snapshot predates the move keeps the fence | n/a | green |
| ordering: the move is recorded before the barrier write (ACK delivered inside `Write`, write held until the waiter decides) | n/a | green |
| release: a barrier pending across a move fails promptly with the fence error | n/a | green |

All nine pass three times under `-race`. `pkg/cluster` (`go test -json`): 1284 started, 0 failed. The pkg/daemon barrier, demotion and readiness cells pass.

## Validation

**Mutation matrix** (`scripts/mutate-9508.py`, Go, the whole `pkg/cluster` package per run, scored by test name, every run bounded): **12 of 12 KILLED**, 0 VOID.

| Mutant | Killed by |
|---|---|
| F1 a move is never recorded | both route cells, ordering, release, capture order |
| F2 the move is recorded after the write | ordering |
| F3 a barrier pending across a move is not failed | ordering, release |

## PR #9616 — userspace-dp: decline host-bound sessions in the #8356 re-derivation [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-10)

Branch: `fix/9563-host-bound-revalidation-decline`

## Summary

`revalidate_zone_policy_on_session_hit` re-derived ZONE POLICY for every forward session hit, `LocalDelivery` included. Every local-delivery resolution sets `egress_ifindex` to the LOCAL interface. For a lan host's SSH to the firewall's own lan address it therefore asked `lan -> lan`, a pair that host-inbound admission never consulted. Install stamps generation 0, so the first hit always re-derives: the default policy denied it and the owner's own first ACK revoked the session.

## PR #9621 — userspace-dp: wait for a joined neigh-monitor to exit before #6637 gates [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-10)

Branch: `fix/9556-neigh-monitor-reap-lag`

## Summary

The two #6637 neigh-monitor leak gates took their starting count with a single instant read of `/proc/self/task` and asserted it was zero. A monitor that the previous test had joined correctly can still be listed there for milliseconds after `join()` returns, because the kernel removes an exiting task only after it has woken the joiner. A serial `make test-rust` therefore reported `before=1` with no leak and no unlocked spawner.

A standalone probe spawned, joined and counted a thread named `neigh-monitor`:

| load | joins | still listed after `join()` | max linger |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| machine as-is (load 9.1) | 5000 | 43 | 14.3 ms |
| one busy loop per core | 5000 | 394 | 34.5 ms |

## Change

- Both preconditions now use `await_neigh_monitor_count(0)`, the same bounded wait their `during` and `after` reads already use. A real leak, or a spawner that skipped the serial lock, is still listed when the 5 s bound ends and still fails. The message now says the thread outlived the wait.
- **Two control cells bind the call sites.** Each is named to run immediately before one gate under `--test-threads=1`. It takes the serial lock, starts a stand-in thread named `neigh-monitor`, and releases the lock with the stand-in still listed for about a second: the reap window stretched until it is deterministic. A gate that samples its starting count instantly then fails every time; a gate that waits passes. A load-pair run of the real spawner and the gate reproduced the original failure 1 time in 200 at base and 0 in 200 at head. That is too rare to tell them apart, so the control cells, not the load-pair, bind the fix.
- The await helper and the serial-lock doc in `neighbor_manager.rs` now record the exit-side race beside the start-side one.
- The #6637 rule that every spawner stops and joins its monitor still holds: the thread had been joined, and only its `/proc` entry remained.

## Validation

- **Controls**: On `4ca7ac6e0`, under `--test-threads=1`, each lingering-monitor control ran immediately before its gate, and all four cells passed. A load-pair of the real spawner and the gate failed 1 time in 200 at base (`before=1`) and 0 in 200 at head: the mechanism is real, but too rare to separate them, which is why the control cells bind the fix.
- **Mutation**: 5 of 5 KILLED on `4ca7ac6e0`, none void, each scored by the failing test's name against its own target (table in `docs/log/9556.md`). P1 (`stop_inner` no longer joins the monitor), P2 (bringup never spawns it) and P3 (the guard's `Drop` no longer stops) are the gates' own kills, and they still hold with the bounded wait. C1 and C2 revert a gate's starting count to an instant sample. Each is killed by its own gate as the only failure, because the control cell before it leaves a monitor listed.
- **`make test`, both legs**: exit 0 on `4ca7ac6e0` (`origin/master` `81efb7aad` plus this commit). Go: 77 packages ok, no FAIL. Rust: 5,813 passed, 0 failed, across all 11 test binaries. Lands via merge commit with no further rebase: the `origin/master` delta since the tested base `81efb7aad` shares no files with this change, and whenever master has moved past that base the merged tree must pass `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` (nothing beyond master's own diagnostics) and `cargo check --tests --benches` in `userspace-dp` before the merge.

Closes #9556

## Summary

- **Adjudicates every multi-site elision admission at its site (#8921 item 2).** `compactNormalizeInScope` is keyed on (container keyword, head), so an admission is live wherever a container of that keyword declares that head. `multisite_adjudication_8921_test.go` checks each of the 531 recorded (pair, site) cells: normalizing `C <id> H <v>;` must build exactly the tree the parser builds for `C <id> { H <v>; }`. It compares every `Node` field except source position; the braced tree is taken as parsed and must be a fixed point of the pass. Each cell has a negative control, and the whole set is cross-checked against the compiled #2419 census (393 equivalent, 0 divergent).
- **Records the item 1 decision: the predicate stays keyword-keyed** (`docs/config-schema.md`). The pair only decides whether the fold fires; identity length and the head's statement come from the schema node at the site, and 58 of the 202 pairs are multi-site only through one `schemaNode` reachable by two paths. Parent qualification is the tool for a pair that must be admitted at one site and refused at another. The docs say so, along with what the #8690 rejection-vs-acceptance arm can and cannot see.
- **Fixes the fold dropping authored-quote and bracket provenance.** The fold and `splitBracedPackedChildren8886` moved `Keys` without `KeysQuoted`/`KeysBracketed`, so the #9027 gate refused elided `group g1 export A "export";` and `api-auth api-key AAA "api-key";` while their braced spellings committed. Both masks now move in lockstep with the keys.
- **Fixes commit-check ordering.** `schemaValidateExpandedTreeForNode` expanded groups on the tree as authored. A packed group body, or a packed inline neighbor beside an `inactive:` sibling, failed to merge with its braced counterpart and was refused, while the compiler accepted it. It now runs strip -> normalize -> expand, as the compiler does, and passes that tree as the definitions source.

## PR #9647 — ipsec/daemon: attribute IPsec re-initiation from the loaded generation (#9511) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9511-ipsec-child-sa-rg-attribution`

## Summary

- HA IPsec SA sync advertises **child SA names** (`ipsec.ActiveConnectionNames`). The #9139 per-RG attribution looked every name up as a **VPN name**, so every VPN with `traffic-selector` entries (children named `<vpn>-<selector>`, none named `<vpn>`) fell to RG 0. On per-RG failover that caused both a blackhole (the node taking the VPN's RG **skipped** the tunnel) and a duplicate IKE SA (the node taking RG0 **initiated** it while the live peer held it).
- **No wire change.** The same name goes to `swanctl --initiate --child`, and publishing the VPN name would break that initiate for exactly these VPNs (#9075, GEMINI-050-072).
- `ipsec.SANameIndex` inverts the render per VPN. A name that two VPNs render is re-initiated only by a node that owns **every** candidate's RG; for candidates that span groups, RG0 must be declared.
- **Attribution follows the generation strongSwan actually LOADED**, not the promoted config. They differ after a failed IPsec render or reload, and a walk of the failed-apply scenarios against master showed that attributing from the promoted config was worse than master in one reachable state. `ipsec.Manager.ApplyNotifyLoaded` signals "loaded" right after promotion, **before** teardown. Both apply sites record the loaded config through `applyIPsecTracked`.

## Residual (not fixed here)

**Attribution can still be wrong in one state.** Before this xpfd process has loaded an IPsec generation, attribution is computed from the promoted config. After an xpfd restart where the boot IPsec apply fails, charon is still running the previous generation, so that config may not match what charon runs. That is the same answer master gives. Refusing to re-initiate was not adopted here. A clustered node's first IPsec apply completes before cluster comms start, so "nothing loaded yet" is reachable only after a FAILED first apply. Whether that failure can be routine (charon not ready at boot) and whether a failed apply is retried, so that a refusal would lift, are open questions. Tracked in #9641 (High), which prefers asking charon what it has actually loaded. `TestAttributionFallsBackToPromotedConfigBeforeFirstLoad9511` pins the current behaviour so that fixing #9641 has to update it on purpose.

## Test plan

- [x] `pkg/ipsec` cells: the index over every section the renderer emits, cross-VPN collisions, renderer-skipped and render-error VPNs, sanitised-name aliasing, IKE-only rows, and `ApplyNotifyLoaded` (silent on a failed reload, once on success, before teardown despite debt)
- [x] `pkg/daemon` cells: attribution table; both failover directions with RG0 declared; every-candidate and undeclared-RG0 rules; per-config cache (concurrent cold misses, stale-install guard); loaded-generation transitions (failed addition, failed deletion, RG move, absent name); held-open teardown with a concurrent reader; commit, lease-rebind and restart wiring through a real Manager; the pinned #9641 residual
- [x] Mutation matrices on each committed tree, scored by test name and message via `go test -json` (tables in `docs/log/9511.md`). Round 7 on fd67f56bb: 23/25 KILLED, 0 VOID, and 1 ESCAPE (M15, miss mutex removed: the cold-miss cell was too weak under load; strengthened to 120 VPNs and 10 cold starts)
- [x] M15 and F1 re-scored 3x on the final head 7a1cb6615: M15 3/3 KILLED, F1 3/3 KILLED
- [x] `make test` (Go + Rust) on the PR head 7a1cb6615: exit 0. Go 77 packages ok; Rust 5811 passed, 0 failed

The final head differs from fd67f56bb only in comment lines in production code, plus a strengthened test

It runs on a local merge of origin/master and this head, because master's delta since the tested base touches code the HA config exercises (userspace-dp forwarding, `pkg/configstore/store.go`). ## PR #9649 — daemon: pin policy-rematch on an added deny; correct the #9386 record [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9573-rematch-added-deny-record`

Closes #9573

## What

The #9386 ACCEPT record (`docs/log/9386.md`) names `security policies policy-rematch` at commit as a mitigation for the accepted fail-open, in which the #8356 re-derivation skips a type-constrained ICMP DENY. For a commit that ADDS the deny ahead of an unchanged permit, that is false. This PR corrects the sentence and pins the measured behaviour:

| mode | deny inserted before the permit | deny appended after |
|---|---|---|
| rematch off (default) | nothing swept | nothing swept |
| `policy-rematch` | nothing swept | nothing swept |
| `policy-rematch extensive` | the permit's old id swept, only because the insert shifted its positional `policy_id` | nothing swept |
| `extensive`, permit at `policy_id 0` | nothing swept (id-0 exclusion) | n/a |

There is no production change. `TestRematchAddedDenyTable9573` uses strict-compiled flat-set fixtures, preconditions that the insert really shifts ids, and a levelling control per mode. Whether `extensive`'s positional sweep is intended is still an open design question. The cells make any change to either behaviour deliberate.

## PR #9650 — cmd/xpfd: stop gating the #5286 wiring cell on a 50 ms wall clock [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9502-helper-probe-no-wallclock`

Closes #9502

## What

`TestBuildUpgradeSystem_WiresHelperProbe_5286` asserted two properties inside one `HelperHealthy(target, 50ms)` call: the production assembly consults the control-socket status seam, and it fails closed on an up-but-not-forwarding helper. `HelperHealthProbe` checks the remaining budget before the status query. Under load, 50 ms could pass before the first evaluation, so the seam was never called and the cell reported **"not wired"** about correct wiring. That cell sits in the `make test-go` gate every lane runs.

The fix splits the cell:
- **`WiresHelperProbe_5286`** now asserts wiring only: an armed+forwarding fake with a 10 s budget. A wired probe returns after one evaluation (0.00 s measured), and the message now says a missed query at this budget is the wiring, not latency.
- **`FailsClosedWhenNotForwarding_5286`** (new) keeps a 50 ms budget and asserts only an error, which is monotone under load, plus the not-forwarding cause when the query ran.
- **`WiringAbsorbsAStall_9502`** (new) stalls the unit-active fake 150 ms (3× the old budget) and still requires the status query to be consulted. This is the deterministic load control.
- **`ArmedForwardingTarget_Healthy`** moves off its 200 ms budget too.

**The issue's first option did not hold.** It said to just raise the budget, on the grounds that the fake returns instantly and a large budget would not slow the test. But a not-forwarding evaluation is not a definitive exit: the probe polls every 500 ms until the deadline. A multi-second budget would cost that whole budget on every run, which is why this takes the issue's second option and splits the cell.

## Validation

- **All four cells** pass at origin/master `a35c2133f`.
- **Old-budget control** (temporary test, not committed): the old 50 ms shape under the same 150 ms stall gives `statusCalled=false`, `last: <nil>`, deadline exceeded. That is exactly the false "not wired" state, so the stall cell is not vacuous.
- **Mutation matrix**, scored by test name and expected message:
  - M1 (wiring reverted to `upgrade.NewSystem`): KILLED by the wiring cell.
  - M2 (`Status: nil`): KILLED by the wiring cell.
  - M3 (gate ignores `forwarding_armed`): KILLED by the fail-closed cell.
  - 0 VOID.
- **`make test`:** see `docs/log/9502.md`.

No module docs change: the #5808 deadline property is pinned at the probe level in `pkg/upgrade`, which is unchanged.

## PR #9652 — userspace-dp: refuse a reused snapshot generation carrying new content (#9520) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9520-snapshot-content-digest`

## Summary

- The helper admitted an `apply_snapshot` that reused its installed `(generation, fib)` pair **without comparing content**. After a republish landed but its response was lost, the Go retry rebuilt its content and re-sent the same generation. A closing policy-schedule window installed that way left permits cached (flow cache, keyed on the pair) and stamped (session policy, keyed on the generation alone) under the open window **fresh**.
- Every `apply_snapshot` now carries `ConfigSnapshot.ContentDigest` (Go's `snapshotContentHash` of exactly what is sent). `requestApplySnapshotLocked` is the only send site and stamps it.
- The helper refuses, before any mutation, a reused generation whose digest differs or is empty, at any fib, with `SNAPSHOT_CONTENT_CONFLICT_PREFIX`. `update_fabrics` and `update_neighbors` clear the installed digest when they change enforced content.
- That refusal, and only that refusal, proves the helper holds the generation. So Go consumes it and republishes once on the next generation, and every caller commits the generation actually sent. #5134's "a failed apply does not burn a generation" still holds for every other failure, and no retry happens once `BeginControlShutdown` has latched.
- A failure other than an in-band refusal may have landed, so it marks the helper's content **unknown** until an apply succeeds. While it is marked, the route-overlay dedup and `syncSnapshotLocked`'s hash dedup and generation-only catch-up stand down. Otherwise a revert to the content Go last saw accepted is skipped while the lost response's content stays enforced.
- The idempotent #4036 retry (identical, non-empty digest) is still ACKed; `>=` was not tightened. Snapshot protocol 14 -> 15, because an old helper that ignores the digest keeps the defect.

## Design review

Hostile Codex plan review: `PLAN NO`. Hostile Codex code review: `MERGE NO`, blocking on Go bookkeeping skipping a publish after a lost response; that is now fixed (the unknown-outcome mark above). A confirmation review (`MERGE NO`) raised one more finding, traced in source and confirmed real: a timeout-but-landed apply on the Compile path is re-armed by the next status tick against the classifier plan it did not publish. It predates this PR, which neither introduces nor worsens it (the mark only stands the publish shortcuts down and never enables ctrl), and its fix is retry debt plus a ctrl latch in the #7468 arming path, so it is filed separately as #9642 (High). Every finding of both rounds has a written disposition in `docs/log/9520.md`; the one rejected code-review finding (persisting the neighbour-update digest clear to an observability-only state file) carries its reason. Plan-round summary:
- The empty-digest gap is closed.
- Partial updates now clear the installed digest.
- The retry is skipped during shutdown.
- Retry-failure rows are added, and the docs and wording are fixed.
- The any-fib scope is kept, with reasons: the same content at an advanced fib is still admitted, and the generation-only policy stamp makes different content there the same fail-open.

## Test plan

- [x] Rust `server/tests.rs`: `_9520` refusal cells (exact pair, advanced fib, no digest, after a partial update), positive controls, and the #5169 reuse and fib cells updated to carry digests
- [x] Go `apply_snapshot_identity_9520_test.go`: acceptance shape on the scheduler path, plus the overlay, worker-arm and deferred-sync paths; #5134 negative rows; shutdown skip; digest identity-freedom; one-send-site census; real-socket classification; Rust prefix agreement; structural Compile adopt pin
- [x] Go, code-review round: overlay revert after a lost response, sync shortcuts with and without one, only a success clearing the mark, a failed republish still failing closed, the ctrl generation after a republish
- [x] Mutation matrix, name-attributed, recorded in `docs/log/9520.md`
- [x] `make test`: exit 0 on `8534dcb81` (`origin/master` `6d930698c` plus this commit). Go: 77 packages ok, no FAIL. Rust: 5,821 passed, 0 failed, across all 11 test binaries. Lands via merge commit with no further rebase: the `origin/master` delta since the tested base `6d930698c` shares no files with this change, and whenever master has moved past that base the merged tree must pass `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` (nothing beyond master's own diagnostics) and `cargo check --tests --benches` in `userspace-dp` before the merge.
- [ ] Cluster smoke: not run. The change is control-plane admission and bookkeeping on paths the loss cluster does not fault-inject; a timeout-but-landed publish cannot be produced on demand there. The cells drive the real Go publish paths and the real Rust handler.

## Docs

`docs/flow-cache-simplification.md` (new #9520 section, stale Compile claim corrected), `docs/userspace-dataplane-architecture.md` (the hash doubles as content identity, and the #7468 in-band refusal wording is corrected), `userspace-dp/src/server/README.md`, and the v15 notes in `protocol.go` and `control.rs`.

## PR #9660 — fairness: make an rss-expectation INDETERMINATE on a truncated snapshot [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9369-rss-verdict-truncation`

Closes #9369

## What

`CoSFairnessRSSSummary.SourceRowsTruncated` was written on every summary and read by nothing. The coordinator keeps only the first 4096 sorted `(ifindex, queue, worker)` triples, so a resolved queue could be judged from a partial prefix of its per-worker distribution. That prefix flips the verdict in **both** directions. With the issue's witness, complete `[1,3,0,…]` versus truncated `[1,0,…]`:
- `cstruct-max:0.1` and `balanced` fail on the complete data, but the prefix falsely passes them.
- `max-worker-flow-share:0.8` passes on the complete data, but the prefix falsely fails it.

The exporter converted the result straight into `xpf_fairness_rss_skew_violation`, so a false pass read as a clean fairness board.

This PR:
- **Verdict.** On a truncated snapshot, every constrained expectation is now **INDETERMINATE**: `Pass=false`, `Indeterminate=true`, and a reason that says so. `any` still evaluates, and an unresolved interface still fails. This matches the throughput path, which already excludes truncated active-worker counts.
- **CLI.** The `show … fairness` table's `Pass` column becomes `Result` (`PASS` / `FAIL` / `INDETERMINATE`).
- **Prometheus.** A new `xpf_fairness_rss_expectation_indeterminate{ifindex,queue_id,kind}` gauge (0/1) is emitted for every resolved expectation, and the violation sample is **withheld** while indeterminate.
- **Scope of the flag.** The flag is snapshot-global, so fully retained queues are also held indeterminate. That is conservative and never wrong. Per-queue completeness is the stronger follow-on and needs the coordinator to publish per-queue truncation.
- **Docs.** `docs/fairness-regimes.md` and `docs/per-5-tuple/state.md` are updated.

`TestFormatFairnessRSS` pinned ordinary verdicts on a truncated snapshot. Those rows arrived verbatim in a pure code-motion commit (#1990), and its own warning says derived values are partial, so the cell now expects `INDETERMINATE`.

## PR #9662 — feeds: refuse whole-address-space entries; correct the RETH MAC doc [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9248-ungraded-findings`

Closes #9248

#9248 carried three findings from the #9075 validation that were never graded. Each was graded by tracing its consumer; the record is `docs/log/9248.md`.

## 1. A dynamic-address feed installed `0.0.0.0/0` / `::/0` — real, changed here

Feed prefixes are merged into the address sets userspace policy lowering matches (`policies_lower.go`, `policies_addrbook.go`) and the NAT/policy simulators, so one whole-space line in content this box does not author turned every policy on that dynamic address into "match anything": a permit failed open and a deny dropped everything.

`parseFeed` now refuses a line whose **canonical** prefix — the string that would be installed — is the whole IPv4 or IPv6 space. Testing the canonical form matters: `::ffff:0:0/96` renders as `0.0.0.0/0` and passed a mask-length check.

- A response that also carries usable prefixes counts and samples the refused line like a malformed one, so the installed feed reports `Degraded`.
- A response of only refused entries is a fetch failure whose error names them. The last-good set stays enforced under the feed's normal failure handling, including any hold-interval expiry, and `LastError` carries the reason.
- The boundary is an accidental whole-space line, not a hostile provider: `0.0.0.0/1` plus `128.0.0.0/1` covers the same space and still installs. Short real prefixes such as bogon `224.0.0.0/3` still install.

## 2. `shouldSyncAtBulkStart` treats a zone absent from the bulk snapshot as syncable — real, split out

An RG-unmapped zone is governed by RG 0 (the live `ShouldSyncZone` falls back to `IsLocalPrimary(0)`). On an RG 0 secondary its sessions are peer-owned, so the default keeps a stale session the authoritative bulk omitted. This is HA session-sync code that needs `make test-failover`, so it is tracked as #9655 and not changed in this PR.

## 3. `docs/reth-mac.md` described one shared MAC with a reserved byte 5 — doc defect, corrected here

`config.RethVirtualMAC` builds `02:bf:72:CC:RR:NN` with the node id in byte 5, and `cluster.RethMAC` explains why the MAC is per node. The doc now:

- says so, with per-node examples;
- says a failover changes the RETH MAC and that the takeover GARP / unsolicited-NA burst refreshes neighbour caches;
- gives the three-argument `RethMAC`;
- names the shared router identity correctly: `StableRethLinkLocal` builds `fe80::bf72:CC:RR`, and both the doc and a `pkg/cluster/reth.go` comment had written `fe80::bf:72:CC:RR`.

- [x] Mutation matrix on `1b7b0cb3b`, scored from `go test -json` by test name and expected message (the later amend is docs only):

## PR #9664 — configstore: refuse to persist what the same build's reader refuses (#9617) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9617-persist-size-gate`

Closes #9617

## Summary

A configstore writer could durably persist an artifact that the same build's reader refuses at the next load. The reader is `ReadBoundedFile` with the 16 MiB `MaxConfigSize`. Two reviewers each found one member of this class:

- **muse-spark-review-008 H4:** an accepted commit whose active DB exceeds the ceiling bricks the next boot.
- **muse-spark-review-009 CSA-R-CONFIGSTORE-002:** `commit confirmed` writes a `confirm.json` that restart refuses, so the rollback window is lost.

## Change

- **Write-side ceiling.** `writeTreeMarked` and `encodeConfirm` check the assembled bytes against the reader's exact ceiling (`checkPersistSize`, `ErrPersistExceedsReadCeiling`) before any durable write.
- **Commit-confirmed preflight.** `commitConfirmedLocked` encodes the rollback record before promoting the candidate, through the same `encodeConfirm` the write uses. The preflight record is sized so it is never smaller than the one later written:
  - the original rollback target for a nested re-arm;
  - the #8565 tombstone form (`resolved: true`), so a window that arms can also be resolved;
  - `widestConfirmDeadline`, a stand-in as long in JSON as any deadline. A clock-read deadline is not an upper bound, because its zone suffix grows from `Z` to `+hh:mm` across a DST change.

  Any encode failure refuses the commit with the candidate intact. The real deadline is still taken at the arm site, so the persisted deadline and the live timer describe one window.
- **Retry loop.** The persist retry loop does not re-serialize a tree the ceiling refused (`persistRefusedTree`), and releases it when a different tree is installed.

## Validation

- `go test ./pkg/configstore`, including the 12 `_9617` cells.
- `make test` on the rebased head: PASS on `cb315dad2` (Go and Rust suites, exit 0; tested base `98812e579`). Landing check against master `0bb7bef21`: the file intersection is empty, and the merged tree builds and vets.
- Mutation matrix every round, scored by test name and failure message. The final round killed 7 of 7: zone suffix `Z`, no fraction, a stand-in one byte narrower (each against both the width cell and the tombstone cell), and a clock-read deadline.
- Codex hostile review, rounds 1 through 5. Round 5 returned MERGE YES with no findings. AGY is infra-blocked (#9370).
- Landing: the file intersection with master was non-empty (`pkg/configstore/README.md`, `store.go`), so the branch was rebased onto master and re-tested.

## Docs

`pkg/configstore/README.md` covers the write-side ceiling, the commit-confirmed preflight and what is not gated (text rollback and rescue files). The session log is `docs/log/9617.md`.

## PR #9668 — networkd: keep interface names inside the managed directory [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9494-networkd-name-confinement`

Closes #9494

## What

`buildFabricBondModels` emitted the bond name raw (`bondName := ifName`) even though its own members use `config.LinuxIfName`. Bridge domains are named `"br-" + bd.Name`, and nothing validated the name. `networkd.Apply` joins the name into `filepath.Join(networkDir, "10-xpf-"+name+suffix)`, which Cleans the path. So a committed name with a `/../` component made xpfd (root) write a `.netdev`/`.network`/`.link` file **outside `/etc/systemd/network`**, while Apply returned nil. The stale-file sweep cannot see those files, so they persist. The issue measured this end to end: admission, then the builders, then the sink.

This PR closes the hole at all three layers, following the issue's fix direction:
- **Bond model:** it now uses `config.LinuxIfName(ifName)`, like its members.
- **Commit check:** a `ValidateBridgeDomainName` keyValidator on the `bridge-domains` wildcard rejects `/`, `\`, NUL and whitespace.
- **Defence in depth in `networkd.Apply`:** an empty name, or one carrying `/` or NUL, counts as a write failure. The Apply fails, and nothing is written for that name. This covers names that reach Apply without strict admission: a tolerant load, HA peer sync, a rollback slot, or day-0.

The `"br-" + bd.Name` sites are unchanged. With the gate plus the belt, no existing bridge is renamed.

**Blast radius of the new commit gate:** the shipped and test configs carry 8 `bridge-domains` lines, and none uses a separator. `pkg/config`, `pkg/networkd` and `pkg/dataplane` pass unfiltered.

## Validation

- **New tests:**
  - `networkd`: Apply writes **nothing** outside the managed directory (checked with a filesystem walk), and a `fab0` control is byte-identical to a clean run.
  - `config`: the commit check rejects traversal and backslash names, while `bd0` commits.
  - `dataplane`: the bond carries the Linux interface name, and every member's `BondMaster` matches it.
- **Mutation matrix:** 5 of 5 KILLED by the target test with its expected message, 0 VOID. The mutants were: raw bond name, belt bypassed, keyValidator removed, validator accepts `/`, belt accepts `/`.
- **`make test`:** see `docs/log/9494.md`.

No module docs describe networkd file naming or bridge-domain name syntax; the validator's doc comment states the contract.

## PR #9670 — userspace-dp: retry resource accept errors instead of exiting the helper [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9172-v031-accept`

## Summary

- **Defect (#9172, finding V031).**
  - The control-socket accept loop turned every non-`WouldBlock` accept error into `Err`, and `main` turns that into `exit(1)`.
  - Under descriptor or memory pressure, the errors that reach that arm say nothing is wrong with the listener: `EMFILE`/`ENFILE` when no descriptor can be allocated, `ENOBUFS`/`ENOMEM` when the socket cannot be.
  - Transient pressure therefore became a supervisor crash-loop, with up to 60 s of no forwarding per cycle.
  - The session-socket thread had the opposite defect: it `continue`d with no sleep and spun a core on a persistent `EMFILE`.
- **Fix.** Both loops decide through `accept_step`.
  - Resource errors retry on a backoff that doubles from 50 ms to a 1 s ceiling and resets on the next successful accept.
  - Each episode writes one journal line when it starts and one when it ends; a quiet gap over 5 s starts a new episode.
  - Any other error keeps the control loop's previous behaviour: it fails, and the supervisor restarts the helper.
  - The session loop retries other errors and says once that it is not exiting. errno does not reveal where an error came from, and exiting would take forwarding down with the HA session socket.
- **Deliberately no exit-on-time bound.** A bound on "no successful accept" cannot tell a descriptor leak from fluctuating pressure. Measured at `RLIMIT_NOFILE=256`, an empty listener returns `EMFILE` at the limit and `EAGAIN` once one descriptor frees, with no accept in between. Recovering a helper wedged by a genuine leak is #9651.
- **Correction on record.** An earlier revision of `docs/log/9172-v031.md` recorded V031 as refuted, but that probe covered only a pending connection. The log carries the correction.
- **Split.** `lifecycle.rs` crossed the 1500-LOC modularity floor that `TestTouchedFileCrossedModularityThreshold` enforces. The new test module therefore lives verbatim in `server/lifecycle_accept_step_tests_9172.rs`, declared with `#[path]`, so the module path and test names are unchanged.
- **Docs.** `userspace-dp/src/server/README.md`.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test accept_step_tests_9172`: 8 passed on the split commit, and again on the rebased commit.
- [x] Rust mutation matrix on the pre-split commit, scored by test name and panic message:
  - baseline: 8/8 pass;
  - 7/7 mutants killed: EMFILE not transient; the session loop passing `retry_unclassified=false`; `retry_unclassified` ignored; a log line per failure; no quiet-gap reset; no reset on success; a retry bound reintroduced.
  - Re-verified on the split commit with a spot check: baseline green, and the wiring-scan and gap-reset mutants killed.
- [x] `make test` (Go + Rust) on the rebased commit `0286b1e33`, rebased onto `origin/master` `9e63a98e3`: `MAKE-EXIT=0`, no failing test, no disk-full lines. The first landing attempt stopped on a file overlap with master in `userspace-dp/src/server/README.md` (distant hunks), so the branch was rebased and every check below re-run on it. The earlier run, on the pre-split commit, failed only `TestTouchedFileCrossedModularityThreshold`, which the split answers.
- [x] Hostile Codex review: MERGE YES.
- [x] Landing check against `origin/master` `4db3056d6` immediately before merging: no file overlap with master's delta since the tested base, and the merged tree passes `go build ./...`, `cargo check` and no new `go vet ./...` lines.

Refs #9172, #9651
