## PR #9750 — config: keep a flat apply statement's group names at wildcard name slots [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9685-apply-groups-at-wildcard-slots`

## Summary

A flat `set routing-instances apply-groups g1` was silently lost. At a schema node with a wildcard name slot, the tree walkers took `apply-groups` as an instance name, so SetPath stored `Keys=["apply-groups"]` with a child `["g1"]`. Group expansion and the #9422 exclusion read names from the statement's own `Keys[1:]`, found none, and dropped the node. The inheritance, or the exclusion, did not happen on a strict-clean commit, while the hierarchical spelling worked.

A census of `setSchema` finds 12 wildcard slots. On master, 18 of the 24 flat apply statements placed at them lost their name. The slots include `routing-instances`, `interfaces`, `bridge-domains`, `routing-options rib-groups`, `security zones security-zone <z> interfaces`, and seven more.

`schemaChildFor` is now the single lookup. It returns a declared child first; at a wildcard slot it returns `applyStatementSchema` for `apply-groups` / `apply-groups-except` / `apply-macro`, and the wildcard otherwise. Every walker that resolves a node's keyword uses it:
- SetPath, delete and deactivate;
- the compact normalizer;
- `resolveSchemaChild`, which the #8992 elided-delete guard calls. Without this, that guard refused `delete routing-instances apply-groups g1` as a packed run.

The multi-value absorber keeps trailing group names on the statement rather than treating them as sibling instances, so `[ g1 g2 ]` stays one statement. A declared child still wins, so the top-level `apply-groups` declaration is untouched.

**Two #9657 cells had pinned the defect.** `TestTableIDGateHonoursAnExcludedGroup_9657` asserted it deliberately and named this issue. `TestApplyStatementSpellingsStillCommit_9657` expected a keyword-name warning that only the defective one-key flat shape produced; the same test already asserts the two-key statement is never warned. Both now assert the fixed behaviour. A braced one-key stanza keeps the warning bound, and the #9657 production comment is updated. Details in `docs/log/9685.md`.

Not changed: CLI completion still offers only the wildcard placeholder at these slots.

## PR #9753 — frr/config: redistribute a bare BGP export in every family it carries [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9667-redistribute-per-family`

## Summary

A bare-token `protocols bgp export` was written only under `router bgp`, and that node's FRR redistribute grammar (BGP_NODE, `FRR_IP_REDIST_STR_BGPD`) is IPv4-only. So `export static` redistributed IPv4 statics only, and an IPv6-only BGP deployment using the shorthand advertised nothing it originated. The issue's other premise was partly stale; measured on the strict channel at `580d959e0` and posted on the issue:
- `protocols bgp export ospf6|ripng` and `protocols ospf export ospf6` are refused, with the wrong reason ("not a known protocol"). `ospf6` and `ripng` are known FRR keywords; the strict token set simply lacked them.
- `protocols ospf3 export ospf` commits clean and renders nothing.

**Decision** (posted on the issue): both options, each where it fits.

- **BGP renders each family where its grammar lives.** IPv4-capable sources render under `router bgp`, as before. IPv6-capable sources render under `address-family ipv6 unicast` through `resolveBGPIPv6Redistribute`. That block is opened whenever an IPv6 redistribute line exists, with or without an IPv6 neighbor, and joins the neighbor block when one exists. `export static` renders in both families; `export ospf6` renders in IPv6 only.
- **Single-family routers refuse a cross-family bare token at strict commit.** `protocols ospf export ospf6` and `protocols ospf3 export ospf` are refused with the family named; the tolerant path downgrades to a warning; the #9510 render drop stays as the backstop. A policy-statement's `from protocol` is still filtered per term at render, because the same policy is valid under another router.
- **One family table.** `config.RedistributionSourceFamilies` replaces the #9510 source table in `pkg/frr` and the commit gate's own shorter token list, so the gate and the renderer cannot disagree. The gate now admits the shared keyword domain, so `protocols ospf3 export ripng` is no longer refused, and it still requires the exact lower-case spelling.

## Validation

- New cells:
  - `TestBGPBareTokenRedistributesEachFamily_9667`: static, ospf, ospf6, direct and bgp land in the right family; no `redistribute bgp` in either;
  - an IPv4-only control that opens no IPv6 block;

## PR #9756 — configstore/daemon: pre-flight a recovered commit-confirmed target [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9615-recovered-confirm-preflight`

Closes #9615

## Problem

`Store.Load` re-arms a `commit confirmed` window that was still live at restart (#4577). That path never runs the #6707/#9588 rollback-target pre-flight. The pre-flight has exactly one production caller: the arm-time gate in `commitConfirmedAndApply`. When the timer fired, `executeConfirmedRollback` promoted the target and applied it without conditions, on the premise "validated at commit-confirmed time". For a recovered window that premise is false in two ways:

- the box may have upgraded inside the window, and the new build's refusal classes can cover the old config;
- a target that binds a dynamic-address feed has no installed snapshot right after boot, and #5645 fails that closed.

## Fix

Refusing to re-arm would make the unconfirmed commit permanent. So the window always stays armed and the pre-flight runs in two places.

**At boot:** `checkRecoveredConfirmTarget`, in a new startup phase `recovered-confirm-preflight` after manager-init so the feed manager exists. If the recovered target fails, the daemon raises an alarm, recorded three ways:
- a slog error naming the reasons and the deadline;
- a journal entry (`confirm_rollback_target_refused`);
- the local CLI's pending-window `[ALARM: …]` line (`Store.ConfirmAlarm`).

The operator can confirm or re-commit before the deadline.

**When the timer fires:** `confirmRollbackTargetHandledAtFire`, called before `PromoteRollback`, so nothing has been promoted yet:
- **Feed-only refusal** (it disappears once every binding resolves): deferred. `Store.DeferConfirmTimer` re-arms the same generation every 5 s, at most 24 times.
- **Any other refusal, or a feed still unready at the cap:** the store is promoted to the target and persisted as committed, as #6538 does. The daemon enters the bootstrap/lifeline safe state instead of applying a target the dataplane refuses.
- **Appliable target:** unchanged.

Store additions:
- `PendingRollbackTarget`, `DeferConfirmTimer`, `RecoveredConfirmWindow`, `NoteConfirmTargetAlarm`, `ConfirmAlarm`.
- Window fields: deadline, recovered mark and alarm text. They are set at arm (recovered=false) and at Load (recovered=true), and cleared by cancel and `PromoteRollback`.

## Validation

- **New cells** (8, in `pkg/daemon/confirm_rollback_preflight_9615_test.go`):
  - a healthy target is applied once;
  - a refused target is not applied, the store reverts and bootstrap is entered;
  - a feed-only target is deferred for 24 attempts without promoting, then takes the safe state;
  - a recovered refused target raises the alarm (reason plus deadline) and stays armed;
  - a recovered healthy target raises no alarm;
  - an in-process window, including one re-armed over a recovered window, is not reported as recovered;
  - the deferred timer fires the same generation, and a stale generation is refused;
  - AST wiring: the phase follows manager-init and calls the check; the fire path checks before `PromoteRollback`.
- **Suites:** `go test ./pkg/daemon/ ./pkg/configstore/ ./pkg/cli/`: 4559 passed, 0 failed.
- **Static checks:** gofmt and go vet clean; refactoraudit modularity gate green.
- **Mutation matrix:** 12/12 killed, scored by test name (table in `docs/log/9615.md`). The mutants: fire-time call removed; feed-only classification forced false; retry cap removed; phase body emptied; alarm not recorded; healthy boot target alarms; healthy fire target swallowed; Load not marking recovered; in-process window reported recovered; deferred timer never fires; deferral ignores generation; arm keeps the recovered mark.

## Not changed

- The remote CLI's `ConfirmPending` flag does not carry the alarm text; the local CLI, journal and syslog do.
- The refused-target safe state follows the existing nil-target branch. That branch does not re-sync the rolled-back config to a cluster peer.

Docs: `pkg/daemon/README.md` (new subsection under commit-confirmed); log `docs/log/9615.md`.

## PR #9759 — config: normalize a brace-elided routing instance before expansion and validation [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9620-elided-instance-normalize`

Refs #9620 (member H7). Refs #9736.

#9620 stays open after this PR: its remaining members land in two more PRs. #9736 also stays open. This PR makes the elided and braced spellings reach the same verdict on it, but both still accept a trailing token after a value statement (see Residuals).

## Defect

A brace-elided routing instance packs its statements onto the node whose first key is the instance NAME. The #8662 scoped fold cannot name an instance (#8787), so `compileRoutingInstances` read the Keys run itself (#8787, #9055). That ran **after group expansion and after `SchemaValidate`**, so the elided body was compiled from a node neither of them had seen.

Measured through `configstore.CheckText`, the strict commit gate, at `0e950bd5b`:

| Instance body | Commit gate result | Braced spelling |
|---|---|---|
| `ri1 routing-options static route 10.9.0.0/16 next-hop 10.0.0.2;` | accepted, 0 static routes | 1 route |
| `ri1 instance-type virtual-router protocols bgp group G peer-as 65001 neighbor 10.0.0.1;` | accepted, `BGP=nil` | neighbor compiled |
| `ri2 instance-type virtual-router protocols ospf area 0.0.0.0 interface ge-0/0/1.0;` | accepted, `Interfaces=[ge-0/0/1.0]` (bound into the VRF), `OSPF=nil` | OSPF, no instance interface |
| `ri1 instance-type virtual-router protocols bgp group G description foo;` | accepted, instance `Description="foo"` | empty description |
| `ri1 protocols { bgp { group G { peer-as 65001; hold-time 1; neighbor 10.0.0.1; } } }` | **accepted, `HoldTime=1`** | refused: FRR rejects the timers line |
| `ri1 routing-options { static { route 10.9.0.0/16 { apply-groups G; } } }` | **route with no next-hop** | next-hop inherited from G |

## Change

- `normalizeElidedRoutingInstance9620` (new) rewrites a brace-elided routing instance into the braced shape the parser builds for the same statements. `normalizeCompactNodes` calls it for `routing-instances` children, so it runs wherever the #8662 normalizer runs: both compile cores, before group expansion, and the `SchemaValidate` walk. The run is split by the instance schema:
  - a keyword with args takes its values;
  - an apply statement (`apply-groups`, `apply-groups-except`, `apply-macro`) ends the value statement before it and stands alone, so group expansion sees it. `apply-macro` also owns the rest of the run and its braced body, which are its arguments;
  - quotes and brackets never move a boundary, because HA sync, rollback files and `show configuration` render the tree without them;
  - a non-container keyword takes its values and then every token up to the next declared keyword, as the one-line braced statement would, so `vrf-target export target:x` stays one statement;
  - a container keyword, or an undeclared first keyword, takes the rest plus the braced body;
  - a braced body after a value keyword stays instance statements;
  - apply statements are skipped.
- `compileRoutingInstances` no longer reads the Keys run. Removed: the #8787 keyword loop, the #9055 re-dispatch, and the `isRoutingInstanceKeyword8787` / `routingInstanceKeywordOwnsBody9055` predicates, along with the #9055 predicate test. The #9323 anti-drift test and its comments now point at the schema, which is the single keyword set.
- docs/config-schema.md gains the section "Brace-elided routing instances". The log is docs/log/9620.md.

## Validation

- `pkg/config/routing_instance_elided_normalize_9620_test.go`: 22 spellings, including inline apply statements, `apply-macro` with a braced body and with keyword-spelled arguments, and a bracketed interface list. Each elided spelling and its braced spelling normalize to one tree (positions aside, quote and bracket masks included), at top level and inside `groups`. Apply statements under `routing-instances` are untouched. A separate test pins that quotes and brackets do not move a boundary: `interface [ ge-0/0/0.0 protocols ]` splits exactly like its unbracketed text. The compiled witness fields are checked on both spellings, strict and lenient.
- `pkg/configstore/routing_instance_elided_commit_gate_9620_test.go`: both spellings must reach the same `CheckText` verdict. `hold-time 1` is refused in both elided shapes, as are an undeclared first keyword and an inline `apply-groups` naming an undefined group. A description is inherited through an inline `apply-groups`, and an `apply-macro` body binds no interface. The next-hop is inherited through `apply-groups` in both shapes, and `vrf-target export target:…` commits. An undeclared token after a value gets the same verdict in both spellings.
- Targeted `go test -json` at the rebased head `d9d472cd7`, scored by name, over the fold, normalizer, #9323, #8787, #9685 and routing-instance tests in pkg/config and pkg/configstore: 390 test names, 0 failures. That includes 69 #9620 names and master's 12 #9685 names.
- Mutation matrix at the rebased head `d9d472cd7`: 16 mutants plus one combination, 0 VOID. Each run was scored by test name from `go test -json` against the expected failure message, and the unmutated baseline passed all five targets. The matrix ran as foreground batches, because the harness stops background jobs when the host is low on memory.
  - **Killed:** 14 mutants and the combination. 22 of 22 (mutant, target) cells matched their message.
    - Normalizer hook disabled.
    - One-line extension disabled.
    - Apply keywords no longer a boundary.
    - Declared args ignored.
    - Braced body not attached.

    - Undeclared keywords skipped.
    - An apply keyword at a keyword position treated as undeclared.
    - An apply statement given no argument.

## PR #9760 — cluster/config: stop a negative redundancy-group id aliasing RG0 [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9723-negative-rg-wire-alias`

## Summary

Strict commit refuses a negative redundancy-group id, but the tolerant path (persisted-config load and HA peer sync) only warned and kept the group. `compileChassis` parses the id with `strconv.Atoi`, so `redundancy-group -1` really is -1. #8337's heartbeat saturation maps every negative id to wire byte 0, the byte RG0 uses. `localRGIDForWireByte` ranged over a Go map, so a node holding RG0 and RG -1 attributed the peer's RG0 entry to either group. The reviewer measured 46 wrong lookups in 400, and RG0's entry missing 3 times in 200 heartbeats, which feeds election.go's "Peer has no RG info" arm on both nodes.

**Two changes:**
- **Tolerant compile drops negative ids.** `dropNegativeRedundancyGroups` removes them in the `lenientChassisRG` branch, with one warning per dropped group, so a loaded or synced config never gives the cluster manager RG -1. Ids above 255 are kept on purpose: they saturate onto byte 255, which no runnable group uses, and #8337 keeps and advertises them. A negative id is the one out-of-range value that aliases a live group, and it can never index `rg_active` anyway.
- **The wire-byte lookup is deterministic.** `localRGIDForWireByte` prefers a local group whose id equals the byte, then the smallest saturating id, then `int(b)` as before. With in-range ids only, the result is unchanged.

The #5694 identity-gate comments claimed a negative token collapses to 0. Atoi accepts it, so compileChassis keeps the negative id; the comments now say so.

## Validation

- New cells:
  - strict commit still refuses `-1`; the tolerant compile keeps only RG0 and announces the drop;
  - scope control: an id above 255 is still kept on the tolerant path;
  - `localRGIDForWireByte` over `{0,-1}`, `{-1}`, `{300,255,256}`, `{300,256}` and an in-range control, 400 trials each;
  - 200 real peer-built heartbeats with `{0,-1}` configured directly on both managers, with the peer's RG0 entry present under id 0 every round.
- `#8337`, `#8317`, `#4434` and `#5694` cells: green. `go test ./pkg/config/ ./pkg/cluster/`: 10531 passed, 0 failed.
- Mutation matrix: 5/5 killed (tolerant drop not called, off-by-one predicate, dropping ids above 255, exact-id preference removed, saturating matches unsorted). Table in `docs/log/9723.md`.
- `make test-failover` on the loss userspace cluster (pkg/cluster changed), run twice, each time 22 passed and 0 failed, with #8341 a tracked known gap:
  - on the original head: iperf3 at 20.4 Gbps;
  - after rebasing onto 557e38f12, which carries #9640's change to the same `heartbeat_manager.go`: iperf3 at 18.5 Gbps across reboot, rejoin and manual failback, with IPv6 transit OK.
  Both ledger entries are committed.


- `make test`, both legs, is green on integration tree 4dba84557: origin/master 5f28e89ac merged with the pairwise file-disjoint heads of #9723, #9645, #9680. Go: 77 packages ok, no FAIL lines. Rust: 5864 passed, 0 failed.

Closes #9723

## PR #9762 — userspace-dp/cos: key flow-fair buckets by routing domain and tunnel [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9645-flow-fair-hash-routing-domain`

Closes #9645

## Problem

`exact_cos_flow_bucket` hashed only the 5-tuple. `SessionKey` identity also carries `routing_domain` (#7160) and the tunnel `discriminator` (#7188). Two sessions that differ only in those fields — identical 5-tuples in two routing instances, or two GRE tunnels that differ only by key — therefore landed in the SAME flow-fair SFQ bucket for every seed. They split one fair share by construction rather than by chance.

Severity is Low, as adjudicated in #8869: this is fairness coupling, not an isolation boundary.

## Fix

- Both fields are mixed into the bucket hash, each **only when non-default**. A default-instance flow with no discriminator keeps the exact pre-change bucket, so the seed-0 pins (410/1284) and the loss-cluster 5201 fairness baseline stay valid without re-validation.
- The discriminator match is exhaustive with no `_` arm, as in `session/key.rs`, so a new class must decide whether it separates fair shares.
- Tags are small values, and every u32 is mixed as two 16-bit halves. `mix_cos_flow_bucket` only carries upward and the bucket keeps the low bits, so a difference above bit 15 never reaches the bucket.
  - A first draft that mixed `(tag << 32) | value` collided `Unkeyed`/`Unparseable` and `Keyed(1)`/`Pptp(1)` for every seed.
  - The cells caught it, and they now include upper-half-only pairs.

## Validation

- **New cells** in `flow_hash_tests.rs`:
  - routing domains separate, including ids that differ only in the upper half;
  - every discriminator class pair separates, including GRE keys that differ only in the upper half;
  - the default routing domain with no discriminator matches a verbatim copy of the old function across seeds and v4/v6 ports.
- `cargo test flow_hash`: 14 passed, 0 failed.
- Mutation matrix: 8/8 killed, scored by test name (table in `docs/log/9645.md`). Mutants:
  - routing domain not mixed, or mixed when default;
  - keyed value dropped;
  - unkeyed not mixed;
  - pptp shares the keyed tag;
  - unparseable shares the unkeyed tag;
  - halves collapsed to the draft's high-bit mix;
  - upper half dropped.

## Not changed

Source IPv4 addresses that differ only in their top octet share the same carry-only limitation in the existing mix. Changing that would move the default-instance mapping and needs the fairness re-validation the seed-0 pins demand.

Docs: `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/cos/README.md`, `docs/cos-traffic-shaping.md`, `docs/log/9645.md`.

## PR #9763 — nat64: key the BIB allocation by the flow's routing domain [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9680-nat64-bib-routing-scope`

Closes #9680

## Problem

`SourceNatFlowKey` carries `routing_scope` so that identical flows from different routing instances do not share an allocator identity (#9062). NAT64 pinned that scope to 0 at all three sites (allocation, release and the HA synced reserve), per the constant `NAT64_ROUTING_SCOPE_9062`.

Identical IPv6 5-tuples arriving in two routing instances that reach the global NAT64 prefix installed as two sessions (#7160). They built byte-identical allocator keys, though, so the second flow reused the first flow's translated `(pool v4, port)` through `live_by_flow`. That violates the per-flow uniqueness NAT64 documents (#4381), and a release by one tenant could free a port the other tenant's live session still uses.

## Fix

The routing domain comes from the one place that already has it, the flow's forward `SessionKey`:

- **Allocation:** the poll path passes `flow.forward_key.routing_domain` to `allocate_source_for_worker`, which threads it into `allocate_source_with_holder`.
- **Release and synced reserve:** `release_nat64_allocation_with_mode` and `reserve_synced_nat64_allocation_with_holder` already receive that forward key (`is_reverse` returns early), so they read `key.routing_domain`.

The three sites agree by construction. The removed constant's comment warned that they must, or a release silently misses its allocation and leaks the pool entry. `routing_domain` is config-derived and already on the session-sync wire (#7160), so a standby reserves under the scope the active allocated with. The test-only `allocate_source` keeps its signature and passes 0, the default instance.

## Validation

- **New cells** (4, in `nat64_tests.rs`):
  - distinct bindings per routing domain, with a same-domain reuse control;
  - release keyed by domain: a wrong-domain release leaves the other tenant live, and the own-domain release frees it;
  - synced reserve keyed by domain;
  - poll-path wiring: the single production allocate call's last argument is the flow's routing domain. The cells above drive the allocator directly and would pass on a poll path that kept passing 0.
- `cargo test nat64`: 290 passed, 0 failed. The whole test binary compiles, including the 8 updated call sites.
- **Mutation matrix:** 5/5 killed, scored by test name (table in `docs/log/9680.md`). The mutants pin scope 0 at allocation, release and the synced reserve; drop the scope in the for-worker pass-through; and make the poll path pass 0.

## Not changed

- Reverse keys stay domain-agnostic by #7160 design. An end-to-end reply-demux check (two VRFs, overlapping IPv6 clients, a shared NAT64 prefix) remains the issue's lab follow-up.

Docs: `userspace-dp/src/FEATURES.md` (`nat64.rs` row), `docs/log/9680.md`.

## PR #9764 — userspace-dp/HA: decide local ownership before a synced NAT reserve [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9678-synced-reserve-ownership-gate`

Closes #9678

## Problem

`SessionDomain::upsert_synced_session` took the coordinator's pre-publish NAT reservation (#6600) for a peer-synced session before anything asked whether this node owns the flow.

The worker refuses a peer upsert that would replace a locally owned session while that session's owner RG is locally forwarding-active (`upsert_synced_with_origin` + `synced_entry_allows_local_replace`). But `reserve_flow` retires a `live_by_flow` incumbent that holds a DIFFERENT translated tuple first. So a same-flow peer upsert, in a dual-primary window or a failover race:

1. evicted the local flow's live allocation T1;
2. reserved an `Untracked` T2;
3. then the worker refused the replace and kept forwarding on T1, which no longer had an allocator record, so T1 could be handed to another flow.

Every refusal inside the reserve happens after that unlink. Even an import answered `RejectedReserve` had already freed T1.

## Fix

The import now applies the worker's own predicate first:
- the shared map holds a local-origin entry for the key, and
- the incoming owner RG does not allow a local replace.

When both hold, the import returns **before the reservation, the shared publish and the worker fan-out**.

- **Why the publish too.** Skipping only the reservation would still publish the peer's decision into the shared maps. That is the #6600 shape: a shared entry naming a port this node does not hold, which `materialize_shared_session_hit` on another worker would forward on.
- **Why `Applied`.** It matches the worker's refusal, which is silent, and the outcome this import already reported. A new refusal token would reach the Go control plane as a peer error during a dual-primary window.
- **Recovery.** Once the RG is no longer locally active, the next sync of the flow imports normally.
- **Race guard kept.** An active node with no local session for the flow still reserves before publishing.

## Validation

- **New cells** (4, in `ha_tests.rs`), each with one worker and a local flow F allocated on port 50010:
  - RG active, the peer names a free port 50020: 50010 stays held, 50020 is not stranded, the shared map keeps the local entry, and nothing is fanned out.
  - RG active, the peer names a port another flow holds: 50010 stays held.
  - Control, RG not locally active: the import replaces, reserves and fans out.
  - Control, RG active with no local flow: the import still reserves before publishing (#6600).
- **Suites:** `cargo test afxdp::ha` / `session_glue` / `coordinator`: 76 / 155 / 241 passed, 0 failed.
- **Mutation matrix:** 3/3 killed, one per guard term (table in `docs/log/9678.md`).
- **`make test-failover`** on the loss userspace cluster (HA session-sync import changed): 22 passed, 0 failed, iperf3 20.8 Gbps. #8341 is a tracked known gap. Ledger entry committed.

## Not changed

The guard reads local ownership from the shared map, which the poll path publishes for local sessions. A worker-local session absent from the shared map is still refused by the worker, but its allocator record is not protected by this guard.

Docs: `docs/session-sync-architecture.md` (new #9678 paragraph under the #6600/#7581 reservation), `docs/log/9678.md`.

## PR #9765 — userspace: refuse a local-address set past the shim map capacity [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9646-local-address-map-capacity`

Closes #9646

## Problem

`userspace_local_v4` and `userspace_local_v6` are shim hash maps of 8192 entries each (`userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs`). `syncLocalAddressMapsLocked` updated every desired key and returned the first kernel refusal. The desired set is the snapshot's local addresses plus the host addresses netlink enumerates, including VRRP VIPs.

Both classifier-map callers turned ANY sync error into `userspace_ctrl.Enabled=0`:
- `syncUserspaceClassifierMapsFailClosedLocked`;
- the `applyHelperStatusLocked` re-sync, which runs every second.

With ctrl disabled, the shim drops all transit. One address past the capacity therefore took the dataplane from forwarding to dropping everything, and the only operator-visible cause was a map update error.

## Fix

- **Preflight.** `syncUserspaceClassifierMapsLocked` checks the desired local-address set against the capacity **before any classifier map is written**. The set is built once and handed to `syncLocalAddressMapsWithSetsLocked`, so there is no second netlink dump, and a set of exactly 8192 fits.
- **Named error.** An oversized set returns `localAddressCapacityError`, naming the map and the capacity, and it leaves every map on the plan the helper enforces.
- **Carve-outs, exactly two:**
  - The **fail-closed sync** (same-plan and deferred-startup applies) keeps ctrl, and the apply returns the named error.
  - The **status poll** keeps maps and ctrl and alarms once per transition, through a latch that a fitting sync clears. Without this, host address growth past the capacity would drop transit on the next tick.
- **Unchanged:**
  - Every other classifier-sync failure still fails closed.
  - The retain/rollback path still fails closed on this error too, because a refused publish has already mixed the maps.
  - A new-plan bootstrap still programs ctrl disabled first.
  - Add-before-prune (`TestSyncLocalAddressMapsAddsBeforeRemovingStale`) is kept.
- **Drift guard.** `userspaceLocalAddressMapCapacity` is bound to both shim `with_max_entries` declarations by a test.

## Validation

- **New cells** (all unprivileged; the real-BPF-map tests SKIP here without memlock):
  - past capacity (v4 and v6): the named error, and ctrl is never written;
  - at capacity: passes the preflight, and the ordinary unloaded-map failure still fails closed;
  - the status poll keeps a ready helper's ctrl enabled on a capacity refusal, latches the alarm and clears it once a sync fits; its control shows an ordinary failure still fails closed;
  - the shim capacity drift guard.
- **Suites:** `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ ./pkg/daemon/`: 5063 passed, 0 failed. gofmt, go vet and the refactoraudit modularity gate are clean.
- **Mutation matrix:** 8/8 killed, scored by test name (table in `docs/log/9646.md`). The mutants: preflight removed; either carve-out removed; v4 off-by-one; v6 check dropped; capacity constant drifted; latch never clears; every error classified as capacity.

Docs: `pkg/dataplane/README.md` (#9646 note beside the publish-ordering section), `docs/log/9646.md`.

## PR #9768 — test/incus: give every HA smoke the unshaped port and a total verdict [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9690-9691-ha-smoke-throughput`

Closes #9690

- `make test`, both legs, is green on integration tree 27352f67a: origin/master 9f520a5b2 merged with the pairwise file-disjoint heads of #9678, #9646, #9691. Go: 77 packages ok, no FAIL lines. Rust: 5861 passed, 0 failed.

Closes #9691

## Problem

Four HA smokes carry a throughput verdict: `test-double-failover`, `test-chained-crash`, `test-active-active` and `test-stress-failover`.

- **#9691 — they measure a shaped port.** They started iperf3 without `-p`, so they measured port 5201. `cos-iperf-config.set` classifies 5201 as `iperf-100m` (`transmit-rate 100m exact`) on the `reth0.80` path to `IPERF_TARGET4`. Their verdict therefore depended on whether an earlier lane had left CoS applied on the shared cluster:
  - with CoS applied, active-active failed at "0 Gbps" and stress-failover at about 0.09 Gbps;
  - double-failover and chained-crash hit the silent path described next.
- **#9690 — sub-Gbit runs emit no cell.** `test-double-failover` and `test-chained-crash` parsed `Gbits` only, into the literal `0`, and their verdict had no else. A sub-Gbit run emitted no throughput cell, and the ha-smoke ledger recorded PASS with no `throughput_gbps`.

`test-failover.sh` had both defects and was fixed in #7673 (port) and #6897 (total verdict). Its siblings were not changed, and the selftest's wiring and port-agreement cells read `test-failover.sh` only.

## Fix

- **Each sibling:**
  - sources `iperf-throughput-lib.sh`;
  - defaults `IPERF_PORT` to the unshaped 5211 and passes `-p ${IPERF_PORT}`;
  - judges throughput with `iperf_throughput_verdict` and a catch-all `case`, as `test-failover.sh` does.
- **Script-specific:**
  - `test-stress-failover` keeps reading the last interval `SUM` line, because its client is killed before a sender summary.
  - `test-active-active` now emits its throughput cell whether or not the run completed.
- **Selftest:** `iperf-throughput-selftest.sh` checks wiring and port agreement for all five smokes. For each one:
  - it sources the lib and calls the total verdict;
  - the verdict has a catch-all;
  - there is no inline Gbits parse in either spelling;
  - it passes `-p ${IPERF_PORT}`;
  - the default port resolves through the CoS term, class and scheduler to a class with no transmit-rate.

## Validation

- `make test-iperf-throughput-lib`: 24 passed.
- `bash -n` is clean on all five scripts; `make harness-census` is OK.
- **Selftest mutation matrix:** 6/6 killed (table in `docs/log/9691.md`). Each mutant changes one sibling:
  - drop `-p`;
  - default the port to 5201;
  - drop the catch-all;
  - stop sourcing the lib;
  - restore an inline Gbits parse;
  - stop calling the verdict.
- **Not run:** the destructive smokes themselves (they reboot or force-stop cluster nodes). The selftest is the gate for this change.

Docs: `docs/log/9691.md` (`docs/log/9690.md` points to it). `docs/engineering-style.md` already mandates 5211 for throughput rows.

## PR #9769 — cluster: serialize session-sync apply across receive loops [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9715-session-sync-per-key-apply`

## Summary

Every installed fabric connection runs its own `receiveLoop`. When the session-sync stream moves between fabrics (a fabric flap, or the #9508 preferred-fabric switch), the old loop can still be applying frames it already read while the new loop applies newer frames for the same key. Two defects follow from the #2198 F3 assumption of a single-threaded apply.

- An install took `recvGenMu` separately for its guard and its record, with the dataplane write in between. An older install parked in its write recorded its generation and content over a newer install's. An older delete was then admitted and removed the session.
- A delete ran its dataplane delete after the guard released the lock. So a delete admitted before a newer install removed that install after it landed.

An accepted `BulkStart`'s generation-map reset had the same gap: an install parked across it recorded its pre-reboot generation after the reset.

## Change

- `SessionSync.applyMu` is held:
  - from each install's guard, through its dataplane write, to its record or rollback;
  - from each delete's guard through its dataplane delete;
  - around `resetRecvGen`'s map reset.
- Lock order: `applyMu` → `recvGenMu`.
- One lock rather than per-key stripes:
  - it is uncontended while one loop applies;
  - it serializes only during a stream move;
  - it also covers the reverse-companion row a forward install writes.
- The F3 note, the #6368 rollback comment and the `pkg/cluster/README.md` generation-guard paragraph are corrected.
- Tests: `sync_apply_serialize_9715_test.go` parks loop A inside the mock's dataplane write or delete while loop B applies the same key.
  - Cells: install v4/v6, delete v4/v6, the BulkStart reset, and a serialized control.
  - `mockSweepDP` gains `onDeleteV4`/`onDeleteV6`.
- No HA wire change: the lock is local.

## Validation

- [x] Mutation matrix on 0473d75b3, one `applyMu` acquisition removed per mutant: 5/5 KILLED, each by its named cell.
- [x] `go test -race ./pkg/cluster`: exit 0.
- [x] `make test` (Go + Rust) on 0473d75b3: exit 0. Go 77 packages ok; Rust 5864 passed, 0 failed.
- [x] `make test-failover` on the loss userspace cluster: 22 passed, 0 failed, **20.5000 Gbps**.
  - Run on local merge 70058368f = origin/master 80db775c4 + 0473d75b3.
  - Ledger row ad880749c65c1031.json: PASS, exe MATCH.

Closes #9715

## PR #9771 — userspace-dp: remove a shared alias only while it names the session [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9679-shared-alias-owned-removal`

Closes #9679

## Problem

The shared, cross-worker NAT reverse-alias map (`reverse_session_key` and `reverse_canonical_key` slots) and the forward-wire alias map each hold one entry per key. `publish_shared_session` overwrites a colliding session's alias and only counts the displacement (#1760).

`remove_shared_session(A)` derived A's alias keys and deleted whatever occupied them, with no check that the stored entry was A. So removing a session that a colliding session B had displaced also removed B's aliases. A worker with no local copy of B then missed both lookups and sent B's replies to new-flow adjudication.

The removal runs on every Close-delta drain, terminal delete and coordinator delete. The collision classes include DNAT to a shared backend and identical 5-tuples in two routing instances.

## Fix

`remove_shared_alias_owned_by` deletes an alias, and its owner-RG index entry, only while the stored entry's key is the removed session's. A same-session republish stores the same key, so an owned alias is still removed.

The reverse order is unchanged: when the removed session had displaced the survivor at publish, the survivor's alias was already lost at that publish, and removal cannot restore it. The displacement counter already makes that visible.

## Validation

- **New cell** `removing_a_displaced_session_keeps_the_survivors_shared_aliases_9679`, covering two collision pairs: interface SNAT, and identical 5-tuples in two routing domains.
  - For every alias slot a pair shares, removing the displaced session keeps the survivor's alias, and removing the owner clears it.
  - The pairs must together cover all three slots, so no slot's check can go untested silently.
- **Suites:** `cargo test session_glue`: 156 passed, 0 failed.
- **Mutation matrix:** 4/4 killed (table in `docs/log/9679.md`). One mutant per slot reverts it to an unchecked delete, and one never removes an owned alias.
- **`make test-failover`** on the loss userspace cluster: 22 passed, 0 failed, iperf3 13.7 Gbps. #8341 is a tracked known gap. Ledger entry committed.

Docs: `docs/session-sync-architecture.md` (new bullet beside the shared reverse-NAT map description), `docs/log/9679.md`.

## PR #9772 — daemon: give the commit-tail routing reconcile a retry owner [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9693-routing-reconcile-retry-owner`

Closes #9693

## Problem

Every config apply reconciles the kernel policy-routing rules and then republishes the userspace route snapshot from that kernel state. The rules are next-table, rib-group and firewall-filter PBR. #5844 and #5696 made both failures deferred commit errors, but nothing re-ran them.

A transient ip-rule or republish failure left stale or missing cross-VRF policy in the kernel, and a FIB rebuilt from that partial state, until an unrelated apply re-ran the reconcile. On the applies nobody waits on (boot, DHCP lease callback, feed, config-poll), the joined error was only logged at Warn. The code said so itself: "This commit-tail reconcile has no dirty-retry engine".

## Fix

This follows the repo's retry-owner pattern (`proxyARPReassertLoop` #4001, `fabricIPVLANReassertLoop` #6791, `serviceReloadDebtReassertLoop` #6800).

- **Debt.** The apply latches `routingReconcileDebt` from the two errors (`noteRoutingReconcileResult`), and a clean apply discharges it. The failure count is monotonic, and `RoutingReconcileDebt()` reports the latch, the count and the last error.
- **Retry owner.** `routingReconcileReassertLoop` starts unconditionally in Run and re-runs the reconcile every 30 s while the debt is owed.
  - It takes `applySem` before reading the active config.
  - It re-checks the debt inside the semaphore, since a commit in between runs the same reconcile.
  - It re-runs `applyPolicyRoutingRules` plus `reconcileRouteLeakSnapshot` with `commitOverlayForConfig`.
  - It never re-runs the FRR apply, whose manager owns its own degraded retry.
- **Extraction.** `applyPolicyRoutingRules` is extracted from `applyRoutingRules`, so the commit path and the retry owner run the same reconcile.

## Validation

- **New cells** (7, in `routing_reconcile_debt_9693_test.go`):
  - the debt latches and discharges;
  - the retry owner runs only while owed and retries until it succeeds;
  - it reconciles the active config and waits while a commit holds `applySem`;
  - it re-checks the debt inside the semaphore, so it reconciles nothing when a commit discharged the debt while it waited;
  - wiring: the apply latches after the republish, Run starts the loop, both share `applyPolicyRoutingRules`, and the retry never calls the FRR apply;
  - the retry re-runs the route-leak republish too, and a republish failure alone keeps the debt;
  - with nothing owed the retry owner does not queue behind a commit.
- **Suites:** `go test ./pkg/daemon/ ./pkg/routing/`: 3054 passed, 0 failed. gofmt, go vet and the refactoraudit gate are clean. No cluster gate is required (daemon routing-reconcile code, not cluster/HA).

## PR #9773 — config: warn when a bound interface's MTU exceeds one UMEM frame [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9727-jumbo-mtu-umem-budget`

Closes #9727

## Problem

The userspace dataplane receives into fixed 4096-byte UMEM frames, with 256 bytes of headroom, and binds AF_XDP without multi-buffer (`XDP_USE_SG`) support, so a frame larger than one UMEM frame cannot reach a worker:
- in copy mode the kernel drops it and counts it in `kernel_rx_dropped`;
- a zero-copy driver may refuse the XSK setup, and the #7191 arm then fails closed.

The interface `mtu` leaf accepts any value of at least 1. So a jumbo MTU on a bound interface committed clean and quietly became drops or a refused bind.

## Fix

A commit-time advisory, `appendUserspaceRxMTUAdvisoryLocked`, runs at both compile sites beside the #7509 advisories. It names the interface, its MTU and the single-frame receive budget:
- **Budget:** `4096 − 256 − 14 − 4` = **3822** (UMEM frame, headroom, Ethernet header, one VLAN tag).
- **Scope:** interfaces the userspace dataplane binds. This mirrors the dataplane's own rule, which pkg/config cannot import:
  - zoned interfaces, except in the `mgmt` and `control` zones;
  - excluding tunnels, `fxp*`, `em*`, `fab*`, `lo0` and local fabric members.
- **Effective MTU:** the unit MTU when set, otherwise the interface MTU.
- **Severity:** a warning, not a refusal. Commit cannot tell copy mode from zero-copy, and a jumbo MTU remains right for kernel-forwarded traffic.
- **Suppression:** silenced on the tolerant boot and peer-sync paths, like the #7509 advisories.
- **Drift guard:** the Go constants are bound to `UMEM_FRAME_SIZE` and `UMEM_HEADROOM` in the helper source.

## Validation

- **New cells** (in `userspace_rx_mtu_advisory_9727_test.go`):
  - acceptance: MTU 9000 on a zoned interface warns naming 3822, and MTU 1500 does not;
  - the 3822/3823 boundary, and unit MTU overriding interface MTU in both directions;
  - silence for each exclusion (fxp, em, lo0, tunnel, local fabric member, mgmt zone, control zone) and for an unzoned interface;
  - suppression on the tolerant paths;
  - the UMEM constants drift guard;
  - end to end: compiling real set commands carries the advisory.
- **Suites:** `go test ./pkg/config/ ./pkg/configstore/`: 10152 passed, 0 failed. No existing warning-count or golden cell moved. gofmt, go vet and the refactoraudit gate are clean.
- **Mutation matrix:** 9/9 killed (table in `docs/log/9727.md`). The mutants: budget off-by-one; unit MTU ignored; mgmt/control zones treated as bound; fxp/em not excluded; tunnel not excluded; fabric member not excluded; tolerant paths not suppressed; both call sites removed; UMEM frame size drifted. One mutant first scored VOID on a spelling that did not compile and was re-run on one that does.

## Not changed

- The issue's optional "show the budget in interface or binding status".
- The failed-MTU-apply warning.
- The TX side (#9395, #9758).

Docs: `docs/log/9727.md`.

## PR #9775 — userspace-dp: keep forwarding an oversized DF-clear IPv4 datagram, measured [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9395-df-clear-oversize-policy`

Closes #9395

#9328 made an oversized DF-clear IPv4 datagram distinguishable (`ForwardOversizeNoDf`) and recorded it (`egress_mtu_exceeded_forwarded_no_df`, a sampled exception), but left the policy open. This PR records the decision with the measurement it asked for: **keep forwarding, with the exception recorded.** No behaviour change; comments, docs and test message wording only.

## Measurement (loss userspace cluster, build 5f28e89ac, one lock cell)

- **Setup.** Sender: cluster-userspace-host (LAN). Receiver: xpf-mouse-target, 172.16.80.201 on VLAN 80. fw0 was primary. Delivery was read at the receiver (UDP receipts by size, `/proc/net/snmp`), not from ping replies. The sender's PMTU cache was flushed before every cell.
- **Configured MTU 1400 on a 1500-byte link** (`set interfaces reth0 unit 80 family inet mtu 1400`; kernel `ge-0-0-2.80` 1400, physical `ge-0-0-2` 1500):
  - DF-clear 1450-byte datagrams, all delivered **whole**:

    | | delivered | receiver `Ip.ReasmReqds` | mlx5 `tx_xsk_err` / `tx_xdp_err` |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | UDP | 10/10 | unchanged, 0 | 0 |
    | ICMP | 5/5 | unchanged, 0 | 0 |

  - `egress_mtu_exceeded_forwarded_no_df` was recorded for both protocols (len 1464).
  - **Positive control:** DF-set 1450 drew `Frag needed and DF set (mtu = 1400)`, so the decision really saw 1400.
- **Physical link at 1400:** not reachable. `set interfaces reth0 mtu 1400` does not reach the RETH member link (#9761).

## Decision

Keep forwarding, with the exception recorded, decided from the plain-forward measurement above. A drop would break that working path, and a downstream router that cannot carry the datagram may fragment it (RFC 791).

**Scope.** The decision covers what this arm does, not every path's outcome. What the measurement does not cover (transformed paths, and a datagram larger than the physical link, #9758) is stated once, on `EgressMtuDecision::ForwardOversizeNoDf`, and every other comment and doc refers to it. The exception is sampled (see `record_exception`): it shows that such decisions happen, delivered or not, but is neither a count nor a loss counter.

**#2301 re-read.** Its Impact names oversized UDP, ICMP, ESP, GRE and non-first fragments with no DF qualifier. For DF-clear IPv4 on a plain forward it does not hold when the link carries the datagram (delivered in the measured topology). The paths where it can still hold are the ones `ForwardOversizeNoDf` lists.

## Changes

- `icmp_ptb.rs`: the `ForwardOversizeNoDf` doc holds the one statement of the policy and what it does not cover. The header, the `Forward` variant, the decision function's doc and the decision arm no longer call the DF-clear case `Forward` or a blackhole.
- `gre.rs`, `frame/wg.rs`: the encap-guard comments name `ForwardOversizeNoDf` and drop "downstream-fragmentable".
- `frame/tcp_segmentation.rs`, `frame/prop_tests/segment.rs`, the dispatcher's seg-miss doc, `afxdp/README.md`, `docs/userspace-native-gre-plan.md`: older comments that named `Forward` or a universal blackhole for this case now refer to the variant.
- `tx/dispatch/mod.rs`: the record-site comment refers to the variant.
- `oversized_v4_without_df_forwards` and `oversized_no_df_is_forwarded_and_counted_9328`: refer to the decided contract.
- Test assertion message wording (no assertion logic) in four test files: `tx/dispatch/tests/ptb.rs`, `icmp_ptb_tests.rs`, `frame/tests_segment_tcp.rs`, `frame/prop_tests/segment.rs`. "Blackhole band" is now "oversize band" there and in `tx/dispatch/tests/segmentation.rs` and `frame/tcp_segmentation.rs`.
- `tx/README.md`: the #9328 paragraph.
- `docs/log/9395.md`: the measurement record.

## Filed during the measurement (none queued)

- **#9757 (MEDIUM):** deleting a unit's family `mtu` leaves the VLAN sub-interface kernel MTU, and the userspace egress MTU, at the old value. The cell's restore hit it: `reth0.80` stayed at 1400 on both nodes for four minutes, until a second lock cell reset it and verified the reset.
- **#9758 (LOW):** no IPv4 egress fragmenter for the physical-link case.
- **#9761 (LOW):** an interface-level `mtu` on a `vlan-tagging` interface whose zone units are all tagged never reaches the parent link.

- [x] Targeted cargo tests: `icmp_ptb` (47), the #9328 cells (2), the oversized cells (26).

## PR #9776 — cluster: accept a BulkEnd only on its BulkStart's connection [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9716-bulkend-connection-fence`

## Summary

The #9174 V013 incarnation check refuses a `BulkEnd` only when both boot incarnations are known and differ. When either side is un-incarnated (a peer on an older build, or a bulk primed without one), completion was matched on the epoch alone.

Every peer process restarts its epoch at 1. So a legacy `BulkEnd` buffered on a dead peer process's still-established socket could complete the replacement's live bulk. The receiver then:
- reconciled against a partly received table;
- latched `bulkEverCompleted`;
- released the VRRP sync hold.

## Change

- The receiver records the connection that carried the accepted `BulkStart` (`bulkRecvConn`, under `bulkMu`), and accepts that bulk's `BulkEnd` only on it.
  - `BulkSync` pins one connection for a whole bulk, so a legitimate end marker never arrives on another.
  - The check runs after the incarnation check, so `BulkEndsDeadIncarnationDropped` keeps its meaning.
- Two new counters, rendered by `show chassis cluster` when nonzero:
  - `BulkEndsForeignConnDropped`: end markers refused by the fence;
  - `BulkEndsEpochOnlyMatched`: completions the incarnation check could not judge.
- The recorded connection is cleared with the epoch and incarnation on a full disconnect.
- `docs/sync-protocol.md` documents the fence and both counters.
- No wire change. A legacy peer's bulk, started and ended on one connection, still completes.
- Not changed: the between-bulks un-incarnated `BulkStart`. With no incarnation on the wire, a rebooted peer restarting its counter and a stale frame are the same bytes, and the #9174 cells pin accepting it.

## Validation

- [x] Mutation matrix on 161c17fe2: 4/4 KILLED, each by its named cell.
  - Mutants: the fence disabled; the connection record removed; the epoch-only count removed; its condition inverted.
- [x] `go test -race ./pkg/cluster`: exit 0.
- [x] `make test` (Go + Rust) on 161c17fe2: exit 0. Go 77 packages ok; Rust 5868 passed, 0 failed. It ran with `GOFLAGS=-p=4 CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4`: the first run was killed by the host for low memory during its Rust leg, after its Go leg had passed.
- [x] `make test-failover` on the loss userspace cluster: 22 passed, 0 failed, **19.8000 Gbps**.
  - Run on local merge d1d77a860 = origin/master 199f0a0cf + 161c17fe2.
  - Ledger row fc1c0b34ed35b083.json: PASS, exe MATCH.

Closes #9716

## PR #9779 — userspace: owner-RG export errors carry no deltas [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9699-owner-rg-export-all-or-error`

Closes #9699

## Problem

The owner-RG session export produces the bulk window that the peer reconciles authoritatively (#5085): any session missing from a completed window is deleted on the peer. Its contract, stated at `ErrOwnerRGExportUnterminated` and in `daemon_ha_userspace_export.go`, is one complete window or an error, never a partial one.

Three Manager return sites broke that contract. When the export request succeeded but applying the helper status that came back with it failed, each returned the deltas collected so far together with the error:
- `ExportOwnerRGSessionsPaged`'s page loop;
- the unpaged fallback `exportOwnerRGSessionsUnpagedLocked`;
- `ExportOwnerRGSessions`.

The runtime passthrough then wrapped those deltas into a snapshot and returned it with the error. Both production callers discard deltas on error today, so no receiver is fed a partial window; the defect is the API shape.

## Fix

- **Manager sites:** all three return `nil` deltas beside the error.
- **Runtime passthrough:** it builds its snapshot through `runtimeOwnerRGExportSnapshot`, which drops deltas on error whatever the manager returned; the status still rides along. The rule is a function of its own so it is exercisable: a first matrix showed that a cell driven through a real manager cannot see it.
- **Not changed:** `DrainSessionDeltas`, which has the same shape but a different contract. Drained incremental deltas are consumed and must not be discarded.

## Validation

- **New cells** (in `owner_rg_export_all_or_error_9699_test.go`): one per exit (paged, unpaged fallback, direct `ExportOwnerRGSessions`, runtime passthrough). There is also a direct cell for `runtimeOwnerRGExportSnapshot`, with a success control, and a wiring cell.
  - Each uses a fake helper whose responses carry deltas and a helper status. The status apply then fails deterministically in a test manager, because no shim maps are loaded.
  - Each asserts an error and zero deltas.
- **Suites:** `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ ./pkg/daemon/ ./pkg/dataplane/runtime/`: 5070 passed, 0 failed. gofmt, go vet and the refactoraudit gate are clean.
- **Mutation matrix:** 5/5 killed (table in `docs/log/9699.md`). The first run scored the passthrough mutant ESCAPED, which is what led to the extraction.
- **`make test-failover`** on the loss userspace cluster (session-sync export path): 22 passed, 0 failed, iperf3 20.9 Gbps. #8341 is a tracked known gap. Ledger entry committed.

Docs: `docs/log/9699.md`. The contract is stated in code at both places the issue cites. No module doc restates it.

## PR #9781 — test/incus: test-ha-crash must see established streams survive a takeover [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9692-ha-crash-established-streams`

Closes #9692

## Problem

`make test-failover` plus `make test-ha-crash` are the mandated HA gates, with the pass criterion "0 / very low packet loss across failover/failback".

`test-ha-crash`'s phase 1 (hard VM stop) and phase 2 (`systemctl stop xpfd`, the #68 fail-closed path) each started a 4-stream, 120 s iperf3 client through the primary, but only checked:
- the takeover;
- a new TCP connection;
- a ping.

Then they `pkill -9`'d the client; phase 1's comment said "sessions are dead". Two kinds of regression therefore passed the mandated gate, as long as new connections worked:
- a survivor that lost or refused the synced sessions;
- a stopping node whose teardown broke established flows.

The client also ran on port 5201, which the CoS fixture shapes to 100 Mb/s.

## Fix

- **Recovery check.** `established_streams_recovered` runs in both phases before the client is killed. After `RECOVERY_WAIT` (10 s) it requires two things:
  - iperf3 is still running;
  - the most recent `[SUM]` interval is at or above `RECOVERY_MIN_GBPS` (0.5), parsed by the shared `iperf_sum_rate_gbps`.

  A stalled `0.00 bits/sec` interval fails.
- **Port.** The client is pinned to the unshaped port 5211.
- **Comments.** The "sessions are dead" comment is replaced, and the header lists the new check.

## Validation

- `bash -n` and `shellcheck -S warning` are clean; `make harness-census` is OK.
- The lib parses a real `[SUM]` interval line, and a `0.00 bits/sec` line fails.
- **Calibration on the loss cluster:** `make test-ha-crash` PASSED, 44 passed / 0 failed; master's rows read 42, and the two extra are the new cells. Ledger row `96ba779e7b0a7b54.json` (exe_check=MATCH).
  - After the phase 1 force-stop, the established streams' last `[SUM]` interval was 20.0 Gbps.
  - After the phase 2 daemon stop it was 14.9 Gbps.
  - Both are far above the 0.5 Gbps floor, so the threshold is not what makes the cell pass.

## PR #9784 — grpcapi: govern config RPCs by configuration regexes; gate Load and Rollback [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9633-grpc-config-rpc-authz`

Closes #9633

## Problem

On gRPC, for a non-superuser, the gates ran in this order:
1. permission bits;
2. `authorizeRPCCommand` — the **operational** regexes. It denied any method with no canonical command whenever the class carried operational regexes.
3. `authorizeRPCConfigMutation` — the `*-configuration` regexes, but only for `Set` and `Delete`.

Two defects followed:

- **V069.** The documented `permissions all; deny-commands "request system zeroize"` class could configure at the console, where `dispatchConfig` runs only the configuration gate, but not through the remote `cli`. Every config RPC was denied in step 2.
- **V068.** Both unenforceable-pattern advisories returned early unless the class had a **deny** source. An `allow-commands` pattern that permits no producible command, and so refuses the class everything, got no warning at commit or at authorization.

Narrowing step 2 alone would have let `Load` and `Rollback` write paths the configuration regexes forbid, with no check of any kind.

## Fix (the issue's suggested order)

1. **The configuration gate learns `Load` and `Rollback`.**
   - `load set` and `load merge` are adjudicated per written path. Hierarchical content is parsed and rendered as set lines, so every leaf meets `AuthorizeConfigMutation`.
   - `load override` and `rollback n>0` replace the whole candidate, and the paths they delete cannot be adjudicated one by one, so a class with configuration regexes is refused them.
   - `rollback 0` stays available.
   - A class with no configuration regexes is unaffected.
2. **Then the operational gate returns early for config-mode methods**, matching the console. The exempt set is bound by a test to the reviewed `methodsWithoutCanonicalCommand` table; the other unresolved RPCs stay denied.
3. **Allow-side advisory.** `UnenforceableAllowSurfaces` counts a command as permitted only when the allow leaf decided it. It is wired into the commit advisory and the gRPC one-shot warning.

## Validation

- **New cells.**
  - The documented `limited` class can `EnterConfigure`/`Set`/`Delete`/`Load`/`Commit`/`CommitCheck`/`Rollback`/`ExitConfigure` over gRPC and is still refused zeroize.
  - Unresolved operational RPCs stay denied, with a guard against checking nothing.
  - The exempt set is bound to the reviewed table.
  - For a `deny-configuration "system host-name"` class:
    - refused: set-format load, hierarchical merge touching the path, override, `rollback 1`;
    - allowed: a merge that avoids the path, and `rollback 0`;
    - an unrestricted control is refused nothing.
  - The allow advisory fires for a pattern that permits nothing, stays silent for one that permits a command, and warns end to end at commit.
- **Suites:** `go test ./pkg/grpcapi/ ./pkg/config/ ./pkg/cli/ ./pkg/authz/`: 11561 passed, 0 failed, and re-run green at the final head after the matrix. gofmt, go vet and the refactoraudit gate are clean.
- **A prior cell pinned the old behaviour.** `TestUnmappedRPCDeniesARestrictedClass7172` had a `Commit` row asserting that config-mode RPCs are denied to any class with operational regexes. That recorded #7172's fail-closed choice, made while gRPC could not adjudicate config-mode RPCs; this change removes that premise. The row is replaced by a comment naming the #9633 cells that now bind those methods, and the cell's other rows still assert the denial.
- **Mutation matrix:** 9/9 killed at the final head (table in `docs/log/9633.md`). The mutants: exemption removed; an operational method exempted; Load/Rollback not delegated; override not refused; rollback n>0 not refused; hierarchical content not parsed; restricted check inverted; allow detector always permits; commit advisory dropped.
  - The first run killed 8/9. The operational-method mutant escaped because its cell chose which methods to skip from the production exempt set it guards. Both exempt-set cells now read an independently spelled reviewed list, and the binding cell asserts set equality.

## Not changed

- On the console, `load` remains the stated gap.
- REST is not changed here.

Docs: `docs/system-login.md` (the load/rollback paragraph now states what gRPC enforces), `docs/log/9633.md`.

## PR #9786 — userspace: report whether the learned-route import is capped NOW [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9654-learned-route-capped-now`

Closes #9654

## Problem

Since #9054 a capped learned-route import (#8355) changes forwarding: NoRoute frames go back to slow-path delegation. Nothing reported whether a box is capped at this moment.

`xpf_learned_route_cap_hits_total` (#9019) counts capped snapshot builds, so it can't answer that. It stays non-zero after recovery and does not move while one capped snapshot stays in force.

The issue records two designs that failed review:
- a daemon-side flag on the retained snapshot;
- a helper field projected from the coordinator's candidate `forwarding` and decoded as a Go `bool`. That reports "capped" after a first-worker spawn failure, and it reads an older helper as "not capped".

## Fix

- **Source.** `Coordinator::learned_route_import_capped_now` reads the published runtime view (#6592), the state workers load. It answers only while at least one worker record is live, and returns `None` otherwise: after a teardown, before the first worker registers, after a first-worker spawn failure, or with every worker dead.
- **Presence.**
  - `ProcessStatus.learned_route_import_capped` is `Option<bool>` and is omitted when `None`.
  - Go decodes it as `*bool`, so absence reads as unknown, both from a helper with no live worker and from one that predates the field.
  - No protocol version bump is needed: absence of this additive field already carries the skew-safe reading.
- **Metric.** `xpf_learned_route_import_capped` (1/0) is emitted only when the flag is known. The #9019 counter is unchanged.

## Validation

- **Rust:** `cargo test --tests` (userspace-dp), 5877 passed, 0 failed. The eight #9654 cells:
  - no live worker with a capped view;
  - following the published view;
  - ignoring an unpublished candidate;
  - every worker dead;
  - teardown;
  - a real same-plan `refresh_runtime_snapshot`;
  - a real `reconcile` with the #4952 first-worker spawn-failure seam;
  - the `refresh_status` projection with JSON omission.
- **Go:** `go test ./pkg/api/ ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/`, 3582 passed, 0 failed. This covers decode/omit and emit-only-when-known, and the collector coverage canary now requires the family through the real `Collect`.
- **Static checks:** gofmt, go vet and the refactoraudit gate are clean. The change adds no rustfmt hunk over master.
- **Mutation matrix:** 10/10 killed (table in `docs/log/9654.md`). The mutants: liveness gate ignored; candidate read instead of published view; dead flag ignored; projection dropped; unknown serialized as null; unknown emitted as 0; capped value lost; wire key renamed; emit unwired; describe unwired.
- Not unit-drivable: a successful full reconcile, because a worker cannot bind AF_XDP here. The cells model "live worker" as the registered record the accessor reads.

## PR #9787 — daemon: the fail-closed HA stop closes kernel transit before the detach [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9686-ha-stop-closes-transit`

Closes #9686

## Problem

On an HA node an orderly stop is non-hitless unless `hitless-restart` is set. That fail-closed branch of `runShutdownSequence`:
- clears `rg_active`;
- stops the subsystems;
- calls `rt.Teardown()`, which detaches every XDP program and removes the pins.

Nothing on that path lowered `net.ipv4.ip_forward` or `net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding`, or installed the #7191 transit barrier. The only writers of either are the transit-gate helpers. So the stop that is named fail-closed left the kernel routing any transit that still reached the node (surviving interface addresses, static/BGP or link-local next hops) with no policy, session or NAT, for the whole downtime and into the next start until re-arm.

## Fix

- **Close before detach.** Once `hitless` is decided, a non-hitless stop calls `markDataplaneNotArmed`, the transition bootstrap and `--no-dataplane` already use. It installs the barrier, writes both sysctls to 0, and drops the #7178 arm-track.
- **Placement.** It runs after `stop(); wg.Wait()`, so no reconcile goroutine can re-arm. It runs before the `rg_active` clear, the Kea stop, every blocking teardown, and `Teardown`.
- **Condition.** It keys on `hitless` alone, because forwarding can be open from an earlier arm with or without a published runtime.
- **Hitless stops** (standalone, or `hitless-restart`) keep the dataplane attached with the shim dropping transit, and leave forwarding untouched.
- **The #9035 order guard** now counts the transit close as a third fail-closed action, and `pkg/daemon/README.md` documents it.

## Validation

- **`TestFailClosedHAStopClosesTransitBeforeTheDetach9686`** drives the real `runShutdownSequence` with temp sysctls and a fake nftables installer. Its dataplane fake records what the sysctls and the barrier held at the moment `Close` or `Teardown` is called:
  - HA fail-closed: `Teardown` sees 0/0 and barrier `install`, and the node is recorded not armed;
  - HA `hitless-restart` and standalone: `Close` sees 1/1 and no barrier call;
  - the end state holds after the stop returns.
- **Test seams.** #6928 and #6787 drive the same non-hitless shutdown, so they now seam the sysctls and installer. Without the seams, those tests would write the host's `/proc` and program a real barrier; under `sudo make test-root` that would disable the test machine's forwarding.
- `go test ./pkg/daemon/`: 2652 passed, 0 failed. gofmt, go vet and the refactoraudit gate are clean.
- **Mutation matrix: 3/3 killed.**
  - close dropped;
  - condition inverted;
  - close moved to just after `Teardown`. The end state is still 0/0 with the barrier installed, so only the at-call witness catches it; it also reds the #9035 guard.
- **Lab (loss userspace cluster, one lock cell):** `make test-failover` 22 passed, 0 failed. Then an orderly stop of xpfd on the RG0 secondary:
  - armed: ip_forward=1 all.forwarding=1  barrier: inet-absent bridge-absent;
  - after `systemctl stop xpfd`: **ip_forward=0 all.forwarding=0  barrier: inet-present bridge-present**;
  - after restart it rejoined in 5s: node0=secondary node1=primary, and read ip_forward=1 all.forwarding=1  barrier: inet-absent bridge-absent.
  - The cell's final CoS re-apply printed FAILED because it targeted fw0, which was then the RG0 secondary and refuses commits. The post-deploy apply earlier in the same cell passed verification, and `show configuration class-of-service` still reads 51 set-lines on both nodes afterwards.

Docs: `pkg/daemon/README.md`, `docs/log/9686.md`.

- The `sync_auth.go` residual comment references #7441 and this change.

## PR #9790 — userspace: restart a helper that answers no status poll for 30s [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9651-wedged-helper-liveness`

Closes #9651

## Problem

Since #9172 (V031) the helper's control-socket accept loop retries resource errors, so transient fd or memory pressure no longer drops forwarding. The cost is a descriptor leak at `RLIMIT_NOFILE`: it leaves the helper alive and forwarding on its last applied state, with a control socket that accepts nothing (no config, status or session installs). There is no process exit for the #5838 supervisor to act on, and the daemon only logged a failed status poll.

The issue records three helper-side recovery designs that failed review. All of them rest on accept results or errnos, and those cannot tell a leak from recovering pressure.

## Fix

Take the Go-side liveness signal the issue recommends. The daemon already polls status every second, and the supervisor already owns fail-closed restart with a bounded backoff.

- **Counting.** `noteStatusPollResultLocked` counts consecutive status polls that got **no answer at all**. An answer resets the count, and so does an in-band refusal, because a refusal is an answer. So a helper under recovering pressure, which gets any poll through, is never restarted.
- **Threshold.** A helper is wedged after 30 unanswered polls **and** 30 s since the first. The count binds when polls fail slowly at their deadline; the span binds when they fail fast.
- **HA grace.** The kill waits out 10 s after an `update_ha_state`, so a failover's own control-socket load cannot become a restart mid-flight.
- **Recovery.** `killWedgedHelperLocked` SIGKILLs the helper, and recovery belongs to the supervisor: the unexpected-exit path disarms the shim, records the crash and restarts with its backoff. Nothing here restarts a helper itself.
- **Wiring.** `statusLoop`'s answered branch resets the count, and its failed branch feeds it and kills when asked. A RETH link cycle still skips the whole tick, so no poll is counted then.

## Validation

- **Cells** (`helper_liveness_9651_test.go`):
  - the kill, through the real supervisor: a crash is recorded for the killed pid, a restart is scheduled, and the node is not takeover-ready;
  - recovering pressure, as rounds of 29 failures each followed by an answer;
  - in-band refusals, which never count;
  - fast failures, bound by the span;
  - slow failures 3 s apart, bound by the count. At the real 1 s cadence the span always binds first, so an off-by-one in the count is otherwise invisible;
  - the RG grace;
  - a source cell binding `statusLoop`'s wiring.
- `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/`: 2443 passed, 0 failed. gofmt, go vet and the refactoraudit gate are clean.
- **Mutation matrix: 7/7 killed.** The mutants: refusal counted, span ignored, count off by one, RG grace ignored, kill omitted, answer does not reset, failed branch unwired.
- **Cluster regression gate** (one lock cell: deploy, CoS, `make test-failover`): **22 passed, 0 failed**, ledger row `4372c27d477ae4ed.json` (test-failover PASS, exe_check=MATCH). A deploy plus a hard failover and failback did not trip a restart.

Docs: `pkg/dataplane/README.md` (helper supervision section), `docs/log/9651.md`.

## PR #9794 — daemon: install #9641's colliding generations through SyncApply [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9495-9623-9624-ipsec-naming-land`

Closes #9623

- `make test`, both legs, is green on integration tree 497615830: origin/master 1231745de merged with the pairwise file-disjoint heads of #9495. Go: 78 packages ok, no FAIL lines. Rust: 5877 passed, 0 failed.

Closes #9624

Refs #9495 (measured here, not fixed; see below).

## Problem

The swanctl names xpf renders from an IPsec VPN name had two defects that this PR closes.

- **#9623: HA published a name strongSwan does not know.**
  - A VPN name reaches swanctl raw as the connection name, the child name of a selector-less VPN, and the prefix of every other child.
  - `GetSAStatus` display-sanitizes every SAStatus field (#6584), which escapes C1 control runes, U+2028/U+2029 and invalid UTF-8.
  - For such a name, `ActiveConnectionNames` published over HA SA sync, and `TerminateAllSAs` terminated, a different string than the one charon loaded. So on failover the peer's `--initiate`/`--terminate` matched nothing, and the tunnel was not re-initiated.
- **#9624: two VPNs could render the same swanctl SA name.** Examples: VPN `blue` with selector `red` (child `blue-red`) beside VPN `blue-red`, or `a`+`b-c` beside `a-b`+`c`. swanctl identifies a child SA by name alone, so it cannot tell such tunnels apart.

## Fix

- **#9623:** `validateIPsecSANamesDisplaySafeStrict` rejects a VPN name that is not `termsafe.DisplaySafe` at commit and commit-check, naming the VPN. The tolerant load and peer-sync path warns and keeps the VPN under its exact name.
  - `termsafe.DisplaySafe` is exactly the condition under which the display spelling equals the raw one.
  - A raw operational name in SAStatus was rejected as an option because it would reopen the #6584 terminal-injection class.
  - `TerminateAllSAs`' name selection is split into `terminateIKENames`, with behaviour unchanged, so the cells drive the real parse and sanitize pipeline.
- **#9624:** the pure name derivation moves into a new leaf package, `pkg/ipsecname`, imported by BOTH the renderer and the compile gate.
  - The package provides `SwanctlValue`, `ChildBase` and `Disambiguator` (moved verbatim), `ChildNames` and `SANames`.
  - `validateIPsecSANameCollisionsStrict` refuses a config in which two VPNs render one SA name, naming both. A tolerant load warns and keeps them.
  - Placement: a daemon commit pre-flight was rejected, because it would not run on `commit check` or `xpfd check-config`. The strict compile gate covers every commit path.
- **Fixtures.**
  - The #9511 attribution cells install their colliding configs through `Store.SyncApply` (`syncedStore9511`).
  - #9641's cells now do too (`syncApplyC1Plus9641`), for C1 and for the C2 built on it, because a commit re-validates the whole candidate.
  - Both helpers require the strict compile to fail on the #9624 collision and nothing else, so a tolerant apply cannot hide another fixture mistake.

## Not in this PR: #9495

#9495 (a VPN name carrying `{` `}` `#` `=` or a space breaks out of its swanctl section header) is **measured here, not fixed**. `docs/log/9495.md` records the measurement against the pinned strongSwan:
- a key written inside a VPN name reaches charon, measured on `mode`;
- an injected `updown` would be applied, which is inferred, not observed;
- a dotted selector name is a whole-file outage;
- `:` silently renames, and non-ASCII fails to load.

The #9623 gate rejects only non-display-safe names, and the #9624 gate only collisions, so none of those characters is refused yet. #9495 stays open for that gate.

## Validation

- **Cells:**
  - `TestIPsecVPNNameMustBeDisplaySafe9623` and `TestPublishedAndTerminatedSANamesMatchTheRenderOnlyWhenDisplaySafe9623`;
  - `TestIPsecSANameCollisionsFailCommit9624`, the `pkg/ipsecname` unit cells, and the drift guard `TestSANameDerivationMatchesTheRenderIndex9624`: the gate's derivation equals `BuildSANameIndex`'s names, owners and `Collisions()`;
  - the #9511 and #9641 attribution cells on their SyncApply fixtures.
- **A red that was fixed.** The branch's earlier full `make test` at 1e9a3171d failed on the #9511 fixtures (the gate is right, the fixtures predated it). That was fixed in 26a5dff59, and the #9641 follow-up in 4c68939b5.

## PR #9795 — cluster: age out generation tombstones oldest-first; keep delete generations above the stamp cap [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9719-gen-tombstone-eviction`

## Summary

Two arms of the `genGuardMapCap` safety valve (#2198 F1) were permanent rather than momentary.

- **Receiver.** An applied non-zero delete keeps its key as a tombstone (#2221) and never frees it. A long-lived connection churning closed sessions filled the map. After that, every NEW key was skip-recorded, and the #2170/#2221 ordering guards were off for every new session until the next bulk.
- **Sender.** Above the cap, a new key was not stamped, so its delete carried generation 0, which the receiver applies unconditionally.

## Change

- A FIFO tombstone order (`genTombstoneOrder`), under `recvGenMu`, records tombstoned keys oldest first.
  - An applied non-zero delete marks the key as the newest tombstone.
  - A re-install or a gen-0 delete forgets it.
  - `resetRecvGen` resets it along with the maps.
- Recording a NEW key at the cap first evicts the OLDEST tombstone (`putGenEvictingTombstones`).
  - A live entry is never evicted (#2198 F1).
  - Evicting the oldest tombstone re-opens only that key's reorder window.
- The sender latches a per-family overflow flag when a stamp is skipped. After that, `takeDeleteGen` draws a fresh generation for an unstamped key instead of 0. Before any overflow, the legacy 0 is unchanged.
- `GenTombstonesEvicted` counts evictions. The cap, guard and field docs and `pkg/cluster/README.md` are updated.
- No wire change.

## Validation

The code gates ran on `580ef8030`, #9719 stacked on #9717's pre-amend head. After #9717 landed, master was merged in. #9719's +/- lines against master are identical to its lines on `580ef8030`.

- [x] Mutation matrix on 580ef8030: 8/8 KILLED, each by its named cell.
  - Receiver mutants: no eviction on record; no tombstone marking; newest-first eviction; re-install or gen-0 delete keeping the tombstone.

## PR #9796 — docs: re-measure the steering number the re-steer kill rests on [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `docs/9488-steering-floor-remeasure`

Closes #9488

## What

`docs/fairness-regimes.md` justified "hardware steering does NOT beat the floor" with #1203/#789's measured 49–55% per-flow CoV at P=12. #9488 asked for three things:
- re-measure that at master, with an unsteered control;
- cite the new measurement in the doc;
- state #1748 R1's 16.8% → 3.8% and how to read it.

## Measurement

Build `e1cebdf8b` on `loss:xpf-userspace-fw0`, run as one `with-cluster.sh` lock cell.

**Setup**
- **Push:** 70 s `iperf3 -P 12 -p 5210` to queue 10 (`iperf-24g`, `24g exact`, so `shared_exact`). equal-flow-enforcement was not configured.
- **States:** three runs unsteered and three re-pinned, in alternating order.
- **Re-pin:** at t≈14 s, one exact-5-tuple `ethtool -N ge-0-0-1` rule per established socket, `action <i mod 6>`. This is R1's recipe.

**Results over t45–70**

| state | per-flow CoV (9 windows) | `xpf_fairness_cstruct` | aggregate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| unsteered | 41.5–55.4%, mean 47.2% | 0.447–0.601 | 22.05–22.74 G |
| re-pinned `[2,2,2,2,2,2]` | 6.7–13.9%, mean 9.7% | 0.000 | 22.64–22.80 G |

- Moving all 12 flows at once cost 2681 / 2851 / 4770 retransmits. All of them fell in the 1 s intervals t14–16, while the 13 rules went in; at most 3 occurred in the rest of each run.
- After every re-pinned run, the running NIC was confirmed restored: 0 rules, ntuple off.
- Every run is in `docs/log/9488.md`, with per-worker flow counts.

## Outcome

Re-placing established flows beats `Cstruct + ε` at HEAD, so the doc's empirical half no longer holds.

Acceptance item 3 asks for the architectural question to be filed as its own issue: is moving an established flow safe under AF_XDP per-queue UMEM ownership? It is filed as #9778, with this measurement attached. Nothing here reopens #1748 or #1751, and the doc keeps #1765's verdict standing until #9778 answers.

## The issue's premise did not hold

#9488 treated #1203's number as confounded, repeating #1203's own final comment: flow-fair MQFQ gated off for `shared_exact`, plus 1024 flow buckets.

The code #1203 actually ran was PR head `979482dff` (merge-base `38881341c`). It already had:
- `queue.flow_fair = queue.exact`, since `2a20cc8a0` (#785 Phase 3);
- `COS_FLOW_FAIR_BUCKETS = 4096`, since `891f07525`.

The gate that comment cited survived only in a stale doc comment in `types/cos.rs`, which `0b10d25f3` later scrubbed. So the doc does not repeat the attribution. It says why that controller stayed at 49–55% was never established. `docs/log/9488.md` records the probes and their positive controls.
