## PR #9860 — host-inbound: state the reinject-path residual #9637's lab measured [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-11)

Branch: `fix/9637-host-inbound-ingress-zone`

## Summary

Junos admits host-inbound traffic by the zone of the interface it arrives on. The kernel `xpf_hostinbound` chain judged it by the zone that owns the destination address (#9637), which went wrong in both directions:
- **exposure:** a client on a zone that denies ssh reached ssh on another zone's address;
- **over-refusal:** a zone that admits ssh was refused on another zone's address. This was measured live: from `lan`, TCP/22 to the `wan` and `sfmix` addresses timed out while ping answered.

- **Ingress-zone rules come first.** Per view and family, the chain now emits `iifname <view netdevs> <fam> daddr <every judged address>` for each of the view's service accepts, then the zone's counted drop.
  - They sit ahead of the unchanged destination-address rules, which still judge every netdev no view claims.
  - Both rule sets judge the same destination addresses, so no packet reaches the accept policy that did not before.
  - An incomplete netdev enumeration therefore costs coverage, never admission. That was the objection that deferred #3718 Option A.
  - The text oracle and the netlink mirror emit them rule for rule, and the counter pre-pass covers them.
- **Which netdevs a view claims** (`hostInboundViewIngressNetdevs`): its own unit rows' netdevs, by the snapshot `LinuxName`, so a RETH unit resolves to its member netdev. It excludes:
  - trunk parents;
  - netdevs claimed by two views;
  - lifelines;
  - l3mdev-enslaved netdevs (#6619, new `config.HostInboundVRFEnslavedNetdevs`).
  
  Scopes are per view rather than per zone, because #3362 overrides split a zone.
- **Smoke.** `test-host-inbound` probes from the LAN host, so every probe arrives on `lan`. It now scores ssh ADMIT at the `wan` VLAN sub-units too, and asserts `lan` owns `reth1.0`. It used to assert the over-refusal.
- **Docs.** `docs/host-inbound-service-matrix.md` gains "Ingress-zone judgement (#9637)". It also rewrites the destination-only statements (#7284, #5699, #3718, #6936 matrix) and marks #3718 Option A delivered for claimed netdevs.

## Residual (measured, not closed here)

The over-refusal remains for destinations owned by interface-mode source NAT.
- The XDP shim reports those as non-local (#290), so the SYN goes to the userspace dataplane.
- The userspace dataplane applies its ingress-zone check and reinjects the SYN through `xpf-usp0`.
- The kernel chain sees `iifname xpf-usp0` and judges the SYN by the address owner.

On the loss cluster, where `lan-to-wan` is `source-nat interface`, LAN ssh to the wan addresses is still refused (a capture showed those SYNs on `xpf-usp0`).

The exposure direction is closed on the direct path, which was measured. #9637 stays open for the reinject path.

## Validation

- `go test` for pkg/daemon, pkg/dataplane/userspace, pkg/config and pkg/nftables: 14624 passed, 0 failed.
- `TestHostInboundIngressZoneVerdictsOnRealKernel9637` re-executes the test binary under `unshare -rn`. Three client namespaces reach a port-22 listener through the rendered ruleset:
  - the destination-only ruleset reproduces the exposure and the over-refusal;
  - the ingress-scoped ruleset inverts both;
  - a netdev no view claims is still judged by destination.
- T1 parity (`TestNftNetlinkParity`) gives `IngressNetdevs` to every rendering branch. The resolver cells cover the unit-row claim, override views, trunk parent, VRF member, lifeline and shared claim.
- `TestHostInboundFilterNoStanzaDefaultDeny` is re-pinned from "no accept names lan's address" to #3405's actual subject: nothing arriving on lan is accepted, and lan's ingress drop exists.
- Mutation matrix: 15/15 killed (`docs/log/9637.md`).
- gofmt, go vet and the refactoraudit gate are clean.
- Lab (loss userspace cluster): head `3434c155a` was deployed to both nodes, and the probes and both smokes ran inside ONE lock cell.
  - **Exposure closed:** a WAN VLAN 80 client routed through the firewall sent TCP/22 to the LAN VIP `10.0.61.1`. Before the deploy it was REFUSED (admitted); after, TIMEOUT (dropped). Ping answered both times.
  - **Residual unchanged:** from the LAN host, TCP/22 to `172.16.50.8` / `172.16.80.8` timed out before and after (see Residual). The LAN VIP stayed admitted.
  - fw0 rendered 16 ingress-zone rules.

  - `make test-host-inbound-failover`: **69 passed, 0 failed**, and the matrix was identical at baseline and after failback (18 cells).

## PR #9863 — daemon: bind a fabric overlay created outside an apply into vrf-mgmt [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-12)

Branch: `fix/9813-fabric-overlay-vrf-rebind`

## Summary

A fabric overlay (`fab0`/`fab1`) carries the session-sync address, and session sync binds its sockets to `vrf-mgmt`, so the overlay must be a member of that VRF. Only the apply bound it: step 0b before networkd, and the authoritative step-2.7 re-bind after it.

Two paths create an overlay outside an apply, and neither sets a master:
- the #6791 re-assert loop, through `ensureFabricIPVLAN`;
- the deferred `OnXSKBound` callback, which can run after step 2.7.

An overlay can also lose its master without being re-created, for example through an out-of-band `ip link set nomaster`. Session sync over that fabric then stayed down until the next apply of any kind. On master, a probe in a private netns showed the re-created `fab0` at master index 0 while `vrf-mgmt` was at index 6.

## Change

- After its ensure step, the re-assert pass binds every configured overlay that the last apply published in the management-VRF set but whose master is not `vrf-mgmt`.
  - Its cheap gate counts such an overlay, so an overlay that is up but unbound gets bound without being re-created.
- `createDeferredFabricOverlays`, which is now the `OnXSKBound` callback, binds each overlay it creates.
- Nothing is bound when the last apply did not manage `vrf-mgmt`.
- The tenant routing-instance half of this issue follows as a second PR from this lane. That is why this PR references #9813 rather than closing it.
- Docs: `pkg/daemon/README.md`, `docs/log/9813.md`.

    - an overlay already in the VRF is left alone;
    - nothing is bound outside the published set;
    - the deferred creation binds;
    - an AST pin checks that the callback is the binding creator.
  - A kernel cell runs in a private netns (`unshare -rn`) and covers both the re-create and an out-of-band nomaster. It skips without `CAP_NET_ADMIN`.

## PR #9865 — config: match group zone statements by the zone they name, and apply `<*>` groups to leaf zones [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-12)

Branch: `fix/9801-9831-group-merge-named-leaf`

Closes #9801
Closes #9831

## Defects

Both are in group expansion (`mergeNodes`, `pkg/config/ast_groups.go`). Both drop zone content from configurations that strict commit accepts.

**#9831: a group's leaf zone is dropped by any inline leaf zone.** The leaf branch found its inline peer with `leafListPeer`, which matches on the keyword alone. Measured at master:

| Configuration | Compiled zones |
|---|---|
| group `security-zone zga;` + inline `security-zone trust;` | `[trust]` |
| group `security-zone [ zga zgb ];` + inline `security-zone trust;` | `[trust]` |
| group `security-zone [ zga zgb ];` + inline `security-zone zga;` | `[zga]` |
| group `security-zone zga;` + inline `security-zone trust { tcp-rst; }` (control) | `[trust zga]` |

**#9801: a `<*>` group is not applied to a zone written as a leaf.** The wildcard branch visited only destinations with `!d.IsLeaf`. With `security-zone <*> { screen edge; }` applied, `security-zone trust;` compiled `ScreenProfile=""`, while `security-zone trust { }` compiled `"edge"`. `tcp-rst` behaved the same way.

## Change

The helpers are in the new `pkg/config/group_merge_zone_leaf_9801.go`, called from two sites in `ast_groups.go`. Both rules apply only to `security-zone` statements directly under `security zones`.

- **Identity (#9831).** A group zone statement's inline peer is the statement naming the same zone (`zoneGroupLeafPeer9831`).
  - A different zone is adopted.
  - The same zone keeps the #7648 expansion and the inline-wins override.
- **Keys past the zone name.** A group zone statement carrying extra keys, such as `security-zone [ zga zgb ];` or a mistyped `security-zone trust scren edge;`, is not overridden by that zone's inline statement, because the override would drop the extra keys.
  - A braced zone takes a packed statement through #7648.
  - Otherwise the statement is adopted, as master adopted it beside a braced zone.
  - #9656 then judges it exactly as it judges the same text written inline. Duplicate zone statements compile as one zone (#4818).
- **Wildcard (#9801).** A two-key `security-zone` leaf takes the wildcard merge and becomes the container its braced spelling is (`zoneLeafTakesWildcard9801`). Interfaces and routing instances are left alone: written as a leaf, they compile no instance at all (#9838).

**Why zones only.** Earlier heads of this branch matched every schema container with instance args by identity. Two Codex rounds found that rule wrong for other schema families:
- **Round 1:** a value list matched by its first member compiled a duplicate next hop.
- **Round 2:**
  - `multi` named containers such as CoS `schedulers`;
  - compiler-canonicalised keys: `ospf area 0` beside `area 0.0.0.0` compiled two areas.

Both rounds traced to one mechanism, so the generic classifier was removed rather than patched again. Other named instances keep master's keyword override. That class, with the measured constraints, is #9859.

## After

| Configuration | Master | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| group `zga;` + inline leaf `trust;` | `[trust]` | `[trust zga]` |
| group `[ zga zgb ];` + inline leaf `trust;` | commits `[trust]` | refused by #9656: `only zone "zga" compiles, and "zgb" is dropped` |
| group `[ zga zgb ];` + inline leaf `zga;` | commits `[zga]` | refused by #9656 |
| group `[ zga zgb ];` + inline `zga { tcp-rst; }` | refused by #9656 | refused by #9656 |
| group `trust scren edge;` + inline leaf `trust;` | commits, typo dropped | refused by #9656 |
| group `trust apply-macro M;` + inline leaf `trust;` | commits | commits |
| `<*> { screen edge; }` + `security-zone trust;` | no screen | `edge` |

*(truncated — 135 lines total)*

## PR #9867 — host-inbound: enforce the fine junos-host program as a first-match subchain [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-12)

Branch: `fix/9504-host-deny-shapes`

## Summary

#9504: a fine `to-zone junos-host` policy whose shape the kernel projection could not render left the WHOLE ingress zone unenforced on the direct host-bound path — including the canonical management ACL (`permit <mgmt-net> junos-ssh;` then `deny any;`), because a permit could be projected only as a `saddr !=` subtraction of later denies and a narrow-application permit cannot be expressed that way.

**Measured first, and it changed the fix.** The issue rates a restricted PERMIT with no following deny as a gap where "the coarse gate admits and the fine policy denies". It does not: `evaluate_junos_host_policy_l3_aware` (policy.rs) and `policymatch.matchJunosHost` both DELIVER on no match — xpf applies no implicit junos-host default-deny on any path, by design, as the management lifeline. So that half is unenforced on the userspace path too, and the old warning claiming it "is enforced only on the userspace AF_XDP local-delivery path" was false for it. The rows where the kernel really diverged from xpf's own runtime are `then reject`, a deny on a `tcp-rst` zone, and any deny sitting behind a permit the subtraction model could not carry.

- **First-match subchain.** Each ingress zone's program renders into its own nft chain entered by an `iifname`-scoped `jump`: `deny` → drop, `deny` on a `tcp-rst` zone → TCP RST then drop, `reject` → TCP RST / ICMP administratively prohibited, `permit` → `return`. The chain's end returns, matching the runtime's deliver-on-no-match. A `return` is not an `accept`, so the coarse host-inbound gate stays the sole admit authority.
- **Verdicts mirror the runtime** (`enqueue_deny_reply` / `enqueue_policy_reject_reply`, reject_reply.rs) rather than coarsening every class to a silent drop.
- **Every rule carries `meta nfproto`.** With first-match order a family-less IPv4 rule could match an IPv6 packet ahead of that packet's own earlier term. Under the old DROP-only model family bleed changed no verdict, so nothing covered it.
- **Set subtraction, the poison sentinel and `PermitSubtract` are gone.** Suppression now covers `reject`; a permit is still never suppressed, and its warning says what is actually true, with the remedy (an explicit `then deny`, which the kernel now enforces).
- **Remaining un-representable:** feed-tainted source or destination, mixed direct+term or ALG applications, an application scoped to an IPsec/ident exempt tuple, and scheduler-gated policies. Each keeps both halves: no kernel rule AND a commit warning.

## Validation

- `go test ./pkg/config/ ./pkg/daemon/ ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ ./pkg/nftables/`: 14700 passed, 0 failed.
- **The T1 netlink-parity gate RAN** (`TestNftNetlinkParity`, not skipped): the netlink installer's chains, jumps, returns and rejects are bit-equivalent to the exec-`nft` oracle, loaded into a private netns.
- Mutation matrix: 17/17 killed (`docs/log/9504.md`), including the issue's decisive check — every remaining `representable = false` site mutated one at a time, to prove no class is silent.
- gofmt, go vet and the refactoraudit gate are clean.

Docs: `docs/host-inbound-service-matrix.md` (the §4146 contract: the first-match model, the representable subset, the remainder, and the no-implicit-default-deny semantics), `docs/log/9504.md`.


- `make test`, both legs, is green on integration tree a073d09d3: origin/master f6f026c13 merged with the pairwise file-disjoint heads of #9504. Go: 78 packages ok, no FAIL lines. Rust: 8373 passed, 0 failed.

Closes #9504

## PR #9868 — tooling: refuse a negated close keyword in commit messages and PR bodies [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-12)

Branch: `fix/9551-close-keyword-lint-nowf`

## Summary

A negated close keyword still closes the issue. GitHub honours `KEYWORD #N` wherever it appears, so a sentence that disclaims the link — or a scope heading above it — closes the issue anyway. It had already done that twice in this repo, and nothing checked for it.

- **`scripts/close_keyword_lint.py`** — a deliberate superset of GitHub's documented grammar (all nine keywords, `OWNER/REPO#N`, the URL form, optional whitespace around the colon), with emphasis and code-span markers stripped first so `**fix** #N` is still seen as a pair. It refuses a pair whose own clause carries a negation cue, or that sits under a scoping heading, and names the safe spellings at the point of refusal.
  - The clause ends at a line break, a table pipe, or `.!?;` plus whitespace. Commas deliberately do NOT end it, and a cell pins the price of that: `is not cosmetic, it fixes #N` is refused.
- **`scripts/close_keyword_lint_ci.sh`** — both pull-request legs (the body, and the commit messages in a range) in the one place a CI job and the selftest both call. The verdict is the worse of the two, so "the lint could not read its input" outranks a refusal, and the body arrives through the environment, never interpolated into a command line.
- **`scripts/git-hooks/commit-msg`** plus an installer — catches it before the commit exists. The hook fails OPEN in a worktree that predates the lint, and the installer honours `core.hooksPath` and refuses to replace a different hook.
- **`make close-keyword-lint`**, **`make install-git-hooks`**, **`make test-close-keyword-lint-lib`**, and a `run-selftests.sh` leg.

## What is NOT in this PR, and why

**The GitHub Actions job.** Pushing `.github/workflows/close-keyword-lint.yml` needs an OAuth token with `workflow` scope; this one has `gist, read:org, repo`, and the remote rejects the push. The file is withheld rather than routed around, and **every sentence that would have described that job as running is corrected** — the lint's own docstring, the Makefile comment, and `docs/engineering-style.md` now say plainly that nothing checks a PR *body* automatically yet.

So until it lands, a PR body is only checked when someone runs `make close-keyword-lint PR=<n>`. The commit path is covered by the hook and by `make close-keyword-lint`.

**The unblock is one command by the repository owner:** `gh auth refresh -h github.com -s workflow`. #9551 stays open for that half.

## Validation

- `make test-close-keyword-lint-lib`: **57 cells**, OK. Every negation cue and every heading cue has a cell in which it is the only cue; the accept rows are the controls for each clause boundary. Temp repos strip `GIT_*`, so no cell can commit into the real repository.
- Mutation matrix (`scripts/mutate-9551.py`): **42/42 KILLED by their expected cell; not clean: []**, each mutant killed by its expected cell.
- `make selftest`: **180 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed** — run at the pre-cut head `683c39674` (the same tree plus the withheld workflow file). The cut removed no selftest leg: `run-selftests.sh` calls `close_keyword_lint_ci.sh`, which is unchanged. `make harness-census`: pass, on this head. The lint over this branch's own commit: 1 source checked, 0 refused.
- **This branch changes no Go or Rust file** (`git diff origin/master -- '*.go' '*.rs' go.mod go.sum 'Cargo.*'` is empty), so the Go and Rust suites are master's own. A full `make test` was run at the pre-cut head anyway and passed (78 Go packages ok, 0 Rust failures), which covers the Makefile wiring.

Refs #9551

## PR #9869 — cluster: judge the stale-session reconcile only by mapped zones [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-12)

Branch: `fix/9655-zone-snapshot-rg0-fallback`

## Summary

At BulkEnd, `reconcileStaleSessions` deletes a session absent from the peer's authoritative bulk, but only in a zone this node does not own. It judges ownership by a `zoneOwnershipSnapshot` taken when the bulk started, and that snapshot had two defects. This PR fixes those. It deliberately does NOT ship the issue's headline.

## What ships

- **A map changed mid-bulk no longer judges by stale answers.** `SetZoneRGMap` bumps a generation only when the map's CONTENTS change, and the reconcile skips a bulk whose snapshot came from an older generation — the old answers could delete a session in a zone that has since moved to this node. An identical map re-set by a config apply is not a change, so a commit during a bulk does not cost it its reconcile.
- **A snapshot naming no zone judges nothing.** Both shapes now take no snapshot: a map never installed (ownership not wired yet) and a map installed naming no zone. The bulk deletes nothing and the next one tries again.
- **A zone the map does not name is kept whole.**

## What is withheld, and why

The live sweep answers an RG-unmapped zone with RG 0 ownership (`IsPrimaryFn`), and answering the reconcile the same way would finally delete a stale peer-owned session there on the RG 0 secondary — the issue's headline. Measured against the code, that is the worse trade:

- `buildZoneRGMap` maps a zone only through RETH interfaces, so a zone of node-local (non-RETH) dataplane interfaces is RG-unmapped too, and no cluster-mode commit rule rejects one.
- On the RG 0 secondary that answer deletes that node's OWN live flows in such a zone at every bulk, and a TCP flow dies on its next non-SYN packet.
- Sessions carry no origin flag that tells a local flow from a stale synced copy.

Deleting only the SYNCED copy needs a per-session origin bit, which rides the one `session_value`/HA-wire prerequisite covering pair identity (#9604), `route_table_id` (#9752) and the origin bit. This issue stays open for that half rather than growing a wire change here, and a comment on it records the dependency.

## Validation

- [x] 4 cells: an unmapped zone's session survives on either node, with controls proving the fixture still reconciles the mapped peer-owned zone and keeps this node's own RG 1 session; a zone map naming no zone skips, as subtests for installed-empty and never-installed; a map whose contents changed mid-bulk skips while an identical re-set map does not.
- [x] Master's `TestReconcileSkipsNonEmptyBulkWithoutZoneSnapshot` guard stays green.
- [x] Mutation matrix on 2afb2dd99: 8/8 KILLED, each by its named cell. Z1 and Z2 are the mutants that would reintroduce deleting in an unmapped zone.
- [x] `go test -race ./pkg/cluster` on 2afb2dd99: exit 0, no data race.
- [x] `make test` (Go + Rust) on 2afb2dd99: exit 0. Go 78 packages ok; Rust 8373 passed, 0 failed. It ran with `GOFLAGS=-p=4 CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4`, to keep peak memory down on the shared host.

## PR #9870 — dataplane: plan the interface MTU for a tagged-only VLAN parent [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-12)

Branch: `fix/9761-parent-mtu-tagged-units`

Closes #9761

## Defect

`planPhysDesired` (`pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface_desired.go`) is the single planner for a physical netdev's MTU write (#8119/#8120). It skipped every tagged zone reference before it read the interface-level `mtu`.

So a `vlan-tagging` interface whose zone references are all tagged units got no plan. The loss cluster's `reth0`, with units 50 and 80, is one. Its interface-level `mtu` was never written. The issue measured `set interfaces reth0 mtu 1400` leaving the RETH member `ge-0-0-2` at 1500.

## Fix

- **What a tagged reference plans.** Only the interface-level `mtu`, on its parent, and only when one is set. Its addresses, DHCP and unit MTU belong to its VLAN sub-interface.
- **What stays the same.**
  - An untagged unit's MTU still overrides the interface level.
  - A tagged-only parent with no interface-level `mtu` still gets no plan.
  - Two tagged references plan nothing, as on master, because another component owns the MTU of the device they resolve to. A fabric interface resolves to the local fabric member, whose MTU the fabric setup owns. A per-unit tunnel resolves to its tunnel device, whose MTU the tunnel manager owns, even when a WireGuard unit shares the interface's own device (#6941).
- **No actuation change.**
  - `mapZoneInterface` already runs its per-phys setup, including the one MTU write, for tagged references, with the parent as the resolved netdev.
  - It reconciles addresses only for untagged references, so a plan made from tagged references cannot touch the parent's addresses.
  - A RETH resolves to the node's local member, so each node writes its own member link.

**Not changed here:**
- A VLAN child's unit MTU can be written before its parent's MTU in the same apply, and when it is, a commit that raises both converges on the next commit. That order predates this change for interfaces with an untagged unit plus tagged units, and this change exposes it for tagged-only ones. Review rounds 2 to 5 tried two ways to reorder the writes, and each broke something else. #9845 (LOW) records the constraints.
- A unit MTU above its interface-level MTU still commits clean (#9837, LOW).
- A failed or unreadable MTU is only logged (#9841, LOW).

## Tests

## PR #9871 — config: route a group container to every same-keyed stanza, and drop a wildcard it cannot match [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-12)

Branch: `fix/9802-group-container-wildcard-adoption`

Closes #9802

## Defect

Both halves are in the container branch of `mergeNodes` (`pkg/config/ast_groups.go`). Measured at master `ef390f3ac`, and identically at `ad2ba883a`, so the #9801/#9831 landing changes no row. Strict commit accepted every row.

The group is `groups { G { security { zones { security-zone <*> { tcp-rst; } } } } }`, applied with a top-level `apply-groups G;`.

| Row | Configuration | Compiled at master |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | the target `security` has no `zones` | a zone literally named `<*>` |
| P3 | screen stanza first, zones stanza second | `[<*>(rst=true), trust(rst=false)]` |
| P4 | the group carries `security-zone zg { }` and `<*>`; target has no zones | `[<*>(rst=true), zg(rst=false)]` |
| P5 | an `interfaces <*>` group; target has no `interfaces` | an interface literally named `<*>` |
| P6 | two `interfaces` stanzas | only the first stanza's interface |
| P7 | two `zones` blocks in one `security` | only the first block's zone |
| P9 | as P3, with the zone written as a leaf | `[<*>(rst=true), trust(rst=false)]` |
| P2 | zones stanza first (control) | `trust(rst=true)`: correct |
| P8 | target has `zones { }`, empty (control) | nothing adopted |

- **The phantom is #9423's, reached by a route its fixtures cannot take.** Those fixtures all place the parent container in the target, so the wildcard reaches the wildcard branch and "applies nothing, invents nothing". With the parent container absent, the group container is appended wholesale and never recursed into, so the wildcard never reaches that branch at all.
- **The first-stanza merge loses the group.** Split stanzas are a supported spelling: #5691, fixed by #5741, made the AST pre-passes aggregate across all roots, and the compiler unions them.

## Change

New helpers in `pkg/config/group_container_wildcard_9802.go`, with two edits to the container branch.

- **Prune.** A wildcard-keyed node in an adopted subtree matched nothing by construction, so it is dropped before the #6767 charge, and a container whose whole body was wildcard-keyed is not adopted at all.
- **Prune scope, measured.** The discriminator is the node's SHAPE, not the schema. A zone's `interfaces` member slot is declared as a wildcard child WITH children, exactly like a dynamic instance name, so a schema-shape predicate also pruned `interfaces { <ge-*>; }` inside an adopted zone and turned its strict refusal into a clean commit.
  - Only a wildcard container, or a wildcard leaf carrying an instance name (two or more keys), is dropped.
  - A single-key wildcard leaf is a MEMBER and stays refused by the compiler's interface-reference check (#9423).
- **Routing.** `splitWildcardChildren9802` divides a group body: wildcard-keyed children go to every same-keyed destination container (`sameKeyedContainers9802`), one clone each, charged as the wildcard branch charges its fan-out; the rest go to `receivingContainer9802`, the first destination already holding a match for one of them, else the first, as before.
  - Splitting is what keeps a concrete block from being duplicated across stanzas.
  - A level spread over two blocks is one level, the rule `siblingsExcludeGroup` already applies to `apply-groups-except` (#9422).

## After

| Row | Master | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | zone named `<*>` | no zone, and no empty `zones` stanza |
| P3, P9 | `[<*>, trust(rst=false)]` | `trust(rst=true)` |
| P4 | `[<*>, zg]` | `zg` |
| P5 | interface named `<*>` | no interface |
| P6 | first stanza only | both interfaces |
| P7 | first block only | both zones |
| P2, P8 | unchanged | unchanged |
| `interfaces { <ge-*>; }` inside an adopted zone | refused, naming the token | refused, naming the token |

## PR #9910 — make: run Miri over a registered subset, and census the claims about it [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-12)

Branch: `fix/9499-miri-gate`

Closes #9499.

`make test-rust` already makes an integer WRAP an executed failure — that was
member 1, landed in #9833. This is member 2: **UB**. Nothing in the tree ran
Miri, and four comments said otherwise.

## The finding, restated precisely

The defect was never "Miri would find something". It was that four in-tree
comments asserted Miri coverage while **no make target ran Miri at all**:

- `frame/mod.rs` — "the deterministic example tests keep miri coverage of the same fns"
- `frame/README.md` — the same sentence, plus the `prop_tests/` table row
- `frame/prop_tests/inspect.rs` — "These also run under miri (no proptest loop)"
- `frame/tests_ttl_descriptor_dscp.rs` — "miri-coverable twin"

Each is accurate about the tests' SHAPE and false about the world. A reader
takes them as a protection that exists.

## A registered subset, because the measurement refused a whole-crate leg

| filter | result |
|---|---|
| `afxdp::types::cos::` | **12 passed, 0 failed**, 76 s, no unsupported operations (re-measured through the leg itself with isolation ON: 12 passed, 46.28 s) |
| `afxdp::frame::` | **stopped after 1021 s** — 94 tests passed, then `unsupported operation: open not available when isolation is enabled` |
| `queue_ops::` | **no result line** — still running at the 1800 s bound |
| `checksum::` | **no result line** — UNJUDGED, neither clean nor broken |

Three of four probed modules were not viable, so the leg is a named subset
(`userspace-dp/MIRI.registry`) with a floor per module, not a crate-wide run.
`cos` is the one that matters most on its merits: `FlowFairState::new_boxed`
writes `MaybeUninit` fields through raw pointers, and a missed field or a bad
drop target is invisible to every other gate in the tree.

**Isolation stays ON.** A module that needs `-Zmiri-disable-isolation` is
reading files in its tests, which makes it both a poor UB oracle and a slow
one. It belongs in `MIRI.unregistered` with that reason, not in the registry
behind a weakened flag.

## The scoring is the gate, not the exit status

`cargo miri test -- <filter>` that matches NOTHING prints
`0 passed; … N filtered out` and **exits 0**. A leg trusting the exit status
would report a clean run over a filter that matched nothing — the same defect
class this issue is about. `scripts/miri-leg.sh` judges the LOG, and five
states are FAILURES rather than skips: no `test result:` line, `0 passed`, a
count below the registered floor, any `failed > 0`, and an
`unsupported operation` (Miri refusing to execute is a VOID measurement, and a
VOID scoring clean is a coverage claim nobody made).

## PR #9926 — config: scope the #9802 wildcard prune, and route each group child independently [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-12)

Branch: `fix/9802-followup-prune-scope-and-routing`

Refs #9802. The merged change for that issue (PR #9871, merge 4cc9b66e6) introduced three regressions. This repairs them and pins each one with a cell that fails at 4cc9b66e6.

## What regressed, measured at ef390f3ac against 4cc9b66e6

| Configuration | Before #9802 | At 4cc9b66e6 | Here |
|---|---|---|---|
| `description "<*>"` inside a wholesale-adopted group container | kept | **dropped** | kept |
| compact zone member `interfaces <ge-*>;` | strict **refuses** | **commits clean** | refuses |
| block member `interfaces { <ge-*>; }` | refuses | refuses | refuses |
| group body with `screen` and `zones`, target splitting them across stanzas | `trust.ScreenProfile=edge` | **lost** | `edge` |
| group pair `from-zone trust to-zone untrust` beside a `to-zone dmz` stanza | one set `[qu,pg]` | **two sets, `pg` first** | one set `[qu,pg]` |

The second row is the serious one: a strict refusal naming the token became a clean commit. The last row changes policy evaluation order, since a second zone-pair set placed the group's policy first.

## Causes, both in the merged change

- **The prune keyed on node SHAPE** (`!IsLeaf || len(Keys) >= 2`). An ordinary two-key leaf matches that: a scalar whose value spells a wildcard, and a COMPACT member (`Keys=[interfaces, <ge-*>]`). Every cell I wrote used the BLOCK spelling, so the matrix could not see it — three placements of one spelling are not three spellings.
- **The routing bundled all concrete children** to a single receiving stanza, and a shared first key could capture a multi-key container.

## The fix

- The prune is schema-scoped: a wildcard-keyed **container**, or a wildcard inside the **identity span** (keyword plus args) of a child the schema declares as container-shaped. A scalar value and an args-0 member slot are excluded, so the compiler's own checks judge them as they judge the braced spelling (#9423).
- Each concrete child routes **independently**, preferring an exact key match over a shared first key.

## Validation

- **Positive controls.** Each new cell fails at 4cc9b66e6 with its own message: the scalar is dropped there, the compact member commits, `screen` is lost, and the policy pair compiles as two sets.
- **Suites.** `go test ./pkg/config/ ./pkg/configstore/`: 10388 tests, 0 failures.
- **Mutation matrix** at 797f46102: baseline clean (27 tests), 8 of 8 mutants killed, 0 VOID, 0 escaped.
  - Three cells were rewritten because the matrix showed they could not fail for their own mutant, which is the same fault that let the original regressions land. Two predicate clauses (`scalar`, an args floor) escaped as redundant and were deleted; the identity-span cell needed three fixtures before one was reachable, because `schemaAtAncestorPath` does not resolve through a wildcard hop and the #8662 normalizer folds a zone statement before the prune runs.
- **`make test`** (Go and Rust) on integration tree 3a88eeea5, as bounded foreground legs: race gates ok; `go vet ./...` clean; `go test ./...` 74 ok, 5 with no test files, 0 failures; uncached refactoraudit ok; `cargo check --benches` 0 errors; release cargo 5884 passed, 0 failed; debug filtered cargo 2489 passed, 0 failed.
- **Landcheck.** Master 2356b577d's delta has an empty intersection with these files, and the merged tree passes `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...`.
- **Codex.** The round that found these could not run again on this host; the findings it produced are recorded above with my own measurements, and every one was reproduced before acting.

## PR #9930 — api: gate deactivate, activate and annotate against deny-configuration regexes [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-12)

Branch: `fix/9890-rest-config-verbs`

Closes #9890.

A deny-configuration restriction was bypassable by choosing a different verb on
the same path — and the verb that bypasses it can **disable enforcement** rather
than merely edit it.

## What was wrong

`restConfigMutationRoutes` held exactly `POST /api/v1/config/set` and `/delete`.
These three are registered POST routes whose handlers mutate the candidate **by
path**, and none was in the gate:

| route | handler writes via |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/config/deactivate` (`server.go:799`) | `DeactivateFromInputAs` |
| `POST /api/v1/config/activate` (`:800`) | `ActivateFromInputAs` |
| `POST /api/v1/config/annotate` (`:813`) | `AnnotateAs` |

So a principal denied `set system root-authentication` reached the same subtree
with a different verb.

**`deactivate` is the one with teeth.** An inactive node is excluded from
compilation, so deactivating a denied subtree does not edit its contents — it
**removes its enforcement**, and the next legitimate commit by anyone ships that
removal.

**The omission was not a decision.** The route table's comment explains only why
`load`, `commit` and `rollback` are absent and never mentions these three, so a
reader checking whether the surface was complete found prose that looked
considered. Nothing had to be built either: the shared evaluator already knew all
three verbs — `configMutationVerbs` carries set, delete, deactivate, activate,
copy, rename, insert, annotate. They were simply not listed.

## Why a table row was not enough for `annotate`

Its handler reads `AnnotateRequest.Path`. The gate read `input`. A row alone
would have adjudicated an **empty string** and allowed everything *while looking
gated*.

Each route now declares **which body field carries its path**, the gate reads
that field and only that field, and an unrecognised field **fails closed**. A
fallback between fields would recreate the same silence one layer in — and that
is not hypothetical, it is the escape the matrix caught (below).

## The remedy is a census, because a hand-maintained list is what failed

`restConfigRoutesUngated` states, for every other registered POST config route,
why no regex is evaluated for it. `TestEveryConfigPostRouteIsGatedOrDeclared9890`
reads the registrations out of `server.go` and asserts every route appears in

## PR #9933 — config/networkd: refuse a leading-dash interface name, and end option parsing [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-12)

Branch: `fix/9885-iface-name-option`

Closes #9885.

`ValidateInterfaceName` is an allowlist over **characters**, and `-` is on it
because `ge-0-0-0` is the normal spelling. It has no notion of **position**, so a
name beginning with `-` passed every check and committed strict-clean.

That name then reaches an argv slot. `pkg/networkd` built
`networkctl reconfigure <names...>` with no separator, so a leading dash is read
as an **option**.

## The damaging case is the one that does not error

`--help` and `--version` **exit 0 without acting**. So ONE badly named interface
leaves EVERY interface in that batch unconfigured, while `Apply` reads success
and clears the #4954 retry debt. A name like `-x` would at least fail loudly —
which is why the harmless-looking name is the dangerous one.

## Both halves are fixed, because they fail independently

**The validator** gains a third actively-dangerous class beside whitespace and
glob metacharacters. It is the only one about **position** rather than about
which characters appear, so it sits outside the allowlist loop — no tightening
of that loop could ever have caught it. The message names the consequence, since
an operator told only that a character is disallowed will try a different one.

**`networkctl reconfigure` now carries `--`**, the same belt the repo already
applies to scp (#4589). This covers a name that predates the validator or
arrives from a path that does not run it.

**The separator was verified against the real tool rather than assumed.** On
systemd 261, `networkctl list -- lo` and `networkctl list lo` produce identical
output — so it is both accepted and inert. Asserting getopt behaviour would have
been a claim; running it is a measurement.

## The argv site was censused, not taken from the report

```
git grep -n 'runNetworkctl(\|"networkctl"' -- pkg/ | grep -v _test
```

**Exactly one** place puts interface names into argv (`networkd.go:567`). Every
other `runNetworkctl` call, and `pkg/daemon/linksetup.go:690`, passes the literal
`"reload"` and no names. A review enumerates what it noticed; the primitive
enumerates what exists.

| leading-dash refusal removed | `TestLeadingDashInterfaceNameIsRefused9885` |

## PR #9935 — userspace-dp/HA: a peer's delete must not tear down this node's live local session [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-12)

Branch: `fix/9714-dual-primary-peer-delete-ownership`

# #9714: a peer's delete must not tear down this node's live local session

Under a dual-primary split both nodes forward the same flows and each holds its copy
as a LOCAL session. A delete the peer sent reached the helper as an ordinary
`sync_session` delete and removed the shared rows, the steering row, the DNAT steering
hold and every sibling worker's replica.

Two hostile review rounds found the same root cause from opposite sides: **Go performs
key-only teardown around a helper decision it cannot make atomic** — round 1 found it
BEFORE the helper, round 2 AFTER. Per the "same root cause in 2+ rounds, remove the
mechanism" rule, the model is deleted rather than patched a third time.

## The through-line: silence read as assent

Three findings are the same defect at three layers, and this is the sentence a
reviewer needs:

- **Finding 1 (Go).** `sendSessionSyncBatchOutcomes` pre-filled `[]error` with nils and
  `break`ed on an unreachable helper, leaving the unsent tail at the zero value — which
  every caller read as "applied". A chunk is up to 256 requests, so one transport
  failure manufactured up to 255 phantom successes, and the peer batch then deleted 255
  BPF mirror rows for sessions the helper still holds.
- **Finding 7 (helper).** `delete_synced_session_gen_marked` returned a `bool` in which
  a stale-generation REJECTION and a successful APPLY were both `false`. Three outcomes
  squeezed into two states, and the two that merged are opposites.
- Both are **silence read as assent**: in one, `nil` was the zero value; in the other,
  `false` was the only other state.

The mirror does not heal. `refresh` writes with `BPF_EXIST` *specifically* so it will
not recreate a deleted entry, so a row deleted on a guess is gone until the session is
rebuilt. That is why the tri-state (`Applied` / refused / `errSessionSyncNotAttempted`)
is load-bearing rather than tidiness.

## What changed

- **Applied-set inversion (F1).** Teardown is driven by keys the helper EXPLICITLY
  applied, not by the complement of the refused set — a strictly larger set that also
  contains transport failures and never-sent requests.
- **One decision, taken before anything is mutated (F2, F4).** The handler resolves the
  complete candidate set without mutating, then performs exactly one delete or none.
  `bare` is now `resolved_domain.is_none()`, not `key.routing_domain == 0`: domain 0 is
  ALSO the default routing instance, and reading the flattened value as "unknown" sent
  an AUTHORITATIVE single-domain delete into the ambiguity probe — a guard refusing the
  very case it exists to permit. A marked delete with no shared authority now does
  nothing; "no shared entry" is not "no session", because the install path publishes to
  BPF before the shared map.
- **Validate and remove the SAME entry (F3).** `delete_synced_session_gen_marked` cloned
  the entry and released the lock in the same statement, then removed it much later —
  at `645cb8862`, the tree this fix was applied to, the clone is
  `session_import.rs:837` and the removal `:912`. **The window was literally those 75

## PR #9936 — daemon: read the IPsec SA publisher's cancel handle under its mutex in tests [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-12)

Branch: `fix/9844-ipsec-sa-sync-loopcancel-race`

Closes #9844

## Defect

`TestIPsecSASyncHotEnableStartsAndStops8967` read `d.ipsecSASync.loopCancel` with no lock.

Every production writer takes `loopMu` — `ensureIPsecSASyncLoop`, `stopIPsecSASyncLoop` and `clearIPsecSALoopIfCurrent` (`pkg/daemon/daemon_ipsec_sa_sync_loop.go`). The last of those runs on the **publisher's own goroutine as it exits**, so the synchronisation was correct on the writing side and simply absent on the reading side. Any lane's `go test -race ./pkg/daemon` could therefore go red on a file that lane had not touched — which is how this was found, in the `-race` gate for #9766/#9767.

## Fix

The cells read the handle through `ipsecSALoopCancelForTest`, which takes `loopMu`. The handle is only ever compared against `nil`, so reading it under the lock changes nothing any cell asserts; it just stops the read racing the write.

## Evidence

A positive control first, because a flake fix with no reproduction cannot be told apart from luck:

- **unmodified master, 200 runs** of the cell under `-race`: **1 DATA RACE** — write at `daemon_ipsec_sa_sync_loop.go:172` (`clearIPsecSALoopIfCurrent`) against the cell's unlocked read, the exact signature the issue reports;
- **unmodified master, 1000 runs**: **1 DATA RACE**. It reproduced in both campaigns, so the control is real and not a one-off;
- **with the fix, 1000 runs**: **0 races**; the sibling cell, 200 runs: **0 races**.

Reverting the accessor to a direct field read IS the mutation for this change, and the control above is that mutant: it races, the fix does not.

## Validation

- [x] `go test -race ./pkg/daemon/` (whole package): exit 0, 0 data races.
- [x] `make test` (Go + Rust): exit 0. Go 78 packages ok, no FAIL; Rust 22 `test result:` lines, 0 failed.

## PR #9958 — cluster: tell a barrier waiter why it woke, instead of inferring it [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-12)

Branch: `fix/9822-store-walk-fence-flake`

Closes #9822

## What the issue left open, and the answer

The issue recorded two unknowns: the failure rate and whether it depends on load, and **whether the fault is in the test or in the code under test**.

It is in the code, and it needs no load at all once the interleaving is named.

## Defect

`WaitForPeerBarrier` told a fence from a disconnect by comparing the fence epoch it captured at START against the epoch at wake-up: changed meant fenced, unchanged with no ack meant the connection went away.

Every caller of `noteStreamConnLocked` bumps the epoch **under `writeMu`**, releases `writeMu`, and only then calls `onStreamMoved`, which sweeps every pending waiter. All three do this — `sync_conn_write.go`, `sync_bulk.go` and `captureBarrierFenceForBulk` — and the split is deliberate, so the sweep does not run under `writeMu`.

So the sweep can land arbitrarily late. A barrier starting in that gap — admissible precisely because an ACKed re-prime discharged the fence — captures the **already-bumped** epoch. At wake-up it sees no epoch change, no ack, and reports `session sync disconnected during barrier wait` for a connection that never went away.

That is exactly what the issue observed: `TestAStoreWalkRePrimeDischargesTheFence_9508` failing at **seq=2**, the barrier after the re-prime, with the sweep's own `released_barrier_waiters=1` logged immediately before it.

**The misreport is not cosmetic.** The caller's remedy for a fenced barrier is to re-prime and retry; its remedy for a disconnect is not.

## Fix

`barrierWaiters` holds a `*barrierWaiter` carrying a `fenced` flag. `onStreamMoved` sets it under `barrierWaitMu` *before* closing the channel, and the woken barrier reads it under the same mutex, so the reason cannot race the wake-up. The waiter is **told** why it woke instead of inferring it.

`handleDisconnect` deliberately does **not** set the flag: that one IS a disconnect and should say so. The epoch comparison stays, because it still catches a move the waiter was registered before.

## Evidence

- **Deterministic reproduction on unmodified master**, no load required (`TestABarrierInsideTheStreamMoveWindowIsFencedNotDisconnected_9822`): bump the epoch as a write does, discharge the fence as an ACKed re-prime does, start a barrier, then run the deferred sweep. On master it fails with exactly `session sync disconnected during barrier wait seq=1`.
- **Mutation**: dropping the reported reason and inferring from the epoch alone — kept compilable, since a non-building mutant measures nothing — makes that cell FAIL; restoring the fix makes it pass.
- `TestAStoreWalkRePrimeDischargesTheFence_9508`, the cell the flake was reported against, and the rest of the #9508 suite: **20 consecutive runs**, clean.

## Validation

- [x] `go test ./pkg/cluster/` (whole package, 93.7s): exit 0.
- [x] `go test -race ./pkg/cluster/`: exit 0, 0 data races.
- [x] `make test` (Go + Rust): exit 0. Go 78 packages ok, no FAIL; Rust 22 `test result:` lines, 0 failed.
- [x] `go vet` and `gofmt`: clean.
- [x] **`make test-failover`** on local merge `a842102fe` (origin/master `773146dd4` + `e54e9a328`), parents verified, deployed under the cluster lock with CoS re-applied: **22 passed, 0 failed**, iperf3 **20.8 Gbps**, post-deploy reassert verified node0 primary for every RG. Ledger row `db01bcaa45eea2e7`: PASS, exe MATCH, `build_git_sha` = the gate merge. This gate is not optional here — the change is in session-sync barrier handling, which the HA smoke exercises.

## Docs

`docs/log/9822.md` records the interleaving, the fix and the runs. No module doc changed: the barrier contract is unchanged — a fenced barrier was always meant to report a fence, and this makes it do so — and the reasoning lives beside the `barrierWaiter` type.

## PR #9959 — userspace-dp: a shared steering row must outlive every session that still needs it [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-12)

Branch: `fix/9560-steering-row-owners`

# #9560: a shared steering row must outlive every session that still needs it

The steering map is shared: several sessions can occupy the same row, and aliasing makes
that ordinary rather than exceptional. Before this branch a teardown deleted the row it
named, unconditionally — so one session's delete removed a row another session was still
steering on, and the victim's packets fell to the non-owning RSS queues, where they are
adjudicated as new flows.

This adds an ownership registry (`SteeringRowOwners`): a row goes from the map when its
LAST owner releases it, and only then.

## The part worth reviewing: the mechanism was never the risk

A census from the table's own removal PRIMITIVE showed the mechanism sound — one
chokepoint, `delete_steering_row`, taking a `SteeringMap` and recording `owner_lock_held`
on every write. The matrix agreed: `R3`, which mutates the registry's own `retire_worker`,
is KILLED.

Then `R8` — which mutates that function's **call site** — SURVIVED, with `ALL_FAILED`
empty across 70 cells.

**The mechanism was covered and its production WIRINGS were not**, which is the failure
the registry itself cannot see. Four call sites were undefended. All four are now closed
with cells that kill their mutant by declared target.

### Three of the four already had correctly-named cells

This is the part that generalises past this issue, because a missing cell and a cell that
cannot fail look identical on a green board — and the second is worse, since it reads as
protection and stops anyone writing the real one.

- **R8** asserted that a LIVE worker's claim SURVIVES the sweep — a negative control with
  no positive case. It could not distinguish *correctly selective* from *does nothing at
  all*.
- **R10** passed `has_routing_domains=true`, which #9517 DEMOTES to redirect — so a cell
  named for the kernel-local publish never entered that branch.
- **R9** asserted `>= 1` claimed rows, true under both the entry-level publish and the
  key-level mutant, and drove the function through DIRECT calls that bypass the wiring.
  It tested the transform while the defect lived in the feed.

## Two dead observables, abandoned rather than tuned

Both of these are recorded because the instinct they defeat is a strong one: **a cell that
fails at base looks like a cell that needs strengthening.** Twice here it was not.

**R9.** Strengthening the row count to `> 1` FAILED AT BASE — a reverse entry-level
publish claims exactly one row, the same as a key-level publish. Row count cannot separate
those arms *by construction*, so no tightening could ever have killed the mutant. Replaced
with a cell on the RELEASE SEMANTICS: seed a predecessor holding a wider row set, then
assert the install released what its own decision does not name.

## PR #9961 — config: read authored quote/bracket provenance when splitting a packed run [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-12)

Branch: `fix/9635-authored-value-provenance`

Closes #9635

`security { ike { policy P1 { proposals [ P "proposal-set" ]; } } }` — a policy
referencing a proposal that happens to be *named* `proposal-set` — was refused at
commit with `proposal-set: missing value`, in the braced spelling as well as the
brace-elided one.

The packed splitter ended the multi-value statement at the first token naming a
sibling, producing `proposals P;` plus a bogus `proposal-set;`. The operator had
marked that token as a value three times over — quoted, and inside a `[ ... ]`
list — and neither the splitter nor the #8437 fusion gate read any of it.

## The rule

It is about the statement **before** the token, not the token alone.

An authored value may stay a value only where the preceding leaf can accept
another one: a `multi` or `valueList` leaf. A fixed-arity leaf is saturated past
its declared args, so `pre-shared-key ascii-text "s" "mode" aggressive;` keeps
splitting at the quoted `"mode"` — which is what Junos does, and what the earlier
attempt recorded on this issue regressed by declining *every* split whose
boundary landed on a quoted token.

Both readers ask the same question through the same helpers. Teaching only the
splitter leaves the fusion gate refusing what the splitter just kept whole —
measured, and the reason this is one change rather than two. A node with no
provenance recovers the previous behaviour exactly.

Both call sites already computed the masks; call site 2 even carried the comment
*"The split DECISION does not read them yet; that ... is issue 9635."*

## Measured

At `origin/master 773146dd4`:

| spelling | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `proposals [ P "proposal-set" ];` braced | REFUSED | commits, `Proposals=["P","proposal-set"]` |
| the same, brace-elided | REFUSED | commits, same |
| `pre-shared-key ascii-text "s" "mode" aggressive;` | two statements | two statements (unchanged) |
| `proposals P proposal-set;` (bare, a real missing `;`) | refused | refused (unchanged) |

## PR #9965 — config: normalize the clone `display inheritance` expands, as the commit does [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-12)

Branch: `fix/9743-inheritance-display-normalize`

Closes #9743

`show configuration | display inheritance` expanded groups on the **raw** tree,
while both compile cores normalize first (`compiler.go`, and `schema_walk.go` via
`normalizeCompactForValidation`). Since #9620 the #8662 normalizer rewrites a
brace-elided routing instance into its braced shape, and group expansion binds
against that shape — so the display omitted properties the commit applied.

## Measured

At `origin/master 766da5332`, one configuration written two ways:

```
groups { G { routing-instances { blue instance-type forwarding description inherited; } } }
apply-groups G;
routing-instances { blue { interface ge-0/0/0.0; } }
```

| group body | display shows `description inherited` | shows `instance-type forwarding` | compiled |
|---|---|---|---|
| elided | **no** | **no** | both present |
| braced | yes | yes | both present |

Both spellings commit identically; only the display differed. `instance-type
forwarding` decides whether the daemon creates a VRF at all, so the display was
wrong exactly where an operator checks what a group contributes.

## The change

Normalize the expansion clone in `FormatInheritance` **and**
`FormatPathInheritance` before `ExpandGroupsTagged`. The issue names the path
variant, and fixing only the first would have left the
`show configuration <path> | display inheritance` entry point defective.

The **clone** is normalized, never the caller's tree: these are read-only
operations on an operator's candidate and normalizing is a rewrite.
`cloneForExpansion` never aliases the caller.

## Cells

After the change the two spellings' displays are **byte-identical**, for both
entry points, so the cells claim equality rather than presence — they are one
configuration written two ways, and any rendering difference is the defect. A
separate cell holds the display against the **compiled** config, because matching
displays alone would be satisfied by breaking both in the same way.

## PR #9966 — config: adjudicate `load` and `rollback` on every surface, from one evaluator [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-12)

Branch: `fix/9892-load-regex`

Closes #9892.

A `*-configuration` regex is an authorization control over configuration
mutation, so a denied path must stay denied **whatever verb carries it**.
`load` is the verb that can carry every denied path at once — `load override`
replaces the whole candidate, and `load merge` can bring a whole denied subtree
in one call, up to 16 MiB on REST.

#9633 closed this on gRPC. REST and the CLI were still open.

## The CLI's gap was worse than absent

`cli_dispatch.go` **does** run `checkConfigRegex` on every config-mode line,
including `load`. It then delegates to `configMutationPath`, which returns
`ok=false` for any verb outside `configMutationVerbs` — and `load` is not in
that map. **The gate executed and declined to adjudicate.** Someone auditing
that path sees a gate on it, which is worse than seeing none.

It could not have done better there, either: **at dispatch time the content has
not been read yet.** Terminal input arrives only after the paste completes,
dozens of lines later, so the adjudication had to move to `handleLoad` where the
content is finally in hand.

## One evaluator, not three agreeing copies

#9633's implementation **moved** into `pkg/config` beside
`AuthorizeConfigMutation`, which it calls per line. The gRPC original is
**deleted**, not left alongside — `go vet` caught an unreachable remnant of it.

Two renderings of "hierarchical content as set lines" drift, and the drift is
invisible because each copy looks right on its own. Six call sites now, one
renderer:

| surface | load | rollback |
|---|---|---|
| gRPC | `authz_config_rpc_9633.go` | same |
| REST | `authz_config_regex_9154.go` | same |
| CLI | `cli_config.go` (inside `handleLoad`) | `cli_dispatch.go` |

## What is refused rather than adjudicated, and why

`load override` and `rollback n>0` replace the whole candidate, so the paths
they **delete** cannot be enumerated one by one. They are **refused** for a
restricted class, and the message says so — refusal is the honest answer and the
docs must not imply coverage. `rollback 0` returns to the committed
configuration, every path of which was adjudicated when it was written, and
stays available.

identical surfaces; #9633 already closed it on gRPC, and the REST route table's

## PR #9968 — userspace-dp: deny host-inbound on an unzoned tunnel's decap re-ingress [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-12)

Branch: `fix/9941-unzoned-tunnel-decap-host-inbound`

## What this fixes

A packet arriving inside a tunnel whose interface has **no security zone** and **no
addresses** was admitted to the routing engine's own addresses. The issue asked
whether that was reachable. It is, and the reproduction is in the suite.

## The reachability chain

Three independent behaviours have to line up, which is why this survived the
default-deny work of issue 3405:

1. A decap re-ingress rebuilds a logical packet for the inner header
   (`logical_ingress::build_logical_ingress_packet`, called from `gre.rs:923`
   and `wg/decap.rs:214`) and resolves the tunnel's zone with
   `ifindex_to_zone_id(...).unwrap_or_default()`. An unzoned tunnel therefore
   lands on **zone 0**, not on an error.
2. `host_inbound_admits` reads zone 0 as `None`, and `None => true`. Zone 0 is
   the "no zone information" case, and the admission predicate treats it as
   admit rather than deny.
3. The interface-keyed backstop from issue 5659 — which exists precisely to put
   a deny sentinel in `ifindex_host_inbound` for an interface that has an empty
   zone — was scoped to `registered_local` interfaces only. A tunnel is not
   registered local, so it never got a sentinel, and step 2's `None => true`
   was the final word.

Each step is defensible alone. The composition admits SSH from inside an
unzoned, unnumbered tunnel.

## The fix

`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding_build/interfaces.rs` widens the issue-5659
backstop's scope guard from `registered_local` to `registered_local || tunnel`:

```rust
if iface.zone.is_empty()
    && (registered_local || iface.tunnel)
    && !iface.host_inbound_configured
    && !is_host_inbound_lifeline(&iface.name)
{
    state.ifindex_host_inbound.entry(iface.ifindex).or_default();
}
```

`registered_local` was the right test for an ordinary interface and is the wrong
test for a tunnel: it asks "did this interface register the address we are
delivering to", and a decap re-ingress delivers to addresses that **other**
interfaces registered. The tunnel is the ingress, never the address owner, so
the flag is false for exactly the interfaces that need the sentinel most.

## PR #9969 — frr: state the vtysh funnel's real scope — buffered reads, with the stream exempt [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-12)

Branch: `fix/9755-stream-path-funnel-contract`

Closes #9755

`Manager.vtysh`'s comment claimed *"nothing in this package can reach vtysh
except through here"*. That was false for one path: `StreamBGPRoutes` calls the
executor's `VtyshStream` directly, so it takes no `diagcmd.VtyshLimiter` slot and
gets no 15 s `vtyshTimeout`, and the #9143 census had no row for it.
`pkg/diagcmd` stated the worst case as four children, and `pkg/frr/README.md`
said the same.

## Which contract, and why

Of the two the issue offers, this **keeps the exemption and makes it visible**
rather than routing the stream through the funnel.

A full-RIB stream is deliberately allowed a 10-minute progress budget, against
the funnel's 15 s. Making it hold one of four shared slots would let a single
slow reader occupy a quarter of the budget for **every** FRR status surface on
the box for ten minutes — trading a documentation inaccuracy for a real
availability regression.

A shared limiter would also imply a cross-surface bound that does not exist, and
that is `pkg/api`'s own stated reason for keeping `ribStreamLimiter` REST-local:
the gRPC and CLI `show route protocol bgp` paths call the **buffered**
`GetBGPRoutes`, which runs to completion before any client sees a byte and so
cannot be pinned by a slow reader. That rationale was already written at the call
site; reading it first is what stopped me from "fixing" the inconsistency in the
direction that breaks something.

## Censused before choosing

Every direct executor call in `pkg/frr`:

| call | status |
|---|---|
| `executor().Vtysh` | the funnel, bounded |
| `executor().VtyshStream` | **the only operational-read bypass** |
| `executor().FrrReloadPy`, `executor().VtyshLoad` | the apply path, already excluded for its own reason |

`StreamBGPRoutes` has exactly one production caller.

## Four sites stated the invariant, not three

The issue named three. A sweep after the first commit found a fourth:
`status_parse.go`'s own header said *"All vtysh shell-outs in this file go
through m.vtysh"* — in the very file that defines the exception. A claim repeated
in four places goes stale in four places.

All four now say **buffered**, name the exception, and state the real aggregate:
**four buffered plus two streaming children — six, not four.**

## Defect

`userspace-dp` statically links libxdp and libbpf. Nothing recorded which versions went into a binary, bounded them to a supported range, or checked the library behaviour the code relies on. The only guard was #4976's ring-struct layout asserts.

## What the binary actually links

A `-Wl,-Map` link trace corrects the issue's premise that both libraries come from the build host:
- **libbpf** originates in `libbpf-sys`, which vendors and builds version 1.6.3, pinned in `Cargo.lock`.
- **libxdp** originates on the build host (`/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libxdp.a`, 1.6.3).

But *which* archive satisfies each name was decided by SEARCH ORDER, from a bare `-lxdp` and `-lbpf`, and order is not a property this build controls. The same host directory also holds a static libxdp and a static **libbpf 1.7.0**, and a `cargo rustc --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- -Lnative=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu` puts it ahead of every build-script `-L`. Measured: under bare names that single flag makes the link take the host's libbpf 1.7.0 while the binary reports the vendored 1.6.3 — this issue's acceptance criterion, failing.

## Fix

The build no longer asks the linker to FIND either library. It copies both into one directory it owns and links them under names nothing else supplies.

- **libxdp version.**
  - `build.rs` reads it from pkg-config (or from the command `PKG_CONFIG` names) before anything else. A libxdp outside `>= 1.6.3, < 1.7` fails the build naming the version, instead of failing later in the C compile or for a missing `libxdp.a`.
  - `debian/control` declares the same range as build dependencies, and `make deb` runs `dpkg-buildpackage` without `-d`, so a host outside it is refused before the build starts.
- **libxdp archive: link what was validated, under a name only this build uses.** The C bridge compiles against pkg-config's includedir; `build.rs` copies pkg-config's `<libdir>/libxdp.a` into `OUT_DIR/xpf-linked-libxdp/` as **`libxpfxdp.a`** and links it as `static=xpfxdp`.
  - Copying rather than predicting fixes the check-then-link race: the script validates an archive and the LINK happens later, and Cargo decides whether to re-run a build script by MTIME, so a libxdp replaced by one carrying an older mtime would be linked under the previously recorded version.
  - The recorded version describes the copied bytes: the source is read, the snapshot written from those bytes, the version read and range-checked, then the source re-read and the build failed unless it still holds the copied bytes and reports the same version.
- **libbpf archive: the same, for the sibling.** `build.rs` copies `libbpf-sys`'s vendored `libbpf.a` (from `DEP_BPF_INCLUDE`'s parent) into the same directory as **`libxpfbpf.a`** and links `static=xpfbpf` **before** the bare `static=bpf` that `libbpf-sys` emits.
  - That order is load-bearing: libxdp's undefined libbpf symbols are resolved by the libbpf that follows it. With the snapshot ahead of it, the trailing bare `-lbpf` extracts no members at all.
  - No version/copy window is closed here, deliberately: the archive and the `libbpf_version.h` whose version is recorded are both outputs of the `libbpf-sys` build script in the same cargo invocation, inside a target directory Cargo locks.
- **What the unique names buy, and what they do not.**
  - Gone: ACCIDENTAL substitution. No system or SDK directory, no dependency `OUT_DIR` and no path in this repo holds a `libxpfxdp.a` or a `libxpfbpf.a`, so a `-L` from RUSTFLAGS, from `cargo rustc --`, from a rustc wrapper or from a dependency cannot supply one — and a snapshot that goes missing FAILS the link instead of silently falling through to a system archive.
  - Not defended: a deliberately planted archive under one of these names on an earlier `-L`, a linker script or explicit archive argument naming one, a custom linker or rustc wrapper, or replacing a snapshot after the build script runs. Each has to be constructed on purpose by someone who could equally edit `build.rs`.
  - The snapshot directory is swept each run: an `OUT_DIR` outlives a build, and an earlier revision of this script had left its own `libxdp.a` there — exactly the fall-through candidate above.
  - This DELETES the prediction and flag-parsing machinery — `linker_library_dirs`, `-print-search-dirs` parsing, the canonical compare, `refuse_link_search_overrides`, `refuse_shadowing_libxdp_archives` and their pure halves — along with the question of which program rustc invokes as the linker, which rounds 2, 3 and 4 each re-litigated. Round 5 showed the flag check could never have seen a `cargo rustc -- -L` in any case, since it is not in `CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS`.
  - Limits, stated in the README: a host libxdp upgrade is adopted only when the build script re-runs; the version/copy bound is observational, not atomic, so an archive changed and changed back inside the window passes; the build trusts pkg-config to describe the archive in the libdir it names; and libelf, zlib and zstd are still taken from the host, unrecorded.
- **libbpf version.**
  - `libbpf-sys = "~1.6"`.
  - `build.rs` records the full vendored libbpf version from the libbpf-sys that `Cargo.lock` pins (1.6.3). It fails unless the vendored `libbpf_version.h` is 1.6 and matches that version.
  - The build host's libbpf (pkg-config) is recorded too, as exactly that: it is not linked, and it does not identify the headers the prebuilt `libxdp.a` was compiled with. A different major.minor from the vendored copy produces a build warning.
- **Re-runs.**
  - `build.rs` tracks `libxdp.a`, `libxdp.pc`, `libbpf.pc`, `xsk.h`, `libbpf-sys`'s `libbpf.a` and `libbpf_version.h`, and `Cargo.lock`. It also re-runs when `PKG_CONFIG`, `PKG_CONFIG_PATH` or `XPF_LINKED_LIBS_STAMP` changes. Nothing re-runs it on RUSTFLAGS, the target linker or `LIBRARY_PATH` any more, because no decision reads them.
  - Cargo compares only mtimes. So every cargo run in the Makefile's helper recipes passes `XPF_LINKED_LIBS_STAMP`, a content hash of the library files printed by `userspace-dp/build_support/linked-libs-stamp.sh`, and `build.rs` re-runs when it changes. That script reads libxdp's version before any file probe and names it in every failure (it runs before cargo, so otherwise an out-of-range libxdp shipping no `libxdp.a` would fail here without naming the version), and it hashes a per-file `sha256sum` manifest rather than piping the files into one digest, so a read failure cannot become a well-formed hash of partial input under dash.
  - A raw `cargo build` outside the Makefile relies on mtimes alone.
- **Report.**
  - `ProcessStatus` gains `linked_libxdp_version`, `linked_libbpf_version` and `build_host_libbpf_version`. They are `serde(default)` in Rust and `omitempty` in Go, so either side of a version skew still decodes the other.
  - The helper logs the three versions once at startup.
  - `protocol_wire_v1.json` is regenerated for the three fields.
- **Canary.**
  - `csrc/xsk_bridge.c` fills the socket config in one helper shared by both create paths, and sets `libxdp_flags` from `XSK_LIBXDP_FLAGS__INHIBIT_PROG_LOAD` there. The flag no longer crosses the FFI from Rust.
  - Both create functions reach libxdp through two function pointers. A test-only seam points them at captures that record the flags passed and return `-EINVAL`.
- **Shared checks.** The pure checks live in `userspace-dp/build_support/libversions.rs`, which `build.rs` and the crate's tests both include.

## PR #9972 — dataplane: reset a VLAN sub-interface's MTU when its unit statement is gone [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-12)

Branch: `fix/9757-unit-mtu-reset`

Closes #9757

Deleting a unit's `family inet mtu` left the VLAN sub-interface's kernel MTU —
and with it the userspace egress MTU, which `pkg/dataplane/userspace` reads from
that same device — at the old value.

The apply wrote the MTU only when `unit.MTU > 0` and had **no other branch**, and
nothing else writes a VLAN unit's MTU. So the committed configuration stopped
describing the running state: DF-set traffic between the stale value and the link
MTU kept drawing Frag-Needed from the box, and DF-clear traffic kept recording
the #9328 `egress_mtu_exceeded_forwarded_no_df` exception.

Measured on the loss userspace cluster at `5f28e89ac`: after
`delete interfaces reth0 unit 80 family inet mtu`, `show configuration` had no
mtu statement while `ge-0-0-2.80` and `ge-7-0-2.80` both sat at 1400, read nine
seconds after the commit. The only repair was to commit an explicit `mtu 1500`
and delete it again.

## The change

With no unit statement, the target is the **parent link's live MTU** — what a
freshly created VLAN child inherits — so the device lands where it would have
been had the statement never existed, rather than at a number this code invented.
A constant would be wrong the moment an interface-level `mtu` lowers the parent.

`family inet6 mtu` compiles into the same `unit.MTU` and is covered by the same
branch.

Written only on a real difference: this path runs on every commit, so an
unconditional write would churn the link and the log. That is asserted by a cell,
not left to review.

## Cells

A unit **with** a statement sits beside one **without**, in the same apply. A
"fix" that stopped writing MTUs entirely, or one that reset every child to the
parent — which passes the headline row — fails a control instead.

Two of the three are red at `origin/master 3f414db4d`. The idempotence cell
passes there **vacuously**, because nothing writes at all; recorded as such
rather than counted as a fix cell.

## Mutation matrix — 4 of 4 killed

Re-run at `d15577b3d` after the file split below, since anchors follow the code
and a matrix scored against the pre-split file measures a tree that no longer

## PR #9973 — daemon: give the caller-less auto-rollback apply a retry owner and a degraded signal [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-12)

Branch: `fix/9811-rollback-apply-retry`

Closes #9811.

A `commit confirmed` timeout promotes the **store** to the rollback target C1 and
then applies it — the store has already moved, so the dataplane must be brought
into agreement unconditionally. When that apply failed, the failure was **only
logged**.

That is a **divergence, not a stale rule.** Under the #5679 contract a failed
full apply keeps the old compiled policy live, so the node goes on **enforcing
the abandoned configuration C2** while the store, `show configuration`, the peer
resync and `/health` all report C1. On the ordinary commit path an operator sees
such a failure and re-commits; this is a background timer callback with **no
caller to report to**, so nothing retried it and the divergence stood until some
later unrelated apply happened to succeed.

## Not a new mechanism — the fourth instance of an existing one

`proxyARPReassertLoop` (#4001), `fabricIPVLANReassertLoop` (#6791),
`serviceReloadDebtReassertLoop` (#6800), `routingReconcileReassertLoop` (#9693).
A persistent debt latched by the failure, and an always-on re-assert loop that
re-runs the idempotent operation until it succeeds. Same `applySem`-before-read
ordering #4001 established, same repeated owed-check inside, same
overridable-`Fn` seam so the retry is observable without breaking a real publish.

## The decision inside it that is load-bearing

**The retry re-reads the ACTIVE configuration rather than replaying the one whose
apply failed.** Replaying is the obvious implementation and it is wrong in the
silent direction: an operator who commits a new configuration between the failure
and the next tick would have that commit **undone** by the retry owner — a
convergence mechanism turned into a config regression.

Re-reading converges on the same invariant (*the dataplane enforces what the
store reports*) and is also what **discharges the debt after an unrelated
successful commit**, which would otherwise pin a converged node at 503 forever.
Both halves are one cell.

## Why `/health` returns 503, when its neighbour deliberately does not

`rollback_history_degraded` sits directly above this in the same handler and is
explicitly **non-fatal**, with the reasoning that *a perfectly forwarding
firewall must not be pulled from rotation over a degraded recovery aid*. That
reasoning is right and it does not transfer: there the node forwards exactly what
it reports. Here it forwards something it does **not** report, which is
`config_persist_degraded`'s class (*"a restart would load a stale config"*). An
orchestrator that keeps steering traffic at a node whose policy is not the policy
it published is acting on a false premise. It is transient by construction — the
retry owner re-applies every 30s until it converges.

The raw apply error is withheld from the unauthenticated payload under the #5031

## PR #9974 — daemon: fail the apply when a post-link-cycle rxvlan re-disable fails [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-12)

Branch: `fix/9946-rxvlan-postcycle-failclosed`

## What this fixes

`programRethMAC`'s link down/up cycle resets the member NIC's ethtool features,
so `rx-vlan-offload` comes back **on**. `finishRethMemberLinkTail` re-disables it
— and when that re-disable failed it logged a warning and the apply reported
success.

That re-opens, *after* activation, exactly the hazard issue 5268 made an
activation precondition. The XDP dataplane derives 802.1Q identity solely from
the in-frame tag, so a NIC that strips the tag into `skb->vlan_tci` makes every
tagged frame parse as `vlan_id=0`; `resolve_ingress_logical_ifindex` then falls
back to the physical parent ifindex and the frame is classified into the
parent's zone. Untrusted VLAN traffic lands in a trusted zone.

## Reachability — the issue's own conditional, resolved to High

The issue filed at High "with that conditional stated" and named the deciding
check: whether the 1 Hz reconcile re-runs `ensureRxVlanOff`. If it did, the
window would shrink to ~1 s and this would be a hardening note.

It does not. `ensureRxVlanOff` has exactly **one** production caller (the
per-phys compile setup in `compiler_iface.go`), and no daemon ticker reaches
`applyConfigLocked` — the periodic work is per-subsystem (DDNS, IPsec rebind,
RA, HA reconcile) and none of it re-runs the config apply. Nothing re-asserts
the knob until an operator commit, a reboot, or a peer's config sync. Unbounded
in operator time, so **High stands**.

The `rxVlanOffCache` refutation recorded on the issue is sound — the cache is a
per-compile field, so a later apply genuinely re-checks — it just does not
shorten the interval, because nothing schedules that next apply.

## The fix, and why it is not "promote the warning"

The old code ran `ethtool -K` **blind**. A blind probe cannot distinguish "the
NIC refused" from "the NIC has no such feature": on virtio `-K` fails *"not
supported"*. Promoting the warning alone would have failed commits on every
virtio VLAN parent — a NIC incapable of the hazard. `ensureRxVlanOff` already
documents that trap.

So the re-disable now **queries first**, and the classification is *shared* with
`ensureRxVlanOff` rather than restated, because the parse is the part with a
defect history: pre-5268 it was `strings.Contains(line, "off")`, which matches
the feature name `rx-vlan-off`**load** and so read every line — on or off — as
"off", meaning an active offload was never disabled.

Scope matches the compile-time gate exactly, **in both directions**.
`config.InterfaceHasVlanSubinterface` moved to `pkg/config` (beside
`DHCPLeaseIfName`, which exists for the same "so the two derivations can never
drift" reason) and is used by both `rxVlanOffloadActivationError` and the new
path. Wider, and every plain-parent deploy starts failing commits over a setting

Branch: `fix/9932-dhcp-client-head-fold`

Closes #9932

`family inet dhcp;` with the `family` brace elided compiled `DHCP=false`,

DHCP interface — so an interface whose **only** address source was DHCP came up

The #9620 walk splits a **run** after a container head; `family inet dhcp` is a

the family node where `afNode.FindChild("dhcp")` never looks.

## Admission evidence, in the order this pass demands

| pair | schema reach | elided == empty stanza |
|---|---|---|
| `(inet, dhcp)` | **1** — `interfaces * unit family inet` | yes |
| `(inet6, dhcpv6-client)` | **1** — `interfaces * unit family inet6` | yes |
| `(inet6, dhcp)` / `(inet6, dhcpv6)` | **0** — not declared at all | n/a |

That last row is why the inet6 fix is on `dhcpv6-client` and not on `dhcpv6`:
the compiler reads a bare `dhcpv6` child the schema declares nowhere, so no
pair can route it. That undeclared-but-compiled alias is an #8787-class
observation, recorded in the log rather than fixed here.

`set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet dhcp` gives `DHCP=true`, because
`SetPath` builds the head as a **child** while the hierarchical text parser
leaves it on the container head's `Keys`. So the exposure was configuration
**text** — a saved config, `load merge`, a restored backup — which is why the
interactive CLI never showed it. A cell holds that path so the bound stays true
rather than living only in prose.
