## PR #9979 — config: pop to the declaring level when expanding a packed body (#9620 H9 — a discard that permits) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-12)

Branch: `fix/9620-h9-packed-reader-pop`

Closes #9620

H9 was the last open member. **It is a DENY that PERMITS, not a formatting
matter** — traced to the runtime as asked, not inferred.

```
MODIFIER-ONLY SOLE TERM -> action=Accept
CONTROL, discard KEPT   -> action=Discard
```

`term t1 then count C1 discard;` commits strict-clean and **accepts the packet
the operator wrote it to discard**. The chain: the elision leaves `Action=""`;
`filters.go:125` sets `NextTerm` for a modifier-only term (Junos fall-through);
the Rust evaluator applies modifiers and continues; nothing later terminates, so
`FilterResult::default()` returns `FilterAction::Accept`.

Two decoys on the way. `compiler_filter.go:472` has `default:
FilterActionAccept` — that is the **retired-eBPF** struct and its own comment
says it is not the enforcement path. And `firewall_snapshot_render.go:131` prints
`then accept` for an empty action, so `show` **agrees with the wrong behaviour**
instead of contradicting it.

## The mechanism was in the READER

`packedBodyChildren` built a strictly **nested** chain, refining one schema level
per statement. That is correct only while every statement is a child of the one
before it. `count` is a child of `then` and so is `discard` — a **sibling** — so
after consuming `count C1` the walk asked `resolveSchemaChild(count, "discard")`,
got nil, and dropped the whole body under "outside the modelled grammar, do not
guess".

The walk now keeps its open levels and attaches each statement to the **deepest
open level that declares it**, popping the levels below.

## One mechanism, two members

| spelling | master | fixed |
|---|---|---|
| `term t1 then count C1 discard;` | `Action=""` (**permits**) | `Action=discard Count=C1` |
| `term t1 then discard count C1;` | `Action=""` (**permits**) | `Action=discard Count=C1` |
| `term t1 from protocol tcp then discard;` | `Action=""` (**permits**) | `Action=discard` |
| all three policy-options rows | accept | accept (unchanged) |

The third row is the `term from … then` member the #9620 notes recorded as
"accepted and compiled wrong at base, and remain so" — subsumed by the same pop,
exactly as the ruling predicted.

## PR #9980 — nftables: guard a bare lo0 port match with meta l4proto [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-12)

Branch: `fix/9953-th-port-l4proto-guard`

## What this fixes

`th sport` / `th dport` load two bytes at an offset into whatever the
kernel calls the transport header and compare them to a port number. The
load is unconditional — nothing in the rule establishes that the packet
is TCP or UDP — and the `inet xpf_lo0` input chain carries no `iif`
predicate, so every packet arriving at the kernel input hook is evaluated
against every term.

The host-bound set reaching that hook is not "TCP and UDP to the
firewall". The AF_XDP shim's local-destination arm hands host-bound
traffic to the kernel on every bound interface keyed on the DESTINATION
being local and NOT on protocol, so SCTP, GRE and ICMP to a
firewall-local address take that arm exactly as TCP and UDP do; and the
lifelines (fxp0, em0, fab*) are never AF_XDP-bound at all and are served
on the kernel path unconditionally. So an operator's
`destination-port 22` term is evaluated against a GRE or ICMP packet,
reading two arbitrary header bytes as a port: an accept term fails OPEN
when they happen to match, a discard term drops traffic the operator
never named.

Both renderers now emit `meta l4proto { tcp, udp }` alongside a port
match that carries no protocol predicate, driven from one SSOT in
pkg/nftables so the netlink builder and the nft text oracle agree by
construction rather than by the parity CI noticing afterwards. Protocol
numbers resolve through the shared appid SSOT rather than as literals,
and the text form is the numeric spelling issue 3436 requires.

Three scope rules, each a fail-open if inverted:

  - it keys on the EMITTED protocol predicate being empty, not on
    len(term.Protocols). An unresolvable token is kept verbatim by issue
    6806 precisely so `nft -f -` rejects the ruleset and the prior
    generation is retained; supplying a fallback there would replace a
    deliberate fail-closed with a rule that loads and matches.
  - a term carrying an icmp-type or icmp-code is left alone. The ICMP
    lowering already supplies the protocol dependency, and adding
    {tcp, udp} on top makes the rule match NOTHING — merely dead for an
    accept term, but a fail-OPEN for a discard term, which stops
    dropping what it was written to drop.
  - a term comparing no port is untouched, or a discard written to stop
    GRE would stop only tcp/udp.

Reachability was settled before any code was written, because the issue
made it conditional: "if that set is empty this degrades to a
parity/robustness fix". It is not empty — it is the normal host-bound
path, measured at the shim's local-destination arm, which is keyed on
destination and not protocol.

Validation. Reproduction first on both render paths: all six port shapes

#9932's fold already places `dhcp` under `family inet` — which is why the *head*

`FindChild` and the `Children` range in `compiler_interfaces.go` cannot see that,

## PR #9982 — userspace-dp: a differential for overlapping route-leak resolution [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-12)

Branch: `fix/9955-leak-overlap-resolution`

## What this lands

Issue 9955 asked, as its acceptance, for a differential over a GENERATED
set of overlap shapes rather than a single hand-built case, and named the
fix point: the routes.go boundary is where the ordering information is
dropped, so that is where it is either carried through or the overlap is
refused.

This lands the differential. It drives the real build_forwarding_state
and lookup_forwarding_resolution rather than a re-implementation of the
helper's rule, because a re-implementation would agree with itself and
prove nothing.

It measures three divergences, and they share one cause.

Shape family 1, two overlapping leaks: 5 of 10 shapes resolve
differently. The kernel installs leaks as ip RULES (pkg/routing/rules.go
assigns monotonically increasing priorities) and evaluates them in
priority order, first match wins, prefix length irrelevant. The helper
sorts each table by descending prefix length then preference. Every shape
where a broad next-table leak meets a more specific rib-group import
diverges; every shape where the more specific prefix also carries the
better priority agrees, because there both algorithms rank the same entry
first. That 50/50 split is exactly why the generated set was required: a
single case drawn from the agreeing half shows no defect, and one drawn
from the diverging half does not reveal that half the space agrees by
luck.

Shape family 2, a leak overlapping an ordinary route in the same table:
the helper prefers the more specific route. In the kernel these are not
peers — the leak is a rule at priority 150 and the main table is reached
only via `from all lookup main` at 32766, so the rule fires first
whatever the prefix lengths are.

Shape family 3, a leak into a table that MISSES: kernel FIB rules fall
through on a table miss and evaluation continues to main, so a leak into
a table that cannot route the packet costs nothing. The helper ends the
leak arm with an unconditional `return
lookup_forwarding_resolution_v4_inner(...)`, so the miss becomes the
final answer and the packet is blackholed where the kernel forwards it.

The finding is that the named fix is necessary but NOT sufficient, for a
structural reason rather than a matter of effort. The kernel mechanism is
two-stage — priority-ordered rules WITH FALL-THROUGH, then per-table
longest-prefix-match — and the helper models it as one sorted list per
table with unconditional recursion. No choice of comparator over a single
list reproduces a two-stage mechanism with fall-through; fall-through is
not an ordering property at all, it is a retry on miss. And ordering
leaks by priority within a prefix-length-sorted list is not even well
defined on its own: placing a leak relative to an ordinary route requires

## PR #9983 — config: adjudicate the path the store acts on, not the wire string [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-12)

Branch: `fix/9938-authz-resolved-path`

Closes #9938.

Three ways a `deny-configuration` regex was evaluated against a string the
configuration store **never edits**. One defect with three heads, because
`AuthorizeConfigMutation` received raw transport text while every dispatcher
received a lexed, verb-routed, possibly-two-path structure. A patch to any one
string leaves the other two open, which is why the issue filed them as one lever.

**All three reproduced through the gate itself before anything was changed:**

| line | class | before |
|---|---|---|
| `delete security policies p1` | plain deny | refused *(control)* |
| `security policies p1` — the gRPC `Set` wire shape | plain deny | **ALLOWED** |
| `deactivate security "policies" p1` | plain deny | **ALLOWED** |
| `deactivate security policies p1` | plain deny | refused *(control)* |
| `rename … p1 to … ok` | anchored deny | **ALLOWED** |
| `rename … ok to … p1` | anchored deny | **ALLOWED** |
| `copy … ok to … p1` | anchored deny | **ALLOWED** |

## F-019 — the gRPC `Set` RPC sent a bare path

`cmd/cli/shared.go` sends `SetRequest{Input: strings.Join(fullPath, " ")}`, verb
stripped. Returned verbatim, the gate saw a line whose first token is `security`,
answered *"not a mutation verb, not gated"*, and allowed the mutation.

Fixed at the resolver, where `Delete` **already supplied its own verb** — the
asymmetry between the two *is* the defect, and it is what makes this a defect
rather than a narrative: REST builds `route.verb+" "+input`, `Delete` prepends,
and the CLI's deactivate / activate / copy / rename arms keep theirs. `Set` over
gRPC was the single hole — and since #9633 exempted config-mode methods from the
operational command gate, it had **no second net beneath it**.

Guarded against the obvious over-fix: an input that already carries `set` must
not become `set set …`, which would mangle a `load set` replay into a path
matching no deny — silent, and in the same direction as the defect.

## F-020 — `strings.Fields` keeps quotes; the store's lexer consumes them

`deactivate security "policies" p1` was gated as `security "policies" p1` and
applied as `security policies p1`. The gate now uses the **lexer**.

A quote-stripping pass would have been a smaller diff and the same defect: the
problem is that the gate had its own idea of tokenization, and a second
almost-the-same tokenizer reproduces it. The lexer also turns `annotate`'s
comment into one token, which is what lets the path be extracted without a
second parse.

## PR #9987 — config: adjudicate a change-configuration payload against the operator who plants it [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-12)

Branch: `fix/9939-eventengine-payload-authz`

Closes #9939.

`event-options policy … then change-configuration commands "delete security
policies …"` stores its payload as **data**. The line that plants it is gated as
a path under `event-options`; the payload itself is gated by **nothing**, at
plant time or at fire time.

When the policy fires, `pkg/eventengine` applies the embedded `set`/`delete` and
the daemon commits with `configstore.InternalCommitter()` — and
`commit_authority.go` answers `case authorityInternal: return nil`, so **no
authority check runs on that path at all**. A class denied `security policies`
but permitted `event-options` could delete a guard policy autonomously, as root,
on a routine RPM event.

The absence was a measurement: `AuthorizeConfigMutation` had exactly four
non-test call sites — the two gRPC gates, REST, and the on-box CLI — and **zero**
in `pkg/eventengine`. The same grep finding all four surfaces is what makes
"none in the engine" evidence rather than a failed search.

## Why the gate is at the PLANT

**At fire time there is no principal.** The daemon is acting on its own behalf,
which is precisely what makes this an escalation rather than a missing check. The
commit that plants the payload is the only moment a class is in scope.

It lives inside `AuthorizeConfigMutation` because all four surfaces **and
`load`** already route through it, so one implementation covers gRPC, REST, the
on-box CLI and `load merge`/`load set` — rather than four that agree today. Same
call as #9892 and #9952.

## The measurement that decided the fixture, and nearly the issue

With an **unanchored** `security policies` deny the plant is **already refused at
master**: the payload text is part of the outer planting line, so the path gate
catches it incidentally and the defect does not reproduce. It needs an
**anchored** deny — the idiom Junos documents for complex expressions — which
matches the payload's own resolved path and not the outer joined one. The same
condition #9938 F-029 ran under, where an unanchored deny also hid the mechanism.

That premise is **asserted in the fixture helper**, not commented, because if it
stopped being true every cell would pass for the wrong reason. There is also a
cell for the unanchored case itself, so a reader does not conclude the outer gate
was always sufficient.

## Token boundary

The payload walk uses the **same rule the compiler's own reader applies**
(`eventChangeConfigCommands`, #6659): a quoted value is one command per token, an
unquoted tail is a single command that must be re-joined. A different rule here
would adjudicate a command the engine never runs, or miss one it does — #9938's

## PR #10033 — userspace-dp: judge stale reverse hits by the forward companion (Closes #9604) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-14)

Branch: `fix/9604-reverse-rederivation`

Closes #9604.

#8356 re-derives zone policy on the established-session hit path, forward entries only: GATE 1 returns None for every reverse hit, and companion_keeps_alive holds the forward half open on reverse traffic. A flow that sends no forward packet after a tightening commit (server push, one-way UDP reply, quiet TCP client) keeps its old verdict until idle expiry. This judges a stale reverse hit by its FORWARD companion's tuple/protocol/zones under the same generation stamp and revokes both halves on a non-permit verdict. The reverse pair itself is never evaluated (GATE 1's reason stands unconditionally).

## Production change

## PR #10042 — config: reject tagged-unit MTU above parent MTU at commit (#9837) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-15)

Branch: `fix/9837-vlan-mtu-gate`

Closes #9837.

On a vlan-tagging interface, a unit family MTU above the interface-level
MTU committed clean while Linux refuses a VLAN child MTU above its
parent's: every apply only warned and the child kept its old MTU. New
strict gate `validateVlanUnitMTUStrict` rejects that shape at commit,
naming the interface, unit, and both values. The gate compares against
the EFFECTIVE parent MTU — the lowest-numbered referenced untagged
sibling unit MTU when one overrides, else the interface level — matching
`planPhysDesired` precedence, so runtime-fine mixed shapes
(ifc 1400 + unit0 1500 + tagged 1500) still commit; a referenced sibling
pins the parent even with no interface-level `mtu`. Tolerant
load/peer-sync downgrades to a warning (#1960).

The compiled unit MTU is order-dependent (pre-existing compiler quirk:
inet arm overwrites, inet6 arm takes min); the gate judges exactly the
compiled value the dataplane would write, pinned in both orders.

Review fold (parent review; GPT NEEDS-MAJOR was real): hierarchical LoadMerge replays through FormatSet, which renders an empty braced container as a terminal `set` line; SetPath rebuilt it as a leaf, so the gate refused braced input the operator never wrote as a leaf, and no-op merges into configured instances grew leaf twins. Fix: a flat path ending AT a wildcard instance slot now builds (or reuses) the container; declared value carriers (`flow-server`, `next-hop`, `area`, `filter`, apply statements) stay terminal leaves as before.

Delta-2 (parent review delta; GPT MAJOR real): container-only dedup twinned legitimate bodyless leaves elsewhere (`groups { G; }` refused as a duplicate; monitor address double-compiled with independently-summed weights). Fix: terminal replay reuses a same-key node in EITHER shape (identity-preserving), and empty-container creation is scoped to the #9838 subjects — other slots keep the terminal leaf they always built. A bare #9838 leaf survives replay alone and still refuses.

Delta2 P2 (parent review delta2; GPT P2 real, reachability confirmed): a raw LoadOverride retains disjoint top-level roots (parser appends without merging), but SetPath descended into the first root only — a no-op merge of a later-root target twinned it (duplicate-interface refusal; doubled RI). Fix: top-level terminals resolve identity across every same-named root before creating; no authored-leaf conversion or deletion.

Ingress note (pinned): the merge ingress normalizes a hier leaf to the empty container — flat `set` cannot express leaf-at-container-position, and Junos `load merge` agrees — so it commits there (first disjunct), while CheckText / LoadOverride refuse the same text (second disjunct). A never-matching leaf twin is still refused: it means the bare spelling was actually authored.

## PR #10045 — userspace-dp: rebase compiled snapshot above helper high-water (#9824) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-15)

Branch: `fix/9824-rebase-generation`

## Summary

`Compile` reserves its snapshot generation before its unlocked build, so an
interleaved partial (or a landed-but-unacked publish) can leave the snapshot
at-or-below H (max helper-installed). The XSK-startup deferral then stores it
verbatim and strands `publishedSnapshot >= lastSnapshot.Generation` forever,
or the helper rollback-refuses with no retry. The fix rebases unconditionally
to `m.generation += 2` under `m.mu` right after `resampleForCompileLocked`:
H ≤ m.generation+1 always, so the offer is strictly above H on every path and
first attempts admit. The allocator saturates instead of wrapping, and the
rebase refuses fail-closed within two of MaxUint64 (restart recovers), so the
claim holds unconditionally. Closes #9824.

Residual (pre-existing, explicitly unclaimed): post-store drift + lost
conflict-retry recovery is #10041, pinned by Cell R as pre-existing shape.

## PR #10047 — dataplane: retry refused VLAN child MTU after parent raise in same apply (#9845) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-15)

Branch: `fix/9845-vlan-mtu-order`

## What was wrong

`mapZoneInterface` (`pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface.go`) writes a tagged reference's unit MTU to its VLAN sub-interface in the VLAN branch (child write, `:810`), which runs BEFORE the per-phys setup later in the same call writes the parent netdev's planned MTU (`:921-932`). Linux refuses a VLAN child MTU above its parent's CURRENT MTU (`vlan_dev_change_mtu`), so a commit raising both to 9000 logged one warning, raised the parent, reported success, and left the child at its old MTU until the next commit.

Reproduced pre-fix (`TestRaiseParentAndChildMTUTogetherConvergesInOneApply_9845` RED): log shows `WARN failed to set VLAN sub-interface MTU name=ge-0-0-9.50` then `INFO set interface MTU name=ge-0-0-9`, child stuck at 1500 after one apply.

## Fix (per the issue's Fix direction)

Keep the child write inline on its validated link; if the kernel refuses it, retry that same write once, right after the parent's per-phys MTU write in the same call — and only when that parent write actually moved the host:

- `compiler_iface_unit_mtu_9757.go`: `applyVLANSubInterfaceMTU9757` now returns a `vlanMTUPending9845` token (same `netlink.Link` + same MTU) iff the kernel refused; lookup failures still return nil (nothing validated to retry on). New `retryVLANSubInterfaceMTU9845` re-attempts once on that exact object — no re-resolve by name, no kernel admission modeling (macsec `VLAN_HLEN`, async propagation left to the kernel).
- `compiler_iface.go`: VLAN branch captures the token (`:721-722, :810`); parent block records `parentMTUWrote` (`:919-931`); retry fires iff token non-nil AND parent write succeeded (`:932-937`).
- #4960 gap closed as flagged: successful parent/child MTU writes record `set interface MTU` / `set VLAN sub-interface MTU`; converged applies record nothing.

Why each rejected shape from the issue is avoided:

| Rejected shape | How this fix avoids it |
|---|---|
| Early parent write ahead of the #5268 RX-VLAN gate | Parent write unmoved; retry sits strictly after the gate and the parent write |
| Once-per-apply guard suppressing retry | No guard added; retry is a local same-call token, gated on parent-write success only |
| Failed parent read vetoing reductions | Initial child write stays inline and ungated (`TestFailedParentReadDoesNotVetoChildReduction_9845`) |
| Re-resolve by name (foreign-device rename) | Retry reuses the refused attempt's link object (`TestRetryReusesTheValidatedLink_9845`) |
| Later zone error dropping queued reductions | Nothing deferred past the call; reductions apply inline (`TestChildReductionAppliesInlineWithNoRetry_9845`) |

`compiler_iface.go` stays at 1995 LOC (under the 2000 floor); new logic lives in the split 9757 file. README passage updated (it asserted next-commit convergence).

## PR #10048 — config: merge duplicate syslog host blocks by address (#9854) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-15)

Branch: `fix/9854-syslog-dup-host`

Fixes #9854.

## Defect
Two `system syslog host <addr>` statements for one address compiled two `SyslogHostConfig` destinations (`pkg/config/compiler_system.go` pre-fix: fresh struct per AST node + unconditional append). `applySystemSyslog` builds one `SyslogClient` per entry (`pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:1312`), so a message matching both was sent to the same address once per statement. Measured at master:

| Configuration | `System.Syslog.Hosts` |
|---|---|
| `system { syslog { host 10.0.0.1; host 10.0.0.1; } }` | 2 destinations, both no facilities |
| `system { syslog { host 10.0.0.1; host 10.0.0.1 any any; } }` | 2 destinations: empty + `any/any` |
| group `host 10.0.0.1 any any;` + inline braced `host 10.0.0.1 { }` | 2 destinations |

Flat-set `set` usually merges the same lines into one node (SetPath) — except a bare `host X` leaf plus a `host X <body>` container, which stay separate nodes (`ast_edit.go:508-553` vs `:720-738`) and are folded by this same merge. This is the #8436 duplicate-named-block class, disposition "append both", at the `system syslog host` site the census skips (`dupConservationSkipped8436`).

## Fix
`compileSystem` find-or-creates on the host address (Junos merge semantics), mirroring the zone merge (#4818) and BGP neighbor merge (#9192), with apply-groups precedence (not position): the compile expands TAGGED on all three funnels (`ExpandGroupsTagged`, new `ExpandGroupsWithVarsTagged`), and each instance node carries its provenance — an INLINE scalar always records (last inline wins, matching flat-set overwrite), an INHERITED scalar records only first (first group wins, matching the expansion's peer-override). Facilities UNION in first-seen order with exact-pair duplicates dropped (flat parity). `allow-duplicates` is OR; first-seen host order preserved. Tags ride the `cloneForExpansion` copy and no reader except the coalescing branches on them. `file`/`user` destinations share the append shape but are out of scope here; host only per the issue.

## Known gaps (out of scope)
- Duplicate `syslog` STANZAS still reset: `case "syslog": sys.Syslog = &SystemSyslogConfig{}` reallocates per stanza, so sibling `syslog {}` blocks and twin top-level `system {}` blocks compile only the LAST stanza's hosts (measured: `hosts=[10.0.0.2]`, first stanza wiped). `mergeDuplicateBlocks9023` has no `syslog` site. Needs `sys.Syslog` find-or-create plus a cross-stanza index and `file`/`user` coverage — next lane.
- Group-vs-group across MIXED shapes is positional, not precedence-ordered: a packed earlier-group node sorts after the inline container while a braced later-group body merges into it ahead, so G1-packed-111 + G2-braced-222 merges to 222 (measured). Same-shape groups resolve correctly. Recovering application order needs ordinal provenance, which `InheritedFrom` does not carry. Documented in the `#9854` code comment; deliberately unpinned.
- Pre-existing, expansion-side (master-identical, untouched): a packed GROUP host leaf beside ANY inline packed host leaf is dropped whole at expansion (`leafListPeer` matches any same-keyword leaf, even a different address) — measured: group `host 10.0.0.1` + inline packed `host 10.0.0.2` compiles only .2. Whole-destination loss; own lane.

## Verification
- `pkg/config/syslog_dup_host_9854_test.go` (13 tests): 3 issue rows, facility merge order, inline scalar last-wins, group/inline precedence (port + source-address, both value directions, packed + braced control), group-applies counter-case, first-group-wins (expansion + compile-rule cells), flat bare+body both orders, valueless source-address guard (lenient path — strict rejects the shape), allow-duplicates both directions, exact-pair dedupe (hier single + double + flat parity), distinct-address + single-host controls, hier==flat conservation.
- RED matrix on round-1 code (fix stashed): all 4 packed group/inline precedence cells FAIL (inversion: group 999 beat inline 514), exact-pair dedupe FAILS, mixed group-vs-group cell FAILS; braced/group-applies/controls pass as designed. Guard test mutation-checked (guard removed -> `source-address = ""` RED).
- `go test ./pkg/config/ -run TestSyslogDupHost9854 -count=5` green; full `go test ./pkg/config/ ./pkg/daemon/ -count=1` green (`ok pkg/config 176s`, `ok pkg/daemon 84s`); `go vet ./pkg/config/` clean. `docs/log/9854.md` added.

## PR #10049 — dataplane,daemon: keep registered XDP link pins; repair before release (#9847) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-15)

Branch: `fix/9847-xdp-link-pin`

Closes #9847.

## Summary
- Every `CompileUserspaceShim` deleted every `xdp_*` link pin, and the attach loop then short-circuited registered links on "already attached" without re-pinning — so after a second compile, `Close` detached XDP from every interface (a bpf_link survives only while a handle or a pin holds it).
- The pin sweep is now scoped: pins for interfaces with a live registered link are kept (`removeUserspaceShimXDPLinkPinsExcept`). Registered links never take the pinned-reuse path the sweep exists to prevent, so the mlx5 fresh-attach rationale is unchanged.
- `AttachXDP`'s already-attached short-circuit re-pins a missing pin (`ensureXDPLinkPinned`). The helper is library-aware: it `Unpin`s first to forget cilium's cached pin path (`RawLink.pinnedPath` makes same-path `Pin` a nil no-op), then `Pin`s, then stats the file as the verdict — a nil `Pin` with no file is an error. Same attach error string; callers untouched.
- `Close` re-pins missing pins BEFORE releasing the handles (after the last handle closes there is nothing left to pin), closes every handle either way, then reports a degraded (non-hitless) shutdown naming the still-unpinned ifindexes. Hitless shutdown claims preservation only on success.
- `shim_pins.go` split out of `loader.go` verbatim (refactoraudit 1500-LOC floor; #6740 precedent). loader.go lands at ~1400 LOC, below its pre-change count.

## Test plan
- [x] 15 `_9847` cells — 5x green (sweep scoping, library-aware re-pin incl. disappearance-after-pin and silent-Pin regressions both proven lethal to the naive helper, AttachXDP wiring, unpinned check, Close repair/degraded/pinned polarities with pin-before-close event order)
- [x] `pkg/dataplane`, `pkg/dataplane/userspace`, `pkg/daemon` suites green
- [x] `make test-go`: race legs + tree-wide vet + `./...` green except pre-existing `pkg/docsref` failure (`docs/pr/9604` cited by `docs/log/9604.md`; byte-identical on origin/master, untouched by this diff)
- [x] `pkg/refactoraudit` green after the split; #7079 ordering guard green unchanged
- [x] `TestManagerTeardownClearsLinkMembership` fixture now provides the `xdp_11` pin its Close-polarity leg requires under the new contract

## Notes
- No TC symmetry: the per-compile TC sweep only ever sees legacy-daemon leftovers (shim attaches XDP-only; legacy never sweeps). Verified, not assumed.
- No kernel-privilege cell: the kernel half (pinned link survives handle close) is cilium's documented `link.Link` invariant, asserted by composition.
- Shutdown-path transit barrier explicitly DEFERRED (see docs/log/9847.md): the sweep makes in-process unpinned links nearly unreachable, so the residual is a double-failure; barrier is its own issue.
- Mechanism + alternatives recorded in `docs/log/9847.md`.

Branch: `fix/9862-groups-except-nested`

Closes #9862.

`apply-groups-except H` was honoured for a directly applied group and ignored when H arrived through another group: the nested body was pre-merged under the outer name, so the except checks never matched. The fix tags each clone with leaf provenance (`Node.fromGroups`, memo-transparent) and filters nested contributors per node against an accumulated exclusion set, while the outer group keeps its veto exactly.

# WireGuard decap hot path: lock-free roam snapshot (#9644)

Closes #9644.

## Summary

`note_worker_observed_endpoint` ran on every authenticated
transport-data record and took the peer's roaming `Mutex` even in
steady state. This adds a per-peer lock-free last-observed snapshot
(`RoamSnapshot`: seqlock + drain generation, one cache line),
compared before any lock; the mutex is taken only on change, and
the control-thread drain keeps its cadence (post-drain re-report,
per-pass activity refresh, restart invalidation at consumer start).

Plan: `docs/pr/9644/plan.md` v5-final (uncommitted worktree file;
raw reviews under `docs/pr/9644/reviews/`, audit-only).

  real, zero findings invented).

## Approved contract (§11.7, quoted verbatim per review condition)

The lane implemented §5.2/§5.5 under the EXACT weaker contract of
§5.3: (1) suppressions may act on coherent-but-stale snapshots per
exceptions E1–E4, including values that are neither queued-latest
nor just-adopted (ancestor suppression); (1a) concrete harms:
permitted suppressions can omit a needed endpoint re-report and/or
its worker-drain `last_authenticated_rx` refresh. The consumer may
retain or adopt an endpoint other than the latest authenticated
observation, affecting endpoint-dependent transmissions; DNS-hold
may also expire early. OP-1 concerns expected observation latency,
not end-to-end recovery. Recovery requires a later relevant report
to be recorded and consumed, or another effective-endpoint update;
without further relevant events, recovery is not guaranteed
(Codex-r5 finding 3 line-46 exact text, adopted); (2) no formal
packet-count or elapsed-time recovery bound — recovery rides on
OPERATIONAL ASSUMPTION OP-1 (µs-scale coherence observation,
assumed not proven); (3) mailbox semantics are
stale-observation-permitting, NOT ordinary last-write-wins
linearizable; (4) landing gated on the baseline-first measurement

## PR #10062 — nat: repair arrival ports before NAT translation (#9782) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-15)

Branch: `fix/9782-pool-nat`

Closes #9782.

Pool-mode source NAT to a proxy-ARPed address never completed a connection on the loss cluster while interface SNAT on the same path worked (pool 3/3 CONNECT-FAILED, interface 3/3 OK, binding minted).

**Root cause:** `enforce_expected_ports` repairs DMA-race-torn arrival bytes against the PRE-NAT expected tuple. In the generic rewrite, copy-builder, and TCP-segmentation TX paths it ran AFTER `apply_nat_*`, overwriting just-written PAT/DNAT port translations with the original ports (valid checksums, but unmatchable by the reverse index keyed on the translated tuple). An interface-PAT collider reproduced the identical failure, proving the bug port-rewrite-general, not pool-specific. Preserving flows no-op under enforce, which is why only port-changing flows broke.

**Fix:** repair-then-translate at all 8 authoritative sites (enforce immediately before `if apply_nat`, after all `None` gates), NAT-aware debug-only mismatch diagnostic (3 dispatch sites honor the fabric gate), prop-test migrations to pre-NAT expected inputs.

**Commits:** cells-RED first (16 cells), fix-GREEN second, harness+ledger third, history fourth; then parent-review folds (collider comment, fresh-session verdict hardening, sync-gap instrumentation, attesting ledger row).

(no chassis-cluster stanza, or members whose slots map to the other node)
got its interface-level `mtu` planned onto `fab0` itself, a device the bond
setup owns (`ApplyBonds` + `routing/bond.go`, MTU in the bond signature).
The #9761 exception tested the derived `LocalFabricMember` alone; it now
also requires zero configured members.

One correction to the issue's framing: the competing owner here is the
**bond** setup, not the IPVLAN setup (which skips nonlocal members).
Full analysis, including why the resolver is intentionally unchanged
(bond-mode `fab0.10 -> fab0` is correct; resolving to a slave would
misparent VLAN children via `mapZoneInterface` and move the wrong write
rather than remove it), is in the lane brief on the issue plus
`docs/log/9872.md`. Parent rules at review if the resolver half is
still wanted.

Parent-review fold (GPT NEEDS-MAJOR, sustained): the planner skip alone
loses convergence on retained bonds — a unit-0 MTU override written while
an untagged unit existed would stick forever once the unit is removed
(same sig → KEEP, planner silent, networkd stamps MTU only at creation).
`reconcileBondMTU` completes the handoff bond-side: KEEP + adopt converge
the live MTU to the interface level, compare-then-write, hard error on
set failure with tracking retained for retry.

Master merge (`00ed0eaf3`, #9873): the merged table crosses 9873's `st10`
name with the 9872 trailing-dot suffix; all 192 such cells misplanned
because `stUnitCarriesVlanID9873` parses strictly, so `st10.` keeps the
verbatim lexical ref (vlan 0, untagged plan) by deliberate #9873 doctrine.
Neither lane's source is wrong — the table enumerates tagged shapes only,
so it now skips trailing-dot on st bases (premise-pinned 192) and a new
pin locks the verbatim behavior. 9873's own pins hold.

## PR #10075 — Fail closed on unrepresentable/valueless from leaf (#9875) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-15)

Branch: `fix/9875-from-leaf-widen`

Closes #9875.

A firewall-filter term whose `from` block carried a match leaf the dataplane does not enforce (`term.UnknownFrom`, #3307) or a value-bearing leaf written with no operand (`term.ValuelessFrom`, #8480) compiled to a term missing an entire authored constraint. Every mirror then rendered only the surviving match set — byte-identical to a term authored without the leaf — so an `accept` term over-permitted and a `discard`/`reject` term over-dropped with no signal past the boot warning. The strict gates reject both spellings, so this is the tolerant load / peer-sync path (#1960), like the #3406/#6459/#6463 family.

This change records the leaf (`compileFirewall` populates `ValuelessFrom` via the same raw-node helper the #8480 gate walks, so the sets can never drift), carries a `from_unrepresentable` fail-closed marker on every mirror (userspace snapshot wire bool + Rust `UnrepresentableFilterFrom` whole-snapshot refusal, lo0 netlink plan refusal + oracle `__xpf_refuse_unrepresentable_from__` bareword, PBR steering drop), and bumps `ProtocolVersion` 19 -> 20 under the #8892 v10/v11 arm (v19 taken by #9874, see sequencing) (an old helper ignoring the key enforces the widened term — the defect itself). Whole-snapshot refusal, not term poisoning: poisoning a discard/reject term to match-nothing would fall through to the implicit accept (fail-OPEN).

Also in the stack: the #8480 helper now reads prefix-list leaves through `firewallPrefixListRefs` (fixes the self-named-list false positive, proven by execution — behavior changes only for self-named references), and the six newly-visible compact-blind prefix-list sites are classified `open` in the #8690 register with hand measurements (#6940 pattern: pre-existing blindness exposed by the fix, not a lane regression).

SEQUENCING (done): #9874 merged first and took v19. This lane rebased onto it and re-bumped to v20 (both consts, #8892 digest re-measured over the combined wire: `15332c48...f7b65a`, pins, fixture regen with both keys), re-gated, and pushed together with the review fold below.

## PR #10077 — Gate braced family via shared AF walker [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-16)

Branch: `fix/9876-braced-family-gate`

Closes #9876.

## Mechanism
The #8480 gate took `fam.Children` as the filter level (`compiler_firewall_valueless_from_8480.go:143-156` on base), so the braced-nested `family { inet { filter } }` shape presented an AF node where the gate required a `filter` node and was skipped — while `compileFirewall` descends both shapes. The two prefix-list leaves declare no args (`schema_cos.go:527-528`) so they also escape the generic #8597 belt (`missingArgs > 0`, `schema_walk.go:710-711`): a valueless prefix-list in this shape committed strict-clean as match-ANY. Measured on base `d3e959067`: gate=nil, `CompileConfig`=nil, `FiltersInet["F"].Terms[0]` with `Action="discard"` and empty `SourcePrefixLists`.

## Fix
- The #8480 gate descends `family` nodes through `firewallFamilyMembers9883`, the single dual-shape extractor shared by `compileFirewall` and the #3884/#4296/#9017 gates — gate and compiler cannot drift again (#2419/#6526 doctrine). ## PR #10079 — Fail closed on unknown NAT match leaves (#9877) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-15)

Branch: `fix/9877-nat-partial-loss`

## What

A typo'd NAT `match` leaf beside a valid one was silently dropped on the tolerant path and the rule compiled constrained on the surviving dimensions with zero operator-facing warning (STEP-0 at base `d3e959067`: lenient `SourceAddresses=[10.0.0.0/8] constrained=true warnings=[]`; strict `SchemaValidate` rejects; #8430 passes).

This PR records dropped leaves on the typed rule, rejects at strict commit, and warns + skips the rule (fail-closed) on the tolerant path. Go-only, no wire/Rust: a dropped leaf leaves no snapshot trace for Rust to re-derive, so Go-skip is the identical dataplane outcome with no merge-order coupling.

## How

- **Record**: `default:` arms in the source/destination/static match switches → new exported `json:"-"` `UnknownMatchLeaves` on `NATRule`/`StaticNATRule` (first-seen deduped).
- **Gate**: `validateNATUnknownMatchLeavesStrict` in `runUniformGatesNAT` (shared `lenientDestNATAddresses`), before #8430; #8430 suppresses marked rules (one mistake, one warning); message states the disposition.
- **Poison**: warned skip in all three userspace builders via shared predicates (new `SourceNATRuleExcludedReason`; NPTv6 consults; unkeyable-DNAT-`off` reports); keyable exemptions install warned. Show surfaces annotate via the same predicates; source hits line gated on the verdict (#8185); #6812 walk excludes marked rules before `seen`-marking.
- Mechanical: #6534 showaudit census row, #6812 sweep `fixtureConstantAxes` entry.

Closes #9877.

## PR #10082 — Validate valued modifiers on typed leaves (#9880) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-15)

Branch: `fix/9880-valued-modifier`

Closes #9880.

The strict schema gate refused every valued modifier on a generic typed leaf, so valid Junos NTP authentication (`server <addr> key/version/routing-instance`) and `threshold <n> action` could not be committed while lenient compiled the same tree.

## Mechanism (verified on base `4eedd01d7`)

Two presence-only reject sites: `validateModifierChild` (`len(node.Keys) > 1` unconditionally rejects, never consulting the modifier schema) kills the block spelling; the `validateTypedLeaf` tail loop (every trailing token must be a bare child keyword) kills the packed spelling. In-package census bounds the blast radius to exactly the five NTP modifiers (the only other typed leaves with children take the `tailValidator` path).

## Change

- `pkg/config/schema_walk.go`: `validateModifierChild` + `validateTypedLeaf` (tail loop, modifier-only branch) consume a modifier's declared `args` as value tokens, each run through the modifier's own `checkValue`; missing → `modifier %q requires a value`, excess → `unknown modifier` on the first excess token. `args == 0` behavior byte-identical.
- `pkg/config/schema_system.go`: `key`/`version` get `ValidateIntegerMin(1)` (#6940 shape: Atoi-drop to the 0 sentinel, consumers gate on `> 0`); `action` gets `ValueEnumOf` + `ValidateEnum([accept, reject])` (repo's own contract). `routing-instance` stays arity-only.
- `pkg/config/compiler_system.go`: comment-only clarification. `docs/config-schema.md`: the #2448 sentence is now historical.

## Review fold: modifier-headed multi-token statements (dd2c8868b)

Parent review found the round-1 tail loop admitted address-less statements: `server prefer key 5` passed `prefer` as the value (valid hostname) while the compiler reads every token as a modifier with no address and yields zero servers (measured on round-1 code: strict ACCEPT, `servers=[]`; block spelling still rejected). Fix: `validateTypedLeaf` disambiguates the head once — a head naming a known modifier means NO value on this node, so multi-token modifier-headed fails as `missing value` with no sibling rescue (measured: the node's modifiers drop even beside a supplying sibling). Lone-token verdicts byte-identical. New cells 9–10 pin this; the commit accept cell now asserts the SERVER LIST before modifier fields. Full evidence: `docs/log/9880.md`.

## Tests

New cells drive `SchemaValidate` (strict), never lenient compile; plus three `compileTreeStrict` operator-commit cells. Base run (pristine base + new files): cells 1,3,4,5,7,9 FAIL; 2,6,8,10 PASS (guards). Mutations M1–M5: 5/5 KILLED (M5 killed by cell 9 only).

## PR #10085 — config: refuse unquoted leading-bracket as-path regex (#9881) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-15)

Branch: `fix/9881-aspath-bracket`

Closes #9881.

An unquoted leading-bracket as-path regex (`[0-9]+`) is lexed as list sugar and silently compiles to the valid-but-different `0-9 +`. The strict gate now rejects any as-path tail carrying unquoted bracket provenance with a quote-or-unbracket diagnostic, instead of guessing at an ambiguous reconstruction.

## What changed

- **Plumb**: interactive `set`/`delete` parse and apply with the grouped pair (`SetAsQuotedGrouped`/`DeleteAsGrouped`), matching load-merge/replay — the bracket bit reaches the AST on every authoring path.
- **Hygiene**: dup re-issue re-stamps both masks; copy/rename re-keys by role (containers keep structural grouping, leaves clear authorship, same-path rename retains); member-delete rebuilds the mask in lockstep; whole-group delete allowed (member paths keep the #9799 refusal).
- **Lexer signal**: per-gap tokenless-bracket loss (empty `[]` pair incl. POSIX `[]...]` head, stray `]`) marks the following token; span-end checks taint the last key. Balanced non-empty lists never mark.
- **Flag + gate**: `ASPathDef.RegexUnquotedBracket` follows the winning span incl. loss marks; strict branch checked before validity; lenient downgrade automatic.
- **FRR fail-closed**: omitted lists (undefined/invalid/flagged) never dangle — reject terms over them render one bare deny-all, other terms skip the dangling OR-branch.

Design brief, two plan reviews, and adjudication are on the issue. Residual `LoadMergeAs`-hierarchical filed pre-merge as #10084 (FormatSet drops leaf provenance; probe-proven). Parent-review fold (4 items incl. the FRR HIGH) folded post-PR; per-item report on the issue.

A braced filter under an undeclared address family folded into the IPv4 pool on the tolerant path while the #9017 warning told the operator it compiles to NOTHING — an inverted diagnostic. This quarantines undeclared families out of BOTH pools, making the message true on every route (fail-safe direction; fail-closed end-to-end via the #3296 backstop — see issue brief).

## Mechanism (base `15be546a1`, STEP-0 verified PRESENT)
- `pkg/config/compiler_firewall.go:245-251`: `dests := []map[string]*FirewallFilter{fw.FiltersInet}`, only `inet6`/`any` special-cased → every other token (incl. typos) lands in IPv4 and enforces.
- `pkg/config/compiler_firewall_family_9017.go:91-99`: lenient warns NOTHING and CONTINUES into the fold.
- Measured: braced `family inett` lenient → `inInet=true inInet6=false` + NOTHING warning (contradiction); flat-set → `inInet=false` + warning (true); strict braced rejects.

## Change
- `compileFirewall`: skip family tokens outside the schema-declared set (`firewallFamilyPermitted9017()`, the same source the #9017 gate reads — a fourth declared family permits itself everywhere).
- #3884 collision gate: ignore quarantined families (else its `silently overwrites` warning contradicts the token warning on `inett/X`+`inet/X`).
- #9017 message text unchanged — the quarantine makes it true. Strict still rejects, naming the token.

- Shared shape-aware extractor `firewallFamilyMembers9883` for compileFirewall + #3884/#4296/#9017 gates with residue coverage on structured multi-key nodes. Before: compiler read Keys[1] while the gate read Keys[0] — `family { inett inet { filter F } }` lenient installed F + warned NOTHING (bypass), and the converse committed a strict silent void. Branch: `fix/9886-netdev-name-belt`

## Summary

Closes #9886 (F-049). An interface name that is not exactly one systemd
`[Match]` pattern rendered raw into generated units: `Apply` wrote
`Name=ge 0` with a nil error, and the lenient compile manufactured `"ge 0"`
out of `"ge\n0"` via the #1798 scrub with only a warning. The predicate
expressing the refusal existed with zero production callers.

- `pkg/rendersafe`: shared `RendersAsOnePattern` (ASCII-whitespace grammar
  predicate) + `SafeInterfaceName` (the render contract: one pattern AND
  control-free); `config`'s helper delegates.
- `pkg/networkd`: pre-`expected` belt in `Apply` over Name and OriginalName
  — a refused row writes no file, sweeps its stale poisoned units
  (deleted-interface semantics), and fails the commit like a #2987 write
  failure.
- `pkg/daemon`: `writeLinkFile` guard refuses render-unsafe target /
  OriginalName before any mutation (positional, device-map, bootstrap
  callers).
- `pkg/config`: post-expansion gate over `interfaces` + `bridge-domains`
  identity keys, `chassis device-map interface` entries (all three instance
  shapes), and `fabric-options member-interfaces` references (all five
  spellings) — strict arm hard-errors, lenient arm drops/strips with loud
  warnings (#5834 shape).

## Surfaced deviations from the issue text

1. **Drop+warn, not hard-error, on the lenient path.** Plan review killed
   hard-error with executable mechanics: `SyncApply` rejects on lenient
   compile error and the repo's comments state that rejection alarm-loops
   against a pre-gate primary, while every semantic gate on lenient
   downgrades/drops/quarantines (zero hard-error precedents). A scrubbed-only
   hard-error middle path was weighed and rejected (still loops pre-#1798
   skew, needs invasive provenance tracking, permanent commit blocker for
   one never-usable member). Full reasoning in the issue thread
   (adjudication comment) and the gate comment.
2. **Belt placed pre-`expected`, not beside #9494.** A write-loop refusal
   would pin a previously rendered poisoned unit in `expected` forever; the
   pre-`expected` belt sweeps it. #9494 stays put (slash-names have no
   stale-poison case).
3. **ASCII-whitespace predicate, not verbatim `strings.Fields`.** Fields
   splits NBSP/NEL, which the kernel accepts and systemd treats atomically;
   the shared predicate refuses exactly the set no kernel device name can
   contain, so it cannot refuse a working config.
4. **Globs deferred to #10089** (filed): one-pattern globs pass this belt
   by design; #10089 owns render-side glob refusal plus the strict-path
   `bridge-domains "ge*"` hole found during review.

## PR #10092 — shim: drop-and-count QinQ frames (#9888) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-15)

Branch: `fix/9888-qinq-shim-drop`

A double-tagged frame left the inner TPID as eth_proto after the single unwrap and took the non-IP XDP_PASS arm above the ingress gate — an unadjudicated handoff to the kernel, which while armed forwards bridged frames by MAC with no zone policy.

## Fix

After the single unwrap, a still-VLAN ethertype (inner 0x8100/0x88a8/0x9100, or a legacy 0x9100 outer the shim never unwraps) is an explicit XDP_DROP with a new appended `qinq_drop` counter, on the armed guard, its unreachable-by-construction match twin, and the degraded-path arm. Flat predicate (`is_vlan_tpid`), no unwrap loop — verifier cost unchanged in shape (565,984 processed insns, 43.40% headroom). Go reason table +1 with the 8258 agreement/cap guards moved 16→17, and the Rust debug-log reader (third copy of the index) likewise +1 with its own shim-agreement test (disposable-map reconcile already resets on MaxEntries change). Same change corrects the stale L2 doc contract and extends the L2 canary to the double-tag shape (parser-contract coverage; disposition enforced by the BPF cells). New BPF cells are wired into `make test-shim-run` by name. Scope is complete-L2-header frames: runts truncating inside the tag take the `None` path and carry no L3 payload.

Disclosed cost: a single legacy-0x9100 outer may hide ARP/LLDP the shim never unwraps — dropped fail-closed rather than passed. Passing an opaque, unconfigurable shape unadjudicated on bridged ports is the hole; the drop stands, stated plainly in code, tests, and `docs/log/9888.md`.

## PR #10095 — Cap MonitorInterface budget and sends (#9891) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-16)

Branch: `fix/9891-monitor-budget`

Closes #9891.

MonitorInterface was the one monitor stream with no subscriber budget and no send deadline: 1s ticker, unbounded for loop, blocking stream.Send. This gives it a 64-stream budget (matching the sibling EventBuffer streaming cap) refusing past cap with ResourceExhausted, plus a 30s handler-side per-write send bound and a 10s peer-idle bound on the proxy leg.

Sizing note: the issue text cites MonitorPacketDrop 256 TrySubscribe, but 256 there is the channel bufSize; the real sibling cap is `defaultMaxSubscribers = 64`. The new budget matches 64.

Design notes (review fold): a Send timeout TRANSFERS its slot to the Send worker (64 bounds active handlers plus in-flight timeout workers); the 30s claim is handler return, not client observation (trailers queue behind pending DATA) or H2 transport reclamation (queued DATA + trailers outlive the slot until drain/disconnect, bounded per-connection by MaxConcurrentStreams 256). Timeout ownership is terminal — a timeout never returns success, so a continuing stream always holds admission. Proxy Recv severs a stalled peer with Unavailable (no transfer — conn close unblocks Recv promptly); proxy NewStream carries a separate 10s establishment bound that stops on success (no lifetime limit on healthy monitoring).

## PR #10096 — Harden NDP NA learns: frag/source/CAS (#9893) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-15)

Branch: `fix/9893-ndp-frag-learn`

Closes #9893.

## What
An L2-adjacent sender could steer neighbor entries via a non-first fragment carrying NA-shaped payload (RFC 6980 violation), via an NA with a spoofed source, and via an Override=0 interleave. This hardens all three:

1. **RFC 6980**: `parse_ndp_neighbor_advert` walks `walk_ipv6_ext_chain` directly (same one-walk cost) and refuses when `walk.fragment.is_some()`, counted via `NDP_NA_FRAG_REFUSED`.
2. **Source validation**: requires `neighbor_ip_is_learnable(src)` on `l3+8..24`, counted via `NDP_NA_BAD_SOURCE_REFUSED`.
3. **Atomic CAS**: new `insert_ndp_na_if_override_allows` checks Override=0 vs live differing MAC under the same shard lock as the write, closing the get-then-insert TOCTOU. `insert_if_changed` delegates with `override=true` (ARP/RX byte-identical; `debug_assert` + `unwrap_or(false)` fallback, never panics).

Counters are crate-local globals bumped only for NA-shaped frames (ordinary fragmented transit does not pollute); Prometheus export is #10097.

Accepted residuals: Truncated/OverLimit chains refuse without counting (unconfirmable as NA); first-defect attribution (doubly-defective counts once as fragment); on-link = HL255 + unicast predicate, no FIB prefix check.

## PR #10098 — Gate meta fast path on declared L3 end (#9894) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-15)

Branch: `fix/9894-meta-flow-length`

Closes #9894.

## Mechanism (verified on base `0f69a61`)

The XDP shim bounds its L4 read by the frame end **including** trailing slack (`parse_l4`, `userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs:1949-2030`, reads against `data_end`; `total_len` never read outside a struct declaration), so a short declared length with trailing bytes arrives with a metadata tuple spelled from out-of-datagram bytes. The SessionFlow fast path (`inspect.rs:1363-1368`) returned that tuple verbatim on `metadata_tuple_complete` — a predicate with no length dimension (`:881`, `(meta, flow)`). Executed probe on base: short `total_len=20` + slack `(1111,443)` -> production path returned `Some((1111,443))` while the declared-end parse returned `None`.

## Fix

**Core** (`frame/inspect.rs`): new `meta_l4_ports_in_declared_end` — `[l4,l4+4)` within `declared_l3_end`, one comparison, no re-parse. Gates both metadata-return sites; gate failure falls through to the authoritative frame parse (not to `None`). Shim untouched.

**Review fold** (parent GPT/SPARK NEEDS-MAJOR, commit 2):
- GPT-1: agreement arm keeps IPs-only #3290 arbitration (session key must equal the shim `USERSPACE_SESSIONS` probe key, `lib.rs:1856-1866`, and the restored ident, `mod.rs:1805-1844`). Frame-wins reverted; #3290 test restored verbatim; parse→forward consistency cell added.
- GPT-2: `ports_unknown` marked explicitly at flowless input-filter/PBR sites (`poll_descriptor`, `forwarding/pbr.rs`), never derived in the flow-blind builder (suite caught the cache-hit/DMA-race over-gate). Two loop-level except-term cells, both revert-verified RED.
- GPT-3: refusal carried to immediate TX (`forward_request.rs`), deferred neighbor (`pending_neigh_flow_key`), and `authoritative_forward_ports` meta fallback. No `cos_classify.rs` change (portless flowless arm already).
- SPARK-4/5: over-reject pins restored (the #3290 test + helper truth-table + TCP distinguisher); fast-vs-fallback distinguisher + fall-through coverage added. Protocol-omission note evaporated with the revert.

Scope note: the triage said "inspect.rs only", but the review explicitly required the TX/neighbor/filter carries with file:line precision. Delta outside inspect.rs is small same-pattern arms; `matching.rs`/`cos_classify.rs` logic untouched.

The pool-utilization alarm divided used ports by the nominal address x port capacity, but admission refuses at the per-pool tracked-flow cap (`min(nominal, 262144)`, `allocator.rs:2036`), so a large pool AT the refusing cap with a low ports ratio never raised. - `AppliedNATPoolStatus` -> daemon sampler -> `natpoolalarm.PoolStatus` now carry `LiveFlows` + `MaxTrackedFlows`.
- `evaluate()`: port-bearing utilization is `max(used_ports/capacity, live_flows/max_tracked_flows)`; the single raise/clear state machine is unchanged, so one transition emits one line even when both legs cross (no double-syslog by construction).
- `MaxTrackedFlows == 0` (helper predating the counters) makes the flow leg inapplicable: `LiveFlows` ignored.
- Fold (review-converged): address-only pools refuse at the SAME cap (`allocator.rs:3608,4076,4223`; live proof `tests_addr_only_sibling_9131.rs:418-419` — `used_ports == 0` with `live_flows == 2`), so the flow leg is evaluated INDEPENDENTLY of port translation: address-only pools raise/clear on live/max alone, share the single switch, and are recorded inapplicable only when NEITHER leg is measurable. The #7361 compiler advisory is narrowed to the true partial-signal claim (ports leg dead + collision mode silent).

## PR #10101 — configstore/journal: close four link-following paths with sibling discipline (#9897) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-15)

Branch: `fix/9897-journal-symlink`

Closes #9897.

Converts all four cohort sites to the sibling O_NOFOLLOW/Lstat/EvalSymlinks discipline, keeping both factory-reset copies in one change. Deferred scope lives in [#10100](https://github.com/psaab/xpf/issues/10100) (OPEN, verified — filed from this lane's security plan review): R-1 interior symlinks under wiped trees (`tls/key.pem`, `.configdb/active.json` other than the `master.key` shape) survive `RemoveAll` silently with no `Skipped` entry; R-2 rendered-leg following (`StripManagedSectionFile` resolves-and-rewrites at target, swanctl/kea `Remove` without link checks, temp-sweep removes). Both are under-wipe/silent-survival, distinct from this cohort's root/segment members.

## Change

- F-037 `pkg/configstore/db.go` — `NewDB`: spelling normalized once (`filepath.Clean`, empty preserved) before the gate and used consistently; `Lstat` pre-gate refusing a symlinked final component (names link+target, hints "symlink the PARENT"); the 0700 enforcement runs as `fchmod` on an `O_NOFOLLOW`+`O_NONBLOCK` handle with an `fstat` `IsDir` check. Absent dirs still created; intermediate links still pass.
- F-038 `pkg/configstore/journal/journal.go` — new `openSegmentNoFollow` (`Lstat` pre-check incl. dangling + `O_NOFOLLOW` + `O_NONBLOCK` + fstat `IsRegular`), used by `tailSegment` and `readAllLocked`. Absent stays a tolerated gap; symlinked parents still work. Refusal is LOUD (Tail error, propagated by every `ListCommitHistory` caller) — silent partial history would be its own audit-integrity hazard.
- F-108 `maybeRotateLocked` — `Lstat` gate on the current path before `Stat`/`Rename`; symlink refused naming link+target. Rotated-slot links still shift by rename but are inert (readers refuse).
- F-040 — new shared `configstore.ResolveFactoryResetRoot`: validates lexical AND resolved paths (either refusal wins) plus canonical-identity denylist completion (existing forbidden entries canonicalized; aliases of forbidden dirs refused — completes, not extends, the denylist). Absent stays a clean no-op, dangling final links refused. Both wipe copies resolve first and wipe the resolved target; both early-gate resolvers (`grpcapi` + `cli`) validate the resolved root but return the original path (wipe re-resolves authoritatively; byte-identical ordinary roots incl. symlinked TMPDIRs). Durable-seam wants + failure-injection sentinels + all six forbidden-root registrations normalized to resolved form with create-then-register ordering.

Design record: MEDIUM tier — brief + adjudication on the issue; implementability CONCERNS all adopted; security KILL adjudicated to implement-with-hardenings (strictly narrows vs base; deterministic core is pre-existing #5684/#5768 doctrine; see issue comments). Parent review (GPT NEEDS-MAJOR + SPARK NEEDS-MINOR) folded in `f229f6e02`: spelling normalization + 5-way fixture, canonical identities + alias parity row, both failure-injection sentinels, absolute parity outcomes, `O_NONBLOCK` on the DB open.

## Accepted residual (stated accurately)

The validated root is a PATHNAME, not a pinned handle — every wipe syscall re-resolves it across blocking dir fsyncs and recursive `RemoveAll` traversals, so the window spans the whole wipe (the earlier "microseconds" phrasing was withdrawn on the issue). Exploiting it takes parent-dir write DURING the wipe, plus exact-xpf-name collisions (#5768 scoping; #9013 per-artifact refusals still apply). Closed: the deterministic plant. EXCLUDED: concurrent namespace mutation during a wipe. Full closure needs descriptor-relative traversal (dirfd `openat`/`unlinkat`; openat2 `RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS` the direct form but not mandatory) across both wipe copies — excluded as disproportionate, same as every path-based guard in the repo. Acceptance requested on the issue on this explicit basis.

## PR #10106 — Preserve configuration compiler intent (#9899) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-15)

Branch: `fix/9899-config-residuals`

## Scope

Closes #9899

Implements the eight live residuals verified on base `1fe6fa0aa`:

- **F-030/F-031:** enforce canonical unsigned tunnel keys (`0..2^32-1`), authored TTL (`1..255`) and VLAN/inner-VLAN (`0..4094`) at schema and compiler boundaries. Explicit empty values do not inherit/default. Lenient compilation quarantines the invalid interface/unit and preserves valid siblings.
- **F-099/F-101:** reject unterminated hierarchical leaves at EOF and non-nil, wrong-length editing provenance masks without mutation. Flat-set EOF and optional terminators before closing braces remain compatible.
- **F-102:** use the existing canonical numeric protocol primitive consistently across appid, application/filter gates, DNAT and junos-host readers; retain named-protocol compatibility.
- **F-103/F-105:** include inet-precedence classifiers (including entryless names) in both completion positions, and preserve quoted operands even when equal to the matching statement head.
- **F-107:** compile the supported implicit-inet firewall spelling instead of accepting and discarding it. Compact normalization precedes alias relocation, on cloned compiler/validation views; existing collision and unsupported-match gates remain authoritative.

**Already resolved on base, not reimplemented:** F-100 is stale after #9881 (`rekeyBracketProvenance`); F-104 is already fixed by #9875. File/line evidence, scope decisions and reproduction records are in `docs/log/9899.md`.

Junos explicitly makes `[edit firewall]` and `[edit firewall family inet]` equivalent: [official documentation](https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/software/junos/routing-policy/topics/concept/firewall-filter-stateless-guidelines-for-configuring.html). This is why F-107 implements the alias rather than refusing valid syntax.

## Bounded prerequisites and inventories

The shallower alias exposed two pre-existing flexible-range reader defects inside existing census horizons. With parent authorization, this also expands packed range bodies/runs using the existing resolver and merges same-name fragments in the shared reader. Explicit-family regressions failed on a detached checkout of the original base (lost byte-offset and false duplicate-range refusal); distinct range names still refuse under #5823. Defaults are applied after all fragments; lazy per-term identity tracking is linear.

No blanket splitter, census horizon, or broad allowlist was added. The compact inventory falls from the first measured eight new divergences to only the alias of the existing #9056 `interface-specific` compact limitation. The existing #8880 unsplittable population gains one measured alias: both implicit and canonical `filter F filter G` packed runs retain only F; their braced twins and separate packed roots retain F/G. Two newly visible #2399 ignored reject-message flag combinations remain recorded. These inherited limitations are explicit, not claimed fixed.

Spelling coverage is measured at **1,205 enumerated / 762 compared / 443 blind**: +21 comparisons and +16 value-less flags; other blind categories do not grow. Generated and hand-maintained inventories track the new schema copy.

Master-green fix: TestContractSnapshotGolden9821 failed on fcfdafcb5 (15133 vs 15067 bytes) after the #9899 merge.

Cause: the P2 tunnel-fallback fix added AuthoredUnits bool to InterfaceConfig without a JSON tag. ConfigSnapshot embeds the whole typed Config, so the bit leaked onto the Go→Rust wire: the 9821 diff was exactly two added "AuthoredUnits": true lines, nothing else.

The bit is compiler-internal quarantine state consumed only by the Go emitter (tunnelemit.go); its decision is already encoded in the emitted endpoint rows, and no Rust consumer reads the bit. This follows the established HasPreference precedent (types_routing.go): json:"-" IS LOAD-BEARING for compile-time state, and nothing is lost because the config DB stores the TREE while compileInterfaces recomputes the bit on every load.

The after-lock seam waits until repayment releases the mutex and probes `TryLock`: this is the lock-use guard. FIFO/types are a separate order proof once lock use is established, requiring `[session_v4, delete_v4]` and an absent receiver entry; the adverse-order control requires `[delete_v4, session_v4]` and a present receiver entry. The AST lexical bracket check remains defense in depth.

## PR #10147 — userspace: off-lock HA lease refresh (#9629) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-17)

Branch: `fix/9629-ha-mutex`

# userspace: serve HA lease refresh off the snapshot mutex (#9629)

Fixes psaab/xpf#9629 (split from #9172 finding V035; residual of #7209).

## Problem

`update_ha_state` is the only refresher of the helper's per-RG forwarding
lease, consulted per packet by `is_forwarding_active`. It dispatched under the
snapshot-wide `ServerState` mutex, which `apply_snapshot` holds across a 10 s
worker-readiness barrier — while the daemon refreshes every 3 s against a 10 s
stale window. A hold past ~7 s expired the lease behind the lock and the
per-packet check reported a healthy RG inactive (outage). Production stacks
three serializations (verified in code): Go `m.mu` across the apply RPC (G1),
serial helper accept loops with only cross-socket concurrency (H1), and the
`ServerState` mutex (H2). This change fixes all three legs with an independent
channel end-to-end; either side alone degrades to today's behavior (no flag day,
see matrix in `docs/log/9629.md`).

## Change

- Helper (Rust): lease-only `SessionDomain::try_refresh_ha_leases` over the
  shared `rg_runtime` cell (never changes active/membership off-lock;
  transitions/CLEAR/join-leave route to main); new leaf `ha_mutex`
  serializing both writers across load→store (`ServerState→ha`, µs hold,
  poison-recovered); `SocketMode` dispatch split (session `update_ha_state`
  fast-path only, never `ServerState`; main path byte-identical).
- Go: `requestHAWatchdogSession` via the session socket under per-request
  `sessionMu`; `UpdateHAWatchdog` snapshots + marks baseline under brief
  `m.mu`, sends OUTSIDE `m.mu` when the helper advertises the new
  `ha_session_refresh_supported` status bit (explicit capability, NOT protocol
  version); legacy main path byte-identical for old helpers. NeedsLock sentinel
  + prefix contract; session path never sets `helperHAStatePublished`.
- Design questions answered in `docs/log/9629.md` (plan + 2 hostile reviews +
  full adjudication of all 22 findings before implementing).

## Evidence (deterministic; all GREEN)

- Clean-base RED (`/tmp/9629-red-base` @609433efb, 2 test files, 0 prod diff):
  `server::tests::update_ha_state_lease_stays_active…9629` FAILED 4.01s,
  mid-hold inactive, served 4.009s. Post-fix: literal 12s cell (SEED 10/HOLD
  12s/refresh ~5s/sample 11.5s) GREEN + 5x; fast proxy + race-closer + 5
  equivalence cells GREEN + 5x each (40 timing runs, zero FAILED); 9
  decision-table tests; `server::tests::` 139; full `cargo test` 6117 passed.
- Go: 8 session cells (mu-free, sentinel classifier ×2, throttle-success,
  old-helper fallback ×2, success-no-flag, outside-mu+mark-once, one-IPC
  3-RG, prefix agreement) + SITE 5 cap cell + census registrations; FULL
  package `ok`.
- Wire fixture +1 (`ha_session_refresh_supported:false`, documented regen).
  Lint: rustfmt intersect clean on own hunks; clippy zero on new symbols;
  `gofmt -l` empty; `go vet ./...` clean.

Branch: `fix/9815-ri-member`

Closes #9815

## Why
Routing-instance unit members written with the dash spelling could miss a slash-spelled `interfaces` stanza. Tagged unit 0 then bound the parent device and other tagged units used the unit number instead of the VLAN ID. The same spelling split left those devices in the default-instance next-table ingress set. Cross-spelled tunnel units also needed the declared tunnel-map key so bind and scoping could not disagree.

## What
- Add exact-first, deterministic `LookupInterfaceByLinuxName` fallback matching Linux interface names.
- Use it for daemon unit producer-key binding and `resolveKernelIfNameWith` unit resolution.
- Probe the matched declared stanza spelling for per-unit and interface-level tunnel aliases in both daemon binding and shared scoping resolution.
- Track bare-origin Linux aliases in `DefaultInstanceIngressIfaces` without changing unit-claim rules or reth physical ownership.
- Add daemon and routing VLAN matrices, 8+8 tunnel rows (per-unit and interface-level in both spelling directions), the ordering invariant, and kernel netns VRF-master assertion.

## PR #10159 — dhcprelay: add DHCPv6 relay agent (#9553) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-17)

Branch: `fix/9553-dhcpv6-relay`

## Summary

Implements the supported RFC 8415 DHCPv6 relay subset for
`forwarding-options dhcp-relay dhcpv6` and closes #9553.

Supported configuration and runtime behavior:

- IPv6 server groups with validated global-unicast server addresses.
- Group interfaces, family/group active-server-group fallback, and scalar
  family/group Interface-ID inheritance and precedence.
- Valueless `relay-agent-interface-id` at family or group scope selects the
  authored interface at runtime; a scalar value overrides it. An explicit
  valueless group flag suppresses an inherited family scalar and resolves to
  that group's authored interface.
- Junos Interface-ID modifier forms remain outside xpf's scalar API at both
  scopes, in flat and braced forms: `use-option-82`, `prefix`, `host-name`,
  `routing-instance-name`, `logical-system-name`,
  `use-interface-description`, `include-irb-and-l2`,
  `keep-incoming-interface-id`, `no-vlan-interface-name`, and `use-vlan-id`.
  Strict config rejects all 40 scope/form cases; tolerant config warns and
  leaves the override empty, so unsupported names never become literal
  Option-18 bytes.
- Client multicast intake on `ff02::1:2`, upstream UDP/547 forwarding, RFC
  8415 Relay-Forw/Relay-Reply validation, and client UDP/546 delivery.
- HA master gating, mandatory non-empty matching outer Interface-ID,
  configured-server source/port checks, hop-count and nested-chain validation.
- Fail-closed default rejection of nested downstream Relay-Forw requests and
  valid nested Relay-Reply responses; #9553 exposes no downstream trust knob.
- Default 100-pps ingress token bucket with a two-second burst, per-reason
  `inet6` counters, cancellation-safe socket teardown, startup retry, and live
  link-address/ifindex rebuild.
- Portable first-usable-global link-address selection and existing
  interface-name validation.

Relay-Forward input at hop 8 is discarded; input hop 7 is forwarded as hop 8.
Relay-Reply hop 8 is accepted, while hop 9 is discarded, matching RFC 8415
Table 1 and Section 19.1.2. Live nested Relay-Forw input is rejected before
building an outbound message.

The former full-stanza #9411 refusal is retired only for this schema-declared
subset. Unsupported or incomplete remainder stays under the scoped #9553
strict refusal / tolerant warning gate; apply-groups, apply-groups-except, and
apply-macro metadata remains legal. DHCPv4 relay compilation remains separate.

## Ratchets and baseline disposition

- #8436 duplicate-block conservation records the DHCPv6 group container in the

## PR #10162 — docs: record established-flow move safety verdict (#9778) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-17)

Branch: `fix/9778-queue-safety`

Closes #9778

Verdict at stated HEAD 1c9b202fbcfe7dd5c607729bc4127db8d03360ed: an established-flow ntuple move is NOT SAFE without the unlanded #1749 ownership-transfer barriers. A concrete two-direction (or one-way-flow) interleaving lets the old owner's GC emit Close, remove shared state, and broadcast DeleteSynced to the new WorkerLocalImport replica; the next packet tears down and re-misses the flow. Per-queue UMEM ownership is not the ntuple hazard; cross-queue XDP_REDIRECT remains queue-bound.

Full code-cited verdict and R2/R4/R5/R6 analysis: docs/log/9778.md and issue comment https://github.com/psaab/xpf/issues/9778#issuecomment-5711236952. Hardware-steering docs now replace the deferral. No production code changes.

## P2 recovery boundary

A disposable `xpf-9852-recovery` VM was launched from the cached appliance image, but it booted without the Incus VM agent and without a network device; `incus exec` reported `VM agent isn't currently running`, and `incus info` showed loopback only. It was deleted afterward, so no real forced-failure reboot or management-reachability observation is claimed.

The recovery procedure is a console-only **emergency bypass**. First disable the unit and remove its `RequiredBy` link (`systemctl disable xpf-transit-closed.service`), mask it, reload systemd, and reset its failure. Before starting networkd, physically disconnect every transit/data NIC; if that is unavailable, move or mask each persisted transit `.network`/`.netdev` definition out of `/etc/systemd/network`, daemon-reload, and verify the definitions are absent. Do not rely on `ip link down`, because networkd can re-enable persisted links. Start networkd only with transit definitions isolated and verify service state, network links, management address, and ping from the serial console. After fixing nftables/xpfd, unmask, enable, and start the barrier, then require the journal line `transit barrier installed (inet + bridge forward DROP)` and successful `nft list table bridge xpf_transit_barrier` plus inet listing before restoring moved definitions and reconnecting data NICs; reload/reconfigure networkd and verify links and management reachability. Enable → disable → mask mechanics were dry-run against a temporary systemd root and all exited 0. Real reboot/networkd ordering, bridge transit, and forced-failure recovery remain for the Incus/HA lab; exact steps and expected observations are in `docs/log/9852.md`.

## PR #10168 — daemon: watch link unregister for transit gate (#9848) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-17)

Branch: `fix/9848-link-watch`

Closes #9848

Adds an always-on RTNL link watcher for the transit gate. The watcher runs in the dataplane-enabled Run context and WaitGroup, independently of SNMP, HA, and bootstrap sequencing. Every successful or failed subscription attempt re-reads kernel XDP truth; closed update channels (including ENOBUFS) back off, resubscribe, and re-sync. RTM_DELLINK events wake the existing buffered coalescing gate path, so unregister bursts trigger one fresh census rather than synchronous per-event reasserts. The periodic tick remains the completeness fallback, and an unarmed daemon cannot be reopened by watcher re-sync.

Fail-on-revert coverage:
- Four new cells: all-links-gone DELLINK closure without a tick, lost-notification resubscribe closure, unrelated deletion while another XDP link remains attached, and unarmed re-sync staying closed.
- RED compile proof before implementation.
- Temporary blind-close mutation fails the hardened unrelated-delete cell (no gate wake), proving the regression assertion is live.

Validation:

## PR #10181 — logging: bound syslog failure stalls (#9911) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-17)

Branch: `fix/9911-syslog`

Closes #9911

Timed-out TCP/TLS syslog writes now arm the reconnect cooldown, so subsequent events fail fast before another write or dial. TLS timed-out connections are detached because crypto/tls state is corrupt after a timed-out Write. Close marks clients closed, detaches sockets without waiting on the Send mutex, closes TLS raw sockets before close_notify, and uses a bounded deferred join.

Regression coverage includes text/binary sends, EventReader fanout, Close interruption and drop accounting, a non-unblocking socket join bound, TLS close_notify shutdown, TLS timeout recovery, and partial-frame resync.

Validation after hostile review: targeted 8 top-level tests PASS; targeted -race PASS; full pkg/logging suite 345 PASS, 0 FAIL; full pkg/logging -race PASS. ## PR #10183 — config: refuse WireGuard routing-instance scope (#9909) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-17)

Branch: `fix/9909-wg-vrf`

## Summary
- Add a dedicated strict/tolerant compiler gate for WireGuard routing-instance scope.
- Strict commit rejects both `tunnel routing-instance` and `routing-instances <name> interface <member>` paths, including runtime-normalized `RIListMember` and every declared routing-instance type.
- Tolerant load warns, quarantines every WireGuard record sharing an affected persistent device, and removes its RI-list membership before routing or userspace snapshot consumers can act.
- Bare RI members are expanded through the daemon-parity unit/device machinery; partially surviving bare memberships are narrowed to explicit surviving units.
- Record the #1434 S6 audit, hostile RED-to-GREEN evidence, and final validation in `docs/log/9909.md`.

## Decision
The selected issue contract is commit refusal. `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/wg_control/sock.rs` still wildcard-binds the outer UDP socket and explicitly defers VRF/routing-instance socket binding to #1434 S6; no supported WireGuard VRF-fd path has landed. The inner wgN must not be allowed to pair with a main-table outer socket.

## Hostile review fold (RED -> GREEN)
The four hostile-review cases were reproduced against the pre-fold validator in a temporary config harness before implementation:
- P1-1: `interface wg1.1` was refused but bare `interface wg1` was accepted for a per-unit WG on unit 1.
- P1-2: tolerant load left the shared interface-level `wg0` endpoint alive after a scope-only unit override violation.
- P1-3: tolerant quarantine deleted a bare RI member wholesale, stripping a surviving GRE sibling.
- P2: undeclared `wg0.99` falsely matched parent `wg0`.

The temporary harness was removed after all four cases passed with the fixed validator. Permanent cells additionally cover slash/dash aliases, forwarding instances on strict and tolerant paths, shared-device endpoint removal, bare-member narrowing, and runtime `RIListMember`.

## Baseline RED
A temporary Rust test called the real `bind_wg_socket(0)`, observed `SO_BINDTODEVICE=\"\"`, and observed `ip route get 198.51.100.1` using the host main-table path (`via 172.16.100.1 dev ix0`). The temporary harness was removed. No Rust production code changed. The host lacks `CAP_NET_ADMIN`, so an isolated positive kernel-VRF bind observation was unavailable.

## PR #10194 — userspace-dp: version host static libraries (#9931) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-17)

Branch: `fix/9931-build-libs`

Closes #9931

This records and enforces the host-supplied static libelf, zlib and zstd
archives that libxdp/libbpf consume. The build uses pkg-config with a
static-only header/archive fallback, validates lower floors and Debian
bounds, snapshots each archive under a unique link name, rejects earlier
linker shadows, and exposes linked versions in the Rust ProcessStatus and
startup log.

The static-only fallback requires the selected header and archive to
canonicalize to the same installation prefix. Prefix extraction uses the
innermost /include or /lib layout marker, so a valid install below a
marker-containing parent (for example /var/lib/xpf) is accepted. A
mismatched-prefix fixture fails before C compilation with both paths/prefixes
named; a matched-prefix fixture passes. LD_LIBRARY_PATH is intentionally not
treated as a link-time static archive search path.
