## PR #10202 — userspace-dp: enforce policy on queued ICMP errors (#9948) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-17)

Branch: `fix/9948-icmp-policy`

Closes #9948

## Fix
- Authorize the actual queued prebuilt ICMP wire identity with the flowless L3-aware zone policy before either NAT64 or same-family request can transmit.
- Fail closed for HAInactive, PolicyDenied, and every other terminal/non-sendable disposition. FabricRedirect is the explicit peer-owned exception: #3291 adjudicates it on the owning peer and TX #1946 transmits its prebuilt frame.
- Thread the actual packet ingress zone (logical ingress unit, or authenticated fabric override) into embedded finalization. Build FabricRedirect prebuilts from the finalized peer MAC and zone-stamped source MAC.
- Deny/recycle queued frames and emit PolicyDeny with the policy_deny counter incremented for policy-denied queued errors.

## Regression coverage
- Same-family WAN->LAN default-deny denial: no queue, recycle, PolicyDeny event, and counter.
- Same-family HAInactive forged-error denial with an explicit permit.
- Same-family split-RG FabricRedirect passthrough: target ifindex 21, peer destination MAC, WAN zone stamp, inverse peer parser acceptance, no local deny.
- NAT64 WAN->LAN default-deny denial with rewritten IPv6 event identity, event, and counter.
- NAT64 HAInactive denial with an explicit permit.
- NAT64 split-RG FabricRedirect passthrough with peer L2/zone stamp and inverse peer parser acceptance.
- Existing active-HA permit controls retain positive forwarding.

## PR #10214 — nat: gate address-only pool utilization (#9995) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-17)

Branch: `fix/9995-natpool`

## Summary

`port no-translation` source pools are address-only: they preserve the original source port, so `PortLow`/`PortHigh` and allocator `UsedPorts` do not describe a port-utilization budget. The CLI, REST, gRPC, and Prometheus surfaces now avoid presenting those structural zeros as healthy full availability and 0.0% utilization.

The configuration contract is explicit at `pkg/config/types_security.go:1198-1205`: `PortLow`/`PortHigh` are irrelevant when `PortNoTranslation` is true.

## Behavior

- CLI source-NAT summary and detail render port range, allocated/used, available, and utilization as `NOT APPLICABLE` for a valid address-only pool.
- REST and gRPC stats return zero numeric port fields and `Utilization: "NOT APPLICABLE"` for that mode.
- Prometheus omits the port capacity and usage series for a valid address-only pool (the metrics API has no string N/A representation). A refused pool still emits its existing `total=0` refusal signal.
- Normal PAT pools retain their existing numeric output.

## Verification

- Targeted CLI regressions: 2 passed.
- Targeted REST/metrics regressions: 2 passed, including live occupancy rows proving the used-series omission.
- Targeted gRPC regression: 1 passed.
- Full affected package suites (`go test -json -count=1 ./pkg/cli ./pkg/api ./pkg/grpcapi ./pkg/natpoolalarm ./pkg/ipsecname`): 1,169 CLI, 1,191 API, 1,120 gRPC API, 83 natpoolalarm, and 8 ipsecname tests passed after the review fold.

Closes #9995

## PR #10215 — config/wireguard: reject cross-unit duplicate pubkeys [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-17)

Branch: `fix/9997-wg-dupkey`

## Why

Under an interface-level WireGuard tunnel, per-unit peer slices inherit the interface peers and append unit-owned peers. Two units could author the same pubkey with different AllowedIPs, pass strict commit, and then have the later unit silently dropped by first-wins merged emission.

## What

- Add a deterministic merged-view validator for interface-level WireGuard that excludes expected inherited parent peers and rejects a key authored by two different units before emission.
- Name both canonical unit refs in the strict diagnostic.
- Preserve unit-only and cross-interface behavior.
- On tolerant loads, emit a warning naming the pubkey and both units while retaining defensive first-wins emission; ascending unit order means the lowest-numbered unit's copy survives.
- Qualify the tunnelemit merge comment to its true per-unit strict scope.
- Add three issue-specific fail-on-revert tests, including the inherited-parent redeclaration control and the lowest-unit survivor identity, plus docs/log/9997.md.

## Validation

```text
FAIL: TestWireguardCrossUnitDuplicateLenientWarns9997 (no duplicate warning)
```

## PR #10234 — config: preserve named group leaf instances (#9859) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-17)

Branch: `fix/9859-group-leaf`

## Why

Group leaves that name a child-bearing instance were matched by keyword alone. An inline instance could therefore erase a distinct group instance, while compiler-canonical aliases (for example `01` and `1`) could either duplicate or merge incorrectly. The same admission path also misclassified interface-family `address [ ... ]` as a named container whose first value was its identity, producing duplicate address members when a group single address overlapped an inline bracketed list.

## What

- Match named group leaves by their schema identity span while preserving the legacy path for value lists, scalar leaves, zones, and unresolved schemas.
- Compare compiler-facing identities for OSPF areas, VRRP groups, chassis redundancy groups, regular and CoS interface units, and WireGuard peer public keys. Equal aliases merge with inline precedence; unequal instances are adopted separately.
- Keep CoS `shaping-rate` on scalar inline-wins semantics even when an optional `burst-size` body makes the parsed node a container, including ordered groups and unrelated `apply-groups-except` provenance.
- Preserve packed-leaf source-order behavior and the #10056 parity guard.
- Treat only `inet`/`inet6` interface-family `address` as a bracketed value-list exception. Validate address members, union bracketed and single forms across both AST shapes, deduplicate overlap across all same-keyword nodes, and preserve `KeysQuoted` and `KeysBracketed` masks. Packed options such as `primary`, `preferred`, and `vrrp-group` remain on their existing path.
- When uncertain contributors are unioned, clear `peer.fromGroups` and chained address-member provenance atomically. This keeps hierarchical and flat-set nested-group expansion shape-parity under `apply-groups-except` without selectively pruning one representation.

## Validation

RED on baseline code commit `ca61334fe44ca8b01f6e86ef1ffd86e34a044052`, with the address regression copied onto that baseline (`artifact://29966`): the basic overlap compiled `[10.0.0.1/24 10.0.0.2/24 10.0.0.2/24]`, nested H1/H2 exclusion lost members, and both quoted-CIDR mask cells failed.

GREEN on head `c2938c45a6deda3bb13f9e7993aebc4d8f7c9fa7`:

- `go test ./pkg/config -run 'TestGroupBracketedAddressUnion9859|TestBracketedInterfaceAddress' -count=1 -v` — all address, hierarchical/flat, quote-mask, and packed-option cells passed (`artifact://29960`).
- `go test ./pkg/config -count=1` — passed after the final child-mask regression.
- Final JSON pass-event count: 10,585.
- `go test ./pkg/config -run '9859' -count=1` — 54 named-leaf pass events.
- `go test ./pkg/config -run '9855|10056' -count=1` — 19 packed-leaf compatibility pass events.
- `go test ./pkg/config -run '9801|9831' -count=1` — 23 zone compatibility pass events.
- `gofmt -d` on all five changed Go files and `git diff --check` — clean.

## Review ruling

The conflicting advisory claims are recorded explicitly:

- “Container union still calls `mergeBracketedAddressInto9859(..., s)` on unpruned `s`; implement clone + `pruneExcluded9862`.”
- “Selective pruning is shape-dependent; flat probe excluding H1 kept root address A but pruned chained B; equivalent hierarchical leaf has both values in Keys; #9424 requires dual-shape parity. Union-and-clear must treat address list atomically until member-level provenance exists.”

The decisive H1/H2 regression reproduced the disagreement: prune-only returned `[A,C,D]` for flat syntax while the hierarchical form retained `[A,B,C,D]`. The implementation therefore keeps atomic address union, recursively clears uncertain node/chain provenance (including `peer.fromGroups`), and does not selectively prune.

## PR #10238 — config: drop non-numeric chassis RG/node identities [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-17)

Branch: `fix/10002-chassis-id`

Closes #10002

## Why

Tolerant chassis compilation used an Atoi-then-default-zero path for the two schema-unvalidated identity slots. A typo such as `redundancy-group reth0` therefore became redundancy-group 0, and a malformed RG-scoped node identity could overwrite node 0 priority. The existing #5694 AST gate warned on tolerant load and rejected strict commit, but the tolerant compiler still applied invalid non-numeric identities. A quoted-empty node token also flattened to an empty value, bypassed the gate and defaulted to node 0.

## What

- Drop a non-numeric or explicitly quoted-empty redundancy-group instance before it enters the compiled RG map.
- Ignore a non-numeric or explicitly quoted-empty RG-scoped node statement before it writes priority to node 0.

## PR #10240 — eventengine: bind remediation to planting class (#9984) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-17)

Branch: `fix/9984-plant-class`

## Why

`event-options` remediation was attributed only to the configuration writer at enqueue time. A queued payload could lose its authenticated planting class, fall back to root behavior, or partially mutate a batch before a later target was denied. Legacy payloads were not visibly quarantined, and flat/grouped config shapes could bypass attribution stamping.

## What

- Add `event-options ... plant-class` schema/compiler support and stamp every execution-affecting policy mutation atomically while the config transaction lock is held.
- Carry planting class through config-store, rollback, REST, gRPC, and CLI mutation paths; preserve it through commit, reload, SyncApply, and rollback.
- Cover flat `set` children, block-tail commands, child-value markers, and apply-groups policies without creating duplicate top-level stanzas.
- Prevent metadata-only marker writes from laundering legacy payloads or deleting attribution; existing attributed policies can only be rebound to the authenticated caller's class.
- Revalidate the stamped class against the authorization snapshot immediately before every set/delete batch; missing, deleted, unknown, or denied classes are quarantined before candidate mutation, while explicit `super-user` stamps remain allowed.
- Include quoted/bracketed token masks in the raw fallback signature so an otherwise uncompileable command-provenance change cannot retain stale attribution.
- Add invalid-class metrics, strict `Apply`/snapshot-backed `ApplyWithConfig`, daemon wiring, and documentation.
- Record the new schema leaf in the #2419 compact inventory, #7484 spelling census, #8939 flat-set loser count, and #8690 permanent-exclusion register.

Closes #9984

## PR #10242 — config: validate system host-name admission [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-17)

Branch: `fix/10003-hostname`

Closes #10003

## Why

`system host-name` had no admission validator. Spaced, overlong, malformed-label, and bad-charset values could commit and reach the kernel/durable hostname apply path. The compact hierarchical spelling is read from packed `system` keys, so it needs the same gate as the nested/set leaf. Linux `sethostname(2)` also rejects values above `HOST_NAME_MAX` (64 bytes), even though the DNS-wide total is 253 bytes.

## What

- Add `ValueHostname` + `ValidateSystemHostname` to the system `host-name` leaf.
- Reuse the established LDH/DNS shape: no leading/trailing hyphens, optional absolute-name trailing dot, 63-octet labels, then enforce the Linux 64-byte kernel cap. Empty remains the unset form. Tests explicitly cover raw 64/65-byte values and 64/65-byte values including a trailing dot (the dot counts).
- Gate compact `system host-name value;` compiler reads strictly; `CompileConfigLenient` warns and retains invalid values for tolerant Load/SyncApply no-brick behavior. Compact strict/tolerant/store matrices include spaced, bad-charset, 300-byte, and DNS-valid 65-byte values with and without trailing dots.
- Keep `applyHostname`'s empty and unchanged early returns; add a post-guard tolerant belt that logs and refuses retained malformed/overlong values before `sethostname(2)` or `/etc/hostname`. The belt does not mutate `cfg.Warnings`, preserving the daemon's immutable-after-publish contract.
- Keep the #8597 valueless host-name control, updating its expected diagnostic to the typed leaf's `missing value` form.
- Correct the `ValueHostname` comment to describe leaf-specific validators, and record the DDNS/shared-shape distinction in the issue log.
- Two commits: code/tests (`f1859dd28`), then evidence log (`4631c18a2`).

## Validation

### RED then GREEN

Before implementation, the new config cells were run with:

```text

```

Controlled revert proofs then executed each behavioral failure (all mutations were restored and none were committed):

- Returning `nil` from `ValidateSystemHostname` made the malformed validator/schema/strict Store matrix fail with `expected an error, got nil` or accepted invalid values.
- Removing the compact compiler gate made strict compact tests accept invalid values, made the lenient config test report `warnings=[]`, and made all configstore tolerant cases report `warnings=[]`.
- Disabling the Linux 64-byte condition made direct validator/schema tests accept the DNS-valid 65-byte name.
- Disabling the two existing `applyHostname` early returns made its empty and unchanged subtests attempt `sethostname` and fail.
- Disabling the new tolerant apply belt made the invalid-value subtest call `sethostname` (and would permit the durable write).

After restoring the exact production code, the cells passed:

## PR #10249 — termsafe: retain incomplete UTF-8 suffix at bound [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-17)

Branch: `fix/10009-termsafe`

Closes #10009

## Why
At the #7389 threshold, the streaming writer emitted its whole residual buffer. If that buffer ended at an upstream write boundary in the middle of a valid UTF-8 rune, the display sanitizer correctly escaped those bytes as invalid, making identical valid streams render differently by chunk boundary.

## What
- At threshold emission only, detect a valid but incomplete UTF-8 suffix with `utf8.RuneStart` and `utf8.FullRune`.
- Emit the complete prefix through the existing sanitizer and carry a copied suffix of at most `utf8.UTFMax-1` bytes into the next write.
- Leave malformed encodings in the emitted prefix for immediate `\xHH` escaping; `Flush` still sanitizes a truly truncated final suffix.
- Add #10009 fail-on-revert tests for every split point of 2-, 3-, and 4-byte runes, byte-at-a-time delivery, malformed tails, and Flush safety. Record the implementation in `docs/log/10009.md`.

## Validation

### RED (before implementation)
`go test ./pkg/termsafe -run 'Test(BoundEmissionRetainsPartialRune|BoundEmissionRuneDeliveredByteAtATime|BoundEmissionEscapesInvalidTailImmediately|FlushEscapesTruncatedTail|BoundHeldSuffixCompletedByInvalidByteStaysSafe)_10009'` failed the two valid-rune boundary tests. The old bound path rendered partial bytes as `\\xHH` (for example `\\xc3\\xa9`) instead of the original rune; the invalid-tail and Flush safety pins passed.

### GREEN (after implementation)
The same selector passed all five #10009 test functions. The tests compare the valid stream's expected render across every rune split and byte-at-a-time delivery, and assert that all invalid/truncated output remains valid UTF-8.

## PR #10251 — fix: reject zone-scoped filter addresses (#10011) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-17)

Branch: `fix/10011-filter-zone`

Closes #10011

## Why

Firewall filter address classification used Go's netip parsers directly. They accept IPv6 `%zone` scope text even though the userspace Rust matcher cannot represent a zone. The token was therefore accepted by strict validation, omitted by Rust `parse_address`, and absent from the existing `address_unrepresentable` fail-closed marker path.

## What

- Reject `%`-scoped filter address literals in `classifyFilterAddrFamily`, with a strict diagnostic naming the filter, term, token, and zone/scope cause.
- Keep `recordFilterAddrTokens` keyed on the shared classifier so tolerant loads record the raw token, emit `address_unrepresentable`, and fail the whole userspace snapshot closed.
- Follow the #5875 SNAT-pool precedent: stripping `%zone` would silently change the operator's authored address semantics, while retaining it would ship a token the Rust matcher cannot represent. Rejecting it is safer; tolerant loads retain the raw token and fail closed through the marker.
- Add strict, tolerant, Go snapshot-marker, and Rust runtime regressions.

## Validation

- **RED (strict/tolerant/classifier):** Before the classifier change, `go test ./pkg/config -run 'TestFilter(ZoneScopedAddressRejectedStrict|ZoneScopedAddressLenientWarnsAndRecords|UnscopedLinkLocalCompiles)|TestClassifyFilterAddrFamilyZoneScope' -count=1` failed: scoped IPv6 strict cases were accepted, the tolerant warning was absent, and the classifier accepted scoped IPv6 forms.

- **GREEN (Go compile-to-marker handoff):** Restoring the classifier made that same marker command pass; the scoped token stayed verbatim beside the valid prefix and set `AddressUnrepresentable`.
- **RED (Rust runtime contract):** With the `address_unrepresentable` preflight guard temporarily disabled, `cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml address_zone_scoped_marker_fails_closed_not_dropped_10011` failed 0 passed / 1 failed and printed a compiled `FilterState`, demonstrating the scoped token was dropped while the surviving prefix compiled. This is a runtime-contract guard; the fail-on-revert handoff proof is the Go compile-to-marker cell above.

## PR #10252 — dataplane: render terminal action over next-term contradiction [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-17)

Branch: `fix/10012-filter-render`

Closes #10012

## Why

A tolerant / peer-sync snapshot can carry a real `action` together with `next_term=true`. Runtime enforcement is fail-closed: Rust uses `continue_term = action.is_empty() && routing_instance.is_empty()`, so a real action terminates. The snapshot renderer instead branched on `NextTerm` first and displayed only `then next term (fall-through)`, which lied about the effective decision.

## What

- Make `RenderFirewallFilterSnapshot` use the runtime-effective predicate: only empty action + empty routing-instance is fall-through.
- Render the terminating action for action+next-term and routing-instance+next-term shapes.
- Preserve the contradictory input disclosure with `then next term (ignored — contradictory with terminating action)`; this shows both what arrived on the tolerant path and what runtime actually does without changing enforcement.
- Keep pure fall-through and pure terminal rendering unchanged.
- Add #10012 fail-on-revert tests, including a real `ParseSetCommand` → `ConfigTree.SetPath` → `CompileConfigLenient` tolerant-config path, plus controls.
- Record evidence in `docs/log/10012.md`.

## RED → GREEN proof

Selector:

`go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace -run 'TestSnapshotRender(ContradictoryActionNextTermTerminates10012|PureFallThroughControl10012|PureTerminalControl10012|ImplicitFallThroughWithoutBit10012|RoutingInstanceNextTermHandBuilt10012)$' -count=1`

With the renderer reverted, the four action+next-term subtests were RED (action omitted, bare fall-through claimed, no contradiction annotation); the empty-action-without-bit and routing-instance+next-term parity cells were also RED. Pure fall-through and pure terminal controls stayed GREEN. With the fix restored, the selector is GREEN: 5 top-level tests / 9 pass reports.

## Validation

- `go test -json -count=1 ./pkg/dataplane/userspace`: 1734 top-level tests, 2766 pass reports.
- `go test -json -count=1 ./pkg/cli`: 584 top-level tests, 1175 pass reports.

## PR #10257 — snmp: render unknown-class OIDs as noSuchObject (#10017) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-17)

Branch: `fix/10017-snmp-oid`

Closes #10017

## Why

`getOIDValueSnap` collapsed unknown objects and missing instances into the same nil result. The v2c and v3 GET renderers then emitted `noSuchInstance` for both cases, violating RFC 3416 for an unknown-class OID.

## What

- Added typed absence classification in the shared SNMP lookup:
  - unknown object/column -> `noSuchObject`
  - known scalar/table object with a missing or malformed instance -> `noSuchInstance`
- Updated v2c and v3 default-context GET rendering to preserve the lookup's exception tag.
- Updated v3 non-default-context GET rendering to use the same per-class OID classification; GETNEXT/GETBULK keep `endOfMibView` for an empty context view.
- Added v2c and v3 regression coverage for scalar, ifTable, ifXTable, unknown-object, and unknown-instance cases.
- Updated the SNMP context documentation and recorded the completion evidence in `docs/log/10017.md`.

## RED-then-GREEN proof

The pre-fix targeted run failed the eight unknown-object cells (four v2c and four v3): each returned `noSuchInstance (0x81)` instead of `noSuchObject (0x80)`. The eight unknown-instance cells passed on the pre-fix implementation as preservation controls.

A fail-on-revert mutation temporarily changed both known-object `noSuchInstance` returns in `oidAbsenceTag` to `noSuchObject`. The focused v2c/v3 instance run then failed all eight unknown-instance subtests, proving a blind tag swap is rejected. The production returns were restored before the final green run.

Final targeted run passed all 16 v2c/v3 matrix subtests, both matrix parent tests, and both v3 context tests (20 passing test events).

## PR #10263 — measure: characterize rolling-cut TCP stall and stream starvation [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-17)

Branch: `fix/10023-tcp-stall`

## Summary

- add a non-mutating loss-cluster sampler for 100 ms per-stream iperf3 JSONL, ping, `ss`, journal, and bounded snaplen packet evidence;
- add an offline analyzer for historical iperf3 text and `-J --json-stream` JSONL, including per-stream/SUM masking, truncated-tail handling, ICMP sequence-gap loss, and lifecycle budget phases;
- retain the historical #9486 records and one lock-held, instrumented secondary cut under `docs/log/10023/raw/` with a SHA-256 manifest.

The client-side pcap is the packet source of truth because AF_XDP-owned firewall queues are invisible to the firewall kernel `any` device. Firewall pcap headers, stderr, and statuses are retained and explicitly characterize that visibility limit.

## NEEDS-MAJOR finding closure

1. **Human iperf sender/receiver rows:** completion rows are recognized and skipped as summaries; malformed interior interval rows still fail closed. A completion-only/headerless text capture is accepted when it contains valid completion records.
2. **Clock and iperf-origin attribution:** the historical `1.46 s after forced-secondary` and `1.78 s before shutdown` values are now explicitly **CONDITIONAL / UNRESOLVED**. Historical `clock-skew.log` lacks the LAN-VM calibration and the old `19:51:13.215` origin was a first-ping epoch, not an iperf timestamp. The correction is also posted on [#10261](https://github.com/psaab/xpf/issues/10261#issuecomment-5722259918).
3. **Text-vs-JSON dispatch:** bracket-prefixed iperf text is dispatched to the text parser unless the content parses as JSON; the former `textboot-iperf.log` CLI failure now exits successfully.
4. **Missing fine-grained cut:** a lock-held 60-second cut was run with 100 ms iperf, 100 ms ping, per-socket `ss`, journal lifecycle, and client/firewall pcap recorders. The driver used `/usr/local/share/xpf/staged/xpfd upgrade --rolling` on the secondary and exited 0.
5. **Raw records and 3.000/2.903 reconciliation:** historical, baseline, and cut source records are committed in `docs/log/10023/raw/` (60 manifest entries, including JSONL, ping/ss, journals, metadata, statuses, stderr, pcaps, and exact cut driver output). The report pins `STOP→process-start=2.903 s` versus `STOP→manager initialization=3.000 s` as different journal milestones.
6. **Remote directory safety:** every invocation uses a unique PID/random run ID, refuses an existing remote path before `mkdir`, and never recursively deletes a basename-derived path. `--out /` and non-directory outputs are rejected.
7. **Recorder and transfer completion:** each recorder writes its own status; all required pulls, data/stderr files, pcap headers, and status allowlists are checked before `sampler complete`. iperf/ping/ss require status 0; only time-bounded journal/tcpdump recorders may finish with timeout status 124. Pull failures leave the artifact directory and return 1.

## Instrumented cut result

The actual iperf JSON start event is `2026-09-17 22:46:08.226Z`. The run contains 600 100-ms intervals for each of four sockets and SUM, with zero zero-throughput rows, zero SUM masking, zero cwnd-floor windows, and no stream gaps. Maximum retransmits were 1 on socket 5 and 0 on sockets 7/9/11. Ping returned 571 contiguous replies (1..571), no qualifying gaps, and `max_loss=0.0`. `ss` retained 438 samples and all four source ports (52586, 52592, 52602, 52612) appeared in every sample. The client pcap has 31,352 decoded packets; both firewall captures are valid 24-byte headers with stderr showing 0 packets received by the AF_XDP-invisible filter.

The cut driver logged drain start/complete, STOPPED, STARTED, COMMITTED, re-sync, and election rejoin. Its host window was `2026-09-17T22:46:12.949197045Z` to `22:46:22.569570316Z`. Clock samples bracket every remote read: deploy-host-minus-fw1 is bounded by 54.722542..55.135825 s at sampler start and 54.741208..55.128392 s at end; the LAN offset is likewise bounded at -0.145211..+0.165088 s and -0.141861..+0.175789 s. The fw1 forced-secondary marker maps to host 22:46:12.958..13.372 s, overlapping the driver start within the measurement bound. This healthy cut is a comparison and calibration; it does not prove the historical Sep-13 root cause.

The final no-cut baseline has 50 intervals per stream/SUM, 48 contiguous ping replies, 35 `ss` samples, no retransmits, no zero/masked rows, and `max_loss=0.0`.

## Verification

- `python3 -m unittest scripts/test_cut_stall_analyze.py`: **24/24 OK**;
- `python3 -m py_compile scripts/cut_stall_analyze.py`: OK;
- `bash -n scripts/cut_stall_sampler.sh`: OK;
- sampler guard matrix (`--help`, invalid interval, invalid tcpdump count, `--out /`): all rejected with rc 2 and non-empty diagnostics;
- historical iperf/ping, headerless text, final-tail policy, baseline JSONL/ping, and cut JSONL/ping were re-analyzed successfully;
- `cd docs/log/10023/raw && sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS`: **60/60 OK**;
- source/docs whitespace check is clean; byte-preserved raw captures retain their original trailing spaces where present.

Closes #10023

## PR #10271 — userspace: pin deferred tick debt convergence (#10041) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-18)

Branch: `fix/10041-debt-gen`

## Summary

Issue #10041's coherent repair is already landed on master through #9824, #9642, and #10064:

- #9824 rebases deferred compiled snapshots strictly above helper high-water, closing the equality-landing path.
- #9520 supplies the content digest gate, and #9642 adopts the generation of a conflict retry that may have landed without an ACK.
- #10064 avoids retaining a same-generation resampled tick copy while preserving retry-debt latching and fail-closed control state.

This PR adds the missing fail-on-revert regression suite and verification record. The verify-first check found no remaining production RED, so no production source was changed.

## Regression coverage

`deferred_tick_debt_10041_test.go` uses an independent helper admission model and pins all three issue traces:

1. **Equality landing (r2):** reserve -> lost unallocated worker-arm republish -> deferred compiled apply. The apply-time rebase must offer above the helper and admit on the first service tick.
2. **Resample/no-op writeback (r3-main):** resampled beta lands with a lost response; alpha no-op writeback clears partial debt and helper digest; conflict retry lands with a lost response; the retry generation must be retained.
3. **Tick drift (r3-short):** beta then alpha resampling across ticks, lost conflict retry, then identical re-offer to clear remaining partial debt.

Each cell checks helper-installed content through the model's content digest, compares that digest with the retained snapshot digest at convergence, checks generation adoption, verifies fail-closed ctrl during unknown outcome, and checks terminal convergence.

## RED -> GREEN evidence

- Equality RED with the #9824 rebase hunk reverted in an isolated `81fbf36ab` worktree: `deferred compiled generation = 8, want helper+1 = 10`.
- r3-main RED on pre-#9642 `81fbf36ab`: `helper=9 manager=8 retained=8` after the landed-but-unacknowledged retry.
- r3-short RED on pre-#9642 `81fbf36ab`: `helper 9 manager 8 retained 8 partial 2`.
- GREEN: `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run 'TestDeferredTick(EqualityLanding|ResampleNoOpWriteback|TickDrift)Converges10041' -count=1 -v` (3/3).
- Stability GREEN: same cells with `-count=5` (15/15) and `-race -count=1` (3/3), including the digest comparisons.

## Affected suite

- `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -count=1` — PASS (55.922s).
- `gofmt -d pkg/dataplane/userspace/deferred_tick_debt_10041_test.go` — clean.
- `git diff --check` — clean.

Closes #10041

## PR #10332 — dist: assert reprepro Release freshness (#10123) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-18)

Branch: `fix/10123-reprepro`

# #10123 — build-apt-repo: assert reprepro Release freshness

Closes #10123

## Change

The `XPF_APT_TOOL=reprepro` path now post-checks the emitted
`dists/$SUITE/Release` before returning:

- Release must exist.
- `Date:` and `Valid-Until:` must each occur exactly once.
- Both values must parse as dates.
- `Valid-Until` must equal the emitted `Date` plus `VALID_DAYS*86400` exactly.

The reprepro-specific delta is documented in the script and log: reprepro
chooses `Date` during includedeb/export, so the exact expected epoch derives
from the emitted Date rather than this process's pre-export wall clock. The
same legitimate behavior is pinned without an arbitrary tolerance.

## RED → GREEN

- Pre-fix full new module: **11 tests, 8 failures**. Duplicate/missing,
  one-day-short, and one-second-off Release fields (including real reprepro
  `ValidFor: 0d`) returned success; the three valid controls passed.
- Post-fix full new module: **11/11 OK** against real reprepro 5.3.1,
  GPG 2.4.9, and dpkg-deb. Real `ValidFor: 7d` emitted exactly one
  `Valid-Until == Date + 7d`; real `ValidFor: 0d` failed closed. The fake
  reprepro battery covers duplicate/missing Date and Valid-Until, malformed
  horizon, missing Release, and +1 second exactness.

## Verification

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/dist -p 'test_*.py'`: **101 OK**
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'`: **144 OK**
- `scripts/dist/selftest.sh`: **56 passed, 0 failed**

## PR #10347 — feeds: block private destination SSRF (#10177) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-18)

## PR #10378 — daemon: enforce SSH trust for config archival [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-18)

Branch: `fix/10298-scp`

## Summary

- Enforce the daemon-rendered SSH known-hosts file for config archival scp.
- Refuse missing or empty trust, wrong host keys, and leading-dash destinations before transfer.
- Disable system-wide known-hosts fallback so the rendered trust file is the sole source.
- Document host-key rotation and the cleartext archive threat model.

Closes #10298

## Security behavior

Archival now passes StrictHostKeyChecking=yes, UserKnownHostsFile=<rendered path>, GlobalKnownHostsFile=/dev/null, and BatchMode=yes. A host-key mismatch fails the transfer; an operator rotates a key by committing the replacement under security ssh-known-hosts, after which the daemon rewrites its managed file before the next transfer.

## Verification

- GREEN after fix: TestScpArchiveTransfer10298 — 4 passed, 0 failed; the real /usr/sbin/sshd + /usr/bin/scp loopback cell refused the wrong key and transferred with the rotated trusted key.

## PR #10386 — configstore: persist rollback slot timestamps and comments [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-18)

Branch: `fix/10299-slotmeta`

## Problem

After every commit rewrote all canonical text rollback slots, restart loading used each inode mtime, so retained entries appeared to have one timestamp. `HistoryEntry.Comment` also disappeared across restart.

## Change

- Persist per-slot timestamp and commit comment in a durable `.configdb/rollback-meta.json` sidecar.
- Bind each metadata record to the exact rollback-slot bytes and rewritten file identity (device/inode/mtime) with SHA-256, so a crash during a same-bytes no-op slot rewrite cannot attach an older comment to the new generation.
- Gate metadata identity capture on successful slot publication; handle post-rename durability errors without mistaking the old inode for the new one.
- Restore metadata on load, retaining mtime/empty-comment fallback for legacy or mismatched sidecars.
- Add restart regression cells for distinct timestamps, comment round-trip, and stale duplicate-byte manifests.
- Document the sidecar and RED-then-GREEN evidence.

## Verification

## PR #10389 — fix: close load and REST authz bypasses (#10305 #10306) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-18)

Branch: `fix/10305-loadmerge`

## Problem

#10305: the load authorization gate classified trigger-led bodies as flat while the config store routed the same bodies hierarchically. A restricted caller could place an allowed `annotate`/`copy`/`rename`/`insert` or bare single-token trigger before a denied subtree; the gate adjudicated only the trigger while `load merge` or `load override` reached the unchecked hierarchical body.

#10306: REST configuration gates used wider `json.Unmarshal` structs than their handlers and returned nil on decode errors. Wrong-typed gate-only fields and trailing data therefore made the gate allow a request whose handler would decode and mutate it.

## Change

- Share `config.IsFlatLoadLine` between `LoadMutationLines` and all config-store load classifiers. The shared predicate is exactly the store's four replay verbs plus a path token.
- Decode restricted REST routes once into the exact handler request type with `json.Decoder.Decode`, preserving unknown-field and trailing-data semantics. Restore the body for the handler and fail closed on read/decode errors; unrestricted classes remain handler-decoded.
- Add fail-on-revert regressions across config, configstore, CLI, and REST, including merge/override and load-set controls and all requested REST disagreement instances.
- Record RED/GREEN evidence in `docs/log/10305-10306.md`.

## Verification

Targeted RED-then-GREEN matrices pass in `pkg/config`, `pkg/configstore`, `pkg/cli`, and `pkg/api`. The full `pkg/api` suite passes (675 test functions) and the full `pkg/cli` suite passes (599 test functions). The full configstore suite has the parent-verified pre-existing `TestUnknownSecurityStanzaIsStillAccepted8296` failure; the full config suite has the parent-verified clean-master `TestAggregateChargeOrderFollowsWithinRuleSetRuleOrder_6812` failure. `TestShowTextGolden` is also a known parent-verified pre-existing failure. None are in this scope or changed.

Closes #10305
Closes #10306

## PR #10398 — fix(afxdp): prevent untranslated neighbor-MISS reinjection [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-18)

Branch: `fix/10311-neighmiss`

## Problem

A neighbor-MISS frame could be parked with its translated pending decision while the shared slow-path outlet copied the original untranslated decision. That exposed the internal source and delivered the packet twice when neighbor retry later replayed the translated frame.

## Change

- Preserve the composed NAT decision for non-buffered MissingNeighbor fallthroughs.
- Suppress the slow-path copy for parked frames and for duplicate/capacity/seed-refused MISS outcomes that are recycled rather than delivered.
- Add interface-SNAT, static-SNAT, and NPTv6 RED/GREEN cells, including real `retry_pending_neigh` cross-UMEM delivery assertions.
- Add a duplicate-hop fail-on-revert pin and preserve the production outlet source guard.

- #10311 interface-SNAT/static-SNAT/NPTv6 cells: 3 passed (`artifact://41518`); each parks once, performs no slow-path copy, then queues exactly one translated replay after neighbor resolution.
- Duplicate-hop fail-on-revert cell: 1 passed (`artifact://41521`).

## PR #10399 — fix: resolve native RI members in both directions (#10312) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-19)

Branch: `fix/10312-rimain`

## Problem

Routing-instance member interfaces without a matching PBR routing-instance term resolved in MAIN, allowing WAN-default leakage. Reverse session construction also lost the member routing-domain identity. Three reverse leak-incarnation arms then continued to query MAIN after the client RI fix, allowing stale RI-leak resolutions to bypass #9951 revocation. An invalid RI identity could also be misread as an unstamped MAIN lookup.

## Change

- Resolve native per-family RI tables for forward fallback.
- Preserve native client-domain scope for reverse session, HA-synthesized reverse, and the transit poll session-miss path.
- Keep explicit TUN paths zero-stamped and directional PBR precedence unchanged.
- Fail closed for an unresolvable nonzero native domain instead of falling through to MAIN.
- Centralize leak provenance from the validated install-table identity across reverse synthesis, peer UpsertSynced, shared-hit materialization, and current-incarnation revalidation. `Unresolvable` never queries MAIN.
- Add forward, reverse, family, flowless, terminal, revocation, invalid-identity, and control regression cells.

## PR #10414 — docs: constrain fabric stamp trust boundary [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-19)

Branch: `fix/10105-stampauth`

## Decision

Document-and-constrain. The existing fabric stamp wire format remains unchanged. Fabric DATA links are supported only as a private two-peer L2 domain: direct-attached, a dedicated two-peer VLAN/bridge, or operator-provided MACsec. Shared switching with a live split-RG placement is unsupported.

## Evidence recorded

- The current stamp is a six-byte source-MAC encoding (`02:bf:72:fe:<zone-id>`) with a public deterministic StableZoneID hash; an L2-adjacent third speaker can copy the exact punt shape when the split-RG residual is live.
- The repository's reference HA wiring uses a private two-peer fabric bridge. Production L2 adjacency is not observable from source, so the record distinguishes that known reference from the possible shared-switch attacker placement.
- A strict compiler advisory is emitted when `fabric-interface` or `fabric1-interface` is configured. It is advisory—not a hard reject, because config compilation cannot inspect the cable plant—and is suppressed only on tolerant boot/peer-sync paths with a dedicated option.
- The advisory suppression is independent of existing auth-key leniency; regression coverage catches accidental coupling.
- The measured single-thread Go 1.26.4 baseline on Intel Xeon D-2146NT is preserved with an exact rerun recipe: Ed25519 verify 88,066.9 ns/op (88.07 cores at 1 Mpps), Ed25519 sign 36,552.4 ns/op (36.55 cores at 1 Mpps), and HMAC-SHA256 compute/compare 3,439.1 ns/op (3.44 cores at 1 Mpps). This bounds why signatures are rejected for the stage-9 hot path and why miss-only verification still leaves an L2-spam CPU-DoS concern.
- The decision record explicitly covers replay: a tuple-bound MAC or signature prevents unauthorized stamp cloning but does not prevent exact authenticated-packet replay. Full anti-replay would require epoch/sequence/nonce state, worker-reorder handling, failover transfer, and reboot coordination.
- The mixed-version matrix requires any future armed MAC/signature sender to use a distinct non-legacy marker/envelope; a pre-feature receiver must never mistake it for an authenticated legacy stamp. The selected no-wire path has byte-for-byte old/new interoperability.

## Verification

- `go test ./pkg/config -run 'TestFabricStamp|TestCompileGolden4406' -count=1`
- `go test ./pkg/config -count=1` (passes: `ok github.com/psaab/xpf/pkg/config 237.373s`)
- `git diff --check`

Closes #10105

## PR #10424 — fix: stop expired conntrack wire leakage (#10419) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-19)

Branch: `fix/10419-conntrackleak`

## Problem

Session expiry removed the local row before its Close/shared teardown was drained. A subsequent lookup could miss locally, rematerialize the still-published shared row, and forward an expired wire tuple. Missing-neighbor seeds do not emit Close deltas and needed a separately fenced retirement path.

## Change

- Retire `MissingNeighborSeed` shared state before resource teardown, only when the stored origin and non-zero stable session ID match the expired incarnation.
- Drain all expiry deltas before the next packet poll, ahead of overflow extraction, so ordinary Close teardown cannot be bypassed by shared rematerialization.
- Add fail-on-revert cells for seed removal, same-key/session-ID replacement preservation, ordinary-origin preservation, and the production expiry ordering bridge.
- Record RED-then-GREEN evidence in `docs/log/10419.md`.

## Verification

Temporary revert probes were observed RED:

- `expired_missing_neighbor_seed_retires_shared_wire_state_10419`: 1 failed, 2 passed with retirement disabled.
- `seed_retirement_preserves_same_key_replacement_10419`: 1 failed when the session-ID fence was removed.
- `seed_retirement_preserves_same_id_non_seed_replacement_10419`: 1 failed when the origin fence was removed.
- `worker_loop_orders_expiry_teardown_before_poll_10419`: 1 failed when the immediate production drain was removed.

Final scoped suites:

```text
cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml expiry_shared_retire_10419 -- --nocapture
cargo test: 4 passed (14 suites, 6611 filtered, 0.00s)

cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml 'afxdp::worker::loop_body' -- --nocapture
cargo test: 34 passed (14 suites, 6581 filtered, 0.00s)
```

The live `wire_conntrack_lifecycle` gate remains owned by the #10030 harness lane and is rerun against this product fix after it lands.

## Scope

Only `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/worker/loop_body/mod.rs`, its test-only regression module, and `docs/log/10419.md` changed. No forwarding, CoS, worker queue, poll descriptor, slow path, session-glue test, or Go source changed.

## PR #10425 — [9506] Ship S3 xfrm divert coexistence layer [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-19)

Branch: `fix/9506-s3spike`

# S3 spike report — fence + divert coexistence

## Verdict

**PROVEN-spike; S4 handoff required.** The kernel placement and fail-closed coexistence questions are proven on Linux 7.0.13. The daemon lifecycle machinery required by the T12 permit/overlay/conntrack ACK cells does not exist in this tree; those cells remain owned by S4 and are not claimed here.

## Measured evidence

- **Bridge step 0:** `ip link set st99 master br0` returned `RTNETLINK answers: Invalid argument` (exit 2). `st99` remained unenslaved. Control veth enslaving succeeded. The plan-conditional degraded branch is therefore taken; no bridge-xfrmi packet-receipt claim is made.
- **Priority map:** `xpf_ipsec_divert` forward/input chains were installed in both inet and bridge at priority `-175`; `xpf_transit_barrier` forward remained at priority `0`. `nft -j list ruleset` showed no same-priority tie.
- **Leave-alone proof:** routed UDP without capture was not delivered; inet fence counter advanced to `1 packet / 39 bytes`.
- **NFQUEUE ACCEPT proof:** a real XFRM-decrypted packet reached queue `1101`; the listener returned NFQUEUE ACCEPT; the packet was not delivered to the destination and the inet fence counter advanced to `2 packets / 80 bytes`. ACCEPT resumes normal traversal and does not bypass the fence.
- **Bridge control proof:** ordinary bridged veth traffic was not delivered; bridge fence counter advanced to `2 packets / 168 bytes`. This proves the bridge fence leg only; bridge-xfrmi receipt is intentionally unclaimed after step-0 rejection.
- **Host-bound proof:** a real XFRM-decrypted host-bound packet reached queue `1102`; after ACCEPT it was not delivered locally, proving capture occurs before the local input path while the fence/input policy remains fail-closed.
- **VRF premise:** `st99` enslaved to a VRF. After attachment, queue `1102` received zero packets while a temporary master-name input counter saw `1 packet / 38 bytes`; the forward fence counter also advanced while queue `1101` received zero. This confirms the l3mdev/master substitution premise. It is kernel-hook evidence, not a daemon publication/ACK result.

## T12 mapping

Proven in S3: unique family/hook queue provenance; `-175` divert before priority-0 fence; no bypass flag; NFQUEUE ACCEPT resumes to fence; leave-alone traffic remains fenced; bridge degraded branch is explicit and unattributed combined-flush errors are not classified as bridge-only; VRF hook behavior matches the plan premise.

Machinery-blocked and handed to S4: install-failure publication/rollback; ACK timeout and ambiguous post-commit handling; staged success/mixed-OPEN exclusion; VRF publication/overlay/conntrack ACK; clear/retire and stuck-DOWN lifecycle cells. No implementation for those daemon paths exists in the current tree, so S3 does not fabricate green lifecycle results.

## Shipped layer

- `pkg/nftables/ipsec_divert.go`: separate inet/bridge divert installer, four provenance classes, priority-collision guard, bridge capability classifier, one combined flush when bridge support exists, explicit inet-only degraded branch, and idempotent removal.
- `pkg/nftables/ipsec_divert_test.go`: renderer/provenance tests, live private-netns dual-family install/readback, narrow degraded classifier, and mutation-type-based combined-flush failure test.
- `pkg/nftables/netlink_installer.go` plus daemon test seams: Installer surface for the shippable S3 layer.
- `pkg/config/compiler_ipsec_plaintext_warn.go`: authorized §7.1/§7.2 advisory wording aligned with the measured fence-dropped FORWARD and local-input residuals.

## Verification

`go test ./pkg/nftables ./pkg/daemon ./pkg/config` — passed.
`go test ./pkg/nftables -run '^TestIpsecDivert' -count=1` — passed.

Refs #9506

## PR #10449 — fix(nat64): preserve original embedded ICMP length [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-19)

Branch: `fix/10432`

## Problem
NAT64 embedded ICMP rewrites used the bytes captured in the ICMP quote to populate the translated inner IPv4 Total Length or IPv6 Payload Length. RFC 7915 requires the translated embedded header to retain the original inner datagram length even when the ICMP quote contains only the IP header and 8 L4 bytes.

## Change
- Preserve original inner length independently from physically emitted quote bytes in v6→v4 and v4→v6 embedded rewrites.
- Subtract stripped IPv6 extension-header bytes and add generated IPv6 Fragment Header bytes where applicable.
- Keep all emitted copies bounded by the fixed scratch buffer and fail closed on malformed/unrepresentable lengths.
- Add direct and PMTUD-shape regression cells for 1500-byte originals with truncated quotes.

## Verification
- RED: all four new cells fail on the baseline/reverted production hunk with quote-derived lengths.
- GREEN: `cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml 10432 --quiet -- --nocapture` — 4 passed.
- GREEN: `cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml 'nat64::tests::' --quiet -- --nocapture` — 193 passed.
- Broad `nat64` filter failures were reproduced unchanged on baseline and documented in `docs/log/10432.md`.

Closes #10432

## PR #10451 — grpcapi: propagate caller cancellation through dialPeer [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-19)

Branch: `fix/10440-dialpeer`

## Problem

dialPeer ran each GetStatus liveness probe under context.Background(), so a canceled or short-deadline request could continue walking peer session tables for up to two seconds per fabric.

## Change

Thread the caller context through every grpcapi dialPeer caller. Each probe now derives its two-second timeout from that context, checks cancellation before each fabric attempt, and returns the corresponding gRPC cancellation/deadline status without probing another fabric. Added fail-on-revert cells for already-canceled callers, deadline propagation, and the healthy probe control.

Phase 2a needs authenticated witness surfaces for S5 capture/reinject accounting without claiming downstream delivery from a Rust TUN write. The harness must preserve absent-versus-zero semantics and join Go and Rust observations on one authority tuple.

Keeping those owners separate makes residual uncertainty explicit while run_id, generation, and permit_epoch provide the authenticated join.

## PR #10481 — nftables: attest q0 delivered witness (#10478) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-20)

Branch: `fix/10478-2c-delivered`

## Why

`Written` only proves that the daemon wrote a packet to the userspace TUN. It does not prove that the kernel delivered that packet through the intended transit fence. This change adds an independent, kernel-owned q0 mark/counter witness while preserving the existing transit-gate verdict and reassertion behavior.

## What

- Add the inet-only `xpf_transit_q0_delivered` counter to the exact q0 conjunction (`iifname=xpf-usp1`, `mark=0x58465001`, mask `0xffffffff`) immediately before the final ACCEPT. The CounterObj is non-terminating and verdict-neutral; bridge has no witness counter.
- Read back the named object and exact armed rule/Objref. Any absent, detached, disarmed, malformed, unreadable, or unequal state remains unavailable or reinstalls through the existing fence path.
- Preserve the armed-fence one-second reassertion cadence. Skip replacement only when all four gates hold: (1) witness q0 spec, (2) prior install succeeded, (3) cached spec equality, and (4) canonical live equality. Mutable packet/byte counters and kernel handles are excluded; readback doubt always reinstalls. This preserves a monotonic counter across ordinary ticks.
- Baseline at pipeline Start, export a start-bound windowed delta, and latch unavailable on absence, read error, reset, or negative delta without lazy re-baselining.
- Join the harness on `run_id`, `generation`, and `permit_epoch`, but take `delivered_available` and `delivered` from the Go-owned metrics rather than the residual Rust status fields.

## Validation

Scoped validation passed:

- `GOTOOLCHAIN=local go test ./pkg/nftables/ -count=1`
- `GOTOOLCHAIN=local go test ./pkg/daemon/ -count=1`
- `GOTOOLCHAIN=local go test ./pkg/api/ -count=1`
- targeted fence/witness tests
- `bash -n test/incus/t12-g2-9506.sh`
- `bash test/incus/t12-g2-9506.sh --selftest` (`32 passed, 0 failed`)

One authorized live attestation (no second live run) is archived at `/var/tmp/xpf-t12-g2-9506-1789868847`. MATCH passed with local/fw0/fw1 executable SHA `bde960f1f8fd57e5915961c772fdc832bfdf11cce3669de1460431c53a553878`.

The final top-level T12 post snapshots report tuple-joined Go `delivered_available=1` and `delivered=1` on both nodes: fw0 generation 2 / permit_epoch 3 and fw1 generation 4 / permit_epoch 3; those same snapshots have `written=0`. Separately, the v4-native-8 fixture measurement reports fw0 generation 8 and fw1 generation 10, both permit_epoch 11, with `delivered=4` and `written=3` on each node. Thus the headline delivered `1` and workload written `3` are cross-generation observations, not values from one actor tuple or one counter window; the join tuple prevents treating them as a numerical difference. Within v4-native-8, the delivered delta is 4 versus 3 writes, which is permitted by the q0 superset (`MissingNeighbor` can also match). The final T12 delivered delta of 1 is a separate non-zero proof. A TUN userspace write is kernel RX, not a TX-side scrape.

The same run restored cleanly:

`T12_G2_RESTORE fw0_config_cmp=1 fw1_config_cmp=1 fw0_residue_clear=1 fw1_residue_clear=1 residue_probe_error=0 archive=/var/tmp/xpf-t12-g2-9506-1789868847`

The conservative ledger was `cells=30 pass=0 fail=0 void=30`; exit 2 is the harness's intentional VOID-only outcome, not a delivery or restore failure.

## Reviews and disposition

The implementation follows the parent-approved scout design and leaves existing fence verdict tests unchanged. Commits: `c370420b7`, `d7ab56ad6`, `b45b615fc`, and docs `8c7b3c746`.

Recommend **close #10478 on merge** (`Closes #10478`): every Phase 2c number is explained, the q0 superset is explicitly bounded to the quiesced S5 window, and the one live run proves the delivered witness is available and non-zero on both nodes. The broader T12/G2 product-observer cells remain explicitly VOID; this recommendation is limited to the Phase 2c witness acceptance and does not claim those unrelated observers are green.

Closes #10478

## PR #10537 — cluster: remove dead sync-auth helper and correct security prose (#10493) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-22)

Branch: `fix/10493-sync-auth-prose`

Closes #10493

## Decision

Removed `syncAuthDecision` instead of wiring it back. On origin/master at the issue evidence base (b71c52d60), the exhaustive production call-site search found only the declaration outside tests. The live admission guard is `performSyncHandshake`, which runs Noise_NNpsk0 and rejects a peer that cannot complete the PSK exchange. Reintroducing a dead policy helper would duplicate that guard and leave another security-critical path able to drift.

## Blast radius

- Production callers: none on the verified base; the helper and its helper-only decision matrix are removed.
- Tests: removed the direct matrix and obsolete keyed=0 fixture; strict-session-auth coverage now asserts the established unauthenticated fixture directly, while the real Noise/legacy-peer rejection coverage remains.
- Prose: rewrote the live references in `pkg/cluster/README.md`, `sync_auth.go`, `sync_auth_strict_7441.go`, `status.go`, and `sync_config_crypto.go` to name `performSyncHandshake`/Noise_NNpsk0, directional `Split()` keys, and the #6628 in-place upgrade accurately. Related handshake test comments were aligned as well.

## Test plan

- `go test -count=1 ./pkg/cluster/` (pass; 99.45s)
- `git diff --check` (pass)
- Active `pkg/cluster` sweep has no `syncAuthDecision`, keyed=0, or stale legacy challenge-response claims.

## PR #10570 — #10512: fence commit-time session invalidation [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-23)

Branch: `fix/10512-commit-invalidation`

Closes #10512

## Contract

Commit-time session invalidation is helper-first end to end. Discovery
READs helper authority (`list_sessions_by_policy`: worker fan-out with
policy/family/class/cutoff filtering, 250ms ack deadline, 4096 paging,
capture cap, per-worker errors); deletes are identity-conditional
micro-batches (64 matches/128 gate keys, 30s deadline, procGen churn
fence, semantic breaker, persistent-gap errors); HA propagates scoped
(domain,key,expectedID) deletes for policy revocations and
identity-carrying closes; ordinary stale closes run scoped teardown
(exact-key conditional shared removal + conditional sibling
replication + scoped emit) while skipping only bare-keyed BPF deletes;
ClearAll is a capped single-shot helper clear (262144 keys, ~18MB
transient bound, fail-closed over-cap, BPF-sweep-first with no
authority change on failure); the helper epoch latch re-adopts
monotonically (stale-first accepted, older rejected, zero bypasses);
idempotent senders restamp+retry once across churn while
capture-based batches gap instead.

Key terminals (all fail-closed, all pinned): READ incomplete still
revokes what was gathered (delete-partial) while the joined error
surfaces the gap; a single userspace READ error joins once at the
aggregate (no v4/v6 aliasing); over-returned policies are skipped
loudly in both producers; ClearAll succeeds only on
complete-with-empty with zero continuation (counts are
helper-confirmed deleted, (0,0) on any failure); incomplete/empty and
repeated/any continuations are errors; the absolute deadline is
re-checked post-RPC.

Deliberate deviations (for explicit review): (1) stale-close identity
is delta-carried ONLY — shared-row inference was vetoed as unsound
(a same-scoped-key reincarnation would hand back the survivor's id),
so explicit-close producers capture the removed entry's id at delete
time and identity-less stale closes keep the drop+resync floor.
(2) Policy HA queues per ATTEMPTED match (legacy parity), not per
applied — stale matches' scoped deletes are refused no-ops.
(3) SessionStore carries the scoped surface (compile-enforced, no
optional-assertion fallback for the downgrade ban). (4) Worker NAT
releases stay under the phase-1 fence (bounded microsecond ops on a
#4676 short-hold lock, <1ms worst vs the 200ms fence — deferral
machinery would add leak risk for no measurable gain). (5) #5882's
"mirror cleared + partial counts alongside error" is revised to
fail-closed atomic ((0,0) + error, mirror intact) — Go sweeps
nothing; the helper owns the mirror. (6) ClearAll is capped
single-shot, NOT helper paging (parent-accepted alternative).

## Validation (tip 5856586cd, base b8131f1d, 44 commits, RCs captured)

## PR #10574 — zones: rename-safe invalidation, rematch, and measurement (#10509) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-22)

Branch: `fix/10509-zone-renames`

Closes #10509
Closes #10510
Closes #10511

## Why
Zone and policy names are stable identifiers in both the Go control plane and the userspace dataplane. A rename can therefore make established sessions look foreign, leave owner-absent first-policy rows with stale zone ids, and incorrectly tear down an extensive-rematch session even when another rule still permits it.

## What
- Carry additive config ancestry through local and HA ordered config apply, with numeric concrete/special-zone identities and legacy text/generation fallback for unknown or incapable peers. Store lineage ownership transfers to the daemon copy at bind time; no apply outcome retains store-side state.
- Make extensive retention provenance-first: exact terminal policy paths, rename ancestry, resolved-fingerprint equality, evaluator approval, stable RuleID/counter binding, and explicit default/plain/ambiguous teardown behavior.
- Purge unbound sync-derived id-0 rows from old-minus-new forwarding zone snapshots, while retaining safe no-op behavior for invalid or empty zone-set inputs.
- Rebind both session halves and restamp userspace, shared-alias, and BPF metadata to preserve policy identity, counters, zones, and tunnel-safe invalidation semantics. Rotation order is Go-arm rebind BEFORE removed-zone purge; the predicates are disjoint (bound vs unbound id-0), so the order is benign, not load-bearing.
- Route GRE0 renames to delete with a GRE0-only tunnel-variant wildcard (same-tuple sibling teardown is intentional fail-closed); guard ambiguous tunnel discriminators, track received config size, and cover special-zone/path/helper boundaries.

## Contract
- #10509 preserves the bounded Foreign/drop accounting and does not turn default/plain policy behavior into a rename exemption. The matrix pins mechanism (Drop/Revoke lanes, counters, last-seen, policy-id) over a fixed 3-packet observation window; only the Revoke lane pins an upper bound. Production-window quantification against real sweep timing is follow-up work.
- #10510 is independent of HA ancestry and purges only validated removed-zone ids for sync-derived id-0 rows.
- #10511 retains only extensive sessions with explicit valid ancestry and an alternate permit; generic delete/add, default/plain rematch, changed fingerprints, and ambiguous ancestry retain existing teardown. Provenance survives exactly one HA hop; the blind-rebind ~ms race is documented.
- Unknown or incapable HA peers receive the legacy config frame and existing safe teardown path; capable peers receive the ancestry sidecar. An old decoder sees gen 0 + uncompilable garbage on a sidecar payload (loud parse failure, never silent convergence).

## Validation
Tip `78117a1fd` based on master `b9ecd1441`, 10 commits, all subjects `area: summary (#10509)`.
- Snapshot wire contract 30→31 with re-pinned shape golden covering the additive zone_set_validated marker plus the rename ancestry/rebind/extensive fields (no competing bump on master); Rust serialization omits false in the default wire fixture and round-trips true.
- Full Go pkg/daemon suite: GREEN (97s). The three former failures were diff-caused AST-scan breakage (renamed QueueConfig call, void→bool push, WithAncestry wrapper move), fixed by retargeting the scans; the be2488218 "pre-existing" attribution is withdrawn — the tree is fully green, so no failure attribution remains.
- Full Go pkg/cluster (112s), pkg/dataplane (22s), pkg/dataplane/userspace (61s), pkg/configstore (54s), pkg/policymatch suites: GREEN.
- Targeted Go: evaluator (expand/rematch/scheduler/DNAT-v4+v6/NPTv6/ambiguity/GRE-zero), capture (retention/GRE0-wildcard), HA joint (peer-sync capture+clear), bind-transfer lifecycle, cluster reorder/incarnation/reservation/legacy-gating/decoding/capability cells: GREEN.
- Targeted Rust: 11-test session-hit authority module incl. the zone-rename matrix; 8-test first-policy purge/rotation module (2 pre-existing + extensive rebind, non-extensive purge, missing-destination purge, SharedPromote purge, T1→T2, selectivity); removed-zone derivation; restamp v4/v6 preservation + unmapped-fd convention + mismatch fail-closed; GRE0 gate predicate; tunnel-variant wildcard/sibling delete; default-wire marker: GREEN.
- Full Rust userspace-dp suite: 6627 passed; 39 failed + canary, ALL pre-existing — proven name-by-name identical on clean scratch baselines (23 at 3eaf618fc where the master delta has no file overlap with the failing tests; all 16 packet-path tests re-proven at b9ecd1441 where it touches shared execution paths). The only branch-caused failures found — CoS literal guard, wire fixture, two canary markers — were fixed and re-proven green. Residual master failures: coordinator bind/spawn/threads, fragments, flow-cache, WG/IPsec decap, stage-11 gates, pid/cos-roundtrip guards, server spawn, one apply-snapshot case, and 3 canary violations in untouched files. Every added/modified test is green, including the new case-name presence pins.

### RED-on-revert gate per leg (all verified firsthand this fold unless noted)
- #10509: reverting the fixture to a single hard-coded arrival MAC reds the matrix DMZ/WAN cells (upstream independently landed the same per-arrival-MAC fix; either revert breaks arrival authority the same way). Removing the matrix lane/counter/last-seen/policy controls reds the named shape cells across Drop and Revoke lanes. Positive Drop requires drops>0, revokes==0, rows retained; positive Revoke requires revokes>0, drops==0, rows cleared; permit controls require zero actions with rows retained, plus last-seen/policy-id assertions.

## PR #10576 — config: correct contested trunk advisory wording (#10520) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-22)

Branch: `fix/10520-trunk-advisory`

Closes #10520

## Why

The contested-trunk advisory must describe the dataplane decision that actually follows from the built device and zone state. A full unzoned ingress refusal takes the #6682 unattributed-deny arm before the implicit default and is logged with #9989 / `UNZONED_INGRESS_DENIED`. Host-bound handling is shape-dependent: an **unzoned addressed** or **unzoned tunnel** refusal follows the #5659 empty-zone host-inbound path (when local-target/tunnel exposure arms it), address-less non-tunnel refusals for ordinary, non-gated names retain the deliberate global `None => true` admit path, retained sibling-zone traffic is policy-evaluated, and a genuine ordinary (non-lifeline, non-gated) contested parent uses the #10503 host-inbound sentinel. An all-zoned tunnel `Disagree` remains transit-refused but host-bound-admitted with neither sentinel. Narrow lifelines remain admitted while still being reported.

## What

- Split lifeline wording from AF_XDP bind exclusions. Go's unconditional-admit selector now uses only `HostInboundLifelineInterface`; canonical/configured lifelines (including `fab0`) remain admitted, while prefix-only `fxp*` / `em*` / `fab*` names and `lo0` are explicitly zone-gated in both advisory sites. Rust keeps the broad matcher only for sentinel-skip/bind-exclusion parity, with narrow-name versus gated warning selectors.
- Made an ordinary contested warning defer to the shared-device refusal whenever the base also has device-sharing unzoned units. Address-less overlap keeps `None => true`; addressed overlap uses the caveated #5659 path; neither overlap warning claims #10503.
- Made the Rust contested selector distinguish an actual #5659 marker from an actual #10503 marker and explicit override before selecting narrow lifeline/gated/default text. A pre-existing #5659 entry is no longer misreported as an override.
- Scoped the Go contract comments: ordinary parents contest through fan-UP across all units, while interface-level tunnels contest only collapsed units on the same device; the architecture paragraph carries the corresponding sentinel/lifeline/gated caveat.
- Kept Go device-shape classification aligned with snapshot effective-device precedence: secure-tunnel ownership, `TunnelNameMap`, then canonical fallback. Shared-device map construction is reused when appending the contested advisory.
- Kept interface-level tunnel wording separate from ordinary trunk wording: all-zoned collapsed tunnel units remain transit-denied but host-bound-admitted with neither #5659 nor #10503, while an unzoned addressed/tunnel unit names the #5659 path.
- Added a realistic non-unit base row to the all-zoned tunnel runtime fixture; unit-claim classification remains based on structural `is_unit`. Renamed the bind-excluded classifier test to avoid claiming unconditional `lo0` admission while preserving its three mechanism assertions.
- **Transit scope (#6682):** the advisory's transit text describes the userspace-bound/refused parent path covered by the existing dataplane refusal. This change does not claim or verify kernel forwarding for a broad bind-excluded, unbound NIC such as prefix-only `em1`/`fab-foo`/`lo0`.
- No forwarding behavior is changed; the Rust changes select operator-facing text from state already built by the existing enforcement paths.

## PR #10578 — dataplane: surface detach debt and fence fail-closed (#10519) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-22)

Branch: `fix/10519-detach-debt`

Closes #10519

## Why
`syncInterfaceAttachments` previously swallowed `DetachXDP`/`DetachTC` failures. In the XDP flag-clear arm, the retained link remained kernel-attached and continued to enter the armed transit allowlist, leaving a stale fence pinhole.

## What
- Return deterministic joined XDP/TC reconciliation errors and capture them at both post-acceptance call sites.
- Stamp failing ifindexes on `CompileResult`/`ApplyResult`, emit structured `slog.Error`, and latch a sticky detach-debt alarm that clears only after a clean reconciliation and empty debt census.
- Track flag-clear and substantive Unpin detach debt in `dataplane.Manager`; both XDP fence census paths omit debt members (fail-closed availability loss), while successful/no-link detaches and accepted desired-state reconciliation clear debt.
- Snapshot XDP fence candidates under `m.mu`, release it before kernel Info reads, and preserve the XDP ownership lease across census/fence actuation.
- Capture Unpin errors with nil-preserving `unpin:`/`close:` tags. A substantive Unpin failure returns before Close/delete, retaining the live handle and debt for retry; an already-unpinned `os.ErrNotExist` proceeds to Close. TC close failures retain retry state; XDP close failures retain its fail-closed deletion shape.
- Add arm-a sync/alarm/debt/reaccept tests, AST latch-wiring guard, Unpin failure/retry tests, XDP already-unpinned Close coverage, and gate-inventory coverage for the test debt seeder.

## PR #10596 — dataplane: surface batch-delete recovery errors (#10528) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-22)

Branch: `fix/10528-batchdelete`

Closes #10528

## Why

The NotFound-recovery tail in batchDeleteV4/V6 attempted each remaining key but discarded every non-NotFound DeleteSession error. A partial delete could therefore return deleted,nil and let policy invalidation report convergence while sessions remained installed.

## What

- Capture and return the first non-NotFound per-key recovery error after the complete tail attempt, while preserving successful partial counts and ignoring benign sessionNotFound races.
- Add V4/V6 policy-invalidation mismatch warnings only for a successful delete count differing from the matched candidate count. The warning includes an actionable concurrent-expiry hint; surfaced delete errors retain the existing failure warning with the preserved deleted count and no duplicate mismatch warning.
- Add V4/V6 surface tests, an all-NotFound guard, and a DeleteBatchKnownV4 integration regression using the existing #5448 tail fake. The surface cells also pin that a boom-mid-tail partial has holes: later keys are deleted while the failed key remains.
- Strip raw transport ENOENT at the singular userspace helper-delete boundary while retaining errSessionHelperUnreachable, and pin the helper-dies-between-batch-and-retry race. Reword the adjacent #10513 contract comment so only sessionNotFound is ignored.

## M1 disposition / bounded transient

The existing conntrack GC error path consumes a partial count as its callback prefix. This PR deliberately leaves that established consumer contract unchanged under the Store fix + mismatch-warn-only scope: failed rows remain eligible for the next bounded GC sweep and periodic cluster bulk reconciliation heals the peer. The new V4/V6 store cells pin the non-prefix hole shape, and exact deleted-set propagation is tracked as follow-up #10598.

## Validation

Rebased onto current origin/master before the final gates.

Green:

- go test ./pkg/dataplane -count=1
- go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace -count=1
- go test ./pkg/daemon -count=1
- go test targeted #5448/#10528 cells
- go test targeted #10513 and helper-dies recovery cells

- git diff --check

RED-on-revert evidence:

- V4 swallow-restore mutant: TestBatchDeleteV4SurfacesPerKeyErrorAfterNotFound failed with error=nil (exit 1).
- V6 swallow-restore mutant: TestBatchDeleteV6SurfacesPerKeyErrorAfterNotFound failed with error=nil (exit 1).
- DeleteBatchKnownV4 swallow-restore mutant: TestDeleteBatchKnownV4SurfacesRecoveryLoopFailure failed with error=nil (exit 1).
- Singular ENOENT-strip removal mutant: TestDeleteBatchKnownV4SurfacesHelperENOENTDuringRecovery10528 failed with error=nil (exit 1).

The all-NotFound guard is intentionally green before and after the store fix: it pins the no-false-positive contract that benign sessionNotFound recovery returns (0,nil). The hole assertions pin that failed keys remain present while later successful tail deletes are removed. The helper-dies cell pins errSessionHelperUnreachable propagation without raw unix.ENOENT exposure.

## PR #10933 — Fix #10674: Honor the fragment sentinel in reverse NAT lookup [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-25)

Branch: `fix/10674-frag`

Fixes #10674.

## Shared sentinel-family design decision
This first PR establishes the family-wide choice: sentinel-aware readers, not protocol recovery. Native non-first fragments carry the shim's protocol 255; the reverse NAT discriminator treats 255 as unknown and uses the address-qualified index, while known protocol values still require an exact protocol match. It does not recover the real inner protocol. The family/address key prevents cross-family matches. Existing #10130 routing-domain ambiguity remains fail-closed: a candidate in another non-default domain causes DROP rather than borrowing foreign NAT state. The following PRs in this lane will keep this decision consistently.

## Changes
- Make the reverse NAT L3 index protocol-agnostic for lookup while retaining candidate real-protocol validation for known protocol probes; 255 acts as the native-fragment wildcard without scanning the whole session table.
- Re-point #10130 DNAT and interface-SNAT tail fixtures at native-255 metadata and add exact-protocol decapsulated controls, folding this reader's #10678 cohort cells into the issue PR.
- Add native-255 family and routing-domain negative/ambiguity controls.

Files changed:
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/frag_assoc.rs`
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tests_9950.rs`
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tests_fragment.rs`
- `userspace-dp/src/session/key.rs`
- `userspace-dp/src/session/lookup.rs`
- `userspace-dp/src/session/mod.rs`
- `userspace-dp/src/session/tests.rs`

## PR #10953 — nat: Deduplicate expanded pool members before allocation (#10700) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-25)

Branch: `fix/10700-poolmember`

## Why

Source-NAT pool expansion appended every configured member, while the allocator assigned an independent occupancy bitmap to each vector position. Duplicate or overlapping members could therefore mint the same reverse `(address, port)` tuple twice. Go's aggregate capacity and NAT pool alarm denominator also counted those duplicate addresses.

## What

- Deduplicate expanded IPv4 and IPv6 addresses in the source-NAT parser, preserving first occurrence and ordering.
- Count the union of expanded member ranges for Go reportable and aggregate pool capacity.
- Keep the applied NAT view/alarm denominator aligned with Rust's unique address count; update the strict diagnostic and pool alarm documentation.
- The Go aggregate regression retains 17 distinct host-bit spellings of the same `/16`, asserts all 17 survive the config tree, and confirms their union has 65,536 addresses without poisoning the pool.
- Add fail-on-revert Rust/Go regression coverage. Keep independent allocator-overlap handling unchanged and remove the obsolete test asserting duplicate member positions were separate allocator slots.

Closes #10700.

## Validation

Pre-fix RED: `cargo test --manifest-path Cargo.toml duplicate_pool_members_mint_distinct_ports_10700 -- --nocapture` failed with both translations `(203.0.113.1, 20000)` (`assert_ne!`: left 20000, right 20000).

Post-fix:
- `cargo test --manifest-path Cargo.toml nat::tests_pool_overlap_6979:: -- --nocapture` — 14 passed.
- `cargo test --manifest-path Cargo.toml nat::tests_aggregate_budget:: -- --nocapture` — 19 passed.
- `go test ./pkg/config -count=1` — passed after the corrected aggregate regression (226.483s).
- `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace -count=1` — passed (56.633s).
- `go test ./pkg/natpoolalarm -count=1` — passed (0.017s).
- `cargo test --bins` — 7,075 passed, 1 failed, 6 ignored across two binaries: `src/bin/xpf_userspace` had 63 passed; `src/main.rs` had 7,012 passed, 1 failed, 6 ignored. The sole failure was the known #9894 `afxdp::tests_fragment::flowless_slack_tcp_not_steered_by_port_except_pbr_9894`; central base attribution: `4c2c13779`. No #10946 test failed.
- PR lint check passed.

## Risk

Strict validation still rejects duplicate/overlapping membership. Tolerated loads keep only the first occurrence within one pool; overlaps between separate allocator domains remain subject to the existing peer-collision check.

## PR #10956 — userspace-dp: fence flowless same-family NAT before reinjection (#10679) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-25)

Branch: `fix/10679-espsnat`

Closes #10679.

Flowless same-family packets fail closed whenever a configured NAT candidate requires translation that the flowless path cannot provide. The fence follows policy adjudication and Pref64/NAT64 attribution, applies before TX and MissingNeighbor buffering, and blocks permitted NoRoute reinjection to the kernel FIB. NoRoute probes configured interface identities because the actual egress is unresolved.

At MissingNeighbor, non-first fragments are fenced only for a live reverse-NAT session or a possible scoped L4 NAT candidate. Blanket-only raw ESP/AH non-first fragments retain the Stage-11 park path. The unknown protocol sentinel remains authoritative; the fence does not inspect payload bytes. NoRoute now attributes real non-first fragment drops to the fragment NAT counter rather than the whole-flowless counter.

Regression coverage includes same-family SNAT candidates across protocol families, MAC-less NoRoute, NoRoute fragment counter attribution, Pref64 attribution with SNAT configured, and raw-IPsec Stage-11 parking.

Validation:
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp 10679 -- --nocapture` — 12 passed.

## PR #10958 — dataplane: fail closed on post-teardown apply refusals (#10702) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-25)

Branch: `fix/10702-teardownkind`

Closes #10702

## Why
Rust rejects apply_snapshot after worker teardown when worker spawn/bind/SA readiness fails, but previously returned only free-form text. Go classified every in-band refusal as helperRejectedError, rolled classifier maps back, and left ctrl enabled against dead workers.

## What
- Add the lockstep-pinned SNAPSHOT_POST_TEARDOWN_PREFIX refusal kind in Rust and Go.

- Bump the snapshot protocol to v33 so mixed v32/v33 peers refuse before teardown.
- Pin both Rust apply legs; add fake-helper cells for retained vs post-teardown refusal and the fail-closed/retry-debt behavior.
- Document the protocol and compatibility behavior.

The only failure was the unrelated `flowless_slack_tcp_not_steered_by_port_except_pbr_9894` (the same sole failure on both pre- and post-rebase full runs). The issue-specific Rust tests passed.
