The TCP `no-syn-check` and `strict-syn-check` selectors were parsed but never reached the AF_XDP session-miss gate, so configured midstream TCP followed the default SYN-first drop and could be black-holed.

## What
- Carry both selectors from typed Go config through the flow snapshot and protocol v34 into Rust `ForwardingState` and transit session-MISS admission.
- Allow policy-permitted non-closing TCP misses with `no-syn-check`; `strict-syn-check` takes precedence. RST/FIN misses remain dropped; existing session hits and host-inbound `LocalDelivery` behavior remain unchanged.
- Remove stale accepted-only claims, correct the remaining config-gap documentation, and update regression tests and snapshot goldens. Protocol v34 follows #10958's v33 allocation.

## Validation
- `TMPDIR=/var/tmp GOTMPDIR=/var/tmp go test ./pkg/config ./pkg/configstore ./pkg/dataplane/userspace` — all three packages passed. An initial attempt with the shared `/tmp` tmpfs full failed four #9617 persistence tests with `ENOSPC`; rerunning with temp paths on `/var/tmp` passed.
- From `userspace-dp/`, `TMPDIR=/var/tmp cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp session_admission::tests` — 11 passed; `TMPDIR=/var/tmp cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp tcp_syn_check_selectors_reach_forwarding_state_10703` — 1 passed.
- From `userspace-dp/`, `TMPDIR=/var/tmp cargo test --bins` — fairness binary: 63 passed; dataplane binary: 7078 passed, 1 failed, 6 ignored. The sole failure is `flowless_slack_tcp_not_steered_by_port_except_pbr_9894`.
- The #9894 failure was reproduced on a clean archive of current `origin/master` at `5d4230f9d` using `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp flowless_slack_tcp_not_steered_by_port_except_pbr_9894` (0 passed, 1 failed). No other affected-suite failures were observed.
- Fail-on-revert: forcing both Go snapshot-carrier fields false made `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace -run '^TestTCPSynCheckSelectorsReachTheWire10703$'` fail for configured selectors. Forcing the Rust miss predicate to drop every non-SYN packet made `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp tcp_syn_check_tests` fail on ACK flags `0x10`; restored code passes the full admission module.
- `git diff --check origin/master...HEAD` — clean.

## Risk
Go and Rust protocol v34 snapshots must deploy in lockstep; mismatched versions reject the snapshot. The unrelated #9894 baseline failure remains outside this change.

## PR #10989 — forwarding: reject NOARP neighbors for directed broadcasts (#10690) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-25)

Branch: `fix/10690-noarp`

Closes #10690

Go and Rust previously accepted `NUD_NOARP` neighbors as resolved. For a directed-broadcast route, that could preserve the all-ones Ethernet MAC and let a unicast-shaped permit emit an L2 broadcast. This change rejects NOARP at neighbor admission, removes an existing dynamic row on a NOARP transition, and treats NOARP as unusable in the Rust FIB classifier and Go snapshot publication.

Networkd wrote caller-controlled structured values raw into generated systemd units, while the prior render belt only sanitized Description. systemd.syntax(7) also treats a trailing backslash as line continuation.

## PR #11038 — fix(ipsec): fence host INPUT before capture removal (#9506 F1) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-25)

Branch: `fix/9506-f1`

Part of #9506

## Why
Capture removal deleted the NFQUEUE divert before retiring listeners, while an OPEN S4 permit let the host-input xfrmi DROP overlay retire. During that interval live decrypted host-bound traffic had neither diversion nor an acknowledged DROP.

## What
- Revoke the permit to CLOSING and install/read back the host-input xfrmi DROP before removing the divert.

- On fence install/readback failure, retain the divert. On removal failure, restore the previous capture behind the acknowledged fence. Shutdown uses the same fence-before-removal rule and retains the divert if the host-input DROP cannot be acknowledged.
- Add transition tests for removal ordering, failed removal rollback, readback refusal, and pre-first-install/boot; document this F1 slice.

- Fail-on-revert: bypassing the fence hold makes the removal cell RED; bypassing the no-capture OPEN gate makes the boot cell RED.
- Known master-red #9894 did not occur, so no clean-master attribution run was needed.

## Risk
When capture is absent, the shared permit intentionally remains CLOSING and the host-input DROP remains installed; traffic is denied until a capture generation commits. This slice does not implement the P-MECH permit path or prove live-SA packet behavior. Issue #9506 remains open.

## PR #11042 — cluster: mark unconfirmed fencing degraded (#10701) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-25)

Branch: `fix/10701-fencing`

## Why

A lost heartbeat does not establish that the peer stopped forwarding. The default configuration sends no fence, `disable-rg` sends an unacknowledged fence after election, and `disable-rg-confirmed` can fail open before an acknowledgement arrives. The existing operator output could read these takeovers as clean.

## What

- Track unconfirmed peer-loss fencing, including the default and best-effort modes and every fail-open confirmed-fence outcome.
- Render `Peer-loss takeover: DEGRADED` with reason and time in both cluster status views; mark local health degraded in the information view. Clear the marker when a peer heartbeat returns. This remains diagnostic and does not block takeover.
- Clarify in operator and source documentation that a positive acknowledgement is only point-in-time dataplane suppression, not peer demotion, VIP release, or dual-primary exclusion.
- Add RED-on-revert tests for default, best-effort, confirmed-failure, partial-ack, missing-sync, confirmed-success, and heartbeat-recovery behavior.

## Validation

- `TMPDIR=/var/tmp go test ./pkg/cluster -count=1` — PASS (rebased tree, 112.271s).
- Before implementation, the focused #10701 status tests failed on the expected missing-degradation assertions; after implementation, the focused tests and the full cluster package suite passed.
- No #9894 master-red failure was encountered.

## Risk

This is the accepted diagnostic mitigation, not a mutual-exclusion fix: it does not guarantee zero VIP overlap or change the fixed one-second fail-open confirmation policy. A degraded mark clears on the next peer heartbeat; availability and takeover ordering are otherwise unchanged.

Closes #10701

---

## PR #11043 — grpcapi: bind fabric PSK tokens to unary request arguments [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-25)

Branch: `fix/10709-fabricpsk`

## Why
Fabric PSK tokens were bound to method and time window only, so a captured token could authorize a different ClearSessions filter or failover RG during its accepted window.

## What
- Bind unary fabric tokens to SHA-256 of deterministic protobuf request bytes, in addition to the full gRPC method and time window.
- Carry the digest from both daemon and CLI unary client interceptors through per-RPC credentials; verify the same digest on the server and in clock-skew diagnostics.
- Add fail-on-revert coverage for changed ClearSessions filters and failover RGs, including a captured-token replay over real loopback gRPC. Document the remaining byte-identical unary replay and method-only streaming residuals.

## Validation
- `TMPDIR=/var/tmp go test ./pkg/grpcapi ./pkg/cli -count=1` — PASS on rebased commit.
- `TMPDIR=/var/tmp go vet ./pkg/grpcapi ./pkg/cli` — PASS on rebased commit.
- RED proof: copied only the new regression test into a disposable archive of origin/master at `9f1f688c2614b80f0a6efad3ad641917fb6766b5`; `TMPDIR=/var/tmp go -C /var/tmp/10709-red-master test ./pkg/grpcapi -run TestFabricAuth10709_ -count=1` failed as expected because captured tokens authorized both changed filters/RGs and the real gRPC rg2 replay.

## Risk
The token wire format is intentionally incompatible with method-only peers; cross-node fabric RPCs require both peers on the updated code, with no vulnerable legacy fallback. MonitorInterface is server-streaming and its request body is unavailable when per-RPC credentials are created, so it retains method-only binding and bounded same-window argument replay.

Closes #10709

## PR #11100 — daemon: fence fail-closed boot addresses (#10732) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-26)

Branch: `fix/10732-day0boot`

Closes #10732

On #1960/#10297 fail-closed boots, networkd has already restored retained data-interface addresses while bootstrap suppresses the normal apply path that installs host-input fences. Derive non-management addresses from the live netlink snapshot and install the existing host-inbound and lo0 cold-boot fences before runtime managers/control surfaces start. Preserve known management interfaces and withhold addresses shared with them; do not cycle links or remove networkd files.

If management identity or a complete live address snapshot cannot be established, skip the fence and log the reason rather than risking a management lockout. The fence installation paths also log failures while allowing the control plane to start for recovery.

Regression coverage exercises v4/v6 data-address drops, management/loopback exclusions, shared-address withholding, no-op non-fail-closed boots, incomplete-observation handling, and best-effort behavior when one fence installer fails.

## PR #11116 — daemon: order SSH root-login policy before factory defaults [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-26)

Branch: `fix/10755-sshroot`

The baked image loads `10-xpf-factory.conf` before the daemon-managed `xpf.conf`. Because sshd keeps the first value for `PermitRootLogin`, the factory `prohibit-password` setting masked configured `deny` and `allow` values.

Move the managed drop-in to `00-xpf.conf`, remove the old later-sorting file during apply, and reload when migration is needed. The regression test runs real `sshd -t`/`sshd -T` against the factory policy and checks effective deny/no and allow/yes values.

## PR #11162 — cluster: yield on stale heartbeat echoes (#10775) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-26)

Branch: `fix/10775-hb`

Closes #10775

### Why
When the lower-priority node cannot hear its peer, peer-timeout handling promotes it while the hearing winner keeps accepting stale PRIMARY reports. Without a peer-heard signal, both can remain PRIMARY for as long as the one-way fault lasts.

### What
Add an optional XPFE heartbeat session/sequence echo before the fixed-tail epoch/auth trailers. Track an incarnation-bound lease that renews only on fresh echoed sequences; keep the hearing node secondary while stale PRIMARY reports continue, including in preempt mode. Add Manager-level loss/recovery coverage for both orientations and both preempt modes, plus authenticated maximum-frame coverage. Document compatibility without changing HAProtocolVersion.

### Validation
- gofmt on all four changed Go files: passed.
- go test ./pkg/cluster -run '^(TestOneWayHeartbeatLossYieldsHearingWinner10775|TestHeartbeatEchoFitsAuthenticatedFrameLimit10775)$' -count=1: passed.
- go test ./pkg/cluster: passed.
- go vet ./pkg/cluster: passed.
- RED-on-revert: the regression failed with the prior primary-only expiry guard at preempt/loser-deaf because the hearing winner reclaimed PRIMARY; the corrected guard passed.

### Risk
A real one-way-link HA pair was not available. Tests exercise Manager election and heartbeat/authentication wire paths, but not physical VIP/GARP behavior. Older peers ignore the optional trailer and cannot refresh the echo lease.

## PR #11164 — ha: gate failover duration and stream loss [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-26)

Branch: `fix/10785-failovergate`

Closes #10785

The smoke used only the final whole-run [SUM] throughput and an unscoped `pgrep iperf3` check. A long outage or loss of half the data streams could still pass on the surviving aggregate rate, and the separate pool client could satisfy the process check.

This change enables one-second iperf intervals, rejects interval telemetry gaps and more than two consecutive aggregate intervals below the configured floor, and requires all eight streams active before the unclean crash to resume within three seconds. Main-client liveness now follows its recorded PID and command tuple, so the pool-mode client cannot mask its exit. The final throughput check remains in place.

Regression coverage includes a 60-second outage whose whole-run average is still 11.7 Gbps, loss of four established streams, delayed recovery, missing interval data, and main-vs-pool client PID identity.

Validation: `make test-iperf-throughput-lib` (22 passed); `python3 -m unittest discover -s test/incus -p 'iperf3_sum_parse_test.py'` (23 passed); `bash -n` and scoped `shellcheck` passed. No Go files changed (gofmt/vet not applicable). The destructive live `make test-failover` smoke was not run in this lane.

## PR #11217 — gre: reject stale inner family during encap (#10865) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-26)

Branch: `fix/10865-hostinbound`

Part 1/2 for #10865. The GRE decap path already refuses PT/nibble mismatches; this PR closes the encap sibling by checking the inner IP version nibble against `ForwardPacketMeta.addr_family` before trimming or selecting the emitted GRE Protocol Type. A stale stamp now fails closed rather than putting a mismatched packet on the wire.

The regression uses IPv6 bytes with an IPv4-shaped length field and stale IPv4 metadata, so metadata-only trimming would previously have built GRE PT=IPv4 around an IPv6 nibble. The existing shim test documents keyed/checksummed/sequenced GRE as redirect-only: flag-bearing headers miss shim classification and remain on XSK for userspace decap/policy.

Dedicated PT/nibble-refusal telemetry and the Rust-to-Go-to-Prometheus status path are intentionally deferred to PR2 after this PR lands.

Refs #10865

## PR #11235 — eventengine: defer HA remediation until RG0 promotion [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-26)

Branch: `fix/10874-ee`

Closes #10874

Decision: implement the HA publication gate and defer read-only remediation actions rather than documenting and closing the issue. The daemon closes the gate on RG0 demotion, opens it after the store becomes writable on promotion, and the worker retains accepted actions across the read-only interval. ErrClusterReadOnly is not counted as a permanent rejection, and the lock-retry deadline restarts after publication resumes.

The deliberate peerSyncNever policy (#5962) remains unchanged. Remediation commit history now carries [local-only; not peer-synced] to mark the expected node-local divergence.

Takeover measurement: a fresh failure edge under the current RPM defaults would require 3 successive losses × 60 s test interval ≈ 180 s. That is a material delay for event-options then-commands; this change resumes the retained action at promotion instead of waiting for a re-trip.

Validation: go test ./pkg/eventengine -count=1; go test ./pkg/daemon -count=1; go vet ./pkg/eventengine ./pkg/daemon. Post-rebase targeted failover tests also pass.

## PR #11240 — eventengine: test HA demotion race and clarify re-trip timing [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-26)

Branch: `fix/10874-followup`

Refs #10874

Follow-up to the merged HA remediation deferral change. Adds a deterministic regression test that flips the config store read-only after EnterConfigure succeeds but before the candidate mutation; it verifies the wrapped ErrClusterReadOnly is deferred, the failed candidate is discarded, and the accepted action commits after promotion.

Clarifies the probe timing: a persistent FAIL produces no new failure edge, so waiting without recovery/reset can be indefinite. The approximate 3 × 60 s = 180 s re-trip estimate applies only after a forced reset/re-trip with the defaults (probe-count 1, successive-loss threshold 3, test interval 60 s). The deferred action avoids both the indefinite missed-edge wait and the forced re-trip delay.

## PR #11253 — session: shed half-open flows under pressure (#10890) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-26)

Branch: `fix/10890-sess`

Closes #10890

At the fixed per-worker 90% session-table threshold, a validated TCP initial SYN frees local handshake-incomplete sessions (both directions when present) before the whole install group is admitted. Established and peer-owned entries are protected; if no room can be made, the normal refusal and rollback path remains. A seeded candidate index avoids scanning the table on admission. The worker releases each shed entry’s source-NAT and NAT64 holds through the ordinary teardown APIs, preventing pool-port leaks. Configured aging leaves remain unwired and still emit the accepted-only advisory.

## PR #11359 — fragment-assoc: harden admission and session lifetime (#11058) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-27)

Branch: `fix/11058-frag`

## Summary
- Seed fragment-shard selection with the runtime hot-path hash seed and mix before choosing a shard.
- Scope fragment quotas to the admitting session tuple and incarnation, refuse admission at limits rather than evicting live entries, and require the admitting session to remain live for fragment reuse.
- For shared rows with legacy session ID zero, use the materialized local session ID; skip association publication for failed or idless installs.

## Quota design
A hard aggregate cap on the untrusted claimed source is deliberately not retained: an attacker can fill it before the real sender arrives and block that sender first fragment. The session-scoped quota prevents one admission identity from spending another session quota, while the fixed per-shard cap bounds memory.

## Verification

## PR #11470 — ha: gate confirmed commits on peer snapshot protocol (#10782) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-27)

Branch: `fix/10782-commitconfirm`

Why
Offline commit-confirmed must remain available, but a connected peer unable to represent an active multi-zone scoped policy must not receive or claim that config generation. Capability learned on one fabric must not authorize a preferred replacement connection that has not proved its own version. Successful current config must retire obsolete deferrals without allowing a stale attempt to clear or re-arm a current alarm.

What
- Preserve offline commit-confirmed promotion and defer incompatible active multi-zone config sync without claiming the per-epoch marker.
- Bind protocol authorization at preflight, reconcile, and final socket write to the selected connection incarnation and its own advertised snapshot version; a surviving fabric cannot authorize an unadvertised or v3 replacement.
- Capture compiled config, hierarchical text, and active generation under one Store read lock; serialize peer SyncApply and both rollback promotion paths with the config snapshot/rename serializer.
- Preserve the local applied marker when only the peer push fails; require an active cluster runtime for the gate.
- Serialize alarm transitions with active config promotions. Reports validate their captured peer epoch and selected capability before installation. A stale authorization that encounters a capable or disconnected current peer does not re-anchor a new deferral; only a currently connected incompatible peer reports one. Successful clears carry the authorizing epoch and capability, so delayed old-connection writes cannot erase same-text replacement-peer deferrals. Successful current-config pushes still supersede older-text deferrals.

Validation
- `go test ./pkg/daemon ./pkg/cluster ./pkg/cli ./pkg/grpcapi -count=1` passed on the current merged master tree after round-five changes; all four packages passed.
- Focused `go test ./pkg/daemon -run 'Test(DeferredSnapshotAlarm|ShapeRemovalPush|StaleSnapshotAuthorization|CommitSnapshotStaleAuth)' -count=1` passed.
- RED-on-revert: restoring the generic stale-auth report with its fresh current observation made both `TestStaleSnapshotAuthorizationDoesNotRearmAfterSameTextSuccess10782` and `TestCommitSnapshotStaleAuthDoesNotRearmAfterReconnect10782` fail after successful same-text v4 convergence.
- RED-on-revert: removing both clear epoch guards while retaining the selected-capability equality check made `TestDeferredSnapshotAlarmClearRejectsOldPeerEpochRace10782` fail with identical success/current capability state, isolating the epoch guard.
- Existing stale-v3 report / current-v4 recovery and shape-removal (nil capability state) regressions passed.
- An earlier pre-merge combined package run also exercised configstore and found three unrelated strict IKE fixture failures (`TestPackedIPsecVPNRunKeepsEveryLeaf9088`, `TestPackedIPsecVPNRunIsNarrow9088`, `TestPackedIPsecVPNRunIsSubjectToTheBindInterfaceGate9088`) for a proposal missing `authentication-algorithm`; no configstore source changed in this round.

Risk
A connected peer with no advertisement or v3 on the selected connection remains gated until a compatible capability is proven and current config is pushed. Offline local commits can stay divergent meanwhile; the alarm and Config Sync event remain visible. A stale authorization that sees a capable peer may still return a stale-token error to its caller, but does not manufacture a CRITICAL deferral after convergence. No socket I/O runs under the active config serializer.

## PR #11474 — nat: clear persistent NAT authoritatively (#10784) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-28)

Branch: `fix/10784-natclear`

## Summary
- Make persistent-NAT clearing allocator-authoritative in userspace; report the helper count and clear the Go SHOW mirror only after helper acknowledgement.
- Fence known and unknown pre-clear HA imports, including after same-key replacement, retained-pool allocator rebuild, and same-address pool rename with zero live flows.
- Keep synced PAT and address-only admission from reactivating an idle replacement whose expiry has passed but GC has not reclaimed yet.
- Admit only the exact `clear-persistent-nat` peer action on the fabric listener and deny near-misses.

## Why
The prior clear emptied only the Go display mirror. The userspace allocator retained persistent mappings, and delayed HA idle-lease exports could reintroduce cleared mappings.

## Implementation
Idle leases are removed with their PAT occupancy. Per-key fences protect known leases, and the allocator-wide 60-second barrier protects keys absent when clear runs. A fresh local same-key replacement does not delete or restart the original fence. A synced session can join a live lease or a draining shell, but an expired idle replacement still awaiting GC is not eligible for persistent reactivation: PAT keeps its occupied tuple, while address-only sync can serve without attaching to the expired lease or removing its expiry index.

Retained-pool allocator reseed carries the live batch fence and pruned per-key deadlines without carrying persistent lease associations. The new per-key map is bounded by the target flow capacity; if entries must be omitted, the batch fence is widened through their latest deadline. Active `u64::MAX` shell markers become a finite 60-second fence from reseed because the revoked shell itself is not transferred. Pool renames carry these fences independently of live reservations, including when the destination is a fresh or already-reused allocator and the source has zero live flows. Coexisting same-address pools still do not cross-pollinate.

The fabric listener admits only the exact clear action; suffixed, prefixed, case-modified, whitespace, and sibling clear actions remain denied.

## Validation
- [x] `cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml nat::tests_pool -- --test-threads=1` — 250 passed, 1 ignored, including fresh/reused rename cases and the coexisting-pool control.
- [x] `cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml nat::tests_idle_lease_sync_8121 -- --test-threads=1` — 34 passed, including the clear-path creation-site census.
- [x] `cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml 10784 -- --test-threads=1` — 22 passed.
- [x] `go test ./pkg/grpcapi -run '^TestFabricAllowlistUnary_SystemActionNestedGate$' -count=1` — passed.
- [x] RED before B1 fix: PAT stale sync unexpectedly reactivated the expired replacement; address-only stale sync raised its active-flow count from 0 to 1. Both pass with the liveness gates.

## PR #11476 — ha: roll back strict mirror refusal imports (#10788) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-27)

Branch: `fix/10788-f1-rollback`

## Why
A strict conntrack-mirror refusal must not leave coordinator NAT reservations behind or expose a rejected import through shared authority, steering rows, prewarm state, or workers. A same-key replacement must also preserve the previous translated tuple and its worker-holder ownership. If a reverse mirror write refuses after the forward row was written, rollback must restore the row that actually occupied the BPF bare key, not infer a survivor from route-scoped shared state.

## What
- Keep strict mirror publication ahead of shared authority, DNAT/session steering, reverse-prewarm indexes, and worker fan-out.
- Capture incumbent SNAT/NAT64 worker-holder masks before a same-flow replacement. On strict refusal, release the rejected import's untracked reservations and restore the prior entry's reservation plus every captured worker holder bit.
- Immediately before the forward conntrack write, snapshot the actual bare-key BPF key/value bytes under the tuple lease. If reverse publication fails, restore that exact row; delete the new forward row when no snapshot existed, and fall back to deletion if exact restoration fails. No shared-SessionKey scan or map-order inference is used.
- Preserve the bare `mirror-write-failed` health-error semantics and Go refusal-token classification; document the rollback contract in `docs/sync-protocol.md`.

## Validation
- Passed `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp 10788 -- --nocapture` (11 passed).
- RED-on-revert: removing holder-mask restoration failed the same-key SNAT and NAT64 tests; omitting the BPF snapshot failed the A-then-B-then-refused-C alias test; disabling row deletion failed the no-snapshot deletion test; disabling restore-failure fallback deletion failed its dedicated test.
- `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace ./pkg/api -count=1`: `pkg/dataplane/userspace` passed. Seven `pkg/api` config-handler tests failed because their IKE proposal lacks `authentication-algorithm`; the same seven failures were reproduced on clean parent `fe67d1f3d` in prior validation.
- Full `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp`: 7171 passed, 5 failed, 6 ignored. The five failures are the three `tests_native_gre_ecn` tests, `t9_gre_inner_coarse_deny_remains_first_10585`, and `worker_queue_6929_every_production_producer_routes_through_push_bounded`.
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Risk
Compensation remains best-effort: allocator restoration or both exact-row restoration and fallback deletion can fail. Those residuals are counted and logged; they do not change the already-decided strict refusal.

## PR #11479 — nat: atomically capture holders on synced replacement (#11478) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-27)

Branch: `fix/11478-atomichold`

## Why

Round-2 review found that synced replacement captured the incumbent worker-holder mask and evicted/replaced the allocation under separate allocator-lock operations. A worker release in between can be replayed as a phantom holder on strict mirror refusal rollback. A queued worker upsert can OR a holder bit in the gap that replacement then destroys; restoring the earlier mask can let a sibling release free the tuple while it is still in use.

## What

- Add an allocator operation that captures the incumbent holder mask while holding `lock_live` and returns the guard for eviction and replacement installation, keeping the complete operation in one live-state critical section.
- Use it for synced SNAT pool-port, address-only, interface-identity, and NAT64 reservations.
- Add deterministic barrier regressions for worker release and queued upsert interleavings in SNAT and NAT64 strict-refusal rollback paths.
- Document the lock/rollback contract in `docs/sync-protocol.md`.

## Validation

- Relevant Rust test module: 14 passed. The four new `11478` tests passed.
- RED-on-revert: all four new tests failed when the split capture/reserve behavior was temporarily restored, then passed with the fused operation.
- `make test-rust`: 7174 passed, 5 failed, 6 ignored. The five failures are the known #11472 native GRE ECN, slow-path disposition, and worker-queue failures.
- `make test-go`: failed with the known seven `pkg/api` IKE-auth fixture failures (#11477) and three `pkg/configstore` IKE-auth fixture failures. It also reported unrelated repository-wide gates: 80 files failing the gofmt-clean-tree test, 11 dangling documentation citations, stale generated policy seed, two unclassified applied-marker sites, and the real-kernel routing observation. No Go files were changed; tree-hygiene failures are being tracked separately.

## Risk

This changes allocator synchronization only; no wire format or protocol contract changes. Worker holder updates serialize with the replacement while the existing live-state mutex is held. Rollback continues to restore the captured incumbent mask.

## PR #11490 — routing: reject interfaces claimed by multiple RIs (#11060) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-28)

Branch: `fix/11060-ridual`

Fixes #11060

Resolve routing-instance ownership by actual Linux netdevice across strict validation, tolerant quarantine, daemon VRF binding/reassertion, and userspace membership maps. Slash/dash aliases, VLAN IDs, bare-member fanout, shared tunnel devices, forwarding-instance memberships, and explicit tunnel routing-instance stanzas use the same ownership check. Strict compilation rejects competing claims and names the owners. Unit tunnel stanza identity follows the compiler-resolved `TunnelConfig.Name`, including WireGuard-parent units that override their mode and retain a separate uN device.

On tolerant boot/peer-sync, every contested device is removed from conflicting RI memberships and conflicting tunnel stanzas are cleared so neither the tunnel manager nor list reconciliation can restore the contested scope. Safe generated units remain explicit; an uncontested primary is retained as a typed base-only claim without re-expanding quarantined siblings. VRF unbinding requires the looked-up master to be a `netlink.Vrf` before detaching.

Forwarding instances participate in the device-owner gate even though they bind no Linux VRF device; a forwarding+VRF same-device overlap is strict-rejected and tolerant-quarantined.

Actor model: the observed master index and subsequent `LinkSetNoMaster` are not atomic against arbitrary netlink writers. Daemon config apply and periodic reassert serialize through `applySem`; concurrent out-of-band `ip link` or network-manager master changes are outside this guarantee. No conditional-detach protection against such external races is claimed.

Validation on the merged tree (origin/master 20c731bf1):
- `go test ./pkg/config`, `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace`, and `go test ./pkg/daemon` passed.
- Focused mixed-mode stanza and foreign-master tests passed; both regressions failed when their fixes were temporarily reverted.
- `gofmt -l pkg/routing/vrf.go` produced no output; `git diff --check` passed for both documentation folds.
- Full routing suite had one failure: `TestNextTableIngressScopeOnRealKernel_9420` ran its private namespace but got `RTNETLINK answers: No route to host` for the baseline case, which the test intentionally treats as an unrecognized observation. This is kernel/environment-specific evidence rather than a failure in the changed 11060 path; the test does not accept it as a pass.
- Full API suite had seven #11477 failures: existing IKE fixtures use non-AEAD proposals without `authentication-algorithm`, so commits are rejected by the IKE integrity validator. This is a real suite/fixture mismatch, not an environment-only failure; it is tracked as the pre-existing #11477 set.

## PR #11537 — userspace-dp: honor learned-route preference (#11323) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-30)

Branch: `fix/11323-gapfill-preference`

Closes #11323

## Why
The learned-route importer stamps selected kernel routes at preference 200, but same-prefix gap-fill suppression discarded them whenever any config route existed. A preference-250 floating static therefore stayed active in the helper while FRR had selected BGP/OSPF.

## What
The snapshot builder now compares the best configured preference for each canonical table/family/prefix with the imported preference. ## PR #11538 — config: warn and exclude zero-disposition statics (#11327) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-30)

Why
Bare, receive, and empty qualified-next-hop static routes have no usable forwarding disposition. The Go userspace builder could emit their empty AF_XDP FIB rows while FRR omits them, allowing a more-specific row to shadow an installable less-specific route as NoRoute.

Warn during config validation and use the shared static-route exclusion so zero-disposition routes do not enter userspace snapshots or show surfaces. This branch now merges current master including #11539. The shared exclusion inventory counts six per-route reasons (including #11327 no-disposition and #11328 no-install) plus the seventh order-dependent next-table window. No-install is checked first because it is explicit operator intent; zero-disposition is checked afterward.

## PR #11551 — userspace-dp: omit unresolved recursive statics from helper FIB (#11317) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-30)

Branch: `fix/11317-recursive-static`

Why
A recursive static next-hop is emitted as a bare gateway. The Rust helper resolves it only from a connected prefix in the same table, so an all-recursive config route can remain ifindex 0/NoRoute while its destination still counts as learned-route coverage and suppresses the kernel's resolved copy.

What
Index connected prefixes by family and table before static routes are added. Omit an ordinary config row only when it has bare gateways and none resolve directly or through forwarding-instance qualification. Keep mixed rows so Rust can skip unresolved ECMP legs and forward via a usable direct or explicitly qualified member. Add IPv4 recursive-via-direct and recursive-via-recursive cells, an IPv6 cell, direct/explicit controls, and a mixed direct+recursive ECMP test that exercises Rust forwarding selection.

Validation
- RED before fix: TestRecursiveStaticRouteKeepsKernelResolvedGapFill11317 saw only the config route via 10.10.0.1 instead of the learned copy via 192.0.2.1.
- PASS: go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace -run '^(TestRecursive|TestDirectAndExplicit|TestMixedDirectAndRecursive|TestLearnedRoute|TestGapFillMatchesANonCanonical|TestFBF|TestBuildRouteSnapshotsIncludesConnectedPrefixes)' -count=1
- PASS: go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace -run 'Test.*(Route|GapFill|FBF|Static|Connected)' -count=1
- PASS: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/dev/shm/cargo-11317 cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml static_bare_gateway_single_table_still_resolves -- --nocapture (1 test; 7406 filtered)
- PASS on rebased head: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/dev/shm/cargo-11317 cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml recursive_ecmp_preserves_direct_member_11317 -- --nocapture (1 test; 7412 filtered)

Risk
With interface snapshots, an all-recursive ordinary config route is omitted from the helper FIB so a learned kernel copy can fill it. If none is available, the destination remains NoRoute rather than retaining an ifindex-0 route. Mixed direct/recursive rows remain and the Rust selector excludes the ifindex-0 member.

Closes #11317

## PR #11553 — dataplane: match reverse NAT replies by forward egress RI (#11298) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-30)

Branch: `fix/11298-ri-reverse-admission`

Closes #11298

## Why
Reverse-NAT admission treated the forward ingress/key domain as reply identity, admitting mixed-zero cross-instance replies and refusing legitimate asymmetric routes.

## Change
Ordinary local and shared reverse-NAT admission compares each candidate forward egress-interface routing domain with the arriving reply domain. The independent arrival-zone and quarantined-domain gates remain in force. Same-family embedded-ICMP quote rewriting uses a separate read-only tuple lookup because off-path routers may send errors from another domain; it does not install a reverse session. Quote lookup fails closed when multiple tenants own the translated tuple, including collisions between local and shared entries; routing domain zero is a real tenant. Unique translated shared candidates remain recoverable.

## Regression coverage
Coverage includes local/local and shared/shared cross-domain tuple collisions, a local domain-zero versus shared nonzero collision, unique off-path translated quote recovery, mixed-zero isolation, asymmetric local/shared replies, IPv4 NAT, IPv6 NAT, and NAT64.

## PR #11555 — sessions: index delayed close identity checks (#11299) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-30)

Branch: `fix/11299-index-session-close-scans`

Closes #11299

## Summary
- Replace local SessionTable slab scans with a seeded bare-tuple index that preserves lowest-handle collision behavior.
- Add a seeded shared bare-tuple-to-scope index and maintain it under the primary shared-map lock on publish, removal, and paired clears.
- Keep delayed-close replacement detection bounded and scoped across both worker drain paths.
- Add collision/removal/slot-reuse/shared-clear regressions and a manual loaded-churn measurement.

## Validation
- Release session module suite: 369 passed.
- Release AF_XDP coordinator module suite: 312 passed.
- Release AF_XDP worker module suite: 99 passed.
- Shared publish/remove/clear regressions: 11 passed (publish_shared_session 4, publish_and_remove_shared_session 3, remove_shared_session_if 1, clear_mirror_ 3).
- Release bare_tuple_ regressions: 6 passed; purge_close_ regressions: 6 passed.
- Head high-overlap sample A: 100,000 local + shared rows, 28,348 close checks (28,316 overlapping actual publish/remove mutations), 4,000 publish/remove cycles, 110 ms; 1.740M checks/s, publish p99 1 us, max 8,011 us.
- Same harness/workload on base 0efa2ef: 2 close checks (both overlapping), 4,000 publish/remove cycles, 196 ms; 17 checks/s, publish p99 3 us, max 36,019 us.
- Head low-overlap repeat: 5,674 close checks, 2 overlaps, 74 ms; 517k checks/s, publish p99 3 us, max 23 us.
- Final post-push head high-overlap run: 87,761 close checks (87,760 overlapping actual mutations), 4,000 cycles, 53 ms; 2.723M checks/s, publish p99 8 us, max 11,213 us.

The manual churn cell requires at least one overlapping check, not a throughput threshold: overlap counts depend on thread scheduling. Observed high-overlap head p99 values were 1–8 us versus 3 us in the single base run (which had only two overlapping checks), so these runs do not establish a robust p99 no-regression claim. High-overlap head maxima of 8–11 ms recurred, while a low-overlap repeat maxed at 23 us; the benchmark measures wall time, not mutex hold/wait time, so the tail could be scheduler preemption or a brief lock wait and is not proven to be only a test artifact. The base full-scan path measured 17 close checks/s and a 36 ms publish maximum. This is a synthetic in-process workload, not a real AF_XDP host measurement.

## PR #11593 — userspace-dp: resolve mixed-zero shared NAT replies (#11361) [MERGED] (merged 2026-09-30)

Branch: `fix/11361-mixed-zero-shared-nat`

Closes #11361

Why:
A domain-A SNAT session's shared reverse wire key retains domain A. When
its reply arrives in domain 0, shared lookup misses the translated key
and the canonical untranslated tuple does not match, although the
worker-local reverse index admits the mixed-zero tuple. Publishing a
translated domain-0 alias could evict another tenant from the single-value
FastMap.

What:
On a domain-0 miss, consult the bounded alias-owner history, stamp the
unique non-zero forward domain, and probe the existing wire alias. Validate
it with the domain-preserving reverse-key transform; ambiguous or saturated
history fails closed. Keep the existing 0-to-A fallback and do not publish a
translated-at-zero alias. Thread the owner index through embedded ICMP and
NAT64 lookups. Add A-to-0, 0-to-A, and colliding-tenant regression cells;
document the behavior.

Validation:
- On master 33b80d4, a temporary A-to-0 repro failed at the expected
  admission assertion.
- On master d05ff139, the targeted suite passed 7 tests (7,284 filtered):
  TMPDIR=/var/worktrees/tmp-FrightenedTyrannosaurus-11361 \
  CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/var/worktrees/target-FrightenedTyrannosaurus-11361 \
  cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp shared_nat_ -- --nocapture
- Project-wide suites, formatters, and linters remain the parent lane's task.

Risk:
A-to-0 recovery fails closed after a tuple collision or ambiguity-index
saturation until the shared owner indexes are cleared; ambiguous history
never selects a tenant. Existing 0-to-A behavior is unchanged.

## PR #11612 — forwarding: stabilize ECMP selection across restarts (#11405) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-01)

Branch: `fix/11405-stable-ecmp-hash`

Closes #11405

## Why

The session ECMP selector used the per-process `hot_path_hash_seed`. After restart or HA promotion, a synced flow can be re-resolved with a different seed, selecting a different live member while retaining its stored SNAT rewrite. That breaks path-pinned NAT.

## What

Use a fixed, ECMP-specific domain seed for per-flow member selection. The per-boot secret remains on collision-sensitive caches and maps. A two-seed regression demonstrates that the previous seeded choices can differ while production ECMP remains stable for the same flow and ordered live-member set. Forwarding and multi-WAN descriptions and the stale archived review guardrail now reflect the stable-seed contract. This does not persist a selected egress; a changed live-member set or order can still remap a flow.

## Validation

- On base `1ed0846b0506b28102448f75f1844de34ea5aa44`, `ecmp_flow_member_stays_stable_across_hot_seeds` failed at the assertion that production ECMP uses the fixed seed; it passes with the fix.

- After integrating master `b0dd0c737`, `cargo check --quiet --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml --bin xpf-userspace-dp` passed; `afxdp::forwarding::tests::` passed 174 tests and both ECMP regressions passed individually.
- On final merge candidate `44456887249d`, `go build ./...`, `go test ./pkg/routing -count=1`, `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace -count=1`, `go test ./pkg/refactoraudit -count=1`, and all five queue canaries in `pkg/config` and `pkg/dataplane/userspace` passed.

## Risk

The ECMP mapping is stable but predictable by design; changing the ordered live-member set can remap flows. Per-boot secrecy remains in place for caches and maps where predictable collisions can amplify work.

Branch: `fix/11406-userspace-neighbor-aging`

Closes #11406

## Why
RX source-MAC learns remained indefinitely when an endpoint stopped transmitting, leaving silent stale MACs as forward candidates.

## What
- Stamp RX-only dynamic neighbors with monotonic last-seen timestamps and refresh on matching RX learns.
- Expire idle rows after 60 seconds on a 5-second neighbor-monitor sweep; retain manager-owned and kernel-confirmed entries.
- Advance the affected shard MAC epoch on expiry so cached destinations re-resolve, and allow the duplicate-RX path to relearn entries removed by the sweep.
- Document the process-local lease.

## Validation
- Reproduced RED on master: the idle RX-learned neighbor remained ForwardCandidate instead of becoming MissingNeighbor.
- Focused #11406 regressions: 3 passed.
- Existing RX-learn epoch regressions: 4 passed.
- Pre-policy overwrite and steady-state monitor regressions: 1 and 5 passed.

## Risk
Only RX-only dynamic rows age. Manager-owned and kernel-confirmed entries remain; no kernel neighbor programming or HA synchronization was added.

## PR #11619 — dataplane: inherit first-fragment session for plain fragments (#11412) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-01)

Branch: `fix/11412-plain-fragment-association`

Closes #11412

Plain fragmented flows permitted by an L4-specific policy were re-evaluated without transport ports on later fragments, so a non-first fragment could lose the first fragment's verdict.

This change installs an exact-default no-NAT session decision for committed plain-forward first fragments in the existing authority-, session-, generation-, and owner-fenced fragment association cache. Non-first fragments inherit that decision; denied first fragments still install no association, preserving port-deny behavior. The regression covers first, middle, and last fragments plus an explicit deny-port control.

Validation:
- Reproduced on master: the port-permit test failed because no association was installed; the deny control passed.
- Passed the two focused 11412 tests.
- Passed five related fragment association and filter regression tests.

Project-wide validation is being coordinated by the campaign owner.

## PR #11640 — config: fail closed on unknown filter actions (#11357) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-01)

Supersedes #11625. This replacement uses the same completed implementation with a single logical commit and corrected attribution/risk documentation; #11625 remains open for the parent to close.

## Why
An unrecognized firewall then-action must not gain implicit-permit semantics. Tolerant configuration loads must remain bootable while matching terms fail closed.

## What
- Retain unknown tokens in UnknownActions; after every then block contributes, compileFirewall finalizes the complete term to discard. The uniform gate rejects strict commits or warns on tolerant load/peer-sync.

No runtime/test behavior changed in this resubmission. Current documentation/comment-only changes also passed gofmt, git diff --check, git diff --cached --check, and go build ./pkg/config ./pkg/daemon.

## Risk
On tolerant load, any UnknownActions entry—including malformed known-modifier operands and unknown reject-message types—finalizes to discard. Matching traffic may be dropped, including management traffic. Well-formed known modifier-only terms remain fall-through; strict commit rejects malformed tokens. This is the intentional fail-closed tradeoff.

## PR #11647 — dataplane: age RX-learned neighbors (#11406) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-01)

Branch: `fix/11406-neighbor-aging-reviewed`

Closes #11406
Supersedes #11616

Why:
RX source-MAC learns survive indefinitely when a host stops transmitting,
leaving silent stale MACs as forward candidates. The aging map stores
NeighborRecord while the bulk removal API promises NeighborEntry, so the
public removal contract must keep returning Option<NeighborEntry>.

What:
Stamp RX-only neighbor rows with monotonic last-seen times and refresh them
on matching learns. The neighbor monitor expires idle rows after 60 seconds
on a 5-second sweep, preserving manager-owned and kernel-confirmed entries.
Expiry advances the owning shard epoch so cached destination MACs are
discarded and future resolutions enter the MissingNeighbor/probe path; the
duplicate-RX path can relearn an expired row. Map the removed NeighborRecord
to its entry, preserving Option<NeighborEntry> removal behavior.

Validation:
Reused FixNeighbor11616 evidence on the normal merge with f5584e77d (no new
runs in this mechanical resubmit lane): cargo check --bin xpf-userspace-dp
PASS; cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp sharded_neighbor::tests 56 passed;
11406-focused tests 3 passed; manager_neighbor_replace tests 5 passed.

Risk:
Only RX-only dynamic rows age; manager-owned and kernel-confirmed entries
remain. No kernel neighbor programming or HA synchronization was added.
Bulk-remove metadata is discarded with the removed record; aging and sweep
policy unchanged.

## PR #11713 — ha: repair HA import fan-out refusal (#11360) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-01)

Branch: `fix/11360-import-fanout-refusal`

Closes #11360.

Queue-full HA upserts now return a non-success repair result while each affected worker retains bounded, ordered latest-intent debt. At the repair boundary workers re-read shared authority; if a newer delete removed the row, they run the existing DeleteSynced cleanup and flow-cache invalidation path. Repair results use a wire prefix distinct from terminal semantic refusals, so older Go readers fail closed without classifying a committed row as rollbackable. Repair overflow separately blocks HA takeover readiness and remains latched across later successful socket writes.

## PR #11714 — config: fence lifelines from tenant VRFs (#11364) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-01)

Branch: `fix/11364-lifeline-ri-fence`

Closes #11364
Closes #11365

Why: If a configured cluster control/fabric lifeline is also assigned to a
tenant routing instance, its VRF master becomes shared with data co-members.
LOCAL_IN cannot distinguish the lifeline slave from other ingress on that
master, so the lifeline exemption can suppress the co-members' host-inbound
scope. Separately, mapped em*/fab*/fxp* interfaces get vrf-mgmt ownership by
name class but are not necessarily exempt from host-inbound zone denies.

What: Strict compile rejects configured role-derived lifeline membership in
a tenant VRF. Tolerant compile warns and quarantines only those member keys,
leaving ordinary co-members and their unique or fail-closed VRF ingress scope
intact. Commit validation warns when an actually declared device-map
management-class interface lacks a host-inbound lifeline role. No packet-path
policy changed. Config/device-map guidance and Debian changelog are updated.

## PR #11716 — ipsec: gate shared-bind selector overlap unless disjoint (#11380) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-01)

Branch: `fix/11380-st0-bind-gate`

Related to #11380

## Why
Two route-based VPNs sharing one st0 bind can render identical wildcard traffic selectors under the same if_id. XFRM then cannot distinguish the SAs, so routed traffic may select the wrong peer SA or blackhole.

## What
- At strict compile, compare each VPN pair sharing a bind and nonzero if_id. Reject if both their effective local and remote selector unions overlap; accept only pairs provably disjoint on at least one side.
- Match the renderer semantics: route-based omitted selectors become `0.0.0.0/0,::/0`; parse IPv4/IPv6 hosts, CIDRs, and inclusive ranges; treat omitted/unknown sides conservatively.
- Share the wildcard constant with the renderer, preserve the #2933 device-alias and #9624 SA-name gates, and update regression tests/docs/changelog. Tolerant loads warn and continue.

## Validation
- RED before fix: `TestSharedSt0BindWildcardSelectorsRejected11380` failed because strict compile accepted two VPNs with wildcard selectors.
- Post-rebase focused config cells pass: `go test ./pkg/config -run "^(TestSharedSt0Bind|TestIPsecSANameCollisionsFailCommit9624|TestSecureTunnelBindIfaceUnambiguousCommits)$" -count=1`.
- `go test ./pkg/ipsec -count=1`, `go test ./pkg/refactoraudit -count=1`, `go build ./...`, and scoped `gofmt` pass.
- The full config suite on the change branch also shows unrelated #11312, #10826, and #7484 reds. Targeted tests on clean `origin/master` (`de2d1fe51`) reproduced them: #11312 forwarding-instance FBF/packed-RI cases; #10826 API-key expiration prerequisites affecting multi-leaf/web-management tests; and #7484 slot-escape/spelling-coverage ratchets.

## Risk
No live two-peer XFRM lab validation has been performed. Static compile checks do not prove routed prefixes reach only their intended SA. Existing configs receive a tolerant-load warning; no NHTB-style next-hop demux was found in the IPsec implementation.

## Lab remainder
Not run: a real two-peer IPsec/XFRM scenario proving each routed prefix encrypts only through its intended SA with two VPNs sharing st0. Keep #11380 open until this dataplane proof is captured.

## PR #11721 — config: reject merged duplicate WireGuard AllowedIPs (#11381) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-01)

Branch: `fix/11381-wg-allowedips-gate`

Closes #11381

## Why
Interface-level WireGuard tunnels merge peers authored under multiple units into one endpoint. Per-tunnel AllowedIPs checks cannot see an exact prefix tie between distinct unit peers, so stable LPM ordering encrypts shared-prefix traffic to one peer and the other peer cannot pass the decapsulation source gate.

## What
Extend validateMergedWireguardUnitPeers to check canonical masked AllowedIPs prefixes across the actual merged peer set (interface peers plus first-seen unit peers). Reject a prefix owned by distinct public keys before emission, naming the canonical prefix and both peers. Preserve allowed overlapping, non-identical prefixes. Add issue-specific exact duplicate, host-bit canonicalization, and negative-control cells; update WireGuard interop documentation and the Debian changelog.

Examples include #11312 routing-instance expectations, #10826 API-auth fixtures, #7484 spelling-gate thresholds, existing Go formatting, and environment-dependent CLI/grpcapi tests.
- make test exited 2 on unrelated Go/census failures and the Rust #10204 link-map check. The Go failures and skip-census floor mismatch were reproduced on clean master; this PR changes no Rust code.

Add the <256 boundary and deterministic concurrent lock-order regressions, and document the behavior.

Validation:

- The lock-order regression failed with unlock-before-record and passed after the fix.
- cargo check passed.
- Rust cells passed: #11718 boundary (1), lock race (1), #11360 (6), #7201 bounded drain (2).

Risk:
Internal worker scheduling only; no Go/wire contract changed. Lock nesting is queue-to-repair-debt only; there is no reverse order.

## PR #11731 — nftables: deny unzoned ingress before destination fallback (#11409) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-01)

Branch: `fix/11409-nft-fallback-order`

Closes #11409

## Why
An addressed physical interface with no zone could reach a zoned service by the destination-only host-inbound fallback. Conversely, zone ingress rules included unzoned local addresses and could admit a zoned service to those destinations before the unzoned-address deny.

## What
- Drop unzoned physical ingress to local addresses before residual established acceptance and destination-only zone fallback.
- Use `meta sdifname` for unzoned VRF slaves before rules scoped to a shared LOCAL_IN master.
- Keep source-guard classification row-local for zone annotations: a zone ref to a VLAN unit can fan a zone onto the physical base snapshot while the unzoned unit-0 row shares its LinuxName. The untagged parent remains guarded; the VLAN view claims only its child netdev.
- Keep loopback, tunnel, and lifeline exclusions netdev-wide.
- Restrict ingress-zone service rules to zone-owned destination addresses; mirror text and netlink renderers.
- Add rendered ordering, netlink parity, helper, real-builder alias, and real-kernel packet coverage in both directions; add the changelog entry.

## Validation
- RED before the original fix: `XPF_REQUIRE_NETNS=1 go test ./pkg/daemon -run '^TestHostInboundUnzonedIngressVerdictsOnRealKernel11409$' -count=1 -v` admitted both unzoned-ingress-to-zoned-service and zoned-ingress-to-unzoned-destination SSH attempts (`connected`, wanted `timeout`).
- GREEN: `XPF_REQUIRE_NETNS=1 go test ./pkg/daemon -run '^TestHostInboundUnzonedIngress(Ordering11409|VerdictsOnRealKernel11409)$' -count=1 -v` passed.
- RED with the broad zone-based protection prepass: `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace -run '^TestBuildUnzonedHostInboundIngressPreservesUnzonedUnitZeroAlias11409$' -count=1 -v` omitted expected `ge-0-0-8` guard.
- GREEN after narrowing protection to hard lifeline/tunnel/loopback exclusions: the same production-builder alias cell passed.
- `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace -run '^TestBuildUnzonedHostInboundIngress' -count=1 -v` passed.
- `XPF_REQUIRE_NETNS=1 go test ./pkg/daemon -run '^TestNftNetlinkParity$' -count=1 -v` passed, including the #11409 scenario.
- `go test ./pkg/refactoraudit -count=1` passed; scoped `gofmt -l` returned no paths.

## Risk
New original-direction packets arriving on known unzoned physical interfaces are denied to local addresses. Reply-direction, lifeline, and non-physical reinject paths retain their prior exceptions. Both directions are explicit in the issue acceptance and are included here; no follow-up was filed.

## PR #11757 — cluster: harden duplicate-identity beacon warnings (#11483) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-02)

Branch: `fix/11483-beacon-lows`

Related to #11483

Why
A full replay cache previously evicted live nonces, allowing an authenticated capture to appear new under pressure. Forward wall-clock steps could shorten suppression, process restart discards in-memory replay state, and unsupported/runtime socket failures needed operator-visible warnings.

What
- Form inclusive replay deadlines from max(receipt time, signed timestamp)+30s using the receiver monotonic clock; never evict live nonces and warn when capacity suppresses new beacons.
- Warn on unsupported address families, narrow prefixes, socket setup failures, and runtime read/send failures through a separate shared 30s health-warning budget. These signals remain warn-only and do not affect heartbeat, liveness, or election.
- Make restart-replay uncertainty, node-id repair, and weak/published-key beacon forgery explicit without rejecting configured weak keys or rendering secret bytes.
- Document the bounded-cache tradeoff, precise clock rollback residual, and required lab proof.

Validation
- RED on clean master cbb9c710f: temporary full-cache probe observed a duplicate warning after a live nonce was evicted; the fixed cache suppresses it and reports saturation.
- Runtime socket-warning regression cell failed before the change with zero health WARNs; it passes after the change.
- `go test ./pkg/cluster -count=1`: PASS.
- `go build ./...`: PASS.
- `go test -count=1 ./pkg/refactoraudit/`: PASS.
- Focused config warning cells and `GOLDEN_4406_UPDATE=1 go test ./pkg/config -run TestCompileGolden4406 -count=1`: PASS.
- The full config suite has unrelated baseline failures for #10826, #11312, and #7484; the selected ten-test failure set reproduces on clean master c22f80bb4.

Risk
A sender with an accepted PSK can keep the bounded cache saturated using distinct beacons; the separate rate-limited warning exposes this, but new duplicate signals remain suppressed until entries expire. At the maximum +30s future skew, a stamp is fresh at its 60s suppression deadline; a 1s rollback just after cache expiry can restore freshness.

Lab status
The required two-host/control-L2 shared-address dual-PRIMARY proof has not been run. It must verify delivery with the actual VRF and `accept_local` posture, including sysctl and socket-failure behavior. This PR is related to the issue only; #11483 remains open pending that lab validation.

## PR #11838 — userspace-dp: re-resolve sessions on FIB/config changes (#11373) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-02)

## PR #11844 — userspace-dp: bound fib_dump control deadline (#11840) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-02)

Branch: `fix/11840-fib-deadline`

Closes #11840

Why: fib_dump's ~60-byte request gets the 3 s base even though the helper can produce a 64 MiB response. The armed deadline spans helper processing, Unix-socket transfer, and Go's response decode/framing, so Go can abandon a legitimate round trip while a large dump is still being processed.

What: add a 35 s fib_dump floor budgeted for five response-sized passes at 10 MiB/s: route-row sizing, helper response-cap counting and encoding, socket write, and Go response decode/framing, plus the ordinary 3 s margin. The agreement test reads MAX_CONTROL_RESPONSE_BYTES from Rust and resolves its MAX_CONTROL_REQUEST_BYTES alias, then checks the Go cap and floor. A round-trip cell observes the actual armed deadline; unrelated small verbs remain at base. The floor stays below one-third of controlMaxDeadline and the global clamp is unchanged.

Documentation: pkg/dataplane/README.md has no per-verb control-deadline contract, so no module README change is needed. The source comment/test and docs/log/11840.md record the rationale and contract.

Validation:
- RED before: with the fib_dump map entry removed, the final floor cell failed at 3 s versus 32 s work plus the 3 s margin; it passed after restoration.
- PASS: focused fib/#9344 cells with -count=5 on the final rebased branch.
- PASS: go build ./..., go test ./pkg/refactoraudit -count=1, and scoped gofmt check after the final rebase.
- The full userspace package run reported failures in TestContractSnapshotGolden9821, TestDeferredPublishMarkIsWiredEndToEnd9637, and TestNilUnitSlotCastsNoTrunkZoneVote_6722. All three were reproduced in a clean worktree at current origin/master dfd14ee82.
- make test ran Go race/vet and the Go suite, but failed in broader Go tests, go-skip-census drift, and check-userspace-dt-needed's relative linker-map path. With an absolute CARGO_TARGET_DIR, make test-rust passed its preflight then its release Rust suite reported 7192 passed, 211 failed, and 7 ignored.

Risk: 10 MiB/s is an explicit response-work budget, not a hard real-time throughput guarantee. The existing 120 s clamp is unchanged.

## PR #11874 — test: resync failover clocks after crash reboot (#11872) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-02)

Branch: `fix/11872-clock-resync`

## Why
The no-NTP loss lab returned fw0 2m18s behind after crash reboot. Clock skew breaks fabric-auth and heartbeat freshness, preventing pending-bulk completion and causing otherwise-ready failback requests to be refused.

## What
Read host UTC once, set both node clocks with incus exec date -u -s, and record a harness cell after the crash-reboot wait in both failover smokes, before rejoin/failback readiness checks. The hermetic selftest covers a common timestamp, failure reporting, and still attempting the peer.

- go test -count=1 ./pkg/refactoraudit/
- bash scripts/refactoring-audit-touched.sh

The parent lane will provide live-cluster proof.

Closes #11872

## PR #11875 — fix(routing): detect structural PBR readback mismatches (#11440) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-02)

Branch: `fix/11440-pbr-applied-structure`

Closes #11440

`xpf_pbr_rules_applied` is now explicitly the even-priority PBR-band entry count, not proof that the active rules were installed correctly. New `xpf_pbr_rules_mismatched` compares desired lookup rules with netlink-readable table and match fields and counts missing, mismatched, unexpected, and duplicate entries. Both readback metrics are omitted together if either address-family listing fails. Metric help and docs describe the unreadable DSCP selector and rule action.

The collector builds the desired rule set and degraded-term count once per scrape. Count-only routing APIs were removed and callers migrated to the structured status/build APIs.

Red-before / green-after: on pre-fix `d6a4bc876`, the wrong-table-in-band regression cell failed because both correct and wrong-table rules reported `applied=1`; the post-fix wrong-table, wrong-match, missing, duplicate, and unexpected-slot cells pass.

Validation (rebased on current master):

- `go test ./pkg/routing ./pkg/api -count=5` — PASS
- PBR regression/build and metric-alias canaries with `-count=5` — PASS

## PR #11876 — test: scope failover journal diagnosis to test window (#11873) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-02)

Branch: `fix/11873-journal-window`

## Why
The failback-failure diagnostic searched all retained fw0 xpfd history. A rolling-deploy no-RETH sync-hold timeout could therefore be included in a later failover test's journal grep and blamed on the wrong window.

## What
Capture fw0's journal cursor before preflight and read only entries after that boundary when rendering failback diagnosis. If cursor capture fails, explicitly omit the journal history instead of falling back to an unscoped read. The hermetic selftest models a retained deploy-time transient followed by a test-window failback record and checks that only the latter reaches diagnosis.

## Validation
- RED before cursor helpers existed (3 behavior cells failed); green after, 4/4.
- bash test/incus/failover-journal-selftest.sh
- bash -n test/incus/failover-journal-lib.sh test/incus/failover-journal-selftest.sh test/incus/test-failover.sh scripts/run-selftests.sh
- go build ./...
- go test -count=1 ./pkg/refactoraudit/
- bash scripts/refactoring-audit-touched.sh

An additional selftest-census-selftest invocation reported an unrelated existing real-tree gap: test/incus/fbf-steering-harness-selftest.sh is on disk but not registered by scripts/run-selftests.sh. The parent lane will provide live-cluster proof.

## PR #11885 — userspace-dp: reject duplicate logical ingress keys [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-02)

Branch: `fix/11461-duplicate-ingress-key`

## Why
Parent-bound logical interfaces with the same `(bind_ifindex, VID)` silently replaced each other in the ingress map, making the effective logical identity and zone mapping depend on row order.

## What
Track the first parent-bound owner for each key and return a typed `SnapshotIntegrityError` when another row claims that key with a different logical ifindex. Preserve intentional base-interface fallback replacement. Add rejection and valid distinct-key/zone-mapping coverage, update the previous native-VLAN ambiguity expectation, and document the behavior.

## Validation
- Red-before: the new duplicate-key regression received an accepted build instead of the required error.
- `cargo check --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml -p xpf-userspace-dp` — PASS.
- Forwarding-build test module — 193 passed; the two new parent-bound key cells passed five repeated canary runs.
- `go build ./...` and `go test -count=1 ./pkg/refactoraudit/` — PASS.
- Rust formatters were intentionally not run per `docs/engineering-style.md:1259-1277`.

## Risk
Only conflicting parent-bound `(bind_ifindex, VID)` mappings with different logical ifindexes are rejected; base-interface fallback semantics remain intact.

Closes #11461

## PR #11890 — dataplane: keep unresolved lo0 addresses non-local (#11464) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-02)

Branch: `fix/11464-lo0-local`

## Why
Ordinary Junos lo0 configuration does not create a Linux lo0 netdev. Configured lo0 addresses were placed in the shim local-address map even though the Rust helper drops unresolved ifindex-0 interface rows, so shim and helper local classification disagreed.

## What
Warn at config validation when ordinary lo0 units have addresses; omit unresolved lo0 rows from the shim local-address map; preserve local classification for a real lo0/tunnel netdev with positive ifindex. Add config, shim/helper, and Rust LocalDelivery/NoRoute cells, and document the warning fallback.

## Validation
- Red-before: the lo0 warning and shim-alignment Go cells failed against the original implementation.
- On the rebased head, both new Go cells passed with `-count=5`; the Rust test proved unresolved lo0 is NoRoute and resolved lo0 is LocalDelivery.
- `go build ./...`, Rust `cargo check`, `cargo test` for the lo0 disposition cell, `go test ./pkg/refactoraudit -count=1`, and scoped gofmt passed.
- `go test ./pkg/config -count=5` and `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace -count=5` were attempted. The config suite failed on existing #10826/#11312/#8939/schema-coverage cells and timed out; the userspace suite failed in #9637, #6722, and the #6691 xfrmi fixture. The issue-specific cells passed.

## Risk
Ordinary lo0 remains non-local on hosts without a real Linux lo0 netdev; the warning makes that limitation visible instead of silently advertising local delivery. A real device or tunnel with a positive ifindex retains its local behavior.

## PR #11891 — nat: pass ICMP type through flowless NAT probes (#11509) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-02)

Branch: `fix/11509-snat-flowless-icmp`

Closes #11509

Why:
Flowless SNAT discarded readable ICMP type/code, so an echo-only rule
could remain a possible match for a known error. DNAT had the same
flowless overmatch, causing the NAT safety fence to treat a packet as
translatable when the configured typed rule did not match.

What:
Thread `policy_packet_icmp` through flowless SNAT/DNAT probes and
`retry_flowless_fragment_nat`. A known type/code mismatch now rules out
a typed candidate while unreadable ICMP and protocol-255 cases remain
possible. Static NAT is unchanged because it has no ICMP type selector.

Validation:
- RED-before: the echo-only SNAT/DNAT regression failed on base behavior.
- RED-on-missing-threading: the retry-path cell failed when the source
  NAT probe received `None`; it passed after propagation was restored.
- All three #11509 cells passed five consecutive canary runs; the full
  `nat::tests_l4_match` module passed (21 tests).
- `cargo check`, `go build ./...`, and
  `go test ./pkg/refactoraudit -count=1` passed.
- No Go files changed; Go formatting was not applicable. Rust
  formatters were not run per `docs/engineering-style.md:1259-1277`.

Risk:
Unreadable ICMP type/code remains conservatively possible. Known typed
mismatches no longer trip the translation fence; static 1:1 NAT is
unchanged.

## PR #11905 — test: qualify VRF 9063 static route RIB [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-02)

Branch: `fix/11659-vrf-unit0-pool-tagged-siblings`

Closes #11659

The VRF fixture put its IPv6 static route under unqualified inet6.0. The compiler accepts inet6.0 only in global routing-options; inside routing-instance blue, that route is out of scope and omitted. The helper therefore resolved no route for any candidate set, making the red unrelated to unit-0 sibling inclusion.

Use blue.inet6.0 so the unit-0 pool resolves ge-0-0-0. The helper now also requires the compiled blue instance to contain IPv6 route 2001:db8:ff::/64 via fe80::9 before resolving, preventing the whole-device narrowness row from passing vacuously. The whole-device narrowness row and tagged-sibling default-pool inclusion cell remain unchanged. This is a test-fixture correction; production route and pool code are untouched.

Red-before: go test ./pkg/daemon -run TestVRFPoolDoesNotAbsorbTaggedSiblings9063|TestVRFUnit0DoesNotPullTaggedSiblingsIn9063|TestVRFUnit0DoesNotClaimTaggedSiblings9063 -v -count=1 failed the pool assertion with an empty interface.
Green-after: the same three cells pass with -count=5 after the fixture correction and anti-vacuity guard.

Battery: go build ./... passed; go test -count=1 ./pkg/refactoraudit/ passed; gofmt -l on the changed Go test was empty. The full pkg/daemon run also reported failures in TestUngatedComposedRecoveryConverges10769 (permissions on /root/.xpf_history and /root/.xpf_cli_history) and TestBothPassesBindTheSameNameSet6805; both exact tests reproduced on clean origin/master c0276cc08.

## PR #11918 — afxdp: cap tunnel MSS by overlay route MTU (#11687) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-02)

Branch: `fix/11687-tunnel-tcp-mss`

## Why
Tunnel TCP SYN MSS calculations used only the physical/transport budget, not the overlay route MTU. GRE could advertise MSS 1416 where route_mtu=1400 permits 1360; an explicit gre-out MSS bypassed that ceiling, and WG similarly advertised 1365.

## PR #11922 — userspace-dp: preflight ICMP NAT64 fragment size (#11720) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-02)

Branch: `fix/11720-nat64-icmp-nonfirst-preflight`

Related to #11720. This PR is a scoped preflight correction only; the issue stays open for end-to-end fragmented ICMPv6 translation.

Why: NAT64 preflight did not size non-first ICMPv6 fragments, so the constrained-MTU decision reached generic IPv6 PTB classification.

What: Include only TCP, UDP, and ICMPv6 non-first-fragment protocols in the opaque-payload size calculation; keep unsupported protocols rejected. Add preflight and constrained-MTU dispatch regression cells.

Validation: Rust output-length tests (3) and NAT64 fragment-dispatch tests (4), each run in five consecutive canaries; `cargo check`; `go build ./...`; `go test -count=5 ./pkg/flowexport`; `go test -count=1 ./pkg/refactoraudit/`.

Risk / remainder: This does not translate the packet. `write_v6_to_v4_translate` still rejects real first ICMPv6 fragments and `write_v6_to_v4_nonfirst_into` still only handles TCP/UDP, so the packet can still be dropped later. ICMPv6 checksum conversion needs whole-message context because its pseudo-header includes the full upper-layer length, unavailable from the first fragment. Complete support needs bounded reassembly (or equivalent checksum context), real first+tail dispatch coverage with association-order safety, and valid IPv4 fragment reassembly under constrained MTU.

## PR #11973 — Add packet regression for FIB-only route overlay bumps [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-03)

Branch: `fix/11599-fib-generation`

Closes #11599.

`#11373` already made established-session forwarding stamps compare both config and FIB generations and cold-resolve stale hits. This PR adds the missing packet-level acceptance regression for the FIB-only invalidation path.

The test drives packets through the real poll-descriptor path: it establishes a flow through v1 gateway .1, advances only FIB generation while holding config generation fixed, and changes the default route to v2 gateway .2. The first post-bump ACK must miss the old flow-cache entry, egress via .2 with its live neighbor MAC, and reseed; the next ACK must be a confirmed flow-cache hit with .2 egress. An unchanged /32 control remains via .1 and is confirmed on its subsequent cache hit. A red-before simulation that compared only config generation failed by continuing to egress via .1; the restored full-pair check passes.

Source nuance: Go `PublishRouteOverlaySnapshot` publishes a new snapshot generation; the subsequent `BumpFIBGeneration` changes only FIB generation. This regression holds config generation at 7 to isolate the FIB-only consumer path rather than relying on config-generation invalidation.

Validation on the rebased final head: `go build ./...`, `cargo check --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml --bin xpf-userspace-dp`, `go test -count=1 ./pkg/refactoraudit/`, and repository-wide `gofmt -l` passed. The new packet cell passed five consecutive runs.

The affected flow-cache module run on the rebased head had 45 passes and one unrelated existing failure: `txn_failed_reply_repair_forwards_uncached_then_self_heals_below_cap` (expected tx=1, observed 0; also reproduced in isolation). The full Rust unit binary run on the pre-rebase tree reported 7,293 passed, 180 unrelated failures, and 7 ignored. These unrelated failures are outside this patch; parent review is baseline-verifying the affected-module failure on master.

Closes #11778

`walkGroupToContext` now visits every matching same-keyed source container at each ancestor level and unions their children, aligning nested source lookup with the existing destination-side union behavior. The one-match path keeps its no-copy fast path; on multiple matches it copies before appending, avoiding mutation of source group slices.

Added direct and nested-apply regression cells for a group body split over repeated `system` blocks. They assert that the first and second inherited leaves and the inline destination time-zone all survive. Updated the config group-expansion notes and added docs/log/11778.md.

Red-before: both new cells failed on the first-match walk; the second body and `domain-name` were absent. Green-after: the two cells plus `TestGroupContainerReachesEverySameKeyedStanza9802` passed with `-count=5`.

Validation passed: `go build ./...`, `cargo check --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml` (warnings, no errors), focused regression/destination-union cells with `-count=5`, and `go test ./pkg/refactoraudit -count=1`. Full `go test ./pkg/config -count=5` timed out after 10 minutes with failures in FBF forwarding-instance membership, API-key expiry, packed routing-instance, slot-escape coverage, and `TestSchemaSpellingDifferentialGate`.

`make test` was also run: Go race legs, vet, and build-tag census passed; Go `./...` reported CLI BGP-AS fixture failures and the config failures. Rust reported 7,297 passed, 179 failed, 7 ignored. Harness census found two undeclared library scripts; Go skip census reported 451 sites versus the 400 floor. Details are in docs/log/11778.md. This fix changes neither config types nor commit-time rejection rules, so no additional rejection-contract gate applied.

## PR #11979 — userspace-dp: gate BA classification on ingress binding (#11386) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-03)

Branch: `fix/11386-cos-ba`

Closes #11386

## Why
The egress CoS admission gate omits classifier-only ingress units. Deriving ingress trust from the egress CoS interface map therefore demoted explicitly trusted CS7 markings to best effort. Locally generated replies also have no wire ingress and must preserve their existing egress BA classification.

## What
Retain validated DSCP, inet-precedence, and 802.1p bindings independently from egress scheduler state, and use them to gate transit BA queue and loss-priority lookups across fresh, cached, flowless, cache-hit, and mirror paths. Preserve locally generated reply markings as trusted. Reject conflicting classifier bindings on logical units sharing one ifindex.

## Validation
- Red-before binding-only ingress: observed queue 0 instead of expected network-control queue 7.
- Red-before local generated reply: observed queue 0 instead of expected queue 7.
- `cargo check --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml` — passed (existing warnings).
- CoS classifier suite — 83 passed.
- Binding-only ingress, local generated reply, and shared-ifindex binding cells — each passed 5 consecutive exact runs.
- `go build ./...` — passed.
- Uncached `pkg/refactoraudit` — passed.
- No Go files changed; gofmt not applicable.

## Risk
Adds a small per-ifindex map for valid ingress classifier bindings. Conflicting bindings on logical units sharing an ifindex now fail snapshot integrity, consistently with existing CoS alias checks. Locally generated replies keep their prior BA classification.

## PR #11984 — forwarding: stabilize ECMP identity across ifindex changes (#11686) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-03)

Branch: `fix/11686-ecmp-id`

## Why
ECMP candidate hashes included kernel ifindex, so HA peers with different enumeration could select different members for the same session tuple. Interface SNAT persists the selected source rewrite, so re-resolution on another member could orphan the stored path.

## What
Compute a stable logical-interface identity from the configured interface name during snapshot build and hash it with the gateway and tunnel endpoint instead of ifindex. Add regressions for dual-enumerated IPv4, IPv6, interface-only routes, and interface-SNAT rewrites. Kernel ifindex remains forwarding metadata; flow hashing and weights are unchanged.

Closes #11686

## Validation
- Red-before: including ifindex made the cross-enumeration test select ge-0/0/2 versus ge-0/0/1 and made the SNAT test rewrite to 192.0.3.1 versus 192.0.2.1.
- Both new Rust regressions passed five consecutive runs.
- `cargo test afxdp::forwarding_build::` — 239 passed.
- `cargo check`, `go build ./...`, `go test -count=1 ./pkg/refactoraudit/`, and `gofmt` — passed.
- `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace -count=5` failed in `TestDeferredPublishMarkIsWiredEndToEnd9637`, `TestNilUnitSlotCastsNoTrunkZoneVote_6722`, and `TestRetainedLiveXfrmiLeavesTheAdjudicatedSets`.
- `cargo test afxdp::forwarding::` — 301 passed, 10 failures in zone-ingress and leak-overlap tests.

## Risk
Renaming a configured logical interface intentionally changes candidate identity and may remap flows. This is not a persisted egress pin; the 64-bit identity has the usual finite hash-collision risk.
