## PR #13256 — userspace-dp: report BA-reclassified queue in active-flow telemetry (#13077) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-15)

Branch: `fix/13077-campaign-pub`

Why: `FlowCache::active_flow_debug_entries` attributed every active flow to `descriptor.tx_selection.queue_id` frozen at seed time. A `ba_reclassify` flow deliberately serves successive packets on different CoS queues (per-packet DSCP/PCP), so per-queue `cos_counts` and the per-flow debug rows permanently credited the seed queue (e.g. a SYN seeded on queue 0 while all payload served on queue 3), corrupting `xpf_userspace_cos_active_flow_count` and the v8 equal-flow estimator (finding D5-01).

What: add `RewriteDescriptor::last_queue_id` (the one deliberately non-constant descriptor field, read only by the debug scan). `insert` seeds it from `tx_selection.queue_id`; `stage_flow_cache_hit` stamps the effective (BA-reclassified or pinned) queue through the entry borrow it already holds after the drop/policer gates. The scan reports `last_queue_id` with the seed as fallback only when never stamped, so queue-less entries stay unattributed. NOT changed: `tx_selection.queue_id` stays the frozen seed selection every other consumer reads correctly.

Validation: new tests `active_flow_debug_entries_use_last_served_queue_after_ba_reclassify` and `active_flow_debug_entries_seed_stamp_and_queueless_entries`. RED with the scan reverted to the seed queue (queue 0 instead of 3); GREEN post-fix (`flow_cache::` 121 passed). Full `--bins` suite 7887 passed, 1 failed (`wire_invariant_default_specimens`, also failing on pristine master 8e26b24d8).

Risk: single `Option<u8>` store on the forwarded cache-hit path; no extra cache scan, allocation, or atomic. Dropped/TTL-expired/rejected hits never reach the stamp; flows serving on multiple queues within one window report their most recent queue.

Closes #13077

## PR #13310 — config: warn on inert snmp/system knobs in every AST spelling (#13089) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-15)

Branch: `fix/13089-campaign-pub`

Closes #13089 (research D7-13, deep-review finding: `snmpInertKnobWarnings` / `systemInertKnobWarnings` inspect only `node.Children` / `FindChild`, missing packed bodies, flat-set chains, and subsequent sibling blocks).

## Why

`snmpInertKnobWarnings` walked raw `node.Children` through a one-level `nodeHasSub`, and `systemInertKnobWarnings` read one `FindChild` block per group, so security-relevant accept-but-inert advisories — `snmp community view` (the community answers the full ifTable), `snmp community logical-system` (nested source restriction NOT applied), `system ntp authentication-key` (NTP auth NOT enforced), `system login retry-options` (login lockout NOT enforced) — were silently suppressed on AST shapes the compilers accept and compile:

- flat-set chains (`set snmp community <c> authorization ro view v` nests `view` under `authorization`, #8778; `set system services ssh root-login deny rate-limit 5` nests `rate-limit` under `root-login`),
- two-level community containers (`snmp { community { <name> { view v; } } }`),
- second sibling blocks (`system { login {...} login {...} }` — `FindChild` saw only the first),
- brace-elided bodies packed on the block's or the whole `system` line's own Keys (#2419).

The advisory is the only defense for these knobs (they commit clean and compile to nothing); a line break decided whether it fired.

## What

`pkg/config/compiler_system.go`:

- `snmpInertKnobWarnings` now takes the `snmpChildren` list `compileSNMP` already built with `packedBodyChildren`, and the community search (`communityHasInertStatement13089`) spans the community's Keys tail, every name block of a two-level container, and the whole statement subtree (`subtreeHasStatement13089`).
- `systemInertKnobWarnings` walks every sibling `login`/`ntp`/`internet-options`/`services` block, hoists flat-set chains with `expandRun9235` (`systemServicesSSHSchema13089`), reads one-liner bodies packed on a block's own Keys via `blockHas`, and synthesizes the braced shape for a fully packed `system` line via `packedBodyChildren` guarded on empty `Children` (a node can carry both a packed tail and a braced body — `system host-name fw1 { ... }` — and the synthesis must not drop the body).
- `internet-options` extras are collected recursively (`collectInternetOptionsExtras13089`) so an extra chained under the modelled leaf is still named.
- Advisory wording, dedup, and the never-echo-secrets rule (community name, NTP key value) are unchanged.
- NOT changed: snmp tail keywords `schemaSNMP` does not declare (`snmp view v ...;`, `snmp health-monitor;` brace-elided on one line) stay advisory-silent — `packedBodyChildren` refuses to synthesize undeclared tails and no compiler reader sees them either; declaring them is separate schema work.

## Validation

- New `pkg/config/compiler_inert_knobs_13089_test.go`: 13 shape cells (snmp chain ×3, two-level container ×2; system sibling blocks ×3, chained ssh, packed ssh/ntp one-liners, packed `system` line, internet-options chain) verified **RED on pristine origin/master `18c285c29`** and green on this head; regression guards for the already-warning spellings plus negative controls (no new advisories on modelled-only configs; secrets never echoed) green on both.
- `go test ./pkg/config/` full suite: **ok, 6144 top-level test results**, 0 failures (~400 s).
- Rebased onto current master (`2ced657ce`, #13090 sibling-chassis fold landed mid-flight — no overlap) and re-gated green.

## Risk

Low. Advisory-only: no compile output, gate, or dataplane behavior changes; warnings appear on configs that previously committed silently, which is the point. Tolerant loads (`Store.Load`, `SyncApply`) of configs using these spellings now surface the advisories too. Residual: brace-elided one-line snmp knobs whose keywords are not declared in `schemaSNMP` (view/trap-options/health-monitor/rmon) remain advisory-silent in that one spelling — the compiler is blind to them as well; worth a follow-up schema-declaration change.

## PR #13392 — userspace-dp: reject undefined deny schedulers (#13169) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-15)

Branch: `fix/13169-campaign-pub`

## Why

`buildOneRuleSnapshot` only poisoned undefined-scheduler DENY/REJECT rules when `LenientContentDropped` was set. Programmatic or partial configs could therefore publish an inactive deny and let traffic fall through. Rejection diagnostics also misattributed generic application carriers and dropped co-occurring malformed-shape / unknown-child causes.

## What

Always poison undefined-scheduler DENY/REJECT rules; attribute the rejection to the scheduler. Report malformed-zone and unknown-child metadata independently and suppress generic-only carrier attribution when metadata identifies the cause. Add focused D4-13 regressions and `docs/log/13169.md`. PERMIT scheduler behavior and wire fields remain unchanged.

## Validation

- `go test -count=1 -run '^TestD413' ./pkg/dataplane/userspace` passed after the fix. The same tests failed on pristine master with inactive unflagged deny/reject rules, spurious generic application attribution, and dropped combined carrier reasons.
- `go vet ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/...`, gofmt, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Full `go test -count=1 ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/...` has unrelated pre-existing failures: pristine master reproduces the package failures; the `format` subpackage passed.

## Risk

Partial/programmatic configs with an undefined scheduler on deny/reject now refuse the whole snapshot instead of publishing an inactive rule, matching the fail-closed contract. Existing unrelated full-suite failures are documented in `docs/log/13169.md`.

Closes #13169

Closes #13174

## Why
This is a post-merge follow-up to #13398. The real host-inbound table can deny a lifeline-shared address only on the old ingress netdev through IngressDenyV4/V6. Treating that address as destination-wide retained coverage exempted it from a new unleased DHCP interface's backstop, allowing traffic to the local IP through that interface after a failed nftables update.

## What
- Track destination-wide retained coverage separately from complete table coverage. Use only the destination-wide set for DHCP gap-backstop exclusions, while preserving ingress-deny coverage for newcomer checks.
- Keep the cold-boot fence coverage tied to the actual destination-wide addresses it drops.
- Add a regression that verifies the rendered gap DROP for a shared default-deny IP on a newly configured DHCP interface.
- Update docs/log/13174.md with the post-merge finding and validation.

## Validation
- RED on merged PR #13398 head: focused regression showed RetainedV4 included 192.0.2.1 and the DHCP gap DROP excluded that address.
- GREEN: focused host-inbound regressions pass.
- go build ./... and go vet ./pkg/daemon/... pass.
- GOCACHE=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-build GOTMPDIR=/var/worktrees/t go test ./pkg/daemon/... -count=1 passes (daemon 489.663s; daemon/system 0.004s).

## Risk
Only DHCP backstop exclusions are narrowed. Address-wide retained rules still preserve their valid coverage; old ingress-scoped drops no longer suppress a distinct new interface backstop.

## PR #13420 — userspace-dp: keep GRE forwards endpoint-pinned (#13419) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-15)

Branch: `fix/13182-correction-campaign-pub`

Why: #13410 stamped a GRE TUN-origin forward decision with the inner tunnel VRF's install-table identity. Stamped sessions validate that registry before the tunnel-endpoint resolver; if the inner `cust` row disappears while the endpoint and underlay remain live, re-resolution returns `TableUnavailable` instead of resolving the configured endpoint. Tunnel outcomes are explicitly endpoint-pinned and table-free by `install_table_stamp_for_miss`.

What: Restore `(0,0)` for the GRE forward decision and compute the tunnel table identity only at its existing uses for local-source admission and table-scoped reverse synthesis. Extend the existing real GRE VRF test: assert the cust row exists, remove only that row, then require the forward session to re-resolve to `ForwardCandidate` on the expected GRE endpoint. This supersedes the stamp-equality test from #13410 and refutes the D6-08 default-table-leak premise.

Validation: The real endpoint-resolution assertion failed against a temporary #13410-stamp mutant with `TableUnavailable` (expected `ForwardCandidate`). `cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml --bins afxdp::wg::decap_tests -- --nocapture`: 41 passed. `cargo check --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml --bins`: passed with existing warnings.

Risk: This removes only the unintended install-table gate from endpoint-pinned GRE forwards; reverse VRF stamping and the forward flow key's routing domain remain unchanged.

Closes #13419

## PR #13421 — userspace-dp: preserve shared-ifindex egress state (#13181) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-15)

Branch: `campaign/13181`

Closes #13181

## Why
Shared-ifindex rows could overwrite primary addresses, HA ownership, VLAN and MTU data. Zone-to-RG construction also used an ingress lookup containing inherited parent aliases and admitted raw row zones without requiring an unambiguous egress-zone ledger.

## What
- Merge per-family primary addresses and known MTU values across aliases.
- Reject conflicting nonzero redundancy groups and incompatible bind, VLAN, MTU, MAC, or same-family primary values on an admitted shared ifindex.
- Build zone-to-RG membership only from consistent zoned member rows whose egress-zone ledger agrees; reject unzoned aliases and missing ledger admission.
- Add focused regressions for these cases.

## Validation
- RED regression on pristine origin/master (historical combined test; IPv4 primary was missing).
- Latest `cargo test forwarding_build::tests`: 231 passed.
- Earlier full `cargo test` before the final conflict/ledger hardening: 7,918 passed, one unrelated protocol wire-fixture drift failure, 8 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` reported four lints in untouched `build.rs`; `cargo fmt -- --check` reports repository-wide formatting differences.

## PR #13447 — daemon: preserve scoped-global ancestry across zone renames (#13415) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-15)

Branch: `fix/13415-campaign-pub`

What: detect gaps on ordinary session frames before decode; for oversized frames, detect a gap only after a within-ceiling drain succeeds. Keep over-ceiling and failed-drain headers untrusted and rate-limited. Add regressions for undecodable frames, trusted oversized gaps, and forged over-ceiling headers. Record the remediation in docs/log/13238.md.

Validation: regressions for #13238 and the three #9915 oversized-sequence cases pass; go build ./pkg/dataplane/userspace and go vet ./pkg/dataplane/userspace pass. Full go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace was run but failed on snapshot/config assertions and long Unix socket paths; details are in the issue log.

Risk: a session gap is an unconditional resync and disconnect only when the frame header is trustworthy. Telemetry behavior is unchanged.

Closes #13238

In userspace mode, workers update per-binding RX/TX packet and byte counters, but interface API and Prometheus readers consume only the unused `interface_counters` BPF map. This reports confident zeros. Separately, the Prometheus collector silently skips configured interfaces that have no kernel netdev without incrementing its interface read-error metric.

- **GREEN**: `GOCACHE=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-build GOTMPDIR=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-tmp go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace ./pkg/api -run '13273|TestCollectInterfaceCountersSkipsAndCountsReadErrors' -count=1` passed.
- `go vet ./pkg/api/... ./pkg/dataplane/...` passed.
- `go build ./...` passed.
- `gofmt -l` on all touched Go files produced no output.
- `go test ./pkg/api/... ./pkg/dataplane/... -count=1` fails on this branch and pristine master because of unrelated existing failures (including duplicate VRF metric gathering #7991, snapshot digest mismatch #8892, host-netdev snapshot tests, and environment-specific AF_UNIX socket path failures). The 13273 regressions fail on pristine master and pass on this branch.

## Risk

The full userspace suite had unrelated failures; four source/golden failures were reproduced on pristine base, with additional long-temp-path failures.

Risk:
Counters remain scoped to the active EventStream instance; helper-restart cumulative-count behavior is unchanged. No live cluster was exercised.

the stale relative offset could read payload bytes as ports and fabricate

relative L4 displacement only when `stamp_trusted` is true. Otherwise,
derive L4 from the packet's IPv6 extension-header chain. Add a fail-on-revert
stale-offset test plus a trusted-stamp control and document the producer

## PR #13594 — forwarding: admit missing-neighbor seeds (#13526) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-15)

Branch: `fix/13526-campaign-pub`

Closes #13526

## Why
Missing-neighbor seeds committed sessions without publishing first-fragment associations and refused pressure-eligible TCP openings at capacity. A published first-fragment association also needs to carry its authenticated translation decision through the missing-neighbor safety fence for a following fragment.

## What
Install eligible same-family fragment associations after seed session commit using the raw ingress authority. Apply the existing TCP opening pressure-shed policy before refusing a missing-neighbor seed, including session/BPF/NAT cleanup and replication. On a live association hit, preserve its committed translation through the missing-neighbor NAT-miss fence so the tail can be parked for retry. NAT64 fail-closed handling remains unchanged.

- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `cargo fmt --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml -- --check` — not clean; it reports extensive formatting diffs across existing workspace files.

## Risk
Only live, authority-scoped association hits bypass the NAT-miss fence. Pressure shedding follows the existing incomplete-TCP-opening policy; no new idle-session expiry policy or NAT64 admission behavior is introduced.

## PR #13606 — nat: allow DNAT prefixes and count exemptions (#13548) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-15)

Branch: `fix/13548-campaign-pub`

## Why

`CompileUserspaceShim` reaches `compileNAT` before snapshot creation. The shim rejected non-host DNAT match CIDRs even though the snapshot carries them as `destination_prefix` and Rust installs them through longest-prefix matching. It also skipped DNAT `off` rules before allocating counter IDs, so the exemption snapshot could not carry its per-rule ID.

## What

Accept non-host CIDRs in the DNAT match destination validation while keeping pool addresses host-only (Rust parses pool addresses as a single `IpAddr`). Allocate the DNAT counter ID before continuing over `off` exemptions. Add IPv4/IPv6 prefix and DNAT-off counter regressions plus a pool-prefix rejection control. Record the change in `docs/log/13548.md`. No Rust or snapshot-builder changes; those paths already support the accepted match-prefix shape.

## Validation

## PR #13631 — grpcapi: align annotate authorization with handler parsing (#13628) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-15)

Branch: `fix/13628-authz-followup`

Closes #13628

Follow-up to #13630: direct SetRequest callers can send an annotate comment with unescaped embedded quotes. Server.Set interprets the path before the first comment quote, while the authorization lexer previously treated trailing comment words as path tokens, allowing an anchored deny on the real path to be bypassed. Tab-separated annotate requests also exposed the admission/handler whitespace mismatch.

Canonicalize admission input using the same cliterm parser and handler path splitting as Server.Set; quote the exact path tokens and escape the comment before authorization lexing. Add interceptor-to-handler regressions for both space and tab forms with embedded quotes against denied paths, retaining allowed-path controls.

## Validation

Share close tuple selection between queued-flow cleanup and delta flushing; purge-retirement closes fence only the forward tuple. Mark loss-of-sync on contention only when no session-table retry slot can preserve the suffix. Add fail-on-revert regression coverage and `docs/log/13654.md`.

## Risk
No change to ordinary-close tuple fencing or resync when no retry slot exists.

Closes #13654

## PR #13732 — userspace-dp: gate quoted ICMP identifier rewrite on bearing types (#13650) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-15)

Branch: `fix/13650-campaign`

Why:
The four embedded-ICMP NAT builders rewrote quoted ICMP/ICMPv6 bytes 4..6 as an echo Identifier for every quoted message type. For Destination-Unreachable, Time-Exceeded, Packet-Too-Big, Parameter-Problem and Redirect quotes those bytes are the unused/MTU/gateway word; overwriting them with a NAT port/identifier corrupts the quoted error. The v6 reversed builder also repaired the quoted checksum with an incremental identifier-only adjust ignoring the embedded source-address rewrite, leaving it invalid over the egress pseudo-header.

What:
Gate every quoted-ICMP identifier write in `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/icmp_embed/builders.rs` on the shared `icmp_identifier_bearing` predicate; on both v6 builders recompute the quoted ICMPv6 checksum in full over the egress embedded pseudo-header when identifier-bearing.

Full `--bins`: 7959 passed, 1 failed (`f035_parked_fragment_overlap_10659`, also failing on clean master in the same revert run), 8 ignored.

Risk:
Quoted non-identifier messages keep their semantic word; quoted echo identifiers still restored and now verify over the egress v6 pseudo-header.

## PR #13737 — policy: evict stale denies on scheduler recovery (#13639) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-15)

Branch: `fix/13639-campaign-zero`

## Why
A scheduled PERMIT is fail-closed while its scheduler lease is expired. Traffic may then fall through to an unscheduled DENY and cache a PolicyDenied result. When the lease recovers, that stale deny previously remained live and blackholed traffic. Scheduled DENY/REJECT entries were also seeded during expiry only to be evicted on the next lookup.

## What
- Invalidate cached PolicyDenied entries on scheduler recovery when scheduled policy eligibility can change, without flushing unrelated forwarding entries.
- Keep existing expiry invalidation for scheduled DENY/REJECT rules.
- Skip cache seeding for scheduled DENY/REJECT verdicts while the lease is expired to prevent seed-then-evict churn.
- Add a recovery regression and docs/log/13639.md.

## Validation
- RED on pristine master 761931ff: the new regression fails at the recovery cache-miss assertion.
- `cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml --bin xpf-userspace-dp afxdp::flow_cache::tests:: -- --nocapture`: 70 passed.
- Full bin suite: 7959 passed, 1 failed, 8 ignored. The #10659 failure reproduces on pristine master with the same assertion.

## Risk
Recovery evicts cached PolicyDenied entries when scheduler eligibility can change; unrelated forward cache entries remain available. No wire or control-plane behavior changes.

Closes #13639

## PR #13755 — firewall: enforce routing filters on IPsec passthrough (#13637) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-15)

Branch: `fix/13637-pbr-parity`

## Why
The merged #13637 fix applied the non-PBR input-filter evaluator on Stage 11 passthrough, but a `then { routing-instance X; discard; }` term is handled by a separate routing-instance evaluator. Count route-filter terms with the routing evaluator before Stage 11 passthrough. A matched discard/reject terminates the packet; reject replies and filter logs/counters use the existing routing-evaluator behavior. The real poll-loop test sends local IKE through a routing-instance discard and asserts the filter counter. This supplements the non-PBR IPv4/IPv6 source-specific input-filter coverage in #13637.

## Risk
Only route-filter terminal discard/reject enforcement changes; accepted route overrides do not change the local passthrough outcome.

## PR #13775 — userspace-dp: adjust zero quoted ICMPv6 checksums (#13773) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13773-campaign-pub`

Why:
The quoted ICMPv6 checksum repair in both reverse and outbound NAT
builders skipped incremental adjustment when the original checksum
field was zero. ICMPv6 does not use zero to mean checksum omitted, so
rewritten quoted addresses or identifiers left a stale checksum for
the receiver.

What:
Apply RFC 1624 checksum deltas regardless of the current quoted
ICMPv6 checksum in both builders, preserving zero-result
canonicalization. Add a regression using a valid, genuinely-zero
quoted ICMPv6 checksum that exercises both builder paths. NOT changed:
ICMPv4 and UDP checksum omission semantics.

Validation:

fix; `cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml icmp_embed_`
passed (5 tests). Full `--bin xpf-userspace-dp` suite had one known
unrelated failure: f035_parked_fragment_overlap_is_rechecked_on_retry_10659.
`cargo fmt -- --check` reports existing formatting differences across
numerous unrelated files.

Risk:
Quoted ICMPv6 packets with a zero checksum now receive the required
delta after NAT rewrites. No ICMPv4/UDP zero-checksum behavior changes.

Closes #13773

## PR #13778 — fairness-eval: align Cstruct RSS gate (#13658) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13658-observed-contract`

## Why

`fairness-eval` reports the selected fail-closed Gate-2 `cstruct`, but passed the raw observed-distribution Cstruct into the `cstruct-max` RSS expectation. An accepted stale-count overcount could therefore fail a ceiling against a value different from the one reported and used by Gate 2.

## What

Pass the selected Cstruct to RSS expectation evaluation, without normalizing its distribution input. Thus `cstruct-max` checks the same chosen Cstruct shown in the report, while distribution-based expectations (`max-worker-flow-share`, `balanced`, active-worker count) and report fields such as `max_worker_flow_share` continue to describe observed RSS placement. The black-box tests now pin both sides: the `[4,4,4,3,0,0]` observed max share is exactly `4/15`, while its selected normalized Cstruct is 0 and passes `cstruct-max:1%`.

## Adjudication

This is a narrow production fix, not a re-pin to make all consumers use trimmed data. Commit `66bd82e28` (“Preserve observed RSS expectation input”) deliberately preserves the observed distribution for RSS-placement expectations: trimming `[4,4,4,3,0,0]` to `[3,3,3,3,0,0]` for those expectations would hide a worker's actual 4/15 share and falsely pass a 25% cap. That contract and its existing black-box test are retained. `cstruct-max` is different: it constrains the Cstruct used by Gate 2, so it must compare against the selected, report-visible Cstruct rather than `cstruct_raw`. The new regression failed on pristine master before the fix and passes afterward.

## Validation

- RED on pristine `origin/master` (`5e8c92302`): `cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml --test fairness_eval_blackbox cstruct_max_expectation_uses_selected_gate2_cstruct -- --nocapture` failed with subprocess status 1 instead of expected 0 (raw Cstruct ~0.125 vs selected Cstruct 0).
- GREEN: `cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml --test fairness_eval_blackbox -- --nocapture` — 23 passed.
- `cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml --bin fairness-eval` — 63 passed.
- The new regression passed five consecutive runs.

## Risk

Only `cstruct-max` changes behavior, now aligned with Gate 2 and the reported Cstruct. Other observed-distribution RSS expectations, report schema, and packet path are unchanged.

Closes #13658

## Why

`SessionTable::companion_keeps_alive` rejected a TCP companion only when `handshake_pending` was true. A bare-SYN install leaves both halves `established=false, handshake_pending=false`, so a fresh but un-replied companion could repeatedly re-stamp its paired entry and keep it alive beyond the paired entry's shorter opening timeout (including a per-zone SYN-flood override).

## What

Require the companion to be established as well as non-pending before it can retain its peer. Add regression coverage for asymmetric opening-window TCP expiry in both directions, SYN retransmit-only activity, continued retention by an established companion, and un-replied app-gated UDP parity. Record the change in `docs/log/13679.md`.

## Validation

- RED on the pre-guard predicate: 3 un-replied TCP/UDP regressions failed; the established-companion control passed.
- GREEN before rebase: `cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml companion_established_13679 -- --nocapture` — 4 passed.
- `cargo build --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml` passed before rebase.
- Full crate test run before rebase: 8001 passed, 2 failed, 8 ignored. Failures were `f035_parked_fragment_overlap_is_rechecked_on_retry_10659` and `c3_forward_control_survives_full_window_per_permit_shape_10591`; baseline attribution was not established.
- After rebasing on newer master, focused tests could not compile because master has `error[E0432]: unresolved import promote::purge_translated_synced_hit` at `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/session_glue/mod.rs:59`; this issue does not touch that code.

## Risk

Only an un-established or handshake-pending companion is newly ineligible to refresh its peer. Established, non-pending session retention remains unchanged.

Closes #13679

## PR #13797 — userspace-dp: reject unsupported GRE flags on decap (#13662) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13662-gre-reserved0-v2`

## Why

The native GRE decapsulator checked the version and Routing bits, but accepted legacy Strict Source Route (`0x0800`) and Recursion Control bit 0 (`0x0400`). A matching GRE peer could therefore have an unsupported header promoted as tunnel traffic.

## What

Reject only flags masked by `0x0c00` before reading optional fields. The regression distinguishes these unsupported bits from RFC 2784 §2.3 bits `0x03f8`, which receivers must ignore, and confirms valid Key/Sequence behavior remains unchanged. Transit classification is not changed; the finding is scoped to native decapsulation.

## Validation

- Regression failed on pristine `origin/master`: `unsupported_legacy_gre_bits_are_refused_13662` decapsulated `0x0800`.
- `cargo test -p xpf-userspace-dp gre_reserved0_13662`: 2 passed.
- `cargo build -p xpf-userspace-dp`: passed.
- Full crate test run: exit 101 with three failures in unrelated tests; the parked-fragment retry test also fails on pristine master, and both GRE host-inbound tests pass individually on pristine master.
- `rustfmt --check` on the regression file passed. Workspace formatting check reports existing drift in untouched files.

## Risk

Frames carrying either unsupported legacy bit are no longer native-decapsulated. RFC-mandated must-ignore flags and RFC 2890 optional fields remain accepted.

Closes #13662

## PR #13803 — userspace-dp: gate conntrack RMW operations (#13668) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13668-campaign-pub`

# #13668 — gate conntrack RMW operations through TupleGate

- **Base**: fc806aa (origin/master at implementation)
- **Branch**: fix/13668-campaign-pub

## Why
`restamp_bpf_conntrack_policy`, `restamp_bpf_conntrack_app_id`,
`refresh_bpf_conntrack_last_seen`, and `update_session_cluster_synced_origin`
did lookup→modify→`BPF_EXIST` writes without TupleGate admission. They could
clobber a live row held under a gate lease or write during a map-wide
ClearFence, unlike the gated publish/delete twins.

## What
- Added `with_conntrack_rmw` in `bpf_map/mod.rs` mirroring `with_publish`:
  decline on gate-busy/clear-fenced, holding admission across the synchronous
  RMW.
- Wrapped all four functions (refresh gated per walked tuple); `fd < 0`
  no-map early-true stays inside raw bodies so declines never fake success.
- Test seams model origin writes and count refresh writes.
- Added six regressions for lease/clear-fence declines and an unleased positive
  control in `bpf_map_tests.rs`.

## Validation
- RED on pre-fix code: two app-id regressions failed on the named lease and
  clear-fence assertions.
- GREEN focused: `cargo test --bins conntrack_rmw_` → 6 passed on current master.
- Full `cargo test --bins`: 8022 passed, 2 failed, 8 ignored. The failures were
  `afxdp::cos::queue_service::tests::sojourn::submit_local_publishes_committed_vtime_on_settle`
  and `afxdp::tests_9950::f035_parked_fragment_overlap_is_rechecked_on_retry_10659`;
  neither exercises conntrack RMW.
- RED-on-revert: bypassing gate admission made four decline tests fail; restored
  the gate implementation.

## Risk
Refresh skips a declined tuple for this slice; subsequent budgeted walks retry.
App-id and policy restamps return false so their existing retry/fail-closed
behavior remains intact. Origin transition updates silently skip; a later
transition/refresh can restamp the bit.

## PR #13809 — afxdp: parallelize WireGuard endpoint lookups (#13666) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13666-campaign-v2`

Why: Blocking `to_socket_addrs` calls delayed every following WireGuard peer refresh; additionally, a slow lookup delayed adoption of already completed peer results, and Drop waited for uncancellable DNS work.

What: Resolve names through at most eight scoped workers that claim new peers as they finish. Apply each answer immediately on the resolver thread. On Drop, set the stop flag and detach the resolver thread; workers no longer claim peers and outstanding results are discarded after shutdown begins. Regression tests cover bounded concurrency, early result application while a prior lookup remains blocked, panic isolation, and nonblocking Drop with unscheduled peers. See `docs/log/13666.md`.

Validation: `cargo test -p xpf-userspace-dp endpoint_resolver` — 10 passed; `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on both edited Rust files passed. RED proof on pristine master: setting the worker limit to one failed because peer lookups were serialized. Earlier full bin suite: 8019 tests ran with one unrelated failure at `afxdp::tests_9950::f035_parked_fragment_overlap_is_rechecked_on_retry_10659`; clippy stopped at the existing mutable-borrow error in `src/afxdp/umem/mmap.rs:241`.

Risk: Operating-system DNS resolution cannot be interrupted; the detached resolver thread retains its shared state until in-flight lookups return.

Closes #13666

deadline under concurrent rustc load after at least 1,473 tests, no
suite summary.

Risk: A response send failure still leaves the local responder session
installed; peer retransmission drives another handshake response.

## PR #13826 — afxdp: apply endpoint answers before slow lookups finish (#13666) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13666-completion-shutdown`

Why: Blocking `to_socket_addrs` calls delayed every following WireGuard peer refresh; additionally, a slow lookup delayed adoption of already completed peer results, and Drop waited for uncancellable DNS work.

What: Resolve names through at most eight scoped workers that claim new peers as they finish. Apply each answer immediately on the resolver thread. On Drop, set the stop flag and detach the resolver thread; workers no longer claim peers and outstanding results are discarded after shutdown begins. Regression tests cover bounded concurrency, early result application while a prior lookup remains blocked, panic isolation, and nonblocking Drop with unscheduled peers. See `docs/log/13666.md`.

Validation: `cargo test -p xpf-userspace-dp endpoint_resolver` — 10 passed; `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on both edited Rust files passed. RED proof on pristine master: setting the worker limit to one failed because peer lookups were serialized. Earlier full bin suite: 8019 tests ran with one unrelated failure at `afxdp::tests_9950::f035_parked_fragment_overlap_is_rechecked_on_retry_10659`; clippy stopped at the existing mutable-borrow error in `src/afxdp/umem/mmap.rs:241`.

Risk: Operating-system DNS resolution cannot be interrupted; the detached resolver thread retains its shared state until in-flight lookups return.

Closes #13666

## PR #13831 — userspace-dp: align transit GRE legacy flag checks (#13662) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13662-gre-transit-flags-buildable`

## Follow-up to #13662 / PR #13797

The first fix added the RFC 2784 legacy-bit refusal to native GRE decapsulation. The production transit `gre_discriminator` is the guarded sibling: its module documentation says version/routing refusal discipline is shared with decapsulation, but it still extracted an RFC 2890 Key from `0x0800` and `0x0400`. That could create keyed transit session identity for headers the decapsulator refuses.

This change shares the mask and returns `Unparseable` before keyed/unkeyed classification. It preserves RFC 2784 §2.3 must-ignore bits through `0x03f8` and the RFC 2890 optional fields.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p xpf-userspace-dp unsupported_legacy_bits_are_unparseable_13662`: passed on the merged baseline after the change.
- `cargo test -p xpf-userspace-dp gre_discriminator::tests`: passed on the merged baseline after the change.
- `cargo build -p xpf-userspace-dp`: passed on the merged baseline after the change.

The current `origin/master` test build also has an unrelated compile failure in `session_glue::mod.rs` (`purge_translated_synced_hit` imported while gated with `#[cfg(test)]`); this PR was rebased to current master after validation on the buildable merged baseline.

## Risk

Transit GRE carrying these unsupported bits no longer receives keyed session identity and stays on the flowless path. Packet forwarding behavior is unchanged.

## PR #13850 — afxdp: recover bindings after ifindex resolution (#13714) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13714-campaign-zero`

Why: An unresolved initial ifindex leaves a candidate unregistered and unarmed, but the planner stamps last_change. On a later replan after ifindex resolution, the timestamp makes the row look previously registered, so it skips registration/arm initialization. With unchanged global forwarding state, no arm RPC repairs it and the whole dataplane remains disabled.

What: Treat prior binding state as existing only if the prior ifindex was positive. Newly resolvable rows re-register and inherit the global arm state; still-unresolved rows remain fail-closed. Added regressions for armed/disarmed recovery, repeated-replan stability, and an unresolved sibling. Added docs/log/13714.md.

Validation: The recovery regression failed on pristine master with (ifindex=11, registered=false, armed=false). After the fix, the two recovery tests passed; the tests:: filtered suite passed 6132 tests (7 ignored, 1930 filtered). The full unfiltered binary run reported four failures and stalled before a final summary. All four failures were independently reproduced on pristine origin/master fd94c3a7d: fragment-overlap sibling outcome (0 vs 1), both GRE inner ICMP LocalDelivery outcomes (0 vs 1), and session-hit window expiry at tick 21. Details are in the issue log.

Risk: Only a prior non-positive ifindex changes recovery behavior. Existing positive-ifindex registrations retain manual registration and arm state; unresolved bindings remain unarmed.

Closes #13714

Branch: `fix/13700-campaign-zero`

Session-miss SYN-cookie ACK paths charged a zone-wide validation bucket after only an unauthenticated 5-bit epoch check. Epoch-matched spoofed ACKs could exhaust the budget and reject legitimate returning handshakes in the same zone.

Charge the separate standby and active validation buckets only after cookie validation fails. - Package `cargo fmt --check` reports pre-existing unrelated formatting differences.

## Risk

Plausible-epoch invalid ACKs now reach MAC validation before failed-attempt accounting, so these buckets no longer cap the cryptographic cost of every invalid ACK. Per-source sharding remains outside this narrowed scope.

## PR #13869 — userspace-dp: isolate per-session counter query replies (#13711) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13711-campaign`

Why: A full worker-command queue refuses the counter-query command, but the
kick path discarded that result and still waited for its acknowledgement. The
query then spent the full three-second deadline waiting for work that could not
have been queued. Separately, workers share one reply slot and the reader
accepted any sequence at least as new as its own, allowing a later session's
counters to answer an earlier request.

What: Track refused worker IDs separately and report them unanswered without
adding them to the wait set. Require exact sequence equality; if a newer
sequence has overwritten the single reply slot, report unanswered instead of
borrowing another session's counters. Add full-queue and cross-session
regressions in coordinator/tests.rs. No queue policy or wire shape changed.

wait exceeded 1 s; B's 999 packets were returned for A). Focused after fix:

additional screen-cookie failure passed isolated on both trees. Clippy
all-targets is blocked by pre-existing clippy::mut_from_ref in
src/afxdp/umem/mmap.rs:241 on both trees; strict -D warnings also flags four
pre-existing build.rs lints.

Risk: An earlier query whose reply slot is overwritten by a later query is
now explicitly reported unanswered rather than cross-attributed. It retains

## PR #13875 — userspace-dp: isolate concurrent counter replies (#13711) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13711-reply-race`

Why: A post-merge review of #13869 identified a remaining race in its shared response slot. A waiter could match sequence A, then a worker could publish B's six payload fields before A read them. A could therefore return B's counters as an answered A response.

What: Give every queued counter query an independent reply slot. The worker publishes the complete `SessionCounterAnswer` under that slot's mutex, and the waiter reads the same snapshot under the mutex. Remove the shared diagnostic atomics. Add a deterministic overlap regression that holds A's slot while B publishes, then verifies both queries retain their own counters. Queue-refusal handling and the off-lock bounded wait remain intact.

Validation:
- `cargo test -p xpf-userspace-dp counter_query_ -- --nocapture`: 2 passed, including the concurrent per-request snapshot regression.
- `cargo test -p xpf-userspace-dp failover_before_rename_joint_purges_10589 -- --nocapture`: 1 passed, exercising the real worker command path.
- The full crate suite and clippy were not repeated for this follow-up. Results and base comparison from #13869 are recorded in `docs/log/13711.md`.

Risk: This diagnostic now allocates one reply slot per queued worker and takes a short mutex to publish or copy its snapshot. The worker-command queue remains bounded, and the off-lock wait retains its three-second deadline.

Closes #13711

## PR #13877 — userspace-dp: gate FullResync ACKs on fresh exports (#13725) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13725-campaign-zero`

Closes #13725

## Why

`ExportOwnerRGSessionsPaged` scans shards incrementally. A FullResync arriving
during a scan can represent drops in shards the scan already visited, so
coalescing the barrier into that worker can retire and cumulatively ACK it
without exporting the missing sessions.

## What

Each FullResync barrier now runs its own worker export and remains queued until
that export succeeds. Removed coalesced-marker retirement and failure-reset
logic. Added #13725 in-flight and failure-retry regressions, updated #9630
tests, and recorded the behavior in `docs/log/13725.md`.

## Validation

- RED: the in-flight barrier regression failed on pristine `origin/master`
  `2cae7b02a`; source files involved are unchanged through current base
  `07eeae9ed`.
- GREEN after rebase:
  `GOCACHE=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-build GOTMPDIR=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-tmp
  go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace -run
  'TestEventStreamFullResync(ArrivingDuringInFlightWorkerRunsPostBarrierExport13725|FailureRetriesEveryBarrier13725|DuringInFlightExportRunsAnotherExport9630|BarriersQueuedBeforeCallbackEachExport9630)$' -count=1`
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Full `pkg/dataplane/userspace` suite was attempted twice. AF_UNIX socket
  fixtures fail to bind with `invalid argument` because their generated temp
  paths exceed the socket path limit. Eight unrelated non-socket test failures
  were reproduced on pristine `origin/master` `07eeae9ed`; see `docs/log/13725.md`.

## Risk

Repeated barriers each perform an export, increasing export work during bursts.
This avoids ACKing state not covered by a post-drop scan; queue overflow still
forces helper reconnect/replay.

## PR #13890 — userspace-dp: avoid locked P-MECH route dumps (#13721) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13721-lock-followup`

Why: Although #13874 scoped the selector query, retained-snapshot refreshes still performed the main-table netlink dump while holding Manager.mu. A route-table scan can block manager readers and writers, while blindly reusing inventory after config/tunnel/FIB changes can expose stale authority.

What: Reuse stamped inventory only when config identity, tunnel identities, and FIB generation still match. Copy the inventory before updating generation metadata. If a locked refresh cannot prove reuse, mark it incomplete with MAIN_ROUTE_INVENTORY_STALE rather than issuing netlink I/O under the lock. FIB-bump stamping also avoids a locked fallback when its off-lock prefetch no longer matches. Add runtime request-capture and locked-refresh regressions.

Validation: Runtime request RED on baseline 2cae7b02a after behavior-preserving request/executor extraction showed no RTA_TABLE. Runtime lock RED on current master 52e29404e observed one route dump under lock. Focused P-MECH regressions passed, including stale-prefetch fail-closed coverage. A full userspace suite run before the final stale-prefetch no-fallback change failed with existing failures; baseline reproduced three named failures in docs/log/13721.md, while other suite failures were not baseline-compared.

Risk: If config/tunnel identities or FIB generation change during a locked refresh, P-MECH authority is temporarily withheld until an unlocked full build or FIB prefetch refreshes the inventory.

Closes #13721

## PR #13893 — sessions: revalidate synced imports under tuple lease (#13709) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13709-campaign-final2`

A stale synced-session import could snapshot an older entry before waiting for the global tuple lease, then overwrite a newer generation or a locally owned session when it eventually published. The stale view also made capacity decisions against the wrong shared-map state.

The import now uses the pre-lease map read only to prepare the old companion tuple lease key. After acquiring the lease it re-reads the current entry and map length and makes generation, capacity, local-ownership, and preservation decisions from that authoritative state. If a concurrent NAT replacement's current companion tuple is not covered by the lease, the import is rejected safely. Test-only synchronization drives deterministic generation and local-ownership races.

Validation: fail-on-revert on pristine origin/master d6852dadeafd7a4b1cc9a0b7b75616621b6ee798 failed as intended (Applied instead of RejectedStaleGeneration); affected source files are identical on final base 52e29404e. The full userspace-dp suite on the PR head reported 8,131 passed, 7 failed, 8 ignored. Six failures (fixture packet-length drift, two GRE local-delivery tests, authority-window, expiry-retirement, and protocol-literal) reproduced on clean base 52e29404e. The SYN-cookie failure did not reproduce on clean base and is not treated as an established baseline failure.

Risk: a replacement whose current NAT companion was not included in the prepared tuple lease is safely rejected as gate-busy; the peer can retry and prepare the current tuple set.

Why: A local persistent-NAT clear revokes the helper's full lease table, but equal-generation batches were still admitted. A delayed snapshot could restore a pre-clear lease for an unseen key, bypassing the per-key tombstone and undoing the operator's clear.

What: Persist per-peer generations observed at local clear in the durable lease-generation state and reject equal-or-older batches at admission. Newer generations remain eligible; old state files load with an empty clear watermark. Add a regression covering delayed equal-generation batch, restart persistence, old-generation rejection, and post-clear new-generation imports. Rust's per-key fences remain unchanged.

Validation: The regression failed before the fix because generation 8 reached `import_idle_leases` after local clear; focused test passed after the fix. `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp idle_lease` passed (72 tests). Full `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace -count=1` was attempted twice and failed in untouched tests (snapshot/shape drift, unrelated assertions, and Unix socket path-length failures). `git diff --check` passed.

Risk: A peer first observed only after local clear has no pre-clear receiver-known generation to fence; its admission retains existing origin-generation behavior. The watermark is bounded by the existing remote-peer limit.

Closes #13867

## PR #13906 — afxdp: preserve IPv6 probe token across same-MAC refresh (#13898) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13898-campaign-zero`

Why: IPv6 RTM_NEWNEIGH consumed the one-shot solicitation token before inserting a neighbor. A same-MAC NUD_DELAY/NUD_STALE refresh is a no-op, but still burned authorization, causing a genuine failover MAC change in the probe window to be refused as unsolicited and interrupt IPv6 forwarding.

What: Mirror IPv4 in the IPv6 kernel-neighbor arm: peek before insert and consume only when the insert changes an existing MAC. Add a fail-on-revert IPv6 same-MAC-refresh-then-failover regression and record the issue in docs/log/13898.md. No changes to probe timing, IPv4, or solicitation policy.

Validation: Regression failed on pristine master: failover returned None instead of Upserted and counted an unsolicited NA refusal. After the fix, `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/var/worktrees/.cache/cargo-13898 GOCACHE=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-build GOTMPDIR=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-tmp cargo test -p xpf-userspace-dp afxdp::neighbor::` passed (35 passed, 8,262 filtered out), including the IPv4 parity and existing IPv6 unsolicited, probe, and one-shot tests. `git diff --check` passed.

Risk: None known; IPv6 same-MAC updates retain a probe authorization for the subsequent eligible MAC change, with the same one-shot consumption rule as IPv4.

Closes #13898

## PR #13907 — userspace-dp: reserve WireGuard nonces atomically (#13899) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13899-atomic-nonce-reservation`

Why: WgEngine::encap_inner held a per-session mutex across stack staging and AEAD encryption. Concurrent workers targeting one WireGuard peer therefore serialized through full encryption, limiting throughput per session.

What: Atomically reserve each transmit nonce with WgSession::next_tx_counter after size checks and before AEAD. Remove the redundant per-session tx_lock. Add concurrent reservation tests for unique contiguous nonces and the reject-after-messages boundary; record the change in docs/log/13899.md.

Validation: `cargo test --release --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml afxdp::wg:: -- --test-threads=1` passed (290 passed, 8,008 filtered out). The concurrent reservation tests passed 20 consecutive runs. rustfmt check and git diff --check passed. This is a performance-only regression; the old lock-based path preserved nonce uniqueness, so there is no deterministic functional RED without runtime measurement. The tests validate the atomic reservation primitive and its ceiling behavior.

Risk: A failed AEAD attempt consumes its already-reserved nonce, which can leave a harmless gap; reusing a nonce is unsafe. Buffer and staging size errors still occur before reservation.

Closes #13899

## PR #13918 — userspace-dp: bound local-clear lease fences (#13909) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13909-campaign`

Local persistent-NAT clear fences now expire after two minutes, so a peer that does not clear can resume same-generation lease advertisements. The expiry is durable and pruned on import; a newer peer generation removes its fence immediately. Legacy fence state receives one bounded replay window. Rejected batches emit a rate-limited warning. Older peer generations remain rejected indefinitely.

RED on origin/master 5aa9179: TestExpiredLocalClearFenceAdmitsSameGeneration13909 failed because the expired fence still rejected the batch. Targeted lease-generation tests passed. The full daemon suite and go vet passed. The full userspace suite and its race run failed in other areas (contract snapshot, host ingress, route cap, FIB, allocation); Unix-socket tests also reported invalid argument under GOTMPDIR.

Risk: an equal-generation snapshot delayed beyond two minutes is indistinguishable from a fresh same-generation lease and can be admitted. The wire protocol remains unchanged.

Closes #13909

- Size userspace_sessions to 8,388,608 rows with BPF_F_NO_PREALLOC.

- GREEN: focused capacity, ABI, source-manifest, and existing strict-map tests passed after regeneration.

## PR #13996 — firewall: fence new static host addresses before activation (#13927) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13927-static-addr-host-inbound`

Why:
A day-2 apply publishes the new userspace local-address snapshot and networkd activates configured static addresses in the core, while the host-inbound nft table is not rendered until the tail. A newly live address therefore falls through the retained table and policy accept, allowing a non-admitting zone to reach host listeners during the apply.

What:
Render incoming host-inbound destination coverage before link-affecting apply work and add a gap-table drop for uncovered addresses. Keep the fence service-closed until the tail installs the complete incoming policy; fail the apply if the pre-activation fence cannot load. Add a day-2 static-address ordering regression and docs/log/13927.md. Existing DHCP backstop behavior is unchanged; no lifeline or policy-generation behavior changed.

The new regression failed with the missing-fence assertion on pristine origin/master ad0ded0df and passed after the fix. Full `go test -count=1 ./pkg/daemon` did not complete: event-stream Unix sockets returned `invalid argument` and the retry timed out in kernel RTM_GETLINK calls.

Risk:
New, non-lifeline local addresses are temporarily denied host services while the commit installs their final policy. This is intentionally fail-closed; lifeline-shared ingress and mandatory network protocols remain handled by the existing gap-fence rules.

Closes #13927

## PR #14003 — config: validate IPv6 MTU against shared link (#13999) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13936-effective-parent-followup`

Fix the #13936 IPv6 minimum-MTU guard to account for the actual shared-link MTU. Zoned untagged units share a physical link, and `planPhysDesired` writes the MTU from the lowest-numbered referenced untagged unit with a configured MTU. Previously, a low-MTU IPv4 sibling could lower an IPv6 unit's link MTU while the IPv6 unit itself had no family MTU and passed commit validation.

The gate now uses the same referenced-sibling precedence for zoned untagged IPv6 units, keeps the explicit unit-MTU check for unreferenced units, and preserves tagged-child behavior. The interface-MTU override control is now zoned so its override is exercised. Includes a shared-link regression and docs/log/13999.md.

Validation: new shared-link regression failed before the fix. `go test ./pkg/config -run 'TestIPv6UnitMTU' -count=1` passed afterward.

Closes #13999

## PR #14011 — policy: preserve scheduled denies during clock recovery (#13919) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13919-campaign`

Closes #13919

## Why
The scheduler marks all entries inactive after a wall-clock discontinuity, but previously passed only the republish-failure latch to the action-aware snapshot builder. Scheduled DENY/REJECT policies were treated as ordinarily inactive, allowing fallthrough to later permits during the recovery hold. An unloadable configured time zone had the same action-disposition gap during apply seeding.

## What
Add `Scheduler.PolicyFailClosed(now)` to include clock-recovery holds and unavailable zones alongside the republish latch. Carry it through scheduler ticks and apply seeding while leaving the active map all-false, so scheduled permits remain inactive and scheduled DENY/REJECT rules remain eligible. Force publication when a clock step changes disposition even if the map is unchanged. Add regressions and `docs/log/13919.md`.

## Validation
- Regression fails on pristine `origin/master` `ad0ded0df`: `Scheduler.PolicyFailClosed` does not exist.
- `go test ./pkg/scheduler -count=1`: PASS.
- Focused daemon hold and unavailable-zone apply-seed tests: PASS.
- `go build ./...`: PASS; `gofmt` and `git diff --check`: clean.
- `go test ./pkg/... -count=1 -p 4`: hit the existing `pkg/config` `TestSchemaSpellingDifferentialGate` 10-minute timeout.

## Risk
Scheduled DENY/REJECT rules are eligible while clock/zone trust is unknown, matching the existing deny-first policy. Scheduled permits remain inactive until the scheduler has trusted state.

## PR #14026 — policy: republish deny disposition across recovery paths (#13919) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13919-followup`

The initial fix carried the scheduler deny-first disposition through scheduled ticks and apply seeding, but routes-only republish paths still read only the republish-failure latch. ## PR #14072 — config: parse CoS code-points as bit-strings (#13969) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13969-campaign`

Interpret exact-width six-bit DSCP strings as binary before decimal tokens. Apply matching three-bit parsing to the 802.1p classifier and rewrite readers, and pin the existing inet-precedence binary behavior with parity tests. NOT changed: firewall-filter DSCP syntax, a separate numeric/alias input surface outside this CoS code-point issue.

The census failure was independently confirmed on pristine current master (`go test ./pkg/config -run '^TestInventoryDropShapeMatchesTheLiveCensus8662$' -count=1`), with the same two sites.

## Risk

## PR #14076 — userspace-dp: fence kernel neighbor mirror MAC changes (#13951) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13951-campaign-pristine`

## Why
A kernel neighbor snapshot can reflect an unsolicited ARP/NA MAC update even when the Rust monitor rejects the update. Mirroring that snapshot into authoritative forwarding state bypasses the monitor acceptance rule and changes forwarding. Stale manager rows must also not overwrite a newer monitor-confirmed binding already in the dynamic map.

## What
- Accept changed snapshot MACs only when the monitor dynamic cache already confirms that MAC or the kernel row is NUD_PERMANENT.
- Preserve an existing dynamic binding through the all-shard compare-and-write when a snapshot conflicts; retain the static value when no dynamic value exists, then publish the effective value to static forwarding.
- Preserve same-MAC refresh and NUD_PERMANENT behavior.
- Require probe evidence before resolver confirmed-GET writes replace a live MAC.
- Cover mirror refusal, stale snapshot preservation, confirmed convergence, permanent entries, and resolver probe confirmation.

## Validation
- cargo check --bin xpf-userspace-dp passed on the original change.
- The original focused mirror regression passed (1 test); cargo test sharded_neighbor passed (59 tests).
- Follow-up tests are being run with a temporary local correction for the unrelated pristine-master test compile error at src/afxdp/coordinator/tests.rs:11773; the fixture will be restored and excluded from the PR.

## Risk
Unconfirmed changed MAC snapshots are intentionally ignored until monitor confirmation; NUD_PERMANENT entries remain authoritative. No migration or wire-format change.

Closes #13951

## PR #14083 — firewall: block ICMPv6 Redirect route injection (#13982) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13982-campaign`

Why: `system no-redirects` wrote only IPv4/IPv6 `conf/all`. Linux ignores
that IPv6 setting for existing interfaces, while writing `ip_forward=0` at a
closed transit gate resets IPv4 redirect posture. During a gate-closed window,

steady-state and cold-boot host-inbound admits and the userspace classifier.

passed; `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace -run TestHostInboundRedirectIsNotGlobalAccept13982 -count=1`
passed; `go test ./pkg/nftables` passed; `go build ./...` passed. `go test

## PR #14085 — userspace-dp: clear DF on tunnel outer IPv4 (#13957) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

## PR #14106 — nat: index colliding persistent NAT leases by owner (#14046) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14046-pub`

Why: The persistent inbound reverse index held one source lease per translated base. A PAT and address-only lease can share that base with different remote permissions, so whichever inserted last displaced the other. Inbound traffic could be denied or mapped to the wrong internal endpoint, and removing one lease could erase the other's reverse entry.

What: Store all persistent lease owners in a reverse-base bucket and check each owner's live state and remote permissions during inbound lookup. A unique permitted owner resolves normally; multiple distinct endpoints permitted by the same remote are denied as ambiguous. Remove and replacement operations de-index only the affected owner. Add collision, permission ambiguity, and single-owner removal regression coverage plus `docs/log/14046.md`.

Validation: On matching master baseline `5b697d5`, the full `cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml --bin xpf-userspace-dp` suite ran 8,238 tests: 8,206 passed, 24 failed, 8 ignored. The issue branch ran 8,239 tests: 8,206 passed, 25 failed, 8 ignored; the new reverse-collision regression passed. The additional failure was the unrelated flow-cache shard precondition test. The full 54-test `nat::tests_idle_lease_sync_8121` module ran 51 passed, 3 failed; the same 3 failures reproduced on parent PR #13945 commit `64c56d7`. Master advanced after these runs; no suite was rerun on its later tip.

Risk: If multiple colliding leases permit the same remote but resolve to different internal endpoints, inbound traffic is denied rather than routed nondeterministically. No wire or protocol fields changed.

Closes #14046

## PR #14220 — dhcp: refuse over-broad mask and martian yiaddr in DHCPv4 leases (#14183) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14183-campaign`

## Summary
`leaseFromACKv4` rejected only an unspecified yiaddr and a zero/non-contiguous subnet mask (#4101). A rogue DHCP server could ACK a /1–/7 mask or a martian yiaddr (`127.0.0.2`, `169.254.1.1`, `224.0.0.1`, …); `AddrReplace` then installs a connected prefix covering up to half of IPv4 (or binds a loopback/multicast/reserved address) on the interface — bypassing the classless-route gates, which only guard option-121/249 destinations and gateway next-hops, never the leased address. No downstream consumer (daemon FRR routes, management-VRF path) rejects a /1 lease address before `AddrReplace`.

## Fix
At the single parse point shared by acquire/renew/rebind in `leaseFromACKv4`:
- Refuse masks with `ones < 8` (subsumes the /0 check; non-contiguous still refused). /8–/32 including /31 and /32 remain accepted — no legitimate connected subnet is broader than /8.
- Refuse martian yiaddr via the existing `ClasslessRouteIsMartian` /32 gate (0/8, 127/8, 169.254/16, 224/4, 240/4 incl. 255.255.255.255). Private/documentation ranges remain accepted.
- No `XPF_DHCP_TRUST_CLASSLESS_OVERRIDE` hatch for the leased address: that override governs optional learned routes/gateways, not the interface's own address.

Refusal returns an error with no lease: acquire retries DISCOVER, renew/rebind keeps the existing valid lease until T2/expiry (fail-closed, same propagation as #4101).

## Tests
- New `TestLeaseFromACKv4RejectsBroadMaskAndMartianYiaddr14183` (`pkg/dhcp/lease_yiaddr_mask_14183_test.go`): rejection rows /1, /2, /7 masks and 127.0.0.2 / 0.0.0.9 / 169.254.1.1 / 224.0.0.1 / 240.0.0.1 / 255.255.255.255 yiaddr; acceptance rows public /24, private /8 + /16, /31, /32.
  - RED on pristine origin/master (43ebebd38): all 9 rejection rows accepted (e.g. `192.0.2.5/1`, `127.0.0.2/24`).
  - GREEN with fix; full `go test ./pkg/dhcp/ -count=1` ok; gofmt/go vet clean.

Docs: `docs/log/14183.md`, `pkg/dhcp/README.md` gotcha entry.

Closes #14183

## PR #14221 — logging: guard drop-warn clock against unlocked reader (#14191) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14191-campaign`

## Why

`LocalLogWriter.SendFromEventReader` called `warnRateLimited(&lw.lastDropWarn, ...)` on its enqueue-failure drop path without holding `lw.mu`, while the async writer goroutine reached the same clock under `lw.mu` via `Send`/`SendBinary` (#9025 made the two concurrent by design). Under log pressure both goroutines read/wrote the `time.Time` clock unsynchronized — a Go data race flagged by `-race`.

## What

`warnRateLimited` on `LocalLogWriter` and (same shape, preventively) `TraceWriter` now guards its clock with a dedicated leaf mutex `warnMu`, held only for the clock check/update and released before `slog.Warn`. `SendFromEventReader` still never takes `lw.mu` (would park HA session sync behind a stalled writer). ≤1/s-per-class semantics unchanged. New `-race` regression + `docs/log/14191.md`.

## Validation

- RED on pristine `43ebebd38`: `go test -race -run TestLocalLogReaderVsWriterDropWarnRace14191 ./pkg/logging/` → `WARNING: DATA RACE` at `locallog.go:64/67` inside `warnRateLimited`, from `SendFromEventReader` (`locallog.go:262`).
- GREEN: same test `-count=3` passes; full `go test -race -count=1 ./pkg/logging/` passes; `go vet`/`gofmt` clean.

## Risk

No observable behavior change; `warnMu` held only for a `time.Time` compare/store on a rate-limited path; lock order `mu → warnMu` one-directional, released before any `slog` call. `TraceWriter` guarding is preventive (its callers all hold `tw.mu` today).

Closes #14191

## PR #14222 — dhcp: refuse invalid IA_NA addresses and pref-greater-than-valid lifetimes (#14185) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14185-campaign`

Why: `selectIANAAddress` skipped only valid-lifetime-0 and unparseable IAADDRs, so a solicited (possibly rogue) DHCPv6 server could make the firewall bind loopback, link-local, multicast, unspecified, ULA, documentation, IPv4-mapped, or a configured LAN address on its WAN interface via `parseV6ReplyChecked` → `commitLease` → `applyAddress`. Ranking by preferred-lifetime also let a `pref=0xFFFFFFFF/valid=1s` candidate win, violating RFC 8415 §21.6 (MUST discard).

What: validate every IAADDR candidate before ranking — discard `preferred > valid`, refuse non-global-unicast classes via `config.DelegatedIPv6PrefixRefusalReason` on the `/128`, refuse overlap with the protected configured-prefix set (`overlappingProtectedPrefix` + `Manager.protectedIPv6Prefixes`), and require Is6/non-4-in-6. Each refusal skips only the offending IAADDR so a usable sibling is salvaged, and never sets `sawZeroLifetime` (no synthesized withdrawal; #5927 semantics unchanged). Signature takes explicit `expectedIAID` and `protected` parameters; the sole production caller passes the Manager snapshot. New regression file pins every refused class, the lifetime trap, protected overlap (direct and Manager-installed), and GUA controls. NOT changed: Advertise/Reply matchers and IA_PD extraction (address validation stays at the single parse site every committed lease flows through). Existing reply fixtures that used refused `2001:db8::` IA_NA space moved to `2606:4700::` GUA, mirroring #10856.

Validation: RED on pristine `origin/master` 43ebebd38 with only the new test file (Manager-path protected cell so it compiles on the old signature) — every refused class won ranking, solo refused replies parsed, pref>valid won with 1s valid lifetime, protected-overlap installed. GREEN on this branch: the four `14185` tests pass, full `go test ./pkg/dhcp -count=1` passes, `-race` on the IANA/ParseV6Reply/14185 subset passes, `go vet` and `gofmt` clean on touched files.

Risk: a server offering only special-purpose or configured-overlapping IA_NA space now yields no usable IA_NA and the loop retries (as IA_PD refusals already did); no pin mechanism exists yet (#12533). Fail-closed by design for an address bound on the firewall itself.

## PR #14223 — ddns: keep DHCID across same-name IP moves (#14189) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14189-campaign`

## Why

On a DHCP lease IP change, the DDNS two-pass reconcile deleted the old A record together with its RFC 4701 DHCID (Pass 1), then tried to re-add the new A (Pass 2). `dhcidSharedWithOther` scanned only the ownership store, so the not-yet-published replacement in the desired set was invisible and `KeepForwardDHCID` was false. With any co-resident RRset (e.g. TXT) at the name, Pass 2's `sendAddOwned` Attempt A failed YXDOMAIN and Attempt B failed NXRRSET because the DHCID proof had just been deleted — `errDDNSConflictRefused` on every reconcile, forever: a permanent forward blackhole after an ordinary IP change.

## What

- Hoist the reconcile `desired` struct to package-level `desiredRecord` so helpers can consult the desired set.
- Add `dhcidStillWanted(owned, want)`: true iff the desired set still wants a record with the same ClientID and canonical FQDN (hence the same DHCID).
- Pass 1 computes `keepDHCID := dhcidStillWanted(owned, want)` (the owned key embeds the address, so an IP change makes `stillWanted` false even though the name is still wanted; the want scan is the actual move test) and threads it into `deleteOwnedLocked(..., keepDHCIDForMove)`, OR-ed into `KeepForwardDHCID`. Genuine expiries, withdraw-all, and factory-reset withdrawal pass `false` — last-record DHCID cleanup unchanged; delete stays DHCID-match-guarded. No test-input special-casing.
- Regression `TestIPChangeWithCoexistingTXTKeepsDHCID_14189` against the stateful fake RFC 2136 server via the production manager: publish A=10.0.0.10+DHCID, seed foreign TXT, move lease to 10.0.0.11, assert new A + DHCID present, old A gone, TXT untouched, and full release still removes A+DHCID leaving the TXT.

## Validation

- RED on pristine origin/master 43ebebd38: regression fails (`new A 10.0.0.11 not published after IP change (permanent conflict refusal)`).
- GREEN with fix: regression passes incl. repeat-reconcile stability and teardown cleanup.
- `go test ./pkg/ddns/ -count=1` passes; `go vet ./pkg/ddns/` clean.

## Risk

Bounded to the Pass-1 move path. A failed Pass-2 add after a kept DHCID leaves the DHCID beside the surviving co-resident RRset until the next successful publish or final release (whose DHCID-match delete still removes it). No fail-open: foreign DHCID still refuses; exact-RR deletes unchanged.

Closes #14189

## PR #14225 — frr: fail closed on dangling from prefix-list in policy terms [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14136-campaign`

Closes #14136

## Defect
`renderPolicyTermSequences` emitted `match ip|ipv6 address prefix-list <name>` (or the #5730 inline-ACL form) unconditionally for `from prefix-list`, even when the named list was undefined or every entry was omitted by the #10823 malformed-entry belt. FRR resolves a dangling match to NO MATCH, so a `then reject` term never fired and routes fell through to a later accept or the #2998 BGP trailing permit. Sibling as-path (#9881) and community (#10822) guards already handled this; prefix-list had none.

## Fix
- New `prefixListRefMissingAtRender(po, name, matchKW)`: per-family mirror of the emission loops (same `net.ParseCIDR` predicate and `:` family split as the prefix-list loop and `renderFromPrefixListACL`).
- Term rule mirroring #9881/#10822: a name is fully dangling when every per-family ref is missing. Reject terms over any fully-dangling OR-branch render one bare deny-all; accept/non-terminating terms skip the dangling branch. A mixed list with one rendered family keeps that ref and drops only the dangling family ref. No dangling prefix-list or inline-ACL reference is emitted.
- Updated consumers that asserted the old dangling output (unknown-name, #2607 empty, #7526 bound-agreement, #12070 fixtures now define PL).

## Tests

## PR #14226 — screen: sticky first non-ATOMIC fragment in chained IPv6 headers (#14129) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14129-campaign`

Closes #14129

## Defect
`extract_screen_info` (IPv6) overwrote `is_fragment`/`is_first_fragment`/`ip_frag_off`/`frag_data_off` on every Fragment header sighting. On `[real-first (off=0,M=1)][ATOMIC (off=0,M=0)]` the trailing ATOMIC cleared the real fragment, so `syn-frag` / `icmp-fragment` saw a non-fragment despite a real first fragment + terminal L4 bytes. ## PR #14227 — nfqueue: walk IPv6 extension chain for capture fragments (#13976) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13976-campaign`

Why: ClassifyCapturePayload recognised a Fragment header only when
it immediately followed the IPv6 base header. A fragment behind
Hop-by-Hop, Destination Options, Routing, or AH classified as a
whole packet (IsFragment=false, no FragmentKey), so the IPsec
capture pipeline submitted it for ordinary adjudication instead of
the documented terminal fragment drop, and chains behind the wider
traversable set (Mobility/HIP/Shim6/experimental) were never parsed
at all.

What: classifyIPv6 now walks the extension chain with the same
type set, advance arithmetic, and 8-header bound as the sibling
Rust walk_ipv6_ext_chain (MAX_IPV6_EXT_HEADERS): generic headers
0/43/60/135/139/140/253/254 advance (HdrExtLen+1)*8, AH (51)
advances (len+2)*4, Fragment (44) advances 8 bytes and marks the
packet a fragment wherever it appears, anything else (ESP,
No-Next-Header, TCP/UDP) is terminal. Truncated, overrunning, and
over-limit chains fail closed. Fragment payload offset accounts
for the 8-byte Fragment header so first-fragment ports and
FragmentPiece data match the previous immediate path. Updates
TestClassifyV6NonTransportProtocols10897 to drive HBH/DstOpts as
walked headers and adds TestClassifyV6FragmentBehindExtChain13976
plus docs/log/13976.md.

Validation: RED on the unfixed classifier (every behind-chain
subtest IsFragment=false; the two 10897 rows fail), GREEN after:
go test ./pkg/nfqueue/ -run TestClassify -count=1 and the full
pkg/nfqueue package pass; gofmt, go vet, git diff --check clean.

Risk: IPv6 capture classification only. Chains behind extension
headers now resolve their real terminal protocol (matching the
Rust walker for the same bytes); malformed chains previously
endpoint-classified are now rejected at classification, the
documented terminal-drop disposition.

Closes #13976

## PR #14228 — userspace-dp: carry PPTP call-id pair on HA sync wire (#13965) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13965-campaign`

Why:
The HA import gate withholds a synced Pptp(handle) session unless the
record carries the learned call-id pair the handle is derived from,
but no producer set it: SessionDelta had no pair field, the binary
frame and JSON delta carried nothing, the Go SessionValue had no
field, and the cluster encoder never emitted it. Every synced PPTP
session was withheld on the standby as pptp-call-ids-not-carried.

What:
Stamp SessionDelta.pptp_call_ids from the live association table at
every delta construction; append the pair as the final 8 bytes of
the binary open/update frame and on the JSON leg; decode it
length-gated in Go into sync-only SessionValue{,V6}.PptpCallIDs
(never the BPF ABI) and forward it to SessionSyncRequest; append it
as a final length-gated u64 on the cluster wire, decoded only for
the PPTP discriminator tag with the present bit; thread the verified
call through upsert_synced_session_with_pptp and install the
association on workers via InstallPptpAssociation /
install_synced_association. Shift the pinned-offset codec cells by
the trailer, regenerate the shared 9412 golden, split the PPTP frame
regression into its own named cell, and add Go cluster round-trip
cells plus docs/log/13965.md.

Validation:
cargo test --bins -- codec::tests producer_seq_lock 13965 7188 pptp
(158 passed); go test ./pkg/cluster/ -run '13965|7188' (passed);
TestSessionUpdateGoldenFrameDecodes9412 passed. RED on clean master:
the Go cell fails to build (PptpCallIDs undefined) and no Rust
producer sets the pair. Pre-existing failures on clean master
46672678b, also failing there: TestContractSnapshotGolden9821,
TestFIBImportGoldenSnapshotFresh11419,
TestPartialRepublishRefusesQuarantineOnlySkew12247.

Risk:
Rolling upgrade is append-only and length-gated both ways; an old
peer's PPTP sessions remain withheld, never aliased. No BPF/C ABI

## PR #14230 — userspace-dp: keep tunnel threads on refused defer plan (#14131) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14131-campaign`

## Why

On the `defer_workers=true`, NOT-same-plan leg of `snapshot::apply`, the WG and local GRE/IPIP thread prunes ran *before* the fallible `replan_queues` binding-plan computation. When the candidate removed a live tunnel and its binding plan was refused (slot cap, wild ifindex, NAT-holder width), the handler restored only `guard.snapshot` and the status fields — but a prune stops, joins, and *removes* the thread-map entry (not a tombstone), so neither the tombstone-only liveness sweeps nor the rollback could resurrect the WG rekey/handshake thread or the local-origin TUN reader. The prior snapshot stayed nominally active while its tunnel threads were dead: an availability loss on a refused (fail-closed) apply.

## What

In `userspace-dp/src/server/handlers/snapshot.rs::apply`, compute the binding plan *before* any side-effecting prune. `replan_queues` is pure (candidate snapshot + worker count + existing bindings + arm flag), so hoisting it ahead of the prunes changes nothing on the success path; on `Err` the handler now returns before the snapshot swap and before either prune, making a refused apply fully side-effect-free — the same discipline the #5171 defer-integrity leg already follows. The successful defer path is unchanged: integrity validation, then replan, then the prunes (still against the candidate snapshot), then the snapshot swap and deferred spawn skip. Same-plan legs never replan and are untouched, as are the prune predicates.

Added `apply_snapshot_defer_plan_refusal_keeps_live_tunnel_threads_14131` in `userspace-dp/src/server/tests.rs`: it stands up a live WG + GRE tunnel pair (real threads over TUN stand-ins), then applies a `defer_workers` candidate that removes both tunnels and adds a wild-ifindex (`70_000`) data interface. It asserts the apply is refused with `binding plan refused`, the prior snapshot/generation stays installed, and both thread entries remain live with their deliveries published. Plus `cfg(test)` coordinator helpers in `afxdp/coordinator/tunnel_supervision.rs` to register stand-ins / probe entry liveness / seed the GRE worker gate from the server tests.

## Validation

- New regression RED with the handler fix stashed (fails at "refused apply must keep the WG thread live") and GREEN with the fix, including after rebase onto current master (`4adefde7a`).
- Related set of 8 tests GREEN in one run: the new cell, `apply_snapshot_with_wild_ifindex_is_refused_without_install_9900`, the #5171 defer trio, `wg1866_disarmed_same_plan_apply_does_not_hold_wg_ports`, `wg1866_defer_prune_releases_port_and_sweep_does_not_resurrect`, and `gre1881_defer_prune_removes_only_stale_entries`.

## Risk

Behavior delta only on the previously-broken refusal path: a refused defer apply now keeps the live tunnel threads it previously killed. No wire/protocol change.

Closes #14131
