## PR #14231 — frr: fail closed on dangling route-filter in policy terms (#14137) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14137-campaign`

## Summary
- `renderRouteFilterEntry` skips invalid route-filter entries (malformed prefix incl. `route-filter longer exact`, unknown/`through` match-type, malformed prefix-length-range, invalid `upto`) and writes no inline prefix-list definition, but `emitTermBody` still emitted `match ip|ipv6 address prefix-list <inline>` against the undefined list. FRR resolves that to NOMATCH — fail-closed for permit, **fail-open for `then reject`**: the deny never fires and the route falls through to a later accept or the BGP trailing `permit`. The tolerant path reaches this directly, and `failClosedInheritedInvalidRouteFilters12687` manufactures it by turning an inherited invalid term into `Action="reject"` without making its skipped filter match.
- Fix: the route-filter sibling of the #9881/#10822/#14136 term rules. Per family group (single group, or each half of a split mixed-family term), an all-invalid route-filter set renders one bare deny-all for a reject term and no sequence otherwise — never a dangling inline match, never a bare permit. A group with any non-invalid entry keeps its match line (OR semantics; rendered subset is fail-closed).
- Shared predicate: new `config.RouteFilterEntrySkipped` is the single source of truth for "match set unknowable", used by both the FRR term rule and the #12687 quarantine (which keeps its narrower valid-`through` tolerance and now also quarantines inherited malformed prefixes). Max-length `longer` (`10.0.0.0/32 longer`) is valid with an honestly empty set and is **never** broadened to deny-all — the issue's control.

## Tests
- New `pkg/frr/policy_routefilter_dangling_14137_test.go` (8 tests): RED on pristine master (5 fail), GREEN with fix. Decisive fixture: reject term whose sole route-filter is the `longer exact` shape, followed by accept + permit trailing default; plus invalid variants (unknown match-type, through, bad range, bad/unset upto, malformed v6), accept/non-terminating skip, mixed valid+invalid, split mixed-family invalid half, `/32 longer` no-deny-all control, valid control.
- Updated consumers that asserted the old dangling matcher: `TestRouteFilterMalformedPrefixBelt`, `TestGeneratePolicyOptionsPrefixLengthRangeAtOrBelowBaseSkipped`, `TestGeneratePolicyOptionsThroughSkipped`, two `UptoLen==0` subtests of `TestRouteFilterUptoFRR`.
- `go test ./pkg/frr/ -count=1`: green except 3 pre-existing FRR-binary load failures, confirmed identical on pristine master. `pkg/config`/`pkg/configstore` route-filter & 12687 tests green; gofmt/vet clean.

Docs: `docs/log/14137.md`, `pkg/frr/README.md` rule entry.

Closes #14137

## PR #14235 — xdp: drop LAND packets on every terminal kernel pass (#13953) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/13953-campaign-fix`

## Summary
Drop LAND (equal source/destination) packets on every terminal shim kernel-pass arm, closing the residual #11087 gap H13-03.

## Why
Host-bound session-miss traffic to a non-NAT firewall address bypassed all worker screens. On a session miss, the shim's local-destination and ICMP-to-interface-NAT-local arms passed the packet to the kernel before any screen ran; the same held for the WireGuard steer fallthrough, the early-filter pass, and the degraded control-disabled/binding/heartbeat path. The #11087 LAND drop existed only on the established `PASS_TO_KERNEL` arm. The Linux stack drops IPv4 LAND even with `accept_local=1`, but has no IPv6 LAND backstop — an IPv6 `src == dst` packet to a firewall-local address was delivered to local sockets on every residual arm.

## What
- `userspace-xdp/src/land.rs` (new, `core`-only): the single `is_land` predicate over `ParsedPacket`'s 16-byte address fields (`ParsedPacket` stores IPv4 addresses in the first four bytes of a zeroed 16-byte field, so one compare is family-correct).
- `userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs`: drop equal source/destination with the new `land_drop` degraded-path counter (reason 19) — once in the healthy path after the tagged-only VID-0 drop and adjudicated-interface gate (covering session-miss local, interface-NAT ICMP, WireGuard steer, early-filter, native-GRE inner-PASS, and degraded binding/heartbeat arms), once in the control-disabled path after its tagged-only check, and on the `PASS_TO_KERNEL` arm refactored to the shared predicate.
- `pkg/dataplane/userspace/maps_sync.go`: `degradedPathReasonNames` slot 19 `land_drop`; cap test updated 19 → 20 (the #8258 agreement test auto-enrols it).
- `docs/afxdp-packet-processing.md`: documents which screens apply to host-bound traffic — LAND at the shim, flood screens via the `xpf_hostinbound` input-chain mirror, and the remaining worker screens do not run on terminal kernel passes.
- Regenerated `userspace_xdp_bpfel.o`, manifest and gate verdict.

## Validation
- Host GREEN: `cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml --bin xpf-userspace-dp tests_shim_land_13953` → 2 passed (equal v4/v6 → LAND; distinct → pass; the test `#[path]`-includes the exact `land.rs` the shim calls).
- BPF RED on pre-fix object: a probe running IPv6 LAND to a local address on session miss returned `XDP_PASS` (2), and the `land_drop` reason was absent from the pre-fix Go table.
- BPF GREEN after regeneration: `TestUserspaceXDPLandSessionMissDropped13953` → IPv6 and IPv4 LAND on session miss return `XDP_DROP` with `land_drop` + `transit_drop` and no `pass_to_kernel`; non-LAND controls still return `XDP_PASS`.
- `make generate-userspace-xdp`: verifier PASS, 687,573 processed insns, 31.24% headroom (limit 1,000,000).
- Full sweep `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace -run 'TestUserspaceXDP|TestDegradedPath|TestEveryShimFallback'` → ok (360s). #8258 reason-agreement tests pass with the new slot.

## Risk
One 16-byte compare added after parse on the healthy path and on the cold ctrl-disabled path; no verifier regression. Non-adjudicated interfaces still take `cpumap_or_pass` untouched — the #8279 authority boundary is unchanged (the packet is not delivered to a screened zone's local stack by this shim). No legitimate equal-address traffic traverses this XDP hook — loopback never does.

## PR #14240 — userspace-dp: translate NAT64 non-first fragments on slow path (#14114) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14114-campaign`

Why: `build_nat64_l3_packet_for_slow_path` called only the whole-packet preserve-TTL NAT64 translators, which return `None` for every non-first fragment, and then unconditionally ran the L4 port rewrite. A first fragment that committed ForwardCandidate installs the fragment association and session; its tail can then be adjudicated NoRoute (route withdrawn between fragments), LocalDelivery, or MissingNeighbor — all slow-path eligible — and reaches the builder with the recorded NAT64 decision, where it dropped as `nat64_slow_path_prepare_failed` instead of being delegated to the kernel FIB. The fast path already translates such tails L3-only; the slow path never learned the case.

What: branch on `is_non_first_fragment` in the slow-path builder (both directions), translate via new preserve-TTL twins `write_v6_to_v4_nonfirst_into_preserve_ttl` / `write_v4_to_v6_nonfirst_into_preserve_ttl` (existing non-first translators refactored behind a `preserve_ttl` flag, so the kernel FIB still performs the single TTL decrement), and return before the port rewrite so payload bytes are never read as ports. Whole packets keep the existing path byte-for-byte. NOT changed: fast-path fragment translation, fragment-association install gates, fail-closed drops for ICMP fragments or missing `Nat64ReverseInfo`.

Validation: new regression `nat64_nonfirst_no_route_reinjects_after_l3_translation_14114` drives `maybe_reinject_slow_path_from_frame_with_outlet` in both directions, asserting translated addresses, fragment ident/offset survival, preserved Hop Limit/TTL, verbatim payload, and a fail-closed missing-reverse control. RED on pristine master (panics at the forward delegation assertion), GREEN with the fix. All 288 `nat64_` tests pass, including the #11066 NoRoute sibling and #5146/#9957 fragment tests.

Risk: slow-path-only change; tails without a recorded NAT64 decision still drop fail-closed. No wire, session, or HA format change.

## PR #14241 — config: bare control/fabric lifeline must not cover declared transit VLAN units (#14192) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14192-campaign`

## Defect
`HostInboundLifelineSet` recorded only declared interface base keys and set a bare lifeline base (`control-interface ge-0/0/0`) `true`; declared units were never registered. `HostInboundLifelineInterface` missed the exact lookup for a declared transit VLAN unit (`ge-0/0/0.100`) and its numeric-suffix fallback returned the parent's `true`, dropping the unit from `junosHostNonLifelineRefs` and the coverage projection — exempting a zone-assigned VLAN unit from the `to-zone junos-host` default-deny (D10-01).

- Register every declared unit as an explicit `false` key; re-mark a designated lifeline's own unit 0 (and a role spelled at a declared unit, e.g. `hb.1`) `true`.

- `fxp0.0` seeded explicitly so the management unit survives unit registration.

## PR #14242 — nat: share deterministic NAPT64 BIB across remotes (#14091) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14091-campaign`

## Why
Deterministic NAPT64 allocated one external port per complete remote-specific flow, contradicting RFC 6146 BIB semantics and exhausting a subscriber's deterministic port block across destinations. #13946 fixed only the round-robin NAT64 path; this closes the deterministic follow-up.

## What
- Allocator-integrated persistent BIB keyed by protocol, IPv6 subscriber, source port/ICMP identifier, and routing scope, with a 300-second idle lifetime; remote-specific sessions remain independently tracked and refcounted.
- Fresh allocations stay inside the subscriber's deterministic IPv4/port block; the lock-free block probe still runs before the allocator mutex (#9130), with BIB reuse and expired-lease reclaim handled post-probe and on probe exhaustion.
- Deterministic configuration identity (DeterministicPortedIdentity::{V4,V6}) is carried on persistent leases and the Rust/Go idle/display lease wires; joins require matching identity, pool address/index, in-block port, and validity.
- HA synced-session reservations join the same BIB and reject out-of-block tuples. Idle deterministic NAT64 BIBs sync per NAT64 prefix and reject unknown prefixes, mismatched configuration, wrong families, unknown translated addresses, and out-of-block tuples without stealing a live tuple.
- Deterministic ports are freed with no-recycle semantics on GC, expiry, rollback, revoked cleanup, and idle-import rollback.
- Regression tests: local sharing, distinct transports, teardown/expiry, HA reserve join, idle failover import, configuration identity, and concurrent destinations racing for one BIB.
- Regenerated the protocol wire fixture for the deterministic fields only (unrelated drift removed) and added docs/log/14091.md with RED/GREEN evidence.

## PR #14243 — afxdp: skip NAT64 port rewrite on reverse non-first fragments (#14115) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14115-campaign`

Closes #14115

## Why
Reverse NAT64 non-first fragments arriving via GRE/WG decapsulation carry the real inner protocol (UDP, from `parse_inner_protocol_and_offsets`) in meta, not the direct-XDP shim's 255 no-L4 sentinel. `build_nat64_inner_frame` built the L3-only non-first frame then fell through to `apply_nat64_port_translation`, which walked the output IPv6 Fragment Header to an apparent L4 and overwrote payload[0..4] as ports and payload[6..8] as a checksum — corrupting the fragment tail (short tails could also fail the build).

## What
- Reverse arm: compute wire non-first status once from the input frame, use it for builder selection, and early-return before port translation (mirrors the forward arm).
- `apply_nat64_port_translation`: no-op when the translated output wire is a non-first fragment (defense in depth, wire-authoritative).
- `build_nat64_l3_packet_for_slow_path`: explicit fail-closed on non-first fragments.
- Regressions: decapped real-UDP shape + direct-XDP 255 sentinel control; forward + slow-path pins. No test-input special-casing — gating is on wire fragment status.

## Validation
- RED on master: `nat64_14115_reverse_nonfirst_decapped_payload_not_treated_as_ports` fails (payload bytes corrupted).
- GREEN: `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- nat64_` — 288 passed.

## Risk
Low. Only non-first NAT64 paths change; first/atomic fragments keep the existing #4381 port/identifier rewrite (pinned by existing suite).

## PR #14244 — userspace-dp: forward local-origin GRE non-first fragments flowless (#14119) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14119-campaign`

Closes #14119

## Why
`build_local_origin_tunnel_tx_request` demanded a complete L4 session flow before the local-owner check, but `parse_session_flow_from_bytes` correctly refuses non-first fragments (#2344 — payload is never parsed as ports), so locally originated fragmented datagrams lost every non-first piece at the GRE TUN and peer reassembly could never complete.

## What
When the flow parse returns `None` and the frame is positively a non-first fragment (`frame_is_non_first_fragment`), recover only the L3 source via `parse_packet_source_from_frame` — never ports — and continue flowless. The existing zone and table-scoped source-ownership gates apply to that source before any transmission. Flowless fragments mint no TunOrigin session/reverse, seed no IKE, carry `flow_key: None`, and classify CoS without a flow key; GRE encap carries the fragment verbatim. All other flowless packets still fail closed with the original error. WG needed no change: its encap already ignores the publish-parse outcome.

## Validation
- RED on `bfcf00f8f`: 3 new `14119` tests fail with `parse_local_origin_session_flow_failed`.
- GREEN: 3/3 pass; `tests_native_gre_ecn` 25/25 (incl. #13179 controls).
- Tunnel-filtered run: 228 passed, 1 pre-existing failure (`snapshot_published_tunnel_rows_join_d11_10485`, reproduced on pristine `d40f1f29e`).

## Risk
Owned non-first fragments now transmit session-less like wire-forwarded fragments; replies ride the first fragment's TunOrigin pair. Non-owned/unzoned fragments remain fail-closed; no payload byte becomes a port or session identity.

See `docs/log/14119.md`.

## PR #14247 — userspace-dp: scope IKE exchange exemption by zone and VRF (#14124) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14124-campaign`

## Summary

Closes #14124.

The IKE established-exchange exemption was zone/VRF-blind: the
#6471 live-exchange key was SPI + peer/local IPs only, and the
Stage-11 local claim used the address-global
`owns_ipsec_local_destination`. An exchange admitted on an
IKE-permitting zone supplied the established exemption for the same
SPI/source/destination arriving on a second, IKE-denied zone
(multihomed peer or spoof-capable AF_XDP secondary ingress),
skipping its coarse host-inbound check before delegation to
strongSwan; an address configured only in another VRF was likewise
treated as locally terminated absent a matching transit DNAT.

## Fix

- `IkeExchangeKey` gains `ingress_zone_id` + `routing_domain`. The
  Stage-11 seed (`poll_descriptor/mod.rs`), the match
  (`poll_stages.rs`), and the GRE local-origin seed (`tunnel.rs`
  via `maybe_seed_local_origin_ike`) all carry the admitting
  ingress scope, so a seed vouches only for its own zone/VRF.
- Stage 11 claims through the new
  `owns_ipsec_local_destination_in_table`
  (`types/forwarding.rs`), which additionally requires local
  ownership in the ingress interface's canonical routing table
  (mirroring the `fib.rs` table-scoped local-delivery decision).
  Cross-VRF claims return `NotClaimed` and take ordinary
  forwarding/policy (fail-closed). The unscoped predicate is
  unchanged for its other callers.
- NOT changed: ESP/AH/ESP-in-UDP exemption, fine per-packet
  re-gating, table cap/LRU/idle semantics.

## Regression (RED pre-fix)

- `forwarding::ipsec::tests::exchange_match_is_zone_and_vrf_scoped_14124`
- `poll_stages::tests::stage_ipsec_established_seed_does_not_cross_zone_or_vrf_14124`
  — seed on permit zone, replay same SPI/src/dst on deny zone ->
  `Denied`; same-zone control -> `Passthrough`; tenant-domain
  replay -> `Denied`
- `poll_stages::tests::owns_ipsec_local_destination_in_table_is_vrf_scoped_14124`
  — overlapping destination in another VRF, no transit DNAT

## Validation

- New tests: 3 passed. Targeted suites (`14124 ipsec 10516 10518
  10519 10525 10585 stage11 local_origin`, rebased head): 200
  passed, 0 failed.
- Full `--bins` at base 4adefde7a (`cargo +1.98.1 test --release`):
  8238 passed, 29 failed, 8 ignored; pristine `origin/master`

## PR #14254 — userspace-dp: charge post-NAT fragment quota to arrival tenant (#14127) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14127-campaign`

Why:
The post-translation fragment-overlap key's sender identity was the
shared SNAT/NAT64 pool address, so two permitted tenants translated
through one pool IP shared one 8-incomplete-entries-per-shard budget
and could fail-close each other's fragmented datagrams on a common
post-NAT shard. A fragment routed to a different egress routing
domain with no address rewrite got no post key at all, skipping the
downstream domain's anchor check.

What:
- `OverlapKey` gains `fairness_origin`, stamped by
  `translated_overlap_key` with the pre-translation sender on every
  returned post key (same-family NAT, NAT64 v6->v4, domain-change).
- Reassembly membership compares the translated tuple ignoring the
  origin (`overlap_same_datagram`), so colliding downstream
  datagrams (e.g. NAT64 16-bit ident truncation) still find the
  same entry and drop on overlap.
- The sender-fairness quota charges the origin instead of the pool
  address; cross-origin incomplete entries count again once an
  origin's pending fragments have failed admission (poisoned), and
  the downstream domain reserve still counts all post entries.
- `translated_overlap_key` returns a post key when only the routing
  domain changes, so the downstream domain is anchored.
- NOT changed: pre/post commit order at both TX sites
  (`poll_descriptor`, `neighbor_dispatch`) — the pre admission
  already enters `OverlapAdmissionTokens` before the post check and
  a post drop RAII-fails it.

## PR #14255 — grpcapi: transfer MonitorInterface slot on ctx cancel (#14150) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14150-campaign`

Why: `sendMonitorInterfaceFrame` transferred the `monitorInterfaceLimiter` slot to its Send worker only on the timer branch; the `ctx.Done` branch returned `(ctx.Err(), false)`, so `MonitorInterface`'s defer released the slot while the worker stayed parked in `Send`. That ctx is the reauth-derived context (#9051, `reauthServerStream`), whose cancellation does not cancel the underlying transport `Send` — a revocation-cancelled slow reader parks the worker indefinitely, and repeated cycles admit unbounded parked senders beyond the 64 cap.

What: mirror the `sendMonitorPacketDropFrame` twin — the ctx-done branch stores the transfer flag and drains `done` (release + `false` if Send already completed, else `true` so the caller disarms its defer and the parked worker releases when Send returns). Updated function/defer comments. NOT changed: PacketDrop frame (already transfers on both branches), Recv proxy path (conn.Close unblocks it, no worker-held slot), the limiter. Both existing callers (`MonitorInterface` loop, `forwardMonitorInterfaceFrames`) already honour the `(error, bool)` transfer contract, so no call-site change was needed.

Validation: new `TestMonitorInterfaceCtxCancelTransfersSlot_14150` with a decoupled fake (ctx cancellable independently, Send parks on a separate transport channel — the production reauth shape): RED on pristine base worktree (both subtests: `xfer=false`, `InFlight=0` while worker parked), GREEN with fix; `TestSendBoundary*`, slow-consumer and PacketDrop twin tests pass. Full `go test ./pkg/grpcapi/ -count=1`: 2 failures base-attributed (identical on pristine base), 1 flaky dialpeer failure that passes on base and `-count=3` on head. `go vet`/`gofmt` clean.

Risk: on ctx transfer the slot is retained until the transport actually unblocks Send — intended bounded retention, identical to the existing timer-transfer doctrine.

Closes #14150

## PR #14256 — vrrp: announce existing VIPs on failover GARP race (#14155) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14155-campaign`

Why:
`becomeMaster` bumped `garpEpoch` under `vipMu`, unlocked without recording the
actuated VIPs as pending GARP announcements, then launched `go vi.sendGARP(false)`.
A concurrent `updateVIPs` adding a VIP won `vipMu`, bumped the epoch again, saw an
empty pending set, announced only the new VIP, and reserved that epoch — so the
deferred failover sender was epoch-deduped and pre-existing VIPs never received a
failover GARP/NA, leaving neighbours with stale ARP/NDP until cache expiry.

What:
- `becomeMaster` records the actuated set (`res.applied`) via
  `addPendingGARPVIPsLocked` under the held `vipMu` before unlocking, so an
  interleaving `updateVIPs` carries the unannounced VIPs into its announcement.
- `instance_garp.go` adds a pending-aware full-set gate + `pendingOnly` reserved
  mode draining still-pending VIPs once (500 ms dampener still applies);
  `sendGARPFor` keeps strict epoch dedup.
- Regression `become_master_garp_race_14155_test.go` models the parked deferred
  sender deterministically and asserts exactly one burst per VIP, plus an
  unsuppress control. README + `docs/log/14155.md` updated.
- NOT changed: advert ordering, dampener doctrine, suppress semantics,
  `updateVIPs` scope, reconcile/reaffirm senders.

Validation:
- RED on origin/master (0db0fa57c): only `10.0.141.3` announced, V1/V2 zero bursts.
- RED-on-revert: reverting the `instance_transition.go` hunk alone reproduces it.
- GREEN: full `go test ./pkg/vrrp/ -count=1` ok (6.7s), GARP-related selection
  under `-race` ok, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean, main test `-count=5` (5/5).

Risk:
A suppressed becomeMaster now leaves VIPs pending; pending is pruned to current
membership and only MASTER announcements consume it, so a BACKUP never announces.
A periodic full-set sender finding a reserved epoch with pending VIPs emits each
retained VIP once, subject to the dampener — the intended failover announcement.

Closes #14155

## PR #14259 — fix: register expanded persistent-NAT pool members in compileNAT (#14110) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14110-campaign`

Closes #14110

## Defect
`compileNAT` registered persistent-NAT pool IPs from only `pool.Addresses`, and for a CIDR member only its parsed base IP. The userspace SNAT allocator instead expands `config.SourceNATPoolMembers` (singular `pool.Address` + `Addresses`, every CIDR over its full masked prefix). `preservePersistentNATV4/V6` looks up the translated IP in the persistent table, so bindings allocated to non-base CIDR members or singular-address pools were silently not preserved on Go-side session deletion.

## Fix
- New `config.SourceNATPoolExpandedAddresses`: unique expanded address set reusing `SourceNATPoolMembers`, all-or-nothing `SourceNATPoolUnusableReason`, and the existing masked-interval expansion; deduped first-occurrence like the Rust allocator.
- `compileNAT` registers exactly that set. Fail-closed: unusable pools (bad/over-cap/%zone member, invalid port range, empty) or pools over the aggregate budget (`SourceNATAggregateOverBudgetPools`) register nothing and warn, mirroring the snapshot builder's poisoning. No new persistent-table method, so the #4960 pre-pass exact method-count guard is unchanged.

## Regression RED/GREEN
`TestPersistentNATPoolRegistrationExpandsMembers14110`: /29 + /126 persistent pool, singular-address pool, invalid-member pool, over-cap /15 pool; asserts every expanded member resolves via LookupPool, unusable pools register nothing, set survives recompile, and preservePersistentNATV4 saves a binding for 192.0.2.5.
- RED on master: LookupPool missed 192.0.2.1/.5/.7, 2001:db8:1::2/::3, singular 198.51.100.7; bad/wide pools wrongly registered base IPs; no binding preserved.
- GREEN with fix; targeted config/dataplane NAT suites pass; vet/gofmt clean. Full pkg/config suite timed out under parallel campaign load in unrelated TestSlotEscapeCoverage (passes alone in 33s on clean base) — CI to confirm.

See docs/log/14110.md.

## PR #14265 — afxdp: unwind failed worker bring-up and un-wedge same-plan retry (#14130) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14130-campaign`

Closes #14130

## Why

Three mechanisms from D3-09, all confirmed at `origin/master` `c6f058672`:

1. `plan_workers` registered per-slot `workers.live`/`identities` at plan
   time — before the IPsec-SA readiness gate and before any thread
   spawned. The `IpsecSaNotReady` arm returned without unwinding them, so
   status reported a full fleet with zero running threads.
2. The `SpawnFailed` arm returned without `stop_inner`, leaving
   already-launched workers forwarding the candidate snapshot while the
   handler rolled its in-memory baseline back — a mixed-snapshot window.
3. `same_plan_apply_needs_binding_reconcile` additionally required an
   eligible binding with an EMPTY `last_error`, so a failed bring-up that
   recorded a bind cause suppressed the identical-plan retry forever:
   the retry took the refresh leg, which cannot spawn workers.

## What

- `plan_workers` registers nothing; `spawn_workers` registers each
  worker's slots only in its post-spawn-success arm
  (`register_planned_slots`, alongside the #6242 record insert);
  `publish_runtime` builds the mirror map from the plan.
- Every post-plan failure arm in `bring_up_workers`
  (`IpsecSaNotReady`, `SpawnFailed`, `BindIncomplete`) now runs
  `stop_inner(false)` and re-records its stage, so a failed bring-up
  leaves the coordinator exactly as a completed teardown does.
- `same_plan_apply_needs_binding_reconcile` drops the
  `last_error.is_empty()` conjunct; the live/planned shortfall with any
  unbound/unregistered runnable slot is the recovery signal.
- New `#[cfg(test)]` per-instance `force_ipsec_sa_not_ready` seam so the
  SA-gate unwinding is unit-verifiable unprivileged.

## Validation

- GREEN: `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 14130 8388 8558 6242` —
  12 passed, 0 failed.
- RED on pristine base `c6f058672` (+ the new tests and a 3-line
  test-only seam shim): 5 named 14130 tests fail
  (`ipsec_sa_not_ready_unwinds_…`, `reconcile_partial_spawn_failure_…`,
  `spawn_failure_leaves_no_bound_sibling_14130`,
  `spawn_failure_same_plan_retry_recovers_14130`,
  `same_plan_retry_after_bind_failure_reconciles_14130`).
  `bind_incomplete_same_plan_retry_recovers_14130` is GREEN-on-base
  (that arm already stopped workers); the wedge discriminator is the
  handler-level cell. Full detail: `docs/log/14130.md`.

## PR #14266 — upgrade: fail closed on indeterminate live-version lookup in GC and verify-fail cleanup (#14166) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14166-campaign`

Closes #14166

## Defect
`gc` (flip.go) and `cleanupFailedVerifyCopy` (cutover.go) resolved the live version with `cur, _ := r.readCurrentVersion()`, discarding every error — not just permitted absence (`readCurrentVersion` returns `("", nil)` only for ENOENT). An EIO/EINVAL-class indeterminate lookup left the running dir unprotected: GC could `RemoveAll` it past the N=3 retention window, and verify-failure cleanup could delete the target when it equalled the live dir but differed from `PreviousVersion`. This mirrors the fail-closed guard already in `copyStaged`.

## Fix
- `gc`: on a non-nil lookup error, return a wrapped error and defer **all** version-dir deletion (callers already log GC failure as non-fatal to a committed cut, so a later GC retries).
- `cleanupFailedVerifyCopy`: log and SKIP the delete on lookup error; still rewind the journal to INIT for a clean retry.
- New `readlinkCurrent = os.Readlink` seam (following `statVersionDir`/`statNodeID` precedents) so tests can inject a non-ENOENT failure without root-dependent chmod tricks.
- Genuinely absent `current` behavior unchanged.

## Regression
`pkg/upgrade/gc_current_indeterminate_14166_test.go`:
- `TestGC_IndeterminateCurrentDefersDeletion_14166` — 5 committed versions, live 1.0.0 past retention protected solely by `current`, journal names only 5.0.0/4.0.0; injected EIO => gc errors wrapping the injection and deletes nothing; healthy-read control GCs 2.0.0 and retains live 1.0.0.
- `TestVerifyFailCleanup_IndeterminateCurrentKeepsLiveTarget_14166` — target == live != PreviousVersion; injected EIO => live dir survives, skip logged, journal rewound+persisted at INIT.
- `TestGC_AbsentCurrentStillRuns_14166` — absent `current` still GCs normally (absent != indeterminate).

RED on pristine origin/master in a separate base worktree (seam+tests only: both defect tests FAIL — gc returned nil and removed live 1.0.0; cleanup removed live 3.0.0 — control passes), GREEN with the fix. Full `go test ./pkg/upgrade/...` green.

## PR #14267 — filter: meter input policers on host and passthrough packets (#14120) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14120-campaign`

Closes #14120

## Defect
An interface `filter input` three-color policer was metered only in the TX-selection leg (`resolve_cos_tx_selection*`), which transit packets take at egress. Host-bound (LocalDelivery) and Stage-11 IPsec passthrough packets reinject to the host and never egress, so a burst matching the ingress policer bypassed its token charge and red discard/remarking — the interface-input twin of the lo0 hole fixed in #5857 (research D2-03).

## Fix
- `InputPolicerMeter` threaded through the non-routing input-filter walk: `Inline` (Stage-11; host-bound session hits keyed on the stored disposition) meters in the walk plus a routing-bearing metered walk for policers on/past a `routing-instance` term; `DeferToTxSelection` (transit/flowless) preserves prior behavior so forwarded packets are charged exactly once.
- Session MISS captures policer handles at the LocalDelivery install site, meters the first packet, stores them on `SessionEntry::input_policers`; LocalDelivery HITs replay them (Fresh directly, stale at capture) since host-bound flows are never flow-cached.
- Red folds to a silent `Discard` (never a synthesized reject reply), matching Junos policer semantics.
- Tunnel outer gate meters its PBR-term policer only when the outer destination is firewall-local (interface primary / interface-NAT / FIB-local), preserving transit-decap deferral.
- Docs: `filter/README.md` section + `docs/log/14120.md`.

## Validation
- New cells: `stage11_input_policer_meters_and_drops_over_rate_ike_14120`, `local_delivery_input_policer_meters_inline_without_double_charge_14120`, `local_delivery_hit_replays_input_policer_14120`, `transit_hit_defers_input_policer_to_tx_selection_14120`.
- Pre-existing #12289 underlay cells reddened while the TX deferral was unconditional (policer charged 0 of 1) and pass with the fix — they pin the no-double-charge / tunnel-local boundary.
- Targeted: `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- counts_underlay_once_12289 _14120 filter:: session::` → 834 passed, 0 failed.
- Full bin suite: only the pre-existing master failure set remains (stash-baseline diff identical; this change fixes 2 of those 32).

## Risk
Added per-packet work is gated on policed input filters; unpoliced interfaces pay one enum compare. `SessionEntry` gains one SmallVec field — node-local, no serde/wire change. DSCP/color remarking on delivered host-bound frames remains unapplied (no local-delivery frame-rewrite mechanism), same posture as #5857; drop + charge are enforced.

## PR #14270 — userspace-dp: judge NAT64 errors by original sender and refund undelivered budget (#14123) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

the stateless Pref64 mapping of the actual sender).

## PR #14271 — cluster: do not clobber a heartbeat that lands during the confirmed fence wait (#14158) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14158-campaign`

## Why

Under `peer-fencing disable-rg-confirmed` (#7147), `handlePeerTimeout` checks `peerHeartbeatFreshLocked()` before the fence but not after. `awaitPeerFenceLocked` (`pkg/cluster/fence_confirm_7147.go`) releases `m.mu` for the bounded `SendFenceAwait`; during that window `handlePeerHeartbeat` (a different goroutine) can set `peerAlive=true` and rebuild peer groups for a live, primary peer. On re-lock, the unconditional `m.peerAlive = false` re-assertion clobbered that heartbeat, and `handlePeerTimeout` proceeded to `electSingleNode()` — promoting the local node while the peer (which never received/acked a fence when `SendFenceAwait` errored, e.g. fabric sync down while the control link lives) remains primary: transient dual-active.

The re-assertion exists for the opposite hazard: after a CONFIRMED fence the peer is dark, and a heartbeat that landed in the window would re-arm the #7161 readiness gate and strand both nodes secondary. Both hazards live in the same window; the fence outcome discriminates them.

## What

- `pkg/cluster/fence_confirm_7147.go`: `awaitPeerFenceLocked` now returns `bool` — whether the peer-loss takeover may proceed. On re-lock, if `m.peerAlive` is set (it was false on entry and only `handlePeerHeartbeat` sets it, so this means exactly "a heartbeat landed during the wait") AND the fence did not confirm (`err != nil` or negative ack), it records the unconfirmed fence as degraded and aborts: the heartbeat's peer state and peer-aware election outcome stand. Otherwise behaviour is unchanged, including the `peerAlive=false` re-assertion on the confirmed path and fail-open on every unconfirmed path where no heartbeat landed. Header docs rewritten to state both arms.
- `pkg/cluster/heartbeat_manager.go`: `handlePeerTimeout` returns early when the fence aborts — no `electSingleNode`. If the peer then truly dies, the next heartbeat timeout re-runs the whole path.
- `pkg/cluster/fence_confirm_7147_test.go`: comment-only cross-reference to the #14158 arm.
- Regression `pkg/cluster/fence_heartbeat_race_14158_test.go`: the confirm callback delivers a peer-PRIMARY heartbeat through the real `handlePeerHeartbeat` during the await and returns an error; asserts no local promotion, `peerAlive` and peer groups survive. Control cell: same failed fence with no intervening heartbeat still fail-opens to primary. No test input is special-cased in production code.
- `docs/log/14158.md`: campaign log.

Detection deliberately does not gate on `peerHeartbeatFreshLocked()`: a heartbeat delivered via `handlePeerHeartbeat` in tests does not stamp the receiver's `lastSeen`, and gating on it would miss that case and risk false aborts.

## Validation

- RED on origin/master (55e93ffec) in a separate base worktree (never `git stash`): new test fails — "peerAlive was clobbered by awaitPeerFenceLocked after a heartbeat arrived during the fence wait (#14158)", with the dual-active promotion in the log. Control passes on base.
- GREEN with fix: `go test ./pkg/cluster/ -run 'TestHandlePeerTimeoutHeartbeatDuringFailedFence|TestHandlePeerTimeoutNoHeartbeatDuringFailedFence|7147|9640|10701|TestHandlePeerTimeout' -count=1` — ok (includes the confirmed-window promotion test, the fail-open table, #2080 guard-recheck tests).
- `go vet ./pkg/cluster/` clean; gofmt clean on touched files.
- Full `go test ./pkg/cluster/ -count=1`: only `TestInstallTableProducerToResendEndToEnd9752` fails — it also fails on pristine origin/master in isolation (pre-existing, unrelated session-table resend test).

## Risk

Behaviour changes only under `peer-fencing disable-rg-confirmed` when a heartbeat lands inside the ≤1s fence wait and the fence fails: previously a dual-active promotion, now a deferred takeover retried at the next heartbeat timeout. Confirmed fences and silent-peer fail-open are unchanged — promotion is withheld only against a peer that just proved itself alive, never against a silent one, so the fail-closed direction is preserved. The aborted takeover leaves an operator-visible `EventFence` record and the existing degraded status mark.

Closes #14158

daemon: refuse cross-origin redirects in HTTP RPM probes (#14178)

Why:

then followed endpoint-supplied Location headers to any origin —
CheckRedirect enforced only a hop cap. A configured endpoint (or a
plaintext-HTTP on-path actor) could redirect the probe GET, dialed
with the probe's source/interface/VRF-bound socket, to an internal
address, and an internal 2xx was scored as this probe's pass and
published via RPM transitions to ip-monitoring, suppressing WAN
failover for a path never measured.

target's origin (scheme, hostname, effective port equal to via[0])
via new sameOriginProbeURL/probeOriginPort helpers mirroring the
feeds same-origin rule; the 3-hop cap is unchanged. A refused hop
returns a plain error (never ErrUseLastResponse, which would score
the 3xx) and never renders the endpoint-supplied target. Scheme
equality also refuses https->http downgrades. NOT changed: initial
target admission (operator-configured internal targets stay
legitimate), transport/dialer binding, body drain. README updated.

and scheme-change refusals FAIL on base 805ac16cd (probe followed to
a 200 / dialed the new scheme) and PASS with the fix; same-origin

-count=1 PASS; go vet clean; gofmt clean.

CDN) now fail the probe instead of passing; operators must point the
RPM target at the final origin — the same posture as feeds (#9912)
and ddns (#6545) endpoint-chosen redirects.

## PR #14277 — snmp: pin pending-reservation bound refuting #14186 (not real) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14186-campaign`

## Verdict: claim NOT REAL at origin/master — regression pin only, no production change

**Strongest defect reading:** `allow()` runs pre-auth (`agent.go:957`, before BER/community/USM). When `globalTokens<1`, each distinct spoofed source enrolls `pendingSources++`, and admitted non-pending sources are shed while `globalTokens < pendingSources+1`. If `pendingSources` could reach ~4000, admitted managers would be locked out after refill.

**Strongest refutation (supported by source + executed decisive check):**
- `snmpServeGlobalBurst=4000`, rate 2000/s (`serve_budget_9917.go:45-46`) — not 64. Lockout after refill needs `pendingSources >= 4000`.
- `pendingSources` increments only for a tracked bucket (newcomer at `globalTokens<1`, or admitted `everExpensive` re-enrollment). `perSource` is capped at `snmpServeMaxSources=1024`; displacement decrements the victim's pending count. Invariant: `pendingSources <= len(perSource) <= 1024 < 4000`. No increment path exists without a tracked bucket.
- Pending expires after 1s quiet (`expireExpensiveLocked`); the scarce gate is surplus-work-conserving.

**Decisive check executed on unmodified origin/master (separate base worktree, fake clock):** admit cheap M → drain global → enroll 64/1023/1024 spoofed pendings (table fills: 1024 tracked, `pendingSources=1023`) → refill 2s to burst → **M admitted in every variant** (incl. expensive-M), pending newcomer also admitted. Sustained-refresh probe (1023 pendings retrying every 500ms × 20 rounds): pendings progressively admitted/cleared, M admitted 19/20 rounds (round-0 shed is genuine global scarcity, the intended #9917 backstop). The issue's own decisive check refutes the claim.

**Gate verdict:** NOT REAL. Unresolved check: none reachable — the only way `pendingSources` exceeds 4000 would require >1024 tracked buckets, which the table cap forbids.

## Change
- `pkg/snmp/serve_budget_14186_test.go`: `TestServeBudgetPendingReservationNoStarve14186` pins the decisive scenario and the `pendingSources+1 <= snmpServeGlobalBurst` bound so a future burst/table/pending change making lockout reachable fails loudly. Passes on master by design (refutation pin).
- `docs/log/14186.md`: full evidence.

No production change — altering the reservation would risk the #10113 onboarding guarantee.

Checks main agent should run: `GOCACHE=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-build go test ./pkg/snmp/ -count=1`

Closes #14186

## PR #14278 — cmdtree: placeholder names are not keywords (#14196) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14196-campaign`

## Defect

`resolveTreeWord` resolved every unique keyword prefix including `<placeholder>` keys, and `Canonicalize` marked a placeholder filled only on its unmatched-word arm. A surplus literal after a real value therefore re-resolved as a fake keyword:

```
deny="^ping 192.0.2.1$"  line="ping 192.0.2.1"    -> denied
deny="^ping 192.0.2.1$"  line="ping 192.0.2.1 <"  -> ALLOWED (pre-fix)
```

`ping 192.0.2.1 <` canonicalized to `ping 192.0.2.1 <host>` — a fake keyword in the string the login-class gate judges — while the handler's strict parser rejects the surplus word and executes the denied target. The anchored deny matched neither the polluted full form nor the keyword-only prefix (`ping`).

## Fix

`resolveTreeWord` (`pkg/cmdtree/tree.go`) now excludes placeholder keys from both its exact and unique-prefix arms (still reporting them as prefix matches, so ambiguity/absence reporting is unchanged). A literal angle-bracket word reaches the existing value-slot arms as operator data: consumed once, raw, while its slot is empty; refused once filled, so restricted classes fail closed. No special-casing of the reported input — the rule is a property of the resolver, covering every placeholder node (ping/traceroute `<host>`, `show route <destination>`, `show security log <count>`, …). Completion is unaffected: placeholder names are only offered as end-of-walk candidates and typed-leaf hints, never resolved from typed words. Audited all `resolveTreeWord`/`Canonicalize` consumers.

## Regression (RED on origin/master, GREEN with fix)

- `pkg/cmdtree` `TestPlaceholderNamesAreNotKeywords14196` + synthetic-tree twin: surplus literal spellings (`<`, `<host>`, `<h`) refused on Options, placeholder-with-children, and Options-placeholder arms; controls keep a literal in an empty slot raw and keep genuine keyword abbreviation.
- `pkg/cli` `TestAnchoredDenySurvivesLiteralPlaceholder14196`: decisive authorization fixture — anchored deny on the target-bearing command, bare positive control, negative controls, unanchored-rule control (matched even pre-fix).
- `pkg/cli` `TestPingTargetIdentityWithLiteralPlaceholder14196`: handler argument identity via `diagcmd.ParsePingOptions`.

## Verification

- `go test ./pkg/cmdtree/ ./pkg/cli/ ./pkg/api/ ./pkg/diagcmd/ -count=1` — green.
- `pkg/grpcapi`: 3 failures (`TestSetAnnotateRemainsVerbLedForConfigurationGate13554`, `TestGetGlobalStatsScreenDropDetailKeysAreCanonical`, `TestShowTextGolden`) reproduce identically on a pristine base worktree at origin/master — pre-existing, unrelated.

Log: `docs/log/14196.md`

Closes #14196

## PR #14282 — dhcprelay: validate relay ciaddr unicast against pending request (#14188) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14188-campaign`

dhcprelay: validate relay ciaddr unicast against pending request (#14188)

Why:
DHCPv4 relay `deliverReply` (pkg/dhcprelay/relay.go) in the flag-clear,
yiaddr==0, ciaddr!=0 row unicast the server reply via
`clientConn.WriteTo(replyData, ciaddr:68)` with no validation of ciaddr.
The #6562 pending binding keys only on xid+hlen+chaddr
(pkg/dhcprelay/pending.go `pendingKeyFor`), so a configured server — or a
source-spoofer who passes the #4163 allow-list and guesses the xid —
could put 127.0.0.1, 224.0.0.1, 255.255.255.255, 169.254.x, or an
unrelated off-LAN address in ciaddr and make the relay emit a crafted
DHCP payload to it from the SO_BINDTODEVICE client socket. The loopback /
VRF-wide reflection framing was refuted in research (the write is on the
device-bound clientConn, not the giaddr serverConn); the residual defect
is the unvalidated, unbound unicast destination itself.

What:
- pending.go: record the request ciaddr beside the v4 pending entry
  without adding it to `pendingKey` (a DISCOVER carries ciaddr 0 while
  its ACK may carry the leased address, so keying on it would break
  ordinary exchanges). New `insertPending` / `matchesPending` /
  `requestCiaddr` free functions (Go forbids methods on the instantiated
  `pendingTable` alias), `insertCiaddr` stamping the live entry and its
  owning ring slot, ciaddr carried through `snapshot`/`adopt`
  (`pushLockedCiaddr`) so a config reload does not lose it. Generic
  insert/matches discipline unchanged; v6 entries carry zero ciaddr.
- relay.go: client loop now `insertPending`; reply loop uses
  `matchesPending` and hands the recorded ciaddr to `deliverReply` via
  `interfaceRelay.pendingRequestCiaddr` (server-reply goroutine only).
  The ciaddr row now requires `ciaddr.IsGlobalUnicast()` (admits RFC1918,
  rejects loopback/multicast/broadcast/link-local/unspecified; Go's
  IsGlobalUnicast returns true for 192.0.2.9, so the pending equality is
  what rejects off-LAN) AND `ciaddrMatchesRequest` equality with the
  recorded request ciaddr. On failure: DROP fail-closed — no WriteTo, no
  broadcast fallback (broadcast would still deliver the payload on-LAN) —
  counted in new `RepliesDroppedBadCiaddr`, warn-once then Debug.
  Honest scope cut: no subnet/on-link check — the relay has no client
  subnet/mask (giaddr resolver discards masks, multi-subnet relaying is
  valid); pending equality already pins the destination to the address
  the client itself claimed in the bound request, strictly stronger.
- Stats/CLI: `RelayStats.RepliesDroppedBadCiaddr` wired through Stats()
  and `adoptCountersFrom`, rendered as `Dropped (bad-ciaddr)` in the
  `show services dhcp relay` #6562 section; byte-stable CLI test updated.
- Existing delivery-matrix / exactly-one-send tests and `armedRelay`
  set `pendingRequestCiaddr` from the packet (mirroring production's
  matchesPending handoff); counters-preservation test covers the new
  counter. NAK / broadcast-flag / always-broadcast / L2-yiaddr rows are
  untouched and still precede the ciaddr row.

Validation:

## PR #14283 — dhcprelay: bind DHCPv6 Relay-Reply to soliciting client (#14181) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14181-campaign`

Why: the client-facing :547 loop handed any Relay-Reply to the shared dispatcher, which routed by attacker-controlled Interface-ID to any interface; the pending key (xid/DUID/IA) never recorded which client address solicited, the outer PeerAddr could name loopback or a third party, and the inner type was unchecked, so a forged RECONFIGURE or a redirected Reply matching a pending tuple was delivered by the relay itself.

What: pending table gains a payload generic; the v6 entry records the soliciting client address + request type at Relay-Forw insert. Replies forward only when PeerAddr equals the recorded client and the inner type legitimately answers the recorded request (RECONFIGURE never); loopback peers rejected in decapsulation. Client-socket Relay-Replies may select only the receiving interface's own target (`dispatchFromClientSocket`, new `RepliesDroppedDispatcherLocal` stat); upstream dispatch unchanged. Legacy #10198 fixtures using a `::1` peer/Solicit inner now use the recorded link-local client with an Advertise inner.

Validation: base probe on 805ac16cd forwarded peer-mismatched and loopback replies (RED writes=1); 6 new `14181` tests pass; full `pkg/dhcprelay` suite passes; `go vet` clean. Race run fails only in pre-existing `TestDHCPv6ReplyDispatcherRoutesByInterfaceID10198` arm-vs-dispatch race, identical on clean base.

Risk: servers rewriting peer-address away from the soliciting client (or downstream chains, already refused) now drop; direct clients and link-local shared-socket return pinned by controls. Kernel `[::1]:546` delivery not live-tested — loopback peers are rejected before any write.

Closes #14181

 buildHeartbeat ranged peerGroups and echoed the first nonzero
 heartbeat session/sequence. handlePeerHeartbeat stamps every RG
 from one packet, but a transfer abort restore can put an older
 PeerGroupState back for one RG after newer heartbeats refreshed
 the others, leaving a mixed map. A transmit in that window could

## PR #14291 — configstore: encrypt commit-confirmed records under the guarded tree too (#14172) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14172-campaign`

Closes #14172

## Why

`confirmRecord` serializes the whole record (rollback target with its secret leaves, hashes, deadlines) but carries no guarded-tree field — the guarded tree reaches it only as `GuardedHash`. `encodeConfirm` keyed encryption off `rec.PrevTree` alone, so `commit confirmed` **adding** a master-password over a previous plaintext config wrote `confirm.json` in cleartext while `active.json` from the same commit was AES-GCM encrypted, and `ReadConfirm` discarded the `decrypted` flag so the exposure was silent (D8-05).

## What

- `crypto.go`: `confirmEncryptionCover`/`confirmEncryptionPRF` resolve the confirm profile from **both** trees (PrevTree profile wins when present, else the guarded cover, else plaintext); `encryptTreeJSON` split from `maybeEncryptTreeJSON`; `confirmNeedsEncryption` for the warn decision.
- `db.go`: `DB.writeConfirmCover` carries the guarded profile for arm writes (empty on tombstones/migrations/retries so they keep their armed profile; public `WriteConfirm` signature unchanged). `encodeConfirm` seals under the resolved profile. `ReadConfirm` retains `decrypted` and warns on plaintext records whose PrevTree declares a master-password (#4579 parity); legacy plaintext records stay **readable** for upgrade compat.
- `store_commit.go`: `commitConfirmedLocked` sets/clears the cover around the preflight/provisional/final confirm writes under `s.mu`.
- `store_persist.go`: recovery adds the guarded (active) tree as a second opinion for the unexpected-plaintext warning.
- README + `docs/log/14172.md` document both-tree keying and why an unkeyed hash/MAC alone is not a fix (root-owned 0600 file, key in same dir, no TPM/HSM sealing); tampered plaintext records stay contained by the existing `GuardedHash`/`PreviousHash`/`Resolved`/deadline checks.
- New regression tests in `confirm_encryption_guarded_14172_test.go`: guarded-adds-master-password raw bytes + round-trip, end-to-end `CommitConfirmed`, both-master profile preservation, ReadConfirm + recovery plaintext warnings, no-cover control, tamper containment.

## Validation

- 7 new tests pass on the fix head; 4 fail on a separate pristine origin/master worktree with only the cover lines stripped (the 3 controls pass, pinning preserved behaviour). Never git-stash.
- Targeted confirm/crypto suite and `go vet` pass. Full `pkg/configstore` suite shows only the pre-existing `TestPackedIPsecVPNRun*9088` failures, reproduced identically on pristine base (base-attributed, #14139).

## Risk

Nested re-arm over an encrypted config keeps the PrevTree profile, so pre-fix readers still open existing windows. Master-password removal keeps the record sealed under PrevTree and still decrypts via the self-describing envelope + `master.key`. Commit/boot-paced code only; no per-packet paths touched. Tolerant/strict fail-closed doctrines unchanged (warn-not-reject only for legacy plaintext compat).

## PR #14293 — daemon: accept OpenSSH key types, own .ssh by numeric id, fail closed on empty algorithm lists (#14111) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14111-campaign`

Closes #14111

## Why
Research D5-09 (three-way validated) found three SSH host-auth defects in `pkg/daemon/daemon_hostauth_apply.go`:
1. `validateAuthorizedSSHKeys` required an `ssh-` prefix, so a valid `ecdsa-sha2-nistp256 …` / `sk-*` key value (the full `"<type> <base64> <comment>"` string Junos operators store under any `ssh-*` leaf) was rejected at apply and **all** provisioning for that user was skipped.
2. The `.ssh` directory was chowned via external `chown -R -- <name>:<name>`, which fails for any account whose primary group is not eponymously named — stranding users outside a freshly created root-owned 0700 `.ssh` — while key installation continued under an already-claimed ownership marker.
3. `buildSSHDConfig` silently omitted a nonempty `KexAlgorithms`/`Ciphers`/`MACs` restriction when every token was filtered, reverting sshd to its built-in defaults on tolerant input.

## What
- Key validation: fail-closed allowlist of the OpenSSH `authorized_keys` key-type vocabulary (`ssh-*`, `ecdsa-sha2-nistp{256,384,521}`, `sk-*`, `*-cert-v01@openssh.com`) with a required base64 blob. Option-prefixed (`command="..."`), bare-blob, unknown-type, empty, and CR/LF values stay rejected (#10725 doctrine preserved).
- Directory ownership: `.ssh` is owned by the already-resolved numeric `(uid, gid)` via `os.Chown` behind the `chownSSHDir` test seam, directory-only (the key file keeps `fsatomic.WithOwner(uid,gid)`), and a chown failure aborts that user's key install with marker rollback instead of claiming convergence. Numeric operands subsume the #5005 `--` concern for this exec.
- Algorithm fallback: `buildSSHDConfigErr`/`filterSSHAlgorithmsErr` error when a nonempty list filters to empty; `applySSHConfig` returns the error **before** touching the drop-in (no write/removal/reload), leaving the prior restriction in force. Partial filtering still renders survivors (#4902). String-only `buildSSHDConfig` kept for pure render/compare callers.
- Tests: new `hostauth_ssh_14111_test.go` (decisive ecdsa provisioning check from the issue, vocabulary allowlist both directions, fail-closed apply with byte-identical prior drop-in, numeric ownership); #5026 and #4902 guards updated to the successor contracts; fake-uid isolate helper stubs the chown seam. Campaign log: `docs/log/14111.md`.

## Validation
- RED on pristine `origin/master` worktree (tests copied over): all six behavioral tests fail — ecdsa rejected (`must be a single-line ssh-* public key`), external chown argv recorded, `applySSHConfig` returns nil over all-invalid algorithms.
- GREEN here: new tests + targeted hostauth suites (`TestBuildSSHDConfig*`, `TestApplySSHConfig*`, `TestApplySystemLogin*`, `TestFirstCommit*`, `TestLogin*`, `TestRootAuth*`, belt tests) pass; `go vet ./pkg/daemon/` clean.
- Residual: full `pkg/daemon` run shows failures (e.g. `TestProducerDeltaConvertsToSyncedValue9752`) that reproduce identically on pristine `origin/master` — pre-existing, unrelated.

## Risk
Validation widens from `ssh-*` to the full OpenSSH vocabulary (still fail-closed); an all-invalid algorithm restriction now fails the apply instead of silently dropping to sshd defaults (prior drop-in stays in force); `.ssh` ownership moves from external name-based chown to in-process numeric chown with the same net ownership.

## PR #14307 — config: restore declared units of dotted lifelines (#14302) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-16)

Branch: `fix/14302-campaign`

## Why

#14192 registered every declared unit as an explicit `false` key in
`HostInboundLifelineSet`, but only re-marked the base key when a role
name matched a declared interface. For a dotted lifeline `hb.1`
(`control-interface hb.1`) whose only declared unit is 7, `hb.1.7`
stayed false: the cluster walk's naive-cut guard read `hb.1` as a unit
of bare parent `hb` while `SplitInterfaceUnitRef` resolves it
declared-name-first, so nothing restored the unit.
`HostInboundLifelineIngressNetdevs`, which enumerates only
declared-unit spellings, then yielded `[fxp0]` and the control link
lost its host-inbound ingress exception; the pinned userspace test
`TestHostInboundLifelineIngressNetdevsDoesNotAddUnitParent12848`
failed on master.

## What

In `HostInboundLifelineSet` (`pkg/config/lifeline.go`):

- A dotted role spelling that is itself a **declared interface**
  (`hb.1` declared with units `hb.1.<unit>`) is an interface identity,
  not a unit of a shorter parent, so its declared units are re-marked
  `true` with the base key.
- The cluster walk precomputes those dotted lifeline bases so
  `markBaseLifeline` does not re-demote them (VLAN-tagged or not), and
  the naive-cut prefix demotion is skipped for declared role
  spellings.

Preserved invariants:

- **#14192**: bare lifeline parents keep declared transit VLAN units
  ordinary (`ge-0/0/0.100` stays deny-scoped).
- **#13137**: a non-zero-unit role binding (`ge-0/0/1.100`) keeps its
  bare parent and unit 0 ordinary.
- **#12848**: dotted siblings (`hb.2`) and the bare prefix (`hb`) stay
  ordinary; the helper adds the unit netdev without the parent.

## Validation

- New `TestLifelineDottedDeclaredUnit14302`,
  `TestLifelineDottedDeclaredVLANUnit14302`,
  `TestLifelineDottedUnitControls14302` in `pkg/config` —
  fail-on-revert verified for the dotted re-mark.
- The previously failing userspace 12848 ingress test now passes;
  all `TestLifeline*`/`TestHostInbound*` suites in `pkg/config` and
  `pkg/dataplane/userspace` pass.
- Two unrelated failures (IPsec PSK gate; VRF-scope 6619 subtests)
  reproduce identically on pristine `origin/master` and are not
  affected by this change.

Branch: `fix/14303-campaign`

Why: #14228 taught the incremental SessionDelta producers to stamp pptp_call_ids from the live association table, and the HA import gate withholds any Pptp(handle) record whose pair is absent (pptp-call-ids-not-carried). The HA bulk export (snapshot_all_sessions_export, the full-resync Open deltas in afxdp/ha/export.rs) and the tunnel-remap purge Close delta (afxdp/ha/tunnel_purge.rs) both hardcoded pptp_call_ids: 0, so a PPTP session reaching the standby only via bulk export — after an event-stream reconnect or peer restart, precisely when incremental deltas were missed — was withheld: PPTP session loss on failover-after-resync (fail-closed, no aliasing).

What: carry the pair on the shared SyncedSessionEntry (new u64 field, 0/absent for non-PPTP). build_synced_session_entry stamps it from the verified wire pair at HA import; the local forward-flow publish (poll_descriptor), the forwarding-learn publish (local_delivery), and the shared-promote publish (promote) stamp it from the live table via pptp_call_ids_wire_for, matching the incremental producers. The bulk export and the tunnel purge stamp entry.pptp_call_ids instead of 0. Every other construction site (reverse companions, tunnel/TUN origins, seeds, fixtures) carries 0, which is never read. NOT changed: the Close wire frame (encodes no pair today; the purge delta now carries the value in process, symmetric with other Close producers) and the owner-RG worker export (already stamps via open_export_delta_with_provenance).

Full --bin xpf-userspace-dp suite: 8276 passed, 36 failed, 8 ignored; the 36 failures reproduce identically on clean origin/master 7df06b6eb (base-attributed). git diff --check clean.

Risk: one added u64 on an in-process shared entry; no wire, BPF ABI, or Go change. Non-PPTP sessions carry 0 exactly as before. A PPTP session whose pair this node never held still exports 0 and is still withheld — fail-closed preserved.

## PR #14452 — userspace-dp: reject ports on non-port-bearing application protocols (#14312) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14312-campaign`

userspace-dp: reject ports on non-port-bearing application protocols (#14312)

Why:
parse_applications rejected only the #3712 ICMP-field combos. A port
on any protocol other than TCP/UDP compiled into a wrong-behaving
term: an icmp/icmpv6 term with icmp_type had its ports silently
discarded by CompiledApplications::from_matches (a permit broadens
to every message of that type/code, arbitrary ICMP Echo IDs), and a
port-bearing term on gre/esp/ospf/sctp or any other portless
protocol became a dead range/exact term keyed on ports the packet
never presents, so a deny/reject never matched and fell through to
a later permit. Go strict commit (#3373) and ApplicationMatchDrops
(#9525) poison these before the wire, but a corrupt, hand-built,
mixed-version, or leniently peer-synced snapshot reached the Rust
helper with no mirror of the #3712 / #3723 fail-closed backstops.

What:
Add SnapshotIntegrityError::InvalidApplicationPortProtocol and
record the first offender in parse_applications when the parsed
source/destination ranges are non-empty and the resolved protocol
is neither TCP nor UDP (the ip_proto::has_l4_ports set, SCTP
included, numeric spellings caught via the resolved number).
parse_policy_state_with_counters rejects the whole snapshot after
the #3712 check, keeping the previous good state. The stale
from_matches "stray port is irrelevant" comment now states the
boundary reject. Nine regression tests cover icmp typed/untyped,
icmpv6 source-port, gre, esp, ospf range, sctp, and numeric GRE,
plus a guard that tcp/udp with ports and portless terms still
compile. docs/log/14312.md records the evidence.

Validation:
RED on base 5b122dda5 (separate base worktree, test patch applied
with the not-yet-existing variant mapped to the #3712 variant so it
compiles): 8 rejects tests failed with Ok(state), guard passed.
GREEN on lane: cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp --
rejects_whole_snapshot valid_port_protocol passed 17/17 including
neighbouring #3712 rejects; full policy::tests module passed
234/234.

Risk:
Fail-closed only on snapshots the Go producer never emits; normal
Go-lowered snapshots carry ports only on TCP/UDP, so no legitimate
config changes behaviour. Validation runs once per snapshot parse,
not per packet.

Closes #14312

## PR #14454 — userspace-dp: rebind session zone pair on cross-zone FIB reroute (#14318) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14318-campaign`

## Summary
Fixes #14318 (research-validated D2-09): `SessionTable::revalidate_forwarding_resolution` persisted only the new route, leaving forward `metadata.egress_zone` and reverse companion `metadata.ingress_zone` stale after a permitted cross-zone WAN failover (#11373/#12074) or egress re-zoning (#9384). Replies on the new egress were classified Foreign by `session_hit_authority` and dropped as `foreign_authority_drops` under normal lan→wan2 permit / wan2→lan deny policies.

New `rebind_forward_egress_zone` for zone-only rebinds.
- Threaded through `DeferredForwardingRevalidation.new_egress_zone`, both persist sites (poll_descriptor, session_glue), both reverse-hit permit arms, and the forward-hit Permit arm for #9384 re-zoning.
- `foreign_hit_verdict` direction deliberately unchanged (research lanes refuted that half; with zones fresh, legitimate replies are Owner).

## Tests
- RED on base (separate worktree): new-API test fails compile E0599.
- GREEN: 4 new tests (reroute rebind, None preserves zones, reverse-hit rebind, authority Owner-after-rebind + stale Foreign control).
- Related suites (session_hit_authority/policy_revalidation/fib_route): 59 passed. Pre-existing `c5_last_seen...` failure verified identical on pristine origin/master.

## PR #14456 — forwarding: admit NAT and anycast leak targets and continue past tunnel NoRoute (#14319) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14319-campaign`

Why:
Inter-VRF leaked return traffic to addresses owned only via
interface_nat_tables, or via an IPv6 subnet-router anycast, failed
the table_has_v[46]_route precheck, so the leak was skipped and the
traffic misrouted without a leak_incarnation stamp. A leak target
whose only route was a tunnel route also terminated the walk with
NoRoute when allow_tunnels was false, blackholing outer tunnel
endpoint resolution instead of falling through like a kernel
ip-rule miss.

What:
table_has_v4_route/table_has_v6_route take allow_tunnels, admit
interface_nat_tables_v4/v6 and (v6) subnet-router-anycast ownership,
and ignore all-tunnel route entries and tunnel connected rows when
tunnels are forbidden. The v4/v6 leak loops pass allow_tunnels into
the precheck and continue to the next leak / source-table LPM when
the recursive target lookup returns NoRoute; every other disposition

## PR #14457 — userspace-dp: scope Stage-11 IPsec claim to effective table (#14314) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14314-campaign`

Why:
Stage-11 (`stage_ipsec_passthrough_check`) re-derived its local-ownership table from the raw physical ingress ifindex, ignoring `flow.forward_key.routing_domain`, the validated fabric scope, and input-filter PBR `RouteOverride::Table`. Transit ESP/AH/IKE steered by PBR into a tenant VRF (or arriving on `fab0` for a tenant VRF) whose dst IP is owned by `inet.0` was falsely claimed for XFRM and reinjected into `xpf-usp1`, bypassing the tenant VRF's transit zone policy; host-bound IPsec steered into a tenant VRF was missed. The caller evaluated `ingress_route_table_override` only after the claim and honoured only its `Drop` arm.

What:
- `poll_stages.rs`: `stage_ipsec_passthrough_check` gains `route_override_table` and adjudicates `owns_ipsec_local_destination_in_table` in the EFFECTIVE table: PBR `Table` steer, then the flow's stamped routing domain via `install_tables`, then the validated V2 fabric scope's canonical table, then the ingress interface's table. A nonzero domain with no registry row returns `NotClaimed` (fail-closed, mirroring `NativeRouteTable::Unresolvable`).
- `poll_descriptor/mod.rs`: resolve `ingress_route_table_override_uncounted` BEFORE the claim for IPsec candidates only; `Drop` recycles, `Table` scopes the claim. The counted evaluation still runs exactly once (claimed arm or ordinary miss path), so no PBR term double-counts and `reject` replies are preserved.
- `poll_stages_tests.rs`: decisive regression `stage_ipsec_claim_follows_effective_table_14314` (`10.0.61.1` in `inet.0` vs `172.16.80.8` in `vrf_blue` under PBR Table, flow domain, and validated fabric scope, plus fail-closed orphan domain); #14124 cross-VRF seed cell restamped with the tenant's real install domain.
- NOT changed: host-inbound IKE gating, exchange-key scope, DNAT-to-self, fine lo0/junos-host gates.

Validation:
- GREEN: `cargo +1.98.1 test --release --bins -- ipsec` → 150 passed, 0 failed; `stage_ipsec` → 10 passed (incl. new 14314 regression and updated 14124 cells).
- RED: separate base worktree at origin/master `5b122dda5` with tests-only patch → `stage_ipsec_claim_follows_effective_table_14314` fails at `poll_stages_tests.rs:4444` ("PBR Table(vrf_blue) must not claim an inet.0-owned dst") — pre-fix returned `Passthrough`.
- Full `--bins` suite not run to completion in-lane (900s timeout under parallel build); parent should run it on the final head.

Risk:
A legitimate IPsec flow whose stamped domain lacks an install-table row now takes ordinary forwarding/policy instead of XFRM reinjection — fail-closed, consistent with #10312 native route resolution. Non-IPsec traffic pays no new work.

Closes #14314

Crate-internal `pub(crate)` signature change, all callsites migrated; checks are 0 (fail-open unknown) for unmapped zone ids, preserving the #10620 fence contract. BPF conntrack values carry no zone-check fields, so no BPF restamp is needed. Campaign log: `docs/log/14320.md`.

Branch: `fix/14316-campaign`

Why:
Post-#14123, the V4ToV6 NAT64 ICMP-error arm returned
policy_src_ip: None, so the queued gate's PROTO_ICMP arm was dead
for that producer and IPv4 source/protocol-icmp denies were judged
against the Pref64-mapped ICMPv6 identity. The V6ToV4 arm forced
PROTO_ICMPV6 while reading type/code from the already-translated
frame, so icmpv6 icmp-type terms compared against RFC 7915
ICMPv4 numbers and misfired in both directions.

as policy_icmp; V4ToV6 also carries the original v4 sender.

and evaluates it ahead of the translated frame's pair, keeping
the deny event on the wire identity. poll_descriptor/mod.rs
forwards it at both queued call sites. Unreadable originals
refund the F-077 token and drop, fail-closed. NOT changed:
rule_l3_matches gains no (V4,V6) arm; wire frames byte-identical.

pol14316_v6tov4_icmpv6_type_uses_original FAIL on pristine
5b122dda5 (tests only) and pass with the fix. Rebased onto
9f6630039: both pass; tests_embedded_poll_filter 111 passed,
1 failed (stage11_local_ike 13637, reproduces on pristine
9f6630039, base-attributed). Full bin suite pre-rebase:
8280 passed, 37 failed, all base-attributed by sampling.

Policy-visible identity for V4ToV6 NAT64 errors changes from the
Pref64-mapped source/ICMPv6 to the original v4 sender/ICMP/
original type-code; rules written only against the mapped source

## PR #14461 — userspace-dp: partition fragment overlap and association quotas by ingress zone (#14321) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14321-campaign`

Why: OverlapTracker keyed membership and its 32-entry reserve on the routing domain alone, so a spoofed fragment in an untrusted zone merged into a trusted zone's datagram entry and four senders in one zone could hold the whole domain reserve, refusing new fragmented datagrams in every other zone sharing the VRF. FragAssoc similarly let admitted sessions from one zone consume the whole 64-entry shard.

What: Add `ingress_zone` to `OverlapKey` and `overlap_same_datagram`, and partition the reserve by `(routing_domain, ingress_zone)` as `OVERLAP_CAP_PER_ZONE_PER_SHARD` (old domain constant kept as alias); completed-anchor reclaim scoped to the same zone, incomplete anchors never evicted, 64/shard aggregate cap unchanged. Callers stamp the zone via `frag_ingress_zone` (the `frag_ingress_authority` resolution) in `poll_descriptor` and the neighbor-retry path; parse leaves 0 and `translated_overlap_key` inherits the arrival zone. `FragAssoc` gains `FRAG_CAP_PER_ZONE_PER_SHARD` keyed on (authority zone, routing_table) with prune-before-refuse. New cross-zone tests in `fragment_overlap` and `nat64_tests`; two one-zone shard-fill tests now fill from two zones. NOT changed: sender quota, TTLs, range geometry, shard hashing.

Validation: Base-adapted RED (zone-blind encoding of the same tests) on a pristine base worktree failed both new tests (ShardFull starvation; cross-zone poison). Head: `cargo test --bins cross_zone` (2 passed), `fragment_overlap` (41 passed), `frag_assoc` (35 passed), `f035`/`9950` (9/28 passed). Full `--bins` suite shows the same pre-existing parallel flake sets on base and head (43 common failures; no overlap/frag-assoc failure on head) — see `docs/log/14321.md`.

Risk: Fragments of one datagram arriving in different zones now track separately (deliberate: cross-zone aliasing was the defect); same-zone fragments are unaffected. Single-zone deployments see identical quotas (zone 0 reserve is the old domain reserve when one zone uses a VRF).

Closes #14321

## PR #14462 — userspace: reflect zone-quarantine scrub in policy fingerprints and stable-key maps (#14330) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14330-campaign`

Closes #14330

## Problem
`PolicyResolvedFingerprints` / `PolicyResolvedIdentityStrippedFingerprints` hashed the raw `buildPolicySnapshotsWithAddressBook` output, and `PolicyIDsByStableKey` / `PoliciesByStableKey` (via `walkPolicyRuleSlots`) emitted every global policy — none applied the `scrubPoliciesForQuarantinedZones` step the publish path runs via `quarantineCollidingZones` / `policySnapshotAfterZoneQuarantine`. A commit whose only enforcement change was a zone becoming quarantined (StableZoneID collision `z174`/`z214`, or a poisoned `DroppedEnforcementChild` zone) produced identical fingerprints/ID maps while the published snapshot dropped or narrowed the rule, so `daemon_policy_invalidate` never flagged live sessions for policy-rematch re-evaluation.

## Fix
- Both fingerprint functions now run `policySnapshotAfterZoneQuarantine(cfg, rules)` before hashing (the same SSOT `policies_reject.go` uses). Partial quarantine prunes the scope → digest changes, key retained; sole-zone quarantine drops the rule → key removed.
- `walkPolicyRuleSlots` skips a global policy whose `Match.FromZones`/`Match.ToZones` is fully quarantined, using `quarantinedZoneNamesForConfig` (collision losers + poisoned zones; reserved sentinels excluded so defined-`any`/`junos-host` handling stays with its own poison paths). Skipped globals consume no slot/cap and vanish from `PolicyIDsByStableKey`/`PoliciesByStableKey`/`RuntimePolicyIDs`, and published `PolicyID`s now agree with the post-quarantine snapshot — extending the #13168 zone-pair invariant to globals. Partially quarantined globals keep slot/ID; narrowing is signalled via the fingerprint change.

## Tests
New `TestPolicyResolvedFingerprintsReflectZoneQuarantineScrub` in `pkg/dataplane/userspace/policies_resolved_fingerprint_test.go` (4 subtests, each with a `buildSnapshot` positive control that the publish path really drops/prunes):
- RED on pristine origin/master and on the fix worktree pre-fix (3 subtests fail: partial-quarantine fingerprint unchanged, sole-zone collision key retained, poisoned sole-zone key retained).
- GREEN after the fix.
- Nearby suites pass: quarantine/scoped-global/walk/fingerprint tests in `pkg/dataplane/userspace`, `TestPolicy|TestChangedPolicy|TestDeletedPolicy` in `pkg/daemon`; `go vet` and `gofmt` clean.
- Full `pkg/dataplane/userspace` suite fails only on pre-existing `TestSecureTunnelOwnership*` / `TestPartialRepublishRefusesQuarantineOnlySkew12247`, reproduced identically on pristine master.

See `docs/log/14330.md` for the full RED/GREEN record.

## PR #14464 — userspace: inherit collapsing unit .0 routing domain on base row (#14331) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14331-campaign`

Closes #14331

## Defect
`buildInterfaceSnapshotsFrom` emitted a base row resolving RoutingInstance/RoutingDomain from the bare interface key. For an untagged unit `.0` (which collapses onto the base netdev — same ifindex, same live kernel addresses), per-unit VRF membership (`routing-instances vrf1 interface ge-0/0/1.0`) left the bare key unclaimed, so the base row carried Domain 0 while republishing the VRF unit's addresses: VRF locals leaked into Domain:0 in `buildLocalAddressEntriesWithExclusions`, and `localAddressRoutingDomain` rejected the shared ifindex as ambiguous, deleting its ingress-domain entry.

## Fix
When unit `.0` collapses onto the base netdev and the bare key has no explicit/quarantined claim, the base row inherits unit `.0`'s RoutingInstance and RoutingDomain via the same `routingDomainForInterfaceKey` resolution (quarantine sentinel preserved). VLAN/tunnel unit `.0` on its own netdev is untouched; fail-closed ambiguity handling is unchanged.

## Regression
`TestBuildSnapshotUntaggedVRFUnitDoesNotConflictWithBaseRowDomain` builds via `buildSnapshot(cfg)`, asserts base/unit domain agreement, `localAddressRoutingDomain == (vrf1 domain, true)`, and no Domain:0 local entries. RED on origin/master (`base RoutingDomain = 0, want 748221`), GREEN with fix. Full package failure set identical to pristine base (pre-existing failures only). See docs/log/14331.md.

During any degraded window, `is_degraded_local_or_control` returned `true` from an unconditional `destination_is_local` arm before the #10651 native-GRE arm. - `userspace-xdp/src/gre_classify.rs`: new host-executable `degraded_general_local_pass_applies(is_native_gre, destination_is_local)` = `destination_is_local && !is_native_gre`, in the existing core-only module so the host test runs the real decision rather than a source model.
- `userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs`: gate the degraded general local pass through the new predicate; native-GRE frames fall through to the typed #10651 inner gate, reusing one `native_gre` computation. Only inner PASS_TO_KERNEL with a local outer passes to the kernel.

- RED on pristine origin/master: fails to compile (E0432, predicate absent). GREEN with the fix.
- Shim suites: 8 passed (gre_classify incl. pre-existing #10651 truth table, degraded_ndp, wg_classify). Go manifest gate `TestUserspaceXDPShim`: ok.
- Pre-existing failure `local_origin_tunnel_ipv6_nonfirst_fragment_transmits_without_session_14119` fails identically on pristine origin/master (verified in a clean base worktree; base-attributed, unrelated).

## PR #14466 — userspace-dp: resolve WG kernel-path locality in the tunnel routing domain (#14328) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14328-campaign`

Closes #14328

## Defect
`ShimMapsKernelPathView::destination_is_local` resolved the routing domain for the INNER plaintext destination from the OUTER UDP socket's pktinfo `ingress_ifindex` (`userspace_ingress_domains[outer]`) and returned `false` for `None`. When the underlay and `wgN` live in different routing instances (or pktinfo is unavailable), host-inbound over WireGuard was falsely dropped as `rx_degraded_transit_drops`; conversely transit coinciding with an underlay-local address read as local.

## Fix
- `destination_is_local(dst, tunnel_logical_ifindex)` now takes the `wgN` logical ifindex (`spawned_logical_ifindex`, passed by `dispatch_inbound`; also stored on the view at spawn). Coverage (`ingress`) still uses the outer ifindex — the two questions are keyed on different interfaces, documented in the module header.
- New `tunnel_routing_domain` helper: an `ingress_domains` row for the tunnel's own ifindex wins when present; otherwise the runtime forwarding state's `synced_routing_domain_in` answers (the tunnel row's `routing_domain`). Production tunnel rows are absent from `ingress_domains` (Go excludes tunnels from the adjudicated set), so the forwarding state is the production authority; the map precedence lets the test seam state a tunnel domain. Local maps are queried under the tunnel domain only; fail-closed preserved (non-positive/unresolvable/unreadable -> transit). No test-input special-casing.

## Regression
- `locality_uses_tunnel_domain_not_outer_ingress_14328` — the issue's decisive shape: outer ifindex 10/domain 1, wg0 ifindex 20/domain 2, `2001:db8::1` local only in domain 2; asserts local under the tunnel key (incl. Unknown/no-pktinfo delivering), non-local for outer-domain-only and transit addresses, fail-closed for unplaceable tunnel.
- `tunnel_routing_domain_resolution_14328` — resolver precedence + single-instance domain-0 contract.

## Validation
- RED on base worktree (`origin/master` 1ea1f8713, test adapted to old signature): FAILED as expected.
- GREEN: `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp _14328` — 2 passed. Adjacent: `kernel_path` 9 passed, `9594` 10 passed, `wg_` 199 passed / 2 failed (`wireguard_segmentation_*`, failing identically on pristine base — pre-existing).
- Log: `docs/log/14328.md`.
