## PR #14470 — wg: select same-port tunnel endpoint by destination IP and ingress zone (#14326) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14326-campaign`

Closes #14326

## Problem
`wg_endpoint_for_listen_port` (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/wg/decap.rs`) selected the first `wg_engines` HashMap entry matching only `(wg_listen_port, transport_instance)` — it took no `dst_ip`. `wg_outer_zone_matches` compared only the zones of `dst_ip` and `endpoint.source`, never `endpoint.source == dst_ip`, and `tunnel_endpoints.get(id)?` inside the loop aborted the whole lookup when one engine lacked an endpoint row. Two WG tunnels sharing a listen port in one transport instance on different local IPs therefore selected non-deterministically: wrong engine → AEAD failure (fail-closed decap loss), wrong `logical_ifindex` attempted, `is_wg_listener_tuple` exemption misses.

## Fix
- `wg_endpoint_for_listen_port` takes `dst_ip: IpAddr`; a candidate must match port, WireGuard mode, transport instance, `endpoint.source == dst_ip` (same address family; unspecified allowed and then failed closed by the zone check), and `wg_outer_zone_matches(forwarding, endpoint, ingress_ifindex, dst_ip)`. Missing endpoint rows are skipped with `continue` instead of `?`-aborting the scan.
- `wg_outer_zone_matches` gains the same-family `endpoint.source == dst_ip` equality.
- Cross-family sources are deliberately not an equality gate: a v4-bound listener serving mapped-v6 arrivals (#10686) is still admitted on the v6 destination's owner zone, exactly as before (pinned by `mapped_ipv6_wg_underlay_candidate_stays_outside_inner_ingress_gate_10686`, which caught an earlier stricter draft of this fix).
- Callers: `is_wg_listener_tuple` passes its `dst_ip`; `is_wg_underlay_frame` parses the v6 destination before the lookup; `try_wg_decap_from_frame_with_input_filter` resolves `outer_destination_ip` before selection. The explicit zone gate at the AEAD boundary is kept.

## Tests
- New: `wg_same_port_multi_tunnel_selects_exact_dst_ip_14326` — two tunnels (ids 1/2, logical ifindexes 400/401, sources 172.16.80.8/.9, port 51820, same WAN zone/instance, independent established engine pairs): listener tuple recognised for both destinations, each tunnel's record decaps under its own logical ifindex, cross-addressed record fails closed.
- New: `wg_same_port_lookup_skips_engine_without_endpoint_14326` — orphan engine row (no endpoint) must not abort the lookup.
- RED on origin/master (test only): both failed ("record for tunnel B at IP_B must decap via engine B"; "orphan engine row must not abort"). GREEN with fix: 2 passed.
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp decap`: 151 passed, 2 failed (`gre_tun_origin_*`, `ha_inactive`) — identical on pristine origin/master base worktree (149 passed, same 2), pre-existing. `cargo test wg_`: 199 passed, 2 `wireguard_segmentation_*` failures also identical on base.
- `cargo fmt` intentionally not run crate-wide (tree is not rustfmt-clean under the installed toolchain; ~500 unrelated files churn). Only the two touched files were formatted, with pre-existing churn in `decap_tests.rs` stripped.

Full log: `docs/log/14326.md`.

## PR #14473 — userspace-dp: charge SYN-cookie sketch only on failed MACs (#14324) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14324-campaign`

Why: #13952 placed syn_cookie_ack_attempt_limited before
ring.validates(), charging valid and invalid ACKs pre-MAC at 16/s per
(src,dst,dport). Sixteen spoofed ACKs/s from a victim source starve
that victim's legitimate cookie ACK, and NATed clients behind one IP
to one service share 16 conn/s, defeating the #13700 invariant that
valid cookies never consume the failed-attempt budget.

What: validate the cookie first in
validate_syn_cookie_ack_on_session_miss; return Validated without
touching the sketch. Only failed MACs charge the per-key sketch:
active arm reports ActiveBudgetExceeded when per-key or zone-wide
budget is spent (fail-closed preserved), standby charges the sketch
and stays fail-open NotApplicable. Sketch, rate, and lifecycle are
unchanged; comments and the constant name now say failed attempts.
Rewrite the two #13952 brute-force tests to the post-MAC contract and
add spoofed-starvation and NAT regressions. NOT changed: MAC strength,
verdict enum, zone-wide budgets, sketch sizing.

Validation: RED on base db3cdaebb with only the new tests added: both
syn_cookie_spoofed_failures_do_not_starve_valid_ack_14324 and
syn_cookie_nat_valid_acks_not_throttled_14324 failed with
ActiveBudgetExceeded vs Validated (NAT at the 257th ACK; test build
raises the limit to 256/s, production is 16/s). GREEN on lane:
syn_cookie_ 122 passed, screen:: 340 passed.

Risk: plausible-epoch invalid ACKs now pay one SipHash before any
per-key refusal (the issue's accepted tradeoff; comparable to the
sketch hash, verdicts still bounded by the zone-wide budgets). The
sketch bounds failed attempts per key, not candidate MAC checks;
brute force was never blocked from guessing, only from starving
valid cookies, which this restores.

Closes #14324

## PR #14474 — policymatch: scope feed-publication debt per rule and fail excluded-empty feeds closed on omitted IPs (#14337) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

What: Evaluate scheduler then application before addresses in ruleMatchesWithMemo, and scope consulted debt per address side via child memos (shared resolved-prefix cache) that commit only when decisive — the failing side's own debt, or both sides on a match; apply the same scoping to the fragment skipped-deny L3 probe. Resolve tokens for excluded sides when the query IP is omitted so the both-families-empty gate fails closed and debt is recorded, while non-excluded sides keep unspecified-tuple semantics. Treat a declared DynamicAddress AddressBinding as a book name in isBookName and unqualify zone-local names before overlay/binding/debt lookups, mirroring the snapshot builder.

Validation: New feed_publication_debt_scope_14337_test.go — RED on clean origin/master (app-mismatch over-taint, nil-IP fail-open, absent-overlay isBookName, nil-IP debt recording fail; source-mismatch/matching-rule/junos-host controls pass), GREEN with the fix. Risk: Simulator-only (match-policies/test policy/REST/gRPC/daemon reauth verdicts); no dataplane enforcement change. Fail-closed direction preserved: a matching rule or a debt-bearing deciding side still reports indeterminate debt, and excluded-empty still fails closed. Rule evaluation order changed to app-first, which is verdict-neutral except for debt accounting and matches the fix direction in #14337.

## PR #14479 — userspace-dp: reject duplicated IPv6 Fragment headers in screen extraction (#14325) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14325-campaign`

## Summary

The #14129 sticky-fragment downgrade in `extract_screen_info` left an
inconsistent fragment state for a chained IPv6
`[Frag#1(offset=0, M=1), Frag#2(offset=65528, M=1)]` packet: the second
non-ATOMIC sighting only cleared `is_first_fragment`, while
`ip_frag_off`/`frag_data_off` kept Frag#1's values (offset 0).
`check_tcp_flag_screens` skips on `!is_first_fragment` and
`check_ping_of_death`/`check_teardrop` require
`(ip_frag_off & 0xFFF8) > 0`, so the packet evaded **both** screen
families.

## Fix

- `userspace-dp/src/screen/extract.rs`: a second non-ATOMIC Fragment
  sighting now returns
  `Err(ScreenParseError::MultipleIpv6FragmentHeaders)`. Reachable
  duplicates (`[first][non-first]`, `[first][first]`) fail closed; a
  lone ATOMIC followed by a real header is still governed by the real
  header (#10661), ATOMIC second sightings stay ignored (#14129), and
  `[non-first][*]` is unreachable as a chain (the walk breaks at the
  first non-first header). RFC 8200 allows each extension header at
  most once and receivers key reassembly on the first header, so there
  is no sizing semantics to preserve between two non-ATOMIC headers.
- `userspace-dp/src/screen/packet.rs`: new
  `ScreenParseError::MultipleIpv6FragmentHeaders` variant mapping to
  the existing `ip-malformed` reason — every `extract_screen_info`
  caller already drops parse errors fail-closed, so no caller change.

## Tests

- `screen/tests_14129_chained_frag.rs`: the issue's decisive
  `[Frag#1(0,M=1), Frag#2(65528,M=1), 4 bytes]` shape with
  single-header teardrop/ping-of-death controls, a hand-reconstructed
  pre-fix `ScreenPacketInfo` proving both sizing screens pass it, a
  duplicated-first case, a reachable-orderings matrix, and an
  `[ATOMIC][real-non-first]` guard that still parses and drops via
  teardrop.
- `afxdp/frame/tests_10661_atomic_chain.rs`: the
  `[real-first][real-non-first]` cell now asserts the screen leg
  rejects (tracker/forwarding/shim legs unchanged).

RED: on pristine `1ea1f8713` the three new tests and the updated 10661
cell failed (pre-fix parse: `ip_frag_off=1, is_first_fragment=false`).
GREEN: targeted run 18 passed; `screen::` suite 342 passed; full
`--bins` 8305 passed with the same 42 pre-existing failures as
pristine master.

Full write-up: `docs/log/14325.md`.

## PR #14486 — config: keep all bracketed child-block address-set members (#14345) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14345-campaign`

## Summary

`addressSetMemberValues` iterated `member.Keys[1:]` on the inline branch but appended only `vn.Keys[0]` for each child node, so a bracketed child block such as `address { [ a1 a2 ]; }` inside an `address-set` compiled to just `[a1]` with 0 errors and 0 warnings on strict `CompileConfig`. ## PR #14487 — config: retain junos-host terminal deny for empty permit programs (#14349) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14349-campaign`

## Summary
`junosHostProjectProgram` drove the #11065 terminal deny from whether a permit emitted a `JunosHostReturn`. A sole permit skipped on tolerant load (#12040) or with an empty cross-family intersection (v4 source × v6-only application) emits no return in either family, so the projection returned `Representable=true` with no rules, the userspace wrapper dropped the empty program, and coarse host-inbound alone decided for all IPv4/IPv6 host-bound traffic.

Track `hasAuthoredPermit` for every permit term in `junosHostProjectProgram` (before the `skipPermit` continue and before `junosHostBuildRule`) and drive the terminal deny from it. Per-family `done` flags from a match-all permit still suppress that family's terminal.

RED on base (all three defect cells empty), GREEN with the fix.
- Updated `junosHost9572AssertSSHDrop` to accept exactly the trailing terminal deny a skipped authored permit now leaves after a following deny (fail-closed, authored deny-by-default semantics).
- `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestJunosHost|TestHostInbound'` passes; `go vet ./pkg/config/` clean. The `pkg/dataplane/userspace` `TestJunosHostIngressScopeCoverage6619` VRF failures reproduce identically on pristine `origin/master` and are base-attributed/unrelated.

fallback for a promoted standby; installClusterSyncedV4/V6 restores/records

preserve=false namespace reset evict; preserve=true reclaim retains.

TestInstallTableProducerToResendEndToEnd9752 (PptpCallIDs golden drift,

## PR #14496 — frr: resolve defined policy-statement before bare protocol token in IGP export (#14369) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14369-campaign`

frr: resolve defined policy-statement before bare protocol token in IGP export (#14369)

## Why

`redistributeEntriesAt` took the bare-protocol branch (`knownRedistProtocol`) before the defined-policy-statement branch, so `protocols ospf export static` with a policy-statement named `static` rendered a bare, unfiltered `redistribute static` and the policy's route-map was dead — a silent filter bypass on redistribution into OSPF/OSPFv3/RIP/IS-IS, inconsistent with the BGP renderer in the same package which resolves defined policies first.

## What

- Reorder `redistributeEntriesAt` (`pkg/frr/redistribute.go`) to check the defined-policy-statement branch first on the raw export name (before `direct`→`connected` normalization, so a policy named `direct` is honored), falling through to the bare-protocol branch (self-drop and family-fit unchanged) only when no such policy exists. All four IGP redistributors funnel through this function, so OSPF/OSPFv3/RIP/IS-IS are fixed by the one reorder; BGP is untouched (already policy-first).
- Thread the resolved-as-policy bit from `redistributeEntries` into `applyQNHMetricRouteMap11447` so a defined policy named `static` uses the policy QNH map (`policyMaps[export]`) instead of clobbering its route-map with the bare-protocol `staticMap`.
- Add `pkg/frr/redistribute_policy_precedence_test.go`: OSPF/RIP/IS-IS fixtures (policy named `static`, reject term `from protocol static`), the no-policy negative, a policy named `direct`, and the QNH policy-arm cell.

## Validation

- New tests FAIL on `origin/master` (bare `redistribute static` / bare IS-IS lines rendered, filter discarded) and PASS after the fix.
- Targeted neighbours pass: `TestGenerateProtocols`, `TestRedist`, `TestISIS`, `TestOSPFRedistribute`, `TestQNH`, `TestBGPExport`, `TestRedistProtocol`; `go vet ./pkg/frr/` clean.
- Full `pkg/frr` suite: only three pre-existing environmental failures (`TestFamilylessIPv6NeighborWithoutPolicyIsV6Only11564`, `TestFRRLoadInet6OnlyNeighborIPv4Deactivation11374`, `TestFRRLoadBGPClasslessRIBSuppression11426` — FRR binary harness `privs_init: could not setgroups`), also failing on the unmodified base.

## Risk

A policy named as a protocol keyword with no `from protocol` term now skip-and-warns instead of rendering a bare redistribute — the documented policy-branch outcome, matching BGP's reading. Bare-token rendering with no such policy defined is byte-identical.

Closes #14369

On a VLAN trunk, an unzoned, quarantined, or admin-disabled unit 0 (or a disabled native-VLAN unit) stripped USERSPACE_INGRESS_IFACE_FLAG_TAGGED_ONLY from the trunk parent. Rust also prunes (parent,0) keys and native egress marks whose sole owner is disabled/unzoned on tagged-only parents. Pre-existing owner fixtures now carry their zone. NOT changed: XDP shim, adjudication, duplicate-key rejection, ambiguous-native rules.

## PR #14499 — cluster: cross-clean scoped and bare generation tables (#14358) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14358-campaign`

Why:
#10512 stamped scoped generation entries on every install but only reclaimed them on scoped policy deletes. Normal closes leaked genSentScoped/recvGenScoped live entries to cap, and a scoped policy delete never tombstoned the bare receiver space, so a delayed same-generation install could resurrect a revoked session on the HA standby once the scoped tombstone was evicted.

## PR #14500 — appid: keep dropped-constraint applications inert in catalog and tuple fallback (#14355) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14355-campaign`

Closes #14355

## Defect
On the tolerant load path, an application with a dropped match constraint (value-less `destination-port;`, malformed `icmp-type bogus`, unimplemented RPC/UUID leaf) compiles to `DestinationPort==""` / `ICMPType==nil`. `BuildCatalog` emitted a protocol-wide `(0,0)` CatalogEntry for it and the AppID-disabled tuple fallback stamped every TCP/UDP/ICMP session with its name — contradicting the #9525 contract that a leniently-loaded bad app is inert. The tuple fallback also rejected port 0 inside a valid explicit `0-N` range that the strict gate and catalog accept, and `ProtocolNumber` did not resolve the hyphenated `icmp-v6` spelling accepted elsewhere.

## Fix
- `config.ApplicationMatchWidened` (new): the widening subset of `ApplicationMatchDrops` — only drops that lost a constraint. Never-matching retained constraints (port/icmp on a protocol that cannot satisfy it) are excluded, so `protocol 0 destination-port 80` keeps its faithful #4008 catalog row.
- `BuildCatalog`: widened app is unemittable (no row, no AppNames name; name-derived id still consumed). `compileApplications` gates AppNames identically (byte-identical parity, pinned by new `TestAppCatalogParityOnDroppedConstraintApps14355`). Tuple fallback `consider` skips widened apps.
- `portInSpec`: range endpoints via new `canonicalRangePort` (0..65535, mirroring strict `validatePortSpec`) + `NormalizeExplicitPortRange` sentinel rejection; bare ports still 1..65535 (`0`, `0-0`, `+80`, `70000` never match).
- `ProtocolNumber`: `icmp-v6` → 58, mirrored in `filterProtocolResolvable`/`protocolIsICMPFamily`, `validateProtocol`, `normalizeProtocol`, userspace canonicalization (→ `icmpv6`), and Rust `proto_number`/`parse_protocol` + filter mirror test list.

## Regression
`TestAppIDSkipsDroppedConstraintAppsAndSupportsZeroRangeAndICMPv6` (`pkg/appid/catalog_dropped_14355_test.go`; the issue-named `catalog_test.go` does not exist): RED on master (`broken-tcp shipped 1 catalog row [{Protocol:6 DstPortLow:0 DstPortHigh:0}]`), GREEN with fix. Covers direct fixtures + end-to-end `CompileConfigLenient`, catalog/AppNames/fallback, 0-N parity, icmp-v6.

## Verification (targeted; full suites exceed job cap here)
- `go test ./pkg/appid/ -count=1` PASS
- `go test ./pkg/dataplane/ -run TestAppCatalog` PASS
- `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestApplicationMatchWidened14355|TestFilterProtocolNamedSetMatchesRustMirror|TestApplicationReferenceMatchDrops|TestPredefinedApplicationsCarryNoMatchDrops|TestFilterProtocolResolvable'` PASS
- `go vet` + `go build ./...` clean
- Pre-existing unrelated failures in full config/dataplane suites (#14139 PSK, manifest/method-count canaries) untouched. Main agent: please run full `./pkg/config/ ./pkg/dataplane/ ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/` and `cargo test filter_protocol_accept_set_subset_of_resolver`.

Log: `docs/log/14355.md`

Branch: `fix/14371-campaign`

Why: isPeerRemote compared the remote IP against peerIPOf, which parses

lookup storing all v4+v6 answers, unmapped. isPeerRemote consults the
cache (literal fallback for zero-value SessionSync). Unresolvable
hostnames keep non-peer treatment plus a loud warning naming the
address; construction never panics. NOT changed: cap math
(8 cap / 2 reserve), outbound bypass, finishSetup/closeSetupConns,
notePreAuthRejected, shouldInitiateFabricDial, and no commit-time
hostname rejection (hostname configs stay valid — spec option (a),
not (b)).

(F-DR3-H4-2: no panic, non-peer treatment, exactly one

reserved slot under flood". GREEN post-fix; existing
TestPreAuthAdmissionCapReservesPeerSlot and
TestPreAuthOutboundBypassesCap stay green; admission tests pass under

## PR #14509 — config: scope managed-routing host-inbound check by routing instance, skip bare parents (#14354) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14354-campaign`

Closes #14354

## Defect
`validateHostInboundManagedRoutingMismatch` (strict-commit gate via `compiler_tailgates.go`) false-rejected valid configs:
1. Zone lists bare `ge-0/0/0;` with a per-unit override `ge-0/0/0.0 { host-inbound-traffic { protocols { ospf; } } }`; `protocols ospf area 0.0.0.0 interface all` rejected on the synthetic bare parent key `"ge-0/0/0"`, whose effective set ignores the `.0` override.
2. `interface all` expanded over the global zone-interface map with no routing-instance tag, so a tenant-VRF `interface all` demanded ospf admission on MAIN-zone interfaces (and vice versa) — over-admission pressure on unrelated zones.

- Each collected `managedRP` carries its owning routing instance (`""` = global/MAIN, `ri.Name` for routing-instances).
- `interface all` expansion skips bare parent keys that fan down onto configured units (`InterfaceUnitRefKeys` > 1 key): no daemon runs on the parent key, and the unit checks carry the per-unit overrides.
- `interface all` checks only zone interfaces owned by the statement's routing instance, resolved lazily via `fabricZoneRoutingInstanceByInterface` / `ForEachRoutingInstanceInterfaceMembership` — the same membership traversal (RI lists, tunnel stanzas, dual-claim omission, forwarding exclusion) the dataplane uses.
- Fail-closed preserved: an unadmitted unit in the statement's own instance still rejects/warns, now named by its logical unit. Explicit refs, bare-ref→unit-0, lifelines, quarantine/conflict handling unchanged. No test-input special-casing.

`TestManagedRoutingMismatchUnitOverrideAndVRFAllScoping` (`pkg/config/host_inbound_managed_routing_14354_test.go`): bare-member+unit-override+global `all` (helper + strict compile), fail-closed bare member naming the logical unit, VRF `all` scoping both directions (own unadmitted interface still warns), VRF `all` via strict compile, explicit RI refs.

- GREEN: regression + `TestManagedRoutingMismatch13142`, `TestManagedRoutingHostInboundAdmissionCommitGate11571`, `TestManagedRoutingMismatchSurvivingBranches11571`, and wider `TestManagedRouting*/TestHostInbound*/TestFabricZone*/TestProtocolInterfaceMembership*/TestRoutingInstance*` sets pass; `go vet ./pkg/config/` clean; gofmt clean.

With the type unknown, the evaluator's fragment-association override also could not distinguish type 8 from type 3, over-denying legitimately permitted ICMP types while leaving the configured type semantics unenforced on the one policy gate that runs on this path.

What:
Parse the real ICMP type/code from the already-built owned logical-ingress frame with the existing `policy_packet_icmp` helper (the same helper the main transit path uses) and pass it to `evaluate_policy_result_l3_aware`. The helper returns `None` for non-ICMP protocols, the fragment sentinel, and truncated or non-first-fragment frames, preserving fail-closed behaviour there; TCP/UDP stay bit-identical. Validation:

GREEN with the fix: all 4 cells pass, and the full `afxdp::ipsec_inner::tests` module passes (36 passed), including the existing TCP/UDP port cells.

Risk:

- Mirror `ddnsCheckIPURLValid` and runtime `validateCheckIPURL` both require https — a plaintext URL slipping past commit (lenient/peer-sync/hand-built) fails closed in `CheckIP` before any fetch; Surface A publishes nothing (transient miss, never withdraw).
- Existing CheckIP-against-plaintext test fixtures migrated to TLS servers (update-backend http tests untouched); `SetCheckIPRootCAsForTesting` lets daemon tests trust a test CA via the real cached client. `pkg/ddns/README.md` + `docs/log/14372.md` updated.

## Validation
- F-DR3-H5-1: strict reject incl. non-credentialed + upper-case HTTP; https/upper-case-https/bare-host accepted; lenient warns.
- F-DR3-H5-2: `CheckIP` refuses http (incl. credentialed) before transport, no key in error; TLS positive returns the IP.
- F-DR3-H5-3: Surface A http scope yields no observation, never contacts the attacker server, warns once.
- Full `pkg/ddns` suite green; targeted `pkg/config` DDNS/checkip suites and daemon checkip tests green. RED sensitivity verified by reverting production gates with tests kept. (Full `pkg/config` run exceeded the 300s harness timeout, interrupted without verdict — not claimed.)

## Risk
Operators with a plaintext `checkip-url` must move it to https: strict commit rejects it; lenient load warns and the runtime probe publishes nothing until fixed. Bare-host checkip-urls and backend update endpoints unchanged.

Full `pkg/frr` suite: only 3 pre-existing BGP FRR-load failures, confirmed identical on unmodified base. `pkg/config` targeted OSPF tests pass (full suite exceeds the local 600s timeout in this environment; change is render-only).

## PR #14520 — nat: require unique-owner proof for nonzero-domain shared exact hits (#14384) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14384-campaign`

Closes #14384

## Why
`lookup_shared_forward_nat_match_with_admission` returned a shared NAT exact hit for any nonzero routing domain without consulting the ambiguity index, while the domain-0 exact branch and both fallback branches require a unique-owner proof. Two forward owners in domain D DNATing to the same backend publish the same domain-preserving reverse key, the second displaces the first, and a domain-D reply was attributed to the last publisher — minting a reverse session under the wrong forward session's decision/zones/policy.

## What
In the exact-hit branch, require the owner-RG indexes and, for nonzero domains, require `nat_ambiguities.is_unique_for(reverse_match_key(reply_key), exact.key)` — the domain-neutral probe the publish path observes/marks (`store.rs` publish). Non-unique, absent, saturated, or no-index hits fall through to the existing canonical/owner paths, which fail closed. Domain-0 behaviour, the canonical and owner paths, and the ICMP quote path are unchanged.

## Validation
- New regression `shared_nat_exact_hit_refuses_ambiguous_same_domain_owner_14384` (two same-key owners in domain D → `None`; single-owner domain-D control resolves; fixture asserts the exact slot holds the last publisher): fails on master, passes after the fix.
- `shared_nat_*`, `lookup_forward_nat*`, `publish_and_remove_shared*`, `icmp_quote*` test groups pass.
- `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` clean on the changed production file (test file carries pre-existing repo-wide fmt drift, untouched outside the new test).

## Risk
Legitimate nonzero-domain exact hits published without ambiguity recording (e.g. restamp/import paths) now fall through and may miss instead of resolving; that fail-closed direction matches every other branch in the function.

- **Runtime (load-bearing)** (`pkg/feeds/feeds.go`): `Manager.Apply` skips a plaintext-http feed server (`isPlaintextFeedURL`, replacing `warnPlaintextFeed`) — no worker, no snapshot — so bound address-names stay unresolvable and fail **closed** (#5645). `Apply` now refuses plaintext HTTP, so existing runtime fixtures serving loopback `httptest` servers were converted to `httptest.NewTLSServer`, trusting the fixture cert via the new lab-only `Manager.SetLabFeedTLSRoots` seam (HTTPS counterpart of `SetPrivateFeedAllowlist`; production never calls it). Fixes DR8-H3 (#14394): the kernel lo0 mirror dropped `match-start layer-4` and rendered every flexible-match-range at the L3 base — fail-open on host-bound traffic for `then discard` terms, wrong fall-through for `then accept` terms. Both renderers (netlink + text oracle) made the identical error, so parity could not catch it.

- `Lo0FlexMatch` now carries `MatchStart`; `lo0FlexMatch()` copies it.
- Netlink builder renders `layer-4` with `PayloadBaseTransportHeader`; oracle renders `@th`. Layer-3/empty stay byte-identical (`@nh` / network header).
- Any other match-start is unrepresentable in all three gates (`flexMatchRepresentable`, `lo0FlexMatchUnrepresentable`, converter `FlexMatchUnrepresentable` marker): the term matches nothing — no rule — never a widened rule at the wrong base.
- Stale "only layer-3" comments/docs corrected; userspace snapshot builder and Rust matcher untouched (already honour layer-4).

## Tests

- New `pkg/nftables/netlink_flexmatch_layer4_14394_test.go`: TH base for layer-4, NH controls, match-nothing + plan-level no-rule for `payload`/`bogus`/`layer-5`/`Layer-4`.
- New `pkg/daemon/lo0_flexmatch_layer4_14394_test.go`: `@th,0,8 & 0xff == 0x11` in oracle, `MatchStart` carried in spec, no-rule for unrepresentable starts, layer-3/empty controls.
- Parity: new `layer-4-transport-base` row and `unrepresentable-match-start` row (real nft + netlink install).
- RED on pristine master f8a69b7a4: oracle rendered `@nh,0,8 & 0xff == 0x11` for a layer-4 term; `payload` was representable. (The committed nftables test cannot build on master — the `MatchStart` field did not exist.)
- GREEN: new tests pass; full `pkg/nftables` passes; `TestNftNetlinkParity` flex subtests pass; flex-focused `pkg/config`/`pkg/dataplane/userspace` pass. One unrelated daemon failure (`TestNftRuleFromTermAddressSemantics3433/unresolved_positive_prefix-list`) is pre-existing on pristine master f8a69b7a4 and untouched by this change.

Closes #14394

## PR #14527 — config: reject misplaced VRRP authentication one level up (#14403) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14403-campaign`

Closes #14403

## Mechanism
The #4288 gate (`validateVRRPAuthenticationAST`) only inspected a `vrrp-group` node's own Keys/direct children via `vrrpAuthLeaf`; `parseVRRPGroups` only visits `vrrp-group` children. An `authentication-key`/`authentication-type` on the owning address node (H1-a), `family` (H1-b), `unit` (H1-c), interface (H1-d), or nested under the group under `virtual-address`/`track-interface` (H1-e) was never read and never gated — the group compiled with `AuthKey==""` and activated claiming the VIP with unauthenticated adverts.

## Fix (`pkg/config/compiler_interfaces.go`, same gate/function)
- `vrrpAuthLeafRecursive`: scans the group's whole subtree (H1-e).
- `vrrpMisplacedAuth`/`vrrpDirectAuthLeaf`/`collectVRRPGroups`: any non-group node directly carrying an auth leaf whose subtree contains a vrrp-group (H1-a..H1-d). Strict: hard-reject naming the misplaced keyword with the existing #4288 message. Lenient: warn + drop every affected group via `stripVRRPGroup` (base address survives).
- Scope guard: no vrrp-group in subtree → not reported.
- Secret hygiene: `safeVRRPPathKeys` truncates ancestor Keys at the auth token; group paths use only `vrrpGroupIDKeys` — Keys-packed secrets never leak into errors/warnings. Tested for both ancestor-packed shapes.

Note: H1-a as a direct address child was already hard-rejected on strict by the unrelated #9424 address-list gate (wrong diagnostic, and lenient only warned without dropping the group); it now gets the #4288 reject/drop as well.

## Regression (`pkg/config/vrrp_misplaced_auth_14403_test.go`)
Per-cell H1-a..H1-e × both leaf names: strict reject naming keyword + #4288 + no secret leak; lenient warn-and-drop (group not active, base compiles). Ancestor Keys-packed no-leak cells. Controls: no-auth group still commits/activates; auth leaf with no group nearby (family level) does not hard-reject; existing #4288 position control unchanged.

RED on origin/master (H1-b..H1-e compiled clean, lenient left groups active), GREEN after fix. Full `pkg/config` suite timed out in this sandbox at 300s both before completion (large suite); VRRP/interface/compiler targeted suites pass and `go vet` is clean — main agent should run the full `pkg/config` suite.

Docs: `docs/log/14403.md`.

## PR #14531 — config: install IS-IS interface auth from packed line (#14410) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14410-campaign`

## Why

The IS-IS interface loop in `pkg/config/compiler_protocols.go` read only
`child.Children` (via `expandFlatRun`), plus a `child.Keys[2:]` shim
recognising only `passive`/`level`. The packed spelling

```text
protocols { isis { net 49.0001.0000.0000.0001.00;
  interface ge-0/0/0.0 passive authentication-key IFACEKEY authentication-type md5; } }
```

packs the whole tail onto the interface node's own Keys with no
Children, so the loop read nothing: `AuthKey == ""` / `AuthType == ""`
on a clean strict commit, while the FRR renderer still emitted
`ip router isis` and gated circuit auth on the empty key — an
unauthenticated IS-IS adjacency where the operator configured MD5.

The #8662 fold cannot rescue it: it keys on the FIRST tail token and
`passive` is not a scoped interface pair, stranding the whole run; the
#8880 decline strands even a scoped head when a following router-level
`authentication-key` sibling shares the keyword.

## What

- `pkg/config/compiler_protocols.go` (IS-IS `interface` case): when the
  node carries a packed tail (`len(child.Keys) > 2`), read the body
  through `packedBodyChildren(child, isisInterfaceSchema8939())` — the
  schema-driven SSOT the OSPF interface loop uses — before the existing
  `expandFlatRun`. Braced spelling untouched. Mixed tail+braced body:
  the do-not-guess decline (tail ending in a leaf returns braced
  Children alone) is detected and the tail is expanded from a
  childless view so both halves are read; an unmodelled tail still
  expands to nothing. NOT changed: #8436 find-or-create, router-level
  auth, metric -1 preservation, BFD sub-children, the Keys[2:] shim.
- New regression `pkg/config/isis_interface_packed_auth_dr13h3_test.go`:
  braced positive control, passive-first fixture, scoped-head fixture
  with router-level sibling (sibling asserted to land on the router),
  head-keyword matrix, mixed packed+braced cell, routing-instance
  spelling.
- `docs/log/14410.md` records the mechanism and evidence.

## Validation

- RED on base `3541ce77e`: all five subtests fail
  `AuthKey = "" / AuthType = ""`; braced control carries
  `IFACEKEY`/`md5`.
- GREEN after fix and after rebase onto `195f4137a`:
  `TestISISInterfacePackedAuthDR13H3` passes;
  `TestProtocolAuthFlatRunKeepsEveryLeaf8939`, `TestISISMetric*`,
  `TestElidedAuthenticationKey*` pass.

## PR #14534 — session: fail closed on ambiguous shared-egress reverse-NAT matches (#14374) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14374-campaign`

Closes #14374

## Problem (DR4-H2)
`find_forward_nat_match_expiry` and `find_forward_nat_match_inner` (`userspace-dp/src/session/lookup.rs`) returned the first reverse-index candidate passing tuple + egress-domain checks. The reverse index is domain-agnostic; two tenants (domains A/B) with identical tuples egressing through the same shared uplink (domain W) are indistinguishable, so the first candidate won and `install_reverse_session_from_forward_match` durably minted a reverse session from the wrong tenant's decision (wrong domain/zones/policy, exempt from re-derivation).

## Fix
Both matchers track the first passing candidate; a second passing candidate with a different forward key in a different routing domain returns no match (`None` / `Absent`) and bumps the new `NAT_REVERSE_AMBIGUOUS_TOTAL` counter, surfaced as `xpf_userspace_nat_reverse_ambiguous_total` (Rust ProcessStatus → Go → Prometheus, following the embedded-error-suppressed pattern). Same-key duplicates and same-domain 1:N collisions keep established first-wins behavior. Expiry/idle-crossed semantics preserved.

## Tests
- RED→GREEN: `shared_egress_overlapping_tenants_are_ambiguous_14374` fails on master (first-wins returns tenant A), passes after fix; `shared_egress_single_candidate_control_still_matches_14374` control green.
- `cargo test reverse_egress_domain_11298`: 5 passed (incl. existing asymmetric-egress demux). Full `session::` suite: 442 passed.
- Go: `TestEmitUserspaceDynamicBufferMetrics` re-anchored 108→109 with new series asserted; `pkg/api` green. `pkg/dataplane/userspace` has one pre-existing failure confirmed on clean master.

Log: `docs/log/14374.md`

## PR #14548 — config: compile packed RA interface openings with flag first (#14420) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14420-campaign`

Closes #14420

## Mechanism
Packed (brace-elided) RA interface opening `interface ge-0/0/0 managed-configuration default-lifetime 0;` puts the whole body on the interface node's own Keys with no Children. `compileRouterAdvertisement` iterated `inst.node.Children` only (via `expandFlatRun`), and the compact normalizer only folds valued-leaf heads (`"interface default-lifetime"` etc.), so a zero-arg flag opening (`managed-configuration` / `other-stateful-configuration`) stayed packed and the loop saw an empty body: `ManagedConfig=false`, `DefaultLifetimeSet=false`, no prefixes. `pkg/ra` then advertised Router Lifetime 1800 for an explicit `default-lifetime 0` — RFC 4861 §6.2.1 "this router is NOT a default router" inverted (#4119's defect by a dropped leaf; distinct from the flat `set` route fixed in #8939). Braced twin and valued-leaf packed opening already compiled correctly.

## Fix
- `compileRouterAdvertisement`: expand the instance body with `packedBodyChildren(inst.node, schemaForPath("protocols","router-advertisement","interface"))` before `expandFlatRun` — the same schema-driven expansion the OSPF/OSPFv3 interface loops use. Tails outside the modelled grammar return Children unchanged (no behaviour change there).
- No sender change: `DefaultLifetimeSet` now reaches `buildRA`, which already honors explicit 0.

## Regression
- `pkg/config.TestRAInterfacePackedOpening14420`: managed opening (ManagedConfig + DefaultLifetimeSet/0), other-stateful opening (whole tail incl. prefix), packed-vs-braced parity, valued-leaf control.
- `pkg/ra.TestBuildRA_PackedOpeningPreservesExplicitZero14420`: packed spelling marshals RouterLifetime 0 + ManagedConfiguration true, matching braced twin.

## Validation
RED on origin/master `70702de41`: packed managed/other openings dropped (`ManagedConfig=false, DefaultLifetimeSet=false`, prefix lost), twin mismatch; control passed. GREEN after: both new tests, `TestRAInterfaceFlatRunKeepsEveryLeaf8939`, `TestRADNSServer*6695`, `TestBuildRA_FlatRunPreservesExplicitZero8939`, `TestBuildRA_4119_*`; gofmt/vet clean; re-verified on rebased head `57dc68397`. Full `pkg/config` suite exceeds the 300s harness cap, timing out in pre-existing `TestPathologicalWildcardFanoutIsRefused6767` (group-expansion stack, untouched by this change).

## Risk
Low: one reader widened via the established `packedBodyChildren` helper; braced/flat spellings unchanged; unmodelled tails fall back to prior behaviour.

An `event-options … then change-configuration commands` payload is live configuration the event engine executes with internal commit authority after #9939 plant-class adjudication, but `show event-options` printed `ThenCommands` verbatim and `RedactedClone()` never inspected the `commands` leaf. Compare clones fingerprint masked tokens with the existing `\x00xpf-sha256=` suffix so secret-equality survives in diffs.
- Stored `ThenCommands`, the compiler reader join semantics, and event execution are untouched. `docs/log/14413.md` records the change.

## Validation
- New regression tests RED on master (PSK verbatim in all four `RedactedClone` formats + gRPC show output), GREEN post-fix: quoted hierarchical, quoted flat-set, unquoted flat-set, block + bracket shapes across all four formats; `FormatCompareRedacted` identical-trees clean / changed-PSK fingerprint-only; helper table (IKE PSK, BGP/OSPF-MD5 keys, SNMP community, DDNS token masked; GRE `key`, host-name, login-class, delete controls verbatim); compiled `ThenCommands` and post-display stored commands still raw; CLI twin via configstore commit.

## PR #14553 — config: merge cross-container duplicate ipsec policies (#14430) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14430-campaign`

Why:
compileIPsec built a fresh IPsecPolicyDef per policy block and stored it unconditionally, so two same-name policy blocks under two different ipsec containers (or two security roots) wholesale-replaced each other: the first container's strong proposal list and perfect-forward-secrecy were silently discarded, leaving the second block's weak suite with no PFS. Find-or-create in the IPsec policy loop in pkg/config/compiler_ipsec.go, mirroring the IKE-policy / gateway / VPN loops in the same file; scalar leaves stay last-wins when restated, and a twin stating neither leaves earlier values intact. The proposals arm skips a reference already present so a twin re-listing the same proposal does not render it twice. NOT changed: same-parent #9023 fold, proposal gates, resolvability gate, proposal-set expansion, algorithm allowlist.

Validation:
New pkg/config/compiler_ipsec_policy_duplicate_dr17h1_test.go (cross-container strict+lenient, two-security-roots, same-parent and single-container controls, dedup control). keys and the #12923 default-policy choice keep the guard (their
pair/value semantics are first-match sensitive); bare leaves such
as `rip;` still suppress a genuine duplicate. Regression cells in
`pkg/config/group_merge_ospf_auth_container_dr14h1_test.go` cover
the OSPF main/control/application-level (protocols/ospf/area/
interface)/two-group/downgrade/rollover/reverse-precedence cases,

extensions; `pkg/frr/ospf_group_auth_container_14414_test.go` pins

downgrade, missing rollover key, and dropped `from` conditions;
they pass after the fix (`go test ./pkg/config -run 14414`,

#7648, default-policy #12823/#12923/#11821, apply-groups) stay
green; remaining full-package failures reproduce identically on
pristine origin/master. gofmt and go vet clean on changed files.

## PR #14566 — config: poison lenient policer discard+marking conflict to discard (#14443) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14443-campaign`

Closes #14443

## Mechanism
Merged firewall policer / three-color-policer `then { discard; loss-priority high; }` (group `then` beside inline `then`, or duplicate policer roots) strict-rejected via #8445, but the lenient arm in `compiler_uniformgates_filter.go` only appended a warning. The single-valued `ThenAction` is last-wins and the `loss-priority` arms were unfenced, so the marking won: `ThenAction="loss-priority high"` → snapshot `DiscardExcess=false` → excess traffic metered and forwarded, authored discard unenforced on lenient load/HA-sync/restore.

## Fix

## Tests

## PR #14702 — config: compile NAT rules with a packed match (#14415) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14415-campaign`

Closes #14415

## Mechanism
`rule r1 match source-address 10.0.0.0/24 { then { ... } }` parses with the match packed into the rule node's Keys and only `then` in Children. The NAT compilers read match only via `FindChildren("match")` (Children-only), so the packed match was never seen: `matchAuthored` stayed false (disarming #8430/#9874), SNAT compiled unconstrained, and DNAT published no entry — silently deleting a `destination-nat off` exemption.

## Fix
- `compileNATSource`/`compileNATDestination`/`compileNATStatic` expand each rule node via `packedBody` with its rule schema and read match/then from the expanded node.
- `packedBodyChildren` leaf-body guard: when the deepest packed node is a leaf, return synthesized roots + real children as siblings if every real child is a declared sibling statement repeating no root head (preserves #6818 leaf decline, pinned by existing test).
- The primary normalize admission ("rule match") was measured and rejected: without `packedStatements` on NAT rule, the fold attached the braced `then` under the synthesized `match` and #9877 recorded `then` as unknown leaf. Documented in docs/log/14415.md.

## Regression
`pkg/config/compiler_nat_packed_match_dr14h2_test.go`: SNAT packed (SourceAddresses + matchAuthored), DNAT off packed+braced (destination, Off, installed via DestinationNATRuleExcludedReason), DNAT pool packed, scope-only control, fully-packed control. RED on origin/master, GREEN after. Sharded NAT/compact suite: only pre-existing failures also present on base (TestElidedDepthCoverage8850, TestPackedOptInHoldsForEveryLeafPair8768, TestZoneInterfacePackedApplyMacroOwnKeysCompiles12835). Full pkg/config suite exceeds local timeout; main agent should run it.

## PR #14743 — config: reject routing policy-term conflicting then actions (#14425) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

## Why
A merged routing policy-statement term carrying both `then accept` and `then reject` resolved silently: the compiler assigned the single `PolicyTerm.Action` field last-write-wins, and group expansion dropped the group terminal via the inline-wins override, so the conflict never reached any gate. Single-action controls (same-reject both sides, accept+local-preference, reject-only, modifier-only) unchanged.
- Full `pkg/config` suite minus `TestSlotEscapeSweep` (times out on pristine base too under host load): head failure set identical to base — 51 pre-existing IPsec/plaintext failures, no new failures.
- `go vet ./pkg/config/` clean; gofmt clean on touched files.

## PR #14753 — config: require family segment before filter in packed unit gate (#14629) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14629-campaign`

## Summary

Follow-up to #14435/#14565 (merged `fda4502d5`). The #14435 gate exemption `unitPackedTailHasFamilyFilter14435` (`compiler_interfaces_unsupported.go`) returned true if `family inet|inet6` appeared **anywhere** in a packed unit's Keys tail, without requiring the filter to sit inside/after that family segment. `unit 0 filter input DISCARD-BAD family inet { address ...; }` (filter FIRST, family later) therefore exempted the unit-level filter from the #12090 gate while `packedBody` expanded only the trailing family segment — the filter, the addresses and the family were all dropped and the unit strict-committed as an empty `Unit{Number:0}` (no addresses, no filter, no family), lenient also silent: accepted-but-dropped, fail-open. Found by campaign hostile review (Fix14435b).

**Fix:** rename the helper to `unitPackedTailHasFamilyBeforeFilter14435` and make it schema-arity-aware. It walks the unit tail with the same open-levels stack `packedBodyChildren` keeps, consumes each statement by the unit schema's own arity (a value spelling `family`/`filter`/`inet`, e.g. `description family`, is never a keyword), honours quoted-token provenance, and returns true only when an unquoted `family inet|inet6` segment is reached **before** any unit-level `filter`/`simple-filter` hit. A filter hit first, an apply statement, a quoted keyword-position token, or a token outside the modelled grammar returns false (do-not-guess, fail-closed for the exemption). Both call sites updated (braced-filter-child exemption in `isInterfaceDirectFilterConsumerPath12090`, packed-tail exemption in `isInterfacePackedFilterConsumer12090`); old helper name removed, no shim. No compiler reader change: genuinely consumed spellings (family-first, point-to-point-first, tunnel-first, `family inet filter input …`) compile identically; only the previously mis-exempted filter-first spelling now strict-rejects (#12090, naming `filter input`) and lenient-warns (#1960 posture preserved).

Closes #14629

## Test report

- **New regression** `TestPackedUnitFilterFirstFamilyRejects14629` in `compiler_interfaces_packed_unit_dr17h6_test.go`: reject cells (inet/inet6 braced bodies, output direction, packed family body, `simple-filter` first, filter-first-then-braced-family-filter) each asserting strict #12090 rejection **and** a lenient #12090 warning; accept controls (family-first, point-to-point-first, family-packed filter, `description family`/`description filter` values consumed by arity, tunnel-first) asserting no #12090 diagnostic and populated `FamilyInet`/filter/address/tunnel hooks.
- **RED/GREEN verified:** restoring the HEAD (pre-fix) gate makes the five filter-first reject cells strict-compile clean (the bug); with the fix all cells pass. Pre-fix behaviour also measured directly: strict compiled the filter-first spelling to an empty `Unit{Number:0}` with no warning.
- **Focused suites pass:** `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestPackedUnit|TestFilterKeyword|TestPackedCompoundFamilyFilter|TestInterfaceMplsAny|PackedUnitFamily|TestCompactFilterHeads|TestInterfaceFilterPackedRun|TestMemberlessRange|12090'` — PASS (includes the unchanged #14435 p2p/tunnel, #9620 packed-family and #12090 population tests).

### Full-suite note (pre-existing upstream failures)

`go test ./pkg/config/` on this base additionally hits failures that reproduce **identically on a clean `origin/master` worktree** (48b24754c, newer than this branch's base) — a nil-pointer panic in `validateRethRedundancyGroupTokensAST`/`nodeVal` under the `TestCompactBlock*` census tests and `TestAuthKeyWithoutTypeInRoutingInstanceIsRefused14400` (#14400/#2419 area). They are unrelated to this change (different subsystem, present without it) and are not addressed here.

This branch is based on 09c6b9ed9; `origin/master` has since merged #14436 (`c4848b1ae`, packed interface-instance tails), which also touches `compiler_interfaces_unsupported.go` (nearby hunks, same helper call sites, does not change the helper). The diff here is expected to need a mechanical rebase onto current master; the helper rename/ordering fix composes with #14436 (it only narrows when the #14435 exemption applies).

## PR #14754 — grpcapi: bind persistent-NAT clear generation in signed request (#14580) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14580-pnat-generation`

grpcapi: bind persistent-NAT clear generation in signed request (#14580)

Closes #14580

## Why
The forwarded `clear-persistent-nat` origin/generation rode unsigned gRPC metadata (`x-peer-persistent-nat-*`). The #4107 fabric token binds only method + protobuf request digest + window — no metadata — so a captured token replayed inside its window with `generation=MaxUint64` durably poisoned `RemoteGenerations[origin]=MaxUint64` on the receiver: every genuine peer lease batch was then silently dropped (`batch.Generation < generation → return nil`, no log) forever, surviving restart with no expiry or self-heal (Y06-02).

## What
- **Signed body (root fix):** origin/generation now travel inside `SystemActionRequest` (`persistent_nat_origin=9`, `persistent_nat_generation=10`; protobuf regenerated), so the existing #10709 request-digest MAC binds them. A replay whose origin/generation differs from the minted call is rejected `Unauthenticated` by the fabric interceptor before the handler/watermark runs.
- Deleted the unsigned-metadata extractor; both proxies (grpcapi `SystemAction` fan-out, CLI peer dial) forward via the signed body (`persistentNatClearRequestWithGeneration`, proto.Clone — caller's request never mutated).
- Legacy `x-peer-persistent-nat-{origin,generation}` keys added to `reservedPeerMetadataKeys`: stripped on both listeners, never honored. A legacy forwarded clear (empty body) clears locally with no fence (pre-#11486 semantics); non-forwarded calls smuggling the fields are rejected `InvalidArgument`.
- **Manager defense-in-depth** (`pkg/dataplane/userspace`): a forwarded clear jumping a *known* peer's watermark by >1024 generations is refused (error, `PersistentNatGenerationJumpsRejected` counter, Warn log, nothing persisted, helper never invoked); first contact with an unseen origin remains unbounded. Stale lease batches dropped against the watermark are now counted (`PersistentNatStaleBatchDrops`) and rate-limited-logged instead of silent.
- CLI `peerSystemActionFn` test seam now takes the full `*pb.SystemActionRequest` so tests observe the signed body.
- Docs: `pkg/grpcapi/README.md`, `pkg/cli/README.md`.

## Validation
New decisive tests (fail on master, pass here):
- `TestFabricAuth14580_PersistentNatGenerationForgedReplayRejected` — token minted for gen=3, replayed with MaxUint64 → `Unauthenticated`, handler never reached; genuine body admitted; changed-origin control also rejected.
- `TestPersistentNatClearGenerationFromSignedBody14580` — extractor matrix incl. legacy-metadata-never-honored.
- `TestPersistentNatForgedGenerationJumpRefused14580` — MaxUint64 clear refused before helper; watermark unpoisoned across restart (gen-9 batch admitted); genuine +1 accepted.
- `TestPersistentNatStaleBatchDropCounted14580` — stale drop counted, helper untouched.

Updated #11486/#14148/#10784 proxy tests assert the signed body and absence of generation metadata. Targeted `pkg/grpcapi`, `pkg/dataplane/userspace`, `pkg/cli` suites pass; `go vet` clean on all three packages.

Pre-existing failures verified identical on a pristine `origin/master` worktree (unrelated, not introduced here): `pkg/grpcapi TestShowTextGolden` (#14139 ipsec PSK check) and `pkg/cli TestCompleteConfig_PredefinedApplicationSets_5763` (#14339 application shadow check).

## Risk

## PR #14755 — firewall: reject no-protocol disjoint L4 filter terms (#14445) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14445-campaign`

Why:
A firewall-filter term with no protocol that combines a port or tcp-flags predicate with an icmp-type/icmp-code predicate ANDs matcher arms no single packet can satisfy: ports require TCP/UDP, tcp-flags requires TCP, and icmp-type/code require ICMP/ICMPv6. The term could never match, so a then discard/reject term silently fell through to the implicit accept (fail-open), while each predicate alone with no protocol remains legitimate and enforceable.

What:
Extend validateFilterCrossFieldStrict in the Go compiler to strict-reject no-protocol port+icmp and tcp-flags+icmp pairs (all port polarities including *-except; lenient path keeps the existing cross-field warning) and extend the Rust check_cross_field_satisfiability backstop to fail the whole snapshot closed with the combined predicates port+icmp-type/code and tcp-flags+icmp-type/code. Ports plus tcp-flags together stay accepted because one TCP packet satisfies both. NOT changed: the matcher, single-predicate no-protocol terms, and the explicit-protocol #3723 arms.

Validation:
New Go TestFilterNoProtoDisjointRejected_14445 (9 cells) and TestFilterNoProtoSinglePredicateAccepted_14445 and Rust filter_disjoint_noproto_14445 tests fail on pristine 809a538ce and pass on this head; targeted Go cross-field suites and 12 Rust filter/crossfield tests pass. Full pkg/config suite shows only two failures reproduced identically on pristine base. go vet is clean.

Risk:
Leniently loaded legacy configs carrying this shape now warn in Go and have their userspace snapshot refused in favour of prior-good state; no committed valid config changes behaviour.

Closes #14445

## PR #14757 — dhcprelay: bind IA-less Confirm/Release/Decline replies (#14599) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14599-campaign`

Why: the DHCPv6 relay's pending key (xid + Client ID DUID + lowest IA type/IAID) could never match a server Reply carrying no IA, yet RFC 8415 makes the IA-less Reply the conformant shape for Confirm (§18.3.3 NotOnLink), Release (§18.3.7 Success), and Decline (§18.3.8). Those replies were dropped as `RepliesDroppedNoRequest`: a roaming client never learned NotOnLink and kept a stale address, and the drop counter misdirected operators.

What: `insertPending6` (`pkg/dhcprelay/pending6.go`) records the primary IA-bound binding plus, for exactly Confirm/Release/Decline, an IA-less alias key carrying the same recorded client address and request type. The production client loop and the test arming helper insert through it; `pending6KeyFor` is unchanged, so IA-echo (NoBinding) replies match as before, and every #10699/#14181 check (configured server source, outer peer-address equality, legitimate answer type, Interface-ID routing) applies on the alias path unchanged. Regression tests in `relay6_noia_14599_test.go` cover the probe rows, the drop boundary, the IA-echo control, and forged cells on the alias path. README and `docs/log/14599.md` document the alias.

Validation: RED on origin/master 8f89c2d89 — Confirm NotOnLink, Release Success, and Decline Success rows failed with client writes=0 (dropped as unmatched); GREEN after the fix — `go test ./pkg/dhcprelay/ -run 14599 -count=1` passes all 7 new tests, full `go test ./pkg/dhcprelay/ -count=1` passes (including #10699/#14181 suites), `go vet` and `gofmt` clean. An IA-less Reply to a recorded Solicit/Request/Renew/Rebind is still dropped, pinned by tests.

Risk: forged IA-less replies gain no new acceptance surface (same xid + exact DUID guess, configured server source, recorded peer). Confirm/Release/Decline transactions occupy two pending ring slots for their TTL; eviction remains availability-direction only. No live-cluster smoke (fake-conn scope per the issue's decisive check).

Closes #14599

## PR #14760 — dhcp: accept any server reply in REBINDING (#14600) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14600-campaign`

Why:
REBINDING required the granting server in both v4 and v6 matchers
(the rebind parameter was discarded), defeating T2 in failover-pair
deployments: RFC 2131 4.3.2 and RFC 8415 18.2.5 define REBINDING/
Rebind as any-server, so a partner ACK was rejected and the client
fell through to full re-acquisition with address/PD churn.

rebind mode require only a present valid server identity while

answering server (leaseFromACKv4 serverID, parseV6ReplyChecked
v6ServerDUID), so the partner becomes the next RENEW binding.

TestRebindAcceptsAnyServer14600 and update 9944 rebind cells.

(stash renew.go only): new + updated 9944 tests fail. GREEN:
targeted matcher tests pass; go test ./pkg/dhcp/... -count=1,
go vet, git diff --check pass.

Risk:
Any server passing xid/chaddr/DUID on the interface socket can
now answer at T2 (RFC semantics, including NAK revocation);
bounded by those checks plus required server identity. No lab
failover capture; predicate and storage are unit-covered.

## PR #14761 — daemon: re-resolve web-management bind after address convergence (#14582) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14582-webmgmt-rebind`

Closes #14582

## Defect (Y07-01)
`reconcileWebManagement` runs early in `applyConfigLocked` (deliberately, for credential revocation) before `applyDataplaneAndHACore`/networkd applies interface addresses. `resolveInterfaceAddr` read the live kernel, found no address yet, fell back to loopback, and the fingerprint recorded that as converged — `show system services` reported Listening, the `StateFailed`-only re-assert gate never re-drove it, and the DHCP lifeline fast path skipped web-management entirely. Off-box REST/J-Web stayed silently down until a later commit (fails closed to loopback; no exposure). Verified RED by executing the real reconcile + re-assert path against the kernel seam: address appearing afterwards changed nothing.

## Fix
- **Degraded is recorded, not converged**: `resolveInterfaceAddrDegraded` → per-leg `api.Config.HTTPBindDegraded/HTTPSBindDegraded` → `mgmtEndpoint.{http,https}Degraded`; `reconcileTo` treats a degraded-change as a leg change and advances the flag only on a successful rebind.
- **Honest state**: new `sysservices.StateStale` — a degraded (loopback-fallback) or address-replaced leg reports `addr (stale bind)`, never Listening, reflecting the address actually bound. `Daemon.effectiveListeners` folds in a per-leg re-resolution (`mgmtBindStaleLegs`) so the vanished-address case (fingerprint still matches an old resolution) is also Stale. `mgmtListenerDown` keys on `Failed || Stale` on that same snapshot, preserving the #6803 invariant that operator view and retry trigger are one question. The `xpf_management_listener_state` metric now also emits the https surface and the stale series (its test updated: 12 series).
- **Same-commit convergence**: second `reconcileWebManagement` in `applyConfigLocked` after `applyDataplaneAndHACore`, warn-only (retry debt, not a commit failure).
- **DHCP sibling**: `rebindWebMgmtForLeaseChange` on the management-only fast path — gated by `webMgmtBindsToDHCPInterface` (bound interface has a DHCP/DHCPv6 unit), serialized under `applySem`, re-reads the active config under the semaphore, non-fatal (the #2884 shape).

Auth safety unchanged: the fallback stays loopback, the nil-auth publish still gates on live addresses, and degraded→real rebinds flow through the existing sanctioned/intersection logic.

## Regression (`pkg/daemon/webmgmt_rebind_14582_test.go`)
- `TestWebMgmtRebindsWhenInterfaceAddressAppears14582` — decisive z4 cell: no-address-yet → Stale + owner-down; address appears; one tick → Listening at `10.0.0.1:443`; healthy leg not bounced.
- `TestWebMgmtRebindsOnAddressReplacement14582` — vanished/replaced address reports Stale, rebinds to the new address, stale socket closed.
- `TestWebMgmtDHCPLeaseChangeRebindsBoundInterface14582` — gate controls (DHCP vs static) + lease rebind counted via the seam.
- `TestWebMgmtPostNetworkdReconcileResolvesInSameApply14582` — source wiring (post-networkd reconcile + DHCP fast-path call).

Sensitivity: reverting the gate to Failed-only reds the decisive cell at the owner-down assertion (verified). Bounded daemon suite (`14582|6803|8597|5714|5715|6401|Management|Mgmt|WebMgmt`), `pkg/sysservices`, and the #8195 metric tests pass; `go vet` clean on touched packages.

## PR #14762 — config: stop empty redundant-ether-options panicking the RETH gate (#14729) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14729-campaign`

## Why

#14441 (86f517f8c) deleted the `rg == nil` guard in `validateRethRedundancyGroupTokensAST` when it added the elided-spelling expansion, so an interface with an **empty** `redundant-ether-options` stanza — `redundant-ether-options { }`, or the bare leaf `redundant-ether-options;` — reaches `nodeVal(nil)` and panics the pre-walk on commit, commit-check and the tolerant load / HA-sync path alike:

```
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
  nodeVal(...)                               compiler_applications.go:1340
  validateRethRedundancyGroupTokensAST       compiler_reth_rg_token.go:113
  runPreWalkGates                            compiler_prewalk.go:778
```

`TestCompactBlockEquivalenceInventory2419` (found by the #14442 lane, reproduced on clean `origin/master`) hit it deterministically via the census's empty-stanza skeleton fixture, so the test could not run at all. Any operator config carrying an empty reo stanza crashes the same way, bricking the boot the #1960 no-brick rule protects.

An empty stanza carries **no** `redundancy-group` token — the absent-token case #6782 deliberately scopes out (like no reo stanza at all). A present `redundancy-group;` leaf with no value still produces a node and must still be gated.

## What

- `pkg/config/compiler_reth_rg_token.go`: restore the `rg == nil` guard after the #14441 expansions, with the absent-vs-present distinction recorded at the site. `nodeVal` deliberately unchanged (its callers nil-check explicitly; nil-tolerance would reclassify present-but-empty tokens as absent and mask the next dropped guard). The #6782 classifier, suppression and compiler reader are untouched.
- `pkg/config/compiler_reth_rg_token_6782_test.go`: new `TestEmptyRedundantEtherOptionsDoesNotPanic14729` — both empty spellings commit clean on strict + lenient, keep the address, no #6782 warning, `RedundancyGroup=0`; plus the boundary cell proving a present-but-valueless token still rejects naming `reth0` / warns+suppresses lenient.
- Census fallout the panic had masked (census now runs: 1202 checked, 72 divergent):
  - Removed the 13 `interfaces xpfname` lines fixed by #14442 and the 2 RA M/O lines fixed by #14420 from `compact_block_divergences_2419.txt` (regenerated via `XPF_GEN_2419=1`, drift classified in `inventoryNotes`).
  - `interfaces xpfname mtu`: `filedStillOpen` → `filedFixed` (`#14442`); RA M/O pair anchored in `filedFixed` (`#14420`). Known-true control re-anchored on the hand-verified `interfaces xpfname aggregated-ether-options lacp active` so it keeps two anchors from two compiler files.
  - Deleted the 15 stale rows from `compact_block_permanent_exclusions_8690.txt`; the two `family inet6` unit rows reclassed `open` → `partial` to match their new drop shape.
- `docs/log/14729.md`: defect, fix, census fallout, RED/GREEN.

## Validation

- **RED** on `origin/master` (9307e0940): `TestCompactBlockEquivalenceInventory2419` panics in `nodeVal(nil)`; minimal probes (`interfaces { xpfname { redundant-ether-options { } } }`, `interfaces { reth0 { redundant-ether-options; } }`) panic in `CompileConfigLenient`. New test panics identically with only the production fix reverted.
- **GREEN** with fix: `TestEmptyRedundantEtherOptionsDoesNotPanic14729`, `TestCompactBlockEquivalenceInventory2419`, `TestCompactBlockCensusReport2419`, all #6782/#14441 reth tests, `TestFlatRunResidueSchemasResolve9792`, and the #8690 register gates pass; `gofmt`/`go vet` clean; `go build ./pkg/config` ok.
- **Base-attributed, not touched**: `TestPermanentExclusionsMatchTheInventory8690` (16 stale `open` rows from #14409/#14426/#14428-era fixes) and `TestCompactNormalizeScopePreservesCompiledResult8690` (4 unexaminable `policy-options … from` sites) fail identically with this change stashed — other lanes' inventory obligations, unblocked (not caused) by this fix.

One nil guard restored to its pre-#14441 form in a single AST pre-walk gate; the present-but-empty token keeps its strict-reject / lenient warn+suppress behaviour (pinned by the boundary cell). Census artifacts only record measurements the panic had hidden. No compiler, wire or schema change beyond the panic itself.

sources drop per node; no-`from protocol` terms expand over the
node-fitting domain (#14380). The per-peer `route-map out` remains
the per-peer gate; bare protocol tokens keep the existing unfiltered
global path. This is not the #2473 leak (that was an *unfiltered*
`redistribute ospf`). `redistReferencedNodes14380` records both BGP
nodes so the maps are defined and join the ApplyFull collision belt.

encoded the bug are narrowed/updated, and the #9667 caller census

## PR #14766 — ddns: name-level guard for skip-existing/strict-fail (#14604) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14604-campaign`

Closes #14604

## Summary
The skip-existing/strict-fail RFC 2136 conflict guard used per-type `RRsetNotUsed`, so a LAN client could plant an A/AAAA at a foreign name holding only another type (AAAA/MX/TXT). Now uses name-level `NameNotUsed` (ANY/NONE); skip-existing keeps `errDDNSConflictRefused`, strict-fail keeps its hard error. The manager threads `SiblingFamilyOwned` (from its durable ownership scan, `crossTypeSiblingOwned`) so a legitimate dual-stack client's sibling-family publish keeps the per-type guard and A+AAAA both publish. Documented residual: a name already xpf-owned for one family plus a foreign RR of another type cannot be classified backend-side.

## PR #14768 — daemon: bind web-management per address family with zoned link-local (#14583) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14583-campaign`

Closes #14583

## Why
`resolveInterfaceAddr` returned a single IPv4-first address: dual-stack web-management interfaces silently had no IPv6 listener (host-inbound admits http/https for both families; IPv6 is first-class), and link-local-only interfaces produced a bare `[fe80::…]:443` bind that fails EINVAL without a zone.

## What

## Validation

Full `pkg/daemon` suite exceeded the 300s job cap — targeted subsets pass, full run not claimed.

## PR #14769 — flowexport: resolve IPv4 route masks via OIF output lookup (#14610) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14610-campaign`

Why:
fibMatchMask set RTA_IIF with no RTA_SRC whenever the flow's ingress
ifindex was positive, which is always in production. The kernel IPv4
input path rejects a zero source as martian (EINVAL), so every IPv4
srcMask/dstMask lookup failed, was cached as (0,false), and exported
as an unresolved 0 indistinguishable from a real /0. The #2866
feature was dead for every IPv4 record; the unit tests faked the
lookup so nothing exercised the real netlink call.

What:
- pkg/flowexport/routemask.go: fibMatchMask now performs an output
  route lookup — vrfOifForIfindex maps the ingress ifindex to its
  l3mdev master (MasterIndex via LinkByIndex) and sets
  RouteGetOptions.OifIndex, which needs no source address and
  selects the enslaved interface's VRF table. A non-enslaved or
  unresolvable ifindex omits RTA_OIF and keeps the main-table
  lookup, bit-identical for default deployments. Seams
  routeMasterLinkByIndex/routeLookupWithOptions allow unit
  assertion of the query shape. False "bit-identical" comment fixed.
- pkg/flowexport/README.md: #3744 section documents the OIF output
  lookup and the #14610 EINVAL mechanism.
- pkg/flowexport/routemask_netns_14610_test.go: netns-gated
  real-netlink regression (IPv4 /24 both halves with positive
  ifindex, IPv6 /48 unchanged, VRF-enslaved member resolves to the
  VRF table's /16) plus a no-netns OIF query-shape pin.
- docs/log/14610.md: issue log.

NOT changed: MaskResolver signature, (ifindex,IP) cache key, async
background populate, miss counting, wire format.

Validation:
- Probe (private netns): the old IifIndex query returns invalid
  argument with no routes while production fibMatchMask(192.0.2.5,
  iif) returns (24,true).
- RED: new test cannot build on current master (seams absent); the
  old query shape is EINVAL for IPv4 in the same harness.
- GREEN: unshare -rn go test ./pkg/flowexport/ -run TestFibMatchMask
  -count=1 -v passes; go test ./pkg/flowexport/ -count=1 passes;
  go vet ./pkg/flowexport/, gofmt, git diff --check clean.

Risk:
One extra LinkByIndex call per background cache populate (bounded
by the 32-inflight cap and TTL cache); session-close hot path
unchanged. Torn-down interfaces fall back to the main table
instead of failing the lookup. No lab deployment run; kernel
behavior covered in-netns.

Closes #14610

## PR #14771 — ipsec: render dynamic hostname as responder IKE identity (#14590) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14590-campaign`

Closes #14590

## Problem
Junos `dynamic hostname <fqdn>` identifies a dynamic-IP peer by the IKE identity it presents (hub `dynamic hostname X` ↔ spoke `local-identity hostname X`). xpf rendered it as `remote_addrs = <fqdn>` — a DNS-resolved dial address — with no remote `id`, so migrated hub/spoke tunnels never came up when the peer name was not in DNS (the normal dynamic-peer case).

## Fix
- **Compiler** (`pkg/config/compiler_ipsec.go`, both gateway paths): every `dynamic` block is responder-only; the FQDN is kept in `DynamicHostname` as the expected identity. Schema/struct docs updated (identity, not DNS-resolved). A DNS-dialed peer remains expressible via gateway `address <fqdn>`, unchanged.
- **Render** (`pkg/ipsec/policy.go`): `remote_addrs = %any`, `remote { id = "@<fqdn>" }` (explicit `remote-identity` still wins), PSK scoped by `id-1 = "@<fqdn>"`, no `start_action`; shared `responderOnlyGateway` helper also drives responder DPD (`ike.go`) and no eager re-initiation (`manager.go`), including directly-constructed configs where the compiled flag was not carried.
- **PrepareConfig** (`policy_addr.go`): family hint is pure — literal addresses classify directly, a dynamic identity is family-agnostic (IP literal still classifies) — so the bounded DNS resolver + worker pool are deleted; no DNS on the commit/apply path.

## Tests
- RED on master: config `ResponderOnly = false, want true` (flat/block/nested/set forms); ipsec `remote_addrs = "branch.example.net", want "%any"`, no remote id.
- New: `pkg/config/compiler_ipsec_dynamic_identity_14590_test.go`, `pkg/ipsec/dynamic_hostname_identity_14590_test.go` (render, explicit-remote-id precedence, address-gateway control).
- Updated tests pinning the old DNS reading (DynamicHostname render, PrepareConfig family, #9641, #14140, #6469, #13540, parser test) and `pkg/ipsec/README.md` / `docs/config-schema.md`.
- GREEN: `go test ./pkg/ipsec -count=1`; focused `pkg/config` ipsec tests; `go vet` clean.
- Pre-existing: `TestValidateIPsecEndpoints_Accept` fails identically on pristine `origin/master` (#14139 PSK rejection) — verified in a base worktree, untouched here.

Live charon proof (`swanctl --list-conns` `id: @X`) is lab-bound; render/compile tests are the gate. Log: `docs/log/14590.md`.

## PR #14773 — firewall: report no PCI address for a USB NIC behind its host controller (#14595) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14595-campaign`

Why:
ExtractPCIAddr/extractPCIAddr returned the last DDDD:BB:DD.F sysfs component with no bus check, so an x86 USB NIC behind an xHCI controller (`.../0000:00:14.0/usb2/2-1/2-1:1.0`) inherited the controller BDF `0000:00:14.0`. Only a sysfs device path whose last component is the BDF itself (or `virtioN` directly below its PCI function, a 1:1 channel linksetup already enumerates under that BDF) names a PCI device; any other tail yields `""`. Validation:
RED on base: hermetic x86 xHCI fixture gave both USB NICs `pci="0000:00:14.0"` (TestEnumerateUSBNICsX86ReportEmptyPCI14595, TestClassifyNetdevUSBBehindXHCINoPCI14595, usb rows of TestExtractPCIAddrNonPCITail14595 failed pre-fix). GREEN after: devicemap 14595 + #4884 controls pass, full pkg/devicemap passes; daemon 14595 cells pass (TestExtractPCIAddrLinksetupNonPCITail14595 incl. virtio controls, TestExtractPCIAddrLinksetupBootstrapUSBNIC14595, TestEnumeratePCINICsSkipsUSBNIC14595, TestEnumeratePCINICsUSBRenameSkipped14595 — only enp8s0→fxp0 renamed); scoped daemon suites (14595|12545|Enumerate|Bootstrap|Lifeline|DeviceMap) pass. Full pkg/daemon has one unrelated failure TestHostInboundTeardownClearsEnforcedThenFailedReinstallFences_5790 (host-inbound teardown, untouched by this change).

## PR #14774 — ddns: require TSIG-signed responses to signed UPDATEs (#14603) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14603-campaign`

Why:
A TSIG-signed RFC 2136 UPDATE accepted an unsigned response:
miekg/dns only verifies a reply MAC when the reply carries a TSIG
RR, so a forged unsigned NOERROR recorded phantom publishes and
deletes as settled, and a forged YX/NOTAUTH suppressed or
mis-skipped legitimate publishes — exactly in the deployments
that configured TSIG per the documented #4483 mitigation.

What:
`exchange()` now runs `validateTSIGResponse` on both the UDP leg
and the TCP truncation retry whenever a TSIG key is configured:
the reply must carry a TSIG RR matching the configured key name
and algorithm (canonical, case-insensitive), else it is a
transport error that never reaches the rcode verdict, records or
drops no ownership, and counts no conflict/PTR-skip. A truncated
TSIG exchange via a non-`*dns.Client` exchanger fails closed.
The fake DNS server in tests gains unsigned / wrong-key /
wrong-algorithm / wrong-secret / TCP-only forgery controls;
README, config-schema, and the commit-time warning comments
state the real mechanism. NOT changed: the no-TSIG warned
posture, DHCID guards, and the other DDNS backends.

Validation:
RED on base (production reverted, one unit test excluded to
compile): all 14 unsigned upsert/delete wire subtests and the
unsigned-TCP test failed with forged rcodes accepted as
verdicts; signed controls passed. GREEN: full
`go test ./pkg/ddns/ -count=1` passes, the TSIG selector passes,
pkg/config DDNS warning tests pass, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean.

Risk:
A TSIG-configured server that strips TSIG from responses now
fails closed with retries instead of accepting verdicts — the
intended posture; properly signing servers are unaffected.

Closes #14603

## PR #14775 — ddns: publish both families for dual-stack clients under replace-owned (#14602) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14602-campaign`

Why: under the default replace-owned policy a dual-stack DHCP client
never got both its A and AAAA. identity4 yields cid:/mac: identities
while identity6 yields duid:<duid>/<iaid>, and dhcidRR digests the raw
prefixed string, so the two families of one host always produce
different RFC 4701 DHCIDs. Whichever family published first owned the
name; the sibling's Attempt B (DHCID-matches-ours) could never match
and was refused every cycle (owned=1, err=nil), silently losing half
of each host's forward DNS. The #2700 fixture used one identical
identity for both families, a shape identity6 cannot produce.

What: sendAddOwned takes a sibling branch when the manager threads
SiblingFamilyOwned (upsertLocked's crossTypeSiblingOwned store scan,
merged for #14604): it adds this family's forward RR plus its own
per-family DHCID under a per-type RRsetNotUsed prerequisite, leaving
the sibling untouched. The store, not the wire digest, is the
cross-family ownership proof. Each family's delete already replays
its own identity, so teardown removes only its own A/AAAA+DHCID;
the identical-identity shared-DHCID keep-alive is unchanged. A name
with no owned sibling keeps every guard; a foreign same-type RRset
still fails the branch's RRsetNotUsed. Rewrites the #2700 fixture
with production-shaped identities (per-family DHCIDs) and updates
the README DHCID contract. NOT changed: skip-existing/strict-fail
(their sibling bypass already landed with #14604).

Validation: new TestDualStackProductionIdentitiesBothPublishReplaceOwned
fails pre-fix with "AAAA missing — v6 family lost the DHCID race"
(winner varies with map order) and passes after: A+AAAA present,
owned=2, SkippedConflict=0 across 2 cycles, concurrent foreign claim
refused with no ownership, full teardown orphan-free. Rewritten
TestPartialDualStackTeardownKeepsSharedDHCID passes. go test
./pkg/ddns -count=1 PASS, ./pkg/dhcpserver PASS, go vet clean;
#14604 cells still pass.

Risk: a name co-resident with a foreign RR of the sibling's type is
accepted once the manager owns the sibling (the store cannot
classify the foreign RR) — the same residual #14604 documented for
skip-existing. Per-family DHCIDs mean a name can carry two DHCID
RRs; RFC 4701 readers see both as ownership markers, and each is
removed by its own family's guarded delete.

Closes #14602

the secure-tunnel, VLAN sub-interface, and merged non-VLAN models
(stateless survives only if every DHCPv6 unit is stateless; IA types
union), so stateless and PD-only DHCPv6 do not widen the keep.
The #10718 unit-sink census records the closed-enum keep sink.
CLAUDE.md, pkg/networkd/README.md and docs/log/14594.md record the
contract.

## PR #14777 — config: gate RA default-lifetime against max interval (#14605) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14605-campaign`

Why:
RFC 4861 §6.2.1 requires AdvDefaultLifetime to be 0 or within
[MaxRtrAdvInterval, 9000], defaulting to 3*MaxRtrAdvInterval.
`crossCheckRAIntervals` checked only `min <= 0.75*max` (#4525), so
`default-lifetime 10` with `max-advertisement-interval 600` committed
and hosts lost their default route (and inherited RDNSS/PREF64)
seconds after each RA. An unset lifetime stayed a fixed 1800s even at
max 1800 — one interval, no loss tolerance.

What:
- `crossCheckRAIntervals` (strict commit / commit-check / CheckText /
  #9619 peer pipeline) rejects an explicit positive `default-lifetime`
  below the effective max (configured max, or 600s when unset) or above
  9000, naming RFC 4861 §6.2.1; tolerant Load/SyncApply warns as before.
- New `RAInterfaceConfig` helpers (`EffectiveMaxAdvInterval`,
  `DefaultRouterLifetime` = min(3*max, 9000), `EffectiveRouterLifetime`)
  are the single derivation used by `buildRA`, Manager `Status()`, and
  `show`; inherited RDNSS/PREF64 floor at the derived default
  (RFC 8106 §5.1), so explicit-0 keeps DNS/NAT64 while declining
  default-router duty.
- NOT changed: the 0..65535 per-leaf wire bound, send-sink clamps, and
  explicit PREF64 RFC 8781 handling.

Validation:
- RED (sender.go + store.go swapped to HEAD, tests kept): new CheckText
  cells get nil for dl=10/max=600 and dl=9001; wire cells decode 1800s
  at max 1800 instead of 5400s.
- GREEN: `go test ./pkg/ra -count=1` ok; targeted configstore cells
  (#14605, #4525, #9619 peer pipeline, shipped HA configs) ok;
  `go test ./pkg/config -run 'TestSchema4119|TestSchema3895|TestCompile4119'`
  ok; `go vet` (ra/configstore/config/cli), gofmt, `git diff --check`
  clean. The full `./pkg/configstore` suite exceeded the 280s lane
  timeout under concurrent sibling lanes (unrelated contention);
  targeted RA/shipped-config cells pass — main agent should rerun the
  full configstore suite unloaded.

Risk:
Previously committable lifetimes in (0, max) or (9000, 65535] now fail
strict commit but still load tolerantly with a warning; their
RDNSS/PREF64 are floored at 3*max while the short Router Lifetime is
honored verbatim. Unset lifetimes with max > 600 now advertise 3*max
(the RFC default); `show`/Status report the derived value.

Closes #14605

## PR #14780 — telemetry: emit Junos sd-syslog RT_FLOW envelope (#14611) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14611-campaign`

Why:
sd-syslog wrapped the flat RT_FLOW body in a NILVALUE RFC 5424 header
(`xpf - - - RT_FLOW SESSION_OPEN src=...`), so SIEM parsers keyed on
`RT_FLOW_SESSION_*` MSGID and the `junos@2636` SD lost policy, zone
and NAT attribution. `structured` carried the SD only as RFC 3164 MSG
