## PR #14784 — cluster: chunk persistent-NAT lease batches below sync cap (#14607) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14607-campaign`

Why:
QueuePersistentNatLeaseBatch wrote the whole idle persistent-NAT lease
snapshot as one session-sync frame with no byte budget. Past roughly
215k-250k idle leases the frame exceeds the receiver's 16 MiB cap,
receiveLoop returns, and its deferred handleDisconnect tears down HA
session sync on every 30 s push, so the #8121 idle-lease rebuild never
converges. An export failure in the same daemon loop was logged only
at Debug, hiding the no-snapshot regime.

What:
- pkg/cluster: shared named maxSyncPayload constant used by the
  receive loop, the handshake reader (oversize now also counted), and
  the lease sender.
- encodePersistentNatLeaseBatchFrames splits one origin/generation
  batch into complete sub-cap batch payloads; records stay whole,
  oversize/unencodable records drop and count via
  MalformedRecordsDropped, and QueuePersistentNatLeaseBatch refuses
  any frame over the cap. Chunks are additive at the same generation:
  chunk one carries the clear barrier, the rest rebuild the set, and
  empty batches still emit exactly one barrier frame.
- pkg/daemon: export failures are counted
  (PersistentNatLeaseExportFailures) and logged at Warn rate-limited
  to once per minute, replacing the Debug-only log.
- NOT changed: Rust helper export, receiver import semantics, wire
  version, or message type 41.

Validation:
- New cluster cells pass for 262,144 remote-less leases, 1300x1024
  IPv6-remotes leases, and 300,000 leases: >1 frame each, every frame
  <= maxSyncPayload, and a receiver fed all frames in order delivers
  every lease under the same origin/generation. Encoder-bound and
  oversize-record cells pass; empty batch yields one barrier frame.
- Existing TestPersistentNatLease* and TestQueueStampsFullSetSeq pass.
- New daemon cell passes: first export failure Warns and counts, a
  second inside a minute counts without re-warning, a third after the
  interval Warns again.
- go vet ./pkg/cluster ./pkg/daemon clean. Full pkg/cluster suite has
  only TestInstallTableProducerToResendEndToEnd9752 failing, identical
  on the base commit (pre-existing, base-attributed).

Risk:
Mixed-version peers see ordinary type-41 additive chunks at one
generation and import the union; pre-#11486 peers ignore type 41 as
before. A single record over the frame budget drops counted instead
of disconnecting sync (unreachable for legal <=1024-remote leases).
The Rust helper export response is not paged; the capped transport
was the HA sync frame, now chunked.

Closes #14607

## PR #14785 — grpcapi/authz: non-root management-port holder no longer kills xpfd or impersonates it [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14581-management-port-holder`

Closes #14581

## Problem
#8233 made a persistent `EADDRINUSE` on `127.0.0.1:50051` fatal keyed only on the error, with no holder-UID check. Any non-root local process — an SSH remote forward (`ssh -R 127.0.0.1:50051:...`), a compromised service UID — holds the port as well as a second xpfd, so xpfd exited into a `Restart=on-failure` loop while the squatter impersonated the management server (including harvesting secrets in `set`/`load` RPCs).

## Fix (acceptance criteria from the issue)
1. **xpfd does not exit for a uid≠0 holder** — at the #8233 grace expiry the supervisor now attributes the LISTEN socket from `/proc/net/tcp{,6}` (`pkg/authz.LookupListenerOwner`: exact row wins, wildcard fallback, neighbour/ESTABLISHED rows are not the holder). Fatal (`ErrManagementPortHeld`) requires a **privileged** holder (uid 0 or xpfd's own uid — the duplicate-xpfd case, preserved). Non-root or unattributed holders stay supervised, alarm at ERROR on the grace cadence, and the daemon binds when the squatter leaves.
2. **cli/pkg/upgrade refuse a non-root server** — `pkg/authz.DialContext` (wired via `grpc.WithContextDialer` into `cmd/cli` dialOpts and `pkg/upgrade` grpcCluster) verifies at dial time, before any RPC byte is written, that a loopback server is privileged-owned, using the mirrored ESTABLISHED-row lookup. Non-loopback fabric targets are untouched (their #4107/#4122 chain owns them).
3. **sshd drop-in denies forwarding** — `DisableForwarding yes` in both the image factory drop-in (`scripts/image/bake.py`) and every daemon-managed drop-in (`buildSSHDConfig`).

## Tests
- New: injected-holder supervisor cells (non-root/root/own-uid/unattributed/lookup-failure), a **real-socket** non-root holder cell (uid-aware, skips where a root runner makes holder≡daemon indistinguishable) plus recovery-after-squatter-leaves, /proc fixture attribution matrix, client foreign-uid refusal, bake `sshd -T` forwarding assertion. Existing #8233 fatal test now injects a uid-0 holder (its premise is the duplicate-xpfd case).
- Mutations verified: always-fatal, Privileged=any-found, and client-accepts-foreign each fail the new cells.
- Suites: `pkg/authz`, `pkg/grpcapi`, `pkg/upgrade` pass; `cmd/cli` and `pkg/daemon` full runs hit pre-existing base failures (9-file gofmt backlog incl. `pkg/config`/`pkg/dataplane`, and a load-flaky credential test passing in isolation on both trees) — daemon SSH shards pass on head. `go vet` clean on all touched packages.
- Remaining validation per the issue: the VM check (`ssh -N -R 127.0.0.1:50051:127.0.0.1:9` as a read-only login across `systemctl restart xpfd`) needs a live appliance; the forwarding denial now removes that actor on baked images.

## PR #14786 — nat: dedupe deterministic pool to first occurrence (#14623) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14623-campaign`

Why:
Go expandPoolV4 appended every expanded pool address verbatim, while
Rust expand_pool_address keeps only the first occurrence via the
seen-set threaded by its production caller. On a tolerated overlapping
pool (pre-#5144 lenient load or mixed-version sync) every later pool
index shifted, so the CLI/gRPC/REST deterministic lookup named a
different external address and reverse-attributed a translated tuple
to the wrong subscriber with no error.

What:
Apply the same first-occurrence seen-set in expandPoolV4 mode 1 only,
keyed on the host-order u32 so a bare host, its /32 form, and a
CIDR-enumerated host collide. Mode 2 stays verbatim because it mirrors
NAT64 parse_pool_v4, which has no seen-set and derives host_count from
the verbatim pool length. Add the decisive overlapping-pool regression
(pool [203.0.113.1/32, 203.0.113.0/30] -> [.1,.0,.2,.3]) with
forward/reverse witnesses, and re-pin the legacy duplicate-address
test to first-occurrence semantics. NOT changed: the Rust dataplane
(already dedupes), the strict commit gate, and the mode-2 pool.

failed with pool [.1 .0 .1 .2 .3] vs want [.1 .0 .2 .3]; forward
100.64.0.4 returned 203.0.113.1 instead of 203.0.113.2.

./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run Deterministic -count=1 PASS; go vet

## PR #14789 — postrm: restore transit sysctls only on xpf-owned hosts (#14620) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14620-campaign`

Closes #14620

## Defect
`debian/xpf.postrm` `cleanup_transit_state` unconditionally wrote `1` to `ip_forward` and `ipv6/conf/all/forwarding` on `remove|purge` whenever `xpfd transit-barrier remove` exited 0 — which it does vacuously when no barrier ever existed (`RemoveTransitBarrier`: absent → nil). A foreign host that merely installed the package and never committed a config (xpf never wrote the sysctls there, per the #10733 contract) had forwarding silently flipped 0→1 on uninstall: an unfiltered IPv4/IPv6 router, plus loss of v6 RA acceptance.

## Fix
- **Daemon** (`pkg/daemon/daemon_transit_gate.go`): `recordTransitGateOwnership()` runs from every latch arm of `shouldManageTransitGate()`, before any gate sysctl write. It durably writes `/var/lib/xpf/transit-gate-owned` (`fsatomic.WriteFileDurable`) with the host's pre-xpf values (`ipv4=`/`ipv6=`), never overwriting an existing record so priors survive restarts/reinstalls. Best-effort: failure logs Warn, gate still actuates fail-closed.
- **postrm**: restores ONLY when the ownership record exists, restoring each recorded prior (new `restore_transit_sysctl` helper; values normalised 0|1, missing/corrupt → 1 so an owned host is never stranded transit-closed). No record → log + leave both sysctls untouched. `remove` leaves the record; `purge` consumes it after the restore (package-derived runtime state under `/var/lib/xpf`, not `/etc/xpf`).

## Regression
- `test/debian/postrm-test.sh`: decisive z6 cell `remove_never_owned_keeps_sysctls_closed` (no record, 0/0, stub barrier-remove succeeds → both stay 0) — **RED on the pre-fix postrm** (`FAIL: IPv4 forwarding opened on never-owned host (#14620)`), GREEN after; purge twin, owned/mixed/corrupt-record controls, purge-consumes-record; pre-existing owned cells seeded via `mark_transit_owned`. Barrier-failure cell still stays 0. Full suite passes under `sh` and `dash`.
- `pkg/daemon/transit_ownership_record_14620_test.go`: record-on-latch (priors captured, never overwritten) and no-record-on-never-owned.
- Note: the container test run wrote `/var/lib/xpf/transit-gate-owned` during the suite (same host-writing class as the pre-existing sysctl test seams; system file removed, follow-up cleanup harmless).

## Checks for main agent
- `go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run 'TestTransitOwnership|TestForeignNeverCommitted|TestCommittedForeignHost|TestApplianceMarkerOwns|TestFirstCommitRollbackRetains' -count=1` (could not complete in this sandbox: host lacks CAP_SYS_ADMIN, netlink socket fails; unrelated churn in transit test files also in flight)
- `go vet ./pkg/daemon/` (earlier run killed by sandbox, rerun)
- Full `./pkg/daemon/` and `./pkg/fsatomic/` suites on a privileged host.
- Residual: hosts owned by a pre-#14620 daemon have no record, so the new postrm leaves their sysctls at the shutdown-closed 0 (fail-closed) rather than restoring 1 — stated in `docs/log/14620.md`.

## PR #14790 — ipsec: require remote identity on responder-only PSK gateways (#14591) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14591-campaign`

## Summary

A responder-only (`dynamic`, `remote_addrs = %any`) PSK VPN whose gateway has no `remote-identity` rendered a `secrets{}` entry with **no `id` selector**. That secret matches any peer, and strongSwan selects keys by the claimed IDi — so a holder of *another* site's PSK could authenticate into this VPN by claiming that site's identity, landing on this VPN's st0/zone (Y09-04, residual of #3952).

## What changed

- **Render belt** (`pkg/ipsec/policy.go`): a responder-only PSK VPN whose gateway has no remote-identity is now **skipped by name** — the same fail-closed class as #14139's missing-secret skip. No connection, no orphan secret, and the rendered-set exclusion makes Apply unload it and tear down any stale SA. Pubkey (certificate) VPNs are unaffected.
- **Commit gate** (`pkg/config`): new `validateIPsecResponderIdentityStrict`, wired into `runUniformGatesIPsecEvent` with `lenientIPsecResponderIdentity`. Strict commit hard-rejects with a message naming the fix; tolerant load / HA peer-sync downgrades to a warning while the render belt keeps the unscoped connection from loading. The auth determination mirrors #14139's `ipsecVPNAuthNeedsPSK`, so cert VPNs are never rejected.
- With a remote-identity configured, the existing render already emits `remote { id = ... }` and scopes the secret to it (#3952); the new tests pin **both directions** of credential isolation (rw secret never claims the site identity, site secret never claims the rw identity).
- Migrated the pre-existing responder-only fixtures that encoded the vulnerable shape to carry a remote-identity; updated `pkg/ipsec/README.md` and `docs/config-schema.md`.

**NOT changed:** `dynamic hostname <fqdn>` rendering (#14590's separate mechanism) and no-ID secrets for non-responder shapes (fixed peers are scoped by gateway address).

## Validation

- **RED on base** (`c4848b1ae`): `TestResponderOnlyPSKScoping14591` rendered the unscoped rw connection + secret (`secret = "rw-secret"` with no `id-` selector); the config gate did not exist.
- **GREEN:** new `pkg/ipsec` + `pkg/config` tests pass; full `pkg/ipsec` suite passes; `go vet` clean.
- Full `pkg/config` suite shows only the pre-existing census-family failures (`TestCompactBlockEquivalenceInventory2419` panic, ISIS #14400 cell) — outside this change's scope; Main should confirm base attribution on current master.

## Risk

A persisted responder-only PSK VPN without a remote-identity now loses that tunnel at render (warning names the fix) and is rejected at strict commit. Operators must configure `remote-identity` on the gateway — deliberate, fail-closed. See `docs/log/14591.md`.

⚠️ Worktree note for Main: the sibling #14588 lane's uncommitted edits collided into this lane's worktree via the shared stash registry during the run. The commit was staged hunk-by-hunk and **contains zero #14588 content** (verified). Four duplicate unstaged #14588 files remain in `/var/worktrees/wt-14591` — discard them with the worktree; do not commit them here. The branch was **not** rebased (dirty worktree); HEAD is an ancestor of master, so the diff is clean — rebase at merge time as usual.

Closes #14591

## PR #14791 — ra: advertise deprecated PD prefix with preferred lifetime 0 (#14606) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14606-campaign`

Why:
A DHCPv6-PD IAPREFIX with preferred lifetime 0 (deprecated, RFC 8415 §21.22) lost that value at two sentinel collisions: `buildRAConfigs` left it unset, and `pkg/ra` substituted the 7-day default for every `PreferredLife <= 0` then clamped to valid. LAN hosts therefore preferred the ISP's dying prefix for its whole valid life, inverting graceful renumbering (RFC 9096 L-15).

What:
Add `config.RAPrefix.PreferredLifeSet`, mirroring `DefaultLifetimeSet` (#4119). The compiler sets it when the `preferred-lifetime` leaf is present; `buildRAConfigs` stamps it on the PD path after the #14598 remaining-lifetime decay (inside the `ValidLifetime > 0` branch, preserving the no-clock sender-default sentinel), so a preferred lifetime decayed to 0 mid-life also advertises deprecated. `buildRA` honors an explicit preferred life including 0, while unset keeps the 7-day default. `configEqual` and `sortRAPrefixes` include the wire-affecting flag; the golden fixture gains `PreferredLifeSet: false` throughout. NOT changed: valid-lifetime decay/expiry — the separate #14598 fix this composes with (rebased onto it; the conflict resolution keeps `RemainingLifetimes` decay + `remValid <= 0` skip and only adds the flag).

Validation:
RED pre-fix (new tests cannot compile without the field; wire cell emitted preferred=7200). Mutation: reverting `sender.go` re-reds preferred=7200/want 0; reverting daemon stamping re-reds PreferredLifeSet=false. GREEN post-rebase: `pkg/ra`, `pkg/daemon`, `pkg/config` 14606-targeted tests pass (deprecated grant {0,7200}→wire pref 0, 3600 control, no-leaf 7-day-default control, legacy-unset delegated control, decayed-to-zero cell at valid 3200, compiler explicit-0/absent/3600 cells, configEqual restart cell); full `pkg/ra` suite passes; `go vet` clean. Full `pkg/config` suite panicked in `TestSlotEscapeSweep` at the 600s suite timeout under parallel load; standalone that test passes on this branch (118s) and pristine `origin/master` (146s). Full `pkg/daemon` suite not re-run end-to-end post-rebase; RA/PD-targeted tests pass.

Risk:
An operator-authored explicit `preferred-lifetime 0` now also advertises deprecated instead of silently defaulting — the RFC-correct reading of an explicit leaf. Prefixes without the leaf are byte-identical on the wire.

Closes #14606

**Why:** Two source-NAT rules sharing one pool share one allocator and one endpoint-independent lease (#9389), but persistent-NAT grants were recorded on a single flat list. A permissive rule's `any-remote-host` permit therefore authorized arbitrary remote hosts inbound on the strict rule's reflexive binding across security zones.

- `PersistentPermissions` now buckets grants by a deterministic fold of the admitting rule's `(from_zone, to_zone)`; lease and flow keys stay completely zone-unaware, so release/HA/NAT64 paths keep deriving them unchanged.

- Idle-lease records carry `egress_scope` per grant bucket (export one record per bucket, import merges buckets and reclaims expired idle leases inline). Helper wire bumped to protocol **v50** on both sides with manager gates rejecting old/missing scopes. Cluster binary encoding appends `EgressScope` after `RoutingScope`; wire fixture regenerated.

**Validation:**
- New Rust cells: `nat::tests_persistent_zone_14322::{shared_pool_persistent_permissions_do_not_leak_across_egress_zones_14322, shared_pool_strict_first_then_permissive_does_not_widen_14322}` — base RED (`Permitted` where `Denied` required on base `wt-14322-base`) → GREEN 2/2.
- Rust full NAT module: **657 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored**.
- Go suites: `pkg/cluster -run TestPersistentNatLease`, `pkg/dataplane/userspace` lease/snapshot filters, `pkg/daemon -run TestPersistentNat` — all pass.

**Risk:**

- Legacy unscoped grants (scope `0`: NAT64, unknown zone, direct allocator calls) keep today exact behavior.

## PR #14797 — config: model endpoint literal in load classifier and parse adjudicated text in store (#14572) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14572-campaign`

## Summary

#14572 (Y01-01, residual of #14145): a token-initial bracketed endpoint
literal hid denied config from the restricted-class `load` gate while
the store applied it. `ClassifyLoadContent` treated a token-initial
`[` as list sugar and left the scanner at a token boundary, so a
following block/line comment opener blanked every later statement in
the gate's view. The real lexer instead lexes
`[`+identrun+`]:`+identrun as ONE identifier (#5182), so no comment
opens, and the store's hierarchical branches re-parsed the raw body
and applied the hidden `root-authentication` / security-policy
subtrees. A regex-restricted operator (with one allowed free-text
leaf) could write any config path over CLI, REST and gRPC.

## Fix (both halves of "parse once")

- `pkg/config/authz_config_load_9892.go`: the classifier now models
  `tryBracketedEndpointLiteral` via the new
  `bracketedEndpointLiteralEnd` (same shape, reusing the lexer's own
  `isIdentChar`), also immediately after a boundary `]` where the
  real lexer's gap loop retries the literal. A matched literal is
  token text; non-literal brackets keep the #14145 list-sugar
  behaviour, so genuine comments after `[ /* ... */` still hide prose.
- `pkg/configstore/store_command.go`: `LoadMergeAsPlantClass` and
  `parseOverrideContent` now parse the classifier's uncommented text
  instead of the raw body, so the store applies exactly the
  representation the gate adjudicated, by construction.

Not changed: `SyncApply`/on-disk parsers (not gate-adjudicated), the
real lexer, flat routing.

## Tests

- `pkg/config/authz_config_load_14572_test.go`: the issue's decisive
  probe plus the line-comment spelling, both carried on an allowed
  `description` leaf, with bare-denied/allowed premise controls; a
  renderer test proving the denied leaves reach adjudication (no
  refuse-everything pass); narrowness controls (genuine endpoint
  literal loads, genuine comments still hide prose).
- `pkg/configstore/loadmerge_endpoint_literal_14572_test.go`: the
  acceptance property `set(store-applied) ⊆ set(LoadMutationLines(body))`
  over bracket/comment placements (token-initial, mid-token,
  stray-`]`, quoted, genuine comment/list controls) against the
  hierarchical merge branch, plus the same property for override.
- `docs/log/14572.md` records defect, fix and RED/GREEN.

RED on `a615690ed` (tests only): all four bypass bodies ALLOWED for
class `limited`; store applied the denied leaf unadjudicated.
GREEN with fix: focused `14572|14145|9892|10305|10734` runs pass in
both packages; `go vet` clean; full `pkg/configstore` suite passes

*(truncated — 57 lines total)*

## PR #14798 — config: require dh-group on referenced IKE proposals (#14588) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14588-campaign`

## Summary

An IKE proposal with **no `dh-group`** passed strict commit but rendered `proposals = aes256-sha256` — a proposal with no key-exchange method — which strongSwan 6.1.0 refuses (`invalid value for: proposals, config discarded, loaded 0 of 1`), discarding every connection in the file. Finding **Y09-01**, the #7165 commit⇒loadable breach. The DH value gate only sees present-but-bad values; an absent `dh-group` (`DHGroup 0`, no `InvalidSpec`) was invisible to it.

## Fix

- **`pkg/config`** — new `validateIPsecIkeDHGroupsPresentStrict` walks VPN → gateway → ike-policy → ike-proposal (plus the legacy direct-proposal fallback where the ike-policy value names an IPsec proposal) and rejects a DH-less IKE proposal referenced by a rendered VPN at strict commit, naming `dh-group`. It is placed **below** the IKE chain gate so dangling-chain diagnostics still win, and wired through new `lenientIKEProposalMissingDH` so tolerant load / peer-sync warn instead of bricking (#1960).
- **`pkg/ipsec`** — `ikeDHGroupMissing` filters DH-less proposals in `resolveIKESettings` (chain and legacy forms) through the existing `errDHGroupUnresolved` skip sentinel: a lenient-loaded copy skips only the affected VPN and other VPNs load.
- **Out of scope by design**: ESP proposals with no `dh-group` remain valid no-PFS suites (Junos `basic` ESP set); orphan IKE proposals no VPN renders still commit; no default DH group is invented.

## Validation

RED/GREEN (decisive cells from the issue):

- **RED on pristine `d08fbcf95`** (prod reverted, tests kept): `TestStrictRejectsIKEProposalNoDHGroup14588` fails (strict commit accepted the DH-less fixture), `TestTolerantWarnsIKEProposalNoDHGroup14588` fails (no dh-group warning), `TestRenderSkipsIKEProposalNoDHGroup14588` / `TestResolveIKESettingsNoDHGroupSentinel14588` / `TestResolveIKESettingsLegacyNoDHGroup14588` fail (DH-less VPN renders). The issue's controls (`group14` loads, `group99` rejected) pass on base.
- **GREEN after fix**: `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 14588 -count=1` PASS; `go test ./pkg/ipsec/ -run 14588 -count=1` PASS; `go vet ./pkg/config/ ./pkg/ipsec/` clean.
- **Controls preserved**: `dh-group group14` / `14` / `group19` / `2` / `group32` compile clean on strict and lenient paths with no dh-group warning; `dh-group group99` still rejected naming `99`; orphan DH-less proposal, no-PFS ESP proposal, and `proposal-set standard` fixtures still commit; `TestIKEPolicyProposalsDanglingSecondRejected` still names the dangling reference (gate ordering preserved).
- **Full suites**: `go test ./pkg/ipsec/ -count=1` PASS. `go test ./pkg/config/ -count=1` panics in the `TestCompactBlock*`/`TestCompactDepth1*` census (`validateRethRedundancyGroupTokensAST` → `nodeVal` at `compiler_applications.go:1340`) **identically on pristine HEAD** (verified in a throwaway base worktree at `d08fbcf95`); excluding the panic family, the HEAD-vs-base failure sets are **identical (28 pre-existing failures, all `#14139` PSK-presence or older gates hitting pre-existing fixtures)** — no new failures.
- `gofmt` clean on touched files (`pkg/config/compiler_opts.go`'s struct literal is not gofmt-clean on base; added lines match surrounding style).

## Risk

Strict commit now refuses a previously-accepted shape (an IKE proposal used by a VPN without `dh-group`); the operator fix is one line (`dh-group group<N>`). Already-persisted or peer-synced copies still boot with a warning, and the affected VPN is skipped rather than taking every tunnel down with charon's whole-file refusal. Orphan proposals and no-PFS ESP proposals are untouched.

Closes #14588

## PR #14799 — userspace-dp: never complete a TCP handshake on a closing entry (#14630) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14630-campaign`

Closes #14630

## Defect (Y25-01)
SYN → SYN-ACK → RST → bare ACK: `stamp_tcp_close` left `handshake_pending` set and `handshake_completed` consulted only packet flags, so the bare ACK completed the handshake and `propagate_tcp_state_to_companion` re-armed the reverse companion onto the 300 s established window. Forward reaped at RST+2 s; reverse survived as an uncounted orphan row admitting server→client hits for up to 5 min.

## Fix
Gate `promote_from_reverse` / `promote_from_asymmetric_ack` / `handshake_completed` on `!entry.closing` in `lookup.rs`, mirror in the `update_session` HA twin (+ its #1752 reference parity mirror), and refuse to promote/complete a closing companion in `propagate_tcp_state_to_companion`.

## Tests
New `rst_ack_handshake_14630_tests.rs`: decisive RST+ACK sequence (both halves stay on `TCP_RST_TIMEOUT_NS`, `expired==2` at RST+3 s, no orphan, count back to 0), SYN-ACK-first reverse-ACK variant, `update_session` twin, FIN variant, and a no-close control.
- RED on base: 4 failed, control passed.
- GREEN: 5 passed; full `session::` suite 450 passed (incl. #10885/#7342/#13676-78).

See `docs/log/14630.md`.

## PR #14809 — userspace-dp: recycle deterministic ports on release (#14625) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14625-campaign`

Why:
Removing `port deterministic` reuses the same PortAllocator for round-robin PAT because `SourceNatPoolAllocatorKey` excludes mode. Deterministic frees used `free_no_recycle`, clearing the bit with no recycle token; PAT `claim()` reaches free ports only via its fresh cursor or the recycle FIFO, so once the cursor passed a freed deterministic offset the port was stranded — clear bit, reported free, yet `AllocatorExhausted` — until the pool key changed. The HA-synced release path had the identical hole.

What:
- `free_translated_port` loses its `recycle: bool` and always calls `free_recycle`; all callers (live unlink, lease teardowns, deterministic v4/v6 give-backs, GC reclaim, idle-import rollback) and the `freed` vectors updated. `claim_in_block` ignores the ring and the ring holds at most one token per offset (#7174), so recycling is harmless while deterministic and required after a flip.
- The `deterministic` flag stays for BIB/lease identity; stale no-recycle comments updated across `allocator.rs`, `source/{nat64_ports,synced,overlap}.rs`, `nat64.rs`.
- New `tests_det_flip_14625` decisive cell + PAT control; #9130/#14091/#5178 cells that asserted the defective no-recycle contract updated and renamed.
- NOT changed: allocator key (mode-in-key rejected — a fresh allocator would strand live deterministic releases), claim paths, cursor, Go owner-key contract. Full record: `docs/log/14625.md`.

Validation:
- RED on base `d19cc0368` (test + registration only): flip cell failed `Err(AllocatorExhausted)` vs `Ok(20000)`; PAT control passed.
- GREEN targeted (`14625 9130 5178 14091`): all pass.
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp nat::`: 654 passed, 3 failed — `tests_idle_lease_sync_8121` (`..._11496`, `..._11475`, `..._13692`), reproduced identically on unmodified base, pre-existing and unrelated.

Risk:
A still-deterministic pool now accumulates at most `range` recycle tokens per address (bounded by the #7174 dedup bitset); PAT pops go through the normal claim CAS, so no duplicate identity is possible.

Closes #14625

## PR #14811 — config: reject packed tcp-mss tails at commit (#14576) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14576-campaign`

Why:
  `security flow tcp-mss <kind>` read only the selected MSS token;
  a second kind or trailing tokens packed into the same kind node
  (`gre-out mss 1300 all-tcp mss 1350`, `all-tcp mss 1350 bogus 7`,
  `all-tcp 1350 9999`) committed clean and were silently dropped —
  the configured clamp (notably `all-tcp`, the PMTU safeguard) never
  applied while `show configuration` still displayed it. Junos
  rejects these spellings; #8939 requires every leaf to compile or
  the command to fail. (Y03-01)

    `selectMSSToken` branch-for-branch (including the #1979
    mixed-shape precedence and #8824/#8838 branches);
    `mssLeftoverTokens` accounts for every token past the consumed
    value grammar across packed hierarchical nodes, braced `mss`
    children, flat-set value-carrier children, unparseable-child
    fallbacks, and never-read sibling children. Deliberately
    discarded #1979 tokens are not leftover, so mixed shapes keep
    compiling to the flat value.
  - `pkg/config/compiler_security_flow.go`: `checkTCPMSSKindTail`
    rejects leftovers on the strict path and warns on the lenient
    (boot/peer-sync) path, wired into `checkTCPMSSKind` before the
    range gate and into the `ipsec-vpn` branch before its rejection
    so a tail cannot hide behind it.

    opacity, dataplane/wire/show behavior. No synthetic multi-kind
    splitting — Junos has no such statement.

    (pkg/config, 14 defect rows + controls incl. two-set-line,
    braced, #1979 mixed, empty-body, prior typo/range refusals) and

  - RED on pristine master `a615690ed`: every defect row accepted,

    `TestCheckText*` set pass; `go vet` + `gofmt` clean.
  - Full `go test ./pkg/config/` panics in the compact-census
    family and times out in the spelling differential on pristine
    master too (verified in a detached base worktree), and
    `TestGroupRouteFilterORBesideInline14416` fails identically

  A legacy persisted/peer config carrying a packed tail now

## PR #14814 — userspace-dp: dedupe NAT64 pool members on first occurrence (#14624) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14624-campaign`

Why: On a tolerated load (legacy, mixed-version, or leniently loaded
config) the same NAT64 pool address can arrive twice, once bare and
once with the /32 host mask Go range-expansion stamps. Both NAT64
pool loops pushed every `parse_pool_v4` result with no seen-set, so
each duplicate got an independent occupancy bitmap and round-robin
placement minted the same (address, port) BIB for two IPv6
subscribers — reply traffic crosses subscribers (RFC 6146 §3.5).
The Go strict message and the overlap.rs #10700 note both claim
first-occurrence dedupe on tolerated loads; #10700 fixed only the
SNAT parser, so both claims were false for NAT64.

What: Add a first-occurrence `FxHashSet` seen-set to both NAT64 pool
loops in `nat64.rs` — the `from_snapshots_with_previous` build loop
and `nat64_rule_identity` — preserving first-seen order so the reuse
key, the #6982 aggregate charge, `PortAllocator` sizing, and
`build_deterministic_v6` host_count all see the identical deduped
pool. Add `nat64_14624` regression tests (unique tuples across 16
subscribers, identity == built pool, deterministic arm over a
duplicated list) and make the #6227 host-count-overflow fixture use
distinct addresses, since repeated copies now correctly dedupe.
NOT changed: `overlap.rs` or the Go strict message — the fix makes
both claims true rather than editing them.

Validation: `cargo test --bins nat64_14624` RED on base (pool_v4
`[203.0.113.1, 203.0.113.1]`, both tests failed) and GREEN after
the fix (2 passed). `cargo test --bins nat64::`: 218 passed.
`cargo test --bins nat::`: 652 passed, 3 failed in
`tests_idle_lease_sync_8121`, base-attributed at origin/master
8316f83a7 (identical failures on pristine base). Full crate suite
not run in-lane.

Risk: A pool now has fewer allocator slots when it carried true
duplicates; tuples stay unique so capacity accounting is more
honest, not smaller for any valid config. Deterministic pools
sized from duplicated lists report the deduped host_count;
subscribers only addressable via the phantom duplicate position
now fail closed, which is the intended BIB-uniqueness behavior.

Closes #14624

## PR #14815 — userspace-dp: make synthetic best-effort residual beside real queues (#14637) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14637-campaign`

Why: The #11428 synthetic best-effort queue was created with
guarantee_enabled=true at the full shaping rate even beside real
scheduler-map queues. The guarantee selector runs before strict-priority
surplus, so backlogged unclassified traffic could starve rate-less
priority classes, and the synthetic queue displaced an operator's
renamed queue-0 class (e.g. exact-capped be) as the default queue,
bypassing its cap for unclassified traffic.

What: In build_cos_iface_config, the synthetic queue is residual-only
(guarantee_enabled: false, shaping rate kept for burst/surplus) when
real queues exist; the no-real-queue case keeps the documented sole
root-shaped guarantee. Default selection among equally-low queues now
prefers queue 0, then literal best-effort, then lowest queue id.

best-effort queues, exact queues, or the priority-first ordering.

10000000), W2 default was synthetic id 1 not queue 0, queue-0 tiebreak
failed (1 != 0). GREEN: 4/4 14637 tests pass including the drain cell

guarantee-enabled control). cos filter: 719 passed, 1 failed
(additive_wire_exhaustive_literals_only_ever_decrease_7689,

  high-water seeds. `peer_for_dest` and the control-thread
  `peer_endpoints()` re-seed both follow the roam with no

## PR #14819 — config: reject Kea-refused DHCP pool values at commit (#14601) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14601-campaign`

Why: the compiler copied DHCP pool subnet, address-range, router and dns-server leaves as raw tokens and the Kea generators emitted them verbatim. A subnet without /len, a range outside the subnet or inverted, or a wrong-family router/dns-server committed clean, then Kea refused the whole rendered file and every pool of that family stopped, healthy pools included — the #9785 outage reached through four more leaves.

What: validateDHCPPoolValuesStrict (pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_dhcp_pool_14601.go) checks each pool, naming server/group/pool/leaf: subnet parses as a prefix of the server family (a bare address is Kea's no-/len refusal); each address-range bound parses, matches the family, lies inside the masked subnet, and low <= high; a v4 router is a valid IPv4 address (the v6 renderer emits no router option, so that leaf stays ungated); every dns-server element parses and matches the family. Wired in runUniformGatesDHCPApp after the #9785 duplicate-subnet gate, with lenientDHCPPoolValues downgrading to a warning on tolerant load/peer-sync so persisted configs still boot (#1960). The #6696 cells that encoded the old mixed-family contract are aligned (test-only, no assertion dropped). NOT changed: the Kea renderer — a mistyped value has no safe kept-pool arbitration, so commit is the gate.

Validation: regression cells fail on origin/master with only the test files present (every refusal case compiles clean; the four controls pass) and pass with the fix — pkg/config TestDHCPPoolValuesRefusedAtCommit14601 (23 cases) + TestDHCPPoolValuesLenientGate14601, pkg/configstore TestCheckTextRefusesBadDHCPPoolValues14601 through CheckText (the Store.Commit composition). Focused config/configstore/dhcpserver runs green; go vet clean. Full pkg/config carries 72 base-attributed failures at this master (sibling gates merged in parallel; verified identical on a clean master worktree); pkg/configstore full suite exceeds the 600s timeout on base and fix alike. No Kea binary in the test environment, so the optional kea-dhcp4 -t render check was not exercised — noted in docs/log/14601.md.

Risk: a persisted or peer-synced config carrying a bad pool value still boots on the tolerant path and reaches Kea exactly as before this gate; only new commits are refused. Residual: domain-name remains ungated (issue dropped its Kea-refusal claim as unverified).

## PR #14820 — cluster: carry deterministic identity on idle-lease sync (#14638) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14638-campaign`

Why:
The cluster idle-lease codec wrote only the 14 non-deterministic
IdleLeaseWire fields, so every idle deterministic NAPT64 BIB exported
with deterministic=true and a V6 identity was stripped in transit and
refused by the peer import gate as identity-busy. The HA guarantee of
the #14242 deterministic BIB feature was silently void on failover,
and the counter pointed operators at identity contention instead.

What:
Add syncMsgPersistentNatLeaseDeterministic (43), whose record layout
appends the seven Deterministic* fields after TimeoutNs; the legacy
type 41 layout is byte-identical. Layout-aware encode/decode helpers
select the deterministic layout iff a batch contains a deterministic
lease, QueuePersistentNatLeaseBatch stamps the matching type on every
chunk frame, and types 41/43 share the generation/sequence handler.
The legacy encoder refuses a deterministic lease instead of stripping
it; the deterministic decoder validates the identity (mode/family,
non-zero parameters) and still demands exact consumption. The Rust
generic source-NAT import now refuses a deterministic-shaped lease as
identity-busy rather than installing it as dynamic. NOT changed:
SessionSyncWireVersion/CurrentHAProtocolVersion (additive type; an old
peer ignores it), the control-socket JSON wire, chunking, or replay
semantics.

Validation:
RED on base: the new reflection round-trip test failed with all seven
fields zeroed (Deterministic=false want true, Mode 0 want 2, HostBase
"" want 2001:db8::). GREEN: go test ./pkg/cluster -run
TestPersistentNatLease|TestLiveSyncMessageCensus|TestPeerCapabilities|TestLeaseCount
-count=1 passes at the final head; go vet clean. Full pkg/cluster
shows only TestInstallTableProducerToResendEndToEnd9752 failing,
identical on unmodified base (base-attributed). Rust: the new
generic-refusal cell and the #14091 BIB cell passed (2/2) and
idle_lease ran 74 passed with the same 3 failures as base; at the
final rebased head the Rust test binary does not compile due to two
stale call sites current master itself carries
(policy_revalidation.rs:461, tests_det_flip_14625.rs:44, E0061) in
files this branch does not touch.

Risk:
Mixed-version pairs lose only deterministic idle leases (type 43 is
ignored by old peers) until both sides upgrade; dynamic leases keep
type 41 in both directions and are never mis-installed. A mixed batch
rides type 43 whole, with dynamic records carrying a validated
all-zero deterministic tail.

Closes #14638

## PR #14821 — userspace-dp: suppress TE and PTB for tunnel-decapped inners (#14642) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14642-campaign`

## Summary
GRE/WireGuard decap fabricates a zero-MAC Ethernet header for the inner
packet (`TUNNEL_DECAP_INGRESS_FLAG`). #12864 gated only `reject`
against reflecting that fake L2; the Time Exceeded and Packet-Too-Big
builders reflected it anyway, queueing an unencapsulated ICMP error on
the underlay with destination MAC `00:00:00:00:00:00` — flooded as
unknown unicast, leaking cleartext inner header bytes, breaking
traceroute/PMTUD across the tunnel.

## Fix (#12864 parity — suppress)
- `icmp.rs`: `can_generate_icmp_error_reply` refuses tunnel-decapped
  inners; `build_local_icmp_error_v4/v6` return `None` on the flag as
  defense in depth (covers TE wrappers and reject builders).
- `icmp_ptb.rs`: `ptb_reply_suppressed` returns true on the flag (the
  dispatch caller still drops the oversize original via
  `mtu_signalled`); `build_frag_needed_v4` / `build_packet_too_big_v6`
  return `None` on the flag.
- Both GRE (`gre.rs`) and WG (`wg/decap.rs`, uncovered-forward
  injector) set the same flag, so both legs in the issue are covered.

NOT changed: session-miss install handling for suppressed TE
(Y32-02, owned by #14643 in `poll_descriptor/mod.rs` — companion PR).

## Validation
- RED on `origin/master` ee661259a (tests only): all three new tests
  fail on the gate assertions.
- GREEN after fix: `time_exceeded_suppressed_for_tunnel_decap_inner_14642`,
  `time_exceeded_v6_suppressed_for_tunnel_decap_inner_14642`,
  `ptb_suppressed_for_tunnel_decap_inner_14642` pass, each with native
  positive controls.
- Adjacent icmp/ptb/reject filter run: 907 passed, 2 failed
  (`tests_policy_revocation_8356` #10507 pair, reproduced identically
  on unmodified base — base-attributed).
- Landing note: current `origin/master` (ffcb0bd38) does not compile
  even without this change (`policy_revalidation.rs:461`
  `persistent_inbound_lookup` arity, from #14793); branch is kept on
  the last verified base. Diff touches only `icmp.rs`/`icmp_ptb.rs`
  + tests, no overlap with the broken call site — rebase at landing
  once master compiles.

Docs: `docs/log/14642.md`.

Closes #14642

## PR #14823 — firewall: align sub-byte flexible-match-range to window MSB (#14634) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14634-campaign`

Why:
A sub-byte flexible-match-range field starts at the byte-offset (bit-offset 0, MSB-first per Junos), so `bit-length 4` at `byte-offset 0` is the HIGH nibble of the first byte. Every boundary right-aligned the field pair into the ceil-byte window instead: the compiler defaulted the mask to the low bits, the userspace snapshot builder passed the pair verbatim, and both lo0 nft renderers did the same. On wire byte `0x45` a `bit-length 4 range 0x4` term compared the IHL nibble (5) instead of the version nibble (4), with a clean commit: a discard term failed open and its counter reflected the wrong field. An explicit Junos `match-mask 0xf` produced the identical wrong snapshot.

What:
Left-shift the field value/mask by (windowBits - bitLength) at each matcher boundary so the pair occupies the TOP bits of the window: `pkg/dataplane/userspace/filters.go` (`buildFilterTermSnapshots`), `pkg/daemon/daemon_nft.go` (`nftFlexMatchExpr`), and `pkg/nftables/netlink_build.go` (`flexMatchExprs`). The compiler's stored `FlexMatchConfig` pair stays field-aligned (comment only in `compiler_firewall.go`); byte-aligned lengths shift by 0 and stay byte-identical, BitLength 0 keeps the 32-bit default, and the #3406 uncapped oversized-width behaviour is preserved. The Rust matcher is unchanged (it already compares the full window); its stale 12-bit fixture now uses the aligned pair. NOT changed: `bit-offset` support (no such schema leaf; strict-rejected via #14347) and the retired eBPF compiler.

Validation:
RED pre-fix (re-captured by reverting the three production files with tests in place): `TestFilterSnapshotFlexMatchSubByteMSBAligned14634` wire {Value:0x4 Mask:0xf} want {0x40/0xf0}; `TestFlexMatchExprsSubByteMSBAligned14634` mask 0f want f0; `TestNftFlexMatchExprSubByteMSBAligned14634` renders `@nh,0,8 & 0xf == 0x4` want `@nh,0,8 & 0xf0 == 0x40`. GREEN: those tests plus `TestFlexibleMatchRangeSubByteCompilesFieldAligned14634` (config), `TestNftRuleSubByteFlexRendersAligned14634` (daemon), and Rust `flex_match_subbyte_4bit_reads_high_nibble_14634` (0x45 discards, 0x54 accepts); cargo `flex_match` 13 passed. Suites: pkg/config flex PASS, pkg/nftables full PASS, pkg/daemon flex PASS, pkg/dataplane/userspace snapshot-flex PASS; full userspace suite has one failure (`TestPartialRepublishRefusesQuarantineOnlySkew12247`) reproduced identically on clean origin/master `ffcb0bd38` (base-attributed). go vet clean on all touched packages.

Risk:
Byte-aligned and 32-bit terms are byte-identical on every wire. Sub-byte terms change enforcement to the authored field (the fix); an operator who had compensated with a pre-shifted mask (0xf0 for a 4-bit field) will now double-shift — that spelling was never valid Junos and is called out in `docs/log/14634.md`. No new allocation on any hot path (compile/render time only).

Closes #14634

## PR #14825 — userspace-dp: make is-fragment match trailing fragments only (#14631) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14631-campaign`

Closes #14631

Junos SRX defines `is-fragment` as `fragment-offset 0 except` (trailing fragments only), but the userspace firewall-filter term bit used the any-fragment predicate: an IPv4 first fragment (MF=1, offset 0) carrying TCP/22 matched `frags { from is-fragment; then accept; }` and bypassed following port terms at the stateless layer.

## Fix
- `term_match_extra_from_frame` (the single builder behind every filter/CoS evaluation path) now derives `TermMatchExtra::is_fragment` from the new `is_term_fragment` predicate = `is_non_first_fragment` (fragment offset != 0, both families).
- First/atomic fragments now carry `is_fragment: false` with `l4_present: true`, so they face port/tcp-flags terms; trailing fragments still match `is-fragment`.
- Internal any-fragment consumers (TCP segmentation, NAT64, embedded-ICMP, checksum guards) keep `is_any_fragment` unchanged. The BPF/XDP filter path (`ip frag-off & 0x1fff != 0`) and lo0 nft mirrors were already trailing-only / refused (v4, #13955), so no change there.
- Docs/comments corrected: filter README, feature-gaps, Rust+Go snapshot field comments, and two stale test assertions that pinned any-fragment term behaviour.

## Evidence
- RED on base: `is_fragment_term_14631_first_fragment_faces_port_term_trailing_matches` failed `left: Accept, right: Discard` for MF=1/offset-0 TCP/22 through `frags{is-fragment accept}; no-ssh{tcp 22 discard}`.
- GREEN after fix: same test passes (plain + first-fragment TCP/22 → Discard; trailing v4/v6 → Accept; v6 first → Discard), plus corrected builder/parity tests. Broader `filter::`/`fragment` run: 721 passed; the only 2 failures (`local_origin_tunnel_ipv6_nonfirst_fragment_transmits_without_session_14119`, `stage11_local_ike_passthrough_honors_ingress_input_filter_13637`) reproduce identically on pristine base and are unrelated.
- Log: `docs/log/14631.md`.

Not rebased onto latest origin/master: current master test cfg reportedly does not compile (unrelated `persistent_inbound_lookup` arity break from #14793, per lane note); this branch is based on 9f838a5f7 which compiles and was verified there.

## PR #14827 — userspace-dp: reassemble outer-fragmented native GRE before decap (#14645) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14645-campaign`

Why:
Native GRE could not receive an outer-fragmented datagram: the head
reached the helper and failed decap on a truncated inner, while tails
were steered to the kernel (local arm) or refused (interface-NAT arm),
which has no GRE terminator. Every fragmented GRE datagram was silently
lost with no xpf counter.

What:
Keep head and tails on the helper path and reassemble in a bounded
per-worker pool before decap. Shim: ParsedPacket.is_fragment (IPv4
flags/offset, IPv6 Fragment header via ExtWalk.fragment_seen) plus the
host-executed gre_classify::native_gre_fragment_stays_on_helper
predicate; fragmented native-GRE packets skip the session/local/
interface-NAT/degraded kernel passes and fall through to XSK. Helper:
new gre_reassembly module (64 datagrams, 64 KiB, 32 fragments, 10 s,
counted drops), wired into stage_native_gre_decap with a
GreDecapStage::Buffered disposition. Counter surfaced Rust->Go->
Prometheus as gre_outer_frag_drops_total /
xpf_userspace_gre_outer_frag_drops_total.

Validation:
New tests_gre_outer_frag_14645: IPv4 and IPv6 outer split head+tail
reassemble to exactly one byte-identical decapped inner (whole-decap
controls pass; head alone does not decap), shim truth table asserts a
native-GRE local tail stays on the helper, overlap is a counted drop.
Go vet clean. Rust GREEN run blocked by unrelated open #14802
(origin/master does not compile: policy_revalidation
persistent_inbound_lookup arity); with that site temporarily patched,
cargo check showed no error in this change's files. Main: please run
cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 14645 after #14802 lands.

Risk:
Incomplete fragments buffer per worker within stated bounds and drop
counted on timeout; a mid-datagram RSS/queue change times out counted
rather than decapping.

Closes #14645

leg, enforcement paths.

## PR #14830 — userspace-dp: aggregate WG admission keys on IPv6 /64 and evict LRU at cap (#14639) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-17)

Branch: `fix/14639-campaign`

Why:
Under load, `source_handshake_allowed` keyed the 2048-entry handshake
table on the full IPv6 /128 and refused a new source at the cap, while
GC reclaimed only entries idle for a full second. One host owning a
SLAAC /64 could refresh 2048 /128s inside that window and keep the
table permanently full, so every legitimate peer in another /64 failed
admission, lost rekey, and saw sessions die at REJECT_AFTER_TIME. The
reply table had the same full-address keying. Both diverge from the
Linux reference ratelimiter, which keys IPv6 on /64.

What:
`wg/cookie.rs`: add `source_bucket_key` (IPv6 → /64, v4-mapped v6 →
canonical v4, IPv4 → /32) applied in both `source_reply_allowed` and
`source_handshake_allowed`; add `evict_lru_if_full` so a new key at
the cap evicts the least-recently-refilled bucket instead of failing
closed (table memory stays bounded at 2048 keys). Cookie MAC binding
on the full IP+port is unchanged. Update the #9908 pinning test and
add three #14639 cells (cross-/64 lockout, per-/64 shared burst,
v4-mapped sharing). Log: `docs/log/14639.md`.

Validation:
RED on base `042b46dd27`: the three new cells fail pre-fix (legit peer
locked out; /64 granted 10 admissions instead of the 5-burst;
v4-mapped form granted a fresh burst). GREEN: `cargo test --bin
xpf-userspace-dp -- afxdp::wg::cookie` 25 passed, 0 failed; the three
`handshake_admission_9908` engine cells pass; full `afxdp::wg::`
suite 292 passed with 2 pre-existing `gre_tun_origin_10038` failures
reproduced identically on pristine base.

Risk:
Hosts inside one /64 now share one budget (reference trade-off);
eviction churn from a multi-/64 flood recreates fresh buckets on the
next initiation, so admission is never permanently denied.

Closes #14639

## PR #14834 — audit: sanitize local log and honor severity sentinels (#14732) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14732-campaign`

Why:
Event-mode LocalLogWriter.Send wrote msg raw to the audit file, so a LF forged an extra audit line and ESC/CSI stored verbatim fired on later cat/tail, unlike SyslogClient.Send (#6585). Its ShouldSendEvent arithmetic dropped every emergency under MinSeverity=SeverityEmergency (-1), and ForwardLogMsg called lw.Send unconditionally, bypassing SeverityNone/emergency-only on the aggregation/NAT-pool/clock-skew path.

What:
LocalLogWriter.Send runs termsafe.SanitizeForDisplay before framing (all formats, incl. SendFromEventReader via Send). Add LocalLogWriter.ShouldSend mirroring SyslogClient.ShouldSend (#5314: 0=any, -2=none, -1=emergency-only, else severity<=MinSeverity) and rewire ShouldSendEvent to it. ForwardLogMsg gates local writers with ShouldSend(severity) exactly as syslog clients. New regression tests + README. NOT changed: SendBinary (self-framing binary records).

Validation:
RED pre-fix: ShouldSend undefined (build) + sanitize/sentinel/forward assertions fail on revert of locallog.go/ringbuf.go. GREEN post-fix: targeted 14732 tests pass; full pkg/logging suite ok.

Risk:
Clean messages take the sanitizer allocation-free fast path, so ordinary/UTF-8 audit lines are byte-identical.

Closes #14732

## PR #14838 — dataplane: gate proto-255 out of USERSPACE_SESSIONS steering map (#14648) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14648-campaign`

Closes #14648

## Mechanism
Protocol 255 is `PROTO_FRAGMENT_NO_L4`/`SHIM_PROTO_FRAGMENT_NO_L4`, the sentinel the XDP shim substitutes for every non-first/short fragment (ports 0/0, both families). The steering publish (`write_steering_row`/`publish_session_rows`/`publish_session_map_key`) had no protocol gate and `uses_kernel_local_session_map_entry` checked domain/discriminator/origin/disposition but not protocol; the #6923 guard sits only on the `sessions_v6` conntrack mirror, a different map from the shim-probed `userspace_sessions`. A peer-synced proto-255 LocalDelivery record passed both sync refusals (not TCP/UDP, not a traversable v6 ext header) and wrote a PASS_TO_KERNEL row the shim hits for every protocol's fragments; a live wire proto-255 session wrote the same sentinel row.

## Fix
- `steering_key_is_publishable` (false exactly for 255) required by `uses_kernel_local_session_map_entry`, enforced by filtering `publish_session_rows` and refusing `publish_session_map_key` — the only two `write_steering_row` callers.
- `reject_fragment_sentinel_protocol`: refuse proto-255 sync Install on both families; Deletes still reconstruct (under-match only).
- Correct the #6923 comment (conntrack mirror ≠ shim-probed steering map).

## Regression (RED on origin/master sources, GREEN after)
- `fragment_sentinel_never_publishes_a_steering_row_14648` — synced 255 LocalDelivery v4+v6: no PASS_TO_KERNEL selection, no steering writes; TCP control still publishes one.
- `fragment_sentinel_never_publishes_a_live_row_14648` — live 255 publish writes nothing; TCP control writes.
- `synced_import_refuses_fragment_sentinel_protocol_14648` — 255 Install refused both families, Delete allowed.

Verified: all three tests FAILED with sources reverted to origin/master (tests kept), pass with the fix. See `docs/log/14648.md`.

## PR #14841 — userspace-dp: commit staged mirror clone before recycling ingress frame (#14641) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14641-campaign`

Closes #14641

## Defect (Y31-01)
`enqueue_pending_forwards` ran the success-path `recycle_ingress_frame` before `commit_staged_mirror_clone(..., source_frame)`. Recycle pushes the ingress offset onto `pending_fill_frames` and, at the 1024-entry `FILL_BATCH_SIZE` threshold, synchronously calls `drain_pending_fill`, publishing the chunk to the kernel FILL ring. On the non-in-place arm (cross-UMEM / tunnel / NAT64) the staged mirror clone holds no snapshot — only the in-place arm snapshots first (`snapshot_staged_mirror_clone`) — so the commit copied bytes out of live ingress UMEM that could already be kernel-owned. The kernel could DMA a different packet into the chunk in between, so the analyzer receives another flow's bytes: wrong mirror content and cross-flow disclosure to the mirror target. Forwarding is not corrupted. The in-tree invariant comment ("not yet returned to fill ring") was false on this arm. `neighbor_dispatch.rs` already commits before recycling; only the dispatch site was exposed.

## Fix
- Move `commit_staged_mirror_clone` above the success-path `recycle_ingress_frame` in `enqueue_pending_forwards`, matching `neighbor_dispatch.rs`.
- Correct the frame-safety invariant comment to state the real guarantee.
- Add a `#[cfg(test)]` `FILL_PUBLISH_HOOK` seam in `drain_pending_fill` (`tx/rings.rs`) that fires immediately after a batch is published to FILL so a test can model kernel DMA ownership; no release-build state or call.

Not changed: recycle batching, `drain_pending_fill` itself, the build-failed recycle (no later read on that arm), the in-place snapshot arm, mirror sampling/counting (#11432, #13656).

## Regression test
`mirror_clone_copies_frame_before_fill_publish_14641` (`tx/dispatch/tests/ptb.rs`): three bindings with distinct UMEMs (non-in-place arm, no snapshot), a 60-byte UDP frame at ingress offset 0, 1023 stale `pending_fill_frames` entries so the success-path recycle crosses the 1024 threshold, and the hook scribbles `0xA5` over the source chunk the instant it is published to FILL (modelled kernel DMA).

- RED (production fix reverted, hook+test present): FAILED — mirror bytes all `0xA5` (165) instead of frame `aa bb cc ...` (170, 187, ...).
- GREEN (fix applied): passes — clone copied while chunk still userspace-owned; publish runs only at the function-tail drain.
- Controls `successful_forward_commits_one_mirror_clone_11432` and `mtu_signalled_forward_does_not_enqueue_mirror_clone_11432` stay green before and after.

## Validation
- `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/var/worktrees/.cache/cargo-14641 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- mirror_ --test-threads=1` → **67 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored** (incl. new test + both #11432 controls). Scratch under `/var/worktrees/.cache` only.
- Base: worktree HEAD `0fd02a585b`; the three touched files are byte-identical between that base and current `origin/master` `51d355c1d8` (empty diff on those paths), so the patch applies unchanged to master.

## Risk
Success-path recycle happens a few instructions later (after mirror commit), within the same request iteration and before the tail fill drain — chunk return latency unchanged in aggregate. In-place (retained) forwards unaffected.

Log: `docs/log/14641.md`

## PR #14845 — userspace-dp: reserve full trailer in session rule-id guard (#14839) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14839-campaign`

Why:
encode_session_record admitted a policy_rule_id whenever
pos + 2 + rule_id.len() + 2 <= 512, reserving only 2 bytes past the
rule_id. The encoder then unconditionally writes the handshake byte,
the provenance byte, and the 8-byte PPTP call-id pair (10 bytes), so
a rule_id sized to the old guard passed it and panicked past the
512-byte frame on the PPTP write, killing the session-sync worker.
rule_id is "<from>-><to>/<name>" from operator config; no name cap
below the 307-374 byte panic window exists in Go or Rust.

What:
session_sync.rs: reserve RULE_ID_TRAILER_BYTES (1 + 1 + 8) in the
capacity guard. Either the whole trailer fits and is written, or
rule_id_len falls back to 0, the established fail-closed
unattributed wire value. No wire-format or capacity change.
codec_tests.rs adds the boundary regression test; docs/log/14839.md
records the analysis.

Validation:
New test RED on the unfixed encoder: panic at session_sync.rs:438,
"range end index 513 out of range for slice of length 512". GREEN
post-fix: the boundary test plus 20 neighbouring codec tests pass.

Risk:
Rule_ids within 8 bytes of the old limit now fall back to
unattributed instead of being carried; pre-existing fallback,
fail-closed, and unreachable for realistic zone/policy names.

Closes #14839

## PR #14848 — firewall: modifier-only terms implicitly accept, only authored next term falls through (#14632) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14632-campaign`

Closes #14632

## Why
Junos nonterminating actions (count/log/forwarding-class/policer/dscp with no terminating action) carry an implicit accept. xpf synthesized fall-through for every empty-action term, so `then count bgp;` ahead of a final discard fell through and blackholed counted traffic (e.g. lo0 BGP/SSH), and a later term's routing-instance/forwarding-class could override the classification.

## What
Fall-through is now only the authored `then next term`:
- Go snapshot builders (`filters.go`, `protocol_policies.go`) copy `term.NextTerm` verbatim — no empty-action synthesis.
- Rust `continue_term := next_term && action.is_empty() && routing_instance.is_empty()` (`compiler.rs`); effective renderer, nft text mirror and netlink lo0 mirror use the same predicate, so a modifier-only term terminates as implicit Accept with its modifiers merged.
- #5142 fail-closed preserved: a real terminating action plus `next_term` still terminates (bit disclosed by renderer).
- Fold-in fixes: four Rust policer fixtures that relied on empty-action fall-through now author `next_term: true` (`single_rate_policer_instances_are_term_scoped_11333`, `cached_three_color_policer_instances_are_term_scoped_11333`, `flow_cache_hit_runs_both/all_three_fall_through_policers`); mixed-version rollout comments in `filters.go`/`compiler.rs` corrected (old Rust also falls through on empty action, so implicit accept requires new Go + new Rust together); stale empty-action line at `docs/config-schema.md:2029` corrected.

## Validation
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp filter::tests` — 204 passed, 0 failed (post-rebase; was 4 failed before fixture fix).
- Go RED/GREEN cells for snapshot/render/nft/netlink modifier-only implicit accept recorded in `docs/log/14632.md`.

## Risk
Behavior change for modifier-only terms ahead of a later discard — they now accept instead of falling through, matching Junos. Mixed-version rollout keeps old fall-through behavior until both Go and Rust are upgraded together; no wire change.

## PR #14853 — userspace-dp: fragment NAT64 IPv6 at the actual sub-1280 egress MTU (#14658) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14658-campaign`

Why:
fragment_nat64_ipv6_frame floored the caller's egress MTU to the
1280-byte IPv6 link minimum after its total_len <= mtu early return.
For a sub-1280 tunnel inner MTU (WireGuard wg_inner_mtu or GRE
native_gre_inner_mtu, composed by nat64_v6_egress_mtu with the RFC
7915 +20 delta), a 1240-byte translated packet was emitted as one
1248-byte atomic fragment — larger than the input — and larger
packets fragmented at 1280. The WG/GRE outer-MTU guards then dropped
the oversized frames with no PTB: a silent blackhole. The 1280 link
minimum is a floor hosts must accept, not the configured egress MTU;
sibling #5159 already forbids this floor for tunnel underlays.

What:
Remove mtu.max(1280) so fragmentation uses the actual caller MTU.
Add a max_data == 0 fail-closed guard (MTU <= 48 cannot carry the
40-byte base + 8-byte fragment header plus an 8-byte-aligned data
chunk), mirroring fragment_nat64_ipv4_frame's max_payload == 0
guard; without it removing the floor would loop on zero-length
chunks. NOT changed: nat64_v6_egress_mtu / post_transform_inner_mtu
(their composed tunnel budgets are correct and prove reachability);
the mtu == 0 unknown path still forwards whole.

Validation:
Rebased onto origin/master 08f11138a5 (RED/GREEN first exercised
at 8653903746; the intervening master commits do not touch this
function). New tests
nat64_v4_reply_fragments_at_sub1280_ipv6_egress_mtu_14658 and
nat64_v4_reply_too_small_ipv6_egress_mtu_fails_closed_14658 drive
build_nat64_forwarded_frames at mtu=1200/48 asserting every
fragment <= MTU, offsets/M/ident, exact reassembly, and a fitting
control. RED with the floor temporarily restored: both fail
(left: 1, right: 2; is_none assertion). GREEN: cargo test --bins
-- 14658 13943 = 5 passed, 0 failed (both new tests plus the
13943 controls).

Risk:
Fail-closed on MTU <= 48 is new but unreachable from real egress
derivation (unknown stays 0 = forward whole). Sub-1280 IPv6 links
are non-conformant underlays per RFC 8200; honoring the configured
MTU matches every sibling fragmenter/segmenter.

Closes #14658

cached-seed or cache-hit paths: MF-selected voice was bleached to the
BA class's marking, and upstream treatment followed the host's DSCP
instead of the operator's filter.

(forwarding_build/cos.rs) so a filter class name resolves to the
global queue id the dscp_rewrite_by_fc_lp matrix is keyed by. Add
resolve_cos_priority_class_lp_rewrite (filter class -> BA class ->
clamped queue) in tx/cos_classify_ba.rs and thread the resolved
filter class through resolve_cos_ba_class_rewrite at all four
callsites; the fresh flowless arm now resolves after its ingress
filter walk. Store the filter class's queue id on
CachedTxSelectionDescriptor and pass it to
reclassify_cached_cos_lp_rewrite, and arm cos_lp_reclassify when
only the filter class has a class-keyed entry. An unmaterialized
filter class now rewrites by its own entry too. NOT changed:
drain-time per-queue uniform rewrite and the #13968 BA-only order.

filter_forwarding_class_keys_egress_rewrite_over_ba_class_14636
covers fresh/cached-seed/cache-hit (Some(46) for a DSCP-10 packet
BA-classified bulk-data but filter-pinned to voice), no-filter and
BA-only controls, and the unmaterialized filter class. RED
evidence: swapping the resolver priority (BA before filter) fails

control test still passes. Filtered suites (cos_classify,

Full --bins: 8398 passed, 50 failed (pre-existing baseline set,

## PR #14855 — nat: register NAT64 persistent pools and swap pool configs atomically (#14679) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14679-campaign`

Why:
compileNAT64 ignored singular pool.Address, silently skipped poisoned members, and never registered PersistentNAT, so valid NAT64 configs failed the #4960 pre-pass and NAT64 bindings were dropped on Go session delete. compileNAT cleared the live persistent table before fallible work, so a failed recompile wiped pool metadata, and destination NAT skipped the #12525 from-scope stamp.

What:
- `config.NAT64PoolHostAddresses`: members via `SourceNATPoolMembers` (singular + list), each must be a bare IPv4 or /32 host mirroring Rust `parse_pool_v4`; any bad member poisons the whole pool.
- `compileNAT64` uses it, hard-fails with the existing "has no valid addresses" error, and stages PersistentNAT registration for NAT64-only pools.
- `compileNAT`/`compileNAT64` stage registrations in `natPersistentStaging`; `CompileConfig` swaps them atomically via `PersistentNATTable.ReplacePoolConfigs` only after both succeed. Standalone wrappers commit on their own success and preserve prior configs on failure.
- Destination NAT checks `HasNATFromScopeStamp()`.
- #4960 pre-pass guards updated for WithStaging names / staged ReplacePoolConfigs call.

Validation:
New `compiler_nat_14679_test.go` cells RED on origin/master 08f11138a5 (singular rejected, poisoned accepted, wipe on failure, unstamped DNAT passed) and GREEN after fix. 14110 persistent-pool tests, pre-pass order/fidelity guards, pkg/config NAT64 tests, and userspace NAT64 tests pass. `TestValidationPassRecordCensus6903` fails identically on stashed base at the same head (pre-existing).

Risk:
NAT64-only pools with any non-IPv4-host member now hard-fail the pre-pass, matching the Rust all-or-nothing rule skip. SNAT prefix pools keep expanded (non-NAT64) semantics.

Closes #14679

## PR #14856 — userspace-dp: release reverse and policy-batch coordinator steering claims on delete (#14840) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14840-campaign`

Why:
An HA import claims steering rows as Coordinator under two owners —
the forward under entry.key and the synthesized reverse under
reverse.key — but the synced delete released only owner=entry.key,
so row(reverse) stayed Remaining for the life of the process and its

Retain the removed reverse incarnation in the synced delete and

the forward DNAT hold there; execute deferred redirects under the

the batch's own tuples). Log: docs/log/14840.md.

limbs), GREEN post-fix (cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp 14840,
3 passed). Full afxdp::ha:: suite 202 passed, 1 failed
(strict_mirror_refusal_..., base-attributed on 5371f5fe19).

Risk:
Deletes release strictly more claims, only for incarnations removed
under the removal lock or batch lease; last-owner protection
unchanged. Abort-path quiesce now also deletes the batch tuples'
steering rows, convergent with its shared removal.

Closes #14840

## PR #14857 — filter: enforce PBR term policers, forwarding-class, and dscp-rewrite (#14659) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14659-campaign`

Why: a matched then routing-instance (PBR) input term bypassed its

TX-selection walk returned before merge_matched_tx_modifiers, the
host-bound session replay capture returned before extending the PBR
term's policer handle, and the non-routing walk returned

policer-drop/log. Transit defers three-color metering to TX selection,

routing_bearing plumbing. NOT changed: loss-priority remains the
documented meter-only no-op (#9503) — ThreeColorPolicerAction carries
no loss-priority field.

0 replay handles, lost next-term drop) and GREEN after the fix;
adjacent filter::, poll_descriptor, cos_classify, and GRE local-delivery

prerouting_scope 11297 cells and stage11 13637, identical on base).

## PR #14859 — userspace-dp: cap MTU-derived tunnel MSS with all-tcp (#14664) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14664-campaign`

Why:
`select_tcp_mss` returned the tunnel value whenever it was > 0, so an MTU-derived GRE MSS of 1416 (WG 1365) replaced a smaller `all-tcp 1200` on tunnel-egress SYNs with no `gre-out` set. Operators set `all-tcp` below the tunnel budget for a smaller downstream link; those flows advertised the larger MSS and depended on PMTUD, the blackhole the knob exists to prevent. The `mss.rs` header and `docs/feature-gaps.md` claimed `all-tcp` clamps every forwarded TCP SYN, contradicting the fallback-only behavior.

What:
- `native_gre_tcp_mss`: with no explicit `gre-out`, return `min(derived, all-tcp)` when `all-tcp` is set; the `gre-out` branch stays `min(gre-out, derived)` irrespective of `all-tcp`.
- `tunnel_tcp_mss`: cap the purely MTU-derived WireGuard value by `all-tcp` when set; `gre-out` remains a GRE-only knob.
- `select_tcp_mss` unchanged (0 tunnel value still falls back to `all-tcp`); header, priority doc, and `feature-gaps.md` now agree that `all-tcp` is a ceiling only on the implicit derived value.
- Five regression cells in `tunnel_tests.rs` through `select_tcp_mss`: GRE capped, WG capped, all-tcp unset keeps derived, explicit gre-out ignores all-tcp, larger all-tcp does not raise derived.
- `docs/log/14664.md` records defect, fix, and RED/GREEN proof.

Validation:
- RED (mss.rs reverted, tests kept): GRE cell left 1416 vs 1200, WG cell left 1365 vs 1200; 3 controls passed.
- GREEN: `cargo +1.98.1 test --bin xpf-userspace-dp 14664` — 5 passed. Broader `tunnel` filter: 240 passed, 2 failed, both base-attributed (fixed upstream post-base by #14846 and the coordinator D11/D14 work), neither on the MSS path.
- Rebased onto current master; final diff is 4 files.

Risk:
Explicit `gre-out` behavior is deliberately unchanged (`min(gre-out, derived)` irrespective of `all-tcp`, pinned by test); only the implicit derived value gains the `all-tcp` ceiling. No caller, formula, gre-in, or plain-forward behavior changes.

Closes #14664

## PR #14860 — userspace-dp: drop transit directed broadcasts per routing domain (#14654) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14654-campaign`

## Why
`transit_dst_is_martian` took no forwarding/domain arguments and never consulted `connected_v4_directed_broadcasts`, while `transit_src_is_martian` in the same file did the domain-keyed lookup — so a transit packet to a connected subnet-directed broadcast escaped the martian drop toward policy/session/NAT (RFC 2644 MUST NOT forward). Conversely, `v4_addr_is_directed_broadcast` scanned all `connected_v4` with no routing-domain/table filter, so a `.255` host in a /16 in one VRF suppressed ICMP errors merely because another VRF owns the /24 whose broadcast is that address.

## What
- `frame/addr_class.rs`: `transit_dst_is_martian(forwarding, ip, routing_domain)` checks the domain-keyed directed-broadcast index; new table-scoped `v4_addr_is_directed_broadcast_in_table` / `dest_…_in_table` / `src_…_in_table` and allocation-free `icmp_error_table_for_meta`.
- `poll_descriptor/mod.rs` (+ flow-cache-hit, TX dispatch call sites): `transit_destination_class_drop` resolves the effective flow domain via `effective_routing_domain_for_flow` and checks original + translated destinations in that domain. `LocalDelivery` stays exempt.
- `icmp.rs` / `icmp_ptb.rs`: reject/Time-Exceeded and PTB suppression scoped to the trigger's ingress installing table.
- `forwarding/fabric.rs`: `ingress_l2_group_unicast_ip` uses the ingress-domain index instead of the unscoped scan.
- New `tests_directed_broadcast_14654.rs` (predicate/domain, descriptor-path, ICMP table-scope cells); `docs/log/14654.md`.

## Validation
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp 14654`: 3 passed.
- Related suites (11413/13981/10689/icmp/pkt-type filters): 57 passed, 0 failed.
- RED: the new test file fails to compile on pristine master (16 errors — new signatures/helpers), so it cannot pass pre-fix; its descriptor cell asserts martian drop with zero TX/session/neighbour state.

## Risk
Cross-VRF hosts that share an address with another domain's directed broadcast are no longer dropped/suppressed in the wrong domain. Ambiguous fabric domains own no broadcasts, matching the existing source gate. ICMP scoping falls back to any-table when the ingress domain has no registry row.

Closes #14654

## PR #14861 — nat: block duplicate address-only mints on idle persistent leases (#14671) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14671-campaign`

## Summary

Fixes #14671 (D5-02): the three same-allocator address-only source-NAT
admission paths ignored idle persistent address-only leases, so a
second subscriber could be minted a duplicate `(translated_ip, port)`
and `persistent_inbound_lookup` then denied inbound persistent-NAT
traffic for both subscribers.

## What

- `userspace-dp/src/nat/allocator.rs`: new
  `persistent_address_only_contended_except` — an IDLE address-only
  persistent lease (other than the candidate's own) contends when its
  recorded permit grants cover the candidate flow's remote endpoint;
  grant-less leases fall back to the `persistent_by_translated` index.
  Live leases are excluded (their flows hold exact live tokens,
  checked separately — #9131). All three admission paths
  (`reserve_address_only_persistent` fresh+pinned,
  `reserve_address_only_roundrobin`,
  `reserve_address_only_maybe_persistent`) now refuse or probe the
  next pool address on contention, alongside the existing live-token
  and PAT checks.
- New regression tests
  `userspace-dp/src/nat/tests_addr_only_persistent_idle_14671.rs`
  (registered in `nat/mod.rs`), log in `docs/log/14671.md`.

Deliberately NOT `address_only_owns_wire_identity`: its persistent
owner counts include an unconditional `Any(base)` key per lease,
which would block same-port flows to unpermitted remotes and the
subscriber's own lease rejoin (both pinned as controls).

## Validation

- RED on base `a801922911`: 2 of 4 new cells failed — H2 minted the
  duplicate `(203.0.113.1, 4000)` on the single-address persistent
  path and via roundrobin.
- GREEN after fix: 4 passed.
- Full `nat::` suite: 667 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored (includes
  #9131 sibling-fallback cells).

## Risk

A colliding second subscriber is now refused/rotated for up to the
idle lease timeout instead of blackholing both — the Junos
persistent-NAT capacity posture, matching the existing PAT-path
precedent. Contention scan is O(leases) on the cold admission path
only.

Closes #14671

## PR #14863 — userspace-dp: ack-gate reinject completions and cap flow queues (#14678) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14678-campaign`

Why:
DrainReinjectCompletions closed the completion stream on any 5ms
timeout, including zero-byte idle expiries, while Rust committed
removal with ack_ready as soon as write_all reached the socket
buffer. A completion written between Go's deadline expiry and its
Close was purged in Rust and destroyed unread in Go, so the pending
entry expired as an ack-timeout uncertain and was fail-closed.
Mid-frame timeouts took the same silent path, and enqueueFlowLocked
appended to per-flow FIFOs without any bound.

What:
Go keeps the completion connection across zero-byte idle timeouts
via a buffered reader; a partial-frame timeout closes the stream
and returns an error so Poll fails pending work closed. Go sends a
one-byte ack (0xAC) only after a full frame is buffered locally,
and Rust ack_ready now waits for that byte, releasing the batch
for redelivery on ack timeout/EOF. CapturePipeline gains
MaxFlowFrames (default 512, counted by FlowQueueDrops); excess
frames return through the existing terminal-DROP path.

Validation:
New TestDrainReinjectCompletionsPreservesConnOnZeroByteTimeout,
partial-frame error/recovery cells, and the per-flow cap cell fail
on base 08f11138a5 and pass with the fix. The #13234 overflow test
and updated #9506 partial-frame test pass. Rust complete_conn
cells (5, including the new unacked-redelivery cell) pass.
Pre-existing pkg/nfqueue failures (ipsec advisory #14139 cell and
long-TMPDIR socket binds) reproduce on unmodified base.

Risk:
Old Go against new Rust never acks, so batches redeliver on
reconnect instead of purging (fail-safe). New Go against old Rust
sends ack bytes the old probe rejects, dropping the connection;
completions redeliver on the next accept. Both sides ship together.

Closes #14678

## PR #14864 — dataplane: account for compileZones mid-loop aborts after host mutation (#14680) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14680-campaign`

Why:
CompileConfig returned (nil, err) when compileZones failed mid-loop, so CompileUserspaceShim returned before inheritHostDivergence, abortAfterHostMutation and ProveArmCoverage. A VLAN create or address reconcile on an earlier interface had already mutated the host, yet HostDivergence stayed empty, no #4960 annotation was attached, and the prior arm-coverage verdict stood. The #10915 S-tag gate also sat after MTU/ethtool/LinkSetUp, so a stuck rx-vlan-stag-hw-parse NIC was brought UP before the abort, and markVLANSubInterfaces was append-only so a reused ifindex was permanently excluded from XDP swap/status.

What:
CompileConfig now returns the partial result on a compileZones failure; compileZones/programZoneMaps publish the deferred XDP sets queued before the abort. CompileUserspaceShim routes a non-nil partial result through inheritHostDivergence and abortAfterHostMutation with the #4960 annotation (nil-result pre-mutation errors keep the bare return). The S-tag gate is hoisted to just after ensureRxVlanParsePreconditions, before MTU/ethtool/buffers/LinkSetUp (disabled interfaces exempt; the late duplicate is removed). markVLANSubInterfaces now replaces the set on the success tail. NOT changed: later CompileConfig phases still return (nil, err), and aborted applies do not rewrite vlanSubInterfaces.

Validation:
New pkg/dataplane/compilezones_midloop_abort_14680_test.go: TestCompileUserspaceShimRecordsHostDivergenceOnCompileZonesMidLoopAbort, TestStagGatePrecedesLinkSetup14680, TestMarkVLANSubInterfacesReplacesStale14680 and TestCompileZonesAbortWiring14680 fail on base 91d5ccc48c (stag cell: host MTU = 9000, want untouched 1500) and pass after the fix; TestCompileZonesSuccessControl14680 passes both ways. Targeted neighbour suites (#4960/#5268/#7289/#8285/#9845/#10915) pass. Full pkg/dataplane suite exceeded the 300s tool timeout without a reported failure; please rerun before merge.

Risk:
CompileConfig callers that check err first are unaffected. Non-Ethernet netdevs now trip the S-tag gate before framing is known (fail-closed, same direction as before, only earlier). HostDivergence may now be retained for zones aborts that previously reported bare, which is the intended operator signal.

Closes #14680
