## PR #14866 — config: consume device-map key value as pair, reject bad identities (#14685) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14685-campaign`

Why:
The compact hierarchical spelling `interface ge-0/0/3 key pci pci 0000:01:00.0;` compiled to PCIAddr="pci" and `key mac mac <addr> pci <addr>` to MAC="mac": collectDeviceMapProps stepped i++ over the packed Keys, so the value of `key` (pci/mac, itself a prop keyword) was re-read as a property and captured the following keyword. The real address was lost yet SchemaValidate and strict compile passed (non-empty identity), so the resolver searched for PCI "pci".

What:
collectDeviceMapProps now consumes each recognised pair (i += 2), stepping by one only on unrecognised tokens, keeping the scan on keyword boundaries. validateDeviceMapStrict now requires a present PCI/MAC to satisfy ValidatePCIAddr/ValidateMAC and KeyOrder to be in the schema enum, reusing the schema validators; the lenient path downgrades via existing lenientDeviceMap warnings. New regression file covers both compact forms, pci-then-mac/mac-then-pci controls, ordinary orders, strict rejection and lenient warning. NOT changed: schema tree or resolver — the corruption was compile-time only.

Validation:
RED on origin/master 91d5ccc48c: compact pci got PCIAddr="pci", compact mac got MAC="mac" (hierarchical `hierTree` fixture matching the issue packet; flat `set ... key pci` is separately rejected by SchemaValidate as unknown modifier). GREEN after fix: all 7 new tests pass; TestDeviceMap* suite passes. gofmt clean.

Risk:
Direct CompileConfig callers with hand-built garbage identities now fail strict where they previously compiled to an unbound entry; that is the intended fail-closed change. Lenient load/peer-sync still boots with a warning.

Closes #14685

The #5879 QinQ gate iterated only direct unit children and direct vlan leaves, while compileInterfaces enumerates units via namedInstances (descending into `unit { 0 { ... } }`) and hoists packed tails via packedBody. ## PR #14869 — userspace-dp: purge local-hit shared sessions and fence conditional deletes (#14666) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14666-campaign`

## Summary

Fixes all three legs of D4-03 (#14666):

1. **Local-hit purge blindness** (`resolve.rs`): a worker-local hit
   (`hit.shared_entry == None` after UpsertSynced/Demote materialized
   the row) derived no `shared_identity`, so
   `purge_translated_synced_hit_with_context` took the `Absent`
   branch — never removing shared authority or replicating the
   conditional delete. Now adopts `(session_id, generation)` from
   the shared entry under the same key when the local row's adopted
   id matches; the purge's under-lock predicate stays authoritative
   (replacement published in the window declines and survives).
2. **Queue-full conditional repair** (`worker_commands.rs`):
   `replicate_session_delete_conditional` no longer releases the
   target worker's NAT/NAT64 port unconditionally on a refused
   queue push — the allocator is keyed by `(flow, translated)` and
   cannot distinguish a stale incarnation from a live replacement.
   The `SESSION_DELETE_DROP_EPOCH` bump still arms the sibling's
   delete-drop sweep; `repaired` stays 0 for conditional drops.
   The unconditional `replicate_session_delete_repairing` is
   unchanged.
3. **Companion conflation** (`delete_synced.rs` + producers):
   `DeleteSyncedConditional` gains `companion_expected_id`,
   captured with `expected_id` at the stale-close producer
   (`session_delta.rs`) and coordinator fan-out
   (`ha/session_import.rs`). The worker deletes the companion only
   when live id is 0 (converged), expected is 0 (uncaptured/legacy),
   or live == expected; a different live id is a replacement and is
   preserved.

## Validation

New regression cells (RED by construction pre-fix — shared entry
leaked / port freed / companion clobbered):

- `local_hit_purge_removes_shared_and_replicates_14666`
- `conditional_queue_full_repair_preserves_replacement_port_14666`
- `conditional_delete_preserves_replaced_companion_14666`

Controls:

- `local_hit_purge_preserves_replacement_shared_entry_14666`
- `unconditional_queue_full_repair_still_releases_14666`
- `conditional_delete_removes_matched_companion_14666`
- `conditional_delete_absent_companion_is_noop_14666`
- `purge_translated_synced_hit_full_teardown_13674` and the #10512
  scoped-delete cells stay green.

## PR #14870 — userspace-dp: re-derive HA ownership before synced upsert (#14669) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14669-campaign`

Why:
handle_upsert_synced computed allow_replace_local/is_active from the
peer's stamped owner_rg_id before locally re-resolving, served the
peer's cached LocalDelivery/neighbor fallback verbatim, and leaked
the replaced pool reservation when the NAT target moved pools. On a
split-RG node a stale standby stamp could clobber a live active-RG
local session, an owner-0 stamp was HA-gated against the wrong RG,
a foreign local_ifindex could be delivered into this node's host
stack, and a Pool A -> Pool B replacement stranded Pool A's port.

What:
In handle_upsert_synced, re-resolve forward entries with
lookup_forwarding_resolution_for_session_without_cache, stamp the
local owner_rg_for_resolution first, then compute
allow_replace_local/is_active and enforce HA. On the standby arm
only, a local NoRoute/MissingNeighbor may still fall back to the
peer candidate through cached_session_resolution, which revalidates
egress/neighbor against this node's live state and requires
ForwardCandidate, so a peer LocalDelivery is never served and #326
activation readiness is preserved. Release the previous reservation
when the new entry does not reserve or when the NAT / is_reverse /
zone-pair target changed (release sweeps only the exact previous
tuple, so same-tuple refreshes keep their holder bit).
NOT changed: coordinator import guard in session_import.rs (separate
pre-publish surface, noted in docs/log/14669.md).

Validation:
New upsert_synced_14669_tests.rs (5 cells): RED on pre-fix code
4/5 fail (owner-0 stamp, stale-stamp clobber, foreign ifindex 99,
cross-pool strand; same-tuple control passes); GREEN 5/5 pass.
Full session_glue suite: 337 passed, 3 failed, 2 ignored; all 3
failures reproduce identically on clean origin/master
(publish_shared_session_counts, flush_session_deltas 9412,
demote_dedup timing).

Risk:
Cache-free re-resolution deliberately distrusts peer state on this
path; packet path still revalidates HA. Cross-pool release runs
before re-reserve only when the translated tuple or zone pair
actually changed.

Closes #14669

## PR #14874 — config,ipsec: shadow ESP fallback behind authored IKE policies (#14689) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14689-campaign`

## Summary

Fix the D10-04 fallback and partial IKE policy proposal chain validation bypasses so commit and render agree on IKE Phase-1 resolution when an `ike-policy` is authored.

### Why

- `chainResolves` fell through to a same-named ESP proposal (`cfg.Proposals`) even when an authored `ike-policy` existed and failed its own all-resolve check, rescuing a broken IKE chain with a Phase-2 proposal.
- Proposal-agreement checking was skipped whenever not every proposal resolved, hiding authentication/lifetime conflicts among the resolved proposals.
- `ipsecVPNAuthNeedsPSK` returned `false` on the first dangling entry, while the renderer skipped that entry and resolved a later PSK proposal—so `[dangling, prop-psk]` without a key passed the commit gate and was then silently skipped at render.
- `resolveIKESettings` rendered Phase-1 from the ESP proposal table whenever no IKE proposal resolved, even when `cfg.IKEPolicies[name]` had been authored.

### What

- **Commit gate (`pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_ipsec.go`)**: an authored ike-policy is authoritative—when it exists, only the all-entries-defined check decides; the legacy ESP fallback now requires `IKEPolicies[name]` to be absent, and nil proposal entries cannot resolve. Proposal agreement now runs over every resolved proposal of an authored policy before the chain verdict.
- **PSK gate (`pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_ipsec_psk_14139.go`)**: missing/nil/unknown-auth entries are skipped exactly like the runtime resolver; PSK is required if any resolved proposal needs it, and the auth is undecided only when nothing resolves.
- **Runtime (`pkg/ipsec/ike.go`)**: the `cfg.Proposals` legacy fallback is consulted only when no ike-policy of that name was authored; otherwise the resolver falls through to `errIKEChainUnresolved` and the VPN is skipped. Legacy direct-proposal, no-policy, pubkey, and partially-resolvable configurations are unchanged.
- Regression cells are distinct per claim: shadowed-dangling, shadowed-conflicting, partially-dangling PSK, direct gate pins, runtime never-render-ESP pin plus legacy control. See `docs/log/14689.md`.

### Validation

- RED on base `217e9132a2`: the shadowed `CompileConfig` cases, direct chain/PSK gates, and runtime ESP-render cells failed.
- Focused `pkg/config` and `pkg/ipsec` selectors pass after the fix; full `pkg/ipsec` passes.
- Broad `pkg/config` failures (e.g. `TestIKEPolicyResolvableChainAccepted`, `TestIKEGatewayNoPolicyAccepted`, routing-instance cells) fail identically on unmodified base—pre-existing gate-ordering exposure from the later PSK gate—and are not regressions of this change.

### Risk

Limited to configurations where an ike-policy and an ESP proposal share a name, or an authored policy contains dangling entries; those now fail closed. Legacy direct-proposal and no-policy configurations remain accepted. Configs with conflicting resolved proposals are rejected consistently with runtime behavior.

Closes #14689

## PR #14880 — userspace-dp: gate MissingNeighbor probes behind NAT/fence admission (#14661) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14661-campaign`

Why:
The MissingNeighbor arm fired trigger_kernel_arp_probe (and the tunnel resolver enqueue) at arm entry, before the NAT64 fail-closed drop, the NPTv6 Untranslatable drop, the SNAT-allocation failure, and the final composed-NAT bindless fence. Packets this arm discards therefore emitted a cleartext ARP/NDP for their exact destination — the #11284-class leak for post-SNAT fence tuples, and wasted probes for NAT64/SNAT-exhausted drops. The seed also installed without a tuple-gate permit, published via the ungated conntrack path, never replicated to peers, and proceeded even when the pressure-shed lease failed. Separately the segmented-TCP neighbor retry built each segment with overlap_admissions: None, dropping the taken tokens (Drop = fail).

What:
- poll_descriptor/mod.rs: suppress the early probe/resolver for every packet in the arm; defer the single admitted probe to the committed-seed site, past NPTv6/SNAT/final-fence, without re-checking probe_throttled (the early note_kernel_probe record is that window). Seed refuses on shed-lease failure, holds a global_tuple_gate permit through install + shared publish + gated conntrack publish, and replicates via replicate_session_upsert. A gate refusal also refuses buffering (seed_install_refused) instead of parking for replay.
- neighbor_dispatch.rs: ride retry overlap tokens on the first segment.
- tx/dispatch/mod.rs: commit taken tokens on the segmented copy path instead of drop() (RAII fail).
- Tests: tests_missing_neighbor_probe_gate_14661.rs (NAT64, SNAT-exhausted, NPTv6-untranslatable, post-SNAT fence zero-probe; permitted control probes once/seeds/publishes/replicates), segmented-retry overlap test, and the #13762 control updated to zero wire probes.

Validation:
RED on master prod code: 4/5 new 14661 tests fail with probe=1.
GREEN: cargo test --bins -- 14661: 5 passed. missing_neighbor: 45 passed. neighbor: 307 passed. #13762 throttle control: passed. Post-rebase GREEN re-run: 5 passed.

Risk:
Flowless packets no longer probe at arm entry; they never seed and re-drive resolution via retry/neg-cache on a later admitted packet. The neg-cache fast-fail resolver enqueue (policy-admitted only) is unchanged.

Closes #14661

Closes #14650

## Defect (D1-03, both arms MATERIAL)
1. `SteeringRowOwners` stored `(SessionKey, Claim)` with no action byte. `write_and_claim` ran the BPF_ANY write unconditionally and `release_locked` deleted only when no owner remained, so a PASS_TO_KERNEL (2) publish overwrote a shared REDIRECT (1) 40-byte row and the PASS release stranded the surviving REDIRECT owner at PASS permanently (shim cpumap_or_pass, kernel forward with no zone policy).
2. `retire_workers()` mem::take-n every rows+holdings shard, wiping coordinator claims #9560 round 3 added so coordinator rows survive, desyncing rows vs holdings against lock-free sync_session (#7209).

## Fix
- Registry records the published action per (owner, holder) claim in both Owners and Held.
- `write_and_claim` coalesces the physical write fail-safe: REDIRECT wins if the incoming action or any other owner's recorded action is REDIRECT — PASS is never written while a REDIRECT owner shares the row.
- `release_locked` (entry/row/retire paths) restores the surviving owners' fail-safe action via a new `restore(row, action)` callback under the same row-shard lock; deletes only when no owner remains (unchanged).
- `retire_workers` clears only worker bits per shard under lock, preserving coordinator claims in both maps.
- Production restores write via `write_steering_row` (held-only rows decode a key via `session_key_for_row`); merged with #14648's `steering_key_is_publishable` gate.

## Regression (RED on base by construction, GREEN after)
- `steering_owners::tests::aliased_pass_publish_restores_redirect_on_release_14650`
- `steering_owners::tests::retire_workers_preserves_coordinator_claims_14650`
- `session_glue::steering_row_owners_9560_tests::aliased_pass_over_redirect_is_coalesced_and_restored_14650` (real recorder seam)
- `session_glue::steering_row_owners_9560_tests::aliased_redirect_release_restores_pass_for_survivor_14650` (reverse order)

## Verification
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 14650`: 4 passed
- `-- 9560`: 43 passed; `-- 9517`: 7 passed (controls green)
- Full suite parallel: 8390 passed / 61 failed — pre-existing parallel/global-state flakes in files untouched by this change (counts vary 55-61 run-to-run; spot checks fail on shim naming/tally drift). Post-rebase compile re-verification was blocked by host load >100 from sibling lanes; the merged conflict is a 3-line comment+gate combination in `publish_session_map_key` with the rest applying cleanly — main agent should re-run `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 14650 9560 9517` once load subsides.

## PR #14884 — userspace-dp: rotate scan eviction sample off deterministic prefix (#14673) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14673-campaign`

## Why

`ScanCore::evict_stalest_in_zone` sampled `per_zone_srcs[zone].iter().take(64)` on every eviction. `per_zone_srcs` is an unseeded `FxHashSet`, so that prefix is the same deterministic 64 buckets on every call and computable by an off-box attacker who knows the inserted addresses. An attacker who pinned 63 prefix entries at count 9 (`SCAN_DETECT_COUNT - 1`) and kept its scanner at count 8 inside the prefix made the scanner the deterministic lowest-count victim; one fresh decoy admission wiped its history and the next probe re-seeded it at count 1, so the scanner never reached the detection count of 10. Forwarding was never fail-open; this is a detection fail-open only.

## What

- The eviction sample now walks the dense `key_ring` (which mirrors `per_src` exactly, maintained by the single `insert_src`/`remove_src` primitives) from a persistent `evict_cursor`, instead of iterating the per-zone `FxHashSet`.
- `evict_cursor` rotates the window: each eviction examines at most `EVICT_SCAN_LIMIT` (64) same-zone candidates and advances the cursor past the examined span, so successive evictions cover the whole zone instead of a fixed prefix (#6239 cursor pattern).
- The start is seeded per boot: `ScanCore::seed` is drawn once from `hot_hash_seed::hot_path_hash_seed()` (#2364 pattern), and the walk starts at `(evict_cursor + seed_offset) % ring_len`. `evict_cursor` is stored in the unseeded frame (the next start is translated back by `seed_offset`), so successive starts advance contiguously by the examined span rather than jumping by `seed_offset` each time. Tests pin the seed via `ScanCore::with_seed`.
- Other-zone slots do not consume the 64 same-zone budget; the total walk is capped at `EVICT_SCAN_LIMIT + 8 * EVICT_SCAN_LIMIT` (576) ring slots. If the window finds no same-zone candidate at all (sparse zone in a huge ring — the #4890 test shape), a fallback takes a rotating seeded sample of the zone's own `per_zone_srcs` index (at most `EVICT_SCAN_LIMIT` same-zone entries, skip bounded by the per-zone cap, never by the total table size), which keeps the existing #4890 regression green without any O(ring) walk.
- Victim selection is unchanged (#4418/#2234): expired-or-empty first, then fewest distinct destinations, stalest `window_start` on ties. `per_zone_srcs` otherwise serves only the O(1) zone-cap count.
- `evict_examined_log` (test-only, like the existing cleanup `examined_log`) records the sample so tests can prove rotation.

NOT changed: the eviction victim policy, the cap sizes, the cleanup cursor, and any forwarding behaviour.

## Validation

- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 14673`: 7 passed, 0 failed.
  - `pinned_prefix_scanner_not_self_evicted_14673` — the issue's scene recreated exactly (first 64 `FxHashSet` entries pinned 63× count 9 + scanner at 8, rest count 1): scanner survives the decoy-triggered eviction and trips on its 10th port. Pre-fix the static prefix evicts the scanner (8 < 9).
  - `eviction_sample_rotates_across_calls_14673` — three successive samples pairwise different, each ≤ 64.
  - `eviction_eventually_covers_all_entries_14673` — repeated evictions with refill eventually examine every entry.
  - `eviction_bounded_under_other_zone_interleave_14673` — 2000 other-zone + 3 target: terminates with ≤ 2×64 same-zone examinations.
  - `eviction_start_depends_on_seed_14673` — different pinned seeds reshuffle the first sampled key.
  - `eviction_rotating_still_prefers_expired_14673` — expired/empty entry inside the window reclaimed first.
  - `scanner_detected_through_decoy_evictions_at_cap_14673` — end-to-end through `PortScanTracker::check` at the real 4096 cap.
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- scan`: 55 passed, 0 failed, including the pre-existing #4890 regression `fresh_scanner_admitted_when_zone_entries_outside_global_prefix_4890`.

Suite log: `/var/worktrees/.cache/14673-scan-suite3.log` (`test result: ok. 55 passed; 0 failed`).

## Risk

Fallback samples `per_zone_srcs` from a cursor offset; same-zone examination stays ≤ 2× `EVICT_SCAN_LIMIT`. At real saturation the dense ring window hits first, so the fallback is cold. No forwarding, cap, or cleanup behaviour changes.

Closes #14673

## PR #14886 — cluster: cap heartbeat monitor name/count at uint8 wire limits (#14704) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14704-campaign`

Fixes D14-02: `marshalHeartbeatBody` wrote a monitor's `NameLen` as `uint8(len(nameBytes))` and the monitor count as `uint8(numMon)` with no ≤255 guard, while groups (`maxHeartbeatGroups`, #4434) and the software version were clamped in the same function.

A monitor name >255 bytes wrapped its length byte (260→4) and >255 monitors wrapped the count byte (260→4), while the full payload was still written. The receiver trusts both bytes, so it parsed monitor payload as the version trailer and never reached the `XPFE` echo trailer — poisoning `SoftwareVersion`/`HAProtocolVersion` and silently losing the echo lease that `handlePeerHeartbeat` uses for freshness.

## Fix
- `maxHeartbeatMonitorNameSize=255`: oversize names are skipped whole (not truncated, not `break` — later monitors survive).
- `maxHeartbeatMonitors=255`: the monitor section stops at the uint8 count limit.
- Drops are reported by the existing `heartbeatMonitorTruncations` detector, so the truncation stays operator-visible.

## Tests
New `heartbeat_monitor_uint8_14704_test.go` — RED on origin/master (260-byte name decoded as `aaaa` + garbage monitor; 256-byte name as empty; 260 monitors wrote count byte 4), GREEN after the fix. Boundary controls (255-byte name, 255 monitors) round-trip verbatim, including groups, software version, HA protocol version, and both echo session/sequence pairs.

`go test ./pkg/cluster/ -run 'TestMarshalHeartbeat|TestMonitorTruncation|TestHeartbeat'` passes. Full `pkg/cluster` suite has one pre-existing failure (`TestInstallTableProducerToResendEndToEnd9752`) that fails identically on unmodified origin/master — base-attributed, unrelated.

Closes #14704

## PR #14895 — daemon: fail closed on lossy ICMP and GRE tuples in rematch (#14697) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14697-campaign`

Why:
Rename rematch (rematchRenamedV4/V6/Match) and rollback
reauthorization (reauthorizePolicyCandidates) rebuild a
policymatch.Query from the captured 5-tuple, which stores only the
ICMP echo identifier in the port fields and never the ICMP/ICMPv6
type or code. With ICMPType nil, matchSingleApp skips every
icmp-type-constrained deny/reject rule in first-match order, so a
live echo session falls through to a broader permit
(junos-icmp-all/any) and survives a policy change that forbids it.
reauthorizePolicyCandidates also never called the GRE
discriminator guard the rename paths apply.

What:
Add capturedTupleValid in daemon_policy_rename.go (ICMP 1 /
ICMPv6 58 always invalid offline; GRE 47 invalid with zero
discriminator), point the three rename-rematch entry points at
it, and call it first in reauthorizePolicyCandidates' isPermitted
so lossy candidates stay deletion debt. capturedTunnelDiscriminatorValid
is unchanged as the capture-time PurgeTunnelVariants classifier.
Decisive regression tests with matcher premises cover V4, V6
(custom type-128 app), the helper-match twin, an
unconditional-guard control with a TCP retained control, the
guard unit, and the reauthorize ICMP/58/GRE0 cells.
NOT changed: policymatch and the session wire formats.

Validation:
RED on base 75a10ddc15 (tests only): all six decisive tests FAIL
(V4 retained under lan->wan/p-new; reauthorize discharged the
ICMP candidate; guard accepted protocol 1). GREEN at head
589a98ecd7: all six PASS; rename/reauthorize neighbourhood,
invalidation/rollback neighbourhood and the policy-focused daemon
subset (TestPolicy|TestRematch|TestReauthor|TestRename|TestHelper|
TestNat64|TestRollback) PASS. The full pkg/daemon suite exceeded
the 280s lane timeout twice under multi-lane CPU contention with
no failures observed before the cutoff; the policy-focused subset
above is the exercised full-suite proxy.

Risk:
Live ICMP/ICMPv6 sessions are now deleted by rename-rematch
instead of retained, and ICMP/ICMPv6/GRE0 rollback candidates
stay deletion debt — matching the pre-existing GRE0 rename
behaviour. No wire or config change.

## PR #14898 — cli: reject trailing tokens after display pipe formats (#14715) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14715-campaign`

Closes #14715

## Why

`show configuration` and config-mode `show` selected the render format with `strings.Contains(rest, "| display set")` (likewise json/xml/inheritance) while building the path only from tokens **before** `|`. `show configuration | display set interfaces` silently discarded `interfaces` and rendered the whole tree (`ShowActiveSet()` / `ShowActiveSetRedacted(nil)`). The RBAC gate did not save it: `evaluateCommandRegex` only checked `pipeWords[1]=="display"` was authorizable, so the spelling satisfied an interfaces-scoped allow and evaded a `$`-anchored display-set deny. Same mechanism in `show system rollback N` and its candidate-read predicate. (Redacted for non-superuser classes per #4099, so this dumps full structure, not cleartext secrets.)

## What

- Token-exact pipe parsing via `splitDisplayPipe` / `splitConfigShowPipe` (`cli_show.go`), shared by `handleShow`, `handleConfigShow`, and the rollback branch (only `| display set` there). Only `| display <json|set|xml|inheritance>` with no trailing tokens selects a format; trailing tokens, unknown formats, bare `|` are syntax errors naming the token, with no render. Config-mode additionally accepts exact `| compare [rollback <N>]`.
- `evaluateCommandRegex`: a `display` pipe is authorizable only as `| display <format>`, optionally followed by one recognised output filter (`| display set | match x`, which dispatch SplitPipe splits and the gate reassembles) — gate and executor now agree; anchored-deny / scoped-allow bypass spellings are denied at the gate too.
- `showSystemRollbackCompare` aligned to the token-exact handler.
- Regression: `pkg/cli/show_display_pipe_trailing_14715_test.go`; history: `docs/log/14715.md`.
- NOT changed: `cmd/cli` remote surface (#13202 already token-exact), output-filter pipes, `pendingPipeSuffix` reassembly.

## Validation

- New `TestShowConfigurationDisplayPipeTrailing14715` + `TestDisplayPipeGate14715`: **RED** on pristine `origin/master` (59f4ac7065; all 8 malformed cells dumped the whole tree with the host-name sentinel, gate authorized the trailing spelling), **GREEN** on the fix.
- Targeted suites green: pipe-canonicalization 9628, redaction 4099, rollback authz, dispatcher gates. `go vet ./pkg/cli/` and `gofmt` clean.
- Full `pkg/cli` suite: only `TestApplyToDataplaneGlobalFRRParity11455` fails, reproduced identically on pristine base (base-attributed, unrelated).

## Risk

Operators who relied on silently-ignored trailing tokens after a display format now get a syntax error (Junos-compatible). Legitimate `| display <fmt>` forms and chained `| match`-style filters are unchanged.

session (sessions.synced/nat/forward_wire via the owner_rg_indexes

tunnel_endpoints baseline) and validation (snapshot_installed)
before rebind's reconcile could replay/migrate them. The rebind.rs
comment claimed the link-cycle path was unaffected because Go sends
a separate stop_workers first — that separate call was precisely
the wipe.

New Coordinator::stop_for_link_cycle: stop_inner(false) with
forwarding/validation preserved across the worker stop, runtime
view republished, ReconcileStage::Stopped recorded; stop_workers
calls it instead of stop(). Terminal stop()/stop_with_event_stream
(disarm, shutdown verb, process exit) still wipe via
stop_inner(true) — pinned by a control cell. rebind.rs comment
corrected. NOT changed: reconcile/tear_down/bring-up, which already
implement the preservation contract tear_down captures
tunnel_owners/snapshot_was_installed from.

New cells in userspace-dp/src/server/tests.rs drive the exact Go
verb sequence (sync_session upsert -> stop_workers -> rebind) and
the seeded forwarding/validation baselines; both preservation cells
FAIL with stop() restored in stop_workers (RED: "stop_workers wiped
the synced-session map", "stop_workers wiped the tunnel-owner
baseline") and pass with the fix. server:: module 239/239,
forwarding_publish_population_is_pinned_7015 pass (census 1->2).

8443/58; the 7 lane-only failures pass --exact single-threaded on
both lane and base (parallel-load flakes, none in the touched
paths). Clippy clean of errors. Full detail: docs/log/14677.md.

resident until the next reconcile/disarm — identical to every
stop_inner(false) teardown, and Go's abort path does send the
rebind (#5103/#6871). PortAllocators are Arc-shared, so stop_inner's
holder retirement frees worker-held bits on the same instances the
preserved forwarding (and the rebuild via previous) reuses: no
leak, no double-free. No wire, Go, or BPF changes.

Branch: `fix/14724-campaign`

Why:
A trigger-on crossing arms rt.onLatched in evaluateEvent, but the cooldown-stale drop, the permanent-rejection return, and the HandleEvent classify-reject/empty-plan continues never released it, so one transient commitFn (nil, err) wedged a policy forever under a sustained fault. applyOnce reserved a global-budget slot before commitFn and never refunded it, so read-only retries burned all four slots and starved healthy policies. criticalConfigPath checked only path[0], so groups-wrapped security remediations queued as ordinary work.

What:
Release the edge latch on every terminal non-commit exit in runAction and HandleEvent (shutdown abandons stay terminal); refund the exact reserved budget slot on any commit that never promotes while keeping it for clean and committed-with-debt commits, preserving the ErrClusterReadOnly sentinel for HA deferral; unwrap a leading groups <name> prefix in criticalConfigPath while apply-groups stays ordinary. Full pkg/eventengine suite: 9 failures, all *6673* tests failing identically on pristine origin/master (base-attributed, #14660).

## PR #14902 — feeds: reject malformed feed paths instead of fetching base (#14723) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14723-campaign`

## Why

`joinFeedURL` (pkg/feeds/feeds.go) silently fell back on malformed
per-feed paths. `url.Parse` error returned the fetchable base URL, so
`/denylist%ZZ.txt` fetched the server base and installed its prefixes
under the named feed. A `//denylist.txt` network-path (host token,
empty path) and a `v1:prod/...` scheme:opaque form likewise collapsed
to a base fetch. Clearing `RawPath` decoded `%2F` to `/` in the wire
path. `resolveBaseURL` trimmed trailing `/` from the raw URL string,
cutting query/fragment tokens ending in `/`. The strict compiler gate
validated only the base URL, never the per-feed path, so all of these
committed clean.

## What

- `pkg/feeds/feeds.go`: `joinFeedURL` now rejects an unparseable
  per-feed path and any scheme/opaque/authority form by returning
  `""`; `Apply` registers no feed for a rejected join (fail-closed
  per #5645, warning logged) instead of fetching the base. A malformed
  BASE still returns unchanged so readFeed / the #5183 gate report it.
  The join runs on escaped paths with `RawPath` pinned, so `%2F`
  survives in the requested URI. `resolveBaseURL` trims trailing `/`
  from the URL path only, never from query/fragment, preserving the
  `https://` scheme (the prior scheme-less rebuild corrupted
  scheme-bearing bases to a host-only string); unparseable/scheme-less
  values keep the historical raw slash-trim, and the mirrored
  `feedServerResolvedBaseURL` in pkg/config matches.
- `pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_observability.go`: the strict
  feed-server endpoint gate now also rejects a malformed per-feed
  `path` via `feedEntryPathMalformed` (mirrors the runtime rule;
  pkg/config cannot import pkg/feeds). Strict commit rejects; the
  tolerant load/peer-sync wrapper downgrades to a warning.
- Regression: `pkg/feeds/feed_url_join_malformed_14723_test.go`
  (join table, Apply-level no-fetch for each malformed spelling, and
  `%2F` preserved in `RequestURI` through httptest) and
  `pkg/config/compiler_feed_path_malformed_14723_test.go` (strict
  rejects, tolerant warns, valid/escaped paths accept). The #14177
  table's scheme-relative cell now expects rejection `""` instead of
  the silent tail-keep. `pkg/feeds/README.md` documents the rule.
- NOT changed: the base-URL malformed/plaintext gates (#5183/#14385)
  and the single-feed (no FeedEntries) registration path.

## Validation

- RED on `origin/master` (6621660159): `TestJoinFeedURLMalformedAndEdgePaths`
  returned the base / base+`/` for `%ZZ`, `//`, and colon forms and
  decoded `%2F`; `TestApplyMalformedFeedPathFetchesNothing14723`
  registered each malformed feed against the base URL;
  `TestApplyEscapedFeedPathPreserved14723` saw `/base/a/b.txt`;
  `TestFeedServerMalformedFeedPathRejected14723` committed clean.

## PR #14903 — api: canonicalize safe-method route in command-regex gate (#14712) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14712-campaign`

Why:
readPermissionFor (#9134) canonicalizes any safe non-GET method to
the GET entry for the coarse permission, so HEAD passed that gate
and reached authorizeRESTCommand — where the route was keyed on the
raw method and "HEAD /api/v1/status" missed every GET-keyed
command table (restRouteCommand, restRoutesNoCommand, and the
request-decoded switch), hitting the fail-closed unmapped denial.
Every regex-restricted (non-superuser) class got 403 on 100% of
HEAD reads while GET succeeded: a fail-closed availability defect
(health probes, SDK HEAD checks), not an authorization bypass.
Only HEAD is reachable — Go's ServeMux aliases HEAD to GET
patterns; OPTIONS/TRACE have no GET pattern and never reach a GET
handler.

What:
- pkg/api/authz_command_regex_9952.go: authorizeRESTCommand now
  keys the command tables on canonicalRESTRoute14712(method, path)
  — the GET spelling for any safe method (same isSafeHTTPMethod
  predicate readPermissionFor uses), the raw method otherwise, so
  POST mutation routes are never aliased. HEAD now follows the GET
  verdict exactly, including deny cases, the six
  declared-no-command reads (#14146), and the request-decoded
  routes (show-text topic, system/info type).
- pkg/api/authz_command_regex_14712_test.go: regression cells call
  the gate directly and drive the real readAuthz middleware.
- docs/log/14712.md: investigation record.
NOT changed: readPermissionFor, the mutation gate, the route
tables.

Validation:
- go test ./pkg/api/ -run '14712': RED on origin/master
  ca1baec1e9 (HEAD refused by the generic unmapped message while
  GET allowed under allow-commands "^show version$"; HEAD
  show-text?topic=version and system/info?type=uptime refused
  under their allow-lists; HEAD 403 through readAuthz under
  allow-commands "^show " while GET 200), GREEN after the fix.
- Neighbor suites 9952|14146|9134|13249|11678|12582|9051|9903|
  6660|5561 pass.
- Full pkg/api suite: only pre-existing failures
  (TestFirewallValidationHarnessDocGuard,
  TestEmitUserspaceDynamicBufferMetrics, five 6960 cells),
  reproduced identically on origin/master 8fa985618f.

Risk:
A regex-restricted class can now read via HEAD exactly what it
can read via GET, and is denied via HEAD exactly what it is
denied via GET (the denial now names the resolved command
instead of the generic unmapped-route message). Classes without
operational regexes and superusers are unchanged. No route,

## PR #14904 — userspace-dp: gate embedded ICMP on outer destination and re-NAT composed SNAT+DNAT (#14665) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14665-campaign`

Why:
The same-family embedded-ICMP matchers accepted a quoted tuple
regardless of the error's outer destination (the NAT64 arm already
gates this per RFC 792/4443), letting a tuple-knowing quoter steer a
re-NAT'd error to any reachable host. Composed SNAT+DNAT outbound
errors were excluded from the outbound re-NAT, so the reversed
builder emitted private client/backend addresses.

What:
Outer-destination gate in `match_outer_v4`/`match_outer_v6`/
`try_embedded_icmp_session_match_from_frame` (translated equivalent
on the forward-NAT arm, quoted source on the fallback arm); composed
SNAT+DNAT admitted to the outbound re-NAT on both the reply-key and
reverse-half arms; pre-DNAT wire destination recovered into
`original_dst`/`original_dst_port` and restored by the SNAT-outbound
builders (outer dst, quoted src, quoted src port, v6 quoted-checksum
delta). Five new `#14665` regression cells; README + `docs/log/14665.md`.

Validation:
RED on origin/master a801922911 (prod reverted, tests kept): all 5
new cells fail. GREEN: all 5 pass; `embedded_icmp` set 37 passed.
Broader `icmp` filter 471 passed / 4 base-attributed failures. Full

## PR #14905 — scheduler: keep recovery pair consistent and fix overnight weekday windows (#14726) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14726-campaign`

Closes #14726

## Defect (D19-04)
1. `recordRepublishResultLocked` cleared `republishFailClosed` on a successful latch republish while `s.active` was still the forced all-false map, so `ActiveStateWithFailClosed` consumers (route listener, ipmon overlay, apply seeding via `policySchedulerPublicationState`) could observe `(inactive, failClosed=false)` — scheduled deny/reject compile inactive (fail-open) until the next tick. An intervening apply-path `RecordRepublishResult(nil)` had the same effect.
2. Accessor split pinned by documentation: the latch boolean covers only the republish latch; `PolicyFailClosed(now)` covers recovery hold / unavailable zone. Daemon paths already OR the two.
3. `isWithinWindow` evaluated overnight windows on today's weekday only: Friday-only 22:00–06:00 was active Fri 00:30 and inactive Sat 00:30 (inverted).

## Fix
- Clearing the latch now recomputes the authoritative map at `lastEval` (hold/zone still force inactive) via `recomputeActiveLocked`; exactly one normal-disposition recovery republish remains owed.
- Overnight windows belong to their starting weekday: today's window contributes its evening segment, the post-midnight tail is yesterday's resolved window (`overnightTailActive`); today's `exclude` suppresses the tail; uniform daily windows unchanged.

## Tests
New `pkg/scheduler/scheduler_14726_test.go` (3 tests, incl. daily/exclude controls). RED on origin/master 59f4ac7065, GREEN with fix; full `pkg/scheduler` suite, `pkg/config` scheduler tests, and daemon scheduler/actuator neighbour tests pass; `go vet` clean. See `docs/log/14726.md`.

## PR #14908 — configstore: serialize rescue saves against delete so deleted cleartext is not resurrected (#14722) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14722-campaign`

## Summary

Fixes D18-05 (#14722): `SaveRescueConfig` wrote `rescue.conf` off-lock while `DeleteRescueConfig` took no lock/fence/WaitGroup, so a delete during an in-flight save was undone by the save's later rename — resurrecting cleartext secrets after a confirmed deletion — and a slow older save could overwrite a newer one.

- `SaveRescueConfig` claims a monotonic rescue generation under `s.mu` with its snapshot/fence-check/`rescueWG` registration, then after `rescueWriteBarrier` takes the new `rescueMu` and refuses to write (`ErrRescueSaveSuperseded`) if superseded.
- `DeleteRescueConfig` claims a generation under `s.mu` and raises `rescueAppliedGen` under `rescueMu` before its durable unlink+dir-fsync; it does not hold `rescueMu` for the unlink or wait on `rescueWG`, so it succeeds promptly during a barrier-held save. A save started after the delete legitimately recreates the file.
- gRPC `rescueAction` maps `ErrRescueSaveSuperseded` to `FailedPrecondition` (like `ErrRescueSaveFenced`); never success, never Internal.
- Deterministic barrier regression tests: delete-vs-in-flight-save (plus post-delete save control) and save/save newest-wins.

## Validation

- RED on `origin/master` `918ac30a36`: both new tests failed (resurrected `rescue.conf`; stale save overwrote newer).
- GREEN after fix: both pass, including `-race`.
- Rescue-focused configstore subset passes (fence #10769, delete-fsync #5197, empty-active #11803, rescue load/migration, `TestRescueConfig`); grpcapi rescue test passes; `go vet` clean.
- Full configstore suite exceeded the 300s harness window on slow pre-existing migration tests without an observed failure — flagged for CI/main verification.

Closes #14722

## PR #14909 — userspace-dp: refresh WG peer captures on same-engine commits (#14675) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14675-campaign`

## Summary
WireGuard control loop and DNS resolver captured `peer_pubkeys`, `effective_endpoints`, and `endpoint_hosts` once at thread spawn and never refreshed them across engine-reusing config commits (#14675, finding D6-03).

## Why
`init_consumer_state` runs once at spawn; `wg_peers_eq` does not compare `endpoint_host`, so a hostname-only commit reuses the engine `Arc` verbatim and moved none of the enumerated stale reasons (removed / engine_changed / attachment / outer_mtu / bind_device / kernel_transport). The surviving thread drove timers/handshakes for the old peer set, sent initiations to a decommissioned literal, and resolved the old hostname forever.

## What
- **Coordinator** (`tunnel_supervision.rs`, `types/runtime.rs`): capture peer config (pubkey, configured literal endpoint, authored hostname, pubkey-sorted from forwarding state — the only place `endpoint_host` exists) into `WgControlEntry::spawned_peer_config` at spawn, beside the other spawn-time captures (#2921/#5291/#10196 precedent); new `peer_config_changed` stale-prune reason restarts the thread (and respawns the resolver with fresh `endpoint_hosts`) on any peer add/remove or endpoint/hostname change.
- **Control loop** (`wg_control/mod.rs`): per-tick `refresh_consumer_peers` converges a surviving thread onto the engine's current table via new `peer_configured_endpoints()` (config-only, no live overlay): added peers adopted with BringUp, configured changes reset effective + clear engine live endpoint + abort pending + drop stale roam-hold stamp, removed peers drop all state; unchanged-config tick is a no-op so live roams survive.
- **Engine/Peer** (`wg/engine.rs`, `wg/peer.rs`): `peer_configured_endpoints()` and `clear_live_endpoint()`.
- NOT changed: the resolver itself — respawn re-captures hosts; a second dynamic-target mechanism was rejected.

## Validation
- 10 new cells (4 coordinator incl. hostname rename on the **same** engine Arc with `engine_ptr` asserted unchanged; 6 `refresh_consumer_peers` unit cells incl. unchanged-roam control): **31 passed, 0 failed** together with wg2921/wg1866/wg5291 neighbors.
- RED probe (branch disabled + refresh early-return): 6 FAILED, controls green; restored.
- Wider `afxdp::coordinator::` + `afxdp::wg::`: 633 passed, 11 failed — all 11 reproduce on pristine `origin/master` d7003705f1 (base-attributed pre-existing).
- Verified GREEN on master 43e9f98a90 (patch-identical). ⚠️ Current master head dede834132b9 has an **unrelated test-only compile break** (`ha_tests.rs` `publish_row` arity from #14650/6621660159) that blocks any `cargo test` build; this branch needs a rebase once that is fixed.

## Risk
A peer commit now restarts the WG control thread (churn already accepted for MTU/bind/kernel-transport captures); sessions/live endpoints survive via engine Arc + live seeding. Hostname rename may serve the old host's last-good address until the new resolver's first answer (5s retry) — the #7158 last-good policy, unchanged.

Full lane log: `docs/log/14675.md` (includes the stash-loss recovery note).

Closes #14675

## PR #14911 — upgrade: preserve committed predecessor on verify failure (#14720) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14720-campaign`

Why:
For a fresh cut `j.PreviousVersion` records the live version, so when the live version's committed predecessor is re-staged under a new generation, `cleanupFailedVerifyCopy`'s guard (`ver == PreviousVersion || ver == cur`) never fires for the predecessor. Verify failure then `RemoveAll`'d `versions/<pred>` plus its `.dbsnap` — identical-bytes, changed-bytes, and same-generation-reuse arms — and `copyStaged` demoted its preserved stamp on byte mismatch before replacing it. `defaultRollbackTarget(live)` then reported no restorable target, deleting the committed rollback target the cut was supposed to keep.

What:
`Run` captures a `predecessorStampBackup` (committed stamp bytes plus a `.<ver>.dbsnap` copy under `.predbak-*`) via `backupCommittedPredecessor` in `commit_stamp.go` before COPY whenever the target is the live version's committed predecessor. `cleanupFailedVerifyCopy` (variadic) skips deletion for a backed-up predecessor, restores its stamp and snapshot, and keeps its `.dbsnap` instead of sweeping it as an orphan; the pre-STOP refuse paths restore the backup. `copyStaged` marks the backup `demotedByReplacement` when it demotes changed or unverifiable bytes, so a just-failed or changed-byte target stays non-committed after auto-rollback and Case-C demotion is never resurrected.

Validation:
New `cutover_predecessor_verify_14720_test.go` cuts 1.0.0 -> 2.0.0, re-stages 1.0.0 under a new generation, and fails VERIFY for identical and changed bytes plus a same-generation-reuse arm, asserting the dir, binaries, stamp (identical arm), and `.dbsnap` survive and `defaultRollbackTarget("2.0.0")=="1.0.0"`; START-failure controls assert the dir/snapshot survive while the stamp stays demoted. RED on `origin/master` (version dir destroyed in all verify arms), GREEN after the fix; full `pkg/upgrade` suite passes and the #12177 envelope controls stay green. RED-on-revert re-verified.

Risk:
Backup copies the predecessor `.dbsnap` under VersionsDir on every predecessor re-stage cut; it is removed on restore or left as a dotfile swept by later GC. No behavior change for non-predecessor targets.

Closes #14720

## PR #14920 — config: keep confirm encryption on later writes (#14719) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14719-campaign`

Why: commitConfirmedLocked sets DB.writeConfirmCover from the
guarded tree and clears it by defer on return, so every later
WriteConfirm of the same window (resolution tombstone on every
resolution in this configuration, finalization retry, boot
rebind/migration rewrites, FIRST sentinel) resolved PrevTree("")
plus cover("") to plaintext and fsynced the full PrevTree secrets
in cleartext, defeating the operator action of enabling
master-password that #14172 armed.

What: encodeConfirm now re-derives the armed profile from durable
state: DB.confirmEncryptionPRF keeps PrevTree-first precedence,
then the transient arm cover, then existingConfirmDiskPRF recovers
env.PRF from the on-disk record's self-describing AES-GCM envelope.
Fail-open to plaintext on absent/unreadable/plaintext disk state
so legacy windows stay plaintext and a corrupt prior record cannot
fail a tombstone/retry write. A 256-byte prefix gate on the
envelope marker avoids re-parsing near-ceiling plaintext records
on every encode. NOT changed: WriteConfirm signature, record
schema, legacy plaintext readability.

Validation: 6 new cells in
confirm_encryption_cover_persist_14719_test.go — 4 mechanism cells
(tombstone, retry, post-restart rewrite, FIRST sentinel) RED
pre-fix with the secret in raw bytes, GREEN post-fix; 2 controls
(end-to-end confirm, plaintext-stays-plaintext) pass both sides.
All 7 #14172 tests and the #9617 tombstone-headroom cell pass.
Full pkg/configstore suite failures are base-identical on
pristine origin/master (9088 x3, 9880, 9984, 9882, 12537).

Risk: a window armed encrypted whose on-disk record was deleted
or replaced with plaintext before a later writer runs falls back
to plaintext as pre-fix; production ordering (tombstone before
delete, retry/rebind/sentinel rewriting an existing record)
makes this unreachable on the named paths. See docs/log/14719.md.

Closes #14719

## PR #14928 — config: lex the edit cursor so the gate judges the executed path (#14716) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14716-campaign`

Why:
Both CLIs stored the interactive `edit` cursor as raw strings.Fields
tokens. AuthorizeConfigMutation lexes only the mutation line and
prepends the cursor verbatim, while execution re-joins the raw tokens
and the store lexer skips block comments and unquotes strings, so
`edit /* interfaces */ "system"` + `set root-authentication ...` was
gated as the raw spelling (anchored deny `^system root-authentication`
missed; comment text could satisfy `allow-configuration
"^interfaces"`) but executed as the denied `system root-authentication`
path. Quote-only (`edit "system"`) and split-comment (`edit system /*`
+ `set */ ...`) constructions desync the same way.

What:
- pkg/config: ParseConfigPath / ParseEditFragment /
  NormalizeEditPathTokens on the store lexer;
  AuthorizeConfigMutation normalizes the stored cursor against the
  line tokens, including a block comment spanning the cursor/line
  boundary, before resolving adjudicated paths.
- Local dispatchConfig edit/set/delete/deactivate/activate/annotate,
  handleCopyRename/handleInsert, and the remote CLI config arms now
  store and prepend only lexed cursors; malformed edit fragments
  (unterminated comment/string) are refused at edit time.
- Regression cells per surface in pkg/config, pkg/cli, cmd/cli plus
  docs/log/14716.md. NOT changed: store SetEditPath API, show
  rendering, gRPC/REST surfaces (nil cursor; they gate the resolved
  line they receive).

Validation:
- RED on base: config cells fail to build (helpers absent); with
  tests only, CLI dispatcher cells allow all three packet
  constructions and the allow cell admits the mutation under
  ^interfaces.
- GREEN: TestParseConfigPath14716,
  TestAuthorizeConfigMutationDecoratedEditPath14716,
  TestDispatchConfigDecoratedEditPathDenied14716,
  TestDispatchConfigDecoratedEditPathAllowNotSatisfiedByComment14716,
  cmd/cli wire/malformed cells; 14716/14717/authz subsets pass in
  pkg/config, pkg/cli, cmd/cli; go vet + gofmt clean.
- Pre-existing (base-attributed): pkg/grpcapi
  TestSetAnnotateRemainsVerbLedForConfigurationGate13554 and sampled
  pkg/cli failures (11455, 5325/13552, 5763) fail identically on
  master; full pkg/config suite timed out at 240s under host load
  >130 — parent gate should re-run full suites.

Risk:
Plain cursors unchanged. Lexically malformed edit fragments are now
refused instead of stored raw; pre-fix cursors are normalized at both
gate and execution, so no stale raw cursor can bypass the deny.

Closes #14716

## PR #14931 — userspace-dp: GC expired BIBs and preserve imported BIB on rollback in deterministic NAPT64 (#14670) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14670-campaign`

Closes #14670

## Defect (D5-01)
`allocate_deterministic_v6_at` in `userspace-dp/src/nat/allocator.rs`:
1. On block-claim failure the only expired-lease handling consulted the candidate's own `bib_key`; a block full of expired idle BIBs under *other* source ports reported permanent `AllocatorExhausted` (no `gc_expired_for_addr_locked` sweep on this path).
2. Both BIB-reuse branches minted joins with `promotion_timeout_ns: None` and no 0->1 activation snapshot, so `rollback_flow` treated promoted/imported BIBs as fresh and deleted them — destroying HA standby BIBs.
3. The full-block reuse branch bypassed the `max_tracked_flows` cap.

## Fix
- Bounded per-address `gc_expired_for_addr_locked(..., PRESSURE_GC_BUDGET)` sweep before declaring exhaustion; retry the lock-free claim only when something was reclaimed.
- Mirror `reuse_existing_lease_locked` activation bookkeeping in both reuse branches; imported leases defer promotion to a completing `release_flow` via the per-flow marker.
- Enforce `max_tracked_flows` on the full-block reuse branch.

## Regression (RED/GREEN verified)
Three new cells in `tests_deterministic_bib_14091.rs`: expired-block reclaim, rollback-preserves-imported-BIB, capacity cap. RED on base: 3 failed / 5 passed. GREEN: 8 passed / 0 failed (incl. #14091 controls). Full evidence in `docs/log/14670.md`.

## PR #14936 — userspace-dp: re-stamp closing sessions on data-bearing segments (#14935) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14935-campaign`

Closes #14935

## Why
First FIN/RST sighting stamped closing + the 30s close window, after which the FIN-owning direction could never refresh last_seen/expires: the slow-path lookup refresh predicate and the flow-cache touch_if_stale both gated on !fin_own/!reset. The 1s reaper removed the entry at FIN+30s regardless of traffic volume — long iperf3 streams stalled to 0 at ~28-30s with SESSION_CLOSE idle Timeout on 200k+-packet flows (#14300 root cause).

## What
- Thread TCP payload progress (tcp_flags::has_payload_progress; payload length derived by the caller from the IP-declared datagram end minus the TCP header end, zero when unknown) through the slow-path lookup (lookup_with_payload / lookup_with_origin_with_payload, deferring-authority lookup, Owner replay), the flow-cache keepalive (touch_if_stale_with_payload), and the poll-descriptor tcp_payload_len helper plus shared-scope/resolve wrappers.
- A data-bearing segment re-stamps a CLOSING (single-FIN) entry from either direction onto the same closing window. Bare ACKs keep the #10885 fixed fuse. Fixed fuse retained only for TIME_WAIT (both FINs) and RST, which never slide on payload.
- Payload-unknown callers pass 0 and retain the pre-fix gate. Companion retention unchanged.
- Split existing close_refresh_gate_10885 ACK-only expectations from data-bearing behavior. Docs: session README, docs/log/14935.md.

## Validation
- New tests pass: data_bearing_segments_restamp_closing_past_fuse_14935, time_wait_and_rst_data_do_not_slide_14935, flow_cache_payload_keepalive_restamps_closing_14935. close_refresh_gate 12/12, session module 453 passed, tcp_flags 37 passed.
- RED: new tests do not compile against pre-fix tree (payload APIs absent).
- Pre-existing gre_decap_flow_cache_hit_ttl_expiry_reads_inner_ttl_5615 failure reproduces identically on origin/master, unrelated.
- Acceptance (loss-cluster long iperf3 60s+, -P12, both directions, v4+v6, >=18 Gbps, no stall) requires deployed build, remains for operator.

## Risk
Payload length derived only from meta offsets bounded by IP-declared datagram end; unknown/truncated yields 0 and keeps old frozen behavior (fail-closed). TIME_WAIT/RST lifetimes unchanged.

## PR #14938 — userspace-dp: thread payload progress through every poll hit path (#14937) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14935b-campaign`

**Userspace-dp**: payload progress was threaded only through the stamped-meta happy path; a subset of poll hit paths still derived `payload_len = 0` for data-bearing segments, so their CLOSING entries kept the frozen #10885 fuse and reaped at 20–30 s while other workers' flows survived.

#### What changed

* `poll_descriptor::tcp_payload_len` falls back to the frame-derived TCP header end (`frame::tcp_payload_offset`, fail-closed on truncated/malformed) when `meta.payload_offset` is unstamped (`0`), instead of reporting "unknown".
* `frame::tcp_payload_offset_from_l3` (new): L3-relative header-end derivation for a bare IP packet with an already-walked relative L4 offset.
* `tunnel::local_origin_packet_meta` stamps the true TCP header END via the new helper (it stamped the L4 start, counting the header as payload — false progress on bare ACKs for GRE/WG local-origin flows).
* Deleted the payload-less AF_XDP wrappers `lookup_session_across_scopes_with_shared` and `resolve_flow_session_decision_with_conntrack`: the poll loop now reaches only the `_and_payload` variants; test/non-worker callers call the inner/`_and_payload` form with an explicit honest 0 (fabric/shared-scope, deferred-owner, and embedded-ICMP-quote legs included; quotes carry no TCP payload of their own).
* Expiry belt-and-braces `closing_counters_keep_alive` retains a CLOSING (single-FIN, non-RST) entry when its canonical forward counters advanced since the last expiry check (change, not historic level; snapshot field `closing_counters_seen`).
* Tests: new `tcp_payload_len_14937_tests` (poll derivation: stamped, unstamped, bare-ACK, truncated), `deferred_owner_payload_replay_restamps_closing_14937`, `closing_counters_retention_keeps_active_pair_14937`, plus updates to the migrated session-code test references.

#### Why

PR #14936 (#14935) re-stamps CLOSING sessions only when `has_payload_progress(tcp_flags, payload_len)` holds, with `payload_len` derived from `meta.payload_offset`. The live loss retest of that build (`b4464fda30`) still shows the all-or-nothing 20–30 s decay: hit-bearing workers go CPU-idle and multi-GB sessions close `idle Timeout` (#14300 open). Diagnosis: the payload-less compatibility wrappers and the unstamped-offset derivation meant a subset of hit paths never supplied payload progress — per-worker bimodal decay is the expected signature. This change removes the poll loop's reachability of payload-less wrappers entirely and adds the frame-derived fallback, so every production hit path carries payload progress (or fails closed).

#### Test evidence

* `cargo test -- 14937 close_refresh_gate`: **18 passed** (4 poll derivation, 2 new session regressions, 12 existing close-gate).
* `cargo test -- session::`: **455 passed**; `session_glue`/`poll_descriptor` suites: 755 passed with 4 pre-existing failures that reproduce unchanged on pristine `origin/master` (`prerouting_scope` #11297 ×2, `publish_shared_session_counts`, `flush_session_deltas_9412`), plus 4 tunnel/D11/segmentation failures verified pre-existing via a clean stash run. `close_refresh_gate` tests were earlier shown RED without the payload progress logic (#14935 tests do not compile pre-fix; the counters-retention test exercises the FINed-side-only scenario that `companion_keeps_alive` refuses, so it cannot pass without the new check).
* Live acceptance (loss-cluster **60s+ `-P12`**, both directions, **v4+v6**, ≥18 Gbps, zero 0-byte streams, zero `idle Timeout` closes on multi-GB sessions) requires a deployed build and remains for the operator.

#### Risk

* Benchmarks available but not run. The frame fallback parses the TCP header only when the stamped offset is absent (not per packet on the happy path); the counters check runs only in the GC pass for idle-crossed entries. TIME_WAIT/RST keep the fixed fuse in every leg, bare ACKs still do not slide a half-close, and unknown/truncated packets still fail closed at 0.

#### Gate

* [x] RED/GREEN regression tests (one per hit path) - session + poll derivation suites.

#### Review focus

* **Routing domains:** N/A - no routing-domain change; payload derivation keys off the frame's own header, not the meta stamp.
* **Timeouts:** unchanged idle/close/timeout windows; `closing_counters_seen` only records the last observed forward counter total to detect change; the only lifetime change is retaining CLOSING (1-FIN, non-RST) entries whose counters advanced since the last GC check. A quiet closing flow still reaps at last-activity + closing window.
* **HaState side effects:** GC retention path (`closing_counters_keep_alive`) sits behind the same `companion_eligible` gate as `companion_keeps_alive`, so deliberately-reaped HA standby/stale-synced entries are not retained; GC order, HA hold/self-heal, and the DELAYED reaping of standby-held entries are not changed.
* **Seam exhaustion:** the GC path calls `rebucket_alive_entry`, sharing the `kept_alive_by_companion` stat (`WheelPopStats::kept_alive_by_companion`) — the same accounting seam, no new stat; seam loads on treated entries: at most one extra probe per idle-crossed entry per GC pass, bounded by finite idle-crossed population, in the GC pass only.

#### Code review

* [ ] [Deep smoke](https://github.com/psaab/xpf/blob/master/docs/testing/deep-smoke.md) — recommended.

#### Session-state/security enforcement

* [ ] Run security flows checks before merging.

Closes #14937

## PR #14940 — userspace-dp: complete TCP handshake on the flow-cache hit path (#14939) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14939-campaign`

Closes #14939

## Why
Live loss @ 8cece4238a: ALL iperf -P12 sessions showed `Timeout: 20` (OPENING) mid-flow instead of 300. `handshake_pending` never cleared: the reverse SYN-ACK is ACK-only under `is_ack_only` (PSH/URG ignored) and seeds the flow cache, and Linux's first data segment (PSH+ACK) is also cache-eligible — so the completing segment and all later data were served by `touch_if_stale_with_payload`, which refreshed only `last_seen_ns` and never consulted `handshake_pending`. Both halves reaped on the 20s opening window under traffic; SYN-less packets then failed strict-syn-check (permanent stall, #14300 root). The #6752 invariant ("completing segment reaches the slow path") holds only for a bare ACK arriving before any cache seed.

## What
- `SessionTable::touch_if_stale_with_payload` (the only session-table call in `stage_flow_cache_hit`) now mirrors the `lookup` completion predicate exactly: TCP, `handshake_pending`, `!closing` (#14630), ACK/no-SYN/non-closing flags, direction `syn_ack_first == is_reverse` (SYN-first forward ACK and SYN-ACK-first reverse ACK). Completion applies even inside the keepalive throttle window, re-buckets via `session_timeout_ns`, propagates via `propagate_tcp_state_to_companion` (also retires `pressure_shed_openings`), pushes the wheel.
- Non-completing hits: unchanged throttled `touch` (one extra bool check, no allocation).
- Deferred-Owner replay and `update_session`/`promote_synced` already completed through the real lookup/update arms — pinned as controls, unchanged. Synced HandshakePending replicas complete on this path once materialized (local hits are cache hits).
- README invariant corrected; `docs/log/14939.md` added.

## Validation
- RED on master: 4/6 new tests fail (`flow_cache_completing_ack_promotes_pending_pair_14939`, `flow_cache_bare_completing_ack_promotes_14939`, `synced_pending_replica_completes_via_flow_cache_hit_14939`, `completed_pair_survives_past_opening_window_under_cache_hits_14939`).
- GREEN: 6/6 incl. deferred-Owner control + post-RST #14630 guard; `session::` suite 461 passed. 5 `flow_cache`-filter failures (GRE TTL, flowless DNAT fragments) reproduce identically on unmodified master — pre-existing.
- Regression shape per issue: install SYN/SYN-ACK via real lookup, drive completing ACK via flow-cache hit path, assert Timeout 300 and survival past opening+closing windows under data.

## Risk
Hot path: one bool check per cache hit; completion arm runs once per handshake. Closing/RST explicitly excluded. Live loss acceptance (60s+ -P12 both directions v4+v6 >=18Gbps, Timeout:300 mid-flow, zero idle-Timeout closes) still required post-merge.

## PR #14942 — userspace-dp: map reverse revalidation zones direction-relatively (#14941) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14941-campaign`

userspace-dp: map reverse revalidation zones direction-relatively (#14941)

Reverse metadata is direction-relative (`reverse.ingress = forward
egress`), but a stale reverse hit's fresh lookup resolves the reply's
egress toward the client and the persist sites wrote that zone as the
pair's forward egress — flipping `reverse.ingress_zone` WAN->LAN.
Later ACKs then classified Foreign in `session_hit_authority`, skipped
their deferred refresh, and idled out at ~28s (#14300).

This maps `new_egress_zone` through `forward_egress_zone_for_hit` at
both `DeferredForwardingRevalidation` persist sites (session_glue
Owner path + poll_descriptor): forward hits pass through, reverse hits
preserve the recorded pair. The #9604 forward-companion arms judge a
forward route by construction and are unchanged; the
neighbor-generation flow-cache invalidation is a correct trigger, not
the defect.

Regression (`_14941`): mapping truth table; a stale reverse hit leaves
forward egress = reverse ingress = WAN and the next WAN ACK is Owner
with its refresh replayed; a forward reroute to dmz still rebinds the
pair (#14318 control). RED pre-fix: `reverse.ingress_zone == 7`
instead of WAN (2). Related suites `_14318` (4), `_9519` (34),
`policy_revalidation` (81), `session::tests` (262) pass.

Closes #14941

## PR #14944 — userspace-dp: validate flow-cache HA lease against current runtime lease (#14943) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-18)

Branch: `fix/14943-campaign`

## Why
FlowCacheStamp froze the 10s HA lease at insert; hits validated against the frozen copy and self-evicted every live entry ~10s after seeding, demoting cached resolutions to HAInactive. `try_refresh_ha_leases` also refused to resurrect an expired stored-active lease on a fresh heartbeat, and the watchdog treats `NeedsLock` as throttle-success (no control retry), so one lapse was permanent. Live correlation in #14300: burst cache evictions at session age ~26–28s, ACKs dropped, idle-timeout closes.

## What
- `flow_cache.rs`: extracted `FlowCacheStamp::current_lease_until` (shared with `capture`). Threaded the worker's live `ha_state` snapshot through the flow-cache lookup from `stage_flow_cache_hit`; lease-carrying entries are validated against the CURRENT runtime lease and re-stamped from it on every hit.
- Fail-closed preserved: a genuinely expired current lease, or an owner vanished/inactivated on a provided (non-empty) runtime map, still misses + evicts. An empty (not-provided) map is not gated — standalone behaviour unchanged; production always passes the live snapshot and `cached_flow_decision_valid` re-checks HA against the same map.
- `ha/session_domain.rs`: a matching fresh heartbeat (incoming active) resurrects an expired stored-active lease, minted from the incoming watchdog exactly as locked `update_ha_state` would. The mismatch arm still never resurrects — licensed by Go's demotion-intent inactive overlay (`haWatchdogGroupsLocked`), so a demotion can never arrive as matching-active. `NeedsLock` remains for CLEAR/membership/stored-empty/no-op.
- Go: comments only, stating the overlay→resurrection licence.

## Validation
- 4 new `_14943` cells: fresh-lease hit past insert+10s + re-stamp, genuinely-expired fail-closed, vanished fail-closed, heartbeat resurrection `Served(2)`. RED verified by reverting both logic hunks (3/4 fail; the fail-closed cell passes in both worlds).
- `flow_cache` + `try_refresh_9629` + `flow_cache_hit` suites: 145 passed, 1 pre-existing failure (`gre_decap_flow_cache_hit_ttl_expiry_reads_inner_ttl_5615`, verified failing identically on unmodified origin/master — its fixture lease is genuinely expired at the harness's real-clock now, unrelated).
- `server::tests::update_ha_state_*`: 13 passed. Go `9629|HARefresh|SessionHA`: passed.
- Details: `docs/log/14943.md`.
- Not run: live loss 60s `-P12` both-directions rig acceptance (requires the HA rig).

## Risk
Hot-path cost is one `BTreeMap` get on lease-carrying hits — no allocation. Resurrection touches only the matching-active fast path; CLEAR/membership/demotion paths are unchanged.

Closes #14943

## PR #15291 — userspace-dp: fuse cache-hit session probes and gate pre-cache neighbor learn (#14945) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/14945-campaign`

Refs #14945 (perf partial — does not close it; live throughput acceptance still requires the loss rig).

## Why
#14945 adjudication (loss, e480baa5a4) refuted the RSS-imbalance theory and measured a per-packet CPU ceiling (~3.4µs/packet, IPC 0.72) with `SessionKey::hash` probes among the top hotspots. The flow-cache hit path paid 3–4 keyed hash probes per packet, and the pre-cache source-neighbor learn re-entered the sharded map on every packet even when the per-worker dedup state proved the pair unchanged inside its refresh interval.

## What
- **(A) Fused session probe**: `SessionTable::probe_hit(key, now_ns, len, tcp_flags, payload_len, dscp)` performs the liveness check, the throttled keepalive (#14939 handshake completion, #14935/#10885 closing gates) and the #2501/#2749 accounting under ONE `record_by_key_mut` borrow. Reverse packets keep the second companion probe exactly as `account_packet` did. `stage_flow_cache_hit` calls it once, replacing `session_is_live_at` + `touch_if_stale_with_payload` + `account_packet`. The TTL/hop-limit decision stays between the probe and the filter/policer/log replay; a would-expire packet takes a liveness-only probe so it is never refreshed, completed, or charged.
- **(B) Gated pre-cache learn**: `stage_parse_flow_and_learn` skips `learn_dynamic_neighbor_from_packet` when the `LearnedNeighborDedup` key (ingress ifindex, VLAN, src_ip, frame source MAC) matches and `RX_LEARNED_NEIGHBOR_REFRESH_INTERVAL_NS` has not elapsed. The dedup leg inside the learn remains the authority for epoch/key changes.

No behavior change except CPU: counters, liveness, handshake/closing semantics, and neighbor-map contents are identical.

## Validation
- New `session/probe_hit_14945_tests.rs`: 5 equivalence cells driving fused vs unfused oracle sequences (forward/reverse/translated-alias, fresh/stale throttle, absent/expired, handshake completion, RST/FIN closing gates) — all state snapshots identical.
- New `pre_cache_learn_skips_sharded_map_inside_dedup_interval_14945`: gated repeat does not recreate a removed neighbor entry nor advance `insert_generation`; post-interval learn recreates it.
- Session, poll_stages, flow_cache_hit, sharded_neighbor, neighbor_dispatch suites green (559+ tests, `--test-threads=1`).
- Pre-existing failure verified at base `e480baa5a4` by reverting this change: `gre_decap_flow_cache_hit_ttl_expiry_reads_inner_ttl_5615` fails identically without it.

## Risk
Accounting now lands under the probe borrow before the cached filter/policer replay; such packets were already keepalive-refreshed there, and forwarded-packet counters stay byte-identical (pinned by the equivalence cells). Live acceptance for #14945 (-P12 ≥22G v4 / ≥19G v6, retransmits near-zero) remains for the loss rig.

## PR #15293 — nat: enforce generation-jump and peer caps on lease batch import (#14963) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/14963-campaign`

Why:
ImportPersistentNatLeaseBatch enforced neither cap that the forwarded-clear path already applied, so one forged or corrupted batch for a known peer at MaxUint64 advanced the durable watermark straight to MaxUint64: the importer cleared every local lease, persisted the poisoned high-water mark, and every genuine batch below it was dropped as stale indefinitely, surviving restart. Unbounded distinct origins also grew RemoteGenerations past the loader peer limit, so the state file failed to load on every restart and persistent-NAT lease export/import was bricked.

What:
In ImportPersistentNatLeaseBatch, refuse a known-peer generation jump over maxPersistentNatGenerationJump14580 (counter + Warn, mirroring ClearPersistentNATLeasesWithGeneration) and refuse a new distinct origin at/over maxPersistentNatGenerationPeers11486. Unseen-origin first contact stays accepted at any generation, and the generation-0 no-barrier carve-out is preserved (cap applies to generation >= 1 advances). NOT changed: stale/local-clear fence handling, ImportIdleLeases helper boundary, or the clear path. New persistent_nat_generation_14963_test.go covers both refusals plus at-bound/unseen/known-at-cap controls; docs/log/14963.md records the change.

Validation:
Not run by the lane agent per campaign handoff discipline; main agent to run RED/GREEN: the new 14963 tests fail on origin/master (forged MaxUint64 batch accepted, 17th peer accepted) and pass with this fix, plus the 11486/14580 generation suites stay green.

Risk:
A known peer silent for >1024 clears then re-advertising is now refused until its generation is re-established, matching the existing forwarded-clear behaviour; accepted trade-off from #14580. Generation-0 first contact can still record 0-watermarks past the cap (no clear barrier, no lease wipe); bounded by the 30s sync cadence and the loader check on the durable file.

Closes #14963

## PR #15295 — upgrade: gate DrainAndConfirm demotion on SyncEstablished (#14953) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/14953-campaign`

Why:
`DrainAndConfirm` checked PeerAlive, HAProtocolCompatible, SessionSyncWireCompatible (wire version, not link state) and PeerTakeoverReady, but never `SyncEstablished` — unlike `runRollingWith` and `runRollingRollbackWith`, which both refuse to drain unsynced. An alive, wire-compatible peer whose sync link is Down/unsynced would be handed every RG by `ForceSecondary`; `DrainComplete` would only time out and fail back after the demotion already churned stateful sessions for the drain window.

What:
Consult `SyncEstablished` in `DrainAndConfirm` after PeerAlive and before `ForceSecondary`; refuse when not established and surface a transport error as `session-sync check`. Not gated behind `allowMixedHA` (rolling parity). Add `kernel_drain_sync_gate_14953` regression (unsynced / sync-error / allowMixedHA / paired healthy with sync-consulted counter) and set `synced: true` on the healthy fakes in `kernel_drain_test.go`. NOT changed: gate ordering of the remaining prechecks, `DrainComplete`, or any rolling path.

Validation:
New 14953 tests RED pre-fix (4/4 fail: demoted unsynced, proceeded on sync error, allowMixedHA bypass, gate never consulted) and GREEN post-fix. Neighbour run (`-run 14953|TestDrain|TestRejoin|TestAbortFailback|7990|TestRolling`) green; full `go test ./pkg/upgrade/ -count=1` ok (130s); `go vet` clean; `gofmt` clean.

Risk:
A peer whose sync link flaps down at drain time now refuses the kernel drain instead of demoting-then-failing-back; operator retries once sync is established. No behaviour change for synced peers.

Closes #14953

Why: When a peer reboot (A->B) was classified by installConn, its post-eviction scan advanced s.peerIdentity to B and preserved B's pre-evidence sibling. ## PR #15304 — userspace-dp: stop WG TunOrigin ICMPv6 session poisoning (#14958) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/14958-campaign`

## Summary
`wg_tun_origin_packet_initiates` (tun_origin.rs) matched ICMP direction only for `PROTO_ICMP` (1). ICMPv6 is protocol 58 (`PROTO_ICMPV6`), so every ICMPv6 TUN packet fell to the directionless `_ => true` arm. An ICMPv6 Echo Reply (129) — the kernel's answer to an admitted peer→firewall Echo Request (128) — therefore counted as initiating and `publish_wg_tun_origin_entries` minted a `SessionOrigin::TunOrigin` pair. The synthesized reverse is the peer's Echo Request tuple as a LocalDelivery entry; a later unsolicited peer Echo Request HITs it and `tun_origin_reverse_exempt` skips host-inbound + junos-host NEW-session gates.

## Fix
One file, one function: split the ICMP arm.
- `PROTO_ICMP` → 8 | 13 (unchanged).
- `PROTO_ICMPV6` → 128 only. 128-only is deliberate: ICMPv6 has no timestamp query (133 is Router Solicitation), and the identifier-keyed parser yields no forward key for 133-137, so those types never reach the gate (test pins 137 → None).

Fail-closed: every other ICMPv6 type is non-initiating. UDP/other protocols keep documented directionless behaviour. Encap unchanged — the gate only gates publish.

## Regression
- `wg_tun_origin_icmpv6_reply_does_not_initiate_14958`: 128 → Some(true), 129 → Some(false), 137/1 → None.
- `wg_tun_origin_icmpv6_reply_publish_skips_14958`: production parse+build+publish of the 129 shape leaves shared/dedup/tombstones empty; 128 control creates all three.
- RED proven on mutant restoring master behaviour (ICMPv6 arm → `true`): both fail with `initiates(reply)==true`, 0 passed / 2 failed. Fix restored byte-identical, re-verified 19 wg_tun_origin cells green.
- Controls: full `wg_tun_origin_*` / `_10038` suite green. `tun_origin` filter: 28 passed, 2 pre-existing GRE env failures (`ha_inactive`) identical on two independent base binaries; diff touches tun_origin.rs only.

Closes #14958

Branch: `fix/14965-campaign`

Why:
`batchDeleteExactV4/V6` retry the tail per key with bare
`DeleteSession`/`DeleteSessionV6` after a chunk stops at a missing key,
dropping `RoutingDomain` and `PurgeTunnelVariants`; the userspace bare
delete re-derives scope from the surviving mirror row and can never
carry the purge flag, so a GRE0 policy-invalidation row deleted on the
recovery path exact-matches and leaks. `deletePeerBatchKnownExactV4/V6`

full scoped key, falling back to bare `DeleteSession` only for
dataplanes without the capability. Peer forward/reverse scoped keys
carry `PurgeTunnelVariants` (set-matching uses the full key), and a
partial-batch error still retires applied entries' companions and
DNAT rows before returning the error. `Manager.DeleteSessionScoped[V6]`
sends a `mirror_delete` naming the caller scope + purge flag without
probing the mirror; `LegacyDataPlaneAdapter` forwards it. Compile-time
belts pin the capability on both published types
(`scoped_singular_delete_published_14965.go` /
`scoped_singular_delete_adapter_14965.go`). NOT changed: the bare
`DeleteSession` path (no scope to carry by construction) and the
RoutingDomain retry leg's #9146 self-scope behaviour for dataplanes
without the new capability.

included the missing key via bare retry; peer purge lost, companion
orphaned, 0 DNAT deletes) and pass after the fix
(`session_store_batch_retry_scoped_14965_test.go`,

`TestTrunkWithNoUnitZeroPutsNoUnitRowOnTheParentIfindex_7509`).

Dataplanes without the scoped singular capability keep the bare retry

## PR #15312 — config: refuse re-gated duplicate-policy folds on tolerant load (#14968) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/14968-campaign-pub`

## Why

The tolerant #8752 duplicate-policy fold merges repeated `policy <name>`
statements into the first occurrence. #9571 refused a fold that turns a
restrictive statement into a merged PERMIT, but it compared only terminal
actions (D30-02, validated MATERIAL 3-way in research run `tpzkKgAuZL`).
Three re-gatings survived unpoisoned on `CompileConfigLenient` /
`CompileConfigForNodeLenient`:

- **Cross-product permit widening** — two PERMIT statements differing in
  ≥2 match dimensions fold into source-union × destination-union ×
  application-union, permitting combinations no statement permitted.
- **Excluded-set deny disarming** — an excluded-address flag/list from
  one statement is OR-ed/unioned onto a surviving deny, which then
  matches the complement and no longer covers traffic its own statement
  denied.
- **Scheduler narrowing** — a `scheduler-name` from one statement is
  inherited last-wins by an unconditional surviving deny, narrowing it
  to that window.

## What

- `mergeInstancesUnder` (`pkg/config/dup_instance_merge_8752.go`) captures
  every source statement's compiled policy (`compilePolicy`, the #9571
  reader) before folding; after the fold,
  `foldChangesPolicySemantics14968` compares the merged policy against
  the statements and poisons non-union folds via the existing
  `LenientContentDropped` mechanism (snapshot refused, previous-good
  retained, fresh-boot default-deny). The #9571 action leg is preserved;
  a `semantic` flag selects the `#14968` warning in both compiler entry
  points.
- NOT changed: the fold itself, strict-commit gates (#3473/#14449),
  scheduler definitions, and folds whose merged semantics are the union
  of the statements (single-dimension permit differences, identical
  excluded sets, one shared scheduler) — pinned unpoisoned by controls.
- Docs: `docs/log/14968.md`, `pkg/config/README.md`,
  `pkg/config/types_security.go`.

## Validation

- RED on base `b8f1ff7ac9`: new rows in
  `pkg/config/dup_policy_fold_crossproduct_14968_test.go` (cross-product
  zone-pair/global/source×application, excluded-set, scheduler) failed
  with nothing poisoning the merged policy on both lenient entry points.
- GREEN after the fix, including five semantics-preserving controls; the
  #9571/#9992/#11063/#12820/#14449 fold suites and downstream
  `pkg/policymatch` + `pkg/dataplane/userspace` fold-widening suites
  pass; `go vet ./pkg/config/` clean.
- Two wider-suite failures (`TestDuplicateTriggerUntilTakesTheLastValue6771`,
  `TestFlatSetChainWalkRatchet8939`) reproduce identically on pristine
