## PR #15313 — ipsec: capture VRF-enslaved st0 in divert, scope host-input fence to tunnel slaves (#14974) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/14974-campaign`

Closes #14974

## Mechanism (D32-01)
A routing-instance member `st0.<N>` enslaved to a VRF (e.g. `vrf-blue`) presents `iifname=vrf-blue` and `meta sdifname=st0.0` at forward/input. Two defects followed:
- `inet xpf_ipsec_divert` emitted only `iifname "st0.0"` queue rules — never matching enslaved ingress, so IPsec capture was bypassed.
- `HostInputFenceOverlay` resolved the xfrmi `MasterIndex` to the VRF name and emitted a bare `iifname "vrf-blue"` DROP — fencing every co-member of the VRF, not just the tunnel.

## Fix
- `IpsecDivertRule.Master` / `ipsecQueueKey.Master`: `buildIpsecCaptureQueuePlan` resolves the master from the live link `MasterIndex` via `ipsecFenceLinkByIndex` (unresolvable → fail-closed quarantine, no keys); `emitIpsecDivertRules` renders `iifname <master> meta sdifname <tunnel>` + queue. Unenslaved rules are byte-identical.
- `HostInputFenceOverlay` gains `SlaveSet`/`MasterSlavePairs` (canonicalised, bound into the counter marker). `ipsecHostInputFenceOverlayForPermit` emits `(vrf-blue, st0.0)` pairs instead of bare VRF masters; unenslaved tunnels stay bare masters. Both renderers (netlink `buildHostInboundNetlink` and text oracle in `daemon_nft.go`) emit `iifname "vrf-blue" meta sdifname "st0.0" … drop` per pair; `VerifyHostInboundOverlay`/`decodeHostOverlayRule` verify the iifname+sdifname unions.
- `ipsecDivertSpecMasters9506` returns tunnel slave names so a divert-transition hold cannot fence the whole VRF.

## Tests
- RED on `origin/master` (detached worktree, tests only): both 14974 test files fail (missing `Master`/`SlaveSet`/`MasterSlavePairs`/`HostInputFencePair`, iifname-only shapes).
- GREEN: `TestIpsecDivertVRFEnslavedCapture14974`, `TestIpsecDivertUnenslavedUnchanged14974`, `TestHostInputFenceOverlayScopedToTunnel14974`, `TestHostInputFenceOverlayUnenslavedUnchanged14974`, `TestIpsecCaptureDivertSpecVRFEnslaved14974`, `TestIpsecCaptureQueuePlanResolvesVRFMaster14974` (incl. unresolvable-master quarantine control), `TestIpsecHostInputFenceOverlayVRFScoped14974` (mixed enslaved st0.0 + unenslaved st1).
- Adjacent: full `pkg/nftables` suite pass; daemon `TestIpsecCapture|TestHostInputFence|TestIpsecHost|TestIpsecPermit|TestRIMember` and netlink-parity suites pass.

Docs: `docs/log/14974.md`.

## PR #15315 — upgrade: preserve kernel-roll leases and rejoin on transient fence loss (#14992) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/14992-campaign`

## Summary
Fixes D38-04 (#14992): `cmd_kernel_roll` stranded a drained node on a transient fence loss.

- `_fence_before_mutate` collapsed an UNCONFIRMABLE lease (peer SSH blip — no successor proved) into `lost_lease`, so the `finally` skipped the restore-forwarding rejoin; it then unconditionally deleted both `/var/lib/xpf/kernel-roll.lease` files. A deleted lease reads `leaseNone` in Go `KernelSelfRecovery.Tick` — a permanent no-op — permanently disabling self-recovery on the drained node.
- Fix: `_fence_before_mutate` gains an `on_unreachable` callback (invoked only on the unconfirmable branch; `on_lost` keeps its legacy both-outcomes behaviour when not supplied — the fence itself stays fail-closed on both outcomes, and no other caller changes). `cmd_kernel_roll` passes it, so only a PROVEN loss (fence `LOST` / keepalive) suppresses the finally rejoin (#5816 preserved).
- Fix: the `finally` now PRESERVES both leases whenever the roll drained the node and did not complete (mirroring `image-roll`'s never-both-down stance), leaving them to expire so the expired-lease `KernelSelfRecovery` fingerprint can fire. Clean success, pre-drain aborts, dry-run, and drained-but-rebooted rolls still release.

Scope: `scripts/deploy` only, per the issue's binding scope narrowing. The cited Go symbols needed no change — the defect was the Python finally destroying the lease state the Go machine correctly keys on.

## Tests
- New `KernelRollTransientFenceLossTests` + `FenceUnreachableCallbackTests` in `scripts/deploy/test_xpf_deploy_lease_renew_fence.py`, with a lease-state-tracking backend (assertions measure real lease presence, not mocks of the code under test).
- RED on `origin/master`: finally skipped the rejoin (`verbs == [('fw0','drain')]`) and deleted both leases; `on_unreachable` unsupported.
- GREEN here: drain + restore rejoin, `clears == []`, both leases present; proven-loss control keeps #5816 no-rejoin; arm-failure control rejoins and preserves.
- Adjacent suites green (81 tests): `test_xpf_deploy_lease_renew_fence`, `test_xpf_deploy_kernel_roll`, `test_xpf_deploy_correctness`, `test_xpf_deploy_recreate_keepalive_6762`, `test_xpf_deploy_daemon_hold_7559`.

Docs: `docs/in-place-upgrade.md` fence/lease-disposition paragraphs updated; `docs/log/14992.md` added.

Closes #14992

## PR #15319 — api: require held lock for config confirm (#14985) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/14985-campaign`

## Summary

Implements #14985 (D36-05, surviving leg only): `POST /api/v1/config/confirm` — and the gRPC `ConfirmCommit` twin, which share `Store.ConfirmCommitAs` — could be driven by a session that never held the config lock.

Mechanism: `ConfirmCommitAs` gated on `ensureHolderLocked`, whose `!configDir` and empty-holder bypasses are correct for candidate mutators but fail-open for confirm. A pending commit-confirmed window survives `ExitConfigure`, and leaving config mode is the routine post-`commit confirmed` state — so after the owner exited, any well-formed REST session token could cancel another operator's auto-rollback and make an unconfirmed config permanent.

Fix (one check in `ConfirmCommitAs`, same `s.mu` acquisition): when a window is pending and the caller is session-scoped, the caller must be the recorded effective holder, else `ErrConfigLockedByOther` (REST 409 / gRPC PermissionDenied). Internal (`""`) callers keep their bypass; the no-pending-window error is unchanged; holder confirms are byte-identical.

Excluded per the issue's binding scope narrowing (not reintroduced): the commit lock-turnover TOCTOU (already closed by the #6808 epoch-bound `CommitAuthority`) and the regex sub-leg (confirm carries no config path for `*-configuration` regexes to adjudicate).

## Validation

- RED on master `3d5bc4cd6c`: `StrangerAfterOwnerExit` — stranger REST confirm returned **200** and cleared the window.
- GREEN after fix: **409**, window still pending; controls `OwnerWhileHoldingLock` and `RESTHolderConfirmsOwnWindow` green before and after.
- Targeted `pkg/configstore` holder/confirm/commit-confirmed cells: ok (222s). `pkg/api` config/confirm surface: ok (43s). `go vet` + `gofmt` clean.
- Full `pkg/configstore` suite exceeded the 600s lane sandbox timeout (unrelated goroutine dump in `TestConcurrentMasterKeyCreateConverges_9898` at the tail). **Main agent: please run full `pkg/configstore`, `pkg/grpcapi`, `pkg/cli` suites before merge.**

## PR #15321 — daemon: enforce faillock on root, ignore comment mentions, and strip managed PAM rules on rollback (#14973) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/14973-campaign`

Closes #14973

## Why
`applySSHPAMFaillock` (D31-05) had three defects: the managed `pam_faillock.so` lines lacked `even_deny_root`, so root password guessing was never locked out; a comment in `/etc/pam.d/common-auth` merely mentioning `pam_faillock.so` was mistaken for an administrator-installed policy and silently suppressed the managed install; and `applySSHConfig` never stripped the managed PAM rules when a later step failed, leaving lockout policy behind after a failed apply.

## What
- Add `even_deny_root` to the managed preauth/authfail/authsucc lines.
- Decide "admin already has faillock" via `hasActivePAMFaillock`: only non-comment, non-blank PAM lines whose module field is `pam_faillock.so` (or a path ending in it) count. Real admin rules still suppress install; comment mentions no longer do.
- `applySSHConfig` records whether its faillock step changed `common-auth` and, via a deferred check on the final named result, strips the managed rules on any failure (drop-in write, `sshd -t` validate, reload, drop-in/legacy removal, sshd-config render) through `setSSHPAMFaillock(false)`. No-op when this apply changed nothing, so pre-existing admin faillock is never removed.
- Managed-block upgrade compatibility: pre-#14973 bodies (without `even_deny_root`) are recognised as known-good variants in `stripPAMFaillockBlock`, so hosts already carrying the old rules upgrade in place (strip + re-add) and remain strippable on rollback, instead of failing every apply as "modified". Tampered bodies are still refused.

## Validation
- New `pkg/daemon/ssh_faillock_14973_test.go`: `even_deny_root` enforcement; comment-mention install (comment preserved, idempotent) with real-admin-rule control; legacy-rule upgrade to byte-identical fresh install, legacy strip, tampered-body refusal; `applySSHConfig` rollback on reload, validate, drop-in-write, and content-build failures, plus success-keeps-rules control.
- Targeted: `go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run 14973|Faillock|11492 -count=1` — ok (includes existing #11492 tests: stock install, idempotence/reversibility, custom stack untouched, appliance skip).
- `go vet ./pkg/daemon/` clean.

## Risk
A failed SSH apply on non-appliance hosts rewrites `common-auth` once more to remove rules it just installed; a failing strip is logged and joined into the apply error, never masking the original failure. Appliance hosts, admin-installed faillock, and unsupported PAM stacks are untouched. No wire or config-schema change.

## PR #15322 — dhcp: gate DHCPv6 REBIND teardown on granting server (#14997) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/14997-campaign`

## Summary

Fixes D40-03 (#14997): `v6RenewMatcher` accepted a DHCPv6 REBIND Reply from any server on transaction-ID + client-DUID alone (the #14600 RFC 8415 §18.2.5 any-server arm), and the run loop trusted its contents to tear down state — an IA_PD `NoPrefixAvail` cleared every held delegation (`pdRefused` arm), a valid-lifetime-0 IA_NA deconfigured the WAN address (`errV6AddrInvalidated`), and a valid-lifetime-0 IAPREFIX withdrew that prefix. Any on-link host that learned the transaction ID and client DUID (both observable on-link; the REBIND is multicast) could tear down the WAN lease and the whole IA_PD delegation with one spoofed packet at T2.

## Fix

Matcher-layer, fail-closed, in `pkg/dhcp`:

- `renew.go`: in REBIND, a Reply from a non-granting server is rejected when it carries teardown content (`v6ReplyTearsDownHeldBinding`: non-Success status at message or requested-IA level, valid-lifetime-0 IAADDR/IAPREFIX in a requested IA). Pure extensions from a failover partner still pass and become the next RENEW binding (#14600 preserved). RENEW is unchanged. RFC basis: §18.2.5 any-server Rebind covers bindings the server actually has; §18.2.10/§21 forbid a different server replacing the binding mid-renewal.
- `dhcp.go`: `RenewalBindingStats` gains `DHCPv6TeardownRejects` for observability.
- `README.md` + `docs/log/14997.md`: extension/teardown split documented, including why DHCPv4 needs no twin (partner NAK in REBINDING is the documented #14600 RFC 2131 §4.3.2 behaviour; v4 has no PD set).

Not changed: `parseV6ReplyChecked`, `extractDelegatedPrefixes`, `reconcileDelegatedPDs`, run-loop arms, acquisition/stateless matchers, DHCPv4, and the synthesis-refuted negative-status parser sub-leg. A granting server's teardown on RENEW/REBIND is byte-for-byte the pre-fix behaviour.

## Validation

- New `dhcpv6_rebind_teardown_14997_test.go`: five destructive REBIND cells from an attacker DUID RED on base (matcher accepted, counter 0) and RED-on-revert with the gate stashed; GREEN with the fix. Controls: partner/granting extension accepted end-to-end (held address kept, partner DUID stored, PD extended), granting teardown on REBIND/RENEW accepted, partner RENEW teardown identity-rejected.
- `go test ./pkg/dhcp/... -count=1` PASS; `go vet ./pkg/dhcp/` clean; gofmt / `git diff --check` clean.

## Risk

A failed-over partner that genuinely holds no binding now has its `NoBinding` Reply ignored at T2; the client keeps the binding until the partner grants an extension or the lease expires into a fresh Solicit (RFC 8415 §18.2.10 posture). No lab failover-pair capture; the gate is at the unit-tested matcher seam and the run loop is unchanged for accepted Replies.

Closes #14997

## PR #15326 — dhcp: remove orphaned WAN address and anchor T1/T2 on co-held invalidation (#14998) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/14998-campaign`

Why:
A co-held IA_NA+IA_PD RENEW/REBIND Reply whose IA_NA IAADDRs are all
valid-lifetime 0 (RFC 8415 §18.2.10.1 explicit invalidation) bypassed
`errV6AddrInvalidated` when a live IA_PD was present: parse returned an
address-less success lease (`LeaseTime` from the PD / 3600s floor),
`commitLease` stored it without removing the held kernel WAN address,
and timers re-derived from the bogus lease — orphaning the WAN address.
A delegated-prefix expiry interrupting the T1/T2 wait also restarted the
full tier wait on every prune (Path A only; Path B past-expiry stays
bounded by the lease deadline).

What:
- `parseV6ReplyChecked` fires `errV6AddrInvalidated` whenever the IA_NA
  is explicitly invalidated, regardless of co-held live PDs, so the run
  loop deconfigures via `abandonLeaseAfterExpiry`.
- `commitLease` removes the previous address whenever it differs from
  the committed address — including an address-less successor — before
  applying the new one.
- `runDHCPv6` anchors T1/T2 to `Obtained`-derived absolute instants and
  resumes after a PD prune via the new `remainingTimer` helper.
- Regression: `pkg/dhcp/dhcpv6_coheld_invalidate_14998_test.go`; contract:
  `pkg/dhcp/README.md`; log: `docs/log/14998.md`.

commit test `removed=[]` want `[prev]`; PD-prune test post-prune T1 wait
`#2 = 20s` want remaining ~1s. GREEN: targeted
`go test ./pkg/dhcp/ -run '14998|5927|13559|14598|CommitLease|RenewalTimers' -count=1`
passed; full `go test ./pkg/dhcp/ -count=1` passed; race subset passed;
`go vet ./pkg/dhcp/` and gofmt clean.

- DNS keeps its own acquisition after the hold (nested takes deadlock; DNS merges live leases, not the gated snapshot).
- Wiring pins updated for the moved spellings (#14582, #11450).

## PR #15333 — daemon: block symlink traversal through user-writable .ssh in login apply and deprovision (#14970) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/14970-campaign`

Closes #14970

## Why
`/home/<user>/.ssh` is writable by the login user while the daemon acts on it as root (D31-02, Critical):
- `applySystemLogin` ran `os.Chown` on the `.ssh` path — follows a planted symlink, re-owning the **target directory**.
- `fsatomic.WriteFileDurable(authorized_keys)` created its temp file inside the (symlinked) directory and renamed it over the target's file — root **overwrite of an arbitrary path**.
- The emptied-key revocation (`applySystemLogin` else-branch) and `deprovisionLoginUser` ran `os.Remove(managedAuthorizedKeysPath)` — unlinks the **resolved victim file** when `.ssh` is a symlink.

## What
- `pkg/daemon/login_password.go`: `checkSSHPathNotSymlink` (Lstat; absent is not a refusal, other errors fail closed), `ensureSSHDirSafeForWrite`, and `removeManagedAuthorizedKeys` (refuses a symlinked `.ssh`/`authorized_keys` instead of deleting the resolved file; raw `os.Remove` error otherwise so `IsNotExist` handling is unchanged).
- `pkg/daemon/daemon_hostauth_apply.go`: key-install leg checks before `MkdirAllDurable`/`Chown` and again immediately before `WriteFileDurable` (key claim rolled back on refusal); emptied-key revoke uses the guarded removal (refusal → fail + marker retained).
- `deprovisionLoginUser` key removal uses the guarded removal (refusal → markers kept, retry next apply).
- Root's `/root/.ssh` is root-writable only and intentionally untouched. Docs: `docs/system-login.md` + `docs/log/14970.md`.

## Validation
- New `pkg/daemon/login_ssh_symlink_14970_test.go`: 4 regressions (symlinked `.ssh` on apply, symlinked `authorized_keys` on apply, symlinked `.ssh` on deprovision, symlinked `.ssh` on emptied-key revoke) **fail on unmodified origin/master**, pass after the fix; legitimate-path control passes before and after.
- Adjacent host-auth suites pass (`TestApplySystemLogin|TestReconcileAbsentLoginUsers|TestDeprovision|EmptiedKeys|TestApplyRootAuth|RootAuth`); `go vet ./pkg/daemon/` clean; full `pkg/daemon` suite shows only the pre-existing `TestRunStartupGoodbyeKeepsDistinctIdentityWithdraw10789` failure, identical on pristine `origin/master`.

## Risk
A pre-existing operator-planted symlinked `.ssh` now fails the login apply closed until replaced with a real directory; legitimate trees unaffected. A link swapped between the Lstat check and the operation is a TOCTOU residual of the same class accepted by the repo's other Lstat-then-act guards (#8482, #9897).

## PR #15334 — configstore: stop minting internal authority for unheld sessions (#14990) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/14990-campaign`

## Summary

`AuthorizeCommitAs` minted `authorityInternal` for a named session that passed `ensureHolderLocked` only via the `!configDir` / empty-holder bypasses, and `ForceExitConfigure` did not mark the evicted holder reclaimed. Since `verifyCommitAuthorityLocked` accepts internal authority unconditionally, a non-holder or evicted session held an unexpiring capability to promote another operator's candidate (D38-02).

## Fix

- `AuthorizeCommitAs`: internal authority only for the explicit empty-session internal caller. A named session must be the recorded holder and receives the epoch-bound holder authority, otherwise `ErrConfigLockedByOther`.
- `ForceExitConfigure`: records the evicted holder in `reclaimedHolders` (mirroring the #9632 lease reclaim) and logs the effective holder.
- One `pkg/api` eBPF fixture now holds its candidate with the REST session it commits as; assertions unchanged.
- Preserved: #5059 editing of an unowned local-CLI candidate by named sessions, and all internal/system commit paths.

## Validation

- New `commit_authority_14990_test.go` cells RED on origin/master (named/not-in-config minted internal; evicted-after-ForceExit minted internal) and GREEN after the fix, with internal/holder/never-evicted/re-entry controls.
- Targeted configstore `14990|6808|9632|5059|4476|7635`, bounded commit/authority run, `pkg/api`+`pkg/grpcapi` holder/commit runs, and `go vet` pass.
- `pkg/grpcapi` 6960 vlan-tagging failures are base-attributed: identical on unmodified `origin/master` (3a10a520d5).

Docs: `pkg/configstore/README.md`, `docs/log/14990.md`.

Closes #14990

## PR #15335 — frr: filter explicit redistribute tokens by node in mixed policies (#15011) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15011-campaign`

Why:
redistProtocolsFiltered gated explicit from-protocol tokens only through the known-protocol allowlist; the self drop and redistSourceFitsNode family check applied only to the no-from expansion. redistributeEntriesAt filters explicit tokens in its own loop, but merges redistProtocolsForNode whenever any term lacks from protocol, re-adding every dropped token. A common Junos BGP export shape (a from protocol bgp term plus a local route-filter term) rendered redistribute bgp under router bgp and ospf6 under IPv4; FRR rejects both lines and one rejected line fails the whole managed frr-reload, so later removals never leave FRR.

What:
Gate explicit tokens in redistProtocolsFiltered through the same self and redistSourceFitsNode filters as the no-from expansion whenever a render node is in hand. The node-less explicit-only set (redistProtocols, self/node "") is unchanged, so per-source map definitions and the collision guard render exactly as before.

Validation:
New cells in redistribute_mixed_explicit_15011_test.go cover redistProtocolsForNode, redistributeEntriesAt, the full BGP managed section, and OSPF/OSPFv3 nodes: RED on the pre-fix tree (redistribute bgp / ospf6 leak at self and IPv4 nodes), GREEN post-fix. Controls pin the no-from expansion, fitting explicit ospf6 under address-family ipv6 unicast, and the node-less explicit set. Full pkg/frr suite shows only 3 pre-existing failures reproduced identically on pristine origin/master 2ed3b1cc71 (base-attributed). gofmt and go vet clean.

Risk:
Only mixed explicit+no-from policies at a render node change; explicit-only policies already took the filtered loop. Inert maps for self/off-family explicit sources may still be defined by the node-less set, unreferenced at non-fitting nodes.

Closes #15011

## PR #15337 — nat: release NAT64 and local SNAT ports exactly once across HA paths (#14961) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/14961-campaign`

Why: HA Session Delete, Drop-Sweep, and Tunnel-Purge leaked NAT64 port allocations and could prematurely free active local SNAT ports (D26-05, issue #14961). The coordinator's dropped-DeleteSynced repair (release_dropped_delete_for_worker) released only the source-NAT leg, stranding the NAT64 translated (pool v4, port) and its BIB active reference for the life of the allocator — the worker is alive, so neither the dead-worker sweep nor generation teardown can see its holder bit. The tunnel-remap purge (purge_remapped_tunnel_sessions) likewise released only the import-time SNAT reservation.

What: release_dropped_delete_for_worker now also calls release_nat64_allocation_for_worker with the same worker id (holder-aware, idempotent — byte-for-byte the worker's own teardown). purge_remapped_tunnel_sessions releases both allocator families, via the new production untracked helper release_synced_nat64_allocation_untracked_for_purge in nat64.rs (mirrors release_synced_source_nat_allocation_untracked; Untracked frees only records no worker adopted), and counts once per reservation actually freed in either family (preserving the #8124 count-only-actual-frees rule). The delete-drop sweep (DeleteDropSweep::step_with_nat, #10288) already released both families holder-aware; it is pinned by new exactly-once tests rather than changed. NOT changed: queued deletes still leave the release to the worker; adopted reservations survive the untracked purge release; reverse entries remain no-ops. Note: Coordinator::purge_shared_sessions_for_tunnel_endpoints and a production release_synced_nat64_allocation_untracked do not exist on current master (the latter was cfg(test)-only), so the purge helper was added under a distinct production name.

RED pre-fix (production fix stashed): a_dropped_deletesynced_releases_the_workers_nat64_reservation_14961, a_dropped_deletesynced_preserves_a_second_workers_nat64_hold_14961, tunnel_remap_purge_releases_nat64_reservation_14961 all failed with NAT64 BIB active_flows stuck at Some(1) vs Some(0). Full userspace-dp suite: 8566 passed, 54 failed — sampled failures (filter cached_tx_selection, cos literal guard, wire_invariant, shim_index) reproduced identically on clean origin/master, so base-attributed, not introduced here.

Risk: holder-aware idempotent releases only; under-release direction preserved (a bounded leaked port over handing a live worker's port to a new flow). No behaviour change outside the cited HA delete / drop-sweep / tunnel-purge mechanism.

## PR #15338 — frr: enable BFD before binding its profile on OSPFv2 and IS-IS (#15015) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15015-campaign`

## Summary

An OSPFv2 or IS-IS interface configured with `bfd-liveness-detection minimum-interval`/`multiplier` rendered only a profile binding (` ip ospf bfd profile xpf-<i>-<m>` / ` isis bfd profile xpf-<i>-<m>`) with no bare enable line. In FRR 10.6 neither profile line enables BFD monitoring by itself, so commit and frr-reload reported success while no BFD session ever ran; convergence silently fell back to the OSPF dead interval / IS-IS hold time.

Primary-source verification against FRR frr-10.6.0:

- OSPFv2 (`ospfd/ospf_bfd.c`): the `ip ospf bfd profile` DEFUN refuses with "ip ospf bfd has not been set" (CMD_WARNING) unless `ip ospf bfd` already allocated `bfd_config`; `ospf_bfd_write_config` prints ` ip ospf bfd` before the profile line. FRR docs: the profile command "Only takes effect if `ip ospf bfd` command is also present."
- IS-IS (`isisd/isis_cli.c`, `isis_nb_config.c`, `isis_bfd.c`): `isis bfd profile` sets only the `bfd-monitoring/profile` leaf; the `enabled` leaf is set solely by `isis bfd`, and `bfd_handle_adj_up` skips circuits with `enabled=false`. `cli_show_ip_isis_bfd_monitoring` prints ` isis bfd` first.

NOT changed (verified self-enabling): OSPFv3 (`ipv6 ospf6 bfd [profile ...]` is a single DEFUN setting `enabled=true`) and BGP (`neighbor X bfd profile` is documented as "Same as `neighbor X bfd`").

## Changes

- `pkg/frr/protocols_render.go`: emit ` ip ospf bfd\n` / ` isis bfd\n` immediately before the profile line in the OSPFv2 and IS-IS interface loops when custom timers select a profile; the IS-IS pair stays inside the interface block before `exit` (#2942). Bare-BFD branch byte-identical.
- `pkg/frr/bfd_profile_enable_15015_test.go` (new): `TestBFDProfileEnableLines15015`.
- `pkg/frr/README.md`, `debian/changelog`, `docs/log/15015.md`.

## Validation

- `TestBFDProfileEnableLines15015`: **RED on base `299c7b6a29`** (profile line rendered alone, no enable line, for OSPFv2 300/3, IS-IS 250/4, and the interval-only cell), **GREEN after the fix**. Controls: bare BFD = exactly one enable line and no profile binding (both protocols); interval-only OSPFv2 gets the pair; no-BFD renders nothing.
- Adjacent suites green: `TestGenerateProtocols_OSPFBFD`, `_BGPBFD`, `_OSPFv3BFD`, `_OSPFv3BFDProfile`, `TestBuildManagedSection_SingleGlobalBFDBlock`, `TestGenerateProtocols_ISISBFDInsideInterfaceBlock`.
- Full `pkg/frr` suite: 3 failures (`TestFamilylessIPv6NeighborWithoutPolicyIsV6Only11564`, `TestFRRLoadBGPClasslessRIBSuppression11426`, `TestFRRLoadInet6OnlyNeighborIPv4Deactivation11374`) reproduce identically with the fix stashed on the same tree — base-attributed at `299c7b6a29`, unrelated BGP neighbor-family tests.
- `gofmt` clean on touched files; `go vet ./pkg/frr` clean.

## Risk

Profile-carrying OSPFv2/IS-IS interfaces gain one rendered line each, matching the two-line shape FRR itself writes back, so existing deployments get working BFD on the next reload with no config change. Lab acceptance (BFD session visible in `show ip ospf interface` / IS-IS running-config on the loss cluster) remains an operator-side verify; the render contract is pinned by the regression test.

Closes #15015

Branch: `fix/14972-campaign`

## Summary
Fixes D31-04: single-path IPv6 static routes and the IPv6 `backup-router` in table 999 (`vrf-mgmt`) were never reaped on delete, preference change, rollback, or reset. They were stamped `RTPROT_STATIC` + the xpf realm (`RTA_FLOW`), but Linux stores no `RTA_FLOW` for IPv6, so they read back realm 0 and `mgmtStaticRouteOwned` never claimed them.

Every management static the reconcile installs — single-path statics and the backup-router — now carries the existing `config.ManagementVRFMultipathStaticProtocol` (0x58, the #12539 ECMP marker) as `rtm_protocol`, which survives the kernel round-trip in both families. Single-path routes keep the realm, so legacy IPv4 routes stay owned and migrate in place; operator `RTPROT_STATIC` routes are still never claimed; ECMP routes are byte-identical. No new protocol number, no wire/config change.

IPv4 single-path routes change `rtm_protocol` 4 -> 88 (realm unchanged; `show route` still renders `static`). networkd foreign-route exposure is the bound already accepted for ECMP in #12539. ## PR #15340 — ddns: reject cross-family sibling claims without wire DHCID proof (#14995) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/14995-campaign`

Why: crossTypeSiblingOwned matched only on canonical FQDN plus
opposite address family. A bare unauthenticated DHCP REQUEST that
merely named a victim's hostname from the other family therefore
entered the ownership store as a trusted sibling; upsertLocked
stamped SiblingFamilyOwned and the RFC 2136 backend downgraded
the claim to a per-type RRsetNotUsed guard, publishing a foreign
A/AAAA plus a second DHCID at the victim's name (RFC 4701 allows
one DHCID RR per owner name) and recording phantom ownership
whose later release aimed the DHCID prerequisite at the victim.

What: demote the store to a candidate source and make the wire
the proof. crossTypeSiblingOwned now returns the sibling record
narrowed to same scope modulo family and same backend endpoint;
upsertLocked threads its ClientID as SiblingClientID, and
reconcileOnceLocked stamps PairedClientID for a same-device
sibling desired in the same pass. pairedIdentityKey/sameDeviceClient
pair only provably same-device identities (verbatim-equal, or a
MAC-based DUID against the v4 MAC/Ethernet client-id).
dhcidDigestClientID canonicalizes the digest to the device, so
one device writes one identical DHCID RR across both families;
dhcidSharedWithOther/dhcidStillWanted compare device digests.
proveSiblingDHCID requires the sibling's exact DHCID on the wire
before any per-type downgrade in sendAddOwned/sendAdd; unproven
claims fall through to the unchanged name-level guards and are
refused with errDDNSConflictRefused. Deletes are untouched.
skip-existing publishes the device marker once per updater as
the sibling proof target. Strengthened the #14602/#14604/#2700
fixtures to a genuinely paired device (Ethernet client-id plus
DUID-LL embedding the same MAC); opaque fixtures fail closed.

Validation: new cross_family_hijack_14995_test.go cells fail on
origin/master 291ddb0066 (foreign A/AAAA published under
replace-owned and skip-existing) and pass after the fix (refused,
no foreign DHCID, no phantom ownership, victim untouched).
go test ./pkg/ddns -count=1 PASS; go test ./pkg/dhcpserver
-count=1 PASS; go vet clean.

Risk: records published before the device canonicalization carry
the legacy per-identity digest, so their guarded delete is a
counted skip (ownership dropped; stale RR remains for the
operator, documented in pkg/ddns/README.md). Opaque cross-family
pairings that cannot prove same-device fail closed (second
family refused) rather than hijackable.

Closes #14995

## PR #15341 — frr: fail closed on OSPF key with no authentication-type (#15014) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15014-campaign`

Closes #15014

## Mechanism (A12-02 surviving leg)

#14977 added a renderer guard omitting an OSPF interface whose `AuthType == ""` but `AuthKey != ""`. The guard was dead: the renderer reads the **unioned** interface (`config.OSPFInterfaceUnion12186.Merge`, #12186), and `Merge` only copied `AuthKey` under a matched `simple`/`md5` type. A key carried with no type — the foreign/tolerant construction the guard was written for (persisted pre-gate config, HA peer sync, rollback; strict commit refuses a bare OSPF `authentication-key`, #14402) — was dropped by the union, so the interface rendered `ip ospf area` with zero auth lines: an unauthenticated adjacency.

The other two A12-02 probes (OSPF `simple` with an unrenderable key; IS-IS area/interface passwords with an unrenderable key and IS-IS keyless type) were already withheld by #14977; they are pinned as regression controls in the new test file so they cannot regress.

## Fix

`OSPFInterfaceUnion12186.Merge` now preserves the first typeless key as auth-configured evidence (a differing second key is a field-name-only conflict; no type is invented, the key is never emitted or logged), so the existing #14977 guard withholds the interface. Typed fragments keep their own key handling. One predicate — "auth configured but no renderable auth line" — now reaches every A12-02 probe.

## Tests

- RED on `origin/master`: `TestOSPFKeyWithNoTypeDoesNotActivate15014`, `TestOSPFKeyWithNoTypeSplitFragments15014` (both rendered `ip ospf area 0.0.0.0` with no auth lines).
- GREEN after: all `15014` tests pass, with byte-identical keyed/plain controls (keyed simple/md5 OSPF, plain OSPF, keyed/plain IS-IS, healthy IS-IS sibling + global).
- `pkg/config` union tests pass; gofmt/go vet clean.

Main agent should run the full `pkg/frr` and `pkg/config` suites once.

## Risk

A tolerant-loaded OSPF config with a typeless key now loses that adjacency loudly (renderer slog) instead of forming it unauthenticated. Strict-valid configs cannot carry the shape and are unaffected byte-for-byte.

## PR #15343 — policy: fail closed on fragment-no-L4 sentinel against protocol-only deny/reject (#14956) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/14956-campaign`

Closes #14956

## Summary
Fail closed on the fragment-no-L4 sentinel (`SHIM_PROTO_FRAGMENT_NO_L4`, 255) against protocol-only DENY/REJECT rules (D24-02 leg 1, 3-way MATERIAL in research run `tpzkKgAuZL`).

A protocol-only application term (no port, no ICMP type/code constraint — e.g. `protocol udp`, compiled as an empty-range `range_terms` entry) matches on the known protocol alone, so for a known protocol the flowless path decides it via `CompiledApplications::matches`. For sentinel 255 the protocol is unknown: `matches()` missed (no `by_protocol[255]` entry) and `has_l4_constrained_term` also missed (empty ranges are not L4-constrained; its 255 arm only scans port/ICMP constraints), so a protocol-only DENY/REJECT was never recorded as a skipped fragment deny in `try_match_rule`. The fragment fell through to a later permit, a default-permit, or the junos-host deliver-on-no-match fall-through — fail open.

## Changes
- `userspace-dp/src/policy.rs`: add `CompiledApplications::has_any_protocol_term` (true iff some protocol carries an empty-range protocol-only term; `match_any` excluded since `application any` direct-matches the sentinel first) and OR it, gated on `protocol == SHIM_PROTO_FRAGMENT_NO_L4`, into the `FragmentDenyOverlap` classification in `try_match_rule`. The existing `note_skipped_frag_deny` / `apply_frag_deny_override_and_count` machinery then drops and attributes the fragment to the skipped deny/reject across transit (zone-pair/wildcard/global) and junos-host (exact/from-any/global) tiers, Deny and Reject alike.
- `userspace-dp/src/policy_tests.rs`: three regression cells covering transit, junos-host (including the lone-deny deliver fall-through), and the global-host tier — Deny+Reject, sentinel fail-closed attributed to policy_id 7, non-overlapping L3 → permit stands, known-UDP → direct deny, known-TCP → permit.
- `docs/log/14956.md`: investigation/fix log.

Leg 2 (multi-zone junos-host scope) was refuted by the Go commit gate and stays excluded per the issue's binding scope narrowing.

## Validation
- RED: with the production fix reverted (tests kept), all three new cells fail.
- GREEN: with the fix, all three pass.
- Adjacent suites with the fix: `policy::` 265 passed / 0 failed; `junos_host` 46 passed / 0 failed; `frag` 398 passed with 4 failures that fail identically without the fix (pre-existing on the unmodified base, unrelated).
- Live-traffic rig validation not run.

## Risk
Low. The new arm fires only for the 255 sentinel against Deny/Reject rules carrying an empty-range protocol-only term; known protocols, port-bearing terms, ICMP-typed terms (pre-existing `packet_icmp` arm), permit rules, `match_any`, and `l4_present` paths are untouched.

## PR #15344 — eventengine: re-arm trigger on 1 on window decay (#15020) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15020-campaign`

Why:
withinMatches decided the #3756 edge-latch re-arm with the in-window
count including the current event, which evaluateEvent appends to the
window before calling it. For `within N { trigger on 1; }` that count
is >= 1 by construction on every event, so `counts[i] < wc.TriggerOn`
never held: once the first crossing armed rt.onLatched, no later event
could clear it. The policy fired exactly once per daemon lifetime (the
runtime is carried across same-revision Apply, and releaseEdgeLatch
runs only on non-admission), so the shipped lab pair
failover-on-probe-fail / restore-on-probe-success in
test/incus/xpf-test.conf went dead after its first outage cycle.

What:
pkg/eventengine/evaluate.go: test the count excluding the current
event (counts[i]-1 < wc.TriggerOn), so the latch re-arms exactly when
the ANDed condition was false before this event arrived — for N=1,
when no prior occurrence remains inside the window. The old re-arm
`return false` is split into an explicit inclusive count gate
(counts[i] < wc.TriggerOn -> no fire) so the latch mutation stays
distinct from the firing decision. Comments in evaluate.go,
engine.go (onLatched), and README.md updated to the pre-event
formulation; regression in engine_trigger_on1_rearm_15020_test.go.
NOT changed: queue.go releaseEdgeLatch, cooldown arming, Apply
carry-over, pruneWindow, and trigger-until semantics — for N>1 the
observable behaviour is unchanged (a sustained burst's pre-event
count stays >= N until decay; below-threshold events never fire).

Validation:

instead of ALL — Junos requires every member to match ("The evaluation

community string with literal members anchored to whole tokens
(`(^| )m( |$)`) so `65000:100` cannot match inside `65000:1000` or
across a token boundary. Single-member/empty renders byte-identical,
duplicates collapse. `then community delete` targets a generated
per-member backing (`<frrName>-xpf-del-<digest>`) because the AND entry
strips nothing per-value under FRR `community_list_match_delete`;

## PR #15348 — configstore: stop rollback rebind blessing stale disk bytes (#15023) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15023-campaign`

Closes #15023

## Defect (A19-01)
`rebindRollbackMetadataLocked` (#14578) hashed whatever bytes were on disk for each rollback slot before writing `rollback-meta.json`:
- live entry: disk bytes replaced `entry.Config.Format()` before hashing, blessing a stale slot left by a prior slot-write failure (ENOSPC/EIO) or a crash during a commit-confirmed slot shift;
- tombstone entry: disk bytes replaced the marker, blessing a slot whose marker write never landed;
- success unconditionally cleared `rollbackPersistDegraded`.

After restart, `rollback N` returned a different generation's config with no warning and health green.

## Fix
`pkg/configstore/rollback_metadata.go` — `rebindRollbackMetadataLocked` only; callers unchanged:
- Live entry: hash the in-memory `Format()`; rewrite the slot durably whenever on-disk bytes diverge (missing/unreadable/oversized included); record only the identity after a verified match or successful rewrite.
- Tombstone: always record the marker; restore it durably when the file still parses as a real config. Bytes that already refuse at load (marker/empty/parse error — the trailing tombstones of a healthy #14578 boot-recovery ladder) keep their identity, so neighbouring behaviour is unchanged.
- A slot that cannot be made to match records an invalid (zero) identity → next load tombstones it (fail-closed); the rebind stays degraded instead of clearing the flag.

## Tests (`rollback_rebind_15023_test.go`)
- `TestRebindDoesNotBlessStaleLiveSlot_15023` — stale `hostStale` bytes at slot 3 rewritten to in-memory `hostC`; restart rb1=hostA rb2=hostB rb3=hostC. **Fails on master.**
- `TestRebindStaysDegradedWhenStaleSlotRewriteFails_15023` — injected ENOSPC: degraded stays true, restart tombstones slot 3 (REFUSED). **Fails on master.**
- `TestRebindDoesNotBlessTombstonedSlot_15023` — tombstone whose file still holds live bytes restored to the marker. **Fails on master.**
- `TestRebindHealthyLadderUnchanged_15023` — control: matching ladder rebound with slot identities unchanged (passes before and after).

Neighbouring suites green: #14578 rebind (runtime/boot/retry), #10723 mixed-generation, #7176 tombstone, broader `TestRollback|TestTombstone|TestSaveRollback|TestLoadRollback|TestPromote|TestBoot|TestAutoRollback|TestConfirmRecovery|TestSyncApply` set. Main agent should run the full `./pkg/configstore` suite before merge.

Docs: `pkg/configstore/README.md` rebind invariant; `docs/log/15023.md`.

## PR #15351 — frr: render Junos loops N as allowas-in N-1 (#15009) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15009-campaign`

## Summary
- `loops 1` now emits no `allowas-in` line (Junos default = 0 own-AS occurrences allowed = FRR no-line), `loops N>=2` emits `allowas-in N-1` (`loops 10` -> `allowas-in 9`). Previously the value was copied verbatim, accepting one extra local-AS occurrence on every peer with `loops` (#15009, A11-03).
- Only `renderBGPAllowASIn` changes; compiler/storage/validation keep the authored Junos `loops` value, and the #11795 range gate (unset = silent, out-of-range tolerant values omitted with warning) is preserved.

## Semantics (evidence)
Junos `loops (Autonomous System)`: hidden when detected >=N times (`loops 1` hidden at >=1, default). Junos worked example: `loops 2` = "own AS can appear up to one time, hidden at two or more". FRR: filtered when count > `allowas-in K`; no line = 0 allowed; bare = 3 (never emitted). Hence Junos N == FRR N-1. The family-`loops` prose ("allowed N") was considered as the refutation; it does not govern the group/neighbor leaf xpf accepts and contradicts the AS-loops definition + example + FRR local-as default (1 occurrence permitted absent allowas-in, mirroring `Loops: 1`).

## Tests
- RED on origin/master `6eeff22941`: new `TestGenerateProtocols_BGPAllowASInLoopsOffByOne15009` failed all non-zero loops cells (verbatim lines), loops-0 control passed.
- GREEN: targeted `TestGenerateProtocols_BGPAllowASIn*` + #11460 AF-scope test pass; `pkg/config` loops controls pass; `go vet ./pkg/frr/` clean.
- Full `pkg/frr` suite: only `TestFamilylessIPv6NeighborWithoutPolicyIsV6Only11564`, `TestFRRLoadBGPClasslessRIBSuppression11426`, `TestFRRLoadInet6OnlyNeighborIPv4Deactivation11374` fail — verified identical failures on pristine master (pre-existing, FRR-load environment).
- Live Junos/FRR run3.sh acceptance not run in this lane; render-level equivalence is pinned by the regression.

Docs: `docs/log/15009.md`, `pkg/frr/README.md`.

- New `opts.lenientPolicerNameCollision`: tolerant load / peer-sync downgrades to a warning (#1960 no-brick); both definitions survive and the pre-gate three-color precedence becomes visible instead of silent.
- NOT changed: Rust precedence, eBPF policer-ID leg, snapshot builders.

## Validation

## PR #15357 — config: warn that DPD threshold is IKEv1-only on IKEv2 gateways (#15025) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15025-campaign`

## Why
DPD `threshold` renders to `dpd_timeout = interval x threshold`, but strongSwan honours `dpd_timeout` for IKEv1 only (its own swanctl.conf documents it as "Timeout for DPD checks (IKEV1 only)"). On IKEv2 — negotiated by default when no `version` is pinned, and the only version on `v2-only` gateways — a dead peer is declared only after charon's global retransmission budget (~165s) is exhausted, so the knob was silently inert on the default path (A16-02: 169s measured vs 6s configured).

## What
Implements the issue's accepted advisory alternative. Programming charon's `retransmit_timeout/base/tries` is daemon-global, not per-connection, and xpf owns only the swanctl snippet; deriving the global budget from the tightest gateway would silently change retransmission for every IKE SA on the box.

- New `appendDPDThresholdIKEv2AdvisoryLocked` (`pkg/config/dpd_threshold_ikev2_advisory_15025.go`): warns at commit when a DPD-enabled gateway with an explicit threshold (`DPDThreshold > 0`, set only by the `threshold` leaf) is not `v1-only` (dual default or `v2-only`), naming the gateways and pointing at `version v1-only`. Warning, never an error.
- Wired into both compile entries; suppressed on tolerant load / peer-sync via `suppressDPDThresholdIKEv2Advisory` (#8357 doctrine — no re-warning on every boot/sync).
- Renderer and DPD parsing unchanged (`dpd_timeout` is still emitted; IKEv1 needs it).

## Validation
- `TestDPDThresholdIKEv2Advisory15025`: RED on pristine `2c0e039020` with only the test file (`dual-default gateway with DPD threshold 3 must warn ...; warnings=[]`), GREEN on this head. Controls stay silent: `v1-only` + threshold, interval-only (no explicit threshold), no DPD stanza, and the lenient path.
- Adjacent suites pass: `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'DPD|DeadPeer|ClusterWithoutNTP|8357'`, `go test ./pkg/ipsec/ -run 'DPD'` (DPDModes, DPDBareAndTuningForms, TolerantDPDClamps). `go vet ./pkg/config` clean.

## Risk
One new advisory per commit for dual/v2 gateways with an explicit threshold; never blocks a commit, suppressed on boot/peer-sync. Residual (issue-accepted): IKEv2 dead-peer timing still follows charon's global retransmission budget.

Closes #15025

## PR #15360 — eventengine: skip no-change remediation commits (#15022) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15022-campaign`

## Summary

A no-`within` event-options policy on `ping_test_completed` whose `change-configuration` restores values already active (the ordinary restore-on-success shape) re-committed an unchanged candidate on every probe cycle. The 30s per-policy cooldown only throttled this to a perpetual full commit+apply every 30s, and every commit pushed an identical entry onto the bounded 50-entry rollback history — evicting the operator rollback ladder in ~24 minutes (report A14-03, consensus MATERIAL).

## Fix

- `pkg/eventengine/engine.go` (`applyOnce`): after `CommitCheck`, if the post-batch candidate equals the active config, skip the commit entirely — exit configure, count the new `SkippedNoChange` stat, return nil so `runAction` still counts the action committed and arms the cooldown exactly as for a real commit. No history entry, no cross-policy global-budget slot spent, no daemon `CommitFn` invoked. A 30-minute run of an unchanged batch now adds 0 history entries.
- `pkg/configstore/store_format.go`: new `Store.CandidateEqualsActive`, comparing candidate vs active under the existing canonical `guardedConfigHash` (#8564 post-persist-round-trip basis), so values the JSON encoding normalizes cannot cause a false skip or false commit.
- `pkg/api`: new `xpf_event_actions_skipped_no_change_total` metric (descriptor, collector, collect site), so a steadily climbing skip count makes the re-asserting policy visible.
- `pkg/eventengine/README.md`: transactional-batch step 4 + metrics list.

Scope: only the autonomous event-engine remediation path skips. Operator/CLI/gRPC/REST commits of an unchanged candidate still record history as before; a batch that genuinely changes the candidate commits exactly as before.

## Tests

New `pkg/eventengine/engine_noop_commit_15022_test.go` drives the exact A14-03 mechanism (no-within `ping_test_completed` policy re-setting the already-active host-name via `HandleEvent` → worker → `applyOnce`):

- `TestNoopCommit_UnchangedBatchSkipsCommit_15022` — history length unchanged, active untouched, `Committed=1`, `Rejected/DroppedStale=0`, global budget count 0.
- `TestNoopCommit_CooldownStillArms_15022` — in-window repeat suppressed; history stays at the seed commit.
- `TestNoopCommit_DaemonPathSkipsCommitFn_15022` — commitFn never invoked on the daemon path.
- `TestNoopCommit_ChangedBatchStillCommits_15022` (control) — a real change still commits and pushes one history entry.

RED evidence: with the gate stripped (Stats field retained so it compiles), the three skip tests fail — 30s timeout waiting for `SkippedNoChange` while the log shows `configuration committed` for the unchanged batch. GREEN with the fix.

Full `pkg/eventengine`, `pkg/configstore`, and `pkg/api` suites carry only base-attributed failures (6673, 9088/9880, REST-6960 families), each reproduced on pristine `origin/master` (0a898fae00). `go vet` clean; `gofmt` clean on touched files (`pkg/api/metrics.go` is gofmt-dirty on base and was left as-is).

Closes #15022

Branch: `fix/15041-campaign`

Why: On an authenticated Noise-keyed link the #6629 config key came from an ephemeral X25519 exchange in ordinary droppable frames; `verifyFrame` admits sequence gaps, so an on-path relay could suppress both exchange frames, let `awaitConfigKey` time out into cleartext `syncMsgConfig`, and read the control-link PSK plus every config secret — after which heartbeat/sync/fabric HMACs are forgeable (A24-03).

The `syncMsgConfigEncrypted` receive arm (sync_conn_read.go) derives the same key first, falling back to the ephemeral key only on unauthenticated connections. NOT changed: unauthenticated mixed-version cleartext fallback, #11773 alarm/counters, frame seal.

Validation: `TestConfigKeySuppressionNeverYieldsCleartextOnAuthedConn15041` fails pre-fix (`got type 8, want syncMsgConfigEncrypted (31)`) and passes post-fix with byte-identical receiver recovery and no cleartext stats; `TestConfigCryptoUnauthenticatedPeerStillFallsBack15041` control plus the #6629/#11773 suites stay green; `go vet` clean. Full `pkg/cluster` suite: one failure (`TestInstallTableProducerToResendEndToEnd9752`), base-attributed on pristine origin/master.

## PR #15372 — ha: index scoped generation entries by tuple for bare deletes (#15039) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15039-campaign`

Closes #15039

## Why
Every bare session delete scanned the full scoped generation map
(`scopedKeysForTuple`): sender `takeDeleteGenV4/V6` under
`bulkSnapshotGenMu`+`genSentMu`, receiver `deleteGenGuardV4/V6` up to
twice under `recvGenMu` inside `applyMu`. Bare deletes are the
production close path and the receiver map is pinned near its cap by
tombstones, so each delete cost O(held scoped entries) — measured
6.9ms per sender delete at 50k held entries — serializing sender
stamping and capping the standby's delete apply rate.

## What
- `scopedTupleIndex` side maps (bare tuple -> set of scoped keys) for
  all four scoped generation maps; no generations held — the scoped
  map stays authoritative for every ordering decision.
- Maintained via `putScopedGenBounded` /
  `putScopedGenEvictingTombstones` / `deleteScopedGen` at every scoped
  stamp, record, tombstone, cap eviction (new
  `genTombstoneOrder.frontKey`), gen-0 delete and cross-space
  coupling; rebuilt/cleared in `resetRecvSessionGen`.
- Bare paths iterate `index.keys(tuple)`; `scopedKeysForTuple` deleted.
- NOT changed: wire format, capabilities, generation semantics,
  install guards.

## Validation
- RED on pristine `origin/master` `192c7455ba` (timing test
  transplanted alone): `sender bare delete = 6.90ms at 50000 held
  scoped entries, want < 2ms`; benchmark 61.8us/874us/7.55ms at
  1k/10k/50k held.
- GREEN: `TestBareDeleteCostFlatWithHeldScopedEntries15039` +
  `TestScopedTupleIndexTracksLifecycle15039` pass; benchmark now
  181ns/197ns/209ns at 1k/10k/50k. #14358/#10512 control suites pass;
  scoped `-race` subset passes; `go vet ./pkg/cluster/` clean.
- Full `./pkg/cluster/` (149s): sole failure
  `TestInstallTableProducerToResendEndToEnd9752`, documented in
  `docs/log/14358.md` as base-attributed on clean `origin/master`
  (install-table golden drift, disjoint from this diff).

## Risk
Index/map disagreement can only miss a reclaim/tombstone the scan
would have made (guards still read generations from the scoped map);
the lifecycle test asserts index/map agreement across cap eviction,
reclaim, namespace reset, gen-0 delete, bare close and scoped take
for v4+v6. Details: `docs/log/15039.md`.

Checks main agent should run: full `./pkg/cluster/` suite at final
head (expect sole base-attributed 9752 failure), loss-cluster smoke
per campaign.

Branch: `fix/15018-campaign`

## Why

`compileSystem` unconditionally reallocated `RootAuthentication`, `Archival`, and `InternetOptions` on every sighting, and the dispatcher calls it once per `system` root — so a second `system` root or a repeated child block silently discarded the earlier block's credentials. After a commit reported success, `applyRootAuth` revoked the earlier root SSH keys and could lock an xpf-provisioned root password (A13-01 management lockout); archival lost its earlier archive-sites.

- `docs/log/15018.md`.

## PR #15376 — ipsec: render hexadecimal PSKs as raw bytes (#15027) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15027-campaign`

## Summary

`pre-shared-key hexadecimal <hex>` committed and rendered the hex digits as a quoted ASCII secret (`secret = "6162..."`), so strongSwan could never authenticate against a peer holding the same Junos hex key. Any qualifier word was accepted identically, and the block spelling dropped the key entirely (A16-04).

## Fix

- `IKEPolicy`/`IPsecVPN` gain `PSKHex` + `PSKQualifierInvalidSpec`; the compiler switches on the qualifier across packed/flat/block shapes (`classifyPSKQualifier`/`pskQualifierValue` in `pkg/config/compiler_ipsec.go`).
- New strict gate `validateIPsecPSKQualifierStrict`: unknown qualifier or malformed (odd/non-hex) hexadecimal refused at commit, warned on tolerant load/peer-sync. The malformed-hex error does not echo key material.
- Renderer (`pkg/ipsec/policy.go`): hex secrets render unquoted as `secret = 0x<hex>`; ASCII keeps the quoted #2126 render; a hex-flagged value that is not valid hex is skipped by name at render.
- Bare VPN-level `pre-shared-key <key>` unchanged (ASCII). `$9$` handling, AST redaction, schema arity unchanged.

## Regression (RED → GREEN)

- Base probe: `hexadecimal`/`bogus`/`ascii-text` all committed with `PSK="6162636431323334"` as ASCII; hex values `616`/`zz`/`0x6162` committed verbatim; block hexadecimal dropped (then #14139-refused as empty).
- `TestIPsecPSKHexadecimal15027` (pkg/config): probe `6162636431323334` compiles hex-flagged; ascii control; bogus refused at commit + warned lenient; malformed hex refused without echoing; block hex carried; block bogus refused; VPN-level hex + bare controls.
- `TestPSKHexadecimalRender15027` / `TestPSKHexadecimalPolicyFallback15027` / `TestPSKHexadecimalEndToEnd15027` (pkg/ipsec): structural (#6824) assertion `secret` == `0x6162636431323334` at `secrets/ike-v1`; bad/odd hex skipped with no orphan secret.

## Validation

- `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestIPsecPSKHexadecimal15027|TestIPsecPSKPresence14139' -count=1`: GREEN.
- `go test ./pkg/ipsec/ -count=1`: fully GREEN.
- `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestIPsec' -count=1`: 7 failures, each reproduced identically with the fix stashed (base-attributed). Full pkg/config suite exceeds the local 600s timeout in the pre-existing `TestParseErrorCap_16MiBInvalidBounded_5827` cell (also on base).

## Risk

Unknown-qualifier configs (never Junos-legal) are now refused at commit / warned on load. Hex tunnels change rendered bytes deliberately (now match hex peers).

Closes #15027

## PR #15378 — vrrp: drop stripped-VLAN sibling adverts on untagged parent (#15049) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15049-campaign`

Why: An untagged-unit VRRP instance on a vlan-tagging parent binds its AF_PACKET ETH_P_ALL tap to the parent netdev. A peer advert for a tagged sibling arrives 802.1Q-tagged on the wire, but the NIC strips the tag into skb metadata before the ptype_all tap, so the frame reads untagged in data. The cBPF prefilter and Go parser both check only the in-data ethertype and no PACKET_AUXDATA was requested, so a same-VRID higher-priority sibling advert was enqueued on the parent instance — demoting the native MASTER / perpetually resetting its master-down timer and leaving the native VIP ownerless. This is the AF_PACKET sibling of #2886, which fixed only the raw fallback.

What: openAfPacketReceiver requests PACKET_AUXDATA (best-effort, debug-log on refusal, mirroring PACKET_IGNORE_OUTGOING). receiverAfPacket now reads via the afPacketRecvmsg (unix.Recvmsg) seam and, for instances bound to a non-VLAN netdev, drops frames whose auxdata reports TP_STATUS_VLAN_VALID (afPacketAuxdataVLANTag, fail-open when the cmsg is absent/truncated, mirroring #2886). VLAN children are exempt and keep their own tagged adverts; untagged native adverts on the parent are kept. The cBPF is deliberately unchanged: the same array is attached to parent and child sockets so it cannot express "drop tagged only on the parent", and golang.org/x/net/bpf's VM cannot execute the SKF_AD_VLAN_TAG_PRESENT ancillary load, so a cBPF-only fix would be untestable in the #5088 bpf.VM harness; the PACKET_AUXDATA/TP_STATUS_VLAN_VALID option is the per-instance equivalent. The #6560 loop test migrated from the retired afPacketRecvfrom seam to afPacketRecvmsg.

Validation: RED pre-fix (new tests fail to build on master: afPacketRecvmsg/afPacketAuxdataVLANTag undefined — the mechanism does not exist); behavioural RED with the drop neutered — parent received [10.0.61.3 10.0.61.2], i.e. the stripped VLAN-100 advert was enqueued. GREEN with fix: the 3 new #15049 tests (parent drops vlan_tci=100, untagged control kept, child ge-0-0-0.100 keeps its own VLAN), #6560 self-frame, #5088 cBPF, #2886 arrival-ifindex suites pass; full go test ./pkg/vrrp/ -count=1 passes; race on receiver tests passes; go vet clean.

Risk: On a kernel refusing PACKET_AUXDATA the drop is inactive (fail-open, debug-logged) — exactly the pre-fix behaviour, never worse. NOT changed: raw fallback path, cBPF filter set, any behaviour outside the cited AF_PACKET mechanism.

Closes #15049

## PR #15381 — config: default generic vrrp-group preempt to true, add no-preempt (#15047) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15047-campaign`

Closes #15047

## Defect (A05-05)
A generic `vrrp-group` without `preempt` compiled `Preempt=false` (Go zero value in the `parseVRRPGroups` constructor). Junos and RFC 5798 default Preempt_Mode to TRUE, so a backup never took over from a track-demoted master: `pkg/vrrp/track.go` only lowers the advertised priority, and `instance_rx.go` resets the master-down timer on every advert when `!getPreempt()`.

## Fix
- `pkg/config/compiler_interfaces.go`: constructor defaults `Preempt: true`; new `no-preempt` arms in both the flat Keys loop and the child-node loop clear it; `no-preempt` added to `vrrpGroupPropertyKeywords` so it delimits packed virtual-address runs.
- `pkg/config/schema_interfaces.go`: new `no-preempt` schema leaf (needed for flat-set structuring + the packed hierarchical one-liner splitter).
- `pkg/config/types_interfaces.go`: document the default on `VRRPGroup.Preempt`.
- RETH collection unchanged: `CollectRethInstances` still takes preempt only from explicit chassis `redundancy-group <id> preempt`.

## Regression (RED → GREEN)
`pkg/config/vrrp_preempt_default_15047_test.go`:
- RED on master: no-keyword flat-set and hierarchical configs compiled `Preempt=false`.
- GREEN: no-keyword (incl. a `track-interface` group) → true; `no-preempt` → false in flat-set, hierarchical, and packed one-liner shapes (packed control also proves the following `priority 150` still parses); explicit `preempt` → true.

Neighbours verified green locally: `TestVRRPPreemptHoldTime|TestVRRPTrackInterface|TestVRRPV6|TestGroupMerge10055`, golden `TestCompileGolden4406|TestGolden` (golden `Preempt:false` rows are chassis redundancy-groups, intentionally unchanged). `spelling_gate_members_7484.txt` gained the two `no-preempt` flag rows; the full spelling-gate suite timed out under shared load in the worktree — please run the full `pkg/config` + `pkg/vrrp` suites in CI.

Docs: `docs/config-schema.md` (#15047 note beside #2850), `docs/log/15047.md`.

## PR #15385 — cluster: carry PD expiry in RA desired set, decay at send time (#15057) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15057-campaign`

Why: buildRAConfigs baked the decayed remaining DHCPv6-PD lifetimes into RAPrefix.ValidLifetime/PreferredLife, so the 2s cluster reconcile hash (raDesiredHash) and ra.configEqual changed every second and ra.Apply hard-restarted the RA sender (3-RA startup burst, new NDP socket, two Info lines) on every pass, indefinitely, on any cluster advertising a PD prefix.

What: DelegatedPrefixesForRA returns the granted lifetimes with the original Obtained (expired prune/skip unchanged); DelegatedPrefix gains PreferredExpiresAt beside ExpiresAt; buildRAConfigs stamps absolute RAPrefix.ValidExpiresAt/PreferredExpiresAt (Unix-nano, Obtained+granted) plus the granted lifetimes; pkg/ra buildRA computes the remaining lifetime at send time (whole seconds, never more than remains, preferred 0 past its expiry, PIO omitted past valid expiry); configEqual and sortRAPrefixes compare the expiries, so decay is a no-op and a renewal moving the expiry restarts. Prefixes without an expiry keep the granted/default path verbatim. Golden compile fixture regenerated. NOT changed: RemainingLifetimes semantics outside the RA desired set; operator-prefix defaults; the sender restart machinery.

Validation: new pkg/daemon/ra_pd_expiry_15057_test.go (granted+expiry shape; five 2s-apart fake-clock passes produce ONE raDesiredHash — the RED mechanism; renewal moves the hash; decayed-to-zero shape; zero-obtained sentinel), new pkg/ra/sender_expiry_15057_test.go (7200->7140 at +60s, 3200/0 past preferred expiry, PIO omitted at/past valid expiry, no-expiry controls byte-identical, configEqual expiry identity). Updated the 14598/14606 producer cells that asserted the old decayed shape; decay is now asserted at the wire. pkg/ra and pkg/dhcp full suites pass; pkg/config golden passes; go vet clean on touched packages.

Risk: a sender whose prefix validly expires between the last prune and the next send now omits the PIO at send time instead of advertising the last decayed value; the next reconcile removes it from the desired set as before.

Closes #15057

dhcp: retry terminal acquisition exits instead of dying (#15070)

Why: runDHCPv6 returned when its 30s link-local wait timed out and

after seam, new constant beside reacquireBackstop in commit.go);
v4 paces the same backoff on hitting the attempt cap (still
bounded by a pending lease expiry), resets attempt/backoff, and
re-enters INIT, preserving the per-cycle DISCOVER-burst bound.
Cancellation still terminates promptly. New
retry_after_terminal_15070_test.go drives both real run loops
through the existing seams; README and docs/log/15070.md record
the lifecycle change. NOT changed: manager registry, Start,
Reconcile, renewal paths, wire exchanges, config schema.

exchanges then return). GREEN: v6 re-waits and Solicits, v4
re-DISCOVERs and leases, with after-paced anti-storm waits and a
cancel-during-pause control. Full pkg/dhcp suite, go vet, gofmt
clean (parent runs full-repo gate).

a retry warning every ~30s instead of once; ctx-bound, so

## PR #15393 — dhcp: re-request missing IA_PD on DHCPv6 renew and rebind (#15069) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15069-campaign`

Why:
buildV6RenewMessage only echoed an IA_PD when prefixes were held, so
after a boot-time NoPrefixAvail, a refusal, a withdrawal, or a #14598
expiry prune the committed set was empty and every RENEW/REBIND carried
no IA_PD. The IA_NA renewed forever, the client never fell back to a

request dhcp renew or restart.

buildV6RenewMessage now takes the configured IA types and the bounded
acquisition hint; when no PD is held but ia-pd is configured it emits
an empty IA_PD (IAID {0,0,0,1}) with the hint, matching acquisition.
doDHCPv6 passes v6opts.IATypes and the pdHintPrefixLength-bounded hint.
Held-PD echo and the not-configured shape are unchanged; no matcher,
parser, reconcile, commit, or run-loop change was needed. New
regression file dhcpv6_missing_pd_15069_test.go, README bullet, and
docs/log/15069.md land together. NOT changed: stateless mode, DHCPv4,
acquisition, or the #14997 teardown gate.

arguments in call to buildV6RenewMessage, want the 5-arg pre-fix
signature). GREEN: go test ./pkg/dhcp/ -run 15069 -count=1 passes all
builder cells, controls, and the run-loop commit test; full
go test ./pkg/dhcp/ -count=1 passes; go vet clean; gofmt clean.

Risk:
A server that keeps refusing now receives one IA_PD per normal T1/T2
cycle (no extra traffic) and the existing refusal arm repeats the
cycle, which is the desired retry. Clients without ia-pd configured
send no IA_PD on renew (pinned by control test).

## PR #15396 — daemon: re-test bootstrap gate under applySem (#15055) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15055-campaign`

Closes #15055

## What

The plain-commit bootstrap gate in `commitAndApply` was tested before `applySem.Acquire` and never re-tested (A32-02). A plain commit that passed the gate while a first commit-confirmed rollback held `applySem` parked, then bound the rollback's reset candidate generation in `commitWithGenBinding` and promoted the empty candidate — reporting success and persisting `committed=1`-empty, so the next boot classified NORMAL (the state #1922 Item 1b / #7291 exist to prevent).

## Fix

- `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_commit.go`: re-test `inBootstrap()` after `applySem.Acquire`, before any store promotion (mirrors the #9884 post-Acquire recheck in `beginBackgroundApply`).
- `pkg/configstore/store_commit.go`: bump `holderEpoch` in the first-commit branch of `PromoteRollback` only, so a holder-bound authority minted before the timeout fails verification at promotion; ordinary rollbacks are unaffected.

## Tests

`pkg/daemon/bootstrap_commit_race_15055_test.go` (5 cells):
- Race cell: parked plain commit is refused with the bootstrap error, no apply, in-memory + reloaded `everCommitted=false`.
- Holder-epoch cell: first-commit `PromoteRollback` bumps the epoch and the pre-rollback authority gets the holder-turnover refusal; non-first control does not bump.
- Controls: plain commit in bootstrap refused + commit-confirmed escape hatch; plain commit outside bootstrap succeeds.

RED before fix (gate cell: commit promoted first and confirmed the window; epoch cell: before=1 after=1), GREEN after. Docs: `docs/log/15055.md`, `pkg/daemon/README.md`.

Note: full-suite and -race verification should be re-run on a quieter host — this worktree's runs were under extreme sibling load (load avg ~90-112) and bounded shell timeouts expired before producing results; the targeted `15055` cells pass.

`classifyIpsecTopologyLinks` marked every xfrmi with a resolved `vrf`/`bridge` master `ipsecReadyUnsafe`. A `vrf` master now leaves readiness unchanged (SAFE when subscribed); `bridge` and every other resolved master stay UNSAFE, unresolvable stays UNKNOWN. ## PR #15402 — feeds: persist feed content epoch under its own digest (#15075) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15075-campaign`

feeds: persist feed content epoch under its own digest (#15075)

Closes #15075

## Why
The persisted feed content epoch (#14395) did not protect across a restart (A50-01): `ShrinkHighWaterSnapshot` stored the epoch prefix set with only `Hash` — the count high-water hash — as its key. Any ordinary non-rebasing install advances `highWaterHash` to the rotated set while the epoch moves only on bootstrap or ack, so the two diverge after one rotation and the restore had no epoch digest of its own to validate the set against; the first post-restart fetch could rebase the epoch unchecked, replacing an enforced deny/allow list wholesale with no refusal or acknowledgement.

## What
- `ShrinkHighWater` gains `EpochHash` (`epoch_hash,omitempty`): the `hashPrefixes` digest of the epoch prefix set, persisted separately from the count high-water `Hash`.
- `ShrinkHighWaterSnapshot` emits it; `RestoreShrinkHighWater` validates the restored canonical set against it. Pre-#15075 records without `epoch_hash` restore the epoch only in the epoch == high-water shape; a set matching neither key is dropped fail-closed while the count epoch still restores.
- On a bootstrap with a restored epoch, the existing #14994 guard evaluates `contentChurnTripped(restoredEpoch, candidate)` and refuses a churned candidate pending the exact-candidate ack instead of rebasing — now reachable across an ordinary rotation + restart.
- `pkg/feeds/README.md` updated; `docs/log/15075.md` records the analysis.

## Validation
- New `feed_shrink_15075_test.go`: non-rebasing 51% rotation keeps all 100 epoch prefixes + diverged `EpochHash`; post-restart 2%-of-epoch candidate refused; restart bootstrapping a disjoint set against the restored epoch refused, installs on exact ack; corrupt `EpochHash` drops the epoch while the count restores.
- Mutants (drop the `EpochHash` emit / ignore it on restore / re-key restore on the high-water hash — the A50-01 shape) each turn the tests red.
- Full `pkg/feeds` suite, daemon `FeedShrink|FeedHistory`, and grpcapi `12170` legs pass; gofmt/vet clean.

## Risk
Scoped to durable shrink-history restore. Additive JSON field; thresholds, ack tuple, hold policy, and true bootstrap unchanged. A mismatched epoch set restores the count baseline only and re-bootstraps under the #14994 guard.

## PR #15408 — flowexport: re-dial collectors after source renumbering (#15073) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15073-campaign`

## Summary
Collector sockets were dialed once at exporter build and never re-dialed. After the implicit source was renumbered (DHCP/SLAAC), IPv4 writes failed permanently on the stale socket and IPv6 kept sending from the removed address while health read healthy, until restart or an unrelated flow-export commit.

## Fix (`pkg/flowexport/transport.go`, shared by NetFlow v9 + IPFIX)
- Extract `dialCollector` as the single dial path shared by `dialCollectors` and recovery; a re-dial re-resolves the destination and re-picks the live implicit source exactly as a fresh build would.
- Write-failure leg: a failure on a proven-healthy socket whose `LocalAddr()` is no longer assigned re-dials once and retries that packet on the fresh socket (old socket closed only after the new write succeeds).
- Stale-source canary: healthy sockets whose source is no longer assigned are re-dialed before the write fan-out; `health()` reports them unhealthy with a not-assigned reason even while writes succeed (IPv6 leg). Enumeration failure conservatively counts as assigned (no churn).
- Still-assigned failures keep existing unhealthy+backoff behaviour with no re-dial churn; failed re-dials park unhealthy behind the existing probe backoff. `conn` moved under RWMutex so health/close never race a swap.

NOT changed: daemon hash-gating, backoff/write-timeout semantics (#4423), health surface shape, pinned source binds (re-dial re-resolves the same pinned source).

## Regression (`collector_redial_15073_test.go`)
- `TestCollectorRedial_WriteFailureRedials15073` — S1 renumbered to S2; failed write re-dials (1→2), closes old socket, delivers this packet from S2, churn-free after.
- `TestCollectorRedial_StaleSourceHealth15073` — IPv6 stale source reports unhealthy + next writeAll re-dials and sends from S2.
- `TestCollectorRedial_StillAssignedNoChurn15073` — control: no churn, no re-dial on ordinary refused write.
- `TestCollectorRedial_RedialFailureParksUnhealthy15073`, `TestCollectorRedial_SourceBoundCollector15073`.
RED on base (fix seams undefined / mechanism absent), GREEN after.

## Validation
- `go test ./pkg/flowexport/ -run 15073 -count=1 -v`: 5/5 GREEN
- `go test ./pkg/flowexport/ -count=1`: GREEN (also after rebase onto current master)
- `go test ./pkg/flowexport/ -race -count=1`: ok (2.5s)
- `go vet ./pkg/flowexport/`: clean

## Risk
Live netns renumbering probe not run in this lane; unit fakes model the LocalAddr-vs-assigned-set kernel contract. Changelog: `docs/log/15073.md`.

Closes #15073

## PR #15411 — grpcapi: size forwarded failover proxy from cluster budget (#15081) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15081-campaign`

Why: proxyPeerSystemAction (and its pkg/cli twin) applied a flat 5s deadline to forwarded cluster-failover ... node <peer> and data failover. The peer's RequestPeerFailover sequence (20s failover-ACK, 3s commit-ready settle, 20s commit ACK; barrier ACK alone can be delayed 30+s by bulk session sync) routinely exceeded 5s, so the operator received a bare DeadlineExceeded while the peer completed the ownership move, inviting a needless retry during maintenance.

What: pkg/clusterfailover gains ProxyFailoverTimeout (2x20s ACK + 2x3s settle = 46s, mirroring the daemon's 2*settle+20s lease sizing) and IsFailoverActionString. grpcapi proxyPeerTimeout and cli peerSystemActionTimeout apply the long budget only to validated node-targeted failovers; all other forwards keep 5s. On a deadline outcome the proxy result is reconciled against heartbeat RG ownership (new cluster.PeerPrimaryRGs): committed transfers report success, anything else reports outcome unknown with verify-before-retry guidance, never a bare DeadlineExceeded. NOT changed: peer-side failover execution, fabric allowlist, cluster timeouts.

Validation: RED on pristine origin/master (forwarded deadline = 4.999s; CLI returned bare DeadlineExceeded after peer commit). GREEN: go test ./pkg/clusterfailover/ ./pkg/cluster/ ./pkg/grpcapi/ ./pkg/cli/ -run 15081 all pass; neighbouring Failover/SystemAction suites pass except two grpcapi cells reproduced identically on pristine master (base-attributed). go vet clean on all four packages.

Risk: a genuinely hung peer now holds the operator command up to 46s before the outcome-unknown report — deliberate, per the issue's cluster-budget sizing; the 5s answer was a false failure report.

Closes #15081

rendersafe refused whitespace, control bytes, glob metacharacters and a trailing backslash, but not a leading `!`, which systemd reads as inverting a `[Match] Name=`/`OriginalName=` list. ## PR #15417 — image: refresh A/B ESP slot loaders on bootloader updates (#15089) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15089-campaign`

## Summary

Fixes A57-01 (#15089): the A/B ESP slots (`EFI/xpf-A`, `EFI/xpf-B`) held a bake-time copy of shim/grub/mm that nothing ever refreshed. Ubuntu `shim-signed` / `grub-efi-amd64-signed` updates install only to `EFI/ubuntu`, while BootOrder keeps booting the stale xpf slots — the Secure-Boot chain stayed on the bake-time bootloader for the life of the appliance (a SBAT/dbx revocation would never reach the booted loader) while dpkg reported the fixed version as installed. `validate.py` asserted only file presence, so the stale state shipped green.

## What

- **`scripts/image/xpf-uefi-slots`**: new `sync_ab_slots()` — cmp-gated, per-file atomic (temp file in the same slot dir + rename, post-rename cmp verify) re-copy of `shimx64.efi`/`grubx64.efi`/`mmx64.efi` from `EFI/ubuntu` into both slots. Runs on every boot before NVRAM registration, and standalone via `--sync-only` (independent of the efivars gate). `xpf.selector` is never touched; failures are logged, non-fatal, and retried at next boot.
- **`debian/xpf.triggers`** (new): `interest-noawait` dpkg file triggers on the three `EFI/ubuntu` loader files, so any package unpacking a changed loader invokes `xpf.postinst triggered`. Installed into `DEBIAN/triggers` automatically by `dh_installdeb`.
- **`debian/xpf.postinst`**: new `triggered` arm runs `xpf-uefi-slots --sync-only` when the helper is installed; exits 0 without it (foreign hosts). A bootloader update now lands in both slots without a reboot, and never blocks the triggering package's configure.
- **`scripts/image/validate.py`**: new `_AB_SLOT_HASH_PROBE` + `_ab_slot_loader_hash_verdict`, applied in `assert_ab_kernel_channel` after the presence verdict — a stale/divergent slot loader fails the Tier-1 gate by name. mm absent from both source and slot (the bake fallback shape) still passes; a loader absent from `EFI/ubuntu` entirely stays the presence verdict's diagnosis.
- Gate-reaction mock updated to serve the new hash probe; docs in `docs/install-images.md` and `docs/log/15089.md`.

NOT changed: the bake's one-time staging (still the initial seed), NVRAM registration / BootOrder logic, `xpf.selector` seeding/promotion, the kernel hold.

Alternatives rejected: holding shim/grub like the kernel (strands bootloader security updates with no verified delivery channel); an apt `Post-Invoke` hook (per-invocation, misses direct `dpkg -i`, can fire pre-configure).

## Validation

- **RED** on `origin/master` (6fd1efe432): new `scripts/image/test_slot_refresh_15089.py` (19 tests) — 6 failures + 10 errors (no hash verdict, no `--sync-only`, no triggers file, postinst rejected `triggered`).
- **GREEN**: 19 new tests pass (hash-verdict stale/missing/mm cells, real-`sh` `--sync-only` refresh incl. selector preservation + in-sync no-op, trigger/postinst wiring, validate wiring). Adjacent suites green (104 tests total): `test_validate_gate_reactions_10770`, `test_validate_ab_substrate_6498`, `test_validate_ab_slots_6494`, `test_uefi_slots_6499`, `test_validate_scenarios`. `sh -n` + `shellcheck -S warning` clean.
- A scratch real-dpkg run (chroot since removed) confirmed the file trigger fires `postinst triggered` on a provider package install ("Processing triggers for xpf").
- Outstanding lab verify (recorded in `docs/log/15089.md`): on a real baked image, `apt install --reinstall shim-signed grub-efi-amd64-signed` + `cmp` across `EFI/{ubuntu,xpf-A,xpf-B}`, and a deliberately corrupted slot failing `validate.py`. The full bake/validate cycle was not run in this lane; the hermetic tests exercise the same sync and verdict code paths.

Closes #15089
