## PR #15419 — grpcapi: bound streamDiagCmd scan wait behind parked scanner (#15080) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15080-campaign`

## Summary
Bounds `streamDiagCmd`'s wait behind a parked scanner goroutine so a diagnostic slot cannot be pinned by the unbounded `c.Wait(); <-scanDone` join (A43-01, #15080).

**Mechanism:** `c.Wait()` joins exec's copy goroutine, which stays blocked in `pw.Write` while the scanner goroutine is parked inside `sendFn` (it holds the `io.Pipe` read end and is not reading). The wait therefore never returned and the handler never reached its `defer release()`, holding a process-wide `diagcmd.DefaultLimiter` slot (cap 4, shared with REST). #14980 bounded the handlers' per-line `Send` via `sendDiagFrame`, but `streamDiagCmd` itself kept the unbounded wait — a `sendFn` that only parks until its ctx is done, or any direct caller with a raw unbounded `Send`, wedged it until the full exec timeout.

**Fix:** run `c.Wait()` in a worker and select over `waitDone`/`scanDone`/`ctx.Done()`:
- `waitDone`-first: unchanged normal path (`pw.Close()`, drain `scanDone`, scan error wins, child exit error as final line).
- `scanDone`-first (send/scanner failure): join Wait (already reaped by the scanner's deferred `cancel()`+`pr.Close()`) and report `scanErr`, not the internal cancel's ctx error — this leg also avoids misreporting every early scan error as a cancellation.
- `ctx.Done()`-first: close both pipe ends (`pr.Close()` unblocks the copy goroutine), join only Wait under `requestExecWaitDelay` (5s), and return `ctx.Err()` without joining `scanDone` — a scanner parked in a ctx-independent `sendFn` is abandoned to the caller's per-write Send bound (#14980) rather than re-wedging the return.

NOT changed: handlers, `sendDiagFrame`, REST surface, monitor handlers, `buildPrimaryServer` keepalive.

Closes #15080

## Validation
- New `pkg/grpcapi/diag_scan_wait_15080_test.go` (3 tests):
  - RED on `origin/master` (`ac543c5b9e`, re-confirmed on pristine `f524416374`): `TestStreamDiagCmd15080CtxCancelUnblocksParkedSend` fails with "streamDiagCmd did not return within 5s of ctx cancel while sendFn parked: c.Wait() wedged on the scanner goroutine, diag slot pinned (#15080)"; draining control passes both sides.
  - GREEN post-fix: ctx-cancel returns `context.Canceled` promptly; real-path sever (real `streamDiagCmd` + `sendDiagFrame`-wired parked Send) returns the sever with the slot transferred (`InFlight=1` while parked) then freed on unblock; draining control (lines in order + exit error as final line) unchanged.
- Adjacent suites green: `TestDiagSendBound14980*` (6), `TestStreamDiagCmd*` (incl. #5060 `ErrTooLong` and #1819 send-error controls), `TestDiagConcurrencyLimitGRPC*`; `go vet`/`gofmt` clean.
- Docs: `docs/log/15080.md`, `pkg/grpcapi/README.md` updated.

## Risk
Fail-closed only on an already-cancelled RPC; healthy streams untouched. On the ctx path the scanner goroutine is abandoned to the caller's Send bound rather than joined — it exits when that Send unblocks on handler-return stream cancel, the #14980/#9891 worker lifetime.

## PR #15421 — authz: exempt session-plumbing probes from the command regex gate (#15077) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15077-campaign`

Why:
GetStatus and GetConfigModeStatus were charged to the canonical command "show version" in `methodCanonicalCommand`, and their REST twins (`GET /api/v1/status`, `GET /api/v1/config/status`) were charged likewise. `cmd/cli` calls `GetStatus` before every dispatched command (its reachability probe, `cmd/cli/main.go`) and `GetConfigModeStatus` at every config-mode prompt, so a class with `deny-commands "show version"` — or an `allow-commands` list naming anything else — was locked out of SSH management entirely and told "cannot reach xpfd", while `show version` itself (ShowText topic `version`) stayed denied. Commit gave no warning.

What:
Remove both charges. The probes return liveness facts (uptime, cluster role, dirty flag), not the version banner, so they are session plumbing: named in `methodsWithoutCanonicalCommand` / `restRoutesNoCommand` and exempted from the operational regex gates (`isSessionPlumbingMethod` on gRPC, `restNoCommandExempt14146` on REST), governed by the coarse `PermView` price alone. `show version` keeps its charge where it is actually served (ShowText topic `version`, `GET /api/v1/show-text?topic=version`). The cli startup probe now reports `PermissionDenied` as an authorization denial instead of a reachability failure. ## PR #15424 — cli: execute top/up-prefixed config commands at target level (#15082) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15082-campaign`

## Why

`top delete … policy allow-all` printed `[edit]`, sent no Delete RPC (remote `cmd/cli`) / executed nothing (local `pkg/cli`), and returned success — both dispatchers treated `top`/`up` as pure navigation and never read trailing tokens. The permit policy stayed in the candidate and committed: a silent divergence between operator intent and committed enforcement (A53-01). `AuthorizeConfigMutation` also treated every `top`/`up` line as ungated navigation, so executing the inner command without unwrapping the prefix in the gate would have let denied deletes ride ungated.

## What

- `pkg/config`: `ResolveTopUpPrefix15082`/`ParseTopUpPrefix15082` split `top <cmd>` / `up [n] <cmd>` once (target cursor, inner tokens, quote provenance; bare navigation vs malformed prefix, prefixed out-of-range counts fail closed). `configMutationPaths` + embedded-payload scan unwrap the prefix so prefixed mutations are adjudicated as the inner command at the target cursor.
- `pkg/cli` + `cmd/cli`: `dispatchTopUp15082` — bare form navigates (`up n` count now honoured), prefixed form installs the target cursor, re-enters `dispatchConfig` (every gate re-runs), executes exactly the un-prefixed command (exactly one Delete RPC on the remote surface for the acceptance probe), restores cursor/prompt on success and error.

NOT changed: gRPC/REST handlers (already-resolved paths), `NavigateTop`/`NavigateUp` store primitives.

## Validation

- RED pre-fix (fix reverted, tests kept): local top/up delete left `allow-all` in candidate with nil return; remote sent zero Delete RPCs; invalid prefixes returned nil.
- GREEN: `pkg/cli`, `cmd/cli`, `pkg/config` 15082 cells pass; `pkg/config` authz subset pass; `go vet` clean on the three packages; `git diff --check` clean.
- Full `pkg/cli` run: 10 failures, all reproduced verbatim on pristine `origin/master` (base-attributed, none in the top/up path). `cmd/cli` dispatch-adjacent subset passes.

## Risk

Only config-mode lines starting `top`/`up` change: trailing tokens now execute instead of being silently ignored; malformed prefixes now error instead of silently succeeding. Bare `top`/`up` navigate as before. Denied mutations are refused by the unwrapped gate before execution.

## PR #15425 — daemon: ignore SIGHUP instead of dying unscored (#15084) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15084-campaign`

Why:
Nothing in xpfd notified or ignored SIGHUP, so the default
action killed the daemon with no shutdown sequence (no HA
fence, no rg_active clear, no priority-0 advert, no RA
goodbye), and systemd scored the death as a clean exit, so the
unit's Restart=on-failure never revived the firewall. One stray
`systemctl kill -s HUP xpfd` (or a closing controlling terminal)
was an indefinite forwarding outage standalone, or an
ungraceful peer-loss failover after which an HA node never
rejoined.

What:
- pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go: ignoreSIGHUP() installs an explicit
  no-op disposition at the TOP of Run (before the mutating
  startup phases, both modes, deferred release): a buffered
  signal.Notify channel logs each HUP ("xpfd has no
  reload-on-HUP; use commit") and discards it; the daemon keeps
  forwarding. daemonSignals() extracts the shutdown set as a
  named seam and SIGHUP is deliberately kept OUT of it — an
  orderly exit-0 stop would still score clean under systemd, so
  the "orderly stop" fix shape is rejected.
- test/incus/xpfd.service (the unit debian/rules stages and
  injects ExecStartPre into): RestartForceExitStatus=SIGHUP
  SIGPIPE, so even a HUP death in a window the capture cannot
  cover (pre-Run, older binary under the upgraded unit) is
  scored a failure and restarted within RestartSec. The
  version drop-in (pkg/upgrade/flip.go) rewrites only
  ExecStart/ExecStartPre, so the directive survives cuts.
- pkg/daemon/README.md (stale "(SIGHUP reload, ...)" claim
  corrected + disposition documented), debian/changelog,
  docs/log/15084.md.

NOT changed: surviving shutdown behaviour (daemon
SIGTERM+SIGINT, interactive SIGTERM only so the CLI keeps
Ctrl-C), commit/apply paths, the flip.go drop-in template, and
in-process SIGPIPE semantics (only the supervisor's scoring of
a SIGPIPE death changes).

Validation:
- RED on origin/master (6fd1efe432): the regression file alone
  does not build (undefined: daemonSignals, undefined:
  ignoreSIGHUP — no SIGHUP capture seam exists there) and the
  unit carries no RestartForceExitStatus.
- GREEN: TestDaemonSignalsExcludeSIGHUP15084 (shutdown set
  excludes SIGHUP, keeps SIGTERM/SIGINT),
  TestIgnoreSIGHUPSurvivesDelivery15084 (two real
  self-delivered SIGHUPs, process alive, single stop release),
  TestUnitRestartForceExitStatus15084 (parses the shipped
  unit), the #5807 startup-signal suite, pkg/grpcapi #8233 and
  pkg/dataplane/userspace #7675 unit consumers; go vet

*(truncated — 67 lines total)*

## PR #15428 — daemon: gate bare xpfd behind a singleton flock before any mutation (#15085) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15085-campaign`

Why: A bare `xpfd` or `xpfd -flag...` — the exact invocation the old
unknown-command error text recommended — booted a second full daemon on
a live firewall. Long before the #8233 management-port refusal fired,
Daemon.Run cleared the live owner's first-apply marker, and the later
phases re-ran compile, closed the transit gate, and re-attached XDP, so
an operator mistake the product itself suggested mutated host-global
state under the running daemon.

What: `daemon.New` now takes a non-blocking exclusive flock on
`/run/xpf/xpfd.lock` (0600, owner pid recorded under the lock, never
unlinked) before the config store is constructed, and the Daemon holds
it until `Run` returns; a second process fails with `xpfd already
running (pid N); use the 'cli' binary ..., or 'systemctl restart xpfd'
...`. `Daemon.Run` refuses any lease-less Daemon before any startup
mutation, and `clearHostInboundFirstApplyMarker` refuses to delete a
marker live-held by another process (`HostInboundFirstApplyLive`). The
cmdUnknown text no longer suggests running `xpfd` directly. NOT
changed: classifyCommand routing (bare xpfd must still start the daemon
under systemd; the singleton, not argv shape, is the gate), one-shot
subcommands stay lock-free, and no pidfile/blocking wait is introduced
(systemd `TimeoutStopSec` bounds predecessor exit; flock releases on fd
close).

Validation: RED pre-fix — `daemon_singleton_15085_test.go` fails to
build on origin/master (singleton API absent). GREEN post-fix —
TestAcquireDaemonLockRejectsSecondOwner15085 (busy refusal names pid +
alternatives, probe reads live, re-acquire after release works) and
TestDaemonRunRefusesSecondProcessBeforeMarkerClear15085 (real
Daemon.Run against a live flock + live first-apply marker: refused,
marker intact, no .configdb created) pass, plus adjacent controls
TestClearHostInboundFirstApplyMarker10751,
TestMarkerOwnershipLifecycle10751, TestFirstApplyMarkerRedirectedInTests10751
and the #12155 real-Run chain test (6/6). go vet/build/gofmt clean.
Full ./pkg/daemon suite shows 37–38 pre-existing failures reproduced on
unmodified origin/master (config-sync/RG0 + golden drift, unrelated);
./cmd/xpfd fully green.

Risk: A daemon started outside systemd now also refuses while another
instance holds the lock — intended. Restart overlap works unchanged:
predecessor exit closes its fd, successor acquires immediately after.

Closes #15085

## PR #15429 — config: fold brace-elided top-level interfaces into braced shape (#15062) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15062-campaign`

## Summary

Fixes #15062 (A01-01): a top-level `interfaces <name> { ... }` committed clean and compiled phantom interfaces (`unit`, `family`), losing the named interface's address/DHCP/MTU — including `fxp0` through the day-0 `CheckText` gate.

## Why

The parser builds `Keys=["interfaces","ge-0/0/0"]` with the interface body as children. `compileSections` dispatched on `node.Name()` and ignored `Keys[1:]`, so `compileInterfaces` received the `interfaces` node itself and named an `InterfaceConfig` after each body child. The scoped compact fold cannot name an operator-chosen interface name (#8879), and the #8879 cell asserted only `err == nil`, so the loss was invisible.

## What

- `normalizeElidedInterface15062` (new) folds the elided node into the braced shape inside `normalizeCompactStanzas` — the #9620 routing-instance pattern. Every compile core and `SchemaValidate` normalize before reading the tree, so strict commit, lenient load, node-aware compile, and `configstore.CheckText` all see the braced shape, and `ValidateInterfaceName` now gates the elided name.
- Hooked in `normalizeCompactNodes` when the `interfaces` child is exactly `schemaInterfaces` (root + `groups` bodies; not class-of-service `interfaces`).
- Untouched: braced form, bare leaf `interfaces <name>;`, top-level apply statements, parser, compiler readers, display rendering (authored shape still renders verbatim).

## Validation

- New `pkg/config/interfaces_elided_normalize_15062_test.go`: elided↔braced tree equality (top level + inside groups) and compiled interface/unit/address/DHCP/MTU digest equality with phantom checks; neighbour shapes untouched.
- New `pkg/configstore/interfaces_elided_commit_gate_15062_test.go`: `CheckText` parity for fxp0/ge (address, MTU, DHCP); invalid name refused in both spellings.
- `#8879` cell now compares compiled values instead of only `err == nil`.
- RED on base (production stashed): phantom `unit`/`family`, named interface lost, bad name accepted elided-only. GREEN after fix on the rebased head; `go vet` clean.
- Full `pkg/config` suite at this base carries pre-existing failures verified identical on pristine master (LLDP block-form panic, IPsec/WireGuard degenerate-key rows, #2419 inventory drift) and times out under parallel lane load; no new failure attributed to this change in exercised suites.

## Risk

Elided spellings now compile what their braced spellings always compiled. Configs that (incorrectly) relied on the phantom/loss behaviour now get the authored interface. `docs/log/15062.md` records the full history.

Branch: `fix/15088-campaign`

## PR #15433 — userspace-dp: bound pending-neighbor park by RX fill pool (#15096) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15096-campaign`

## Summary

Fixes A66-02 (#15096): the per-binding pending-neighbor cap `MAX_PENDING_NEIGH` (4096) ignored the binding's RX frame budget. At the default ring-entries 1024 the whole RX fill pool is 2048 frames (fill = 2*ring; total = reserved TX + 2*ring), so a permitted sweep of a large connected prefix parking one RX frame per distinct unresolved hop could pin twice the pool, drain the fill ring, and stall all RX on the affected queues.

## Fix

- `pending_neigh_cap_for_rx_fill(rx_fill) = min(MAX_PENDING_NEIGH, max(rx_fill/4, 1))` — at most one quarter of a binding's own RX fill pool may be parked; computed once at bind time in `BindingWorker` (production `create` + both test constructors).
- `rx_fill_frames_for_driver` derives fill as total − reserved TX from the existing bind arithmetic, so a reserved-TX policy change moves the cap with it.
- The poll loop's single admission call passes `binding.pending_neigh_cap`; refusals take the existing counted `CapacityDrop` arm (`pending_neigh_capacity_drops`, #2375) and recycle the frame — fail-closed, no silent park.
- NOT changed: probe schedules, pending timeouts, the negative-neighbor cache, per-source/per-prefix sub-caps (optional in the issue; the quarter-pool cap alone restores the fill-ring invariant), and the 4096 ceiling for large rings.

## Regression (RED → GREEN)

- `ring_1024_binding_parks_at_most_quarter_of_fill_pool_15096`: builds the ring=1024 pool from the production bind arithmetic (non-virtio/virtio/mlx5); asserts cap == rx_fill/4 < 4096, Buffer at cap−1, CapacityDrop at cap, DuplicateDrop for duplicates, plus the large-ring ceiling and degenerate-pool floors. Pre-fix the helper compared `len < MAX_PENDING_NEIGH` with no per-binding cap, so this fails on `origin/master`.
- `binding_worker_parks_at_most_quarter_of_its_pool_15096`: a real `BindingWorker` (256-frame mirror pool) carries cap 64 and a recorded refusal moves only `pending_neigh_capacity_drops`.
- `rx_fill_frames_is_total_minus_reserved_tx_15096`: fill derivation across drivers/rings.
- Controls re-pinned: `first_packet_buffers_siblings_duplicate_drop`, `new_key_capacity_boundary`, `record_drop_counts_capacity_separately`, and the live `invariant_n1` buffering half.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p xpf-userspace-dp --bin xpf-userspace-dp pending_admission` → 5 passed
- `… -- rx_fill_frames_is_total_minus_reserved_tx_15096 invariant_n1 pending_admission` → 7 passed
- `… -- neighbor_dispatch umem_sizing` → 56 passed, 1 ignored
- `… -- umem_sizing pending` → 67 passed, 1 ignored

Full log: `docs/log/15096.md`. Lab leg deferred to main: a /64 SYN sweep at ring=1024 should leave `rx_fill_ring_empty_descs` flat with an established flow unaffected.

Closes #15096

positive tag by the #5879 QinQ gate (single S-tag) and the #14574
tagging gate, but compileInterfaces only read `vlan-id`, so the
outer value was silently dropped and the unit compiled untagged
(VlanID=0) on a green commit. Tagged traffic for the unit is lost,
and on unit 0 untagged frames gain the unit's zone.

What: compileInterfaces now walks every outer-only `vlan-tags`
sibling (packed, hierarchical, and `outer { N; }` shapes, via the
new vlanTagsOuterValue15035 / parseVlanTagsOuter15035 helpers in
pkg/config/compiler_interfaces.go) and compiles the value into
VlanID with the shared #9899 0..4094 contract. TPID-prefixed
values (`0x88a8.100`) reject in strict mode; malformed/missing
values fail closed, warning + unit quarantine on the lenient path
(shared skipUnit9899, now unit-scoped). Inner-bearing nodes stay
with the #5879 gate; `vlan-id` remains first-spelling-wins.
NOT changed: the gates, the schema, dataplane writers.
Regression + docs: pkg/config/vlan_tags_outer_only_15035_test.go,
docs/log/15035.md.

Validation: RED on base 142105d5f8 — outer-only compiled VlanID=0,
TPID/malformed compiled clean. GREEN after fix:
TestVlanTagsOuter* (6 tests) plus TestQinQ*/TestVlanID*/
TestSupportedSingleTag* neighbors all PASS; go vet clean; gofmt
clean. Full pkg/config suite (minus the spelling-census tests,
which time out identically on a pristine base worktree on this
box): 85 failures on the fix branch vs 90 on base, zero
branch-only failures — all pre-existing and unrelated.

Risk: strict commits with TPID-prefixed or malformed outer values
now fail with a remedy message; previously silent-untagged
outer-only configs now compile to their authored tag, as the
gates already promised. Lenient loads still boot.

Closes #15035

## PR #15436 — config: reject prefix-less VRRP virtual-address at strict compile (#15050) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15050-campaign`

Closes #15050

## Summary
The packed hierarchical one-liner `vrrp-group 1 virtual-address 10.0.1.100;` carried a bare (prefix-less) VIP past `SchemaValidate` and strict compile: the value rides the instance node's Keys as an unvalidated identity token, so the schema's `ValidateIPv4CIDR`/`ValidateIPv6CIDR` leaf never saw it. At runtime `pkg/vrrp` passes the string verbatim to `netlink.ParseAddr`, which requires a prefix; the failure is recorded as a failed VIP, `ok()` is false, and #5082 fail-closed reverts every promotion to BACKUP — the VRRP-protected gateway has no owner on every node carrying the config (reachable via hierarchical load / day-0 / config-sync, not via `set`).

## Fix
- New compiled-`*Config` gate `validateVRRPVIPPrefixStrict` (`compiler_validate_strict_vrrp_vipprefix.go`), wired beside the #8483 timers gate: strict commit/commit-check hard-rejects a parseable-but-prefix-less VIP, naming interface/unit/group/VIP and the corrected spelling.
- Tolerant load/peer-sync downgrades to a warning (`lenientVRRPVIPPrefix`, #1960 no-brick) and `normalizeBareVRRPVIPs` (tail gates) rewrites the bare VIP with the enclosing unit address prefix, or `/32`/`/128` when no same-family prefix exists — so the tolerant config **actuates** instead of reverting every promotion forever.
- Garbage literals remain the #7577 empty gate's concern (not re-reported).
- Incidental fix in the #15046 children gate: its Keys-packed scan now skips bracketed multi-value tokens of a `multi` leaf, so a bracketed `virtual-address [ a b ]` list's second address is no longer misjudged as an unknown group property (exposed by the new regression's bracketed spelling; bracketed lists are a supported #1813 spelling).
- Neighbour fixtures that authored bare VIPs as incidental setup now author the CIDR spelling (same addresses/assertions): `vrrp_track`, `dual_ast_differential`, #6779 count lines, #7577 control, #5837 DNAT, #15046/#15048 sibling tests; one #15047 fixture tracks its own configured `reth0` instead of an undeclared interface.

## Validation
- New regression (`compiler_validate_strict_vrrp_vipprefix_15050_test.go`): RED on `origin/master` (packed bare VIP commits clean — verified with a probe on a pristine base worktree), GREEN with the fix. Strict rejects packed / bracketed-bare-first / braced / IPv6; CIDR controls commit unchanged; lenient warns and normalizes `10.0.1.100` → `10.0.1.100/24`; host-prefix fallback passes the strict gate after normalization.
- Full VRRP-named suite green except `TestVRRPCrossGroupDifferentInterfacesCommits`, which fails identically on current `origin/master` for the unrelated #15034 unit-without-vlan-id reason. `pkg/vrrp` suite green; `go build ./...` green; `go vet`/`gofmt` clean on touched files.
- Other pre-existing failures confirmed identical on base: `TestZoneInterface*` (#14139), `TestSchemaValidate_Interfaces_AcceptedValuesCompileAsWritten` (#14574), compact censuses #2419/#8690, `TestDualASTDifferential/security-nat*`.

Log: `docs/log/15050.md`. Never merge — review only.

## PR #15437 — userspace-dp: bound L3 reverse bucket cost under SNAT fan-in (#15087) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15087-campaign`

Why:
  l3_reverse_index keyed every SNAT forward session by the
  protocol-erased (family, server, SNAT address) identity in a linear
  SmallVec bucket, so insert (contains), removal (retain), and every
  flowless-fragment probe cost O(bucket) — O(N) in the live
  same-destination session count toward one popular destination
  (resolver, CDN edge, bench target) on the worker session-table path.

What:
  Replace the bucket interior with L3ReverseBucket: a keyed hashed
  handle set plus per-protocol member counts (session/mod.rs), kept
  exact at the same insert/remove sites by passing the member's real
  reverse protocol. The fragment probe (session/lookup.rs) now decides
  from counts plus a bounded 8-member verification walk that
  re-derives live slab records; presence of an unvisited counted
  member answers fail-closed TRUE, matching every live outcome.
  NOT changed: the L3 key shape, 255-sentinel semantics, domain
  admission, the other NAT indexes, or GC ownership.

Validation:
  New session/l3_reverse_bucket_15087_tests.rs (6 cells): structural
  pin fails to compile on pristine master (5 errors naming the
  SmallVec bucket), 100k insert/remove flat (0.48s), probe-vs-control
  flat at 2k fan-in, survivor/mixed-protocol/plain/expiry controls.
  Post-rebase: l3_reverse_bucket_15087 filter 5 passed; session::
  filter 471 passed. The frag-filter cohort's 10 failures reproduce
  on sibling pristine-master binaries (shared global frag-assoc
  state) and are not this change — see docs/log/15087.md.

Risk:
  Fragment gate gains one bounded over-drop corner (all-expired
  bucket larger than the probe budget returns TRUE until GC).
  Per-identity memory grows by a 256-entry counts array plus hash-set
  overhead, bounded by distinct NAT destinations, not sessions.

Closes #15087

## PR #15438 — userspace-dp: reclaim oldest completed anchor across zones at shard cap (#15103) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15103-campaign`

## Why

`OverlapTracker::check_and_record_fragment_detailed` reclaimed completed anchors only at the candidate's own 32-entry `(routing_domain, ingress_zone)` reserve, and only over that zone's entries. At the fixed 64-entry shard cap it returned `ShardFull` with no reclaim at all. Two zones holding 32 completed anchors each therefore starved every third zone in the same routing domain and shard: all new fragmented datagrams for zone C dropped fail-closed for the anchors' TTL, even though completed anchors are the explicitly reclaimable class (#14321). Reachable by #14321's own attacker shape (4 untrusted senders) plus any moderately busy second zone.

## What

- `userspace-dp/src/fragment_overlap/mod.rs`, shard-cap branch only: when the shard is at 64 and the candidate's zone is below its own reserve (guaranteed by ordering — the own-zone check above either reclaimed, refused, or left it below 32), reclaim the globally oldest COMPLETED anchor (`overlap_entry_complete`: `pending == 0`, not failed, ranges cover the terminal end) of any zone in the candidate's routing domain before refusing. Incomplete anchors are never reclaimed; with none reclaimable the refusal is byte-identical to before (same `FRAG_OVERLAP_SHARD_FULL_DROPPED` bump + `ShardFull` reason).
- New observability counter `FRAG_OVERLAP_CROSS_ZONE_RECLAIMED` (global atomic alongside its siblings).
- Module docs (fairness + failure-direction bullets) updated at the mechanism. Callers (`poll_descriptor` pre-check / post-commit TX record) unchanged — they already drop on `ShardFull` and forward on admission.
- NOT changed: sender quota (8/shard), per-zone reserve (32), shard cap (64), TTLs, range geometry, shard hashing, `FragAssoc` (no completed-anchor class; A74-02 is OverlapTracker-only).

Deviations from the issue's fix direction, recorded per instructions:
1. The `and/or reserve per active zone` alternative was not taken: dividing 64 by active zones shrinks every zone's reserve as zones join, changes admitted behaviour for the two-zone case, and contradicts #14321's fixed 32-entry reserve. The primary direction (globally-oldest completed reclaim) fully satisfies the acceptance probe.
2. "Add a FragAssoc refusal counter": the OverlapTracker `ShardFull` refusal already had both a global counter (`FRAG_OVERLAP_SHARD_FULL_DROPPED`) and a binding-local batched counter flushed to binding state; adding a second refusal counter would double-count. The counter added instead measures the new event (cross-zone reclaims), which is the operator-visible signal for this fix.

Security trade, explicit: an evicted completed anchor loses overlap protection for the remainder of its reassembly window — the identical trade #14321 already accepts at the per-zone cap, extended across zones in one domain. The prior behaviour (third-zone blackhole) is the worse failure.

## Validation

- RED (base `fde73e9b28` + test only): `third_zone_admitted_by_cross_zone_completed_reclaim_15103` FAILED — `zone-C victim must be admitted by cross-zone completed reclaim, reason=Some(ShardFull)` (zones A/B = 32 completed anchors each in one shard).
- GREEN (with fix): same test passes; also asserts zone A stays capped via its own-zone reclaim, `len()` stays 64, no `SHARD_FULL` bump, exactly one `CROSS_ZONE_RECLAIMED` bump, and a shard full of incomplete anchors still refuses zone C fail-closed with no eviction.
- Controls: `cargo test --bins fragment_overlap` — 44 passed; `cargo test --bins 9950` — 28 passed (includes `shard_full_drops_without_evicting_live_9950`, `cross_zone_domain_fill_cannot_starve_other_zone_14321`, `completed_entries_hold_shard_capacity_until_expiry_10285`, `completed_anchors_preserve_routing_domain_reserve_14009`).
- `rustfmt --check` on the file was already dirty on base (58 hunks pre-existing); the change adds no new fmt hunks beyond that baseline drift.

## Risk

Under sustained churn of completed datagrams across many zones in one shard, anchors rotate faster than their 30s TTL; the `FRAG_OVERLAP_CROSS_ZONE_RECLAIMED` rate makes this visible. No behaviour change when a shard is below 64 entries or the candidate's zone is at its own reserve.

Closes #15103

## PR #15439 — userspace-dp: honour RouteEntry.reject in FIB route selection (#15098) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15098-campaign`

## Summary
`RouteEntry.reject` was stored by `forwarding_build` (since #13949) but never read by route selection: `select_v4_route`/`select_v6_route` treated only `discard` as terminal. Every reject route lost its dataplane ICMP unreachable and was counted as `no_route`; a reject+next-hop row was **forwarded** as an ordinary gateway, and a next-table leak whose target LPM is a reject route resolved `NoRoute` inside the target and fell through to forwarding. Residual of `3743c24ffd`, whose message claims a FIB change its diff does not contain.

## Fix
- `select_v4_route` / `select_v6_route` (`forwarding/fib.rs`): `discard || reject` is the terminal row, under the identical #13950 drivable-fallback preference gate — a reject row never reaches next-hop selection.
- `Static` arms of `lookup_forwarding_resolution_v4_inner`/`_v6_inner`: return the zero-egress terminal resolution with `RejectRoute` when `reject` is set, `DiscardRoute` otherwise (reject wins if both flags set; the Go producer never sets both).
- Leak walk unchanged: it already returns any non-`NoRoute` disposition immediately, so a target-LPM `RejectRoute` is now terminal rather than a miss. No other consumer changes — the `RejectRoute` disposition, poll arm, reply builder, and counters already existed (#13949/#14021/#14237/#14319).

## Tests
- FIB (`tests_lpm_parity_9522.rs`, snapshot-built via production `build_forwarding_state`): `reject_only_route_rejects_v4_v6_15098`, `reject_with_next_hop_still_rejects_v4_v6_15098`, `leak_into_reject_target_rejects_v4_v6_15098`, plus discard/preference controls.
- Poll level (`reject_reply_tests.rs`): `reject_snapshot_resolves_and_enqueues_icmp_unreachable_15098` — reject snapshot → production FIB → poll arm seam → exactly one ICMPv4 destination-unreachable enqueued.
- **RED** (fix reverted, tests present): 4 failed, 1 control passed. **GREEN**: all 5 pass; neighbouring `afxdp::forwarding::` + `reject_reply` suites 408 passed, 0 failed.

Docs: `docs/log/15098.md`, terminal-reject note in `forwarding/README.md`.

Closes #15098

## PR #15441 — userspace-dp: record refused replay upserts as repair debt (#15105) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15105-campaign`

Why:
Both reconcile replay sites pushed synced-session rows through
`push_bounded` and discarded its refusal at the 4096-command queue cap:
the bring-up replay fans a full shared snapshot into brand-new queues
via `replicate_session_upsert`, and `replay_late_synced_sessions`
appends a fresh snapshot behind a retained prefix. Any shared table
over 4096 rows therefore handed each new worker only the first 4096
rows; the rest were absent, took no SNAT holder reservation, and
carried no repair obligation (#6929 residual; #11360 covered the
import path only).

What:
A refused `UpsertSynced` now records #11360 session-import repair debt,
positioned after the queue prefix at refusal and recorded under the
queue lock, in `replicate_session_upsert` (worker id resolved from the
generation `WorkerCommandQueues` via a new Arc-identity
`worker_id_for_queue`) and in `replay_late_synced_sessions` (worker id
threaded from the spawn caller; existing test callers updated). The
worker re-reads each refused key from shared authority at that FIFO
boundary, so deleted rows take the delete path instead of
resurrecting. The per-worker repair bound rises to
`2 * MAX_PENDING_WORKER_COMMANDS` so a full queue ahead of a larger
snapshot can obligate the whole refused tail. NOT changed: the queue
cap, the drain budget, or any non-replay producer's ordering.

Validation:
New `coordinator/tests.rs` cells
`bringup_replay_over_cap_records_import_repair_debt_15105` and
`late_replay_over_cap_records_import_repair_debt_15105` seed cap+1000
shared rows through the real replay helpers: RED on origin/master
`0e8ce36bba` ("recorded no repair debt"), GREEN post-fix with the queue
still capped at 4096 and the full refused tail (1000 / 1001 rows)
covered by due debt; #9718 late-import control green. Adjacent
`afxdp::coordinator`/`ha`/`session_glue`/`worker_queue` suites: 932
passed, 14 failed — 13 reproduce identically on unmodified
origin/master `3d5c595678` (base-attributed), the 14th was the #11360
overflow fixture, updated to the doubled bound and now green.

Risk:
Steady-state sibling replication now also records debt on refusal
instead of dropping silently; repairs re-read current shared authority
so they cannot resurrect superseded rows. Past the 8192 per-worker
repair bound the behaviour degrades to the pre-fix drop-counter-only
signal rather than failing live traffic closed.

Closes #15105

Branch: `fix/15095-campaign`

Why: the #14645 outer-fragment reassembler buffered every fragmented
proto-47 datagram reaching stage 6, with no check that the outer
destination was a native-GRE endpoint. A transit GRE/PPTP datagram
fragmented upstream was consumed fragment-by-fragment; on completion
decap missed, the stage returned Buffered, and the descriptor was
recycled with no counter. Fragmented transit GRE was never forwarded

when `gre::outer_frame_targets_gre_endpoint` finds the frame's

fragment falls through as `NotGre` to the ordinary flowless /
fragment-association path. Key, transport-domain, egress and
host-inbound checks still run at decap. A completed datagram whose
decap then refuses is counted once via the new
`GreDecapCounters::reassembled_decap_refusals`, surfaced Rust -> Go ->
Prometheus as `gre_reassembled_decap_refusals_total` /
`xpf_userspace_gre_reassembled_decap_refusals_total`. NOT changed: XDP
shim steering (it has no per-endpoint table; the helper now declines
non-endpoint fragments) and no per-source pool quota (the gate removes
the non-peer flood vector).

Validation: new `tests_gre_transit_frag_15095` (5 cells: transit head+
tail NotGre with no endpoints and with a different-pair tunnel,
to-self control byte-identical decap, 65-head non-peer flood cannot
block peer reassembly, keyed-to-unkeyed completed refusal counted
once). RED measured with only the gate conjunct reverted: 3 failed
("must return NotGre, not Buffered"), 2 controls passed. GREEN:
`cargo test -- 15095 14645 14652` = 10 passed;
`-- 14645 gre_outer_frag process_status_gre` = 11 passed; wire fixture
regenerated; `go vet ./pkg/api/ ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/` clean;
targeted `go test` in pkg/api and pkg/dataplane/userspace ok.

buffering until the next apply installs the index entry — strictly

## PR #15444 — userspace-dp: bound wildcard zone-pair expansion to slot budget (#15092) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15092-campaign`

Why:
`configured_zone_pairs()` materialised every concrete zone pair per wildcard/global rule into a `BTreeSet`: both-any inserted Z² pairs and each unscoped `junos-global` cloned the universe for another cross product. At 8000 zones one Any×Any scope is 64M pairs inside the snapshot build (2–3 builds per commit) — a control-plane stall of seconds — while `ColdPathSlotMap` can only assign 255 slots.

What:
- `policy.rs`: new `configured_zone_pairs_bounded(limit) -> ConfiguredZonePairs { pairs, overflow }`. Exact `zone_pair_index` pairs first (unchanged slot priority), then the wildcard/global tier generated as sorted per-scope cross-product streams merged k-way with dedup, stopping at the slots left after the exact tier plus one overflow probe. No cross product is materialised; an Any×Any scope (both-any or unscoped global) subsumes every other wildcard/global scope and becomes the sole stream. Exact-tier members reached again by the merge consume no budget. `configured_zone_pairs()` delegates at the slot budget (every pre-#15092 test config fits, so it equals the old set there).
- `forwarding_build/mod.rs`: builds via the bounded form and ORs `overflow` into `ColdPathSlotMap::overflow_active` — without it a capped 255-pair input is indistinguishable from an exact fit and the operator starvation flag never fires for this tier.
- `cold_path_hist.rs` / `afxdp/mod.rs`: `COLD_PATH_ASSIGNABLE_SLOTS` and the module widen to `pub(crate)` so `policy.rs` clamps to the same constant.
- `docs/log/15092.md`, `docs/userspace-dataplane-architecture.md`: bounded-generation note.

NOT changed: slot assignment/retention/zeroing in `ColdPathSlotMap::build`; the exact-tier set and its priority; policy evaluation tiers. At/under-capacity configs return byte-identical pair vectors.

## PR #15448 — ipsec: promote the recovered set on a commit-path partial clear (#15128) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15128-campaign`

Closes #15128

## Problem (A90-01)
The commit path reaches `clearConfig` via `ApplyGeneration` with an empty config (`pkg/daemon/ipsec_sa_rg_9139.go:103`), not via `Clear()` (factory reset only). On a partial clear where charon still holds a prior connection, `clearConfig` rolls charon back to the prior file and returns `partialApplyError{names: priorSet, hashes: priorHashes, clear: true}`. `Clear()` promotes `pae.names`/`pae.hashes`, but `ApplyGeneration` discarded them and promoted the empty set — so xpf forgot VPNs charon still runs, their SAs were never terminated, and the persisted record said none. Deleting every VPN (e.g. decommissioning a compromised peer) under a partial clear left the deleted VPNs' configs and PSKs loaded in charon and on disk while xpf's record said empty.

## Fix
`ApplyGeneration` now promotes `pae.names`/`pae.hashes` for the clear case too, matching `Clear()`. The empty-set case is already encoded as `names={}` by `clearConfig` (and the `names == nil` encoding still promotes `{}`), so neighbouring behaviour is unchanged. The `partialApplyError` doc comment now states that for `clearConfig`, `names` is the recovered set charon runs.

## Regression (RED/GREEN)
Added to `pkg/ipsec/partial_load_14589_test.go`, driving the exact commit path through the same fake charon as the existing `Clear()` control:
- `TestA90PartialClearViaApplyEmpty` — partial clear via empty-config `ApplyGeneration`: prior file restored byte-identical, `prevConnNames` == charon's loaded set `{a,b}`.
- `TestA90FollowUpAfterApplyEmpty` — a later successful empty-config `ApplyGeneration` with live SAs for `a`/`b` must issue `--terminate --ike` for both.

Both fail on `origin/master` (`prev=map[] want prior {a,b}`) and pass after the fix. The `Clear()` control `TestPartialClearRestoresPriorFile14589` is unchanged and stays green.

## Validation
- `go test ./pkg/ipsec/ -run 'TestA90|TestPartialClearRestoresPriorFile14589|TestPartialLoad|TestNonPartial' -count=1` PASS
- `go test ./pkg/ipsec/ -count=1`: 62 pre-existing render failures on pristine `origin/master`, identical count with the fix (checked by stashing the fix) — no new failures.
- `go vet ./pkg/ipsec/` clean; `gofmt` clean; `go build ./pkg/ipsec/ ./pkg/daemon/` OK

Docs: `docs/log/15128.md`, `pkg/ipsec/README.md` updated.

## PR #15450 — frr: omit multihop BFD peer without a valid local-address (#15135) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15135-campaign`

Why: #14587 keys every iBGP neighbor and every ebgp-multihop neighbor as a multihop bfdd peer, but appends `local-address` only when one is configured. A routine Junos shape — directly connected iBGP, or multihop eBGP, with `bfd-liveness-detection` and no `local-address` — therefore renders the bare line `peer X multihop`, which bfdd 10.7.1 rejects. `frr-reload.py` exits 1 and every commit of such a config fails with a degraded retry that can never converge.

What: `bfdSection.render()` in `pkg/frr/bfd.go` now skips a multihop peer whose `localAddress` is empty or fails the #9493 single-token belt (the same validity test as the BGP `update-source` line), logging a warning naming the peer. The neighbor still renders `neighbor X bfd profile <p>`, so the configured timers reach bgpd's own dynamic multihop session via the profile and the `bfd` block survives on the profile alone. No single-hop fallback stanza (the proven #14587 orphan) and no new commit gate. Neighbors with a valid local-address render `peer X [vrf V] multihop local-address L` byte-identically; single-hop peers are untouched. NOT changed: compiler/validation — the render-side primary fix direction was chosen over requiring `local-address` at commit.

Validation: new `TestBGPBFDMultihopNoLocalAddress15135` (iBGP, ebgp-multihop, whitespace-invalid local-address, and VRF accumulator cells, plus keyed/single-hop controls) fails pre-fix rendering `peer 10.255.0.9 multihop` / `peer 192.0.2.10 multihop` and passes after. The one assertion in `TestBGPBFDMultihopProfile14587` that pinned the bare line is flipped; its with-local-address and single-hop controls stay green. `go test ./pkg/frr/ -run 'TestBGPBFDMultihop' -count=1` PASS; full `pkg/frr` suite shows only 3 failures confirmed identical on pristine `origin/master` (base-attributed, unrelated). `go vet ./pkg/frr/` and gofmt clean.

Risk: only the no-valid-local-address multihop leg changes — those neighbors lose the invalid, reload-breaking static stanza and keep timer delivery via the bound BFD profile. Setting `local-address` restores the keyed stanza exactly as before. The four bfdd dry-run cells from the issue are covered at render level by the new test's four legs; a live bfdd dry-run remains a lab verify.

Closes #15135

## PR #15451 — userspace-dp: carry persistent siblings as lease joins on reseed (#15110) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15110-campaign`

## Why

`reseed_retained_from` re-reserved each live flow through the non-persistent `reserve_flow`. Persistent siblings share one lease and one translated tuple but are distinct flow keys, so the first sibling claimed the occupancy bit as a plain PAT record and every later sibling was refused by the occupied-bit check. The refused sibling was not carried while its session kept forwarding, and the survivor's record named no lease — so its first release freed a tuple still in use: the #6765 reissue / reply-misdelivery hazard for persistent pools, via an ordinary add-an-address pool edit (A76-03).

## What

- Snapshot pass in `reseed_retained_from` now computes the non-deterministic persistent leases that have at least one live flow itself carried in range.
- The port-bearing carry arm carries records naming such a lease via `reserve_flow_maybe_persistent(..., Some((key, lease.timeout_ns)))` — first sibling mints the lease, later siblings join it, bit frees only at lease teardown (last release + carried idle timeout). Both untracked and per-worker holder arms.
- `dropped_persistent_*` counting skips carried leases; idle leases and removed-address leases are still counted/reported (#7560 semantics preserved).
- NOT changed: address-only carry, clear-replay fences (a cleared lease stays fenced; the join falls back to a plain reservation), deterministic BIB leases (kept on the plain path — their `deterministic_identity` cannot be rebuilt from a flow record).

## Validation

- New `nat/tests_reseed_persistent_siblings_15110.rs` (4 cells): binder asserts `refused == 0`, `reseeded == 2`, one lease with `active_flows == 2`, bit held until both siblings release + idle expiry. RED on `origin/master` 780fab7b3c (`refused: left 1, right 0`), GREEN after the fix.
- Controls: plain PAT carry mints no lease; idle persistent lease still counted dropped; out-of-range siblings still skipped.
- Two #7560 cells in `tests_pool.rs` updated from pinning the drop to pinning the carry.
- Full `nat::` suite: 686 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored (debug `--bins`).

## Risk

Carried leases are minted `imported: true` by the existing synced-join constructor, so idle-lease export skips them until a local flow completes — conservative (no peer echo) and self-healing on completion.

Closes #15110

## PR #15455 — userspace-dp: credit exact queues their self-park lag at low rates (#15100) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15100-campaign`

## Summary

A backlogged exact queue parks for its own frame-refill time (1500 B at 8000 B/s = 187.5 ms), but the v8 lease rotation credited at most K×EPOCH = 1.6 ms per visit, banked the rest into an epoch-sized carry (12.8 B at 8000 B/s — never enough to reassemble a frame), and dropped it past the fixed 51.2 ms STALL cutoff. 64k/128k exact classes delivered 0% and 1 Mbps 29.5% of their configured rate.

Fix: rate-relative windows in the shared CoS lease.
- `lag_window_ns_for_rate(rate)` = max(K×EPOCH, one full frame's refill) and `stall_window_ns_for_rate(rate)` = max(fixed floor, 2× lag window) in `types/shared_cos_lease/epoch.rs`.
- Byte-sized carry reservoir/drain stored on `V8State` at lease creation (`lease.rs`), read by `rotate_epoch_v8.rs`. Per-rotation burst stays bounded (max(K×rate×EPOCH, one frame) + bounded drain); a genuine stall beyond the window still cold-resumes to one epoch and drops carry.
- Park-aware wakeup guard in `queue_service/settle.rs`: a queue already holding its need wakes next tick instead of parking for a frame refill.
- Rates whose fixed K window already covers a frame are byte-identical (all pre-existing #1630/#1863 carry cells unchanged in behaviour).

Validation: RED pre-fix — `new_v8(8000)` acquiring at t0 and t0+187.5 ms granted 1 B (want ≥1499); sustained 1 Mbps self-park delivered 24000/180000 B. GREEN — 7 #15100 cells pass; `shared_cos_lease` 109/109, `token_bucket` 27/27, combined neighbouring run 136/136.

Closes #15100

## PR #15456 — userspace-dp: bind neighbor probe token to probed MAC (#15097) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15097-campaign`

## Summary
Fixes A66-05: the kernel-monitor `NUD_PROBE` token no longer authorizes a MAC the dataplane refused.

- Solicited-probe evidence is now MAC-bound (`ProbedNeighbor`): locally-issued probes (warmer/resolver/dispatch) stay key-only; a kernel `NUD_PROBE` records a token only for the lladdr it carries **and** only when that is the dataplane's held MAC.
- On a refused probe (kernel probing attacker MAC `A`, dataplane holding `G`): mint no token, clear stale evidence, and rate-limited re-assert `G` into the kernel (`RTM_NEWNEIGH` REPLACE, `NUD_STALE`) so the kernel re-probes `G`. Genuinely moved hosts then fail to `NUD_FAILED` and resolve fresh.
- MAC-aware solicited peek in both monitor arms (v4+v6) and the direct XSK ARP arm.

Closes #15097

## PR #15457 — config: let nested apply-groups override outer groups (#15033) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15033-campaign`

## Summary
An outer `apply-groups` beat a nested one, opposite to Junos: the nested value met a peer already adopted from the outer group and was dropped as inline-wins. A global group's permissive interface filter (`PERMISSIVE`) therefore beat a per-interface hardening group's `STRICT` filter on a green commit.

## Fix
`pkg/config/ast_groups.go` now tracks, per adopted node, the origin level of the apply-groups application that adopted it (`groupExpandBudget.applyLevelByNode15033`, with `applyOriginLevel15033` set around each level's merge in the extracted `expandLevelRefs15033` so recursive container merges inherit the application's level, not the routing depth). Adoptions are tagged via pre-merge identity snapshots of the destination and descendant lists (first tag wins, so an ancestral merge never re-tags a leaf a nested application placed).

A later, strictly deeper application replaces a shallower adopted scalar/non-union peer (leaf override arm, leaf-list block arm, #4325 container guard). Inline peers never yield; same/deeper peers keep first-wins; leaf-list and range-free port unions are unchanged.

## Tests (RED → GREEN)
New `pkg/config/apply_groups_nested_level_15033_test.go` through strict `CompileConfig`:
- `TestNestedApplyGroupsBeatsOuter15033` — outer `PERMISSIVE` vs nested `STRICT` interface filter → `STRICT` (fails on base with `FilterInputV4="PERMISSIVE"`)
- `TestNestedApplyGroupsScalarBeatsOuter15033` — nested scalar `host-name` wins, inline `domain-name` kept (fails on base with `HostName="OUTER"`)
- `TestInlineStillBeatsNestedApplyGroups15033` — authored inline filter still beats both groups (control, green before/after)
- `TestOuterOnlyApplyGroupsControl15033` — outer-only inheritance unchanged (control, green before/after)

Validation: targeted apply-groups suites pass after rebase onto current master; `go vet ./pkg/config/` clean. Full `pkg/config` suite run recorded in `docs/log/15033.md`.

`protocols { lldp { interface { disable; } } }` (and `interface { ge-0/0/1; }` / `interface { ge-0/0/1 { disable; } }`) panicked `compileProtocols` with `slice bounds out of range [2:1]`. Those block spellings carry `Keys=["interface"]` with the would-be name (or a bare `disable`) nested as a child; `nodeVal` falls back to that child's name, so the compiler treated `"disable"`/`"ge-0/0/1"` as an interface name and then sliced `child.Keys[2:]` on a 1-key node. The panic is reachable on the strict commit, authenticated load-override, tolerant `Store.Load`, and HA `SyncApply` paths with no `recover` above any of them, so a malformed but parseable config crashed xpfd.

What:
`compileProtocols` now treats only a name packed on the LLDP interface statement itself (`Keys[1]`, `len >= 2`) as a named interface. A nameless statement is rejected on strict compile with `protocols lldp interface: an interface name is required` (fail closed) and warned about with the same message plus `(ignored on tolerant load)` and dropped on the tolerant paths via the existing `lenientLLDPInterfaceTokens14616` opt, so a persisted config still boots. The guard makes the #14616 `Keys[2:]` read provably in range. Regression tests in `pkg/config` and a store probe (`CommitCheck` rejects, `SyncApply` tolerates) pin the behaviour; named block/packed/plain/flat controls are unchanged. NOT changed: `nodeVal`, the LLDP schema node, or LLDP runtime.

Validation:
RED pre-fix: all three nameless spellings panic `CompileConfig` and `CompileConfigLenient` with `[2:1]`. FAIL-ON-REVERT measured: tests kept + fix reverted fails `TestLLDPNamelessInterfaceBlockDoesNotPanicStrict15138` with the same panic at `compiler_protocols.go:84`. GREEN: `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestLLDP|TestPrefixList|TestNoSchemaPathPanics' -count=1` PASS (census 1318 schema paths, 0 panics); `go test ./pkg/configstore/ -run 'TestLLDPNamelessBlock|TestLLDPNamedBlockStore' -count=1` PASS; `go vet ./pkg/config/ ./pkg/configstore/` clean.

Risk:
Strict commits carrying a previously-panicking nameless LLDP block now reject instead of crashing; tolerant loads warn and drop that entry. No dataplane or daemon behaviour change.

Closes #15138

producers, and native / fabric-stamp cookie behavior.

native control still sends) fail on origin/master ccc2a6af55 with
the gate assertions and pass after the fix; cookie_reply +

## PR #15465 — userspace-dp: resolve NAT wire survivors from owner index on removal (#15106) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15106-campaign`

**Userspace-dataplane change, not agent infrastructure.** Rust-only (`userspace-dp`); no agent harness operation.

## Why

#14383 reintroduced the #11299 shape: every NAT'd forward-session removal in `remove_shared_session_if` (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/shared_ops/store.rs`) scanned the whole shared session map while holding its mutex, so lock-held close cost grew linearly with the shared table (~0.6 ms/close at 100k rows in a debug build per the issue measurement) — a potential loss-of-appliance-availability risk on the session-close path.

## What

- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/types/mod.rs`: `SharedNatAmbiguityIndex` now also carries a per-wire-key owner multiset — `WireOwnerMultiset` (`FastMap<SessionKey, WireOwnerRoster>`), roster `SmallVec<[SessionKey; 2]>` — under the **same mutex** as the ambiguity aliases, plus a `wire_saturated` latch (fail-closed above the 16_384 wire-key cap, mirroring `saturated`). Methods: `observe_wire_owner` (idempotent per owner), `remove_wire_owner`, `wire_owners_trusted`, `wire_first_owner`, `reset_wire_owners`, `wire_owner_count`; `clear()` resets roster/latches.
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/shared_ops/store.rs`: `publish_shared_session` records the live owner before the wire map write (same order as the existing #14383 observe). `remove_shared_session_if` resolves survivors in **O(1)**: exactly one remaining owner → restore its wire alias + `reset_to_owner`; none → ownership-checked alias delete (#9679) + `forget`; two or more → stays ambiguous. The roster is trusted only when it actually recorded the removed owner (exact count step) and neither saturation latch is set. Untrusted state (saturated, or a session seeded by a bare map insert that never observed an owner) falls back to the exact pre-fix `.take(2)` scan and reseeds the roster when the scan can name every survivor (count < 2); a roster owner absent from `shared_sessions` fails closed.

## Regression / acceptance

- `remove_shared_session_if_resolves_wire_survivor_from_owner_index_15106` (debug + release): seeds 2,000 unrelated NAT'd rows, publishes a colliding DNAT pair through the real path, then removes via `remove_shared_session_if` — survivor restores and `is_unique_for`; a 3-owner leg drains 3→2 (stays ambiguous) →1 (resolves) →0 (roster empty, alias forgotten), all asserted with `wire_owner_count`.
- `remove_shared_session_if_nat_removal_cost_15106` (release-only, `#[ignore]`d manual probe, same shape as the #11299 churn probe): median `remove_shared_session_if` close of a DNAT victim at 1k vs 100k rows, bound 100k ≤ 2×1k. **Exercised:** 1k=1473ns vs 100k=1424ns, ratio **0.97** — passes. RED claim: pre-fix the mechanism cell fails (no roster APIs / scan-backed removal) and the probe's 100k median scales ~linearly; the probe was not re-run against a pristine-master release binary in this lane, so probe-RED is by construction/mechanism, not a measured pristine-binary run.
- Controls staying green: `shared_forward_wire*` (3), `publish_and_remove_shared_session_tracks*` (3), `remove_shared_session_if_*` including #10612/#13672 (3) — all pass. Full `session_glue::tests`: 253 passed / 2 failed — `flush_session_deltas_update_syncs_without_an_rt_flow_create_9412` and `shared_nat_displacement_counter_counts_collisions_not_republishes`, the same failures recorded on this branch before the fix (outside the changed mechanism).
- `cargo clippy --bin xpf-userspace-dp --tests` completed with the crate's pre-existing warning profile. Tree-wide `cargo fmt --check` is dirty on unmodified master under this toolchain; touched files were not wholesale-reformatted to avoid mass churn.

## Risk

Bounded to wire-key owner bookkeeping; no Go, wire-format, or neighbouring-path change. A future publish path that inserts into `shared_sessions` without `observe_wire_owner` degrades to the legacy scan + reseed rather than mis-resolving. New index memory: one roster per distinct wire key (inline 2, same 16k cap discipline as the alias index, fail-closed at saturation).

## Not in this PR

- NAT reverse-alias (`nat_ambiguities`) owner multiset — the issue scopes to the forward-wire leg only.
- Live-hardware validation of close latency at 100k rows (the release probe is the in-repo proxy).

Refs: #11299 (same class, closed), #14383 (introduced the scan).

Closes #15106

## PR #15466 — config: reject unknown SNMP community children (#15124) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15124-campaign`

## Summary

An unknown child of `snmp community <c>` — `client 10.0.0.0/8`, `clinets …`, `client-list-nam L`, or any other undeclared keyword — was skipped by both community walks in `compileSNMP` with no error or warning, so a one-letter typo in the operator-authored source ACL left the community answering **every** source (an empty allowlist reads as allow-all) on a green commit. Prior fixes (#4289, #4834, #5472, #5833, #5898, #8778, #9416, #10687) each repaired a named spelling; none added a default arm. This adds the default arm.

## What

- `pkg/config/compiler_system.go`: judge every community block on the same views the compiler reads (expanded children via `expandFlatRun`, statements chain-nested under `authorization`/`routing-instance`, and the Keys-packed run on the community node scanned with schema arity) against the schema-declared permitted set plus the inert `view`/`logical-system` knobs.
  - **Strict** (commit / commit-check): hard-reject naming the offending token — never the community name, which is a secret.
  - **Lenient** (load / peer-sync): warn and quarantine the affected community to deny-all, sticky across same-name merge blocks, exactly like #5833's malformed-token quarantine.
  - Also warn on both paths about a defined-but-unreferenced `snmp client-list` (the usual residue of a `client-list-nam` typo).
- Deliberately **not** `closedWorld` on the community schema: that flag inherits and was measured (#9265) to refuse the legal flat-set chain `community <c> client-list-name L authorization read-only` and the deliberate accept-with-advisory `view` knob. The gate is scoped to the community level and reads its permitted set from the schema, so a child declared later is permitted automatically.
- Ratchets: `/snmp/community` moves `stillFailOpen` → `coveredDownstream` in `instance_name_armed_9265_test.go` (same verdict `/snmp/trap-group` carries for its #2990 gate); the schema-blind baseline entry stays with the reason recorded.
- Docs: `docs/log/15124.md`, `docs/feature-coverage.md`.

## Validation

- New `pkg/config/snmp_community_unknown_15124_test.go`:
  - Strict cells for `client`/`clinets`/`client-list-nam`/`zzbogus` in flat-set, braced, and Keys-packed spellings — **RED on `origin/master`** (verified in a base worktree: compiled clean, allow-all) and GREEN after.
  - Lenient cell: boots, warns naming the token, quarantines the affected community to deny-all while a well-formed sibling keeps its policy.
  - Controls: the `clients` enforcement is unchanged (listed source admitted, unlisted denied), the #9416 flat-set chain still commits, a braced community with every declared child still commits, `view` keeps its advisory, and a view *named* `clients` is treated as a value.
- Neighbouring SNMP suites (`TestSNMP*`, trap-group, inert-knob, packed-community) pass; the `/snmp/community` 9265 row passes. Pre-existing failures in the 9091/9265 ratchets (BGP teardown containers, DHCP pool subnets, VRRP track-interface rows) were base-attributed on `origin/master`.
- RED evidence was also captured pre-fix via probe: strict compile of all three typo spellings returned no error and no warning, lenient allowed `8.8.8.8`.

## Risk

A community carrying a genuinely unmodelled Junos child now rejects at strict commit instead of silently ignoring it; the tolerant path still boots with a deny-all quarantine for that community only. Inert `view`/`logical-system` knobs keep their accept-with-advisory posture — no neighbouring behaviour changes.

Closes #15124

## PR #15469 — ipsec: reject name-only full match on partial-load recovery (#15141) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15141-campaign`

## Why
#14589 partial-load recovery treated a full NAME-set match from `ListLoadedConns` as "candidate loaded" and returned the candidate hashes. When charon refuses a changed existing connection (e.g. its new certificate fails to load), the connection stays loaded under its OLD content, so the loaded name set equals the rendered set while charon runs the prior generation. `prevConnHashes` adopted a rotation charon never loaded, `promoteConnNames` saw no change, and the SA established under the superseded PSK/auth was never torn down — the #10878 guarantee lost, including on a later loadable generation.

## What
- `recoverPartialLoad14589` (pkg/ipsec/manager.go): the name-only full-set shortcut is removed; the reported set is always re-filed and re-loaded. On a full-set match, the confirm step compares before/after loaded CONTENT (`loadedContentStale15141`) and a content change diverts to the existing true rollback, promoting the prior hashes so a later loadable generation tears the stale SA down.
- `parseListConnsRaw` (pkg/ipsec/list_conns.go): each loaded connection now carries `LoadedConn.Content`, a SHA-256 fingerprint of everything charon reports inside its `list-conn` event (auth subsections, proposals, selectors, endpoints). `LoadedConns.Equal` is deliberately unchanged.
- Summary-lied / raced-to-full recoveries (content unchanged by the verification reload) still promote the candidate hashes and tear down the stale SA on the same apply — pinned by a control cell.

Partial recovery now always pays the subset re-file + verification reload (one extra `--load-all`/`--list-conns` pair on that already rare path). ## PR #15470 — ha: require key confirmation before installing sync peer (#15140) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15140-campaign`

Why:
  Under Noise_NNpsk0 a session-sync msg1 is AEAD-tagged only over
  the prologue and the initiator ephemeral, so a passively captured
  60-byte syncMsgAuthHello re-verifies at a fresh responder with no
  PSK. The responder wrote msg2, split keys, recorded the peer as
  authenticated, and installed the connection — closing the real
  peer, sending it the sync stream, and (RG0 authority) the config
  including the control-link PSK.

What:
  Add a mandatory initiator key confirmation (syncMsgAuthConfirm
  type 44): HMAC-SHA256 under the initiator-to-responder frame key
  over the connect-confirm tag and the Noise channel binding. The
  responder returns a pending result after msg2 and only promotes
  via awaitInitiatorConfirm; recordAuthenticatedPeer and install
  now sit behind it. SessionSyncWireVersion bumps 2 -> 3 (flag
  day, #7163 discipline). NOT changed: the #6628 in-place upgrade
  (already confirmed) and unkeyed dual-accept behaviour.

Validation:
  New sync_auth_confirm_15140_test.go: replayed-msg1 install,
  silent post-msg2, and forged-confirm cells fail on origin/master
  with the replay displacing the legitimate conn; legitimate-pair
  control green before and after. Full pkg/cluster suite passes
  except TestInstallTableProducerToResendEndToEnd9752, identical
  on pristine origin/master. go vet clean.

Risk:
  Keyed pairs must run the same build on both nodes; the mixed-
  base gate refuses a 2/3 pair up front. A pending responder holds
  the connection only until the existing 3s handshake deadline.

Closes #15140

## PR #15473 — config: persist config-sync divergence across restarts (#15142) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15142-campaign`

## Why

SyncApply recorded a #9530 divergence only in process memory and durably deleted the unshared mark before `writeActive`, which degrades without failing. A restart after the heal — or after a failed heal write before the retry landed — discarded a partition-era commit with no alarm, reproducing #9530's own silent outcome.

## What

`unshared.json`'s record gains an optional `discarded` state. `recordSyncDivergenceLocked` persists it before the replacement is written and keeps the record; `reconcilePersistedUnsharedLocked`, called on SyncApply success and on the persist-retry heal, reduces it to a bare form (`digest == adopted`) that `Load` restores as the alarm but that can never re-classify. Pending records keep the discarded commit's digest, so a restart re-raises and a re-sync re-classifies. Local promotions and a different synced config clear the persisted record with the in-memory alarm. NOT changed: `classifySyncLocked`'s mark semantics for live marks, `NoteActiveSharedWithPeer`, or SyncApply's degrade-not-fail contract.

## Validation

New `divergence_persist_15142_test.go`: RED on base in 3 of 4 cells (restart-after-heal lost the alarm; mark deleted before a failed `writeActive`; retry-heal cell saw the same early delete), persisted-clear control passed. GREEN after the fix: all 4 #15142 cells and all existing #9530 cells pass; adjacent Commit/SyncApply/Load/Persist/Confirm/Rollback selection passes (126 tests). Full `pkg/configstore` suite exceeds the 240s test timeout in this environment on unmodified base as well (1037 tests listed).

## Risk

A persisted discarded record whose replacement never becomes durable stays pending and re-raises on restart by design; it is cleared by the next local promotion or a different synced config.

Closes #15142

source/destination/zone equality is unchanged. Regression cells

## PR #15477 — userspace-dp: reassemble fragmented WireGuard outers before decap (#15102) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15102-campaign`

Why:
A worker-decapped WireGuard record whose outer IP datagram was fragmented was lost: the first fragment was claimed and failed AEAD as a truncated record, and non-first fragments (protocol 255) went to the kernel, where transit inners drop as degraded. Any WG peer behind a smaller-MTU underlay hop with DF clear lost such traffic.

What:
Shim: host-executed `wg_fragment_stays_on_helper` keeps UDP tails (255/UDP, WG_RX armed) off every kernel-pass arm; degraded mode drops them with their head. Helper: the bounded #14645 reassembler now keys/rebuilds by upper-layer protocol (GRE 47 / UDP 17), patches the IPv6 Fragment next-header, and restores UDP ports in the completed meta, so GRE and WG datagrams sharing an outer identity cannot splice. `stage_wg_decap` offers WG fragments to the shared per-worker pool only after listener admission (heads via endpoint/zone/ownership gates, tails only against a buffered head); completed datagrams decap exactly once through ordinary `try_wg_decap`, buffered fragments recycle, refusals stay counted in `GRE_OUTER_FRAG_DROPS`.

Validation:
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 15102` at rebased head: 3 passed (real AEAD IPv4 head+tail decaps exactly once, byte-identical inner; stray tail creates no state; replay does not re-decap; shim truth table; IPv6 pool rebuild), 8714 filtered.
- RED on pristine origin/master: same test file fails to compile (no WgDecapStage/offer_for_protocol/predicate); head-alone try_wg_decap premise is None.
- Neighbouring: 14645 suite 4 passed; WG decap filter cells 13 passed.
- Shim verifier: candidate and pristine master both REJECTED on this host/kernel (pre-existing baseline, tracked .o untouched) — must be re-run where master passes before merge.

Risk:
Fragmented UDP tails to a WG-armed box now reach the worker instead of the kernel; only tails whose head was admitted to a configured listener are buffered, others keep ordinary fragment adjudication.

Closes #15102

## PR #15484 — userspace-dp: retry reinject accept errors instead of exiting (#15112) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15112-campaign`

## Why

The #9506 reinject submit and complete accept threads in `spawn_reinject_socket_servers` (`userspace-dp/src/server/reinject_9506.rs`) broke out of their loops on any non-`WouldBlock` accept error; the thread returned and the `UnixListener` moved into its closure was dropped. An idle EMFILE — descriptor/memory pressure with an empty backlog, where the kernel reserves the result descriptor before looking at the backlog — therefore deafened both sockets permanently. Every IPsec FORWARD flow using the #9506 adjudicated re-entry black-holed behind a healthy control socket until a helper restart that nothing triggers (A73-01). #9172 converted only the control and session loops to `accept_step`; these two were the residual.

## What

- Both reinject loops now decide through `lifecycle::accept_step` with `retry_unclassified = true`, exactly as the session loop does: `WouldBlock` keeps the previous 1 ms poll interval; EMFILE/ENFILE/ENOBUFS/ENOMEM retry on the shared 50 ms-doubling-to-1 s `AcceptBackoff` with one onset and one recovery journal line; unclassified errors log-and-continue; the `AcceptStep::Fail` arm (unreachable with `retry_unclassified = true`) sleeps at the backoff ceiling rather than spinning, mirroring the session loop.
- Each accepted connection is served under `catch_unwind` (the issue's optional serving wrap): a handler panic drops that one connection with a journal line and the accept loop continues, instead of unwinding the thread and dropping the listener.
- The peer-credential check and the inline, globally-serialized serving of each accepted connection are unchanged.
- NOT changed: `lifecycle.rs` (`accept_step`/`AcceptBackoff` reused as-is), the Go side (`pkg/nfqueue` already redials per reconnect), any neighbouring behaviour.

## Validation

- New regression cells in `reinject_9506_tests.rs` exercise the real spawned loops: lower the soft `RLIMIT_NOFILE` to just above the open-fd count, drain the remaining slots with `/dev/null` duplicates so the idle listeners' `accept()` returns EMFILE, release the pressure, then prove service — the submit cell's ANNOUNCE applies permit epoch 4242 to the fallback core; the complete cell receives the queued completion and acks it. A third cell pins both `accept()` results through `accept_step` with `retry_unclassified = true` (same textual-wiring shape as the #9172 lifecycle cell).
- RED on `origin/master` (`699145ac4e`, tests only): all 3 FAILED — `complete listener dead after idle EMFILE (accept loop exited): Connection refused`, submit cell likewise, wiring cell found zero `accept_step` calls.
- GREEN after the fix: `cargo test 15112 -- --test-threads=1` → 3 passed; full `reinject_9506` module → 93 passed; #9172 lifecycle accept-step cells stay green.
- Full `--bins` suite on the fixed tree: 8585 passed / 54 failed / 8 ignored. Every failure was reproduced on clean `origin/master` worktrees or traced to concurrent campaign merges landing on `origin/master` after this lane branched (wire-fixture `protocol_wire_v1.json` and shim-tally drift from #15095/#15103/#15438-era merges); none touches the reinject accept path.

## Risk

A genuine descriptor leak now leaves the reinject sockets retrying with backoff and a journal line instead of the threads exiting silently — the same posture #9172 chose for the control/session sockets. Recovering a helper wedged by a real leak remains #9651. No behaviour change outside the two cited accept loops.

Closes #15112

## PR #15488 — cluster: chunk DHCP lease full-sets below the sync frame cap (#15160) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15160-campaign`

Why:
queueDHCPLeaseSnapshot wrote the entire Kea lease set as one session-sync frame with no size check. Past maxSyncPayload (16 MiB, ~165k v4 leases) the receiver's receiveLoop refuses the header and returns, tearing down the connection that also carries sessions, IPsec SAs and config; the re-push on reconnect repeats the cycle and DHCP takeover protection silently stops (B03-01, residual of #14607).

What:
Additive chunk types syncMsgDHCPLeaseV4Chunk=45 / syncMsgDHCPLeaseV6Chunk=46 (no wire-version bump; old peers ignore unknown types, #14607 precedent). Sets that fit one frame keep the exact legacy syncMsgDHCPLeaseV4/V6 shape. Over-cap sets split lease records across sub-cap chunk frames (`sync_dhcp_chunk_15160.go`: {generation, index, total, totalLeases} envelope + standard lease bodies, authority trailer on the last chunk); the receiver admits chunks in full-set-seq order through the existing per-family guard, reuses the legacy decode + semantic/identity filters, and commits the assembled set atomically (held-set store + high-water + callback under dhcpApplyMu) only when every chunk has arrived. Unclosed/inconsistent generations never commit (#7175 posture); a committed legacy set discards pending assemblies; single records too large for any frame drop counted via MalformedRecordsDropped, never over-cap.

Validation:
New pkg/cluster/dhcp_lease_chunk_15160_test.go: RED on base 885446e (chunk symbols undefined; base sender emits one frame regardless of size), GREEN after — 260k-lease v4 and v6 sets (each >16 MiB encoded) cross as multiple frames all <= maxSyncPayload and the receiver holds every lease with authority metadata and exactly one complete-set callback; withheld-final-chunk commits nothing then completes; replayed chunk generation ignored, newer legacy set still applies; small set stays a single legacy-typed frame; malformed/total-inconsistent generations never disturb the held set. Message census tests updated. Full pkg/cluster suite green except TestInstallTableProducerToResendEndToEnd9752, which fails identically on unmodified origin/master 61cfe3a (base-attributed).

Risk:
A mixed-version pair loses only over-cap lease pushes (old receiver ignores the chunk types) instead of the whole sync connection. A live two-node over-cap lease population remains an operator-scale check.

Closes #15160

## PR #15489 — wireguard: reject bit-255 twins of small-order keys (#15132) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15132-campaign`

## Summary

The #14373 WireGuard small-order denylist compared exact bytes, so the seven bit-255 twins — each listed key with byte 31's top bit set, which X25519 masks off per RFC 7748 — passed the Go commit gate, the Rust hydrate gate, and the engine reconcile gate while yielding the identical all-zero static-static DH secret.

## Fix

Mask byte 31 (`k[31] &= 0x7f`) before the denylist comparison in:

- Go `isDegenerateWireguardKeyHex` (`pkg/config/compiler_validate_wireguard.go`) — covers local private key, peer public key, and explicit PSK commit gates.
- Rust `is_small_order_wg_peer_key` (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/wg/mod.rs`) — covers `is_degenerate_wg_key_bytes` (hydrate: local private key, peer key, explicit PSK) and engine `reconcile_peers` admission.

No new table entries: the 7 canonical entries plus masking cover all 14 encodings. A legitimate key with bit 255 set is a different genuine point and stays admissible; the repeated-byte leg, snow DH handling, and absent-PSK semantics are unchanged.

## Tests

- Go `pkg/config/compiler_validate_wireguard_twin_15132_test.go`: all 7 twin peer keys refused at the predicate and at strict commit (plus upper-case spelling), twin private key and twin explicit PSK refused without echoing key material; controls (canonical refused, bit-255-set valid keys commit, repeated-byte/near-miss unchanged).
- Rust `bit255_twins_are_small_order_15132`: each twin yields an all-zero DH under a clamped scalar (executable same-point pin) and is refused by both predicates; valid bit-255-set and near-miss controls stay admissible.
- Rust `reconcile_refuses_bit255_twin_peers_15132`: 7 twin peers refused and counted; valid peer and its bit-255-set variant installed.
- Rust `wg_endpoint_with_bit255_twin_key_is_dropped_15132`: twin peer / twin local private key / twin explicit PSK each drop the row at hydrate; valid fixture and bit-255-set valid peer still hydrate.

## Validation

- RED verified pre-fix (tests present, fix absent): Go twin cells fail for all 7 twins; all 3 Rust twin tests fail (engine reconcile installed 9 peers instead of 2). Re-verified by reverting only the production files with tests in place.
- GREEN: Go `TestWireguardBit255*` + full #14373 degenerate suite pass; Rust `bit255` (3), `14373` (3), `wg_endpoint` (9) pass on the rebased head.
- Base-attributed (identical with/without fix, untouched): 6 `pkg/config` WireGuard failures and 4 `userspace-dp` `wg_` failures on this base, all stale repeated-byte fixtures vs the #14373 gate. Full `pkg/config` suite has pre-existing unrelated failures on this base (not exercised as a gate; WireGuard-scoped failure sets diffed instead).

## Risk

A config whose key is a bit-255 twin of a small-order encoding now fails commit / drops at hydrate where it previously loaded but could never authenticate — the intended fail-closed delta. No legitimate key changes behaviour.

Docs: `docs/log/15132.md`.

Closes #15132

## PR #15494 — userspace-dp: force interface PAT without a synthetic flow key (#15109) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15109-campaign`

## Why

The #14367 forced-PAT arm in `match_source_nat_result_for_tuple_inner` built a synthetic `SourceNatFlowKey{src_ip:10.255.255.253, src_port:flow.src_port, ..flow}`, minted it, minted the real flow, then rolled the dummy back. If a real internal host at 10.255.255.253 already held that exact interface identity, the dummy mint re-entered the victim's live record (`reenter_interface_record_locked`) and the dummy rollback unlinked it — the victim's flows were refused when a peer owned its preserved port and its interface-identity ownership was silently deleted.

## What

- `PortAllocator::allocate_interface_identity_excluding(flow, translated_ip, holder, must_pat, excluded)`: `must_pat` skips the preserve-first arm; the `excluded` predicate is consulted for every PAT candidate so a peer-owned candidate is skipped rather than minted and rolled back. `allocate_interface_identity` delegates with `must_pat=false` and a never-excluding predicate (behaviour unchanged for all existing callers).
- `match_rules` computes `must_pat = peer_owns(flow.src_port)` and passes the existing `peer_owns` closure (combined pool/NAT64 overlap index) into the walk. The post-mint `peer_owns` verification + rollback of the real flow stays as a fail-closed backstop for races.
- No fixed-address `SourceNatFlowKey` literal remains in production code; no synthetic flow key is fabricated.

## Validation

- New regression tests in `tests_iface_nat64_14367` (through `build_forwarding_state`):
  - `victim_at_synthetic_address_survives_peer_owned_preserved_pat_15109` — **RED on base** (production fix stashed): FAILED with `live_flow_count` 0 vs 1, the dummy rollback deleted the victim's record exactly as claimed. **GREEN after fix**, including idempotent re-admit.
  - `real_host_survives_forced_pat_of_colliding_flow_15109` — control: victim + colliding `10.0.0.2` flow keep distinct live records (green on both sides; the collider's dummy key differs from the victim key by `src_ip`).
  - `synthetic_address_without_peer_collision_preserves_15109` — control: no peer collision still preserves.
- Post-rebase on `origin/master@280301bf9c`: 15109 tests 3/3, 14367 suite 10/10, `tests_iface` 37/37 (`cargo test --release --bin xpf-userspace-dp <filter>`).

## Risk

The PAT walk now consults the peer predicate per candidate under the interface allocator lock; the predicate only reads peer occupancy bitmaps and address-only identity maps — the same queries the caller already issued outside the lock. A racing peer mint between walk and post-mint check still fails closed with `InterfaceIdentityExhausted`, never publishing a duplicate.

Closes #15109
