## PR #15496 — upgrade: validate kernel-arm re-stamp before STOP and tolerate it on rollback re-flips (#15170) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15170-campaign`

Closes #15170

## Summary (B17-01)
Flip step 6d (the #6639 kernel-arm re-stamp) ran only inside `flip()`, after STOP and after 6a-6c repointed current/sbin/ExecStart. `loadKernelJournal` errors on any non-ENOENT read/parse failure, so a corrupt or unreadable `/var/lib/xpf/kernel-upgrade.state` failed the forward flip at 6d with the daemon down — and every rollback path re-ran the same 6d on its re-flip, failed again before `StartUnit`, and left the standalone daemon offline across the cut, auto-rollback, STOPPED resume and `--rollback`.

## Fix (both legs the issue names)
- **Pre-STOP probe**: `probeKernelArmRestamp`/`validateKernelArmRestampPreStop` (cutover.go, any journal not yet at STOPPED) read the kernel journal and, when a candidate is ARMED (shared `kernelArmRecordArmed`), `validateGateBin` the xpfd of both target and PreviousVersion. Failure refuses the cut with the daemon live. #6639's forward fail-closed cell is preserved — it just refuses before STOP. Nothing armed = byte-identical no-op.
- **Tolerant rollback re-flip**: `flip()` wraps a 6d-only failure in `restampError` after 6a-6c succeed; `rollback()`, `executeRollback` and `restoreStaleStoppedPrevious` use `flipToleratingKernelArmRestamp` to log and tolerate exactly that, leaving the stale arm record untouched (candidate boot gate refuses as pre-#6639: candidate lost, never an unvalidated promotion) so StartUnit runs. Genuine 6a-6c failures stay fatal.

## Validation
- New `kernel_arm_restamp_15170_test.go`: corrupt journal refused before STOP (no stop call, unitRunning, current untouched); corruption landing at STOP still ends `unitRunning=true` on 1.0.0 via auto-rollback; operator `RollbackTo` completes with a corrupt journal. All three **fail on base `61cfe3a483`** with the exact mechanism (verified by stashing only production files) and pass after the fix.
- `go test ./pkg/upgrade/ -count=1` PASS (full suite incl. 6639 fail-closed + nothing-armed controls); `go vet`/`gofmt` clean.
- Docs: `docs/log/15170.md`.

## Risk
Probe is read-only, no-op when nothing is armed. Tolerant rollback trades a lost kernel candidate for a running known-good daemon and cannot promote an unvalidated kernel (record byte-identical). Residual: corruption between probe and 6d on the forward leg is still found at 6d, but now ends with the daemon running on the previous version.

Never merge — campaign review gate applies.

Branch: `fix/15146-campaign`

Why:
  #14367 made every LOCAL mint ask the interface-domain question: a
  NAT64 or pool mint whose identity an interface-SNAT flow holds is
  refused, and an interface mint whose identity a pool/NAT64 peer holds
  is PAT'd away or refused. The three HA synced-reserve arms never
  asked it: the synced NAT64 reserve consulted only the deterministic
  tuple, statics, and the pool/NAT64 peer index; the synced pool PASS 1
  asked only peer-pool/statics; and the synced interface reserve never
  asked whether a pool/NAT64 peer owned the candidate. A standby could
  therefore import a translation onto an identity a local flow in
  another domain already holds — two live flows on one wire identity,
  with replies misdelivered first-installed-wins.

  nat64.rs: reserve_synced_nat64_port_unless_peer_owns now calls
  nat64_refuse_if_interface_owns (the prefix's build-synced
  iface_allocs plus the combined iface_overlap_owners, falling back to
  overlap_owners) first among its refusals, covering both the narrowed
  and the fallback-scan route through the one helper.
  synced.rs: reserve_synced_on_first_pool_owner takes iface_allocs and,
  on PASS 1 only, both arms also ask iface_owns_for_pool beside the
  peer/static checks, rolling back into the existing Refused outcome;
  PASS 2 is unchanged. reserve_synced_interface_identity takes the rule
  slice and asks peer_owns_for_interface over the combined index
  before booking, refusing on
  INTERFACE_SNAT_SYNC_IDENTITY_CONFLICT_DROPS.
  Tests: afxdp/tests_synced_iface_15146.rs drives every arm through
  build_forwarding_state (real egress E=172.16.80.8).
  NOT changed: local #14367 mint paths, PASS 2 semantics, the
  coordinator/worker bool contracts, release keying.

Validation:
  RED on origin/master 0b9d43a9c5: the 5 defect cells failed, 6
  controls passed.
  GREEN: cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp tests_synced_iface_15146 —
  11 passed. Neighbours: -- 14367 9021 8115 14674 — 47 passed, 0
  failed.

Risk:
  A synced import colliding with a local cross-domain identity is now
  refused instead of publishing a duplicate; that session will not

Branch: `fix/15164-campaign`

cluster: restore owner promptly on peer-failover abort (#15164)

Why:
After RequestPeerFailover aborted locally, the requester reported an
error and demoted, but the owner kept advertising StateSecondaryHold
under its #5079 lease and electRG's Peer transfer out rule promoted
the requester again on the next heartbeat. Under preempt the owner
then reclaimed the RG at lease expiry: ownership moved contrary to
the reported outcome, with an unrequested second RG move.

Add a reqID-bound abort frame (syncMsgFailoverAbort /
syncMsgFailoverBatchAbort, additive so an old peer ignores it and
the lease remains the fallback). abortRequestedPeerFailover(Batch)
records the aborted reqID and sends the abort outside m.mu;
AbortRemoteTransferOut on the owner restores promptly only when the
reqID matches the armed lease. electRG refuses Peer transfer out
while abortedPeerTransferReqID is present; the marker is cleared by
commitRequestedPeerFailover, notePeerTransferCommitted, the raw
heartbeat expiry in applyTransferCommitOverridesOnPeerStateLocked,
ResetFailover, FinalizePeerTransferOut, peer loss, and RG removal.
NOT changed: the #5079 lease, commit, and dual-resign paths.

New failover_abort_15164_test.go is RED on master (abort API absent;
owner hold plus heartbeat re-promotion asserted) and GREEN after:

fails, reproduced identically on pristine master (base-attributed).
Daemon wiring tests for the new hooks pass; go vet clean.

masks the original failover error; a crashed or partitioned

## PR #15504 — cli: execute flat config verbs from the gate lexer, fail closed on non-lexing lines (#15167) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15167-campaign`

Closes #15167

## Defect (V47-S1)
Local on-box CLI gated the raw config line with the config lexer (`AuthorizeConfigMutation`) but executed `set`/`delete`/`deactivate`/`activate` from `strings.Fields` tokens. The lexer stops at a non-ASCII byte (`TokenError`) and the gate judged only the lexed prefix, while unicode-aware `Fields` executed the full path — a restricted login class could mutate any path, including `system login class <self>`, by using a Unicode space (NBSP/EM/VT/FF/NEL/LS) after the verb or inside the path.

## Fix
- `pkg/config`: `lexConfigMutationLineStrict15167` reports whether the whole line lexed cleanly; `AuthorizeConfigMutation` (shared B23-01 decision) fails closed on a non-lexing gated line — including the verb-only prefix `set<NBSP>...` — for classes that configured `*-configuration` regexes. Unrestricted classes keep their ordinary errors.
- `pkg/config`: `ParseConfigMutationLine` exports the gate parse; the local CLI flat-verb arms derive their path from it and refuse non-lexing lines instead of re-splitting with `strings.Fields`. Quoted/tab/comment spellings execute exactly as adjudicated.

## Regression
`pkg/cli/unicode_space_authz_15167_test.go`: NBSP/EM/VT/FF/NEL/LS cells across all four verbs plus the own-class self-escalation spelling are denied with the candidate byte-identical; ASCII controls stay green (denied `system login` still denied, `set system services telnet` still allowed, quoted/tab allowed spellings reach the candidate). RED on `origin/master` dcba0c98be (cells ALLOWED, candidate mutated), GREEN after the fix. Adjacent `pkg/config` Authorize/Parse/TopUp/Split and `pkg/cli` dispatch/14716/14717/7172/14981/15082 selections pass. Pre-existing unrelated `TestUnitAliasVLANSplitDistinctUnitsClean_5878` fails identically on pristine base.

Docs: `docs/log/15167.md`.

## PR #15507 — cluster: seed bulk-send epoch from monotonic clock (#15182) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15182-campaign`

Why:
bulkSendNext was the one within-boot counter initGenState left at
zero, so a restarted daemon re-emitted bulk epoch 1 while a
surviving peer held bulkRecvEpoch at a dead-process high-water.
switched cannot fire on a daemon-only restart (the boot id changes
only on OS boot), so bulkStartStaleLocked refused the restarted
peer's authoritative re-prime between bulks: its pre-existing
sessions were never bulk-transferred and no BulkEnd reconcile ran.

What:
Store the MonotonicNanos seed into bulkSendNext in initGenState
beside syncEpoch, so the first epoch of a restarted process within
a boot is strictly newer than any epoch its predecessor emitted.
No receiver change; the #8966/#9174 guards and the #2198
cross-boot switched path are untouched. Three existing
sync_test.go cells asserted the literal first epoch 1; they now
assert the epoch the bulk actually drew. New
sync_bulk_epoch_restart_15182_test.go exercises the sender seed
and the end-to-end between-bulks acceptance plus controls.
NOT changed: the alternative receiver-side clear of
bulkRecvEpoch/bulkRecvIncarnation on peerIncarnation advance,
because the sender seed fixes the mechanism without weakening
the stale-start guard.

Validation:
TestBulkSendEpochSeededOnConstruction15182 and
TestRestartedPeerFirstBulkAcceptedBetweenBulks15182 fail on
origin/master (seed 0, epoch 1 refused between bulks at
high-water 7) and pass after the fix; controls for #9174 V015,
#8966 and #2198 F2 stay green. go test ./pkg/cluster/ -run
'8966|9174|9716' passed; the three migrated epoch cells pass;
full pkg/cluster suite passed except one timing-flaky
TestWaitForIdleTimesOutWhileQueueAdvances failure that passes
in isolation with and without the fix (count=5 both ways).

Risk:
Wire epochs become large monotonic-nanos values from the first
bulk; wire shape unchanged (8-byte little-endian) and receivers
only compare newer/equal, so mixed-version pairs are unaffected.

Closes #15182

## PR #15510 — userspace-dp: stop converting verdict-queue contention into denies (#15150) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15150-campaign`

## Why

`IpsecInnerVerdictQueue::try_post` returned `Err` on `try_lock` failure and counted E24 as if the queue were full. `post_worker_verdict` then posted an Uncertain deny, which terminalizes the still-Queued `ReinjectCore` entry and cancels the armed permitted write (armed before the post in the worker loop). Every worker takes the same verdict mutex every iteration, so permitted IPsec-inner traffic was lost at the lock-contention rate while the E24 "queue full" counter lied (the queue could be empty).

## What

- `IpsecInnerVerdictQueue::post` (new): blocking producer `lock()`; refuses only at true depth (`len >= IPSEC_INNER_VERDICT_QUEUE_DEPTH`), counting E24 only there.
- `try_post` keeps non-blocking semantics but counts contention on the new `IPSEC_INNER_VERDICT_QUEUE_CONTENDED_TOTAL`, never E24.
- `post_worker_verdict` / `requeue_worker_verdict`: at true-full, a `WouldPermit` is retained unchanged on the bounded fallback instead of becoming an Uncertain deny; `Deny` verdicts keep the fail-closed Uncertain terminal.
- `post_ipsec_inner_verdict` uses `post`.
- Contended counter plumbed Rust snapshot → `ProcessStatus` (additive, serde-defaulted, no wire bump) → Go `ProcessStatus` → Prometheus `xpf_userspace_ipsec_inner_verdict_queue_contended_total`; `protocol_wire_v1.json` regenerated.
- NOT changed: ingress `try_enqueue` E23 try-or-drop (socket producer never blocks; B12-03 is a separate issue), the consumer drain lock, the ReinjectCore permit join, all Deny handling.

## Validation

- 6 new `#15150` cells pass, 5× flake-clean: contended `try_post` counts contention not E24; blocking `post` delivers WouldPermit with the lock held (the issue's "yields WouldPermit with the lock held"); contended and true-full transport WouldPermits drain unchanged (E24 moves only at depth); Deny control stays Uncertain; armed retained WouldPermit still Proceeds to Written.
- RED at base: the contended state drained `Deny{VERDICT_UNCERTAIN}` with E24+1 (the old `contended_try_post_refuses_without_waiting` asserted exactly that).
- Adjacent: `ipsec_inner` suite 71 passed (incl. `verdict_queue_full_counts_e24_never_silent`); server counter projection/serialization cells pass; wire specimen regenerated with only the 3 contended-key additions.
- Go: `TestIPsecInnerStatusWireCensus10695`, `TestIPsecInnerStatusExportEndToEnd10695`, `TestCollectorDescriptorCoverage`, `TestEmitUserspaceDynamicBufferMetrics` pass (census 109→112: base already drifted +2 on origin/master, verified by stash, plus this series). Full `pkg/api` / `pkg/dataplane/userspace` failures are pre-existing NAT-pool/doc-guard/#15034 cells, base-attributed and untouched.

## Risk

A worker may now wait briefly on the verdict mutex (held only for bounded VecDeque push/drain) instead of dropping a permit; the consumer drains every worker tick. No other behavior change.

Closes #15150

## PR #15511 — frr: restore QNH metric overlay after failed reload (#15183) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15183-campaign`

## Why

`frr-reload.py --reload` deletes running lines absent from `frr.conf` — including the memory-only QNH `set metric N` overlay — *before* it reaches a line FRR rejects, then exits non-zero. Two return paths then skipped the restore:

- `reloadLocked`: when both `frr-reload.py` and the additive `vtysh -f` fallback failed, the hard-failure return ran before `reconcileQNHMetricOverlaysLocked`.
- `retryReloadOnce`: a failed degraded-retry attempt returned before its reconcile.

The backup static was exported into OSPF at the default external cost — tying with or beating the primary exporter network-wide — for as long as the rejected line persisted.

## What

- `pkg/frr/manager.go`: run `reconcileQNHMetricOverlaysLocked` on both failure returns. In `reloadLocked` a reconcile error is joined (`%w (additionally... %w)`) so the vtysh/primary causes and the #9947 pytools-missing classification stay `errors.Is`-visible and the hard failure still propagates. In `retryReloadOnce` a reconcile failure only logs; the attempt still returns failed and the episode stays degraded.
- Correct the stale lifecycle claims (QNH reconcile only after a successful load) in `commitManagedSection` / `noteReloadOutcomeLocked`, `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_routing.go`, and the README lifecycle bullet. No QNH pre-clear was added.
- `pkg/frr/qualified_nexthop_metric_failed_reload_15183_test.go`: a stateful executor models a load replacing ospfd state with the metric-free file state (delete-before-fail). Both defect arms assert ospfd keeps metric 10; controls assert the fallback-success path, error-cause visibility, and a later converging retry.
- `docs/log/15183.md`.

## Validation

- RED on `origin/master` (0020495f5f): both tests fail with `ospfd route-map xpf-qnh-static-... sequence 10 metric = 0, false; want 10, true`.
- GREEN after fix; adjacent QNH/reload tests pass under `-race`.
- Full `go test ./pkg/frr/`: only 4 pre-existing BGP failures, reproduced identically on pristine `origin/master` (0c468f7f4a) — base-attributed.

## Risk

A reconcile failure on the hard-failure path now surfaces joined to the reload error (never replacing it). The real-FRR live criterion rides the root-gated live QNH harness, which runs 3-of-4 failing identically on pristine master in this sandbox (pre-existing environment failure) and was not used as evidence here.

Closes #15183

DNAT, NPTv6 and NAT64 for such packets; the XDP shim passes

translate; transit NDP keeps worker FIB/policy adjudication.

flowless_base_resolution NDP bypass makes the main cell fail;
on base the pre-routing call returns Translated with the
internal rewrite. The flowless neighbour filter shows 4
pre-existing failures that reproduce identically with both
production gates disabled.

Risk:

validation and worker host-inbound gates still apply on the
LocalDelivery legs.

## PR #15514 — upgrade: no-op same-version re-run of already-live committed version (#15186) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15186-campaign`

Closes #15186

## Why
A bare re-run of `xpfd upgrade` (or `--rolling`) when the staged version was already live and committed performed a full same-version cut: STOP/START of xpfd (plus `ForceSecondary` on HA), replacement of `.<ver>.dbsnap`, and a commit stamp `{version:<ver>, predecessor:<ver>}` that the reader rejects — breaking rollback to the real predecessor. A VERIFY failure deleted the live snapshot, and the neighbouring refusal advised `dpkg-reconfigure xpf`, which always mints a new generation and is refused again.

## What
- INIT (`cutover.go`): when `stagedVer ==` live `current`, require `.srcgen` equality with the pinned generation, a valid committed stamp, and byte-identical managed binaries (`mismatchedManagedBinary`); then return `already at <ver>; nothing to do` before any journal/snapshot/STOP. Otherwise refuse pre-PREFLIGHT with re-version guidance only. Sanctioned first-cut retry falls through to a real cut; the no-op mints no committed-cut evidence (#12143).
- `rolling.go`: same check via `alreadyAtStagedVersion()` before `ForceSecondary`; in-flight journals still resume through the inner `Run`.
- `commit_stamp.go`: never write `Predecessor == Version` (defence in depth).
- `cleanupFailedVerifyCopy`: dbsnap removal guarded by `ver != cur && ver != j.PreviousVersion`.
- Dropped `dpkg-reconfigure` realign advice from both refusal sites and `docs/in-place-upgrade.md`; documented the already-live re-run.
- Updated `TestPreflipFailedRunInvalidatesEarlierEvidence12143` to stage a new 5.0.0 for its verify-rejected run (re-running live 4.0.0 is now a no-op by design; assertions unchanged).

## Validation
- New `same_version_rerun_15186_test.go`: RED on `origin/master` (stop/start on re-run, dpkg-reconfigure advice, live dbsnap deleted, ForceSecondary called, self-predecessor stamp rejected), GREEN after fix (no stop/start, dbsnap byte-identical, stamp/predecessor preserved, no journal).
- `go test ./pkg/upgrade/ -count=1`: PASS. `go vet ./pkg/upgrade/`: PASS.

## Risk
Confined to the `stagedVer == prev` decision point, the stamp self-predecessor case, and the verify-cleanup snapshot guard. Legacy unstamped same-version live dirs under a pinned generation now refuse fail-closed with re-version guidance.

## PR #15515 — ha: gate kernel self-recovery on drain start and consume its lease (#15181) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15181-campaign`

Why: self-recovery treated ANY expired kernel-roll lease naming this node as a crashed-roll fingerprint, with no age bound, and never removed the lease after acting. A lease left by a crashed or transport-lost roll persisted on /var/lib/xpf, so about 2 minutes after every later ForceSecondary (ISSU) or rolling drain it ran ResetAllFailover against the operator intent — a drained node re-entered election and, with preempt, could reclaim primary during a maintenance window.

What: Tick now requires the expired lease to postdate the current drain (ExpiresAt after the earliest ManualFailoverAt, via the new Manager.LocalDrainedSince exposed on SelfRecoveryCluster and the daemon adapter); a stale or unknown-start drain fails closed. Before ResetFailover, Tick consumes exactly the authorizing lease under the orchestrator kernel-roll.lock flock, only when node and expiry still match, so it cannot re-fire or delete a successor lease. verifyAndPromote now ClearRollLease on PROMOTE, as REVERT/discard already did. NOT changed: the crashed-roll recovery cell, active/other-node/missing-lease no-ops, and the ARMED gate.

Validation: new 15181 cells RED on base (stale lease reset=1, zero drain start reset, lease left after recovery, promote 0 clears) and GREEN after the fix; go test ./pkg/upgrade/ PASS (full suite); pkg/cluster neighbours 15181/13222 PASS; go vet clean. Full pkg/cluster has one pre-existing failure (TestInstallTableProducerToResendEndToEnd9752) also failing on clean origin/master 53419c6cf2.

Risk: a crashed roll whose drain never stamped ManualFailoverAt now fails closed (stays drained for the operator) instead of recovering; all current drain setters stamp it. Consumption takes the flock non-blockingly, so a live orchestrator is never blocked or deleted.

Closes #15181

## PR #15517 — userspace-dp: retire dead workers from IPsec-inner routing (#15149) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15149-campaign`

## Summary
The 1 Hz dead-worker sweep retired NAT, steering, and V_min holdings but never called `IpsecInnerWorkerTransport::retire_worker`. The router kept hashing IPsec-inner flows to the dead worker; its 128-deep queue accepted admits nothing drains, then refused them as WORKER_QUEUE_FULL, and admitted requests completed only by Go ack timeout.

## Fix
- Dead branch of `retire_selected_worker_holders` (`coordinator/status.rs`): `retire_worker(id)` then `join_worker_after_termination(id)`, delivering reaped requests' terminal Deny verdicts to the completion core.
- `ipsec_inner_queue.rs`: retire/join record a Deny verdict (stage `d11_worker_dead`, reason `SUBMIT_UNAVAILABLE`) per terminalized descriptor, only when the tombstone stale-claim wins; drained via new `take_reaped_terminal_verdicts`.

## Validation
- New `dead_worker_sweep_retires_ipsec_inner_worker_15149`: RED on base (live_count stays 2 after sweep), GREEN with fix. Adjacent `worker_transport_*`, `retire_dead_worker_holders_*` cells green.

## PR #15518 — config: make compare surfaces order-aware and duplicate-aware (#15168) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15168-campaign`

## Why
Every compare surface was order-blind and duplicate-blind (B24-01): `diffNodes` keyed siblings by `KeyPath` into a map (last duplicate wins), `nodesEqual` matched children through a map without comparing order, and `CommitDiffSummary` sorted flat set lines before counting. An `insert` reordering first-match policies rendered as `[no changes]` even though which policy wins changed; with repeated `from-zone/to-zone` containers the removed stanza shown was the wrong policy.

## What
- `pkg/config/ast_format.go`: sibling lists diffed as sequences — pair by `KeyPath` with content-equal duplicates first, leftovers in occurrence order; pairs off the LIS of new indices render as moved `-/+`; `nodesEqual` compares children positionally (canonical `match`/`from`-before-`then` only). All four compare entry points (`FormatCompare`, `FormatCompareRedacted`, `ShowCompare(Rollback)`, redacted twins) inherit this.
- `pkg/configstore/store_commit.go`: `CommitDiffSummary` counts via LCS over ordered `FormatSet` lines; a moved line = 1 removed + 1 added, duplicates positional.
- Regression tests + `docs/log/15168.md`. No compiled-config/commit/enforcement change.

## Validation
RED on base `59ebead236`: `TestFormatCompareReorder15168`, `TestFormatCompareDuplicateContainerRemoval15168`, `TestFormatCompareNodesEqualOrder15168`, `TestCommitDiffSummaryReorder15168` failed (empty diff/summary).
GREEN: all pass + identical-order controls; adjacent green (`TestInactive_CompareShowsDeactivate`, `TestCommitDiffSummaryDuplicateLines_13231`, `TestShowCompare*`, redacted-compare tests); `go vet` clean. Full `pkg/config`/`pkg/configstore` suites timed out at 280s under box-wide load (~100, sibling lanes) with no failures observed — main agent should re-run full suites at merge time.

## Risk
Pure reorder now shows the moved stanza on both arms instead of `[no changes]` — that visibility is the fix.

Closes #15168

## PR #15521 — config: defer shifted rollback save when sync persist fails (#15190) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15190-campaign`

Why:
SyncApply pushes the old active onto history, promotes the synced tree in memory, and on a pre-rename writeActive failure continued to saveRollbackFiles unconditionally. The sidecar binds via rollbackActiveBindingForWrite (in-memory tree hash plus the old file identity), so a restart before the persist retry healed saw a generation mismatch and refused every rollback slot; the next save tombstoned the ladder. The standby silently lost its whole rollback history with RollbackHistoryDegraded false.

What:
SyncApply records whether it shifted history and whether the write persisted / was post-rename-visible. On a pre-rename failure with a shift it sets rollbackPersistDelayed and skips saveRollbackFiles, leaving the on-disk slots/sidecar describing the old active so a pre-heal restart yields the readable pre-sync ladder. The persist retry saves the shifted ladder once the synced config is durable (the #14578 rebind still covers the no-shift case). A successful saveRollbackFiles clears the flag. Post-rename failures and successful syncs save immediately, unchanged.

Validation:
New sync_rollback_binding_15190_test.go: degraded-restart cell RED on base (all slots refused, rollback slot 1 unreadable), GREEN after fix (pre-sync ladder readable); retry-heal keeps [C,B,A]; post-rename and successful-sync controls pass. Adjacent 14578/5473/DegradesNotFails suites pass. Full configstore suite exceeded the 300s harness timeout without failures before the kill — please run to completion.

Risk:
A deferred save whose retry-heal slot write fails sets RollbackHistoryDegraded via saveRollbackFiles, as with any rollback persist failure. No behaviour change outside the failed-sync rollback save.

Closes #15190

## PR #15524 — userspace-dp: reseed queue_vtime on vacate re-entry (#15154) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15154-campaign`

userspace-dp: reseed queue_vtime on vacate re-entry (#15154)

Why:
The #4254 frontier reseed ran only at FlowFairState construction. A
shared_exact worker whose last bucket drained vacated its V_min slot
but kept its frozen queue_vtime; on re-entry its first post-settle
publish became the cross-worker V_min, so busy peers failed the V_min
gate, burned the hard-cap, and armed suspension — idle/return traffic

## PR #15525 — userspace-dp: decline TCP-MD5/TCP-AO in segmentation and MSS clamp (#15119) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15119-campaign`

Why: both segmentation builders copied the full TCP header, including a
kind-19 MD5 or kind-29 AO option, onto every output segment while
rewriting seq/lengths/checksums, so each segment failed the receiver's
authentication check, every segment was dropped, and no PTB was sent;
BGP-MD5/TCP-AO sessions stall on the first oversize segment. The
dispatch admission gate admitted on length alone, never reaching the
PTB arm. Sibling: clamp_tcp_mss rewrote the MSS of a TCP-AO SYN or an
IPv6 AH-protected SYN, invalidating its MAC/ICV.

What: shared tcp_header_has_auth_option walk in frame/tcp.rs (kinds
19/29); both segmentation builders (frame copy path + tx prepared-TX
twin) and forwarded_tcp_may_need_segmentation decline authenticated
datagrams so DF/IPv6 traffic reaches compute_forwarded_egress_ptb and
no-DF traffic forwards whole; clamp_tcp_mss declines AO/MD5/AH SYNs.
Regression cells for gate, both builders, PTB emission (Frag-Needed
MTU 1400), NOP control segmentation, and clamp no-ops. Log in
docs/log/15119.md.

Validation: cargo test --bins 15119: 5 passed GREEN; with production
guards reverted 4/5 fail (RED), NOP control passes. clamp suite 19
passed; admission suite 8 passed both sides; tcp_segmentation/ptb
subsets identical branch vs pristine base (2+1 pre-existing WG
failures). Full --bins pre-rebase: 8594 passed, 54 failed
(pre-existing families), 8 ignored. Post-rebase tip does not compile
its test harness due to a pre-existing origin/master error in
afxdp/mirror/mod_tests.rs (MirrorConfigSnapshot missing fields from
#15114/#15113), untouched by this change.

Risk: authenticated oversize TCP now depends on PMTUD instead of
local segmentation, matching the existing AH disposition; no other
behaviour change.

Closes #15119

## PR #15530 — ipsec: terminate demoted RG SAs on failover (#15194) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15194-campaign`

Why:
On RG demotion xpf removes the VIP but never terminates the IKE/CHILD SAs anchored on it. The stale SAs survive in charon (MOBIKE defers, and a non-MOBIKE peer generates no IKE traffic), so on failback `reinitiateIPsecSAs` -> `swanctl --initiate --child` is refused with "not establishing CHILD_SA ... due to existing duplicate", and the returning owner keeps encrypting with SPIs the peer already deleted. The black hole is bounded only by DPD, the next rekey, or peer initiation — on every planned failover/failback, preempt, and monitor-driven demotion without reboot.

What:
- `clearRethServicesForRG` (data RG loss) and the genuine-demotion arm of `applyRG0OwnershipTransition` (RG0 secondary) launch `terminateDemotedRGIPsecSAs(rg)`: reads the LOCAL live SA set, keeps names attributed to the lost RG via the #9139/#9511 `ipsecConnRedundancyGroups` attribution (all candidates must equal the lost RG; unanchored names default to RG0), terminates each. RG0 gated on the existing `genuineDemotion` verdict (initial-secondary seating terminates nothing); data-RG sweep not gated on `IPsecSASync` (local hygiene). Failed live-SA read terminates nothing rather than guessing a connection another RG may own.
- `reinitiateIPsecSAs` belt: before initiating, terminate any peer-advertised name still live locally, so a raced/failed demotion terminate cannot leave a duplicate for charon to refuse.
- New `ipsec.Manager.TerminateConnection`: resolves the IKE connection owning the named SA from `--list-sas` (`ConnectionName`; gateway-named since #15024, children carry VPN names) and issues `swanctl --terminate --ike <conn> --force`. No matching live SA = no-op; failed list returned, never guessed. Test seam `Daemon.ipsecTerminateFn` mirrors `ipsecInitiateFn`.
- NOT changed: advertise gate, `ownsIPsecConn` initiate scoping, SA-sync wire format, `terminateRemovedConns` debt machinery. Docs: `docs/log/15194.md`, `pkg/ipsec/README.md`.

Validation:
- RED: daemon suite failed to build on unpatched master (unknown field `ipsecTerminateFn`); `go test ./pkg/ipsec/ -run 15194` failed `m.TerminateConnection undefined`.
- GREEN: `go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run 15194` 6/6; `go test ./pkg/ipsec/ -run 15194` 2/2; `go test ./pkg/ipsec/ -count=1` full suite green.
- Daemon 9139/9511/RG targeted suites green except `TestApplyIPsecTrackedRecordsOnlyALoadedGeneration9511`, `TestConfigSyncPeerConnectUsesRG0Reconciler`, `TestSyncConfigToPeerGatesOnRG0AuthorityAtPushTime` — pre-existing, base-attributed on clean `origin/master` worktrees. Full daemon suite exceeded the 300s lane timeout twice (targeted suites run instead). On-cluster run-v63 (MOBIKE/non-MOBIKE x trap/start, failback rc=0) is lab-bound, not exercised here.

Risk:
Demotion now forced-terminates exactly the lost RG's IKE SAs; a colliding multi-candidate name spanning a surviving RG is left to the takeover belt. `--force` skips the delete-ack wait by design (VIP already gone). Async sweep races are covered by the belt.

Closes #15194

Branch: `fix/15133-campaign-pub`

Why:
Inbound persistent-NAT lookups passed `rule.from_zone` alone, so an interface-, routing-instance- or global-scoped rule-set (empty `from_zone`) collapsed to `PERSISTENT_NAT_EGRESS_UNSCOPED`, where any grant bucket admits. Two non-zone siblings sharing one pool therefore merged grants: a permissive `any-remote-host` sibling widened a strict `target-host-port` binding to arbitrary remotes inbound (#14322 residual, A91-07). A scoped lookup also returned `Denied` for leases the rule never minted on, so the first sibling in snapshot order vetoed the minting sibling.

What:
- `nat/allocator.rs`: `persistent_egress_scope_v2` folds the rule's six authored scope fields plus the packet zone pair (empty authored zones replaced by the packet's resolved zone), `1`-tagged against the v1 fold; new production entry `persistent_inbound_lookup_for_rule`; leases without the lookup's bucket answer Miss, not Deny.
- `nat/source/mod.rs`: `SourceNatRule::persistent_rule_scope` — the single key both mints and lookups use.
- `nat/source/match_rules.rs`, `nat/source/synced.rs`: mint sites record under the rule scope.
- `afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs`, `policy_revalidation.rs`: admission and mirror lookups pass the rule + packet pair; revalidation resolves the internal zone from session metadata.
- New `nat::tests_persistent_nonzone_15133` (interface/global/RI siblings); #14322 cells exercise the production rule-keyed lookup. NOT changed: lease identity/tuple sharing (#9389), remote cap, wire `egress_scope` encoding, NAT64 unscoped behaviour.

Validation:
- RED on base `85433e0906` (probe with pre-fix lookup spelling): all 3 new cells fail, `Permitted` where `Denied` required.
- GREEN: `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 15133` = 3/3; `-- 14322 14802 14315 15133` = 12/12.
- Main agent to run: full `nat::` suite + Go snapshot/lease suites before merge.

Risk:
Fail-closed only for the cited merge. Mixed-version HA peers fold v1 vs v2 differently until both run this build; standby may miss (fail closed) rather than merge grants during upgrade. Pre-fix v1 buckets expire with their leases.

Closes #15133

Branch: `fix/15205-campaign`

Closes #15205.

## Why
The #3751 strict `within`/`trigger` validator read only the first `trigger` sibling (`FindChild("trigger")` in `validateEventWithinClause`) while `compileEventOptions` applies **every** sibling last-wins (`FindChildren("trigger")`, #6771). A hierarchical clause such as `within 60 { trigger on 3; trigger on typo; }` or `within 60 { trigger on 3; trigger until 5; }` therefore committed clean on the strict path — the compiler silently dropped the bad later count or filled the contradictory field from it (A14-05 strict-gate escape; runtime #3751 belt fails closed, so no fail-open).

## What
- `validateEventWithinClause` (`pkg/config/event_options_within.go`) aggregates `parseEventTriggerSpecs` over `w.FindChildren("trigger")` and runs the unchanged unknown-keyword, both-on-and-until, and count presence/range checks over the aggregate; message texts unchanged. A bare empty `trigger;` sibling is rejected rather than masked by an earlier valid sibling (parity with a lone empty trigger).
- Same-keyword valid re-sets still pass and keep the compiler's #6771 last-wins value; the compiler is untouched. Lenient load/peer-sync downgrade preserved.
- New hierarchical RED/GREEN regression `pkg/config/event_options_within_15205_test.go` (flat `set` merges repeated values under one node, so only the hierarchical shape exercises this defect) + `docs/log/15205.md`.

- `TestEventWithinSecondTriggerSiblingRejected15205` (8 rows: non-numeric/out-of-range count, contradictory `until`/`on`, unknown keyword, missing count, empty `trigger;`, block-form sibling) — RED on `origin/master` (all accepted), GREEN after.

- #3751 controls stay green (`TestEventWithinValid/Rejected/BothOnUntil/Lenient*`); `go vet` clean.
- Pre-existing: #6771 duplicate-trigger tests fail identically on `origin/master` (stale `ev1` name vs the #14660 known-event gate) — verified with the production change reverted; the new control re-pins that behaviour with a valid event name.

time.Duration(math.MaxUint32)*time.Second. The 15071
infinite fixture constructs the wire value; README and
docs/log/15224.md record the cohort. NOT changed: the mixed
ia-na+ia-pd pdRefused commit arm, silence keep-and-retry,
and the REBIND matcher binding.

fails to build (undefined errV6PDRefused). GREEN:

infinite never decays/expires, finite control decays;

## PR #15546 — config: re-emit [edit] header after recursed siblings in compare (#15169) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15169-campaign`

Closes #15169

## Defect (B24-02)
`diffNodes` in `pkg/config/ast_format.go` printed its `[edit <path>]` header once, before its rendering loop. After a recursed sibling printed a deeper header, subsequent parent-level +/- lines inherited that unrelated context (e.g. an added/removed policy shown inside another policy's `then`). At the root no `[edit]` header was printed at all.

## Fix
Confined to `diffNodes`: each level now collects its ordered sections first (own lines rendered into buffers, modified block pairs as recursion arms — preserving the #15168 removals-first/new-order rendering), then emits them with the level's header printed lazily immediately before each run of own lines — bare `[edit]` at the root — re-armed only when a recursion actually produced output. A header with no lines under it is never printed; the all-recursable fast path is untouched. Rendering-only; no fail-open path is involved.

## Regression & controls
New `pkg/config/compare_header_15169_test.go` (5 cells): removed `deny-x` and added `new-x` policies governed by `[edit security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust]` rather than the recursed `keep` policy's `[edit ... policy keep then]` header; root addition opening with bare `[edit]`; single-header control; no-duplicate/no-empty-parent-header control.

- RED on current `origin/master`: addition cell fails (new-x governed by the deep header) and root cell fails (no `[edit]`); controls pass. On the pre-#15168 base the original removal probe also rendered under the deep header.
- GREEN after the fix. Controls green: all four #15168 order/duplicate compare cells, `TestInactive_CompareShowsDeactivate` (#2008 H1), configstore `Compare` suite incl. redacted/rollback compares, config format/redact/parser subsets (156 cells).
- Full `pkg/config` suite does not complete on this host under multi-lane load (times out in the spelling-differential gate on fixed and pristine trees alike); five `TestCompile*` cells fail identically on pristine `origin/master` — pre-existing, unrelated.

Log: `docs/log/15169.md`.

## PR #15550 — userspace-dp: meter inline input policer only from deferring term (#15189) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15189-campaign`

## Why

An input three-color policer on an inline-metered (host-bound / Stage-11) path was charged twice per packet whenever its filter contained any `routing-instance` term, including one the packet never matched. `evaluate_non_pbr_input_filter` gated its routing-bearing remainder on the filter-wide `affects_route_lookup` flag (plus a family-wide policer flag) and re-walked from term 0, so router-bound traffic (IKE/ESP reinjection, LocalDelivery hits on per-packet filters) was policed at about half the configured CIR/burst. D01-01, a regression of #14120 persisting past #14857.

## What

- The non-routing walks (`evaluate_filter_ref_non_routing_counted_v4/v6`) now record the term index they deferred at in the new `FilterResult::deferred_at_routing_term` field.
- The inline caller runs the routing-bearing remainder only when the walk actually deferred, via the new `routing_bearing_remainder_policer_drop_from(.., from_term)`, which threads `from_term` through the runtime TX-selection walks as a term slice (`from_term = 0` on every pre-existing full walk, zero extra allocation).
- A policer on the deferring routing term (or a later term that walk reaches before terminating) still meters exactly once; terms already metered by the non-routing walk are never re-walked; a packet that never defers pays no remainder.
- NOT changed: the tunnel outer gate keeps its full from-0 walk (its input evaluation passes `DeferToTxSelection`, so nothing there was charged twice), transit deferral, counter ownership, and the #14659 fall-through preservation.
- `userspace-dp/src/filter/README.md` (#14120 section) and `docs/log/15189.md` document the fix.

## Validation

- New regression cells in `poll_descriptor/filter.rs`: `stage11_input_policer_not_double_charged_with_unmatched_routing_term_15189` (packet 1: Accept, green=1, drop=0; packet 2: Discard), `inline_next_term_policer_before_matched_routing_term_charges_once_15189`, `stage11_input_policer_after_matched_routing_term_not_charged_15189`, and `local_delivery_input_policer_with_routing_term_charges_once_14120` (the `*_14120` cell whose filter carries a routing-instance term).
- RED: forcing the remainder start index back to term 0 (pre-fix behaviour) fails `inline_next_term_policer_before_matched_routing_term_charges_once_15189` — `first packet must pass` with left `Discard`, right `Accept`.
- GREEN: `cargo test --bins -- 15189 14659 14120` passes 11/11, including all pre-existing #14120 cells and the #14659 cells (`pbr_input_term_enforces_three_color_policer_fc_and_dscp_on_runtime_tx_selection_14659`, `pbr_input_term_policer_replay_contains_pbr_term_14659`, `non_routing_walk_preserves_next_term_policer_drop_before_pbr_14659`). `cargo check --bins` clean.
- Base-attributed: the full test binary does not compile on pristine `origin/master` (460c8c469a) — `afxdp/mirror/mod_tests.rs:1032` omits the `ingress_vlan_id`/`unit_scoped` fields added by #15113/#15114 (E0063, verified via `git show origin/master:...`). Unrelated to this change; targeted runs used a temporarily completed literal, reverted before commit. **Main agent: run the full `--bins` suite and attribute/fix the mirror compile error before merging.**

## Risk

Bounded to inline-metered host-bound / Stage-11 input-filter evaluation. Transit packets still meter exactly once in the TX-selection leg; a policer on or after a matched routing-instance term still meters exactly once via the sliced remainder. No wire, counter, or `show` behaviour change outside the double-charge mechanism.

Closes #15189

## PR #15552 — networkd: order preferred address first within its subnet (#15222) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15222-campaign`

The Junos `preferred` leaf was inert for source selection: networkd ordered only `PrimaryAddress` first and gave the preferred address `PreferredLifetime=forever` in an `[Address]` section. That lifetime never chooses an IPv4 source and does not order same-subnet IPv6, so locally originated traffic used the first-added address in the subnet. `generateNetwork` now runs `orderPreferredFirstPerSubnet` after primary ordering and the per-family DHCP gate: the preferred address moves to the front of its masked-CIDR subnet group, preserving all other relative order, rendering as plain `Address=` lines with no `PreferredLifetime` section. `family inet` preferred is now first-wins like `inet6`. ## PR #15553 — userspace-dp: honour designated primary address in snapshot picks (#15155) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15155-campaign`

## Why

The Go snapshot builder sorts a unit's addresses by the address string and `InterfaceAddressSnapshot` carried no marker for the operator's `primary` designation, so Rust `pick_interface_v4/v6` and Go `pickInterfaceSnapshotV4/V6` returned the lexicographically-first address. On any multi-address egress unit, `primary_v4/v6` — and therefore every `source-nat interface` flow — used an address the operator did not choose (e.g. `10.0.0.10/24` over designated `10.0.0.9/24`).

## What

- Carry `primary` on `InterfaceAddressSnapshot` (Go `Primary` / `primary,omitempty`; Rust `primary` serde-default, pinned in `protocol_wire_v1.json`), marked by `buildConfiguredAddressSnapshots` from the unit's `PrimaryAddress` and overlaid by `mergeInterfaceAddressSnapshots` onto live rows.
- Both pick pairs scan the full family: marked primary wins, else first non-link-local, else first of family — bit-identical for unmarked snapshots.
- `ProtocolVersion` 53 → 54 in lockstep (Go + Rust `control.rs`); shape pin, contract golden, wire fixture regenerated.

## PR #15562 — cli: fix policy simulator / shadow-check fidelity cohort (#15238) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15238-campaign`

Closes #15238

## Cohort (A55-01, A55-02, A55-03) — all in `pkg/policymatch`

**A55-01 — shadow pass names the wrong coverer within the single-wildcard tier.**
`analyzeCrossTierGlobalShadowing` enforced tier precedence (#12893) but iterated the lexically sorted `pairs` inside tier 1. `("any","untrust")` sorts before `("trust","any")`, so a `trust→any` deny authored first lost to an `any→untrust` permit and a scoped global was reported REDUNDANT instead of SHADOWED. The tier walk now iterates `cfg.Security.Policies` (authored order), so probe row 1 reports `policy "scoped-permit" is SHADOWED … (e.g. "to-any-deny")`; flipped authored order still reports REDUNDANT naming the permit (control).

**A55-02 — simulator permits flows the helper drops at transit martian gates.**
`routeDropClass` was destination-only and missed most of the Rust sets (`addr_class.rs` `transit_src_is_martian`/`transit_dst_is_martian`, gated pre-policy in `poll_descriptor`). It is replaced by one shared `transitMartianClass` mirroring both sets plus `routeDropClassForQuery` (source first, then destination). Probe rows now report `RouteDropBeforePolicy=true` for martian sources (0/8, 127/8, 169.254/16, 224/4, 240/4, directed broadcast; `::`, `::1`, ff00::/8, fe80::/10) and for the previously missed destination classes (`this-network`, `link-local`, `reserved`; unspecified dst keeps its established `unspecified` spelling). Advisory-only — Matched/Action/DefaultUsed unchanged; host-bound queries exempt; nil sides unclassified.

**A55-03 — global scoped only to a quarantined zone reported as matching.**
`globalScopeSetMatches` tested raw `cfg.Security.Zones` membership; the snapshot builder drops such a rule (`globalScopeFullyQuarantined`/`scrubPoliciesForQuarantinedZones`), so the published snapshot has zero rules. Quarantined members (`ZoneQuarantineExclusionsForConfig`, same set `zoneKnown` uses) are now skipped: probe row 1 (host global scoped only to z214) → `HostInboundUnmatched`; trust-scoped control unchanged; mixed scopes still match on survivors.

## Regression (`pkg/policymatch/cohort_15238_test.go`)

All three tests fail on `origin/master` (RED verified: A55-01 prints REDUNDANT naming `from-any-permit`; A55-02 14/15 corpus rows unstamped; A55-03 host global matched) and pass after the fix, each with named legitimate controls through the same path. Neighbouring suites (`TestRouteDrop*`, `TestCrossTier*`, `TestAnalyzePolicyShadowing*`, `TestSharedMatcherGlobalScope*`, `TestQuarantinedZone*`, grpcapi MatchPolicies/RouteDrop) stay green.

Pre-existing base failure, unrelated: `TestSchedulerInactiveSkipsLikeRuntime/inactive_scheduled_deny_->_falls_through_to_active_permit` fails identically on pristine master (verified in a clean base worktree) — scheduler inactivity, no overlap with this change.

Docs: `docs/log/15238.md`.

Branch: `fix/15232-campaign`

## Why

- **A48-02:** `ifTableColumns = {1,2,3,4,5,7,8,10,16}` and `IfData` carried no error/discard, Counter32 unicast, or ifLastChange fields; `deriveIfCounters` ignored `RxErrors/RxDropped/TxErrors/TxDropped`. NMS error/discard alarms and flap detection could not work; v1 managers had no packet counter.
- **A48-03:** `snmpEnabled` required a community or v3 user, so a trap-group-only config committed clean but never started the agent/link monitor — configured linkUp/linkDown traps were silently never sent.
- **A48-04:** `buildSNMPIfData` built rows only from netlink links. Bondless reths have no kernel device, so they had no IF-MIB row and traffic appeared on a node-specific member ifIndex on failover.

## What

- `pkg/snmp/agent.go`: serve ifTable cols 9, 11–15, 17–20 (ifLastChange TimeTicks; ifIn/ifOut Ucast/NUcast, Errors, Discards, UnknownProtos Counter32) from new `IfData` fields; walk order remains sorted by construction.
- `pkg/daemon/daemon_snmp_reconcile.go`: `deriveIfCounters` fills the new fields (IN unicast = RxPackets−Multicast clamped, IN non-unicast = Multicast, OUT unicast = TxPackets upper-bound, OUT non-unicast/UnknownProtos honest zeros); ifLastChange tracks per-ifIndex oper transitions as TimeTicks since daemon start; `snmpEnabled` also enables on `TrapGroups`; bondless reths get a synthesized row (stable ifIndex `1<<24+rethN`, owning-member counters, oper = RG-primary && member-up, standalone = primary) via `RethToPhysical` + `cluster.IsLocalPrimary`.
- NOT changed: kernel rows, ifXTable columns, member link-trap ifIndex keying.
- Docs: `docs/log/15232.md`, `pkg/snmp/README.md`.

## Validation

- RED on `origin/master`: daemon 15232 tests fail to build (missing `IfData` fields/helpers); the snmp column mechanism has no served values pre-fix.
- GREEN: `go test ./pkg/snmp/ -count=1` passes (full suite, incl. updated last-column walk tests); `go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run 15232 -count=1` passes; daemon SNMP/IfData subset passes; `go vet ./pkg/snmp/ ./pkg/daemon/` clean. Main agent should run the full daemon suite before merge.

## Risk

Synthetic reth ifIndexes (`>= 1<<24`) appear in ifTable/ifXTable and ifNumber (intended parity). ifLastChange epoch is daemon start rather than agent-restart start, so after a day-2 restart it is a lower bound — still monotonic for flap detection.

Closes #15232

## PR #15568 — logging: fix syslog client lifecycle cohort (#15231) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15231-campaign`

Why:
A47-02 captured os.Hostname() at construction with no hostname term
in the #9326 fingerprint, so renamed devices emitted the old name
until a stanza change or restart. A47-03 mapped slog Debug to Info,
so an info host received the debug firehose mislabelled. A47-04
continued on a system-syslog build error with no retry debt, leaving
the off-box system log off until a commit. A47-05 rebuilt the
daemon's client set from the CLI with the dialing constructor on
every console commit. A47-06 replaced the whole stream set on every
30s retry tick when any single stream was skipped.

What:
Send resolves the hostname per record via syslogHostnameFn with a
construction fallback, and the daemon fingerprint carries the
hostname. slogLevelToSyslog gains a debug arm. applySystemSyslog
arms systemSyslogRetryDebt re-driven by the 30s retry loop.
Daemon-wired reloadSyslog preserves the installed deferred set
(standalone still builds). applySyslogConfig caches clients per
stream fingerprint, preserves healthy clients on partial retries,
and warms only fresh clients.

missing seams and the CLI preservation cell failed (client
replaced). GREEN: go test ./pkg/logging/ -run 15231, ./pkg/daemon/

pkg/logging and Syslog-filtered daemon/cli suites pass; go vet
clean on the three packages. Rebased onto c9ed7ce32f and re-verified.

Risk:
Send now performs a gethostname syscall per record. A permanently
unbuildable system syslog host retries every 30s with one WARN per
tick, mirroring the #14597 stream debt. Standalone CLI behaviour
is unchanged.

Closes #15231

## PR #15570 — ha: mark every commit unshared until peer apply ACK (#15212) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15212-campaign`

Why:
A commit made while the peer was reachable was never marked unshared
(#9530 marked only partition commits), so if the standby failed to
apply that generation and then took RG0 in an unplanned failover, its
pushback silently replaced the commit with no divergence alarm on the
old primary (A24-02).

Mark every local promotion as unshared (persisted `carrying_gen` in
unshared.json), stamp the carrying wire generation on push without
clearing, and clear only on a positive config-apply ACK at or beyond

`SessionSync.OnPeerConfigApplyAck`; daemon wiring + generation
threading through commit/reconcile pushes; ACK state reset on
disconnect. Includes RG0 harness repairs for test breakage from
#15040 on master, updated #9530 cells, and README updates.

silently). GREEN: 15 configstore #9530/#15142 cells; daemon subset
with 6 new #15212 cells (incl. NACK-then-takeover pushback alarm and
ACK control) plus #5863/#7328/#10782; cluster ACK cells; cli/grpcapi
alarm suites; go vet clean. Full configstore/cluster suites exceed
the 300s job cap in this environment (pre-existing slow cells).

takeover pushback instead of staying silent — intended fail-closed

## PR #15571 — config: count keys in parse budget and require full-identity rename/copy sources (#15195) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15195-campaign`

## Summary

Closes #15195 (A01-05 + A01-06, hostile-review cohort, validator consensus MATERIAL).

**A01-05 — parse budget did not count keys.** `parseStatements` charged 1 unit per statement while `parseKeys` appended keys without bound; one node pins three parallel per-key slices, so a key-dense statement reached ~4× the documented ~37 MB live-AST bound at the 16 MiB input cap with zero parse errors.

**A01-06 — rename/copy via partial match mutated a different object.** `matchNodeKeys` returns 1 on a first-key-only hit; `findNodeWithParent`/`childrenAtPath` descended through it, so `rename firewall filter term T2` (naming no node — the node is `[filter F1]`) renamed `term T2` under F1, and `Store.Rename` recorded phantom lineage for the bogus path.

## What

- `pkg/config/parser.go`: `parseKeys` stops appending at `maxParseNodes` and latches the existing budget ParseError; `parseStatements` charges `1+len(Keys)` per statement.
- `pkg/config/ast.go` / `ast_edit.go`: new `matchNodeKeysFull` (exact key list, or prefix-of-wider-node for descent only). `findNodeWithParent` rejects a terminal prefix match as a source; `childrenAtPath` prefers exact matches. Missing source now returns "source not found" before any mutation. Lenient `matchNodeKeys` and the display walkers are untouched.
- `pkg/config/parse_node_budget_8597_test.go`: #8597 heap cells updated for the per-key charge (minimal `a;` costs 2 units → tree stops at `maxParseNodes/2` nodes; below-budget probe sizes halved).
- New regressions: `pkg/config/cohort_15195_test.go`, `pkg/configstore/cohort_15195_test.go`; log: `docs/log/15195.md`.

## Validation

- **RED on pristine `origin/master`** (`fa3fae56a4`, new tests only): key-dense cells `errs=[]`; rename/copy/truncated-source cells mutate the wrong node; store rename succeeds via partial match. Controls (normal keys, #9881 wide-prefix parent) pass on base.
- **GREEN after fix**: `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 15195`, `go test ./pkg/configstore/ -run 15195|Copy|Rename|5822|Insert|TestStore` pass.
- **Neighbour comparison**: broad subset (`TestParse|TestRename|TestCopy|TestInsert|TestDelete|8597|5822|5827|9881|TestShow|TestFormat|TestSetPath|TestNavigate|TestCompile`) — branch fails exactly the 6 tests that also fail on pristine master (incl. `TestCopyRenameClearsBracketProvenance_9881`, verified pre-existing in a clean base worktree), no new failures. The full `pkg/configstore` suite exceeds the local 300 s harness window; its relevant subsets are green and the main agent should run the full suite once.

## Risk

Full-identity matching could refuse a loosely-spelled rename/copy path that previously resolved by first key; all in-repo callers spell full identities (#3982/#5822/#9881 suites green). The per-key charge halves the statement ceiling for 1-key statements to 100k — still ~400× the largest shipped config.

Never merge — review only.

on base-shaped drain (queued=0, want 1) and GREEN after the fix,
with the QueueSessionV4 install stamp asserted;
TestDrainStatusErrorControls15217 covers clean and empty-error
controls; the #9766 locked-callsite census moves to locked:3.
Full pkg/daemon suite failures are base-attributed (see
docs/log/15217.md); gofmt and go vet clean.

eligibility walk as success-path drains; a schema-mismatched batch

## PR #15575 — userspace-dp: stamp deterministic identity on synced-first NAPT64 BIB (#15179) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15179-campaign`

Why:
When the standby imports a deterministic NAPT64 session and no BIB
exists yet, reserve_flow_maybe_persistent minted an endpoint-
independent lease tagged deterministic:true but with
deterministic_identity:None. allocate_deterministic_v6_at joins an
existing BIB only when the identity equals Some(V6(params)), so after
failover every same-socket flow to a new remote failed with
AllocatorExhausted while any synced flow was active and for 300s
after; on expiry the socket received a different port. This broke the
EIM-across-HA guarantee on every failover for mode-2 clusters.

What:
Thread the prefix DeterministicV6 through
reserve_nat64_pool_port{,_capture_and_replace} (Option<DeterministicV6>
replacing the bool) into a new allocator entry
reserve_flow_maybe_persistent_with_identity, which stamps
deterministic_identity:Some(V6(params)) on the minted lease. The
existing reserve_flow_maybe_persistent delegates with None, so source-
NAT synced reserves and reseeds are unchanged. Production caller
reserve_synced_nat64_port_unless_peer_owns passes prefix.
deterministic_v6 after its existing tuple-match validation. Also
correct the stale comment claiming persistent is constructed solely
in synced.rs. NOT changed: the strict join predicate (no adopt-on-
None, which would trust an unvalidated tuple) and round-robin pools.

Validation:
New deterministic_napt64_synced_first_bib_joins_local_15179: RED on
base prod code (identity left:None vs right:Some(V6)), GREEN after.
cargo test deterministic_napt64: 9 passed. cargo test nat64_: 329
passed (round-robin controls migrated false->None unchanged). Full
cargo test compilation on master is blocked by pre-existing #15520
(mirror mod_tests literal missing new fields, E0063 on pristine
master); runs used a temporary local patch to that literal, reverted
before commit and not in this diff.

Risk:
Bounded to the NAT64 deterministic synced reserve; identity comes
from the same prefix config the tuple was already validated against.
No wire/config/round-robin change. Docs: docs/log/15179.md.

Closes #15179

## PR #15576 — ha: isolate flow-export build failures per group and sample per interface (#15230) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15230-campaign`

Closes #15230

## A46-02 — per-group build isolation
Reconcile (v9 + IPFIX) built the full replacement set and returned on the first `NewExporter` error, so one collector whose warn-only source-address was not yet local stopped export for every instance and froze the running config. Now each template group builds independently: groups that build are published with the new config, only the failing group is marked failed (`Daemon.FlowExportFailedGroups()`, family `BuildFailed` stays set, hash not recorded so the 30s retry/next commit retries it), and a failing group keeps its previously running exporter (per-group #3742). Live generations are tracked so a partial swap never closes a retained group; teardown joins each generation via `joinWithBudget`.

Acceptance from the issue: instance `a` is live with the new config and `b` alone is failed — pinned by `TestPartialBuildPublishesHealthyInstance15230` and `TestPartialBuildDoesNotFreezeHealthyInstance15230` (day-2: published `a` carries the new collector address, retained `b` keeps its old source, recovery publishes both and clears the failure).

## A46-05 — per-interface sampling
`BuildSamplingZones` OR-ed unit flags per zone. It now also records `IfacesV4`/`IfacesV6` keyed by authored unit ref, and the daemon callbacks gate on `ShouldExportIface(..., rec.IngressIface, rec.EgressIface)` (names resolved from the records' ifindexes; `EgressIface` resolved in pkg/logging). An unsampled interface in a sampled zone is denied before the 1-in-N counter and counts zone-filtered; nameless records and hand-built zone-only configs keep prior zone semantics.

Acceptance: the probe's ge-0/0/1.0 flow is not exported — pinned by `TestSamplingPerInterface15230` (flowexport) and `TestSessionCloseSamplingPerInterface15230` (daemon, real reconcile→ProcessRawEvent, v9+IPFIX, sampled ge-0/0/0.0 control exports).

## Tests / docs
- New: `pkg/flowexport/sampling_interface_15230_test.go`, `pkg/daemon/daemon_flowexport_partial_15230_test.go`, `pkg/daemon/daemon_flowexport_sampling_interface_15230_test.go` — RED on origin/master (mechanisms absent), GREEN after.
- Controls green: flowexport + logging full suites; daemon #3742/#9166/#14608/#9035 flow-export tests.
- Note: `TestReconcileDHCPRelayWiresIfNameResolver9406` and `TestReconcilePushSharesTheCommitOnlyWhenThePeerReadsSecondary_9530` fail identically without this change's flowexport parts (unrelated DHCP/HA tests; not touched by this PR).
- `pkg/flowexport/README.md` #15230 section (supersedes the stale "returns on first error" note); `docs/log/15230.md`.

## PR #15578 — cluster: keep kernel-upgrade hold across single-RG reset (#15239) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15239-campaign`

Why:
`Manager.ResetFailover(rgID)` cleared the node-global `kernelUpgradeHold` inline, so a per-RG operator reset (`request chassis cluster failover reset redundancy-group 1`, or gRPC `cluster-failover-reset:1`) on a candidate-trialling node (journal ARMED, promotion marker not yet written) made the whole node election-eligible and let the unverified candidate claim primary on every RG before `xpf-kernel-promote` verified the dataplane. The daemon's 5s reconcile never re-asserts the hold, so the release was permanent for the boot.

What:
- `ResetFailover` no longer touches `kernelUpgradeHold`; its per-RG work (manual-failover clear, transfer-commit state, lease, failoverGen, weight recalc) is unchanged and the election stays held.
- `ResetAllFailover` clears the hold synchronously via `ClearKernelUpgradeHold()` before the per-RG resets — the sole synchronous reset producer, preserving the never-both-down property at the all-RG scope.
- Orchestrator transport follows: `grpcCluster.ResetFailover` now issues the single node-local `cluster-rejoin` SystemAction (`ResetAllFailover`, `PermMaint`, fabric-denied, mapped in `SystemActionVerbCommand`) instead of per-RG `cluster-failover-reset` actions that depended on the removed clear. `LocalRejoinComplete` readback unchanged.
- Stale rejoin comments retargeted (`TestResetFailover_ClearsKernelUpgradeHold` now drives `ResetAllFailover`); `pkg/cluster/README.md` + `docs/log/15239.md` updated.

Validation:
- RED on master: `TestResetFailoverSingleRGPreservesKernelUpgradeHold15239` fails (`kernel-upgrade hold cleared by failover reset (rejoin) rg=1`, both RGs primary); GREEN after, with `TestResetAllFailoverStillClearsKernelUpgradeHold15239` + `TestResetFailoverNoHoldUnchanged15239` controls.
- Wire: `TestSystemActionClusterRejoinClearsHold15239`, `TestSystemActionSingleRGResetPreservesHold15239`, `TestSystemActionClusterRejoinNoCluster15239` GREEN.
- Suites: `pkg/cluster` full — only pre-existing `TestInstallTableProducerToResendEndToEnd9752` (fails on pristine base too); `pkg/upgrade` ok; `pkg/authz` ok; `pkg/grpcapi` — only pre-existing base-attributed failures (`6960` vlan-tagging, `8629` census, `10769` sun_path length, all reproduced on base worktree).

Risk:
An operator who used a single-RG reset to force-release a stuck kernel-upgrade hold must now use the node rejoin (`xpfd upgrade kernel rejoin`) or wait for the promotion-marker reconcile. Deliberate: a per-RG verb must not assert node-level verification it never performed.

Closes #15239

## PR #15588 — ha: anchor fabric rollout grace at persisted first keying (#15262) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15262-campaign`

Why:
The #11676 fabric rollout grace was anchored at the in-memory
no-key -> key transition in Manager.UpdateConfig. Every xpfd process
start satisfies that transition, so every restart of a long-keyed
node re-opened up to 5 minutes of tokenless read-only fabric RPCs
(GetSessions, interface monitor, safe ShowText) until the peer
authenticated — recurring read-only disclosure to on-segment hosts
with no operator action (B04-02).

What:
Persist the first-keyed instant per accepted-key-set digest in
/var/lib/xpf/fabric-auth-grace (cluster/fabric_auth_grace.go):
HMAC-SHA256 over a domain tag keyed by each accepted key, no key
bytes stored. UpdateConfig now anchors on the first keying of the
current set: a restart under an unchanged set restores the persisted
time (backwards-stepped clocks distrust a future stamp, which only
shortens the grace); a changed set re-anchors and still gets its
grace; clearing clears. Persist is best-effort via fsatomic with a
Warn naming the reopened-grace consequence. grpcapi docs updated;
the 5-minute length, read-only set, and arming sources are unchanged.

Validation:
RED on origin/master: pkg/grpcapi TestFabricAuth15262 fails to build
(cluster.SetFabricAuthGraceStatePathForTesting undefined) — the
restart behaviour does not exist. GREEN: grpcapi #15262 + #11676
suites and cluster anchor/UpdateConfig/rotation tests pass
(go vet clean).

Risk:
A wiped /var/lib/xpf or a persistently failing anchor write falls
back to anchoring at that apply — indistinguishable from a genuine
new keying; the failure is Warn-logged. Rotation steps that change
the accepted set each get a fresh read-only grace, closed early by
peer authentication as before.

Closes #15262

## PR #15609 — ha: announce RETH VIPs after a live MAC change (#15276) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15276-campaign`

Why:
A commit that changes a RETH member virtual MAC on the RG primary (for example moving the RETH to another redundancy group the same node also owns) was applied live by programRethMAC. That path reported linkCycled=false, so step 2.6b sent no announce, and the 2s direct-VIP reconcile did not announce either because the VIPs were already present. Neighbours kept the old MAC until their own ARP/ND ageing, black-holing inbound traffic to that RETH's VIPs.

What:
programRethMAC now reports macChanged separately from linkCycled (true only where the target MAC was written), threaded through programRethMACWithWorkerJoin and programRethMemberMAC into step 2.6, which folds changed members into a per-RG set. Step 2.6b keeps the address reconcile gated on an actual link cycle but announces for exactly the changed RGs: scheduleDirectAnnounce in direct mode, or the new RG-scoped vrrp.Manager.ReconcileVIPsForRG forced GARP in VRRP mode. Existing call sites and the #5103 canary follow the new signatures; docs/log/15276.md records the evidence.

Validation:
TestC10LiveMACChangeNoAnnounce (live change announces once, no change announces nothing, cycled control announces once, VRRP mode fires no direct announce) and the pkg/vrrp TestReconcileVIPsForRG*15276 cells: RED on base (build failure, the mechanism absent), GREEN after the fix. Affected daemon reth/5103/6871/6915 cells pass. pkg/vrrp carries one pre-existing failure, TestRethOwnershipCollectorsUseTheSharedPredicate, identical on pristine origin/master.

Risk:
Announces are scoped to RGs whose member MAC actually changed and to the existing primary/MASTER gates, so no new announce storm is introduced; a cycled RG keeps its single link-cycle-recovery announce rather than gaining a second one.

  deterministic_v6_tuple_matches, prefix selected by the synthetic

  source_nat_translation_still_valid fires StaleSourceNat only on a

## Why

`build_live_forward_request_from_frame` preserved any `02:bf:73:<id>`
source MAC that parsed as a same-zone V2 stamp, even when the packet
arrived on a non-fabric LAN port. A LAN host could forge another
same-zone interface's scope and choose the interface scope the peer
applies to punted packets (A65-02, MATERIAL 3-way consensus).

  from the real logical ingress identity, falling back to the V1
  zone-only stamp. `fabric_nat_scope_stamp_mac_for_zone` and the
  receive-side stamp parser are unchanged.
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tests_bind_forward.rs`: three regression
  cells driving the anchored builder directly —
  `lan_ingress_forged_v2_stamp_not_preserved_15246` (RED pre-fix),
  `fabric_ingress_v2_stamp_preserved_15246` (fabric control),
  `lan_ingress_unstamped_gets_real_identity_stamp_15246` (LAN control).
- `docs/log/15246.md`: issue log.

  and LAN unstamped cells FAILED, fabric control passed (1 passed,
  2 failed).

  `cargo test --bins -- 15246` — 3 passed, 0 failed.

## Risk

LAN punts whose real ingress has no V2 scope now degrade to the V1
zone-only stamp, the existing fail-closed fallback. Fabric re-punts

## PR #15623 — userspace-dp: choose batch arm from capped CoS peek (#15187) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15187-campaign`

Why:
`build_cos_batch_from_queue` chose its Local/Prepared arm from the uncapped `cos_queue_front` head but popped through the cap-aware `cos_queue_peek_min_bucket(queue, target_bps)`. On a shaped flow-fair queue whose uncapped lowest-finish bucket is over the #1229 v7 cap while a bucket of the other item kind is under it, the first capped peek returned the other kind, the arm-mismatch break left an empty scratch, and the build returned `None` with every item resident. `observed_bps` only decays on TX accounting, so the class (including newcomers) wedged until a CoS config change and stuck Prepared items kept their UMEM frames.

What:
Sample `compute_drain_target_bps` once at build entry and dispatch the arm on the same capped peek the pop uses. The capped peek falls back to the lowest-finish bucket when all buckets are over-cap, so unshaped / all-over-cap / single-kind queues keep byte-identical selection. NOT changed: exact drains and exact/waterfill selectors already preflight through the capped selection and fall back to the other arm.

Validation:
- New `nonexact_mixed_local_prepared_capped_head_does_not_wedge` + mirror: RED on pre-fix builder (both return `None`), GREEN after fix.
- Controls `nonexact_flow_fair_build_applies_v7_bucket_cap` + `shared_exact_surplus_build_is_v_min_throttled` (#13062) stay green; `queue_service` suite 112/112.
- `cargo +1.98.1 check --release --bins` clean.
- [INFERENCE] Full test-binary build on current master is blocked by a pre-existing `mirror/mod_tests.rs:1032` E0063 (`MirrorConfigSnapshot` missing `ingress_vlan_id`/`unit_scoped` from #15114, reproduced on pristine origin/master); validation used a temporary local completion of that literal, reverted before push — this PR does not touch that file.

Risk:
Only arm choice changes, only when capped/uncapped selection disagree on item kind (previously zero bytes every pass). Empty queues still return `None`; no fail-open direction.

Closes #15187

## PR #15627 — userspace-dp: use RFC 1191 plateau for zero-MTU Frag-Needed (#15252) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15252-campaign`

Why:
A pre-RFC 1191 router sends ICMPv4 Fragmentation-Needed with the
Next-Hop MTU field zero. translate_icmpv4_message_to_icmpv6 turned
that into 0 + 20 clamped to 1280, pinning every affected IPv6
client to the minimum MTU regardless of the quoted datagram.
RFC 7915 section 4.2 requires the greatest RFC 1191 plateau below
the quoted Total Length, floored at 1280.

What:
Add the RFC 1191 Table 7-1 plateau table and rfc1191_plateau_mtu
helper in userspace-dp/src/nat64.rs. When the Frag-Needed MTU is
zero, read the quoted IPv4 Total Length from src[8..] (version
checked; a truncated or malformed quote keeps the 1280 floor
rather than dropping the error) and emit that plateau. Non-zero
MTUs keep the plain +20 translation. NOT changed: the v6-to-v4
PTB direction, nexthop capping, and the refuted section 5.2
minus-28 sub-leg.

Validation:
RED on rebased base (production reverted, tests kept): the two
new 15252 tests fail with left 1280, right 1492 at
nat64_tests.rs:2531 and the strictly-below edge at :2562.
GREEN: nat64_v4_to_v6_frag_needed filter 4 passed (new plateau
probe 1500-byte quote yields 1492, plateau edges, plus the
1400-to-1420 control and the 1280 clamp control); full nat64::
suite 221 passed, 0 failed. Rebased onto a8765d38bf and the
frag-needed filter re-verified (4 passed).

Risk:
Only the MTU==0 leg changes; it can now advertise up to 65535
for jumbo quotes instead of 1280, which is the RFC 7915 plateau
behaviour. Malformed quotes retain the previous 1280 floor.

Closes #15252

## PR #15628 — userspace-dp: consume single-use policy rebinds once per generation (#15188) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15188-campaign`

## Summary

userspace-dp: consume single-use policy rebinds once per generation (#15188)

C08-02: after a full snapshot apply with `policy-rematch extensive`, the coordinator's retained `ForwardingState` kept that apply's single-use `policy_session_rebinds`/`policy_rename_ancestry`. Helper-internal republishes (neighbor push, HA fabric refresh) clone the retained state through `publish_runtime_view`, so every worker rotated onto a fresh Arc and re-applied every rebind record — two BPF conntrack restamps plus shared-table restamps per record, on every worker, on every rotation, with no generation check — until the next Go publish cleared them. The Go-side strip (#10509/#11530/#12073) does not cover this helper-internal path.

## Fix

- `Coordinator::clear_single_use_policy_metadata`: clears the retained rebinds/ancestry immediately after the `publish_runtime_view()` in both full-apply sites (`refresh_runtime_snapshot_inner`, reconcile `apply_snapshot`). The published Arc keeps its copy, so the full apply still ships the rename exactly once; every later helper clone ships `rebinds=0`. The choke point deliberately does not strip (documented inline — it cannot distinguish a full apply from a helper republish).
- Worker-side backstop: `last_rebind_generation` in `worker_loop` tracks the config generation whose rebinds were already consumed; a same-generation republish passes an empty record slice. A record is applied exactly once per generation even if a republish still carries it.
- Field docs on the two `ForwardingState` fields record the single-use contract.

## Validation

- New regression cells (all RED with the fix reverted, GREEN with it):
  - `neighbor_push_after_full_apply_ships_no_rebinds_15188` — real full apply, then neighbor push ships `rebinds=0`/`ancestry=0`, neighbor still published.
  - `fabric_refresh_after_full_apply_ships_no_rebinds_15188` — same via `refresh_fabric_links`, fabric link still published.
  - `later_full_apply_still_ships_fresh_rebinds_15188` — control: a later full apply ships its fresh metadata once; retained state stripped again (per-apply, not a latch).
  - `rebind_record_applied_exactly_once_per_generation_15188` — real `worker_loop`: gen-8 apply rebinds the pair to `dmz->wan/p-new`; same-generation republish with a zone-rewritten record must not move the pair; gen-9 fresh record consumed normally.
- Neighbouring rotation suites (10590/9526/5686): 39 passed.
- Note: unmodified `origin/master` does not compile its Rust test target (`afxdp/mirror/mod_tests.rs:1032`, missing `MirrorConfigSnapshot` fields from #15113/#15114 — pre-existing, unrelated). The above runs used a temporary, reverted `..Default::default()` at that one literal; nothing of it is in this PR.

## Risk

Two `Vec::clear()` calls on already-committed coordinator state after the worker-visible store, plus one `u64` compare on the cold worker rotation branch. No wire/config change; per-packet path untouched.

Closes #15188

## PR #15632 — userspace-dp: bucket AllowedIPs LPM by prefix length (#15250) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15250-campaign`

## Summary

Implements #15250 (A69-03): AllowedIPs lookups scanned one flat cross-family `Vec` linearly per packet — `peer_for_dest` on every encap/PTB/segmentation peer selection and `matches_for_peer` on every decap source gate — so cost grew with the configured peer/prefix count on multi-peer hubs. The module docs said the opposite of the code (decap-only, outbound LPM never consulted, "trie", linear scan fine), and `load_table()` paid a `load_full()` Arc allocation per packet.

## What

- `wg/allowed_ips.rs`: per-family prefix-length-bucketed hash maps (33 IPv4 / 129 IPv6 masked-key buckets, longest length probed first) — cost bounded by prefix-length count, independent of table size. Global-LPM semantics (WG §5.4.6), first-inserter tie-break for duplicate prefixes, duplicate-insert idempotence, and fail-closed misses preserved exactly.
- `wg/engine.rs`: `load_table()` via ArcSwap guard (`load()` + one refcount clone); new `peer_for_dest_in(&PeerTable, dst)` + `table_snapshot()` so a caller selecting the same peer more than once per packet pays one load and observes one atomic snapshot; `frame/wg.rs::wg_peer_outer_dst` gained the optional-table form (existing callers unchanged).
- Docs corrected in `allowed_ips.rs`, `engine.rs`, `wg/mod.rs`, `wg/peer.rs`, `wg/tests.rs`, `frame/wg.rs`. `counters.rs` was cited in the issue but contains no AllowedIPs representation claim (grep-verified) — unchanged. `try_encap`'s explicit-pubkey contract unchanged.
- New bench `benches/allowed_ips_lookup.rs` gates the acceptance "lookup cost flat across P=1..1024" (exits non-zero if the bucketed P=1024/P=1 mean-cost ratio exceeds 4×).
- `docs/log/15250.md` + `debian/changelog`.

## Validation

- `cargo test --release --bin xpf-userspace-dp allowed_ips_tests` — 11 passed pre-rebase (12 with the engine scale test post-rebase), including new `lpm_at_1024_peer_scale`, `v6_slash_zero_and_host_route`, `non_octet_boundary_prefixes`, and `peer_for_dest_at_1024_peer_scale_15250` through the production engine.
- Decap controls (`decap_rejects*`): 5 passed. `frame::wg`/`wg_encap`: 34 passed. `wg_control`: 80 passed.
- `wg::` module: 341 passed, 2 failed (`gre_tun_origin_*_10038`, `local_tunnel_resolution:ha_inactive`) — base-attributed: identical failures on pristine base `bda827750b` in a detached worktree; GRE local-origin builder, unrelated to AllowedIPs.
- Bench: flat scan 8.7 → 121.5 → 1125.4 → 8315.3 ns/query at P=1/16/128/1024; bucketed 38.8 → 42.8 → 40.5 → 39.7 ns; flatness ratio 1.02× (gate ≤ 4×) — PASS. The old shape's ~1000× growth is the RED the gate catches for this pure-cost defect.
- Base note: at the original branch base the test target had a pre-existing compile break (`mirror/mod_tests.rs:1032` missing #15113 fields, confirmed with `cargo test --no-run` on pristine base); branch runs temp-fixed then reverted that site. It is fixed on current master, and the rebased head builds clean (12 passed above).

## Risk

No wire, config, or counter change; LPM answers bit-identical (same winner, tie-break, fail-closed miss). Memory stays O(configured prefixes), rebuilt only at config commit.

Closes #15250
