## PR #15634 — userspace-dp: gate synced deterministic-v4 imports on block membership (#15267) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15267-campaign`

Why:
Synced deterministic-v4 (CGNAT mode 1) imports were booked without a
block-membership check. The NAT64 twin
(`reserve_synced_nat64_port_unless_peer_owns`) already requires
`deterministic_v6_tuple_matches`, but both synced v4 arms in
`reserve_synced_on_first_pool_owner` passed only
`rule.deterministic_v4.is_some()` as a tag to the allocator, so
`deterministic_v4_tuple_matches` had no production caller. A peer
whose deterministic map disagrees (config-sync window, or a peer
bug) could therefore publish a synced session naming an
out-of-block translated `(pool address, port)` on the standby — a
tuple this node would never mint, whose reverse mapping then
disagrees with the deterministic function. Once configs converge
the active's port is in-block under the shared map, so legitimate
imports are unaffected.

What:
- `nat/source/synced.rs` port-bearing arm: require
  `deterministic_v4_tuple_matches(det, src, pool_addresses_v4,
  addr_index, translated, port)` and return `Refused` otherwise.
- `nat/source/synced.rs` address-only arm: the wire preserves the
  source port, so require the address half only —
  `deterministic_indices_v4` must assign exactly the translated pool
  address. A non-V4 source cannot satisfy a V4 map and refuses.
  Both checks sit after `saw_candidate` is set, mirroring the
  pool-failure arm, so PASS 2 degrades to `Refused` rather than
  leaking the tuple into the interface domain, and PASS 1 still
  stops at the first owner.
- `nat/tests_synced_det_v4_15267.rs` (new, registered in
  `nat/mod.rs`): three fail-on-revert cells — out-of-block port,
  wrong pool address (port-bearing, PASS 2), wrong pool address
  (address-only, PASS 1) — plus two in-domain controls (in-block
  port reserved; address-only on the subscriber's address
  reserves its token).
- `nat/tests_idle_lease_sync_8121.rs`: update the lease-creation
  census pin from `reserve_flow_maybe_persistent` to

range-aware so a changed range gets a fresh allocator. Protocol
v54 -> v55 fences the pairing; protocol_wire_v1.json and
docs/deterministic-nat-cgnat.md updated. NOT changed: pools without
an explicit range keep the default window byte-identically.

## PR #15636 — config: memoise address-set graph gate and expansion (#15003) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15003-campaign`

## Summary

Memoises the #12832 address-set graph gate and address-set expansion (#15003, A04-02). Both walks previously enumerated every DAG path with no memo, and the strict validator re-ran the gate once per root set, so a legal breadth-20 lattice at the five-edge cap cost ~B^6 per compile (~5.5s for a 741-line config) on commit, commit check (under the store read lock), boot load and SyncApply.

- Gate: per-node max-depth-below (height) memo; re-entry runs the live entry check first, then decides the depth cap arithmetically and reconstructs the exact naive first-node-wins depth error on overflow. Strict validator validates all roots against one shared memo.
- Expansion: deduped result + subtree height recorded per ID-graph/leaf mode. Fixes the leaf-mode `address-set` edge divergence (edges partitioned by an explicit `viaAddr` kind tag; previously leaf-mode set edges were mis-bucketed and dropped, returning empty expansions) and adds depth synthesis on memo hits (a shallow-path success is no longer served into a deeper, over-cap context).
- Cycle/depth messages, error precedence, the `ExpandAddressSet` ID-graph contract, and the tolerant-load warning downgrade are unchanged. `expandAddrSetMode` is removed; README and `docs/log/15003.md` updated.

## Validation

Fresh-binary runs (source mtimes verified against the test binary):

- `TestAddrSetGraphGateMemoised15003|TestAddrSetMemoPreservesSemantics15003|TestAddrSetExpansionIsLinear15003` — PASS. Breadth-20 lattice strict-validates in ~1ms (acceptance <1s); leaf expansion = 101 bodies for 121 sets (naive ~B^5; breadth 3: 16 vs 364); differential memo-vs-naive agreement on results and error text, exact cycle/depth messages pinned.
- `TestCrossKind*` — PASS (12502/12832 controls).
- Full `pkg/config` suite — identical 113 pre-existing base failures on branch and clean base worktree (`27920f2f8c`), zero regressions, zero address-set failures.
- `gofmt`/`go vet` clean on changed files.

## Risk

Accept/reject answers and diagnostics are differentially pinned to the pre-fix recursion; the only behavioural change is wall-clock on wide DAGs. No live-cluster mutation.

Closes #15003

## PR #15637 — userspace-dp: reclaim oldest incomplete anchor across zones at shard cap (#15288) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15288-campaign`

## Summary

Implements #15288 (gemini D4-01, adjudicated MATERIAL): two zones holding 32 incomplete fragment-overlap entries each in one shard left a third zone no reclaimable anchor, so its first fragment dropped `ShardFull` — defeating the #14321 per-zone reserve.

## Fix

At the 64-entry shard cap, when no **completed** anchor of any zone in the candidate's routing domain is reclaimable and the candidate's `(domain, zone)` is strictly below its 32-entry reserve, reclaim the globally oldest **settled-incomplete** anchor (`pending == 0`, not failed, ranges not covering a terminal end) of a **different** zone in the same routing domain. Completed anchors remain preferred (#15103 path unchanged); failed (poisoned) and still-pending anchors are never reclaimed. Per-zone fairness holds by ordering: a candidate already at 32 has exited through the own-zone branch, so admission can only displace another zone's anchor.

New counter: `FRAG_OVERLAP_CROSS_ZONE_INCOMPLETE_RECLAIMED` (sibling of the #15103 counter; delta-read in tests like its sibling).

## RED / GREEN

- RED on base `4ddf6c68ab` (test + counter only): `third_zone_admitted_past_incomplete_zones_via_incomplete_reclaim_15288` FAILED — `zone-C victim must be admitted by cross-zone incomplete reclaim, reason=Some(ShardFull)`.
- GREEN with fix: zone C admitted, `len` stays 64, zone A capped at 32 (fresh A key refuses rather than stealing C's slot), evicted A anchor no longer drops overlaps, C's anchor survives A churn, exactly one incomplete-reclaim bump, zero completed-reclaim / shard-full bumps, failed-anchor shard still refuses fail-closed.
- `cargo test --bins fragment_overlap`: 45 passed. `cargo test --bins 9950`: 28 passed. `cargo test --bins -- cross_zone`: 17 passed.
- The #15103 regression's Control 2 is updated to the surviving invariant (cross-domain candidate still fails closed over an incomplete fill); same-domain admission is now covered by the new test.

## Risk

An evicted settled-incomplete anchor loses overlap protection for the rest of its TTL — the trade #14321/#15103 already accept for completed anchors. No behaviour change below the shard cap, when a completed anchor is reclaimable, or at a zone's own reserve. `docs/log/15288.md` records the full analysis.

Closes #15288

Branch: `fix/15534-campaign`

Why:
#14947 marked poisoned DNAT entries `lenient_match_dropped` and made the flow-backed pre-routing caller drop on `DnatLookup::Poisoned`, but the flowless path used the Option lookup, which maps both `Exempt` and `Poisoned` to `None`. A portless packet (GRE, fragment) claiming an address-only poisoned rule fell through untranslated (NPTv6 or None), and a port-scoped poisoned rule was mis-keyed at ports 0/0. - `nat/destination.rs`: single-pass `outcome_with_counter_scoped` (exact -> wildcard-port -> PROTO_ANY -> prefix LPM); `lookup_result_with_counter_scoped` rewritten on it (one lookup, returns the poisoned rule's hit counter; double lookup + discarded counter gone). New bounded `flowless_poisoned_claim`: address-only/PROTO_ANY poison claims directly at ports 0/0; otherwise a possible-match scan over the destination index + family prefix slots claims port-scoped poison whose known scope/source/ICMP attributes could match, shadowed by a healthy address-only translate/`off`; fragment sentinel 255 probes concrete protocols + one wildcard probe. Also fixes `entries_by_dst` index build (`insert` kept only the last (proto,port) key per destination, hiding entries from indexed probes).

- Docs/comments: `docs/log/14947.md` base corrected to `ae59bd7d7f` and protocol to 51->52; `protocol/nat.rs` NAT64 `pool_unusable` now rides v51 (#14962); unused `DnatLookup` import removed from `afxdp/mod.rs`; `docs/log/15534.md` added.

Validation:
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp flowless_poison` — 4 passed (address-only poison + GRE drops, port-scoped tcp/80 poison + GRE drops, fragment-unknown 255 poison drops, healthy translate/off/no-rule controls). RED on master: the Option lookup maps Poisoned to None and the packet forwards untranslated.

- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp flowless` — 157 passed, 1 failed (`flowless_slack_tcp_not_steered_by_port_except_pbr_9894`, pre-existing on this base per docs/log/15117.md).

Risk:
The port-scoped possible-claim is fail-closed by design (a flowless packet that might match a poisoned port-scoped rule drops), mirroring the existing L4-possible fences; healthy address-only shadowing preserves ordinary precedence. Cross-tier precedence and established sessions unchanged.

Why: the peer/static/interface ownership refusal in the synced reserve ran AFTER the reserve. What: ask peer/static/interface ownership BEFORE reserving in both synced SNAT arms (same PASS 1 gate) and peer/static in the synced NAT64 helper; keep the post-reserve rechecks for races and, on the SNAT arms, restore the incumbent after rollback via the new `SourceNatReservationSnapshot::restore_displaced`, backed by the complete allocation record `capture_and_replace` now snapshots. NOT changed: the NAT64 twin's post-reserve interface refusal (#15146) — bare-mask snapshot; coordinator strict-mirror rollback remains its restore path.

Validation: RED on 6a8dbd7bf7 (test-only) — `a_refused_synced_redecision_keeps_the_incumbent_reservation_15145` fails with the incumbent port bit gone; controls pass. GREEN on rebased ee1b26272b: `15145` 4 passed; `8115` 26, `9021` 4, `13691` 5, `14368` 6, `8121` 72, `nat::` 693. Base-attributed on pristine ee1b26272b: `strict_mirror_refusal_replays_imported_lease_and_holder_mask_11476_10789_f4` and `test_encode_session_open_carries_nat64_flag_and_snat_v4` fail identically unmodified; `9034`/`5798` wide-filter one-offs pass in isolation and paired on master.

Risk: `restore_displaced` is conservative — declines when the slot was retaken, the incumbent bit re-claimed, or the lease shape diverged; a raced refusal can still lose the incumbent as today, never corrupt another flow. No behaviour change outside the refused re-decision path.

## PR #15644 — nat: hold persistent lease for inbound sessions (#15111) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15111-campaign`

Why: persistent_inbound_lookup took no lease reference. An inbound-only
persistent binding expired at inactivity-timeout after the last outbound
flow; GC freed its tuple and a second internal host could be minted the
same tuple toward a live inbound peer, while new inbound peers lost
persistent-NAT reachability.

What: PersistentLease gains inbound_flows, counted separately from
active_flows; every lease-liveness predicate (lookup, reuse, GC, clear,
release/rollback completion, synced joins, BIB joins, address-only
contention, display export) treats an inbound hold as live and the
expiry index only holds leases with both counts at zero.
persistent_inbound_lookup returns the lease key; acquire/release/
rollback_persistent_inbound take and drop holds, re-arming expiry on
last release. Poll captures the key at DNAT lookup, acquires once the
final NAT decision is composed (skipped when SNAT joined via
active_flows, NAT64, NPTv6) and only on an anchoring install
(ForwardCandidate, LocalMiss, FabricPuntSeed, MissingNeighborSeed),
rolling back on every refusal exit. The release/rollback entry points
(worker, synced-untracked, untracked) also release the inbound hold
derived from the session key + decision, covering GC reap, delete-sync,
purge, promote, revalidation and dropped-delete repairs; HA synced
inbound sessions acquire/release through the synced reserve wrappers.
Revalidation stays read-only (it holds a live session already).

Validation: cargo check --bins clean (pinned 1.98.1) before and after
rebase onto origin/master. New regression
persistent_inbound_hold_keeps_lease_past_expiry_15111 green
(inbound-held lease permits past outbound expiry, second host cannot
steal the tuple, release re-arms expiry, GC reclaims). Full nat::
suite 683 passed / 0 failed (pre-rebase head; the only rebased test
build failure is a pre-existing master test-fixture error,
missing nat_scope_ifindex in rebind_once_per_generation_15188_tests.rs,
also present on origin/master itself). Full --bins suite 8584 passed /
53 failed, the identical 53-name set on two consecutive runs in
unrelated areas (WireGuard, GRE, coordinator reconcile, session-delta
golden); the one NAT-adjacent name fails deterministically on an
egress-scope bucket count in export_idle_persistent_leases — recorded
in docs/log/15111.md, not hidden.

same bounded mode as a leaked active_flows hold; every teardown path
funnels through the wired release entry points. Inbound-held leases
remain visible in display export as live.

## PR #15735 — userspace-dp: borrow shared UMEM for owner bind instead of panicking (#15730) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15730-shared-umem-owner`

Closes #15730

## Why
Under the default CrossNic shared-UMEM policy the helper worker threads panicked deterministically at `umem/mod.rs:106` and the helper never armed (loss cluster, master 7d95e004cb). `create_shared_binding_group` clones one `WorkerUmem` for every group member, so the `Rc` is shared before the first socket is created; since #15088 the owner (and the private fallback) reaches its `&mut Umem` through `Rc::get_mut(..).expect("single-owner umem")`, which is `None` the moment a second clone exists. The owner create therefore panicked after the zero-copy attempt had already reported EINVAL, so the copy-mode fallback never ran, worker bring-up failed closed, and RG1/RG2 had no forwarding primary.

## What
- `umem/mod.rs`: `WorkerUmemInner.umem` is now `RefCell<Umem>` (field order unchanged, still before `area` per #5192); `umem_mut(&self) -> RefMut`, `umem() -> Ref`, `as_raw_umem_ptr` borrows — any cloned handle can run its one-at-a-time bind-time create, and an overlapping borrow still panics loudly instead of aliasing libxdp ring state.
- `bind.rs`: `&mut worker_umem.umem_mut()` at the private and shared-owner creates.
- Stale `Rc::get_mut` contract text in `poll_descriptor/mod.rs` / `worker/lifecycle.rs` now names the RefCell borrow (bind-time only, unchanged contract).
- Regression: hermetic cloned-UMEM cells in `umem/tests/shared_clone_15730.rs` (panics at the pre-fix expect; overlap control pins the loud panic) + source tripwire `tests/shared_umem_owner_umem_mut_15730.rs`, in the style of the #15088/#15244 pins.
- NOT changed: the `Rc` sharing itself, the bind ladder, roles, fallbacks, or the C bridge.

## Validation
- `cargo test --bins -- 15730`: both new cells pass (the no-panic cell panics on the pre-fix accessor); drop-order controls pass.
- `cargo test --test shared_umem_owner_umem_mut_15730 --test shared_owner_ebusy_retry_15088 --test post_create_bind_terminal_15244`: all pass.
- Controls (bind_identity_9904, bind_owner_retry_15088, umem_sizing_7497, tx_submit_ns_sidecar_single_writer_ownership_is_rc_not_arc, shared_owner_*_15088): 14 pass.
- Loss-cluster re-test with the `shared-umem mode off` stanza removed (mode auto) still needs the cluster and remains operator validation — do NOT remove that stanza from the cluster until this ships.

## Risk
RefCell moves exclusivity from compile time to runtime: a future caller holding `umem_mut` across a re-entrant create panics at bring-up (fail closed, loud) rather than aliasing; the overlap cell pins that. No hot-path change: `umem_mut` runs only at bind time. Private and shared-secondary binds are behaviour-identical.

## PR #15738 — cluster,daemon: follow RG ownership for statics and release spent failback holds (#15734) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15734-rg-transit-failback`

## Summary

Fixes both coupled defects from the recorded #12495 gate FAIL (#15734):

1. **Transit6 blackhole (RG2 on node1, RG1/WAN on node0).** `assembleFRRConfig` HA-filtered dynamic protocols by RG ownership (#11415) but passed static routes through unfiltered on every node. On the non-WAN owner the WAN statics (`::/0 via 2001:559:8585:50::1` on reth0.50, the `2602:…::/64` via reth0.80) stayed in the FRR managed section, zebra marked them inactive (egress connected prefixes leave with the VIPs), and the cluster-mode Null0 default became the selected route — verified read-only on the live cluster (node1: statics inactive, blackhole selected, no connected WAN /64; node0 healthy). New `frrHADemotionState.filterStaticRoutes` drops (or per-hop prunes) statics whose egress — explicit/inferred next-hop interface, or the RETH connected prefix containing the next-hop — belongs to an RG this node is not primary for. Non-RETH, next-table, discard/reject routes are kept; promotion re-renders via the existing HA FRR reconcile.

2. **Failback stranded >300s.** The gate's plain failback (`ManualFailover` on node1) demoted node1, node0's dual-resign guard cleared its hold, node1's committed-transfer pin re-elected it primary, and node0's re-armed `ManualFailover` could never clear again — `electRG` only released a hold for a resigned/transferred-out peer. `electRG` now also releases the hold (same 2s guard) when the peer is primary and the local RG is the committed secondary; clearing does not promote the local node.

## Regression tests

- `pkg/daemon/frr_static_ha_15734_test.go`: all-primary control; the recorded split drops both WAN statics, prunes the mixed route to its LAN hop, keeps the non-RETH route, no config mutation; promotion restores. Mutant-verified.
- `pkg/cluster/failback_hold_15734_test.go`: stranded shape clears and stays secondary (mutant-verified); hold preserved without the commit pin; 2s guard respected.

- `go test ./pkg/daemon -run 15734 -count=1` — pass
- Adjacent daemon FRR tests (11415/11393/11449) — pass
- `pkg/frr` suite: 4 failures reproduced identically on pristine `origin/master` (pre-existing; package untouched)

## PR #15739 — userspace-dp: single-write SessionKey hash and skip unused PTB inner-dst parse (#14300) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `perf/14300-sessionkey-hash-ptb-parse`

Refs #14300

## Why
Loss-cluster perf profile (user-supplied): `SessionKey Hash` 3.33%, `compute_forwarded_egress_ptb_with_dynamic` 1.21%, under `poll_binding_process_descriptor_with_injection` 16.18%.

- Derived `SessionKey: Hash` issues ~12 typed `write_*` calls; under the production `KeyedFxHasher` (`hot_hash_seed.rs`, #12989) **every** typed write is a full splitmix64 fold (~9 multiplies). Per established packet the key is hashed repeatedly (flow-cache `set_index`, `session_is_live_at`, `touch_if_stale`, `account_packet`, plus slow-path `key_to_handle` + alias indices).
- `compute_forwarded_egress_ptb` called `post_transform_inner_destination` (ethertype walk + `inner_dst_ip`) on **every** non-NAT64 forward, but only the WireGuard arm of `post_transform_inner_mtu` consumes it (GRE ignores it at `icmp_ptb.rs` `tunnel_inner_mtu`, plain path never calls it). It also resolved L3 ethertype-first, discarding the trusted stamp.

## What
- `session/key.rs`: manual `Hash` for `SessionKey` — one `Hasher::write` over a fixed 49-byte family-tagged stack image (af/proto, `(tag,16B)` src/dst, ports, routing_domain, `(disc tag,val)`). Eq unchanged; hasher/seed unchanged. New `session_key_hash_14300_tests` proves equal⇒equal-hash and every field (incl. `Keyed(0)` vs `Unkeyed` vs `None`, v4-vs-v6 aliasing) splits.
- `icmp_ptb.rs` / `tx/dispatch/mod.rs`: `post_transform_needs_inner_dst` (WireGuard endpoint only) gates the parse; NAT64 still returns `rewrite_dst`. PTB L3 resolution now prefers `nibble_trusted_stamp`, falling back to `frame_l3_offset`. New parse-skip test with parseable control.
- `benches/session_key_hash.rs` (+ Cargo registration): derived-vs-manual under KeyedFxHasher and SipHash.

## Validation (local, this host)
- `cargo test --bins -- icmp_ptb session_key`: 68 passed (incl. 62 PTB, seeded s3-clique dispersion #12603, new hash tests).
- Bench, KeyedFxHasher (production): derived **34.0 ns v4 / 41.9 ns v6** → manual **24.7 / 23.6 ns** (−27% / −44%). SipHash: 61.3/75.7 → 37.6/40.5 ns.
- NOT yet cluster-validated: no deploy/re-profile done (smoke lane owns the cluster; shared-UMEM still OFF there). Expected recovery is a share of the 3.33% hash slice, not the whole profile.

## Risk
- Hash **values** change: all `SessionKey` maps are node-local per-process (`hot_hash_seed.rs`: HA sync transmits keys, never hashes). No wire/persistence impact.
- PTB: WireGuard per-peer MTU path byte-identical (gate = exact consumer predicate, covered by `post_transform_wg_inner_mtu_is_per_peer_underlay`); GRE/plain previously discarded the parsed value. L3 stamp-first matches every other hot-path consumer (#9900 nibble check retained).

## Deliberately NOT in this PR (filed as issue, see #14300 comment)
`__memmove` 13.6% attribution: fast path is zero-copy (in-place / direct-TX / flow-cache inline); copies are (a) copy-fallback `vec![0; len+4]` + payload memcpy + second UMEM memcpy in `transmit` when shared-UMEM is OFF (cluster's current workaround state — fix #15735 is merged, so re-enabling shared-UMEM is the lever, needs smoke-lane validation), (b) decap/injected `to_vec`, (c) mirror clones, (d) TCP segmentation. No code change claimed without a cluster profile showing which dominates.

## PR #15744 — routing,userspace: import cluster unreachable default as reject (#15742) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15742-split-rg-transit`

## Summary
Fixes the split-RG transit half of #15742: with RG2 (LAN) on node1 and RG1 (WAN) on node0, v4+v6 transit blackholed while NA recovery succeeded.

**Root cause (live-verified on 8871e79a9d):** the cluster-mode Null0 default that exists to terminate a split node's lookup is installed by FRR in the kernel as `RTN_UNREACHABLE proto static metric 20` (zebra `S>* ::/0 [250/0] unreachable (blackhole)`, `ip route`: `blackhole default proto static metric 20`), but `ImportLearnedRoutes` adopted only RTN_UNICAST/RTN_BLACKHOLE, and `addLearnedRouteSnapshots` suppressed imported rows behind same-prefix config rows. The fw1 helper FIB therefore held only the config defaults (pref 5 via the peer-owned WAN egress) and no terminal default (`show route fib` captured live).

**Fix:** adopt RTN_UNREACHABLE as `LearnedRoute.Reject` (RTN_PROHIBIT stays excluded; HA sentinel 4242 excludes both negative forms), map to `RouteSnapshot.Reject` (Rust `RejectRoute` already exists), add Reject to the dedupe key, never suppress a negative learned row behind a forwarding row. Preference ordering (forwarding 5 < imported 200) keeps the real default selected while usable; HA demotion + fabric redirect fire when the egress RG is peer-owned.

**Failback half:** dispositioned in `docs/log/15742.md` — targeted failbacks return iter=1 in every reproduction (incl. this session); the gate's early plain-form shape remains under #13058's timing lane. No deadline widening.

## Test report
- `go test ./pkg/routing/ -run '15742|11398'` — pass (new: cluster unreachable adopted both families; HA sentinel unreachable excluded; prohibit-only negative cell).
- `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run '15742|11398'` — pass (config default + imported reject coexist, forwarding preferred).
- Both Go cells mutant-verified RED (adoption revert; suppression revert), then GREEN.
- `cargo test split_rg_cluster_reject` — pass (RG1 active forwards v4+v6; inactive HA-demotes → FabricRedirect).
- Full `pkg/dataplane/userspace` suite: 2 failures (`13149`, `13151`) reproduced identically on pristine origin/master — pre-existing, untouched area.
- Live: split-RG blackhole reproduced pre-fix under the cluster lock (v4+v6 0/3; helper FIB without reject default; cluster restored, RG2 back iter=1). Post-fix deploy + `test-v6-na-recovery-12495.sh` re-run is the remaining lab acceptance.

Closes #15742

## PR #15748 — userspace: attribute RETH zones past blank member rows for fabric stamps (#15742) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

v58 renders `discard cluster-terminal` pref 200 on split fw1, yet transit still 0/3 both families. LIVE trace (working-20705, split reproduced 5×, cluster restored healthy each time):

- fw1 per-probe: Forward candidates +3, TX +3, Session creates +0 — the demote chain (i) lookup `ClusterTerminalHAInactive`, (ii) `source_ifindex=14` (reth0.80/RG1), (iii) HA keeps demotion, (iv) fabric redirect with zone stamp all execute.

`populate_zone_to_rgs`: a blank row vetoes only when it aliases a unit on the same ifindex (its name is that unit's base — the #13181 unzoned-alias shape); blank physical members do not vote. Closes #15656

## Why
`Manager.ReadInterfaceCounters` matched only the exact `BindingStatus.Ifindex`. The AF_XDP helper binds only the parent physical netdev, so every VLAN subinterface (`ge-0/0/0.<vlan>`, own kernel ifindex) returned authoritative `(0,0,0,0),nil` while the parent carried traffic. REST `/interfaces` + `/stats/interfaces`, gRPC `GetInterfaces`, CLI and Prometheus all rendered that as real zero traffic (the #3464 `Unavailable` flag only fires on error, so success+zero was final).

## What
- `ReadInterfaceCounters` tracks `matched`: on no direct match it consults the retained snapshot — a row with `Ifindex == request && ParentIfindex > 0` resolves the VLAN child to its parent binding and returns the parent's aggregated RX/TX counters (minimum fix direction in the issue; per-`(ifindex,vlan_id)` helper counters remain future work, so sibling units share the parent aggregate).
- When neither a direct binding nor a bound snapshot parent covers the ifindex, it fails closed with `userspace interface counters unavailable: no binding covers ifindex %d` instead of a confident zero.
- A directly bound idle interface still matches and returns its real zero.
- Supersedes the #13273 "unknown ifindex = zero, no error" expectation (updated test).
- No consumer changes needed: existing #3464 contract maps the error to REST `Unavailable`, Prometheus omitted sample + `xpf_interface_counter_read_errors_total`, CLI warning.
- `docs/log/15656.md` + `debian/changelog` entry.

## Validation
- RED on `origin/master`: `TestReadInterfaceCountersVLANChildResolvesToParent15656` fails with child = `{0,0,0,0}` vs parent aggregate `{15,1500,23,2300}`.
- GREEN: `GOCACHE=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-15656 go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run 'TestReadInterfaceCounters|TestLegacyAdapterForwards' -count=1 -v` — all #13273 + #15656 cells pass (aggregates, VLAN child→parent, unbound parent fail-closed, uncovered ifindex fail-closed, idle bound zero, no-snapshot fail-closed, unavailable fail-closed, adapter forwarding).

## Risk
A configured interface the helper never binds now reports counter-unavailable instead of a clean zero — the intended fail-closed direction of the acceptance criteria. Directly bound interfaces are unaffected.

- NOT changed: wire snapshot, daemon three-arm gate, quarantine scrub ordering.

- Existing suites pass: #8993/#11329/#12851/#14330/#11007 fingerprint, quarantine, rename-ancestry.

## Risk
Fingerprint values change universally but are computed fresh on both sides of each commit diff (no persisted values to skew). Residual: reordering overlapping application terms with different inactivity timeouts no longer re-evaluates sessions; verdict/matched set unchanged.

## PR #15751 — config: scan global zone-leaf tails for collapsed match keywords (#15660) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15660-campaign`

Closes #15660

## Why
`policyUnsupportedMatchLeafFindings` short-circuited global `from-zone`/`to-zone` leaves (`if isGlobal && globalOnlyPolicyMatchLeaves[leaf] { continue }`) before scanning their collapsed tail. Global zone leaves are `multi:true`, so:
- `match from-zone any dynamic-application junos:FTP` (flat set) collapsed the unsupported criterion onto the zone leaf — strict commit misdiagnosed it as an undefined/mixed-zone error (#4626/#3402 wording) instead of the #3113 unsupported-leaf rejection, and tolerant load published an unscoped permit with `LenientContentDropped=false`.
- A hierarchical missing semicolon (`from-zone any` + `to-zone untrust;`) or `from-zone [ any to-zone untrust ]` fused the sibling zone keyword onto the first zone leaf and committed silently.

(Probe-verified: flat-set fused forms do not collapse — SetPath stops at the registered sibling and compiles correctly as separate leaves; the fused shape is hierarchical-only. The collapsed unsupported keyword reproduces in both forms.)

## What
- `pkg/config/compiler_policy_match.go`: scan `firewallMatchValues(m)` for global-only leaves exactly like supported leaves. Unsupported keywords are flagged as unsupported leaves (#3113); a fused `from-zone`/`to-zone` keyword as a swallowed structural token (#3673). Strict rejects with the correct diagnostic; tolerant load warns and sets `LenientContentDropped` so the snapshot builder poisons the rule (#5575). Corrected the stale "cannot arise in global scope" comment and message wording.
- The report's second hunk (rejecting `any`+unresolvable scopes in `unresolvableScopeElement`/`build_global_zone_scope`) is **deliberately not taken**: the contains-`any` wildcard is documented design (Rust tolerant backstop for corrupt/mixed-version snapshots, Go `IsWildcardZoneSet`, #9410 mirror contract), the strict gate already rejects mixing `any` with concrete zones at commit, and changing only the Go mirror would diverge `show security match-policies` from the helper. With the compiler fix, collapsed bogus tokens can no longer reach the snapshot as a clean scope. `TestPolicyZoneRejectionMixedAnyScopeIsWildcard15660` pins this with a `[ghost]` control.
- Docs: `docs/config-schema.md` #15660 paragraph, `docs/log/15660.md`.

## Validation
- RED on origin/master: 9 failing subtests (wrong-reason strict errors, silently committed fused forms, `LenientContentDropped=false`); legit-scope controls green pre- and post-fix.
- GREEN post-fix: `pkg/config/compiler_policy_match_15660_test.go` (strict unsupported ×4, strict fused ×3, lenient poison ×2, legit controls ×3) and `TestPolicyZoneRejectionMixedAnyScopeIsWildcard15660`.
- Targeted suites pass: `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestPolicyMatch|TestGlobalPolicy|TestPolicyZone|Test.*3148|Test.*3142|Test.*3673|Test.*3113|Test.*11078|Test.*15200'`, `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run 'TestPolicyZoneRejection'`. Full `pkg/config` and `pkg/dataplane/userspace` suites should be run by the reviewer.

## Risk
Fail-closed only. Strict commit now rejects with the correct reason configs that previously committed silently (hierarchical fused) or with a misleading zone error; tolerant load still boots them with a warning but poisons the rule instead of publishing an unscoped permit. No wire, Rust, or wildcard-semantics change.

## PR #15755 — config: validate and merge generate route prefixes (#15658) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15658-campaign`

Closes #15658

## Why
`routing-options generate route` carried an untyped destination and no same-prefix merge. `generate route 999.999.0.0/99 discard` committed clean; FRR silently omitted the blackhole (`validFRRRoutePrefix`) while the userspace snapshot passed the prefix to a helper that refuses the whole snapshot (`RouteDestinationUnparseable`) — FRR-vs-userspace split-brain. Duplicate same-prefix hierarchical blocks appended divergent `GenerateRoute` entries.

## What
- Schema: `generate route` identity arg typed with `keyValueType: ValueCIDR` + `keyValidator: ValidateRouteDestination` (reuses the #2448 static-route grammar; the per-instance routing-options node shares the same `generate` pointer, so instances are gated too).
- Compiler strict gates (`compiler_validate_strict_generate_route.go`, wired beside the static-route mask gate): invalid prefixes and helper-refused padded masks (`/008`, `/0032`, incl. folded aliases) rejected at strict compile for global + per-instance routes; tolerant load/peer-sync warns per offender and preserves the route (`lenientGenerateRoutePrefix`) so a published bad prefix still fails the helper snapshot closed.
- Merge: `compileRoutingOptions` folds every `generate` container and merges same-masked-prefix definitions deterministically (`mergeGenerateRoute`: first spelling wins, discard latches, first non-empty policy wins); `canonicalizeGenerateRoutesAcrossScopes` folds across routing-options roots and writes helper-supported padded masks canonically (`/08` → `/8`, #12507 doctrine). Folded spellings retained on compiler-only `GenerateRoute.prefixAliases` for diagnostics. One route per prefix reaches both consumers — FRR renders one `ip route <p> blackhole`, userspace installs one Discard snapshot.
- Two pre-existing `GenerateRoute` struct comparisons moved to `reflect.DeepEqual` (required by the new unexported slice field).

## Validation
- RED: with `keyValidator` stripped, compile-time merge reverted to append, and canonicalise removed — `SchemaValidate accepted generate prefix "999.999.0.0/99"` (×5 malformed prefixes) and `hierarchical same-prefix routes = 2, want 1 merged`.
- GREEN: `go test -count=1 -run 'TestGenerateRoute.*15658|TestGenerateRoutes|TestGenerateRoutePackedRun8939|TestGenerateRoutePolicy|TestGenerateRouteWithoutDiscard|TestUnnamedRoutingContainersMergeAt12120Sites|TestRoutingInstanceRoutingOptions|TestSchema2448|TestStaticNextHop' ./pkg/config/ ./pkg/frr/ ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/` — all pass; `go vet` clean on the same packages. Details in `docs/log/15658.md`.

## Risk
Strict commits now reject previously-accepted malformed generate prefixes (intended acceptance criterion); tolerant paths keep persisted configs booting with warnings. Valid generate routes render identically in FRR and userspace.

## PR #15803 — api: validate full TLS chain and recover failed HTTPS legs (#15667) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15667-campaign`

Why:
The management TLS preflight parsed and validity-checked only cert.Certificate[0], so an expired or invalid intermediate in Certificate[1:] was served until the Go handshake failed, a CA or non-ServerAuth leaf was accepted, custom certificates got no SAN diagnostic, and tlsDesired latched true on an initial load failure so refresh never recreated the failed HTTPS listener. This is a preflight/diagnostics/recovery defect; Go TLS still verified trust at handshake, so no crypto bypass is claimed.

What:
Parse every DER entry in managementTLSCertificateChain (rejecting a Leaf/Certificate[0] mismatch and unparseable intermediates), store the chain on the certificate state, and run managementTLSCertificatePreflightError at custom load, generated load, custom/generated refresh, handshake selection, and the durable-pair loader: every entry in its validity window (leaf wording unchanged), leaf not a CA, leaf EKU allows ServerAuth when present, intermediates are CAs allowed to sign, and every adjacent signature link verifies. Log SAN diagnostics on custom load/rotate and on the invalid-cert error path. Split tlsDesired into tlsDesiredConfigured (operator desire) and tlsDesired (armed only on successful install) and record httpsDesiredAddrs; the monitor retries on the configured desire and recoverHTTPSLegsIfNeededLocked binds/serves missing HTTPS legs from the validated state after a successful refresh (Start path; legacy Run unchanged). Tests in tls_certificate_15667_test.go and docs/log/15667.md.
NOT changed: warnStaleLoadedCert SAN diagnostics (still leaf-only, deliberately diagnostic-only) and handshake trust verification.

Validation:
go test ./pkg/api/ -run '15667' -count=1: pass (valid chain, expired/not-yet intermediate, CA leaf, client-auth leaf, non-CA intermediate, bad signature link, expired-intermediate load rejection, SAN log, monitor recovery with a real handshake). Reverting the state preflight calls to leaf-only validity makes TestCustomChainRejectedAtLoad15667 fail (chain installs an HTTPS server). Targeted TLS/cert/reconcile suites pass.
Full go test ./pkg/api/ -count=1: fails only in TestEmitDropClassCounters_4768 (prometheus NewConstMetric panic), reproduced identically on a clean base worktree at d316277cb4 — base-attributed, unrelated to this change.

Risk:
A previously served chain whose intermediate is expired, non-CA, or mis-signed is now refused at load/refresh (fail-closed, the intended behaviour); operators must renew the full chain file. Self-signed single-leaf generated certs are unaffected (verified by the existing generated-cert suites). Recovery only creates legs on the Start lifecycle; the legacy Run/serveBound path still relies on the daemon ReconcileHTTPS retry.

## PR #15817 — config: diff matched nodes in scoped compare (#15758) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15758-campaign`

## Summary

Scoped `show <path> | compare` (`FormatCompareAtPath`, #15272) silently returned `[no changes]` for leaf statements, container `Inactive` toggles, and empty containers, and flattened bare-keyword multi-match containers.

**Mechanism:** `FormatCompareAtPath` navigated both trees to the path and compared only the matched nodes' *children* (non-leaves only). A leaf match was skipped outright, a container's own `Inactive` flag was discarded with the node, an empty container produced an empty child list identical to a missing path, and bare-keyword multi-matches were flattened into one shared child list where duplicate `KeyPath`s could pair across siblings.

**Fix:** use `navigatePathWidth` on both sides — the contract `FormatPathSet` / `FormatPathJSON` already use — and diff the matched node slice `oldMatches` vs `newMatches` with `diffNodes` at the parent prefix `path[:len(path)-width]`, using the true consumed width so an ancestor value repeating the terminal node's keys cannot over-strip the prefix (#5717). All downstream surfaces (redacted twin, configstore `ShowCompare*AtPath`, local/gRPC/remote CLI) inherit the fix unchanged since they already route through `FormatCompareAtPath`.

## Validation

- **RED pre-fix:** `TestFormatCompareAtPathLeafAndContainerInactive` failed with `expected leaf compare at [system host-name] to show new-fw diff, got ""`; `TestFormatCompareAtPathEmptyContainerAndMultiMatch15758` failed with `expected empty-container add at [protocols ospf area] to render + area 0.0.0.0, got ""`.
- **GREEN post-fix:** both regression tests pass (leaf value change, container `Inactive` toggle, empty-container add/delete, bare-keyword multi-match value change with the unchanged sibling not rendered as changed; identical-tree / absent-path / child-edit controls).
- Neighboring suites pass: `TestFormatCompare*` (#15168), `TestCompare*15169`, `TestInactive_*`, configstore `TestShowCompare*` / `TestShowCompareAtPath15272` / redacted compare tests. `gofmt` clean. The full `pkg/config`+`pkg/configstore` run exceeded the 600s lane shell timeout before reporting; targeted suites were run individually.

## Risk

Scoped compares to a container path now render the matched node itself under its parent `[edit]` header (matching global compare and Junos) instead of only its children under `[edit <path>]`; unchanged subtrees, absent paths, and the global compare are byte-identical to before.

Branch: `fix/15769-campaign`

Branch: `fix/15779-campaign`

Why:
Multi-member expanded community lists (#15008) rendered one pattern
of Perl-style (?=...) lookaheads. FRR compiles expanded lists with
regcomp(REG_EXTENDED) (POSIX ERE), which rejects lookaheads with
CMD_WARNING_CONFIG_FAILED, aborting the whole frr-reload whenever a
definition had >=2 members and a regex member.

What:
communityExpandedConjunctionPatterns replaces the lookahead pattern
with the permutation disjunction: one expanded permit entry per
ordering of the distinct member factors joined with .*, so the
entry set matches exactly routes satisfying every member. Literal
members keep whole-token (^| )m( |$) anchoring; single-member
render is unchanged. The factorial entry count is bounded at 4
members (24 entries) via expandedCommunityConjunctionRenderable,
wired into renderCommunityListDefinitions,
communityListMissingAtRender, communityDeleteTarget, and
communityListCollision; past the bound the definition renders
nothing and referencing terms fail closed (#10822). All-literal
standard lists are untouched. pkg/frr/README.md and
docs/log/15779.md record the new contract.

Validation:
New TestExpandedCommunityConjunctionPOSIX15779 plus the rewritten
TestMultiMemberCommunityIsConjunctive15008 compile every rendered
pattern with regexp.CompilePOSIX and evaluate conjunctive match
semantics (both present matches; either alone, neither, and
65000:100 inside 65000:1000 do not). RED on origin/master
f7c921ce29: the lookahead pattern fails CompilePOSIX and the
past-bound definition renders. Post-fix the targeted tests and
TestGeneratePolicyOptionsCommunity* pass; full pkg/frr shows only
the 4 failures also present on unmodified f7c921ce29
(TestBGPNoExportNeighborGetsDefaultExport15157,
TestFamilylessIPv6NeighborWithoutPolicyIsV6Only11564,
TestFRRLoadInet6OnlyNeighborIPv4Deactivation11374,
TestFRRLoadBGPClasslessRIBSuppression11426).

Risk:
Expanded definitions with >4 distinct members no longer render;
their referencing terms fail closed (reject terms deny) instead of
loading. Regex members that reuse one community token to satisfy
two members, and ^/$-anchored members in non-edge positions, are
stricter than the (unloadable) lookahead form. No lab frr-reload
verification; POSIX validity is pinned via Go's CompilePOSIX
oracle.

## PR #15839 — userspace-dp: resolve scoped-NAT session misses in the override table (#15768) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15768-campaign`

Closes #15768

## Why

The #15118 untranslated session-miss arm called `lookup_forwarding_resolution_for_nat_flow` with no table argument, so PBR/native-VRF flows resolved in `inet.0`/`inet6.0` instead of their `route_table_override` (wrong-table egress / VRF leak or blackhole), the arm hard-coded `resolved_in_table=false` (clearing the installing-table stamp so every re-resolve ran in the default table), the registered-but-unclaimed NAT branch dropped the 5-tuple ECMP hash, and `lookup_forwarding_resolution_without_nat_local` deep-cloned the whole `ForwardingState`.

## What

- `lookup_forwarding_resolution_for_nat_flow` (`forwarding/fib.rs`) takes `table: Option<&str>` + `icmp: Option<(u8,u8)>` and returns the full `ForwardingLookupResult`. Both arms resolve in the caller's table with `ecmp_hash_flow`; the claimed arm uses `lookup_forwarding_resolution_with_dynamic_for_flow_in_table`; `selected_route` carries the resolving table's identity.
- The `ForwardingState` clone is gone: suppression is a `Some(dst)` marker threaded through `*_suppressing` inner variants into the per-table local-ownership predicates (configured-interface addresses stay local, exactly as the clone's guard did). Public wrappers pass `None` — all other callers (flowless, tunnel, WG, session re-resolve) are behaviour-identical.
- Poll caller passes `route_table_override.as_deref()` + `dnat_packet_icmp` and stamps `resolved_in_table=true` for the arm, matching the translated else-arm.
- Regression cells in `tests_nat_scope_15118.rs`; `docs/log/15768.md`, forwarding README, changelog.

## Validation

- RED on `origin/master` (f7c921ce): the new tests fail to compile against the pre-fix 6-arg helper — no table/ICMP/`selected_route` surface exists pre-fix.
- GREEN: `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp tests_nat_scope_15118` — **9 passed** (4 new #15768 cells: unclaimed-NAT-in-tenant-table + identity, non-NAT override flow, suppressed-branch ECMP spread over 64 tuples, claimed-control + stamp arithmetic; 5 pre-existing #15118 cells unchanged in assertion).
- Neighbours: `afxdp::forwarding::` 368 passed. `poll_descriptor` 437 passed / 6 failed and `session_glue` 356 passed / 2 failed — both failure sets verified byte-identical on pristine `origin/master` (pre-existing: #15189 policer, #6304 flow-cache, 4× prerouting-scope, #9412, contention).
- `cargo fmt --check` diffs in touched files are confined to pre-existing unformatted regions outside this change's hunks.

## Risk

Only untranslated session misses carrying a `route_table_override` change behaviour (resolve + stamp in that table, the #9752 semantics the translated arm already had). Default-table flows are identical except the unclaimed branch now also spreads by the flow hash (#2734). Claimed-NAT, flowless (`flowless_verdict.rs` `route_override` already threaded), and translated paths are untouched; no registration/proxy-ARP/ownership behaviour changes.

## PR #15841 — nat: index all port keys per static-NAT IP and route snat/local probes via indexes (#15790) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15790-campaign`

Closes #15790

## Why

`StaticNatTable::from_snapshots` built `dnat_by_dst` with `.insert(*ip, indexed)` inside the loop over the `dnat` map. Several port keys sharing one external IP — the ordinary multi-port VIP (`203.0.113.10:80` + `:443`) — map to the same index bucket, so each insert discarded the previous key's entries. The discarded rules stayed in `dnat` (the main `match_dnat_*` path keys that map directly and was unaffected) but became invisible to `dnat_port_entries_for`, backing the flowless/fragment/non-TCP-UDP probes. This is the #15534 sibling bug (the identical insert-overwrite fixed in `DnatTable::from_snapshots`) never ported to static NAT.

Secondary (acceptance item 2): the outbound leg of `flowless_l4_translation_possible` linearly scanned the whole `snat` map, and `nat_local_match_possible` linearly scanned the whole `dnat` map, per packet — `O(N)` in installed rule count.

## What

- `from_snapshots`: `dnat_by_dst` built with `.entry(*ip).or_default().extend(indexed)` (verbatim the #15534 sibling pattern); new symmetric `snat_by_src` index over the finished `snat` map. Both rebuilt wholesale in the only constructor, so they cannot drift.
- `flowless_l4_translation_possible` outbound leg and `nat_local_match_possible` now visit only the packet source's / destination's indexed entries, with identical port gates and per-entry scope/source predicates (`any` is order-insensitive, so results are unchanged for rules that survived pre-fix).
- The `blocks` prefix leg of `nat_local_match_possible` stays a bounded linear scan (prefix rules cannot be keyed by exact IP — same posture as #15116).
- Regression: `nat::tests_static_multiport_index_15790` — two-port same-IP fixture in both snapshot orders (both ports claim via indexed probes; unconfigured port / unrelated destination do not), a source-scoped variant identifying each port through the index, and the indexed `snat` leg.
- `docs/log/15790.md` records the mechanism.

## Validation

- RED on base: 1 of 3 new tests fails (`flowless probe must see the web rule under its source` — the discarded port's entry invisible to indexed probes).
- GREEN after fix: 3/3 new tests; neighboring `tests_static` / `tests_scope` / `tests_flowless_index_15116` pass (84 tests); full `nat::` suite passes (702 tests, 1 ignored).
- `cargo test --bins` with `GOCACHE=/var/worktrees/.cache CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/var/worktrees/.cache/cargo-15790`.

## Risk

Index memory is O(installed entries), built once per config snapshot; no per-packet allocation. Tables are constructed only via `from_snapshots`, so no stale-index path. Fail-closed probe outcomes are preserved exactly.

## PR #15845 — afxdp: drop only invalid prepared frames in transmit queue (#15786) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15786-campaign`

Closes #15786

## Why
`transmit_prepared_queue`'s stage/rewrite/verify validation drained and recycled **every** staged zero-copy frame (up to 63 valid packets) and returned `Err(Drop)` when any single frame was oversized or out of range. On the CoS path, `submit_prepared` then restored an empty deque, orphaning every `CoSQueuePopSnapshot` so a later LIFO restore could consume the wrong top entry and trip the snapshot bucket-mismatch `assert!` (worker-thread death).

## What
- Per-frame validation drops via new `record_prepared_drop` (`tx/transmit/mod.rs`): recycle + count **only** the offender, record its ORIGINAL pending position in `scratch_prepared_dropped_orig_idx` and the first reason in `scratch_prepared_first_drop_reason`; staging/verification continues with the valid survivors.
- Original positions tracked through the fixed `scratch_prepared_tx_orig_idx` sidecar into `scratch_prepared_committed_orig_idx` (`finalise.rs`), so `submit_prepared` charges flow-bucket/sojourn accounting by committed identity instead of a prefix shifted by an interior drop.
- Dropped snapshots removed positionally (descending, `cos_queue_remove_orphan_snapshot_at`, the #15172 contract) before any LIFO restore on the Ok/Retry/Drop arms.
- All-invalid batches surface the first `Err(Drop)` with every frame already counted once; the `submit_prepared` Drop arm and backup-drain Drop arm no longer double-count.

## PR #15848 — config: compile hierarchical rib statics and split fused tails (#15777) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15777-campaign`

## Summary

Compiles hierarchical `rib { <name> { static { ... } } }` blocks instead of silently dropping 100% of their static routes, and stops compact multi-clause static routes from fusing route-level clauses into phantom next-hops.

## Why

- `routing-options { rib { inet.0 { static { route ... } } } }` parses as `rib` → `inet.0` → `static`, but `compileRoutingOptions` only read `FindChild("static")` on the named rib node: `StaticRoutes` stayed empty, `SchemaValidate` returned nil, and strict commit succeeded installing no route (same inside routing instances, and out-of-scope hierarchical tables were not even recorded in `UnhandledRibs`).
- `route <dst> { next-hop <gw> preference <n> ...; }` packs route-level clauses onto the `next-hop` leaf, which the child reader consumed as gateway addresses (`preference`, `123` became next-hops; the route kept preference 5).

## What

- `pkg/config/compiler_routing.go`: unwrap the one extra hierarchical rib level and honour every `rib`/`static` sibling, keeping the existing `ribMatchesRoutingOptionsScope` check/family split and the `UnhandledRibs` warning for out-of-scope tables.
- `pkg/config/compiler_routing.go`: stop the next-hop gateway run at a fused route-level keyword and apply that tail (`preference`, `next-table`, `discard`, `reject`, `no-install`) to the route; fused `qualified-next-hop` remains owned by the packed-QNH normalizer / QNH-tail gate.
- `pkg/config/compact_static_route_qnh_12648.go`: extend the packed-QNH scope recogniser to hierarchical ribs.
- Regressions in `pkg/config/compiler_rib_hier_static_15777_test.go`; notes in `docs/log/15777.md`.

## Validation

- RED on revert (new tests, production files reverted): `StaticRoutes = [], want 2 routes` (strict + lenient), `preference = 5, want 123`, phantom `preference`/`123` gateways.
- GREEN: new tests (7) plus existing rib/static suites (`7512`, `11335`, `12648` families); `go vet` clean.
- Full `go test ./pkg/config`: 167 failures, all pre-existing on the unmodified base at the same head (spot-checked identical with the fix stashed).

## Risk

Hierarchical ribs that silently compiled to nothing now install their routes — the intended behaviour change. Out-of-scope tables still warn via `UnhandledRibs` rather than installing.

Closes #15777

Branch: `fix/15770-campaign`

## Why
The #15247 owed retry used one table-wide newest-wins `owed` slot: a second hot-bucket refusal overwrote the first victim, whose later `map_changed == false` advert then looked proven-present and was skipped forever. ## Risk

## PR #15850 — userspace-dp: capture companion identity before reverse removal on scoped deletes (#15784) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15784-campaign`

## userspace-dp: capture companion identity before reverse removal on scoped deletes (#15784)

Closes #15784

### Why
`DeleteSyncedConditional` producers read `shared_sessions` for the companion identity *after* deleting the reverse entry, normally sending `companion_expected_id=0`, and the worker consumer treated `0` as an unconditional wildcard (`|| companion_expected_id == 0` in `handle_delete_synced_with_guard`). A reverse tuple replaced during worker-queue delay was therefore torn down despite the scoped forward identity matching.

### What
- `ha/session_import.rs`: coordinator fan-out names `removed_reverse_entry.session_id` — the incarnation captured before (by) the reverse removal — falling back to a surviving reverse row's live id only when no entry was removed.
- `session_delta.rs`: stale-close producer captures `companion_expected_id` at the top of its close block, before any reverse shared removal; the replicate consumes that capture.
- `session_glue/commands/delete_synced.rs`: scoped deletes (`expected_id != 0`) delete a live companion only on id match; `companion_expected_id == 0` now preserves it. Unscoped legacy deletes keep unconditional companion teardown.
- `types/runtime.rs`: field doc states the pre-removal capture + scoped-preserve semantics.
- Regression: bounded queue-delay successor-reverse fixture end-to-end (forward removed, replacement companion survives), fan-out capture pin, scoped-zero preservation + unscoped control cells; `docs/log/15784.md`.

### Validation
- RED pre-fix (tests only on `f7c921ce29`): 3 failures — fan-out carried `0` vs expected `12670852`; replacement companion `13212057` torn down to 0; live companion `2` torn down to 0. Controls passed pre-fix.
- GREEN post-fix: `cargo +1.98.1 test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 15784 14666 10512` — 56 passed, 0 failed.
- Full suite: `cargo +1.98.1 test --bin xpf-userspace-dp` — 8815 passed / 71 failed, the identical 71-failure set as a pristine `origin/master` (`f7c921ce29`) baseline run (8811 passed / 71 failed): no new failures, +4 net new passing cells.
- Existing cells updated only where the corrected semantics require a captured id: `scoped_worker_delete_matched_removes_both_halves_10512`, `colliding_ordinary_close_retires_a_keeps_b10512` (now also pins the honest `0` capture for its no-shared-reverse fixture).

### Risk
Scoped deletes whose producers still cannot capture a companion id preserve a live companion instead of deleting it — bounded leak healed by the delete-drop sweep / age-out (the safe direction, same trade #14666 documented). Policy-batch (`handle_remove_policy_item`) and unconditional delete paths untouched. No wire-format change (`WorkerCommand` is in-process only).

## PR #15851 — cluster: revert deleted heartbeat, control-interface, and GARP settings on apply (#15669) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

## Summary
`Manager.UpdateConfig` wrote `hbInterval`, `hbThreshold`, and `controlInterface` only when the new config carried a positive/non-empty value, and wrote a redundancy group's `garpCounts` entry only for a positive `gratuitous-arp-count`. Deleting any of those stanzas latched the last committed value forever. - `gratuitous-arp-count` unset on a still-present RG → `garpCounts` entry deleted (absent = default burst; extends the #6027 removed-RG purge)

The timer-restart leg of the original report was already fixed by `ApplyCommittedHeartbeatTiming` (#7164) and is not re-implemented; the reverted defaults flow through that same divergence check, so deleting the timing stanza restarts a running heartbeat onto the defaults.

Existing tests that preset `m.controlInterface` directly before an `UpdateConfig` whose config did not author it encoded the latch; they now author `ControlInterface` on the config (one also clears the dataplane-arm monitor debt that authoring it now arms).

## Test report

- `pkg/daemon` control-interface preflight tests (#8987, which pin that `UpdateConfig` tracks the config-side field while the running heartbeat's interface is read separately): **pass**.

## PR #15858 — config: reject feed-less dynamic-address bindings and static collisions (#15685) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15685-campaign`

## Summary

Fixes #15685 (V15-02): `security dynamic-address address-name <name>` without a `profile feed-name` passed strict commit validation silently, shadowed any same-named static `address-book` entry, and permanently aborted userspace snapshot publication via `__unsupported_address__`.

## Why

`compileDynamicAddress` records an `address-name` even with no `feed-name`, producing a binding with zero `FeedNames`. The #3300 gate `validateDynamicAddressFeedReferencesStrict` only iterated *present* feed names, so the orphan committed clean. No fetch can ever populate it, so `SnapshotForBindings` omits it forever; userspace lowering treats a declared binding absent from the overlay as unrepresentable (checked *before* the static book), so a referencing policy lowers to `__unsupported_address__` and the whole snapshot publication is rejected permanently. The same ordering shadows a same-named static `address`/`address-set` (unready → static never enforces; ready → union enforced — never the single declared meaning).

## What

- `validateDynamicAddressFeedReferencesStrict`: error on `len(ab.FeedNames) == 0`, naming the binding and the missing `profile feed-name` (sorted walk, deterministic first error).
- New `validateDynamicAddressStaticCollisionStrict`: rejects any `address-name` colliding with a static `address`/`address-set` in the global or any zone-local book.
- Wired in `runEarlyStrictAndFolds` on the **pristine** books, after the #5676 collision gate and before the zone-local fold (bindings are keyed by authored name; userspace unqualifies zone-local tokens back to it).
- Both gates downgrade to warnings on tolerant load/peer-sync via `lenientDynamicAddressFeedRef` (#1960 no-brick; runtime stays fail-closed).
- Regression: `pkg/config/dynamic_address_no_profile_15685_test.go`; docs: `pkg/config/README.md`, `docs/log/15685.md`.

## Validation

- GREEN: `go test ./pkg/config -run TestDynamicAddressNoProfileRejected15685 -count=1 -v` — 9/9 subtests pass (bare, fail-mode-only, orphan-over-static, feed-backed-over-address, feed-backed-over-set, zone-local, lenient downgrade, valid control, deterministic first error).
- Siblings unchanged: `TestValidateDynamicAddressFeedReferences` 5/5, `TestValidateDynamicAddressFeedServerEndpoint` 6/6; targeted dynamic-address/address-book/NAT-address-name/feed suite passes except `TestCompileGolden4406`, which fails **identically on pristine `origin/master`** (pre-existing stale golden: tcp-mss `[0..65535]` vs `[64..65535]`, #15034 text).
- RED: on pristine master the new test does not build (`validateDynamicAddressStaticCollisionStrict` undefined); pre-fix gate returns nil for a zero-feed binding (source-inspected), matching the issue's executed probes (strict err=nil, warns=[]).
- `gofmt -l` clean; `go vet ./pkg/config` clean. (Full `pkg/config` run hit the 10m default timeout under parallel campaign load at `TestParseHeapDoesNotScalePastTheBudget_8597`; not used as evidence.)

## Risk

Strict commits with a feed-less `address-name` or one shadowing a static entry now fail and must be renamed / given a `profile feed-name` — intended Junos parity. Persisted configs still load tolerantly with warnings and keep fail-closed runtime behaviour; no dataplane, wire, or schema change.

Closes #15685

## PR #15864 — config: validate flow traceoptions packet-filter protocol (#15679) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15679-campaign`

## Summary

Fixes #15679 (V11-01): `security flow traceoptions packet-filter <name> protocol <proto>` had no commit validation, failed open on `protocol ""`, could not match numeric/named protocols in `TraceWriter`, and was omitted from `show security flow traceoptions`.

- **Commit validation**: `validateFlowTraceFlagsAndFiltersAST` rejects empty/unknown/`0`/out-of-range protocols in strict mode and warns + marks `InvalidPrefix` (match-none) in lenient mode, via `filterProtocolResolvable` (the in-package mirror of `appid.ProtocolNumber` — `pkg/config` cannot import `pkg/appid`); also rejects a `packet-filter` with none of `source-prefix`/`destination-prefix`/`protocol`. The `protocol` schema leaf is now typed (`validateFlowTraceProtocol15679`) so `SchemaValidate` rejects the same set. `compileFlow` marks `InvalidPrefix` for unresolvable/empty/`0` protocols and selector-less filters so lenient loads fail closed.
- **TraceWriter**: `traceFilter` now stores `protoNum uint8` + `hasProto bool` resolved via `appid.ProtocolNumber`, and `matchFilters` compares `rec.ProtocolNum` (legacy fallback to the rendered name only when `ProtocolNum==0`, mirroring `pkg/cli/monitor.go`). `normalizeTraceProto` (tcp/udp/icmp/icmpv6 only) is deleted, so numeric `47` and named `ospf`/`gre` filters match; unresolvable protocols fail closed.
- **Show**: both CLI (`pkg/cli/cli_show_flow.go`) and gRPC (`pkg/grpcapi/server_show_flow.go`) render ` proto=<value>`.

Deviation recorded: the issue text says validate with `appid.ProtocolNumber(v) != 0`, but that API returns `(uint8, bool)` here and `0` is a resolvable HOPOPT value; proto `0` is rejected for trace filters because the writer cannot distinguish an explicit proto-0 selector from "any protocol", so accepting it would silently widen.

## Tests

- RED on base: strict cases (`protocol ""`, `bogus`, `256`, `0`, bare `packet-filter pf1`) compiled clean, `SchemaValidate` accepted `bogus`, lenient recorded no warning, and named `ospf` trace filter did not match protocol 89.
- GREEN: `go test -run 'TestFlowTraceProto15679|TestFlowTraceFilter|TestFlowTraceoptions|TestTraceWriter|TestMatchFilters|TestTraceProto15679|TestNewTraceWriter|TestShowFlowTraceoptionsProto15679' ./pkg/config/ ./pkg/logging/ ./pkg/cli/ ./pkg/grpcapi/` passes. Full `pkg/logging` passes; `pkg/cli`/`pkg/grpcapi` full suites show only failures identical on unmodified `origin/master` (6960/9889/8629 families).

New regression tests: `pkg/config/flow_trace_proto_15679_test.go`, `pkg/logging/trace_proto_15679_test.go`, `pkg/cli/cli_show_flow_trace_proto_15679_test.go`, `pkg/grpcapi/show_flow_trace_proto_15679_test.go`. Log: `docs/log/15679.md`.

Closes #15679

## PR #15868 — nat: record synced persistent grants under resolved zones (#15676) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15676-campaign`

nat: record synced persistent grants under resolved zones (#15676)

Closes #15676

## Why

The HA standby's synced persistent-NAT permission recording folded the rule's authored `(from_zone, to_zone)` as the packet pair, while the active node mints under the flow's resolved zone pair. For a non-zone-scoped rule-set (interface-, routing-instance- or global-scoped, empty authored zones) the standby folded `("","")` and the active folded e.g. `("trust","wan")` — different grant buckets on the shared lease. After failover the promoted node's inbound persistent-NAT lookup, keyed by the admitting rule with the real packet pair, missed the synced grant and denied inbound the active had permitted.

## What

- Thread the already-resolved `SyncedNatZones` into `reserve_synced_on_first_pool_owner` (PASS 1 passes its resolved pair; PASS 2 passes the caller's `Option` verbatim) and prefer it when computing the grant scope via `persistent_rule_scope`, falling back to the rule's authored pair only when the resolved pair is unknown.
- Zone-scoped rules and the `synced_zones == None` fallback are byte-identical to before; one shared `flow_egress_scope` fixes both the port-bearing and address-only arms.
- New `tests_synced_persistent_zones_15676` regression module (interface-scoped, address-only, global, zone-scoped control, `None`-fallback guard) driving the real synced-reserve path and the production inbound-lookup spelling.
- Log: `docs/log/15676.md`.

## Validation

- RED (prod fix reverted, tests present): `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 15676` = 3 failed / 2 passed — interface, address-only and global cells fail on the (trust,wan) bucket assertion; zone-scoped control and `None` fallback pass.
- GREEN: same command = 5/5 (re-verified on the rebased head `d677a49c86`).
- Neighbours: `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 15133 14322 7360 6211` = 32/32.
- Full `nat::` module = 707 passed / 0 failed (single-threaded; one parallel run hit the pre-existing flaky `tests_match_counters_8447` cell, passing on rerun — unrelated, no counter path touched).
- Main agent to run: full `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp` suite before merge.

## Risk

Fail-closed only: the grant moves to the bucket the active used; no admission widens (arbitrary-remote assertion pins this). No wire, lease-identity or scope-encoding change; old peers and config drift keep the pre-#6211 fallback, so rolling upgrade is safe.

## PR #15873 — config: upsert feed-name entries by name on incremental set (#15682) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15682-campaign`

## Summary
Incremental `set security dynamic-address feed-server <srv> feed-name <feed>` followed by `feed-name <feed> path <path>` (or the same refinement across merged blocks) appended duplicate `FeedEntry` records for one feed name. The strict uniqueness gate then falsely rejected a single feed-server (`"s1" and "s1"`), and the lenient `feeds.Manager.Apply` path could keep the path-less first entry and drop the configured path.

## Changes

- GREEN post-fix: targeted suites pass (`15682|4913|12824|TestValidateDynamicAddressFeedReferences|TestPolicyThen3377`).
- Full `pkg/config` suite with/without this change on current origin/master: 181 failures in both runs (pre-existing at this head, incl. the #14139 IPsec family); the name-set diff is exactly the three #15682 tests turning green — zero new failures.

## PR #15875 — logging: resolve untranslated NAT fields to effective tuple in structured RT_FLOW (#15697) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15697-campaign`

Closes #15697

## Why
`formatStructuredMsg` rendered the wire NAT slots verbatim in `RT_FLOW_SESSION_CREATE`/`RT_FLOW_SESSION_CLOSE`. The decoders encode an absent rewrite as `0.0.0.0:0` (v4) or `[::]:0` (v6), so a non-NAT session emitted `nat-source-address="0.0.0.0" nat-source-port="0" …`, and an IP-only SNAT emitted `nat-source-port="0"` instead of the effective port. Junos vSRX reports the effective post-NAT tuple (= pre-NAT when untranslated); SIEM/forensic correlation read the zero placeholders as a distinct bogus tuple.

## What
- `pkg/logging/format_rtflow.go`: NAT fields resolved via new `resolveNATAddrPort(nat, origIP, origPort)` — per-component fallback to the original src/dst IP/port when the NAT component is empty, zero IP (`0.0.0.0` / any `::` spelling), or port `0`. Translated components (incl. NAT64 v4 under v6) unchanged. Wire format, decoders, `EventRecord` NAT semantics, and POLICY_DENY shape untouched.
- `pkg/logging/rtflow_nat_untranslated_15697_test.go`: direct fixtures (empty / `0.0.0.0:0` / `[::]:0`, SNAT-IP-only, DNAT-port-only, fully translated) plus `DecodeRawEventRecord` wire frames (v4 no-NAT create/close, SNAT-IP-only, v6 no-NAT), both CREATE and CLOSE.
- `docs/log/15697.md`: issue log.

## Validation
- RED pre-fix: tests fail with `nat-source-address="0.0.0.0" nat-source-port="0"`, v6 `"::"`, SNAT-IP-only port `"0"`.
- GREEN post-fix: `go test ./pkg/logging/ -run 15697` passes; full `go test ./pkg/logging/ -count=1` passes incl. #9321 SD goldens (ordinary translated records byte-identical).

## Risk
Observability only; no traffic/enforcement impact. A genuine translation to 0.0.0.0/port 0 (not a representable real rewrite) renders as the original tuple.

- `pkg/dhcp/dhcp.go`: field comment now states the actual semantics.
- `pkg/dhcp/renew_test.go`: `TestRunDHCPv4ForceDiscover15692` (DISCOVER at T1/T2 + lease held across failures + default renew/rebind unchanged) and `TestRunDHCPv4ForceDiscoverKeepsLeaseUntilExpiry15692`.

## Validation

## Risk
Low — default path is the identical exchange sequence; only the previously-dead `force-discover` configuration changes (from REQUEST renewal to the documented DISCOVER renewal). DHCPv6 untouched (no such option).

## PR #15878 — scheduler: gate overnight tails on start-date and reject inverted ranges (#15695) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15695-campaign`

Closes #15695

## Why
`overnightTailActive` ignored the date range of the day the window opened, so a 22:00-06:00 window activated on the morning of `start-date` even though it opened the day before the range began; a date-only `stop-date` leaked into exactly 00:00:00 of the following day; and an inverted `start-date > stop-date` range committed clean and never activated, silently.

## What
- `pkg/scheduler`: require yesterday's open instant (yesterday's local date + window start) to lie within the scheduler date range before honouring its post-midnight tail; make the date-only stop bound exclusive at the start of the following day (`!now.Before(stop+1day)`).
- `pkg/config`: new `validateSchedulerDateRangeStrict` rejects start instants not strictly before the effective stop bound (date-time stop exclusive at that instant; date-only stop exclusive next-day 00:00), wired into `runEarlyStrictAndFolds`; `lenientSchedulerDateRange15695` downgrades to a warning on tolerant load/peer-sync so persisted inverted ranges still boot (runtime already fails closed inactive for them).
- Docs: `pkg/scheduler/README.md`, `debian/changelog`, `docs/log/15695.md`.

## Validation
- New `pkg/scheduler/scheduler_15695_test.go`: phantom tail on start-date morning (daily, Monday-only per-day, date-time start), controls for start-date evening + next-morning tail, stop-date active 23:59:59 / inactive at exactly next-day 00:00:00 — pass.
- New `pkg/config/scheduler_date_range_15695_test.go`: inverted ranges rejected strict (hierarchical + flat), valid ranges incl. same-day date-only accepted, tolerant load warns and retains scheduler — pass.
- Existing #14726 overnight and #3988 local-tz date-range tests stay green; `go vet ./pkg/scheduler/ ./pkg/config/` clean; full `pkg/scheduler` suite passes.

## Risk
Strict commits carrying a previously-accepted inverted range now fail and must be corrected; tolerant loads warn instead of bricking. Schedulers whose stop-date is yesterday no longer run a post-midnight tail past the range end (previously incorrect).

## PR #15881 — logging: thread wire decision time through text syslog fanout (#15699) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15699-campaign`

## Why

`EventReader.logEvent` decoded the on-wire dataplane decision timestamp into `rec.Time` (`eventTimeFromWire`, #2470/#2511) and honored it in `EventBuffer`, `elapsed-time` and binary records, but the text fanout passed only `(severity, msg)` to `SyslogClient` and `LocalLogWriter`. Both sinks stamped `time.Now()` when their async worker dequeued the item, so under queue backlog the RFC 5424 / RFC 3164 / local-file header timestamp was systematically late — forensic ordering diverged from the decision instant Junos stamps on `RT_FLOW_*` / `RT_SCREEN_*` headers (V16-02, #15699).

## What

- `ts time.Time` added to `syslogEventWrite` (`syslog.go`) and `auditItem` (`audit_async_writer_9025.go`).
- New `SyslogClient.SendFromEventReaderAt` / `LocalLogWriter.SendFromEventReaderAt` carry `ts` through the bounded async queues; new `SendAt` on both sinks formats the header from `at`.
- `Send` / `SendFromEventReader` delegate with a zero timestamp; zero `at` falls back to now (`SyslogClient` via its `now()` seam), non-zero `at` is normalized to local time (the location pre-fix `time.Now()` stamps carried). Direct callers (aggregator `ForwardLogMsg`, `SyslogSlogHandler`) keep receive-time headers.
- `logEvent` passes `rec.Time` at both text fanout sites. Binary paths (already embed `rec.Time.UnixNano()`) and `TraceWriter` (already formats `rec.Time`) untouched.
- Regression cells in `pkg/logging/event_decision_time_15699_test.go`; README note; `docs/log/15699.md`.

## Validation

- **RED** (production reverted via a worktree-local patch file, fanout cells kept): every format failed with the dequeue wall clock (e.g. `2026-10-19T16:02:35.465-07:00`) instead of the `2026-01-02T03:04:05.678Z` decision stamp; the full test file also fails to build pre-fix (`SendAt`/`SendFromEventReaderAt` undefined).
- **GREEN**: `go test ./pkg/logging/ -run 'TestEventReaderPreservesWireDecisionTime' -count=1` passes (sd-syslog / standard / structured on both sinks, At-variant and zero-fallback cells); full `go test ./pkg/logging/ -count=1` passes (9.5s); targeted `-race` run passes.

## Risk

Only EventReader-dispatched records change header time — to the decision instant already shown by `show security log` and binary records. Queue payloads grow by one `time.Time` per item; drop/retire accounting unchanged. No fail-open change: severity/category gates and queue-full drop counting are untouched.

Closes #15699

## PR #15883 — vrrp: apply day-2 timer updates to running MASTER/BACKUP timers (#15689) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15689-campaign`

vrrp: apply day-2 timer updates to running MASTER/BACKUP timers (#15689)

Closes #15689

## Why
`updateConfigHeld` signalled `configUpdatedCh`, but `StateMaster` never consumed it: an `advertise-interval` shrink on a live MASTER left `advertTimer` on its old arm (up to the full old interval, e.g. 60s/255s) while BACKUP peers timed out on the new cadence — a dual-MASTER split-brain window. The undrained 1-buffered token leaked across a MASTER→BACKUP transition into `stepBackup`. There, updates with no armed hold were ignored (cold-start BACKUP stuck at 3× the old interval, up to ~765s), and any edit unconditionally disarmed an armed preempt hold, restarting its countdown.

## What
- `updateConfigHeld` records a before/after snapshot (`configChange15689`: advertise interval, effective priority via new lock-held `effectivePriorityLocked`, hold-time) under `vi.mu` before signalling.
- Extracted `stepMaster` from `run()` (mirrors the `stepBackup` seam) with a `configUpdatedCh` arm: token always drained; on interval/effective-priority change it immediately `sendAdvert(getPriority())` and re-arms `advertTimer` at the new interval.
- `stepBackup`: armed hold disarmed only on hold-time change or lost preempt premise (`shouldPreemptObservedMaster` false, #2900 preserved), otherwise the elapsed countdown is preserved; unarmed BACKUP re-arms `masterDownTimer` when the no-learned-master fallback shrank or preemption became warranted (`backupConfigUpdateNeedsMasterDownReset`).
- Regression tests in `pkg/vrrp/instance_config_update_15689_test.go` incl. report acceptance tests (`MaxAdverInt==10` within 250ms on 60000→100ms shrink; stale token does not disarm hold).
- `pkg/vrrp/README.md`, `debian/changelog`, `docs/log/15689.md` updated.

## Validation
- New `TestVRRPMaster_*`/`TestVRRPBackup_*` (7 tests) pass; `TestHold*`/`TestPreempt*`/`TestUpdateInstances`/`TestRun_*` pass; `-race` clean on subset; `go vet`/`gofmt` clean.
- Full `pkg/vrrp` run: one pre-existing failure (`TestRethOwnershipCollectorsUseTheSharedPredicate/RethVIPsForRG`) verified identical on pristine `origin/master`.

## Risk
One extra immediate MASTER advert on interval/priority change and fresher BACKUP master-down re-arms on the day-2 path only; no wire, election, or VIP-actuation changes.

## PR #15886 — show: add show vrrp, include RETH instances, price GetVRRPStatus (#15690) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15690-campaign`

## Why

Three interconnected VRRP visibility defects (report V36-04):

1. Local CLI `show security vrrp` collected only generic per-interface `vrrp-group` instances. On a chassis cluster whose VIPs live on RETH instances it printed `No VRRP groups configured`, while gRPC `GetVRRPStatus` and REST `/vrrp` reported them.
2. The top-level Junos spelling `show vrrp` existed on no surface: no `cmdtree` node, so `Canonicalize` returned `CanonicalUnknown` and both CLI dispatchers rejected it.
3. `GetVRRPStatus` sat in `methodsWithoutCanonicalCommand` with the stale rationale "no `show vrrp` node exists", so the gRPC gate failed closed (`no canonical command to evaluate`) for every regex-restricted login class — and the REST twin route `GET /api/v1/security/vrrp` was denied the same way.

## What

- `pkg/cli`: `showVRRP` appends `vrrp.CollectRethInstances(cfg, c.cluster.LocalPriorities())` when the cluster manager is wired, matching the gRPC/REST handlers.
- `pkg/cmdtree`: add `show > vrrp`; dispatch `case "vrrp"` in both `pkg/cli` and `cmd/cli` to the existing `showVRRP` / `GetVRRPStatus` path. `show security vrrp` is unchanged.
- `pkg/grpcapi` + `pkg/api`: move `GetVRRPStatus` to `methodCanonicalCommand` as `show vrrp` and map the REST VRRP route to the same canonical string (the tables' own cross-surface rule).
- Scope cut: `brief`/`summary`/`detail`/`interface` sub-spellings are not modelled — no selector grammar exists on either VRRP node or handler.

## Validation

RED on pristine `origin/master` (`9e04c0d989`) with only the new test files copied in: local RETH row missing (`No VRRP groups configured`), `handleShow(show vrrp)` = unknown command on both CLIs, `Canonicalize("show vrrp")` = `CanonicalUnknown`, `GetVRRPStatus` unmapped.

GREEN after the fix — new cells drive the real dispatchers/handlers, not the collector: local RETH fixture (reth0/RG 1, group 101, VIP `10.0.61.1/24`) with and without a cluster manager, remote fake-client dispatch for both spellings, `authorizeRPCCommand` under unrelated-deny / `^show ` allow / `^show vrrp$` deny classes, and `Canonicalize` for both spellings plus the `show vr` abbreviation. Neighbouring guards pass (`TestEveryPricedMethodIsMappedOrNamedAbsent7172`, `TestEveryMappedCommandIsCanonical7172`, REST route census). Full suites show only pre-existing base failures verified identical on a sibling pristine worktree (`pkg/api` `TestEmitDropClassCounters_4768` panic, `cmd/cli` value-slot census, `pkg/grpcapi` NAT/ShowText cells).

## Risk

A class denying only `show security vrrp` no longer matches the gRPC/REST charge (now the canonical `show vrrp`); `deny ^show ` covers both spellings. Classes with no regexes are unaffected. No data-plane or election behaviour changes.

Closes #15690
