## PR #15887 — config: merge ip-monitoring preferred routes across duplicate policy blocks (#15705) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15705-campaign`

Closes #15705

## Summary

Fixes the #15705 defect: `compileIPMonitoring` rebuilt a fresh `PreferredRoute` list for every repeated `policy <name>` block and appended it without destination deduplication.

- A split refinement (`next-hop` in block 1, `preferred-metric` only in block 2) minted a metric-only route whose empty next-hop failed strict validation, so the commit was rejected instead of merged.
- A restated next-hop in block 2 produced a duplicate entry that lost to the first entry in `computeOverlayLocked`'s winner resolution, so the operator's override never actuated.

The compiler now seeds the route map from `existing.PreferredRoutes` keyed by `(routing-instance, canonical destination)` (`staticRouteMergeKey`) before compiling each block, canonicalises the `compilePreferredRoutes` key the same way, and assigns the merged slice back. Attributes merge per-field, last writer wins — exactly what the merged single block (and the flat-set spelling) compiles to.

## Census note

The issue asked to remove `"services ip-monitoring policy"` and `"services ip-monitoring policy xpfname then preferred-route routing-instance"` from `dupConservationSkipped8436`. Measured after the fix, the generic census still cannot probe either site for fixture-synthesis reasons unrelated to this defect (no probeable fixture without a real rpm sibling; container-only children), so deleting the rows would fail the pinned census as stale entries. They stay; the dedicated regression tests are the probe, mirroring the #15006 disposition. Full reasoning in `docs/log/15705.md`.

## Validation

- `TestIPMonitoring.*15705`: RED pre-fix (3 strict rejections + override duplicate), GREEN after (5/5), including routing-instance and canonical-destination (`0.0.0.1/0` vs `0.0.0.0/0`) merges plus a distinct-routes control.
- `pkg/ipmon` `TestOverlaySingleRouteAfterCompilerMerge15705`: the merged policy actuates exactly one overlay entry.
- Neighbouring `TestIPMonitoringFlatSet/Hierarchical/Validation`, sibling tests, and the #8436 census pass with unchanged counts; `go vet`/`gofmt` clean.
- Pre-existing failures on this HEAD (`TestIPMonitoringInterfaceNextHop*`, `TestDuplicateBlockConservationIsPinned8436`) reproduce identically with the fix stashed — not this change.

## Risk

Configs that silently kept duplicate routes now compile the union with last-writer merging (Junos/flat-set semantics); no new rejection is introduced and lenient loads merge identically.

## PR #15890 — userspace-dp: suppress hop-limit=0 ICMPv6 rejection when configured (#15707) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15707-campaign`

Why:
`system internet-options no-ipv6-reject-zero-hop-limit` was ignored by the
userspace dataplane (no snapshot field, ICMPv6 Time Exceeded generated
unconditionally), while the daemon wrote `0` to
`/proc/sys/net/ipv6/icmp/ratelimit` — which *disables* ICMPv6 error rate
limiting (0 = unlimited in `icmpv6_xrlim_allow`) and was never restored
on unset. The compact spelling `system internet-options
no-ipv6-reject-zero-hop-limit;` compiled the flag to false, and local
CLI vs gRPC `show system internet-options` diverged (raw config text vs
typed field).

What:
- Wire v60 -> v61 (both planes, exact-equality fenced): `ConfigSnapshot.no_ipv6_reject_zero_hop_limit` populated from the compiled config.
- Dataplane: `ForwardingState.no_ipv6_reject_zero_hop_limit`; `build_local_time_exceeded_v6` + request fast path suppress the error only for packets that arrived with hop limit 0 (hop-limit=1 still expires; IPv4 untouched).
- Daemon: bogus `ratelimit=0` write removed; `reconcileICMPv6Ratelimit` restores the kernel default 1000 ms if a prior binary left the knob at 0.
- Compiler: reads `Keys[1:]`/packed bodies, admits `(internet-options, no-ipv6-reject-zero-hop-limit)` to `compactNormalizeInScope`, extras collector scans the modelled leaf's `Keys[1:]`.
- CLI renders the same typed view as gRPC.

Validation:
- Config regression tests RED pre-fix (compact spellings false, extras empty) -> GREEN.
- Rust: 4 tests GREEN (suppressed at hop-limit 0, control unset, hop-limit=1 still sent, snapshot wiring).
- Daemon/snapshot/CLI Go tests GREEN; protocol lockstep tests GREEN.
- Neighbouring failures (`TestCompactNormalizeScopePreservesCompiledResult8690`, `wire_invariant_default_specimens`, several grpcapi show tests) base-attributed on origin/master `9e04c0d989`.

Risk:
Rolling upgrade: v61 fences a v60 helper rather than letting it ignore the
flag. Lab verify (hop-limit=0 packet on loss cluster; sysctl after
deleting the stanza) recorded as deferred in `docs/log/15707.md`.

Closes #15707

## PR #15892 — config: model dns-proxy subtree for set/delete round-trip (#15698) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15698-campaign`

Closes #15698

Why:
`system services dns` was modelled childless (`children: nil`), so the flat-set path collapsed `set system services dns dns-proxy forwarders 1.1.1.1` onto ONE leaf node. `DeletePath` then refused with the #8992 packed-run error ("ELIDED ... packed together"), the stanza was undeletable piecemeal, and the FormatSet round-trip left residue. A bare `set system services dns` leaf beside a braced dns container also shadowed the proxy from the compiler: `FindChild("dns")` returned the bare leaf first, `hasDNSProxyChild` saw no children, and the unimplemented-runtime commit warning never fired for that shape.

- `pkg/config/schema_system.go`: model `dns` as a container with a `dns-proxy` child (`interface`, `default-domain`, `forwarders` as a wildcard value-container, `view <name>` with `default-domain`/`forwarders`, `cache-size`) so `SetPath`, `DeletePath`, and tab-completion treat `dns` and `dns-proxy` as containers. Bare `set system services dns` still terminates at the `dns` node as a flag leaf.
- `pkg/config/compiler_system.go`: iterate over `svcNode.FindChildren("dns")` instead of `FindChild("dns")`, and check `node.Keys[1:]` plus `child.Keys[1:]` in `hasDNSProxyChild`.
- New regression cells in `pkg/config/dns_proxy_schema_15698_test.go`; log in `docs/log/15698.md`.

Not changed: the DNS proxy runtime stays unimplemented (`docs/next-features/dns-proxy.md`); the accepted-but-not-served warning behaviour is unchanged. No `closedWorld` was added to the `dns` subtree, so unmodelled Junos dns-proxy keywords still import for vSRX compatibility.

Validation:
- RED pre-fix at `9e04c0d989`: `SetPath` built leaf `[dns-proxy forwarders 1.1.1.1]`; `DeletePath` errored with the ELIDED message; the bare+proxy tree compiled with `DNSProxyConfigured=false`.
- GREEN: `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestDNSProxy.*15698|TestDNSProxyWarned|TestServicesDNSResolvedOwnerWarned' -count=1` passes (full FormatSet round-trip, single-forwarder delete, whole-stanza delete with no residue, bare-sibling warning); `TestParser|TestDeletePath|TestSetPath` pass. Compact inventory unchanged (30 pre-existing NEW compact-blind sites, none under `dns`).

Risk:
The four new dns-proxy leaves classify as blind `unreachable` in the #7484 spelling gate because the compiler records them only as `DNSProxyConfigured` presence; the gate ceilings (162/51/197) are already exceeded by unrelated master drift (measured base 175/68/220 vs this change's 179/68/219), so no ceiling was silently bumped here.

## PR #15894 — nftables: match ct state invalid at raw priority for RST drops (#15727) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-19)

Branch: `fix/15727-campaign`

Why: rstDropExprs matched ct state & 0x4f == 0, but Linux nft_ct_get_eval never writes state 0 (INVALID, UNTRACKED, or a tracked ctinfo bit), so SNAT/interface-NAT RST suppression never fired. At filter priority the OUTPUT conntrack hook (-200) also attaches a NEW entry to the locally generated RST before the rule evaluates, so even an INVALID predicate cannot match there.

What: match ct state invalid exactly (mask == value == CtStateBitINVALID) in rstDropExprs and move the xpf_dp_rst output chain to raw priority (-300), where the RST is still entry-less and reports INVALID. Correct the #14949 oracle to the INVALID mask/value, add a live netns test that installs the real table and counts genuine no-socket RSTs plus a tracked negative control, and update README/afxdp docs and docs/log/15727.md. NOT changed: UNTRACKED is not matched (it needs a NOTRACK decision a locally generated RST never carries) and no conntrack sysctl is touched.

Validation: unit RED pre-fix (mask 4f000000 vs want 01000000; cmp 00000000 vs want 01000000) then GREEN; live RED pre-fix (counter 0 -> 0 under unshare -rn) and still RED with only the predicate fixed at filter priority, GREEN after both parts (counter 0 -> 3, tracked control unmoved). go vet clean, gofmt clean on touched files.

Risk: chain priority change is operator-visible in nft listings (priority raw instead of 0); the drop scope itself only narrows to the intended conntrack-less class. tcp_loose=1 mid-stream pickup cannot attach to the locally generated RST (nf_reset_ct detaches; a lone RST creates no entry), recorded as residual in docs/log/15727.md.

Closes #15727

## PR #15911 — config: validate every OSPF MD5 rollover key (#15715) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-20)

Branch: `fix/15715-campaign`

Closes #15715

## Why
`validateFRRAuthValuesStrict` checked only the scalar `AuthKey`, which `compileProtocols` overwrites with the last keyed md5 entry, so a rollover carrying a whitespace key beside a valid one compiled clean and the FRR renderer silently dropped the bad key (or the whole interface block). `validateOSPFAuthKeyPresenceStrict` accepted a rollover when ANY entry was non-empty, so an empty/keyless md5 entry beside a valid one was silently dropped at render instead of rejected per-entry as Junos does (report V44-01 Cases A/B/C).

- `validateFRRAuthValuesStrict`: check every `AuthMD5Keys` entry by key-id (`md5 <key-id> key`) before the scalar `AuthKey` check (kept for simple/legacy configs).

- `compileProtocols`: coalesce same-key-ID fragments (inline `md5 1;` beside group `md5 1 { key ...; }`, #14414) instead of appending a duplicate keyless entry.
- Tests: new `ospf_md5_rollover_multi_key_15715_test.go` (Cases A/B/C, routing-instance, lenient warnings, valid controls); #14397 empty+valid control -> all-valid; #2889 OSPF assertion -> per-key field name. `docs/log/15715.md`.

- GREEN: `go test ./pkg/config/ -run '15715|14414|14397|TestFRRAuthValueWhitespaceRejected|TestOSPFAuthKeyPresence|OSPF'`, `go test ./pkg/frr/ -run '14414|14388|14397|8443|OSPF|Auth'` pass; gofmt/go vet clean on touched files.

## PR #15912 — config: reject login users referencing undefined classes post-compile (#15717) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-20)

Branch: `fix/15717-campaign`

Closes #15717

## Defect (V44-04, all three deep-review lanes MATERIAL)

Reproduced in-lane on `origin/master` before the fix:

1. **Case B**: `CompileConfig` on `set system login user bob class totally-undefined-class` returned `err=nil` — compile never ran `SchemaValidate` and no post-compile gate checked `cfg.System.Login.Users[*].Class`.
2. **Case A**: a class defined only in an un-applied `groups { staged-rbac { ... } }` satisfied `validateLoginClassRef` (configstore passes the pre-expansion tree as `defsSource`; `collectSchemaRefs` collects from group bodies applied or not), then `ExpandGroups` discarded the group, leaving user `alice` with `Classes=[]` — accepted clean.
3. **Case C**: `collectSchemaRefs` used singular `FindChild("system")` / `FindChild("class-of-service")` in group bodies, missing definitions in a second sibling block.

Runtime impact is fail-closed (unknown class ⇒ no permissions), so this is a silent lockout/misconfig, not a privilege gain. Junos rejects the shape at commit against the effective config.

## Fix

- `validateLoginUserClassReferencesStrict` (new, `compiler_validate_strict.go`): post-compile gate — every login user's non-empty class must resolve via `ResolveClassPermissions(cfg, class)`; first offender rejected naming user and class. Wired **dead-last** in `runUniformGates` with the `lenientLoginUserClassRef` downgrade flag (tolerant boot/peer-sync warns, #1960 no-brick).
- `collectSchemaRefs`: sibling-aware collection (`FindChildren`) for `system` and `class-of-service` at top level and in group bodies.
- The permissive `defsSource` union is **deliberately kept** (peer-node `groups node1` definitions must keep satisfying shared references, #1319 PR 3); the post-compile gate is what makes the poisoning unreachable. See `docs/log/15717.md`.
- Two existing tests migrated (`TestUndefinedLoginClassStillRejected`, `TestLoginClassUndefinedAcrossLoginBlocksStillRejected13536`): strict compile now rejects before `SchemaValidate`; both keep their `SchemaValidate` assertion via the lenient compile.

## Validation

- New `pkg/config/login_class_gate_15717_test.go`: **RED** on pristine `origin/master` (6 failures), **GREEN** after — strict rejection for undefined and unapplied-group classes, lenient warning + stanza retention, positive controls (built-in / top-level custom / applied-group custom / classless user), and both Case C sibling legs.
- Targeted `pkg/config` login/schema/group/CoS suites and `pkg/configstore` commit suites pass. Pre-existing failures on untouched master (`TestCompileGolden4406`, `TestHB166_T5*`, `TestCompileCoS*`, WireGuard group test) fail identically with and without this change.

Why: `deletePath` removed the whole node matched by `findElidedNodeForPath` whenever the remaining path prefixed its packed `Keys`, and `setInactiveAtPath` toggled that whole node when the path exhausted the keys. On a brace-elided node headed by a named container (`interface ge-0/0/0.0 passive;`, `security-zone trust host-inbound-traffic { ... }`, `unit 0 family inet address ...;`), deleting/deactivating a descendant (`passive`, `host-inbound-traffic`, `family inet`) deleted or deactivated the enclosing container and its braced body — the inverse of the operator's intent.

What: `elidedContainerDescendant15714` (`pkg/config/elided_delete_8992.go`) proves the descendant shape (exactly one statement; container first step consuming fewer keys than the address; remainder past a complete child statement, or a body-holding/named descendant below the root) while excluding whole-statement shapes (fully packed `chassis cluster strict-session-auth;`, container-itself, bare leaves). On a proven descendant, `deletePath`/`setInactiveAtPath` brace the node in place via `braceCompactStatement12508` and let the normal descent delete/toggle only the descendant; a refused descent restores the original elided spelling. Packed-run (#8992), bracketed-group (#9799), packed-member toggle (#9793), interface-family (#12661) and repeated-sibling (#12714) handling unchanged and in order. Regression tests + `docs/log/15714.md`.

Neighbour suites (`TestElided*`, `TestToggle*`, `TestCompact*`, `TestPacked*`) show no failures beyond the base-attributed set on unmodified origin/master.

Risk: a successful descendant edit keeps that one container in braced spelling (same rewrite `SetPath` performs on compact leaves, #12508); refused edits restore the original spelling. Unresolvable descendants remain refusals.

## Summary

## PR #15925 — userspace-dp: admit co-moved fabric punts via owner-gated ambiguous stamps (#15916) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-20)

Branch: `fix/15916-campaign`

## Summary

Fixes the #15916 F1 blocker: in the **all-data-RGs-on-one-node** placement (RG1+RG2 on the receiver, RG0 on the peer), the fabric-punt validators rejected every punt by construction — V1b (`zone_encoded_fabric_stamp_valid`) requires NOT ALL of the claimed zone's RGs to be locally forwarding-active, and the V2 check requires the stamped interface's RG to be peer-owned. With every data RG local, both fail, the stamp is `Invalid`, and the frame is dropped before session lookup: 100% blackhole for any flow that ingressed the non-owner's reth member. All prior live rounds used the one-RG-per-node shape, where both checks pass by construction.

## Approach

The all-local shape is byte-identical for (a) the legitimate co-moved punt and (b) a forged clone — no receiver-only predicate can separate them, and a cryptographic stamp is infeasible at stage 9 per the measured baselines in `docs/log/10105.md` (Ed25519 88µs/verify; even HMAC is 3.4 cores @1Mpps) and would need a wire/flag-day change.

This PR therefore introduces a three-way stage-9 disposition:

- **ProvedPeerPunt** — unchanged: at least one bound RG not locally active (+ V2 exact-RG peer-owned for scoped stamps).
- **AmbiguousLocalZone** (new) — V1a holds, zone is RG-bound, but every bound RG is locally active. NOT dropped at stage 9; the claimed zone is withheld from every policy/NAT/host-inbound consumer until the existing V2 owner-RG gate (`gate_fabric_zone_override_on_owner_rg`) proves the packet's own resolution is locally owned (`promote_ambiguous_fabric_zone`). Promotion is wired at the flow-backed, flowless, and MissingNeighbor gates; V2 scope ifindex promotes only with the zone; the flow's routing domain keys from the claimed zone (never MAIN / domain 0 on RI nodes).
- **Invalid** — unchanged terminal drop (wrong dst MAC, unbound/empty zone, unknown V2 identity).

## Security posture change (deliberate, documented)

The documented shared-segment clone residual widens: pre-fix it needed a live RG split; post-fix a forged stamp whose packet resolves to a locally-owned egress is adjudicated **exactly as a local ingress in the claimed zone** — no more, no less. Flows whose resolution is not locally owned promote nothing. The backup side is unchanged (nothing promotes). `docs/fabric-cross-chassis-fwd.md` is updated throughout (V1b/V2 sections, resulting posture, both residual mentions); direct-attached/MACsec fabric remains the closure.

## Test plan

- [x] New regression cells (all-data-RGs-on-one-node shape):
  - `co_moved_punt_admitted_when_all_data_rgs_local_15916` — v4 **and** v6: stage-9 Ambiguous precondition, `invalid_fabric_stamp_drops == 0`, session (fwd+reverse) + forward
  - `co_moved_host_inbound_punt_admitted_when_all_data_rgs_local_15916`
  - `co_moved_v2_scoped_stamp_is_ambiguous_without_scope_15916` — split control validates scoped; co-moved is Ambiguous with scope withheld
  - `ambiguous_stamp_on_routing_instance_node_never_falls_back_to_main_15916` — unpromotable RI ambiguous punt denies, no MAIN install
  - `zone_encoded_fabric_stamp_ambiguous_when_claimed_zone_rg_local_15916` (unit)
- [x] Repinned: old single-primary forged-deny cell renamed to `ambiguous_stamp_with_local_owner_is_adjudicated_like_local_ingress_15916` (asserts the documented residual); multi-RG all-local arm now expects Ambiguous
- [x] `cargo test`: 15916 (5), 6458 (10), fabric (212), 11061+15742 (27), full `tests_fabric_zone_stamp` module (44) — all pass
- [ ] Known unattributed failure: `poll_stages::arp_two_vlans_same_ip_distinct_logical_keys_2370` fails in neighbor-learning code this diff does not touch; baseline attribution was interrupted by a lane retarget notice and is **not claimed** either way — needs a baseline confirm before merge

## PR #15928 — vrrp: note preempt-hold arm baseline unconditionally and preserve in-send priority commits (#15927) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-20)

Branch: `fix/15927-vrrp-hold`

## What
Fixes the two GLM round-3 (#15922) residuals tracked in #15927:

1. **`armPreemptHold` conditional note (blocker):** the note fired only when
   `newHoldSec == snapSec`. In the accumulated in-window-revert interleaving —
   commit 60→1 pending, timer fires, hold snapshot 1s, revert 1→60 lands before
   the arm — the pending record nets 60→60, the note skipped, and the config
   consumer preserved the 1s hold (takeover ~59s early against a live
   lower-priority master). The note is now unconditional:
   `oldHoldSec := snapSec`, the value the hold timer was just armed under, so
   every interleaving reads truthfully.
2. **Consumer trailing arm erasing a priority-only commit (minor):** the
   trailing `armAdvertTimer` note also baselined `oldEffectivePrio := current`.
   A priority-only commit landing during the consumer's `sendAdvert` (wire
   still carried the old priority) netted to no-change, suppressing the
   correction advert for up to one interval. Arms now note only the interval
   dimension they consumed (`armIntervalAppliedLocked` replaces the combined
   note helpers); priority is baselined only by
   `noteAdvertPriority(sentPriority)` from the value a send actually carried —
   captured before the send at the consumer send, periodic advertise, and
   peer-resign immediate send sites.

Regression tests in the #15920 coalesce file pin both interleavings, including
the required hold regression (commit 60→1, timer fires, snapshot 1s, revert
1→60 before arm ⇒ consumer disarms; never preserves 1s).

## PR #15938 — userspace: fail loudly on empty-policy snapshot mismatch (#15742) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-20)

Branch: `fix/harden-empty-policy-snapshot`

Refs #15937, Refs #15742.

## Why
Commit 670274c712 dropped `Policies: policies` from the full snapshot builder while `Summary.PolicyCount` still reported 2 — the helper installed `policies=[]` and default-denied all transit silently; nobody noticed until live probes. PR #15921 restored the field. This PR (driven by #15937) makes the *class* fail loudly and immediately at every layer, each independently sufficient.

## Design (acceptance accounting in one place)
- **Builder invariant** — `validateSnapshotPolicyInvariant` compares the published set against `expectedPolicyCount`: the effective POST-QUARANTINE ground truth (lower → exact quarantine scrub → count survivors). Fully-quarantined configs expect zero and pass; vanished non-quarantined rules error the compile (fail closed).
- **Send-site gate** — at the single `apply_snapshot` funnel, a PARTIAL publish's `len(Policies)` must agree with BOTH its self-declared `Summary.PolicyCount` AND the manager's `expectedPolicyCount` stamp (the last ACCEPTED full count). Full builds bypass the stamp arm via an unexported `fullBuild` provenance bit (builder-set, Compile-affirmed, never on the wire/hash); `stripSingleUseCommitMetadata` clears provenance (and the clear marker) on every partial clone.
- **Single choke** — the stamp is committed ONLY in the send funnel's two success arms (first try AND the #9520 content-conflict republish), for `fullBuild` snapshots, where acceptance is known. Every publisher (Compile, overlay, scheduler, link-refresh, capture, worker-arm, deferred sync — including latch-preserving first-acceptance partials and tail-errored Compiles whose apply already landed) passes through it, so no acceptance path can leave the stamp stale. The status reconciler remains as backstop for landings no response confirmed. One callsite family owns the invariant.
- **Helper (Rust)** — two arms refuse the whole apply before any mutation (prior retained, sticky `snapshot_policy_mismatch_total`, `ERROR` logged): (a) `summary.policy_count != policies.len()`; (b) empty-over-nonempty install, regardless of counts — UNLESS the snapshot carries the authorized-clear marker. Legitimate empty *first* apply succeeds.
- **Authorized clear (no protocol bump)** — additive `clear_policies` (`omitempty` + `serde(default)`). ONLY `Manager.Compile` sets it; the send site spends it after the send; the strip helper removes it from partial clones; `syncSnapshotLocked` re-marks a retained FULL-BUILD clear from its own provenance in both landing states. Delete-all applies end-to-end; lost-response clear retries converge autonomously.
- **Observability** — structured ERROR logs on every refusal; Prometheus `xpf_userspace_snapshot_policy_mismatch_total` + `xpf_userspace_last_snapshot_policy_count` on the existing status collect (no new endpoint); `Last snapshot policies: N` in the existing status display.

## Tests (production paths, mutation-proven)
- Real `Manager.Compile` e2e: count change, clear-all (fails if the Compile marker line is neutered), and **tail-error acceptance** (`TestCompileTailErrorStampsAcceptedCount`: helper accepts, status-sync tail fails, stamp follows the accepted count, accepted-count partial publishes).
- **Overlay-first acceptance** (`TestOverlayFirstAcceptanceCommitsStamp`) and **conflict-republish arm** (`TestConflictRepublishArmCommitsStamp`: G refused on content conflict, G+1 lands, stamp commits from the republish arm — neutering ONLY that arm turns exactly this test RED).
- Lost-response status reconciliation (+stale-status negative), unlanded-clear retry through real `syncSnapshotLocked`, both-zeroed partial refusal, fully-quarantined build, nested-`Summary` census. Fail-on-revert verified for the dropped `Policies:`/nested `PolicyCount:` literals AND for each choke arm independently.

## Validation (corrected counts)

## PR #15940 — userspace: fix recursive m.mu deadlock in apply-time rebuild (#15939) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-20)

Branch: `fix/15939-rgprimary-deadlock`

## Summary
Fixes the recursive `m.mu` deadlock from #15939: `syncSnapshotLocked` (under `m.mu`) → `prepareSnapshotForApply` → `rebuildDerivedSectionsAfterRevalidate` → `rgPrimaryNow()` re-taking `m.mu`.

## Why
`statusLoop` holds `m.mu` across `syncSnapshotLocked`; when link revalidation moved/dropped an interface row, the derived-section rebuild called `rgPrimaryNow()`, which locks `m.mu` again — Go mutexes are not reentrant, so the tick deadlocked (recurring userspace full-suite hang, no cluster needed). Audit found every other `prepareSnapshotForApply` caller (Compile apply, scheduler, overlay, capture-authority, worker-arm) also holds `m.mu`, so the class was wider than the tick; `Compile`'s two direct `rgPrimaryNow()` build calls run off-lock and keep the locking variant.

## What
- `manager.go`: split `rgPrimaryNow` following the `rgProviderWiredForLocked` pattern (#15924) — new `rgPrimaryNowLocked()` returns the provider without locking; `rgPrimaryNow()` delegates after locking.
- `apply_snapshot_identity_9520.go`: the rebuild snapshots the provider once via `rgPrimaryNowLocked()` for both `buildRouteSnapshotsWithRGPrimary` and `markConnectedRGPeerOwned` (previously two separately-locked reads could observe different providers mid-rebuild).
- Regression `TestSyncSnapshotLockedMovedInterfaceRowNoDeadlock15939`: drives `syncSnapshotLocked` under `m.mu` with the #14209/#15043 moved+dropped interface fixture and a wired provider; 30s guard reports the deadlock instead of hanging the suite; asserts one send with rebuilt mirror rows (ifindex 29).
- `docs/log/15939.md`.

## Validation
- `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run 'TestSyncSnapshotLockedMovedInterfaceRowNoDeadlock15939|TestRepublishRetainsRebuiltDerivedSections15043|TestPrepareSnapshotForApplyRebuilds|15919|15742|TestRevalidate' -count=1` PASS
- FAIL-ON-REVERT verified: restoring `rgPrimaryNow()` in the rebuild fails at the 30s guard with the deadlock message.

## Risk
Low: lock-discipline-only change; provider semantics (#15919) and wire shape unchanged.

## PR #15960 — userspace: egress split-RG fabric return on LAN binding (#15958) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-20)

Branch: `fix/15958-fabric-return-lan-egress`

## Summary
Fixes the split-RG fabric return blackhole on fw1 (#15958, split-RG sibling of #15742): the return leg arrived stamped on the fabric binding, counted `forward_candidate`, and never transmitted on the LAN egress — with no counter and no exception-ring entry.

**Root cause (instrumented, hit-exit=20):** both the ICMP echo-reply and TCP ACK shapes died at a `StaleSourceNat` revocation in the companion-less `NoLocalEntry` arm of `source_nat_revocation_on_session_hit_with_ingress`. That arm reconstructs the forward SNAT decision from the reverse row, then demands `metadata.forward_ingress_vlan_id` — which is `None` by construction for an HA-synced reverse companion (reverse synthesis zeroes its ingress identity; a fabric-admitted forward has `ingress_ifindex 0`; HA session sync never carries the field). Every locally installed reverse session without its forward half was therefore revoked on its first fabric-arriving packet. Candidate A (`interface_nat_local_resolution` claiming 172.16.80.8 as `LocalDelivery/14`) was tested and is not the sink — the cached LAN `ForwardCandidate` is served first. Candidate B (cross-UMEM pending fallback) was not the sink either — the same cross-UMEM harness transmits once the revocation is gone.

## What changed
- `policy_revalidation.rs` (fold round): the provenance-only revocation declines for a plain dynamic source-NAT row in the construction shape — fabric row, `ingress_ifindex == 0`, no forward VLAN — covering both the scope-less companion and the scoped V2 synced companion (`nat_scope_ifindex: Some`, `forward_ingress_vlan_id: None` by construction, session_sync.rs:581/:496). Rows with an observed identity or recorded forward VLAN keep the fail-close; static rows keep their validity arm. NAT64/NPTv6 are excluded (type guard: the production `None`-provenance shape is pinned by `fabric_nat64_nptv6_missing_provenance_still_fails_closed_15958`, and the type conjunct independently by `fabric_typed_dynamic_provenance_still_fails_closed_15958` — `Some(false)` + type bit; deleting only `&& !(nat64 || nptv6)` reds exactly that cell, 10 passed/1 failed). V2 shape proven by `fabric_scoped_synced_companion_without_vlan_provenance_survives_15958`; scoped #13789 controls stay green.
- `flow_cache_hit.rs` (F1): a cached `tx_selection.drop` verdict on the early cached-drop arm now records `forward_build_failures` + a `transit_output_filter_drop` exception-ring entry, mirroring the slow-path twin. The previously claimed cache-fallback builder `None` arm was unreachable (the cached drop returns first) and its dead `else` is deleted; the guard test now exercises exactly the early cached-drop arm. Policer-only drops keep existing attribution.
- Tests: multi-binding poll driver (`txn_run_multi_binding_15958`), three packet egress cells on the live snapshot (scope-less ICMP, scope-less TCP, scoped-V2 TCP), validator cells for the NAT64/NPTv6 guard, the real HA-import NPTv6 wire shape, composed DNAT+SNAT, and unknown provenance, plus an F1 revert guard. A stray duplicate `#[test]` double-registering the NAT64 cell was removed. Changelog + `docs/log/15958.md` updated.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo +1.98.1 test _15958` — 11 passed (scope-less ICMP/TCP + scoped-V2 egress, NAT64/NPTv6 `None` guard, typed `Some(false)` type-conjunct pin, real-import NPTv6 wire, legacy-peer pin, composed DNAT+SNAT, unknown provenance, F1); type-conjunct-deletion mutant reds exactly the typed cell
- [x] `cargo +1.98.1 test --release split_rg_fabric_return` — 2 passed; `cached_drop_counts_forward_build_failure_15958` — 1 passed

- [x] `git diff --check` clean
- [ ] Live smoke (post-merge, smoke lane): deploy + re-run `test-v6-na-recovery-12495.sh` split-RG gate

## Round-3 fold (ef55442522)
- (1) Type conjunct re-pinned: new `fabric_typed_dynamic_provenance_still_fails_closed_15958` (`Some(false)` + NAT64/NPTv6 bit, source-only scoped row) — deleting only the type conjunct reds exactly it; the `None` cells stay green via the provenance conjunct.

## PR #15961 — vrrp: correct arm-applied interval growth on the wire, baseline priority at every MASTER send, and recheck hold-time at hold expiry (#15929) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-20)

Branch: `fix/15929-vrrp-inherited`

## Summary
Closes the three inherited coalescing gaps in #15929 (Codex review of PR #15928):

1. **Interval growth peer cadence** — a growth applied by a cfg-derived arm (periodic/consumer trailing `armAdvertTimer`) no longer cancels the peer correction: `sendAdvert` records the `MaxAdvertInt` it actually emitted (`wireAdvertIntervalMS`), and `decideMasterConfigAdvert` sends exactly one correction when the wire still carries the shorter cadence, re-arms only when the wire already matches, and stays silent only when armed==desired==wire.
2. **Unbaselined priority sends** — `becomeMaster` promotion and `updateVIPs` announce now `noteAdvertPriority(sentValue)`; the priority-0 resign/shutdown burst deliberately stays un-noted (sent after BACKUP publishes; a 0 baseline would fabricate a 0→live correction).
3. **Hold-expiry select race** — the hold-expiry case peeks (non-consuming) at the pending record and defers a pending `PreemptHoldTime` change to the `configUpdatedCh` disarm/revalidate path instead of promoting on the stale expiry.

Gap 1 is reproduced with a two-instance harness: the master's wire packets are fed into a real peer BACKUP, which flips its learned interval to 10s and stays BACKUP. Per the issue, reproduction came first: all new tests failed pre-fix (`[{200 10}]` only; pending `200->200`; promoted on attempt 1) and pass post-fix.

Refs #15929

## PR #15963 — test: fail back v6-na gate via operator reset+targeted sequence (#15959) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-20)

Branch: `fix/15959-v6na-failback`

## Why
Refs #15959. The #12495 gate's failback leg stranded RG2 past its 300s deadline on `61c7d45603` and `9e94cf62ab` (node0 left `secondary-hold Manual=yes`), yet a plain operator `failover redundancy-group 2 node 0` from fw1 returned RG2 at iter=1 (~1s). Diffing the gate sequence (hold release, request target, wait conditions) against the operator path (`/var/worktrees/smoke/final-restore.sh`, the #15742 targeted cells, `final3-failback-spot.sh`) shows the **script owned the contract defect**:

- A plain `request chassis cluster failover redundancy-group 2` is `ManualFailover`: a LOCAL yield — it parks the issuer in secondary-hold and clears its transfer-commit pin, and under `Preempt=no` never moves the RG to the peer. Issued as a "failback" on the current primary it strands exactly as recorded.
- Every convergent operator failback runs `failover reset redundancy-group 2` on the **target** node (releases the `secondary-hold Manual=yes` hold), then the **targeted** `failover redundancy-group 2 node 0` on the target node — `RequestPeerFailover`, the coordinated transfer that commits the target primary.
- #15734/#15738 already fixed the product half (spent manual hold released against a committed primary; deliberately not a promotion), so no product change is needed: after that fix the target still waits for the targeted request, which the gate never sent.

## What
- `test-v6-na-recovery-12495.sh` failback: `failover reset` on the target instance, then targeted `failover redundancy-group $RG node <target>` on the target instance. `wait_primary` remains the ownership verdict (#6440); exit 3 still outranks the measurement.
- `v6-na-recovery-12495-selftest.sh`: incus stub gains a stranded model (plain failback = no move, reset = no move, targeted-on-target = move; first plain failover still moves), a per-request CLI log, and faithful reset/targeted/plain classification in the default model (it previously flipped on *every* request, which would have masked this defect). New gate case asserts rc 0 plus reset-before-targeted order and exactly one untargeted request. Stub `date` split: constant `+%s%3N` for attribution, advancing `+%s` so `wait_primary` deadlines expire instead of hanging a stranded case forever (root-caused during validation: the old constant clock hangs any non-converging `wait_primary`).
- `docs/log/12495.md`: #15959 entry recording the contract-owner determination.

## Validation
- `bash test/incus/v6-na-recovery-12495-selftest.sh` — **20/20 pass**.
- Mutant-verified: gate restored to HEAD (plain failback) → new stranded case fails `rc=3 reset_ln=none target_ln=none plain=2`, suite 19/20; fix restored → 20/20.
- `bash -n` both scripts, `git diff --check` clean; shellcheck only pre-existing info/warnings.
- No live cluster moves — validated by reading (issue, #15734 product test `failback_hold_15734_test.go`, `ManualFailover`/`RequestPeerFailover`/`ResetFailover` in `pkg/cluster/failover.go`, CLI dispatch in `pkg/cli/cli_request_chassis.go`, operator smoke logs) plus the hermetic dry shell test above. The smoke lane owns live-cluster confirmation.

## Risk
Test-harness only; no production code changed. The gate still serializes on the #1875 destructive-cluster lease. The split-RG v6 transit blackhole from the same recorded runs is #15734/#15958 territory, untouched here.

## What

Dedup `snapshotContentHash` from up to 3 passes per publish to 1
(`postPublishHash` reuses it; a second spent-marker recompute only on
the authorized-clear path) on publishers
that can prove the hash describes the exact struct sent; audit the
compiler Clone/ExpandGroups fan-out and scope it down with proof.

- `PublishRouteOverlaySnapshotWithLatch`, `RepublishCurrentCaptureAuthority`,

  build the final publish snapshot, hash it once, thread the hash through
  `publishPreparedSnapshotPrehashedLocked` /
  `requestApplySnapshotPrehashedLocked` so the send-site stamp reuses it.

  stamping: publishers capture the pre-send value and rebuild the

  `retryDeferredWorkerArmLocked` go through `requestApplySnapshotLocked`,
  whose `prepareSnapshotForApply` rebuilds derived sections after any
  earlier hash. Their stamp and post-publish hash stay authoritative and

## PR #15967 — userspace-dp: restore IPv4 leak-rib recursive-NoRoute continue (#15934) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-20)

Branch: `fix/15934-leak-rib-v4-continue`

## Summary

Restores #14319's recursive-`NoRoute` `continue` in the IPv4 leak-rib walk (`forwarding/fib.rs`), deleted by e59e745568 (#15768) — the v6 twin kept it, so a tunnel-only leak selection under `allow_tunnels=false` blackholed IPv4 in mixed tunnel/non-tunnel VRF topologies instead of falling through to later leaks / the source LPM (GLM DP retro F1, HIGH). Verified good by triple review.

Folds the two ledger residuals on the same surfaces:
- **DNAT ICMP selector (#15791 residual, rounds 2–3 corrected):** selector composition is now keyed on **hit direction**, not call site (`forward_selector_for_hit`): reverse-direction hits compose stored-first (`stored.or(packet)`) — the arriving packet is a reply (echo-reply (0,0)) and must not override the stored forward identity (echo-request (8,0), #14128) — at BOTH the companion-less synthesized arm and the primary arm when a reverse hit's forward companion is materialized; forward-direction hits keep packet-first. A reverse ICMP hit with **no stored selector** (DNAT-only flows mint none; only a source rewrite records one) waives ONLY the ICMP-selector sub-check: DNAT matching itself becomes selector-optional (`lookup_all_ignoring_icmp_selector_scoped` ignores ICMP type/code and collects every distinct translation) and validity requires one reproducing the stored translation — geometry decides among arbitrary/simultaneous typed rules (type-13, type-8->A + type-0->B) — so withdrawal, replacement geometry, NPTv6 prefix validity, deterministic NAT64 geometry, and the source side all still revoke. ## PR #15972 — userspace: scope ndp except to its owning view (#15931) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-20)

Branch: `fix/15931-nd-except-cross-zone`

Refs #15931

## Why
One zone's `ndp except` removed default ND admission from unrelated zones end-to-end (Codex DP HIGH; Opus DP F1/F2):
- kernel nftables (text + netlink) emitted a single unscoped ND accept, withdrawn chain-wide when *any* view excluded `ndp` — neighboring zones lost ICMPv6 NS admission;
- cold-boot / gap fences mirrored the chain-wide withdrawal;
- host-inbound grouping keyed only on positive token sets, so an `ndp except` interface merged into a positive-equal default view and its exclusion was dropped (F2);
- Rust interface override fell through to the positive set, losing the ND default that zone parity requires (F1).

## What
**Kernel (text + netlink, parity-preserved):** the unscoped ND accept is replaced by per-retaining-view scoped accepts — ingress-scoped (direct + VRF scopes, destination-set constrained), destination fallback for ingress-less views, unscoped only when no scope exists. Excluding views emit nothing; their catch-alls deny ND. Fences emit the same scoped admits (uncounted per the #5719 counterless-fence invariant) ahead of their address drops, preserving a non-excluding zone's ND through cold boot. Non-unicast guards exempt ND only for positively-governing retaining views (explicit-`ndp` parity); empty no-stanza views keep their closed multicast posture.

**Grouping (compiler→snapshot→views):** the canonical host-inbound signature gains the effective except set — view grouping, netdev claims, the ambiguity reporter, and the duplicate-address commit gate all use it — so an `ndp except` interface stays distinct from a positive-equal default view.

**Rust:** interface overrides receive the ND default exactly like zones (withdrawn only on `ndp except`); catalog-multicast ND requires an explicit `ndp` positive (`ZoneHostInbound.ndp_positive`, set via `ndp`/`all` classification), mirroring the kernel catalog guards.

**Docs:** host-inbound service matrix ND row updated to the scoped form.

## Validation
Two-view fixture (A except, B default; B-scoped NS admitted, A not, cold-boot fence preserves B):
- `TestNDExceptScopedToOwningView15931`, `TestNDExceptColdBootFencePreservesB15931` (incl. gap fence + config-less mandatory admit), `TestNDScopedAcceptKeepsCounterDeclared15931`
- `TestHostInboundGroupingKeepsNDPExceptDistinct15931` — compiled `protocols all` + `ndp except` interface vs positive-equal zone default stay in distinct views with correct address ownership
- Rust `ndp_interface_override_default_15931` — ssh-only override keeps ND default in both admit entry points; except withdraws ND but not ssh; explicit `ndp` admits
- Suites: `go test ./pkg/daemon ./pkg/nftables ./pkg/config ./pkg/dataplane/userspace` (incl. T1 `TestNftNetlinkParity` text↔netlink), `go vet` clean, `cargo check --tests` clean. `cargo test ndp_interface_override_default_15931` passes; `cargo test host_inbound` 66 passed (incl. the #5659 sentinel cells — deny-all sentinels are now marked `ndp_excluded` so the override ND default does not resurrect them).
- Pre-existing failures on `origin/master`, unchanged: `TestHostInboundTeardownClearsEnforcedThenFailedReinstallFences_5790`, `TestNftRuleFromTermAddressSemantics3433`.

## Risk
Steady-state scoped ND accepts (unicast and ff02::/16 multicast) carry the aggregate `xpfhia_icmp6_nd` counter; only transient fences are counterless (#5719 invariant). ND from unzoned/ambiguous ingress is now dropped (fail-closed; parent admitted it globally). Multicast ND is admitted for every default-retaining view including empty-token zones, in steady state and through the cold-boot fence. No snapshot wire change; rollback is a plain revert.

## Implementation notes for reviewers
- Scoped ND accepts are emitted *ahead of* the per-view ingress catch-alls and carry the aggregate counter in the steady chain; fence tables stay counterless (#5719) — netlink fence uses the uncounted form.
- Multicast (`ff02::/16`) ND is admitted for every default-retaining view (empty-token included), steady state and cold-boot fence; only `ndp except` views lose it.
- No snapshot wire change: `ProtocolsExcept` already reaches the kernel views and the Rust zone/interface maps (#15671); this change scopes its *effect*.


## Fold (triple review 15972-{codex,opus,glm})
- **B1/F2 multicast ND:** retaining views (incl. empty-token/no-stanza) admit ff02::/16 ND (solicited-node NS, RS ff02::2, RA ff02::1) on their own ingress in steady state *and* the cold-boot fence (text+netlink); excluding views still deny. - **F4/B3:** steady multicast ND accepts carry `xpfhia_icmp6_nd`; Risk/comments corrected (fences remain counterless, #5719).

## PR #15974 — nat64: union zone lists and revalidate sessions against admitting scope (#15932) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-20)

Branch: `fix/15932-nat64-revalidation`

## Why

Retro review of the #15678 NAT64 scoping work (Codex cfg C2, Codex DP 3–4, Opus DP F5/U1) found four defects on master:

1. **Zone-list truncation:** `from zone [ trust untrust ]` collapsed to last-zone-only in `compileNAT64`; the strict gate only checked the surviving singular field.
2. **Cross-generation revocation:** mint selects the NAT64 owner scoped (zone/RI/source) but revalidation re-selected destination-only, revoking valid sessions owned by a second same-/96 rule-set.
3. **U1 (validated as defect):** scope tightening never revoked existing round-robin/rescoped sessions.
4. **Deny double-charge:** a denied `LocalDelivery` established hit charged both the admitting permit and the denying rule.

## What

- **Compile/config (reworked at 84a84d22c3 after GLM F1 executed review):** `compileNAT64` keeps ONE typed rule-set per authored rule-set and unions the zone list into `FromZones` — no Cartesian snapshot expansion (expansion gave each zone sibling an independent PortAllocator over the shared pool: cross-zone double-mint, first-apply `PoolPeerAddressOverlap` denials, reload merge hiding live tuples). One snapshot per (prefix, pool) = one allocator. Strict gate checks every zone on the single rule-set; #5144 enumeration restored to the scoped owner key (the allocator-key dedupe is deleted); `nat64` added to the mixed-scope AST gate; lenient mixed zone+RI keeps both axes on the one rule-set (fail-closed AND). `show security nat nat64` renders one block with its zone union.
- **Wire:** `NAT64RuleSnapshot.from_zones`; snapshot protocol **61 → 62** (Go + Rust constants, shape golden). Rust `Nat64Prefix` unions `from_zones` in scoped matching with singular fallback.
- **Revalidation:** carries admitting provenance (recorded `nat_scope_ifindex`/VLAN/fabric override via `prerouting_ingress_scope`) into new scoped NAT64 predicates; recorded-scope sessions revoke when their owner stops matching or stops holding the tuple (closes U1); scopeless legacy rows keep the destination-only exemption.
- **Accounting:** `LocalDelivery` bound-counter charge deferred until after all host gates (input filter, NAT/policy revalidation, host-inbound, lo0, junos-host); denied hits charge only the deny. Transit/foreign handling unchanged.
- Docs: `docs/log/15932.md`.

## Validation

- Go: `pkg/config` NAT64/#5144/shadow suite and `pkg/dataplane/userspace` snapshot-shape/builder tests pass. One `pkg/config` failure (`TestValidateNATRuleSetMixedScope/source_from_zone_+_to_interface_compiles`) fails identically on unmodified `origin/master` — pre-existing.
- Rust: all five `15932` cells pass (`nat64_zone_list_unions_15932`, `nat64_two_zone_union_shares_one_allocator_15932` — distinct cross-zone mints behind one allocator + reload reuse, `nat64_scoped_revalidation_honours_pool_port_range_15932`, `nat64_scoped_cross_generation_revalidation_15932`, `local_delivery_denied_hit_charges_only_denying_rule_15932`); `nat64_scoped` 5/5; `local_delivery_` 69/69. Earlier full `nat64_` run: 341 passed / 2 failed, both failures base-attributed on clean `origin/master` (9e94cf62ab, isolated target dir): `loop_body_mod_stays_below_refactor_ceiling` (2002 LOC on master, untouched) and `test_encode_session_open_carries_nat64_flag_and_snat_v4`. Also folded: dead scoped-mismatch fn removed, `scope_known==false` leg made non-revoking, scoped revalidation honours the pool port range.

## Risk

- **Protocol collision:** this PR originally bumped the snapshot protocol 61 → 62, colliding with PR #15969 (`source_constrained`). #15969 has merged at 62, so this branch is rebased onto current master and now carries **63** (`from_zones`): Go `ProtocolVersion`, Rust `CONFIG_SNAPSHOT_PROTOCOL_VERSION`, shape golden (regenerated on the merged shape) and the secure-tunnel pin all moved together (bump Go `ProtocolVersion`, Rust `CONFIG_SNAPSHOT_PROTOCOL_VERSION`, and re-pin the shape golden/secure-tunnel pin).
- Mixed-version daemon/helper pairs are fenced by exact-equality versioning. Scopeless imported sessions gain no new revocation, so no behavior change for legacy rows.

## PR #15978 — userspace: redirect split-RG punt-origin return to fabric (#15958) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-21)

Branch: `fix/15958b-both-halves-return`

## Why

Split-RG return traffic (RG2/LAN on fw1, RG1/WAN on fw0) died on fw0, the punt origin. Round-6 live evidence (HuntFreshGLM / DiagFw0Tx): replies session-accounted on fw0 (`Out: Pkts 5/3/3`), candidate-counted, but fw0 fabric `tx_packets` Δ0 and every exported drop counter Δ0 — the return never crossed the fabric. The earlier fw1 both-halves (Fresh/Stale) theory describes a population that never presented (fw1 fabric rx produced no session/cache accounting).

Root cause, pinpointed in the cell: on fw0 the connected LAN prefix `10.0.61.0/24` is HA-suppressed (`connected_rg_peer_owned=true` for RG2 in `snap-split-fw0.json`), so fw0's FIB has no LAN route and answers the LAN-host target with the default route via the WAN gateway (`ForwardCandidate` egress reth0.50/ifindex 13, next-hop 172.16.50.1, owner RG1 locally active).

1. `reverse_resolution_for_session_in_table` only redirected when the resolved owner RG was *inactive*; the gateway route's owner (RG1) is active, so the synthesized reverse companion was stored as a WAN `ForwardCandidate`, not `FabricRedirect`.
2. On the WAN-side reverse hit, re-resolution (`lookup_forwarding_resolution_for_session`; the cached arm refuses `FabricRedirect`) yielded the same WAN gateway candidate, `prefer_local` early-returned it, HA enforcement kept it (RG1 active), and `redirect_session_via_fabric_if_needed` only converts `HAInactive`. The request was built with `target_ifindex=6, target_binding_index=Some(0)` — descriptor target = the ingress WAN binding — and transmitted on the WAN egress. Enqueue/drain succeeded on the wrong binding, so no drop counter could fire (hence the silent live signature).

## What

- `shared_ops/reverse_synth.rs`: fabric-ingress reverse resolution also returns the zone-encoded `FabricRedirect` when the resolved `ForwardCandidate` egresses in a zone other than the session's LAN (ingress) zone.
- `session_glue/resolve.rs` (hit + synthesized-reverse arms): a stored `FabricRedirect` companion is retained when re-resolution yields a `ForwardCandidate` egressing outside the companion's destination (egress) zone, instead of being replaced by the gateway route.
- New packet cells `split_rg_punt_origin_wan_reverse_{icmp,tcp}_fabric_tx_15958b` in `tests_fabric_zone_stamp.rs`: install the forward+reverse pair on the fw0 punt-origin shape (real `snap-split-fw0.json`, RG1 active / RG2 inactive, forward `fabric_ingress=true` provenance `Some(false)`, scope `None`), drive the plain WAN-side reverse hit (ICMP echo-reply + TCP ACK, two packets) through the multi-binding poll→enqueue→drain harness over separate WAN/fabric/LAN UMEMs, and assert fabric binding `tx_packets` increments, WAN `tx_packets=0`, `fabric_redirect_unsendable_drops=0`, fabric frame dst MAC = peer fabric MAC, dst IP = LAN host.
- The fw1 both-halves direction was also exercised first (per the original assignment): with both halves on fw1 the LAN egress already works (Fresh/Stale revalidation declines via the #15176 scope keep), consistent with round-6's finding that fw1 was not the sink.
- Docs: `docs/log/15958.md` follow-up entry; `debian/changelog` entry.

## Validation

- New cells: RED without the production fix (fabric `tx=0`, WAN `tx=1`, no fabric egress) — verified by stashing the two production files; GREEN with the fix (ICMP + both TCP packets).
- Neighboring suite: `tests_fabric_zone_stamp::` 54/54 pass (includes the #15958 LAN-egress cells and the scoped cell).
- Sink-line accounting requested by the assignment: the exit is *counted* — on the wrong binding. Pre-fix, fw0 WAN `tx_packets` increments (in the test harness; live it left via the WAN underlay accounting that the 19-field extract attributed to background), fabric `tx_packets` stays 0, and `fabric_redirect_unsendable_drops` stays 0 because the binding lookup succeeded (for the WAN binding). No new counter was added: nothing is dropped.

Main agent should run: wider `forwarding::tests`, `session_glue`, `shared_ops`/reverse-synthesis suites, and the live split-RG gate before merge.

## Risk

The retained-redirect guard keys on (stored `FabricRedirect`) ∧ (re-resolved candidate egress zone ≠ companion destination zone). A legitimately re-homed companion whose destination zone changed at commit could keep redirecting until revalidation refreshes it (bounded by session expiry; same posture as the existing `HAInactive` retention). The synthesis arm fires only on fabric ingress with a zone mismatch, so local LAN delivery on the LAN owner (egress zone == ingress zone, e.g. fw1 and the existing `fabric_originated_reverse_session_prefers_local_client_delivery_when_rg_active` cell) is untouched.

Refs #15958, #15742

## PR #15983 — config: pass true parent prefix to scoped inheritance redaction (#15979) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-20)

Branch: `fix/h6-redact-parent-prefix`

Refs #15979

## Why
`FormatPathInheritanceRedactedForNode` (`pkg/config/ast_redact.go`) called `redactMatches15942(clones, nil)`, discarding the ancestor context every context-gated predicate tests. With a nil base, `snmp>community`, `dynamic-dns`-gated `password`/`server`, and the other ancestor-gated secret/URL rules saw a truncated flattened path and never fired — so scoped `display inheritance` renders leaked SNMP communities and DDNS credentials in cleartext to any authenticated PermView caller across active, candidate, and every rollback slot. Regression from #15942, merged as PR #15973; unanimously confirmed MATERIAL High by three independent research passes at `c1b86e87` (see #15979 for the full evidence chain).

## What
- Mirror the working sibling `redactedScopedMatches`: compute `parentPrefix := path[:len(path)-width]` and pass it as the base to `redactMatches15942`. The helper only masks `idx >= len(base)`, so identity tokens beyond the consumed width (which live in the clones' `Keys`) stay maskable and the caller's navigation spelling is preserved. This restores exactly the whole-tree flattened-path invariant every other scoped renderer already upholds.
- Add `pkg/config/redacted_inheritance_15979_test.go`: scoped INHERITANCE fixtures at `[snmp, community]` and at a `dynamic-dns` provider (ancestor-gated `password` + credential-bearing `server` URL), an `apply-groups`-inherited community (renders with its inheritance annotation, masked), OSPF MD5 and archive URL/password masking pins, and non-secret over-masking guards (routing-policy `community`, GRE tunnel `key`).

## Validation
- `go test ./pkg/config/ -run '15979' -count=1` — 6 tests pass.
- RED-on-revert: with the fix stashed, the SNMP, DDNS, and inherited-community tests fail with the cleartext sentinels in the render (the OSPF/archive fixtures pin masking where the gating context travels inside the matched subtree).
- `go vet ./pkg/config/` clean; `gofmt` clean.
- Neighboring suites `go test ./pkg/config/ ./pkg/configstore/ -run '15942|15973|Redact|Inheritance' -count=1` match baseline — the sole failure (`TestURLShapedFieldsAreRedactedOnMarshal6733`) fails identically on unmodified `origin/master`.

## Risk
Display-only redaction change on management-plane reads; no dataplane, persistence, HA-sync, or commit path touched. Over-masking is bounded by the same predicates the whole-tree redactor already applies and is pinned by the non-secret guards. Carrying the prefix costs O(path length) per scoped read.

## PR #16093 — userspace-dp: create state-file temps with mode 0600 (#16048) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-21)

Branch: `fix/16048-state-writer-mode`

Refs #16048

## Why
Both state-writer transports created their temp file with no `.mode()` (0666 & umask = 0644 under umask 022) and atomically renamed it onto the destination, so the published state file inherited that world-readable mode. The persisted pretty JSON clones the entire snapshot (topology/policy/NAT/routes/tunnel endpoints), refreshed ~1/s, in a directory that can pre-exist at 0755 — any local account could read the full posture continuously.

## What
- Single `open_state_temp()` helper in `userspace-dp/src/state_writer.rs` creating the private O_EXCL temp with `OpenOptionsExt::mode(0600)` (`STATE_FILE_MODE`).
- Both transports routed through it: `persist_with_io_uring` (io_uring) and `persist_sync` (sync fallback) — neither can drift.
- Because the temp is always freshly created (`create_new`), `.mode()` always applies; `0600 & !umask` can only narrow it. `finalize_durably`'s rename then publishes 0600, replacing any pre-existing 0644 destination.
- Scope per issue fix shape: mode asserted on temp + rename in both transports. Dropping the opaque config from the persisted payload was the alternative "and/or" and is not done here — the snapshot has in-file consumers' history (e.g. status verbs) and removing it is a separate payload change.

Decisive regression `persisted_state_file_is_0600_under_umask_000_in_0755_dir` (`state_writer_tests.rs`): dir forced 0755, process umask forced 000 (restored via drop guard), destination pre-seeded 0644; asserts 0600 for the sync-published file, the bare temp, and the io_uring-published file.

## Validation
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp state_writer`: **14 passed**, including the new regression.
- Fail-on-revert verified: removing `.mode(0600)` turns the new test RED (sync-published file 0666 under umask 000).
- Pre-existing rustfmt diffs at `state_writer.rs:344,544` and `state_writer_tests.rs:476` are untouched (not in this diff).

Perf impact: none — mode is set at `open(2)` on the cold state-writer thread; no per-packet/hot-path cost.

## Risk
A non-root consumer reading the state file would now get EACCES; the helper and daemon run as root and there is no non-owner reader in-tree. Existing 0644 files are replaced with 0600 on the next periodic write via rename.

## PR #16094 — ipsec: reject gateway-less PSK VPN with unscoped secret (#15989) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-21)

Branch: `fix/15989-gatewayless-psk`

Refs #15989

Why: A PSK VPN with no `ike gateway` (`vpn.Gateway == ""`, e.g. a route-based `st0.0` VPN) evaded all #14591-era defenses — the responder-identity lookup of `""` misses, the gateway-references gate continues on empty gateway, and `responderOnlyGateway(nil)` is false at render. It rendered a connection with no `remote_addrs` (charon `%any` responder default) whose secret carried a lone `id-1 = "%any"` selector matching any peer identity, so a holder of any on-box PSK could authenticate into the tunnel by claiming the intended peer's identity.

What:
- `pkg/config`: extend `validateIPsecResponderIdentityStrict` to strict-reject a gateway-less VPN whose effective auth needs a PSK. The trigger is `vpn.Gateway == ""` (renderer: `gw == nil && remote == ""`); inline endpoints (usable IP/hostname, `remote != ""`) keep compiling because the peer address scopes their secret. The existing `lenientIPsecResponderIdentity` wiring downgrades this to the same `ipsec responder-only remote identity` warning prefix on tolerant load / peer-sync — warn, keep the VPN, render belt unloads it — never a hard fail there.
- `pkg/ipsec`: render belt skips a PSK VPN when `gw == nil && remoteAddr == ""`, so no lone-`%any` secret is ever rendered; healthy named-gateway and inline siblings keep rendering.
- Tests: migrate the two tests that pinned the vulnerable shape (`TestRenderConfig_GatewayNameNeverLeaks/empty gateway…`, `TestValidateIPsecGatewayReferences/no gateway is not rejected`) and add decisive fixtures per the issue: `TestGatewaylessPSK15989` in both `pkg/config` (strict reject of the route-based st0.0 PSK shape, tolerant warn-and-keep, inline-IP and inline-hostname controls) and `pkg/ipsec` (no connection, no orphan secret, no sole-`%any` selector anywhere; siblings render with peer-address selectors).
- Docs: `pkg/ipsec/README.md` PSK-selector section notes the #15989 extension.

Validation:
- `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestGatewaylessPSK15989|TestIPsecResponderIdentity14591'` PASS
- `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestValidateIPsecGatewayReferences/(no_gateway_PSK_VPN_is_rejected|inline_endpoint_PSK_VPN_still_compiles)'` PASS
- `go test ./pkg/ipsec/` PASS (incl. `TestGatewaylessPSK15989`, migrated empty-gateway subtest, #14591 responder tests)
- `go vet ./pkg/config/ ./pkg/ipsec/` clean; gofmt clean on changed files
- Pre-existing `TestValidateIPsecGatewayReferences` subtest failures on master (fixtures configure no PSK and hit the #14139 presence gate) are unchanged by this PR.

Risk: Existing gateway-less PSK configs now fail commit until an `ike gateway` or inline endpoint is configured. Tolerant load / peer-sync still boots with a warning, and the VPN is unloaded by the render belt on both HA nodes (deterministic render). Perf: no dataplane/hot-path impact — config validation and swanctl render only.

## PR #16096 — config: price rendered descendants on scoped config reads (#15995) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-21)

Branch: `fix/15995-ancestor-descendant-pricing`

Refs #15995

## Why
`deny-configuration` regexes were evaluated only on the joined *requested* path (`authorizeConfigReadPath: rules.Evaluate(joined)`), so `^security ipsec` could not match a request for `security` — yet `FormatPathRedacted([security])` renders the whole subtree, ipsec included. ShowConfig, scoped ShowCompare/ShowRollback, and their REST/CLI twins disclosed the denied descendant (structural topology / non-secret values; typed secrets stay redacted, so Medium not High). Concealment is the stated contract (#14707 header, `docs/system-login.md`).

## What
- **pkg/config**: `AuthorizeConfigShowPathRendered` + Compare/Rollback rendered wrappers and `AuthorizeConfigPathOnlyRendered` walk the tree(s) that will actually be rendered (`navigatePath` to the requested path, then every strict descendant path) and refuse the ancestor read when any descendant is denied by the *-configuration pair or uncovered by an `allow-configuration` allowlist. Operational pair still charged once on the requested command (a descendant is not a command spelling). Unrestricted classes return before any walk; legacy joined-path-only helpers remain documented for already-priced callers.
- **pkg/configstore**: `ShowConfigTrees`/`CompareTrees`/`RollbackCompareTrees`/`RollbackTree` hand the gates the exact rendered trees (live, read-only, one decision).
- **pkg/grpcapi / pkg/api / pkg/cli**: every scoped Show/Compare/Rollback gate now calls the rendered variants with the target/compare/rollback trees (candidate+active, both compare arms incl. ActiveBaseline, rollback slot). Whole-tree / search / export / typed `/config` arms unchanged — already refused for restricted classes.

Perf: control-plane authz only, no dataplane/hot-path impact; walk skipped entirely for classes without *-configuration regexes.

## Validation
- New decisive suites (deny `^security ipsec` + PermView class): `pkg/config/authz_config_read_15995_test.go` (deny + allowlist descendants, denied-on-either-compare-arm, nil/absent controls, requested-path-only premise), `pkg/grpcapi/authz_config_read_15995_test.go`, `pkg/api/authz_config_read_15995_test.go`, `pkg/cli/config_read_15995_test.go` — `[security]` refused on Show/Compare/Rollback across gRPC+REST+CLI; `[security zones]`/`[interfaces]` still render with content.
- `go test ./pkg/config/ ./pkg/configstore/ ./pkg/grpcapi/ ./pkg/api/ ./pkg/cli/ -run '14707|14987|15942|15995' -count=1` — all pass. Broader read-gate pattern run shows only pre-existing master failures (spot-verified identical on clean master).

## Risk
Fail-closed only: an ancestor read whose rendered subtree contains a denied descendant is now refused where it previously disclosed it. Restricted operators request the allowed sibling subtree instead (error message says so). No shims; REST compare has no `?path=` selector (documented in code, whole-tree refusal already covers it).

## PR #16097 — config: reject $9$ secrets that decode to empty (#15990) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-21)

Branch: `fix/15990-decode-empty`

Refs #15990

## Summary

`decodeJunos9` returned `("", nil)` for `$9$i` / `$9$!`: the first char's skip consumes the whole rest, zero nibble groups remain, the decode loop never runs, and empty output was not an error. Every presence gate tests the *encoded* form only (`"$9$i" != ""` passes), so compile stored `Secret("")`:

- **BGP (K1):** the FRR render gate `if n.AuthPassword != ""` sits *before* the #14977 unrenderable-password belt — an emptied password skipped the belt and the neighbor was emitted with **no `password` line**; a peer tolerating no-MD5 establishes unauthenticated BGP.
- **IPsec (VPN-C1 render leg):** the render tested encoded non-emptiness, stored `decodedPSKs[name]=""` with no decoded-empty check, the #14139 no-secret skip tested the encoded form and never fired, and emission rendered `secret = ""`.

## Fix

- `decodeJunos9` errors on empty decoded output (`junos9_15051.go`) — the root fix. Strict compile now refuses `$9$i`/`$9$!` at every routing leaf via the existing #15051 path (leaf named, secret never echoed); the tolerant path keeps the blob and warns (#1960), so render belts see the undecodable blob, never `Secret("")`.
- `validateIPsecPSKPresenceStrict` tests the **decoded** form (`ipsecVPNEffPSK`/`ipsecEffPSKDecode`): a decoded-empty effective key is absent; a malformed-but-present key counts as present so the refusal below names the real defect.
- New `validateIPsecPSKJunos9Strict` refuses any malformed `$9$` PSK (vpn-level + ike-policy) at strict commit, with a lenient downgrade (`lenientIPsecPSKJunos9`) mirroring the neighboring PSK gates.
- `pkg/ipsec` render belt skips a VPN whose PSK decodes to empty instead of storing it — never emits `secret = ""`.

A valid `$9$` credential renders byte-identical to today (known-answer controls pinned in the new tests).

## Tests

- `pkg/config`: `TestJunos9DecodeToEmptyRejected15990` (decoder + strict refusal at BGP/OSPF/RIP/IS-IS + lenient blob-kept), `TestIPsecPSKDecodeToEmptyRejectedStrict15990` (strict `#15990` refusal, lenient warning, valid-blob control).
- `pkg/ipsec`: `TestGenerateConfig_DecodeToEmptyPSKSkipped15990` — `$9$i`/`$9$!` VPN skipped (no connection, no secret, healthy VPN unaffected), valid-blob control renders `secret = "QZ1agnL21L"`.
- `pkg/frr`: `TestJunos9DecodeToEmptyBGPNotRenderedPasswordless15990` — strict refusal before render; direct render never emits the neighbor passwordless.

All fail on revert of the decoder fix.

Validation: `go vet` clean on `pkg/config`, `pkg/ipsec`, `pkg/frr`, `pkg/configstore`; `pkg/ipsec` suite green; `pkg/config`/`pkg/frr` failure sets are a strict subset of the pre-existing failures at base `8ab367c85b` (none credential-related).

Risk/perf: a persisted config carrying a `$9$i`-style key now warns on tolerant load and its tunnel/neighbor is skipped at render instead of loading credential-less — intended fail-closed behavior. No dataplane/hot-path code touched (compile/render time only), so no perf impact.

## PR #16098 — authz: price group bodies on config reads (#15994) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-21)

Branch: `fix/15994-groups-read-gate`

**authz: price group bodies on config reads (#15994)**

## Why
The config-read gate evaluated only the literal `groups <name> ...` spelling, so a class denied `^security` (or denied `^show configuration security` on the operational pair) read group-authored security subtrees through every scoped render — gRPC ShowConfig/ShowCompare/ShowRollback, the REST config-show/export/compare/show-rollback routes, and the CLI (`show configuration ...`, config-mode `show`, `show system rollback`) — while the directed read of the same subtree was refused.

**Fold note:** rebased onto current master after #16096 (PR #16096, snapshot transport + rendered-descendant pricing for #15995) merged, preserving its snapshot transport: every surface prices and renders the same deep-copy snapshot captured under the store lock (priced path carried); no surface re-resolves the live store between gate and render. The previous head's Opus/GLM/Codex findings (fold items 1–7) are folded in below.

## What
Both arms, in the shared `pkg/config` gate composed onto #15995's Rendered entries so the surfaces cannot drift:
- `AuthorizeConfigShowPath` / `AuthorizeConfigShowSystemPath` / `AuthorizeConfigPathOnly` price every effective spelling: the authored definition path and the recursively unwrapped body path (`readSpellings15994`), `*-configuration` on the effective path and `*-commands` on `show configuration <effective>`.
- Ancestors `groups` / `groups <name>` price every contained path (definitions included, root scope included) via the groups rewrite of the rendered-descendant walk; an unresolvable `groups` scope fails closed **only** for config-restricted classes (unrestricted classes no longer 403 — fold M1).
- Op arm: the operational pair is charged on the effective command for every group-aliased rendered path (ancestors included) on all surfaces; the CLI operational helper charges the unwrapped effective command (`AuthorizeConfigPathOnlyRenderedWithOp15994`) without weakening the literal `checkCommandRegex` verdict (fold 1/2).
- Whole/compare/rollback unscoped renders substitute contained+expanded pricing over the actual arms only when groups are present, and **always** re-charge the bare operational command (with display suffix), so an op-only deny (`display set`, `^show configuration$`) is never substituted away (fold B1); groupless renders keep the #14707 whole-tree refusal.
- REST: `/api/v1/config`, `/config/export`, `/config/search` always price the **active** tree (handlers render active regardless of `?target=candidate` — fold 4); unscoped compare prices both actual arms.
- CLI: `show system rollback N <path> | compare` and the unscoped operational rollback compares price the selected slot N's arms (`RollbackCompareSnapshot(n, true)` — slot + active), never the candidate (fold 5); config-mode whole show/compare and operational whole show price the priced snapshots.
- Docs: `docs/system-login.md` records the folded groups rule.

Perf: management-plane read authorization only; expanded pricing runs solely when the class is regex-restricted and the path/tree involves groups. No dataplane or hot-path change.

## Validation
- `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestGroupsRead' -count=1` — `groups G security...`, `groups`, `groups G` denied/allowed, nested groups, op-arm, whole/compare/rollback, unrestricted (fold M1), `^groups` definition denial (fold 3)
- `go test ./pkg/grpcapi/ ./pkg/api/ ./pkg/cli/ -run '15994' -count=1`
- `go vet ./pkg/{config,api,cli,grpcapi}/`
- Sibling suites re-run; the `pkg/api`/`pkg/cli` 15995 ipsec-fixture failures and `pkg/configstore` `rollback_slotmeta_10299` are **pre-existing on clean origin/master** (verified via stash), unrelated to this change.

## Risk
Authorization changes fail closed for denied group-authored subtrees while preserving allowed subtrees, unrestricted/empty-class behavior, groupless whole-tree refusals, and #15995's descendant pricing (jointly re-verified with it, not regressed). Secrets remain placeholder-redacted on all renders.

## PR #16101 — dhcpserver: render Kea configs 0640 root:_kea (#16062) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-21)

Branch: `fix/16062-kea-config-perms`

## Summary

Rendered Kea configs (`/etc/kea/kea-dhcp{4,6}.conf`) were written **0644 in a 0755 directory**, exposing the full static-reservation inventory (MAC ↔ IP ↔ hostname) to any local account for later spoofing (A10-07, Low).

Fix shape per issue: **render 0640 root:_kea on every render, including tightening a pre-existing 0644 file.**

## Changes

- `writeKeaConfig` renders `0640` on every render. `fsatomic.WriteFileAtomic` replaces the inode at the requested perm, so a pre-existing 0644 file is tightened with no separate chmod and no window at the old mode.
- The Kea runtime group is installed atomically via `fsatomic.WithOwner` (fchown before rename), reusing the existing #2450 cached resolution (`_kea` on the Debian appliance base, `kea` fallback — verified Kea's reading UID/group on the image lineage via the #2450 memfile behavior). Fresh files are `root:_kea` from first install.
- A file already owned by the Kea uid keeps its ownership (`WithPreserveExisting`, mode capped at 0640) — an operator's `chown _kea` is not reverted.
- When no group can be installed (non-root process, unresolved Kea user): plain `0640`, never world-readable; the apply never fails for a mode-only gain.
- Fresh config directories are created `0750` (a pre-existing dir keeps its mode; the file perm is the protective invariant).
- `resolveKeaOwner` gains `warnMissing`: only the memfile pre-seed warns on an absent Kea user, so render-only managers no longer consume the shared once-per-process warning (this was polluting unrelated warn-sink assertions).
- Docs: `pkg/dhcpserver/README.md` + `debian/changelog`.

Refs #16062

## Perf impact

Config-apply path only — not hot/dataplane. Added cost per render: one `os.Stat` + the already-cached owner resolution. No fsync added (stays `AtomicGeneratedConfig`). No hot-path test required.

## Validation

- New `kea_config_perms_16062_test.go` (decisive regression): fresh render and re-render over a pre-existing 0644 file both land 0640 with the Kea group; requested owner is `0:_kea-gid`; no-Kea-user renders still land 0640; a Kea-uid-owned file keeps its ownership. RED-on-revert: restoring the plain 0644 write fails the mode assertions. Passes unprivileged and as root.
- Decisive root check with a real `_kea` user/group: fresh and tightened files stat `640 root:_kea`; `runuser -u _kea` reads the config (Kea keeps working), `runuser -u nobody` is denied; the pre-fix 0644 root:root file was readable by nobody.
- Full `pkg/dhcpserver` suite green except `TestKeaSubnetIDStableAcrossSpellingChange`, which fails identically on clean `origin/master` (pre-existing, unrelated).
- `go vet ./pkg/dhcpserver/` and `go build ./...` clean.

## Risk

A Kea running as a user outside the `_kea`/`kea` primary group would lose config read; Debian Kea runs as `_kea` (the image installs `kea-dhcp4-server`/`kea-dhcp6-server`, and #2450 already depends on this in production). Operators who chowned the config to the `_kea` uid retain that ownership via the preserve arm.

## PR #16102 — userspace: refuse untrusted helper binaries when running as root (#16054) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-21)

Branch: `fix/16054-helper-binary-resolution`

Why: `findBinary` resolved `./xpf-userspace-dp` (then the build tree, argv[0]'s directory, then PATH) on stat + exec-bit alone (#12196). A root `xpfd` hand-run without a configured binary leaf from a low-privilege-writable CWD executed a planted helper as root and trusted its uid-0 peer credentials. The shipped systemd path (CWD=/, absolute configured binary) was already safe; the hand-run/lab arm survived at Low severity.

What:
- Every helper a root daemon resolves — CWD, build-tree and argv[0]-relative candidates, `exec.LookPath` results, and an explicitly configured binary — must be root-owned and not group/world-writable (`helperBinaryTrustReason` in `pkg/dataplane/userspace/process.go`).

- An untrusted explicit path is a hard `not trusted` error with no PATH fallback, matching existing explicit-branch strictness.
- Non-root daemons are exempt: no privilege is gained, and the user-owned build-tree/CWD dev workflow (including the #12196 CWD-over-PATH preference) keeps working. Candidate order otherwise unchanged.
- `helperProcessEuid` seam lets tests simulate a root daemon over real fixture files (real kernel ownership, no mocked stat).

Validation:
- Decisive regression per issue: planted executable user-owned `./xpf-userspace-dp` in a writable CWD is refused/skipped with a loud log under a simulated root daemon; same for the PATH, group/world-writable, and explicit-path arms (`findbinary_16054_test.go`).
- RED proof: removing only the two trust call sites turns all four root-arm cells RED with exactly the pre-fix acceptance; both control cells (non-root CWD preference, trusted explicit path) pass on both sides.
- `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run 'TestFindBinary.*(16054|12196)' -count=1 -v`: all pass; all #12196 cells unchanged and green. `go vet` clean, `gofmt` clean on touched files.
- Full package run: only failures that reproduce identically on pristine `origin/master` (5878/WireGuard-9587/6722 config-compiler cells), verified in a clean master worktree.

Risk: Pre-exec stat leaves the #12196 TOCTOU window, and parent directories are not checked (a root-owned helper in a user-writable directory can be rename-replaced); the packaged `/usr/local/sbin` layout is root-owned and unaffected. Spawn-time check only — no dataplane hot path touched, no per-packet perf impact, no live cluster mutated.

## PR #16103 — api: assert generated mgmt TLS key perms on load (#16060) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-21)

Branch: `fix/16060-mgmt-tls-key-perms`

Refs #16060

## Why
Mint wrote the generated management TLS key 0600 under a 0700 dir, but the load path (`generateSelfSignedCertAtWithStatusMulti` → `LoadX509KeyPair`) served a pre-existing loose pair as-is forever. A loosened dir/key, restored backup, or operator chmod was silently loaded, so the mint-time invariant gave false assurance (K3, Low).

## What
- `generateSelfSignedCertAtWithStatusMulti` calls `assertGeneratedTLSKeyPerms(dir, keyPath)` before any load, on every generated load/refresh.
- Descriptor-bound tighten-only repair following the configstore #9897/#9898 discipline: `O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK` open + `fstat` shape check + `fchmod` on the pinned descriptor. Dir tightened to 0700, key to 0600; stricter modes (e.g. 0400) never loosened; repair logged at Warn.
- Loud refusal (error propagates → `failManagementTLSCertificate`, invalid badge, no cert served) on symlinked key/dir, non-regular key, non-dir dir, or chmod failure. Symlink targets are never chmodded through a link.
- Absent paths and EACCES on open preserve pre-fix behavior: load fails identically and mint's durable write surfaces the real persistence error (keeps `SetTLSCertDirForTest` probing of the root-owned `/etc/xpf/tls` working).
- Operator-supplied (custom) pairs NEVER take this path — no chmod of user keys. Both custom load sites (`loadManagementTLSCertificateWithGen`, `refreshCustomManagementTLSCertificate`) are untouched.
- README documents the invariant.

## Validation
- New decisive regression `pkg/api/tls_key_perms_16060_test.go` drives the real production loader: loose key 0644→0600 without cert churn, loose dir 0755→0700, stricter 0400 untouched, injected chmod failure loudly refuses, symlinked key refused with target untouched, absent pair still mints, loose custom key never chmodded.
- RED verified: neutering the assert call fails the loose-key, loose-dir, chmod-failure, and symlink cells.
- `go test ./pkg/api/ -run '16060|TLS|GenerateSelfSigned' -count=1` PASS; `go vet ./pkg/api/` clean.
- Full `pkg/api` package shows pre-existing NAT-metrics/doc-guard failures that reproduce identically on clean base `fdc92c028b` (verified in a separate base worktree); unrelated to this change.

## Risk
Boot/refresh-time refusal if the generated key path is symlinked or its permissions cannot be repaired — intentional fail-closed. No dataplane/hot-path impact: management TLS certificate load only, no per-packet cost.
