## PR #16104 — api: bound REST connections with counted refusal (#16081) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-21)

Branch: `fix/16081-rest-conn-bound`

Why:
The REST listeners carried per-connection timeouts (#4150) but no
connection-count bound, so an attacker opening many idle/slow
connections could hold one fd, goroutine and socket buffer apiece
until fd exhaustion denied legitimate management clients (DOS-6
from #15987, validated Low at c1b86e871b). Timeouts cap each
connection's life, not how many are live at once.

What:
- `pkg/api/conn_bound_16081.go`: one per-Server `apiConnGate`
  (limit `apiMaxConnsTotal` = 256) shared by every HTTP/HTTPS leg —
  the protected resource is per-process, so the count is too.
- `serveLegLocked` wraps each leg's listener once at serve time
  (Start + reconcile alike; `leg.ln` stays raw); `bindListeners`
  wraps the `Run`/`serveBound` path. Bare `&Server{}` fixtures keep
  a nil gate and unwrapped listeners.
- At Accept, excess connections are closed, counted and rate-logged
  (~1/sec); refusal returns a temporary `net.Error` so http.Server
  retries instead of exiting (a fatal error would self-DoS).
- Admitted `gatedConn`s release exactly once on Close; TLS counted
  at raw TCP; hijacked conns release via the #7011 drain.
- Exported always (even at zero): `xpf_rest_conn_refusals_total`,
  `xpf_rest_conn_active` (pre-gate collector route, #8312 shape).
- NOT changed: per-connection timeouts, auth, handlers; gRPC out of
  scope.

Validation:
- New `conn_bound_16081_test.go` — decisive end-to-end: fill 4
  slots, 3 excess refused+counted, held keep-alive conn still 200,
  close frees a slot; shared-gate-across-planes cell; default pin;
  temporary-error unit cell; metric wiring cell.
- RED on mutation (boundListener unwrapped): `RestConnActive = 0,
  want 4` and `RestConnRefusals = 0, want 1`. GREEN after revert.
- Targeted + descriptor-coverage + dual-stack + Run shutdown +
  timeout tests pass; `go build ./...` ok.
- Full `pkg/api` suite: 6 failures identical on clean fdc92c028b
  base (#10438 NAT, #6960 vlan) — base-attributed, unrelated.

Risk:
Legitimate clients past 256 concurrent connections/server now get
an immediate close; 256 is far above normal management concurrency
and refusals are countable/alertable. Retiring legs keep draining.
Perf: one atomic CAS per accept and per close; no per-request cost
(management plane only; no dataplane hot path, no iperf gate).

Refs #16081

## PR #16105 — security: restrict /run/xpf to 0750 and flock files to 0600 (#16050) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-21)

Branch: `fix/16050-run-xpf-perms`

## Summary
Fixes the F2 finding from #15986: `/run/xpf` was created 0755 and the upgrade/epoch/kernel-roll flock files 0644. On Linux an exclusive flock can be taken on a readable O_RDONLY fd, so any local unprivileged user could flock the upgrade lock (and the epoch/kernel-roll locks) and block all upgrades indefinitely — no write permission needed.

Modes are now **0750 (dir) / 0600 (lock files), asserted via chmod on every use** as well as at creation, because shell first-creators (`debian/xpf.preinst`, `scripts/deploy/xpf-deploy.py` flock(1)) create these files under the caller's umask and Go-only creation modes would miss them.

Refs #16050

## What
- `pkg/upgrade/lock`: dir `MkdirAll 0750` + `Chmod 0750`, file `0600` + `Chmod 0600` before the flock; chmod failure refuses the acquire.
- `pkg/daemon`: singleton dir 0750+assert (file was already 0600+assert); input-barrier marker dirs 0750 + best-effort chmod heal.
- `pkg/cluster`: epoch lock file 0600 + assert (declines the persist on chmod failure).
- `pkg/upgrade`: `kernel-roll.lock` 0600 + assert in `consumeLease`.
- `debian/xpf.preinst`: `mkdir -p /run/xpf && chmod 0750`, chmod 0600 a pre-existing lock, gate flock under `umask 077`.
- `scripts/deploy/xpf-deploy.py`: lease acquire/renew chmod 0750 dir / 0600 lock and `umask 077` (was 022).
- `test/incus/xpfd.service` (staged by `debian/rules`): `RuntimeDirectory=xpf`, `RuntimeDirectoryMode=0750`, `UMask=0027`.
- Docs: mode invariant in `docs/in-place-upgrade.md`; `docs/log/16050.md`.

## Validation
- New decisive regression cells (all pass, incl. as root):
  - `pkg/upgrade/lock`: seeded 0755/0644 tightened on acquire; fresh create under umask 0 lands 0750/0600; `TestUnprivilegedCannotFlockUpgradeLock16050` — control arm (loosened 0755/0644, flock released) the `nobody` setpriv probe **succeeds**, fixed arm (0750/0600) it **fails** (`Permission denied`, exit 66), so the cell cannot pass vacuously.
  - `pkg/daemon`: singleton modes + shipped-unit directives parsed from the unit file.
  - `pkg/cluster`: epoch lock tightened; `pkg/upgrade`: kernel-roll lock tightened.
- Shell: preinst/postinst/preinst-migrate/preinst-safe-segment harnesses pass; redirected real preinst lands dir 0750 / lock 0600.
- Deploy: 34 lease TTL/renew-fence tests pass; generated acquire script executed on a temp root lands 0750/0600/0600.
- `go vet` clean on touched packages. Perf: one chmod per lock acquire; no dataplane/hot-path code touched (no hot-path test applicable).

## PR #16106 — config: enforce SNMPv3 passphrase length floor (#16084) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-21)

Branch: `fix/16084-snmpv3-passphrase-floor`

## Summary
Enforces an SNMPv3 passphrase length floor at strict compile time (#16084, A9-09).

**Why:** the #7530 gate is presence-only — a 1-character `authentication-password`/`privacy-password` compiles clean, and the agent then answers SNMPv3 authentication challenges online with no per-user lockout/backoff, so the credential is guessable after a handful of attempts.

**What:**
- `validateSNMPv3UserKeyMaterialStrict` now rejects any non-empty auth/privacy passphrase shorter than 8 runes (`snmpv3MinPassphraseRunes`), per RFC 3414 §11.2 (Junos enforces the same minimum). Counted in runes, not bytes. The error names user/field/observed length — never the passphrase.
- The existing tolerant-path downgrade (`lenientSNMPv3KeyMaterial`) turns this into a warning on load/peer-sync so persisted configs still boot (#1960).
- Sub-floor placeholder passphrases in existing SNMP test fixtures lengthened to ≥8 chars (values only).
- NOT changed: per-user throttle/source scoping (rides unresolved A9-NV1; Junos USM users likewise have no per-user `clients`), `pkg/snmp` runtime floor.

**Perf impact:** compile-time string length check only; no dataplane/hot-path change.

**Validation:**
- New decisive cells (`snmpv3_passphrase_floor_16084_test.go`): 1-char auth/priv rejection, 7/8 boundary, rune counting, tolerant warning — RED pre-fix (5 FAIL with gate reverted), GREEN post-fix.
- SNMP-scoped config suite + grpcapi `TestShowTextSNMPRenderIsDeterministic` pass; gofmt/go vet clean.

**Risk:** deployments with sub-8 passphrases fail strict commit until lengthened; tolerant boot still loads them with a warning. Severity re-check owed if A9-NV1 shows UDP/161 reachable from untrusted zones.

## PR #16107 — api: gate loopback /metrics behind api-auth on opt-in (#16072) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-21)

Branch: `fix/16072-loopback-metrics-auth`

## Why
On a loopback bind `metricsRequireAuth` is `!isLoopbackBindAddr`, so `/metrics` bypasses auth even with `api-auth` configured, with no peer-UID check (#4162 posture). Any local UID can scrape the full exposition (zone/policy/rule names, NAT pool names, session volumes — names/counts only). The loopback posture is a deliberate Prometheus-friendly default, so this adds an **opt-in** gate rather than breaking the default. Refs #16072.

## What
- **Config surface**: `set system services web-management api-auth metrics-require-auth` (flag leaf) → `APIAuthConfig.MetricsRequireAuth`. Strict commit rejects it without a usable api-auth credential (otherwise the runtime snapshot is nil and the gate would be silently inert); tolerant load downgrades to a warning.
- **Enforcement** (`pkg/api`): the flag rides inside `AuthConfig`; `effectiveMetricsRequireAuth` folds it with the per-listener #4162 bind rule in both `authCheckCredential` and `throttledAuthCheckWithCheck`. Gated loopback `/metrics` → 401 without a credential, 200 with Basic/Bearer/X-API-Key (the local scraper path). `/health` stays exempt; non-loopback unchanged; nil-auth pass-through unchanged.
- **Publishing**: `AuthForRetainedListener` preserves the flag from either side and `sameAuthConfig` counts it, so retired legs only ever tighten. `api.Config.MetricsRequireAuth` is stamped by `resolveAPIBinds` (both levels) and by `NewServer` without mutating the caller; the management reconciler publishes a gate-only toggle via `Server.ReplaceMetricsRequireAuth` — addition immediately, removal only once every live leg is named by the committed config.
- Docs: `docs/architecture.md`, `pkg/api/README.md`.

## Validation
- New decisive regression tests (fail-on-revert noted in each file):
  - `pkg/api/metrics_loopback_gate_16072_test.go` — gated loopback 401/200 matrix, dynamic swap, Cfg stamp, nil-auth, retained intersection.
  - `pkg/config/metrics_require_auth_16072_test.go` — schema/compile/strict-reject/lenient-warn.
  - `pkg/daemon/metrics_require_auth_16072_test.go` — `resolveAPIBinds` stamp, gate-only reconcile.
- `go build ./pkg/api/... ./pkg/config/... ./pkg/daemon/...` ok; `go vet` clean on changed files; gofmt clean.
- `go test ./pkg/api/ -run 'TestMetricsAuthGate|TestNewServerMetricsAuth|TestLoopbackMetrics|TestMetricsGateRetained|TestAuthForRetained|TestServerAuthSwap|TestIsLoopback'` ok.
- `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestMetricsRequireAuth|TestAPIAuth|TestWebManagement|TestValidateWebManagement'` ok (82s).
- `go test ./pkg/daemon/ -run 'TestMgmt|TestResolveAPIBinds|TestPublishNil|TestLiveLegs'` ok (43s).
- Known base timeout: the broad `pkg/config` run exceeds the 600s suite timeout inside `schema_spelling_differential_gate_test.go`; the same gate exceeds 360s on pristine base `fdc92c028b` — base-attributed, not this change.

## Perf / hot path
Not a dataplane/hot-path change. REST control plane only: one bool fold per `/metrics` request, no allocation, no new socket/`/proc` work; non-metrics requests unaffected.

## Risk
Default off — existing configs behave identically. An operator enabling the gate must give the local Prometheus scraper a credential (documented). Gate removal on a retained (unnamed) leg is deferred until the endpoint converges, mirroring credential grants.

## PR #16114 — ddns: scope Cloudflare withdraw to tagged records (#16086) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-21)

Branch: `fix/16086-ddns-foreign-withdraw`

Refs #16086

## Problem (A10-16)
Cloudflare `DeleteLease` deleted every row with `Content==owned`; Route53 strips the owned value from the live RRset. Value equality was the only ownership proof in both, so xpf's withdraw also deleted a foreign publisher's identical record (redundant appliances — the non-hostile case), and the victim's name died until its forced-refresh republishes. Upsert compounded it: the no-write arm ADOPTED an existing same-content row, creating no record of xpf's own.

## Fix (per issue fix shape)
- **Cloudflare comment-tag ownership:** every record xpf CREATEs (POST) is stamped with the `xpf-managed` comment; rows this backend instance created are also tracked in-process. Withdraw deletes only proven-owned (tagged or self-created) same-content rows.
- **No adoption:** the upsert no-write arm now requires proven ownership. An untagged same-content row is not adopted — xpf POSTs its own tagged row alongside so the two coexist and remain distinguishable. PATCH payloads deliberately carry no comment (a PATCH never claims a row reached by value equality, and never strips a genuine tag).
- **Legacy fallback, logged:** when no same-content row is provably owned (records published before tagging), withdraw falls back to the pre-fix value-scoped delete with an `slog.Warn` — skipping would orphan xpf's own legacy record forever once local ownership drops. Different-value rows are never touched in either mode.
- **Route53:** documented value-scoped limitation (RRset members have no record ID/comment provenance, so an identical foreign value cannot be distinguished; distinct foreign values remain preserved).

Also restates the #2770 delete-all-owned and #10715 stale-cleanup tests on tagged rows (their semantics are now 'every PROVEN-owned row'), and updates `pkg/ddns/README.md`, `docs/config-schema.md`, and `debian/changelog`.

## Decisive regression
`TestCloudflareForeignSameContentSurvivesWithdraw16086`: foreign untagged same-name+IP row → xpf publishes (must POST its own tagged row, not adopt) → xpf withdraws → foreign row survives, exactly xpf's row deleted, no fallback warning. Plus tagged-twin, legacy-fallback-logged, and PATCH-never-claims cells.

Mutation-verified: reverting DeleteLease to content-scoped deletes (or UpsertLease to content-only adoption) turns the new tests red.

## Validation
- `go test ./pkg/ddns/ -run TestCloudflare -count=1` — pass
- `go test ./pkg/ddns/ -count=1` (full package) — pass
- `go vet ./pkg/ddns/`, `gofmt` — clean

## Risk / perf
Legacy untagged withdraws remain value-scoped (warned) by design. No dataplane/hot-path impact — control-plane DDNS backends only; one extra map lookup per listed row and a comment field per POST.

## PR #16115 — userspace-dp: refuse disputed unit host-inbound override on shared ifindex (#16057) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-21)

Branch: `fix/16057-shared-ifindex-host-inbound`

## Summary

Refs #16057

Two configured logical units collapsed onto one netdev (shared ifindex) can carry **different effective per-interface host-inbound overrides** (`host_inbound_configured` + service/protocol/except token triple). The dataplane stores that override in a flat `ifindex → ZoneHostInbound` map, so the per-row insert in `populate_interfaces` was **last-writer-wins**: the whole netdev inherited whichever sibling was walked last. A low-trust tunnel unit therefore gained its sibling's management admission (e.g. `ssh`) purely by snapshot row order, and the winning override also occupied the slot ahead of the contested-zone empty sentinel. This is the Rust helper-boundary backstop: Go resolves the effective set per unit *name* (`#3362`/`#3720`), but a drifted or hostile snapshot can still stamp divergent triples onto one ifindex (the issue's fix direction: extend the `ensure_shared_ifindex_value`/`UnitZoneClaim` coverage to the host-inbound override, or refuse the disputed override).

## Fix (userspace-dp, build-time only)

- New `UnitHostInboundClaim` + `unit_host_inbound_claims()` / `unit_host_inbound_claims_admit()`, mirroring the `#7509` `unit_zone_claims` / `unit_rows_admit` pattern: precomputed before the walk, keyed by ifindex, over **configured logical-unit rows only**. Comparing only the effective token triples: unconfigured rows cast no vote (they would fall back to their zone set per-unit), and zone divergence alone is not a dispute (Go merges physical→unit per unit name, so cross-zone stale stamps are judged by their effective sets, not by provenance).
- The walk now refuses **every** override write on a disputed ifindex, base row included — keeping any one would hand the sibling's admission to the whole netdev.
- After the walk, the disputed ifindex gets the same **empty fail-closed `ZoneHostInbound` sentinel** (`ndp_excluded: true`) the `#10503` contested-zone backstop installs, plus a once-per-build `WARNING` naming the ifindex and the operator remedies — so the deny is observable (`#8296`) instead of silently falling back to the zone set or the `None => true` global admit.
- Unchanged, byte-identical paths: units whose triples **agree**, a single configured unit beside unconfigured siblings, `#12646` unit-0-beats-base in both row orders, base-only overrides, and units on distinct ifindexes.

## Tests (decisive regression)

- `shared_ifindex_disputed_unit_host_inbound_refused_in_both_row_orders_16057` — two same-zone units (`st0.0`=ssh, `st0.1`=https) on one ifindex, in both row orders, plus a base row carrying a third override in first/last position: neither sibling's service, nor the base's, nor the zone's any-service set (via port 179) is admitted; the sentinel is present; global ICMP destination-unreachable still passes. Restoring plain last-writer-wins turns the last unit's service assertion RED.
- `shared_ifindex_agreed_or_single_unit_host_inbound_still_admitted_16057` — positive controls: agreed triples keep the override, one configured + one unconfigured unit keeps it in both orders, distinct ifindexes keep their own overrides. Guards against an over-broad refusal.

### Fold (post-review): effective-set comparison + ND wording

Per the Opus hostile review: the dispute comparison now uses the **canonical effective-admission signature** (sorted/deduped token sets + effective ND-withdrawn bit, mirroring Go's `CanonicalHostInboundTokenSigExcept`) instead of ordered raw vectors — reordered/duplicate/non-ND-except-provenance differences no longer falsely dispute. An effective ND-only difference still disputes (counterweight test). The sentinel keeps #10503 fail-closed semantics (ND denied); the warning/changelog text now says so truthfully, and ND 133-136 denied / errors 1-4 admitted are pinned through both admission entry points. New Go producer regression (`TestSharedIfindexReorderedUnitOverridesShareOneSignature_16057`) proves reversed authored order on the same-zone GRE-tunnel fixture stamps differently-ordered slices with equal signatures.

Observed locally (TMPDIR/CARGO_TARGET_DIR under `/var/worktrees`):
- Pre-fold: `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp 16057` — 2 passed; `forwarding_build::` — 316 passed; `host_inbound` — 68 passed
- Post-fold, post-rebase onto `origin/master` (351ca72aec): `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp 16057` — 4 passed; `forwarding_build::` — 321 passed; `host_inbound` — 69 passed (pre-rebase); Go producer + `TestOneOwnersAgreeingUnitsStillResolveOneZone_6722` PASS

## Perf impact

None on the packet/hot path. The claim map is built once per snapshot apply in `populate_interfaces` (config-build path), alongside the existing `unit_zone_claims` precomputation; `host_inbound_admits_iface` and the per-packet lookup are untouched.

## Risk

Fail-closed direction only: a snapshot whose units genuinely disagree now denies host-bound services on that ifindex instead of admitting one sibling's set. Legitimate Go snapshots stamp identical effective sets on collapsed units, so no production config changes behaviour. The changelog is updated.

## PR #16116 — userspace-dp: scope IKE DNAT discriminator on logical ingress (#16047) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-21)

Branch: `fix/16047-ike-dnat-discriminator`

Refs #16047

## Summary
The Stage-11 IKE transit-DNAT discriminator (`ipsec_destination_matches_transit_dnat`) scoped its DNAT probe on the raw physical `meta.ingress_ifindex` (zone / interface-name / routing-instance), ignoring the logical VLAN unit, fabric-validated identity, and ambiguous-stamp promotion that policy and the pre-routing DNAT lookup use. On a trunk whose VLAN units sit in distinct zones/interfaces/RIs it could match a sibling unit's scoped DNAT (or miss its own) and mis-deliver UDP/500 between transit and local charon; an ambiguous claim could be granted before owner proof.

## Fix
- Probe now scopes on the logical VLAN unit (`ingress_logical` from `ike_host_inbound_gate_context_with_ambiguous`), the fabric-validated zone override, and the validated NAT-scope ifindex (`meta.fabric_ingress_ifindex` for ValidScoped, else logical), mirroring `prerouting_ingress_scope`; unknown VIDs suppress the local zone fallback.
- Ambiguous claimed zone enters only via the local-address owner-RG gated override; only with that promotion does the withheld claimed zone + `ambiguous_scope_ifindex` re-scope the probe. Without owner proof it fails closed (claimed-local, host-inbound gate under fabric/logical zone).
- New `stage_ipsec_passthrough_check_with_scope` carries `ambiguous_scope_ifindex` from the poll loop; existing `stage_ipsec_passthrough_check` wrapper unchanged. Contract documented in `forwarding/README.md`.

## Decisive regression
- `stage_ipsec_transit_dnat_discriminator_uses_logical_vlan_16047`: UDP/500 to WAN VIP on VID-80 (wan) matches wan-scoped transit DNAT → `NotClaimed` (transit/internal charon); same packet on VID-50 (lan) → `Passthrough` (local); `from interface reth0.50` DNAT matches only the lan unit.
- `stage_ipsec_ambiguous_claim_does_not_grant_transit_dnat_16047`: ambiguous claim for permit zone without owner proof → `Denied` (fails closed), not transit.

## Validation
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 16047` — 2 passed.
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- stage_ipsec` — 12 passed.
- Four `prerouting_scope` ARP-learning tests fail identically on unmodified origin/master (pre-existing, unrelated to this change).

## Perf impact
Dataplane Stage-11 hot path: no allocation; single bounded DNAT lookup (same walk production performs), no allocation. Ordinary IPsec/non-IPsec paths unchanged — negligible.

## Risk
Scoped to the interface-local IPsec discriminator; DNAT hit counter/translation remain owned by the normal NAT stage (probe stays read-only).

## PR #16118 — logging: route all slog through bounded syslog writer (#16083) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-21)

Branch: `fix/16083-syslog-nonblocking`

Refs #16083

## Why
Non-event slog forwarding was synchronous: `SyslogSlogHandler.Handle` called `SyslogClient.Send` directly for every non-EventReader caller. A blackholed TCP/TLS collector could park arbitrary daemon goroutines (commit/apply, reconcile, API handlers) behind the client mutex for the write/dial timeout. Startup/reconcile under a slow collector therefore degraded unrelated work — a logging concern gating daemon liveness.

## What
- Route all slog through the existing bounded per-client writer (`SendFromEventReader` queue, depth 128) regardless of caller context, carrying `r.Time` for #15699 header parity.
- Replace the handler-wide #2287 goroutine guard with a per-client writer-scoped drop (`goroutineContext`): records emitted from inside a client's own writer loop (drop warnings) are dropped+counted via `DroppedWrites`, never re-queued; unrelated concurrent records for other clients unaffected.
- Bound memory: slog records cap at 64 KiB each (~8 MiB/client); overflow + oversize drops warn at most once a second, outside the writer mutex.
- `EventReader.ForwardLogMsg` syslog branch queues too; local-writer branch stays synchronous (callers rely on the returned error; local file writes are not a collector stall).
- Direct `Send`/`SendBinary` callers keep their synchronous contract.
- Fold (Opus2): restored `aggregatorFlushJoinTimeout`; added orderly shutdown drain — `SyslogSlogHandler.ShutdownTimeout`/`SyslogClient.CloseTimeout` deliver the queued backlog behind a flush barrier within one shared deadline, remainder discarded+counted; `runShutdownSequence` drains the handler last (2s).

- New `pkg/daemon/syslog_shutdown_drain_16083_test.go`: drives the real `runShutdownSequence` with a gated collector; queued + shutdown-complete records delivered before return, writer goroutine exited.
- `go build ./...` passes; `go test ./pkg/logging/ -count=1` passes; `-race` over the touched paths passes. Rebased onto current master (incl. #16122).

## Risk
Syslog delivery becomes at-most-once under backlog by design (drops counted); shutdown waits at most 2s extra for a healthy backlog flush.

## PR #16119 — dataplane: scope tunnel-unit mirrors per logical unit (#16063) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-21)

Branch: `fix/16063-mirror-unit-scope`

## Summary
Fixes SI-5 (#16063, split from #15985): a port-mirroring input naming `wg0.1` mirrored **every sibling tunnel unit** sharing the netdev, because the mirror scope was `(ifindex, VID=0)` and all tunnel units on `wg0` carry VID 0.

Refs #16063

## Fold note (supersedes first head 02c39cb)
Adversarial review (Opus, NEEDS-FIX) proved — and I verified in source — that per-packet unit keying is **impossible** for sibling tunnel units: production shape is `wg0`/`wg0.0`/`wg0.1` ALL on ifindex 42 (Go maps every interface-level tunnel unit onto one netdev); packet metadata at every mirror callsite is `(ifindex, VID)` only, and GRE/WG decap rebinds inner packets to the endpoint's **single** `logical_ifindex` (interface-level WG emits ONE endpoint, lowest unit — `EmitTunnelEndpointNames`). There is no resolved logical ingress per unit to thread. The first head's name-suffix keying read a last-wins map and still mirrored both units. This head takes the issue's other allowed fix direction: **shared-ifindex refusal**, with honest per-unit keying only where a real unit identity exists.

## Fix
- **Go builder (authoritative):** counts unit rows per `(ifindex, VID)`; a unit input sharing that key with a sibling unit is **refused** with a recorded `MirrorExclusion` (`config.TunnelUnitSharedIfindexMirrorReason`) — `wg0.1`-only now mirrors *nothing* instead of *everything*. Bare `wg0` (whole device) still installs unscoped. Also fixes `scopeByName` so a unit row's `LinuxName` can't overwrite the base row's exact-Name scope.
- **Rust:** scoped key stays `(ifindex, VID, unit)`, but the packet's unit comes from `ForwardingState.ingress_unit_by_logical`, built once per snapshot from rows whose `(bind, VID)` has exactly ONE unit row (VLAN units, lone unit 0) — never from last-wins name parsing. Shared tunnel ifindexes are absent, so even a hand-built scoped row matches nothing.
- **Protocol 64 → 65** (rebased after #16117 took v64): Go/Rust constants, #8892 version pin (golden unchanged), 6691 current-version pin migrated.

## Decisive regression (production shape, real builders)
- Go `TestBuildMirrorConfigSnapshotsTunnelUnitScope16063`: rows base+`wg0.0`+`wg0.1` all @42 → `wg0.1` input refused, zero snapshots, named exclusion; bare `wg0` control installs.
- Rust `tunnel_units_sharing_ifindex_have_no_unit_identity_16063`: state built through the **real** `build_forwarding_state` from those rows (ONE ifindex 42, VID 0, units 0/1, no hand-seeded logical indices) → no unit identity for 42; a wg0.1 scoped row mirrors neither unit's packet.

## Validation
- `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run 'TestBuildMirror|TestMixedVersionMatrix_6691|TestSnapshotShapeIsPinned|TestSnapshotProtocolVersionLockstep|TestProtocolVersionMoved'` — PASS
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp mirror::` — 34/34 PASS
- Fail-on-revert: publishing the shared row mirrors wg0.0 (Go cell red); seeding unit identity for 42 turns the Rust cell red.

## Perf impact (dataplane)
Hot path: `resolve_mirror_config` swaps the name-map probe + suffix parse for one `FastMap` probe (`ingress_unit_by_logical`); no allocation; unit map built once per snapshot apply. Go refusal is snapshot-build time only.

## Risk
Mirroring one unit of a multi-unit tunnel now yields a named NOT-INSTALLED refusal instead of silent sibling mirroring; bare-device mirroring remains supported. Mixed-version helpers refuse v65 by exact equality (prior-good retained).

## PR #16120 — filter: reject shared-ifindex filter conflicts on WG units (#16059) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-21)

Branch: `fix/16059-wg-filter-shared-ifindex`

Refs #16059

## Why
The per-interface filter fast maps (`iface_filter_*_fast`) are keyed by `i32` ifindex alone. Units of an interface-level WireGuard tunnel share one kernel ifindex (`wg0.0`/`wg0.1` → one `wg0` netdev via `TunnelNameMap`), so two units naming different filters for the same family+direction silently last-won in `assign_interface_filters` — the losing unit's filter never evaluated a packet, order-dependently (fail-open for a deny filter). GRE input is the designed first-sorting-wins case owned by #10816 and is not re-litigated; zone policy is independent and untouched.

## What
- **Rust (root fix, snapshot boundary):** `assign_interface_filters` now rejects the snapshot with the new `SnapshotIntegrityError::InterfaceFilterSharedIfindexConflict` when two non-base rows (`is_unit != Some(false)`; known base rows carry no Go filter fields) sharing an ifindex disagree on a configured family+direction hook. Identical names and single-claimant shapes (one unit filtered, sibling empty) stay valid and deterministic. Per-unit keying was rejected: every hot-path lookup keys by bare ifindex and WG/output carries no per-packet unit identity, so per-unit maps would be dead state. Mirrors the CoS duplicate-unit gate (#11429). The #6236 final-map aggregate pin moves to known-base rows, preserving its last-wins coverage.
- **Go (commit advisory):** `appendWgUnitFilterShadowAdvisory16059Locked` warns at commit time for the interface-level WG shape (per-unit-stanza units excluded — own device), covering all four hooks, wired into both compile paths next to the #10816 GRE advisory.
- Docs: `docs/log/16059.md`, filter README section, debian/changelog.

## Validation
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- shared_ifindex_wg_filters duplicate_ifindex_output_filter capability_accessors_equal` — 3 passed. The decisive cell proves the pre-fix winner shape (differing WG output filters on ifindex 42) now rejects in both row orders, all four arms reject, and identical/single-claimant shapes compile with the fast map holding the claimed filter.
- `go test ./pkg/config/ -run TestWgUnitFilterShadowAdvisory16059` — ok (fires once for differing output and input filters; silent for uniform, single-claimant, per-unit-stanza, GRE).
- Note: `TestGreUnitFilterShadowAdvisory10816` case (e) fails on current master at the unrelated #15034 untagged-unit gate (verified the failure is in its non-tunnel `ge-0/0/0 unit 1` fixture, untouched by this change).

## Perf impact
No dataplane hot-path impact. The gate is snapshot-build-time only (one extra cold pass over interface rows with a small hash map); per-packet lookups, fast-map shapes, and aggregates are byte-identical for accepted snapshots.

## Risk
Configs unknowingly relying on last-wins differing per-unit filters on a shared WG ifindex now have the snapshot refused at reconcile (prior good state kept) with a commit-time warning — intended fail-closed behavior. Identical-filter, single-filter, and single-unit configs are unaffected.

## PR #16165 — nat: withdraw contested shared-ifindex config names (#16061) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-21)

Branch: `fix/16061-ifindex-config-name`

Refs #16061

## Summary

`ifindex_to_config_name` was written unconditionally per snapshot row, so on an ifindex shared by distinct logical units (interface-level tunnels via `TunnelNameMap`, unit 0 collapsed on its base) the **last row walked named the device**. `nat_scope_ctx_for_flow` / `prerouting_ingress_scope` read that single name for `from interface` / `to interface` NAT matching, so a rule scoped to one sibling matched traffic the dataplane can only attribute to the shared ifindex — and which sibling won depended on row order (SI-4-name).

## Fix

In `populate_interfaces` (`forwarding_build/interfaces.rs`), track the config name claimed by **logical-unit rows** per ifindex:

- While every unit row on an ifindex agrees on one name, that name stands.
- A distinct unit name **contests** the ifindex: the entry is withdrawn entirely. An absent name reads as `""` at every NAT-scope consumer, so an interface-scoped rule matches **neither** sibling — fail-closed, identical in both row orders — instead of matching the last-written sibling.
- Base rows are device aliases, not traffic identities, and never contest: the ordinary base + unit-0 pair keeps the unit's name byte-identically, duplicate rows naming the same unit agree, and a lone base row keeps its own name.
- The #10313 parent fallback (`entry(parent).or_insert(base)`) is skipped when the parent slot is itself contested, so a collapsed unit cannot resurrect even its base name (`wg0`) onto the contested ifindex (caught by the new end-to-end cell).
- One operator warning per contested ifindex per build naming every claiming unit, mirroring the #7509 zone-contest observability rule.
- Updated the stale "config_name stays last-wins by design" pin in `same_ifindex_member_claim_survives_trailing_default_row` (routing-instance/domain semantics unchanged).

This mirrors the established #7509 discipline for zones: an ifindex that identifies no single unit answers with nothing rather than a guess.

## Regression

- `config_name_16061_tests`: contested name withdrawn in both row orders; NAT scope on a contested ifindex reads `""`; agreeing/alias controls (base+unit-0 both orders, same-unit duplicate, lone base).
- `snat_from_interface_never_matches_a_sibling_on_a_shared_ifindex_16061`: end-to-end through `build_forwarding_state` + `match_source_nat_for_flow` — neither sibling's `from interface wg0.0/wg0.1` SNAT rule matches on the shared ifindex in either row order, while a zone-scoped rule on the same traffic still matches (same-device intent stays expressible, just not per-unit).

## Validation

- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp 16061` — 4 passed.
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp forwarding_build::` — 317 passed, 1 ignored.
- Full `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp` — 9012 passed, 63 failed, 10 ignored; all 63 failures reproduce on pristine `origin/master` (failure-set diff verified via stash; pristine run additionally showed one flaky screen test that passed in the changed run).

## Risk / perf

Build-time only; the NAT match path is untouched (it already treats `""` as no-match for an interface-scoped rule). **Perf impact: none on the packet path**; one extra BTreeMap probe per interface row at snapshot build. Deployments with distinct units sharing one ifindex *and* per-unit `from/to interface` NAT scoping will see those rules stop matching (fail-closed, with the new warning line naming the units); zone- or routing-instance-scoped rules on the same traffic are unaffected.

## Risk
At-most-once syslog delivery under backlog (drops counted); shutdown waits ≤2s extra for a healthy flush.

Perf impact: logging goroutines never block on the collector — one bounded non-blocking handoff per record per client.

## PR #16214 — userspace-dp: re-resolve stale SNAT sessions after takeover (#16109) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-21)

Branch: `fix/16109b-takeover`

Refs #16109

## Why
Peer-synced sessions terminalized on the standby (DiscardRoute/ClusterTerminalHAInactive, egress 0) were judged on their stored decision at first hit on the new owner, so the SNAT revalidator revoked-and-deleted live flows. MissingNeighbor-era resolutions also stayed latched after neighbors landed, blackholing established flows after RG activation.

## What
- (i) RefreshOwnerRGS overwrites a stored terminal decision with the live re-resolved decision; genuinely non-forwarding outcomes keep HOLD-clock exclusion.
- (ii) SNAT revalidation declines to judge a stored terminal peer-synced row, otherwise judges the packet's re-resolved decision.
- (iii) Helper-local neighbor_generation as third ForwardingGenerationStamp component, advanced only on effective neighbor-set change (snapshot_refresh + manager-neighbor push). Go fib_generation untouched.
- Surgical ValidationState/ForwardingGenerationStamp literal fixes; one test baseline corrected (contradicted snapshot arm empty->set advance).

## Validation
- cargo test 16109: 3/3 pass.
- Affected suites: 1087 passed, 6 failed — identical 6 on clean origin/master (pre-existing, incl. SessionDecision size 116 vs 112).
- Live forwarding-only: 13.8 Gbps P4.
- Live RG1 failover: still permanent zeros — BUT identical zeros reproduced on clean origin/master in same sequence, so not a regression of this change; takeover fix not sufficient on current master / sequence. Cluster restored to clean master build.

## Risk
neighbor_generation helper-local only, never crosses to Go/shim. Decline-to-judge scoped to peer-synced terminal rows; withdrawn rules still revoke once real resolution exists.

## PR #16227 — dataplane: add SessionValue/SessionValueV6 sync-field parity test (#16176) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-22)

Branch: `fix/16176-sessionsync-parity`

Refs #16176

## Why
`SessionValue` and `SessionValueV6` are hand-maintained twins whose trailing HA-sync fields are duplicated verbatim; a field once added to v4 only left every IPv6 session degraded after a failover, and the only guard was prose. The `SessionSyncMeta` embed was demoted by hostile review (promoted fields cannot be composite-literal keys, the ABI prefix is not contiguous, and the #7097 scrub census would weaken under an embed); the parity test is the endorsed survivor. This PR ships **only** the parity test — no embed.

**Fold (Opus review):** the original classification census was not closed under field additions — a new sync field added to both twins AND the codec without updating the declared list escaped every guard. The census is now exhaustive (below), codec discovery is syntax-aware, and the classification prose is corrected.

## What
- `pkg/dataplane/session_sync_parity_16176_test.go` (new, test-only):
  - Reflection parity by field name+type between `SessionValue` and `SessionValueV6`, excluding exactly `NATSrcIP`/`NATDstIP` (uint32 vs `[16]byte`), `ReverseKey` (`SessionKey` vs `SessionKeyV6`), and v6-only `Nat64SnatV4 [4]byte` (#4565) — with the excluded fields' exact per-family types pinned, not just presence.
  - **Closed classification census** (`TestSessionFieldClassificationIsExhaustive16176`): the field universe is enumerated from both Go twins, both BPF mirrors, and the AST-discovered codec references; every name must be classified in exactly one class — ABI / sync-wire / Go-local — with a justification, every classification must name a real field, and per-class membership is checked against the discovered sets. The exact set is published in the test header, including the `NatScopeIfindex` Go-local justification (node-local ifindex in neither `bpfSessionValue{,V6}` nor the sync codec; only its cluster-stable fold `NatScopeFold` crosses, stamped at `sync_conn_gen.go:595`) and the three ABI-only fields (`AppID`, `IngressIfindex`, `IngressVlanID` — ABI need not be codec-carried).
  - Corrected boundary rule: no field present in the sync codec but in neither BPF ABI struct may be added to `bpfSessionValue{,V6}`, checked against the discovered codec set (positive control pins `State`/`Flags`/`PolicyID`/NAT ports/`ReverseKey`/`RoutingDomain` as intentionally shared; the report's literal assertion is not shipped).
  - Codec discovery is **syntax-aware**: `go/parser` AST scoped to `encode/decodeSession{,V6}Payload`, collecting encode reads and decode writes (incl. nested `val.ReverseKey.*` and copy-through-slice), tail fields via encoder call sites. Comments/strings can neither satisfy nor break membership (`TestCodecFieldRefsIgnoreComments16176` self-check on a synthetic fixture). The previous raw `.Name` text scan is removed.
- No embed, no struct/literal/existing-census change; existing ABI pins (`bpf_session_value_test.go` 152/200, `session_value_offsets_6816_test.go`, `peer_install_scrub_7097`) unmodified.

## PR #16229 — config: add lenient-bool completeness test recursing embedded opts (#16166) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-22)

Branch: `fix/16166-lenient-bool-completeness`

Refs #16166

## Why
Adding a tolerant-path gate requires (1) a `lenient*`/`sanitize*` bool field in `compileOpts` and (2) its `field: true` entry in `lenientCompileOpts()`. Forgetting (2) silently makes tolerant load / peer-sync strict for that gate — the #1960 brick-the-boot class — with no compiler error (zero value is valid). Until now only reviewer vigilance enforced the invariant. A shallow reflect walk would also miss the two lenient bools in the embedded `protocolScopeOpts` (Codex dissent incorporated in #16166).

## What
Test-only PR-0 (no registry, no `Diagnostic` type, no gate moves, no essay deletion, no baseline regen):
- `TestLenientCompileOptsCompleteness16166`: reflects **recursively** over `compileOpts` (embedded/nested structs included, `protocolScopeOpts` pinned by name) and requires every `lenient*`/`sanitize*` bool `true` in `lenientCompileOpts()`. Non-downgrade bools (`skipCompactNormalize`, `nodeAware`, the four `suppress*` advisory bools) are explicitly allowlisted/classified, so any new bool forces a deliberate decision.
- `TestLenientCompletenessWalkRecurses16166`: proves the walk reaches a planted bool inside an embedded struct, so flattening the walk cannot silently green the test.

Census re-measured at this head (`2c8575b70e` base): **298** `lenient*`/`sanitize*` bools — 296 direct in `compileOpts` + 2 in embedded `protocolScopeOpts` — all `true` today (298/298; audit counts 297→299→300 drifted, as the issue predicted).

Scope note: PR-0 enforces links 1–2 only (field + lenient literal); it does not claim link 3–4 (gate call-site / warning surface) — that is the separately gated W2.1 registry.

## Validation
- New tests PASS on this head: `TestLenientCompileOptsCompleteness16166`, `TestLenientCompletenessWalkRecurses16166`.
- RED proof: planting an unregistered `lenientPlantedDirect16166` (direct) and `lenientPlantedEmbedded16166` (inside `protocolScopeOpts`) both FAIL the completeness test, reporting `lenientPlantedDirect16166` and `protocolScopeOpts.lenientPlantedEmbedded16166`; plants then removed.
- `go vet ./pkg/config/` clean, file gofmt-clean.
- `TestCompileGolden4406` and `TestCompactNormalizeScopePreservesCompiledResult8690`: FAIL **identically on pristine origin/master** (pre-existing baseline drift at `2c8575b70e`, verified in a scratch base worktree) — unchanged by this PR, and no baseline was regenerated (issue stop-rule).

None to production: test-only, no compile-behavior or dataplane/hot-path impact, no perf impact.

## PR #16238 — test: complete wire fixture coverage before any manifest-diff (#16132) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-22)

Branch: `fix/16132-wire-fixture-completeness`

## Summary

Refs #16132 — fixture-completeness first, test-only. **No manifest, no codegen**: per the issue's narrowed, escape-gated form, a manifest is built only after a demonstrated drift escapes fixture-completeness, and no such escape exists yet. Existing independent goldens are kept; `#[repr(C)]` BPF map keys stay out of the JSON fixture (separate ABI, own size/offset tests).

## What

- **Populated specimens** (`userspace-dp/src/protocol/tests.rs`, regenerated `protocol_wire_v1.json`): every field a `::default()` specimen cannot show is now exercised — the 92 previously missing top-level `skip_serializing_if` keys plus previously uncovered nested DTOs (FibRoute/FibNextHop, SessionPolicyMatch/Tuple, SessionCounter row/query, pmech inventory tree, NAT port/app terms, key-ring, S5 provenance, WG statuses, and more). Synthetic sentinels only. Default specimens unchanged (additive keys only).
- **Rust census gate** `wire_fixture_completeness_16132`: independently parses `src/protocol/*.rs` **directionally** — serialize and deserialize names separately, modelling `rename`, `rename(serialize/deserialize)`, container `rename_all` (serde's exact field case rules), deserialize `alias`, directional skips, and `serde(transparent)`; it fails loudly on `flatten`/unmodelled custom forms rather than modelling them wrong. Every serializable field's serialize key must appear in a specimen of its type; the four deserialize-only secrets are asserted absent; census/specimen zero-field guards prevent vacuous green. Any directional rename or new alias must be recorded in an explicit exception table (`DIRECTIONAL_DE_EXCEPTIONS` / `KNOWN_DE_ALIASES`) or the gate fails.
- **Go gate** `TestWireFixtureCompleteness16132`: fails (never skips) on missing fixture, strict-decodes every specimen into its Go type with `DisallowUnknownFields`, and requires Go keys from a reflectively fully-populated value to appear in the fixture. Its one-sided allowlists are **self-auditing**: every entry is re-validated each run for existence on its stated side and continued absence on the opposite side, plus duplicate, unauditable-type, and stale-secret checks — an exception that stops being true fails instead of becoming a permanent blind spot. The `fallback_counters` MarshalJSON legacy alias is modelled explicitly as a marshal-emitted (non-tag) key.

## Fold (Opus review)

1. Directional serde renames: census previously read only shared `rename = "..."`, so `rename(deserialize="peer_endpoint_typo")` greened while silently breaking Go→Rust decode. Now censused directionally; that exact witness mutation goes red.
2. Allowlist entries are now re-validated every run (see above); stale and one-sidedness-broken entries go red (mutation-checked).
3. Rebased onto current master; changelog conflict resolved by stacking this entry above master's.

## Validation

- `wire_invariant_default_specimens` and `wire_fixture_completeness_16132` pass; `TestWireFixtureCompleteness16132` passes (128 specimens, 3,270 top-level fields compared).
- Mutation-checked (each restored after going red): renamed fixture key, renamed Go `json` tag, u16 width overflow (`src_port: 70000`), directional deserialize rename witness, and stale/one-sidedness-broken allowlist entries all fail.

## Risk / perf

Test-only; no production, wire-format, or dataplane behaviour change, and **no hot-path/perf impact**. Residual (documented in the tests): a same-key width change where both widths fit the Go field is not machine-caught until a specimen value exercises the range — that demonstrated escape is exactly the trigger the issue sets for building the width-aware manifest-diff later.

## PR #16247 — userspace-dp: add lock-free pre-check to PPTP inbox drains (#16240) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-22)

Branch: `fix/16240-pptp-lockfree-gate`

## Summary
Each of the four PPTP inbox `take_*` methods acquired the single shared inbox mutex before checking the 1s `CONTROL_DRAIN_INTERVAL_NS` gate — 4 global-mutex acquisitions per worker per tick returning empty, with PPTP enabled by default. This adds a lock-free atomic last-drain pre-check inside each `take_*`; the in-lock gate stays authoritative.

Refs #16240

## What changed
- `PptpControlInbox` mirrors all four guarded timestamps (`last_drain_ns`, `last_forget_retry_ns`, `last_call_forget_retry_ns`, `last_call_install_retry_ns`) into `AtomicU64` fields.
- Each `take_*` (`take_pending_in_domain`, `take_channel_forget_retries`, `take_call_forget_retries`, `take_call_install_retries_at`) first does one `Relaxed` load (`gate_closed`); inside the interval it returns empty with no lock. Hot path: one atomic load per take, no lock when gated.
- Mirror is stored under the lock at the same instant the guarded timestamp is set, so a stale mirror can only cause a spurious lock acquisition, never a skipped due drain. `mark_*_sent` sites never mutate any guarded timestamp (verified — they only prune `unsent_queue_ids`), so no mirror store is needed there; the invariant is documented for future changes.
- NOT changed: drain timing, epoch filtering, call sites, or non-`take_*` locking.

## Tests
- New `lockfree_gate_tests_16240`: all four gated `take_*` assert **zero** lock acquisitions inside the interval (via a `cfg(test)` lock counter) and drain exactly at the interval boundary; `mark_*_sent` ack keeps the gate and is not redelivered.
- Smoke: `cargo test pptp` — 94 passed, 1 failed. The failure (`event_stream::pptp_open_frame_carries_the_call_id_pair_13965`) fails identically on unmodified `origin/master` (verified via stash) — pre-existing, unrelated.
- `cargo build` clean.

## PR #16248 — docs: add mutation-inheritance paragraph to engineering style (#16199) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-22)

Branch: `fix/16199-mutation-inheritance-doc`

Refs #16199

## Why

`docs/engineering-style.md` warned "a deleted guard cannot fail" but had no protocol for when a test may be deleted. Naming a replacement test by name alone is insufficient: one mutation may exercise only one of several assertions the deleted test carried, so a deletion can silently drop coverage while the named successor stays green on that mutation.

## What

One doc paragraph in `docs/engineering-style.md` only, with one worked example:

- A test may be deleted only when the change names the subsuming instrument and shows it red on the mutation(s) the deleted test existed to kill — not merely green on the new tree, and not merely named as the replacement.
- References the `scripts/mutate-lib.sh` convention: a failure count is not a kill; the NAMED target must fail (`mutation_verdict_for_target` over `go test -json` names) and, where the reason matters, its own output must carry the expected message (`mutation_verdict_for_message`), or the verdict is not `KILLED`.
- Worked example: a deleted test asserting both "out-of-range port rejected" and "error names the field" needs two mutations (one per assertion); a successor red only on the first does not subsume it and the deletion does not land.

No tooling, no census changes, no skip-annotation or `.unreached`-inventory machinery (rejected/deferred duplicates of `go-skip-census` per #16199).

## Validation

- `git diff --name-only origin/master...HEAD` → `docs/engineering-style.md` only (20 insertions).
- Paragraph present immediately after the "A deleted guard cannot fail" passage; referenced functions verified present in `scripts/mutate-lib.sh` (`mutation_verdict_for_target`, `mutation_verdict_for_message`).
- No code changed, so no test suite run.

## Risk

None to production/operator behaviour — docs only. Perf impact: none (no dataplane/hot-path or code change).

New Go wire-level matrix over the real socket decoder, each row compared against the pre-change prefix-only classification: success, false-positive prefix (token not at start), missing fields (old Rust → new Go), prefix-only, code+prefix (new pair), recognized code without prefix, **unknown code + known prefix → prefix wins**, unknown code without prefix → retained (not forced terminal), right code + wrong retry class → prefix fallback, empty error. Plus a JSON skew test (old-helper JSON decodes empty fields; new-helper JSON carries prose and code together). Rust tests assert both apply legs stamp the code; Go constants are bound to the Rust constants by reading `control.rs` (same convention as the existing prefix pins).

None on the dataplane hot path: the fields are set only on the cold post-teardown refusal path in the control handler and are omitted from the wire when empty.

Low. Additive wire fields; mixed-version Go×Rust pairs classify identically by the fallback rule. The single intentional divergence (recognized code on non-prefix prose) cannot occur from the real helper, which stamps the code only at post-teardown legs.

## PR #16259 — userspace-dp: genericise prefix set over address family (#16189) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-22)

Branch: `fix/16189-prefix-set-generic`

Refs #16189

## Why

`userspace-dp/src/prefix_set.rs` carried twin `merged_ranges_v4`/`merged_ranges_v6`, twin `PrefixSetV4`/`PrefixSetV6` impls, and twin fail-open `MatchAny` defaults (~190 duplicated lines in a 421-line file). Exact duplicates drift silently. The `(1 << (BITS - len)) - 1` host-mask computation is safe only behind the len==0 / len>=BITS guards.

## What

- One generic `PrefixSet<F: PrefixFamily>`; `PrefixSetV4 = PrefixSet<PrefixV4Family>`, `PrefixSetV6 = PrefixSet<PrefixV6Family>` (aliases — every `policy.rs` caller compiles unchanged).
- `host_mask` is a **required** `PrefixFamily` method with the length guards inside each impl (no default body); call sites cannot inline the shift.
- `merged_ranges`, both factories, `contains`, `is_match_*`, `prefix_count`, `heap_bytes` written once behind a small `PrefixKey` (u32/u128) bound.
- NOT changed: `prefix.rs` — family prefix types keep their surface (`PrefixV4::directed_broadcast` stays v4-only), per the narrowed issue scope.
- Fail-open `Default::MatchAny` semantics unchanged per family (#7745 comment preserved).

## Validation

- `cargo test --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml prefix_set`: corpus green (16 pre-existing cells incl. #15091 typed budget, 850k-range memory bound, at-budget control, covered/adjacent merge) + 4 new #16189 cells:
  - `host_mask_guards_boundaries_16189` — pins the required trait method's guarded values directly (len 0/1/24/31/32/33/255 and 0/1/64/127/128/129/255 + `BITS`).
  - `builder_ranges_at_boundary_lens_16189` — range-correctness only: exact retained ranges at len==BITS (/32, /128) and BITS-1 (/31, /127) for both families.
  - `merged_ranges_byte_identical_per_family_16189` — exact retained ranges + distinct counts per family over covered/adjacent/disjoint/len==BITS corpus.
  - `generic_set_boundary_membership_16189` — edge /32 + /128 membership and MatchAny defaults.
- On the guard's observability, stated plainly: `host_mask`'s guard is an **impl-level** contract. `merged_ranges` has **no observable bypass shape** — constructors funnel len==0 to MatchAny and prefix lens cannot exceed BITS, so the builder only ever sees len in 1..=BITS, where the raw `(1 << (BITS - len)) - 1` shifts by 0 at len==BITS (0..BITS-1 overall) and yields exactly the guarded mask. No test through the builder can distinguish `F::host_mask(..)` from an unguarded inline shift; the builder cell is kept as range-correctness only and claims nothing more.
- `cargo check` clean for `prefix_set.rs` (only pre-existing dead-code notes shared with master).

## Risk / perf

Pure genericisation, monomorphised per family — no allocation, wire, or hot-path shape change (same Linear scan + `partition_point` search; `contains` is `#[inline]` as before). Perf impact: none by construction. No production caller changes.

## PR #16260 — image: install UMEM hugepage reservation on every provisioning path (#16243) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-22)

Branch: `fix/16243-umem-hugepages`

Refs #16243

## Why

Plan measured `Hugepage-backed bindings: 0/30`, ~5 GiB of 4 KiB-page UMEM on a ring-entries 16384 rig. The bind code was already correct (`MAP_HUGETLB` first in `umem/mmap.rs`, per-binding `hugepage_backed` status, loud fallback, 80-pages/binding sizing pinned by `umem_sizing_contract_tests`). The defect is provisioning: `etc/sysctl.d/99-xpf-hugepages.conf` existed in the repo but **no path installed it** — not `scripts/image/bake.py`, not `debian/rules`, not any deploy tool — and the architecture doc said so explicitly. The rig therefore booted with `HugePages_Total=0` and every UMEM fell back. (The loss cluster's 18/18-backed fw1 vs 6/18 fw0 fixtures show the same split: hand-provisioned vs not.)

## What

- `scripts/image/bake.py`: `hugepages_conf()` reads the repo conf verbatim (single source of truth; bake dies if the pool vanishes) and `virt_customize` writes it to `/etc/sysctl.d/99-xpf-hugepages.conf` in the appliance image.
- `debian/rules`: installs the same file into the `.deb` for foreign-host/manual installs (dpkg conffile — operator resizes are prompted, never silently clobbered).
- `scripts/image/test_bake_hugepages_16243.py` (new): pins the verbatim bake install, the ≥80×18-page reference pool, and the fail-closed loader.
- Docs: `docs/deploy-quickstart.md` gains the knob/resize/verify procedure + a `0/N` troubleshooting row; the architecture doc's stale "image ships NO reservation" claim is corrected; the conf header names its installers; changelog entry.

## Validation

- `python3 -m unittest scripts.image.test_bake_hugepages_16243 scripts.image.test_bake_transit_sysctls_10765` — OK (4 tests).
- Mutation: `vm.nr_hugepages 1440→600` reds the pool test (exactly the one-NIC shortfall that caused this issue).
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp umem_sizing_contract` — 4/4 pass (pre-existing pins the new bake test relies on).
- `debian/rules override_dh_auto_install` dry-run shows the conffile install line.

## Pending-main checks (cluster reserved by failover lane — no deploy done)

1. Deploy to a ring-entries 16384 rig; confirm `show dataplane status` reports `Hugepage-backed bindings: N/N` and `HugePages_Total ≥ 1440` in `/proc/meminfo`.
2. Throughput spot-check (expect ~22.1 vs 20.4 Gbps class per the documented measurement).

## Risk

Baked appliances now reserve 1440×2 MiB (2.8 GiB) at boot, withheld from ordinary allocation — the documented trade in the conf header; unused at default ring-entries 1024. Topologies above 18 bindings still need an operator resize of the one file.

## PR #16263 — userspace-dp: measure TX descriptors-per-commit and per-kick (#16242) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-22)

Branch: `fix/16242-batch-histogram`

Refs #16242

## What
Measurement ONLY for the batch-depth question — no batch-size or const-assert changes (`TX_BATCH_SIZE=64` / `RX_BATCH_SIZE=64` untouched).

Existing histogram infra (`tx_kick_latency_*` / `tx_submit_latency_*`) measures latency, not batch depth, so this wires new cheap counters into the same owner-profile + stats export path:

- **Per-commit**: `record_tx_commit` at all six TX-ring `writer.commit()` sites (4 CoS exact-direct in `cos/queue_service/service.rs`, `transmit_batch`, prepared `write.rs`), `inserted > 0` only (zero-insert is already `dbg_tx_ring_full`). One bucket `fetch_add` + two scalar `fetch_add`s, Relaxed, no allocation/clock.
- **Per-kick**: worker-local `tx_pending_kick_descriptors` accumulator drained in `maybe_wake_tx` at each actual `sendto` into `tx_kick_batch_hist`.
- Buckets (11): 1..=7 exact, [8,16), [16,32), [32,64), >=64. Scalars give mean batch = descriptors/commits and full-batch share = hist[10]/commits.
- Export: `BindingLiveSnapshot` -> `BindingStatus`/`BindingCountersSnapshot` (Rust protocol) + Go mirrors in `protocol_binding.go`, zeroed on unbound slots; additive wire keys with defaults both sides.

## How to read it (also in `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tx/README.md`)
Under `-P32` load per queue: if mean batch ~= 64 and bucket 10 dominates, batches already fill and raising the cap is dead — close #16242. If mass sits in buckets 0-6, batches are partial and the lever is drain starvation, not the cap.

**Mouse-latency note**: the 64 cap is the #920 L1d/latency purchase, so any future raise must pair before/after histograms under the same `-P32` load with the mouse-latency matrix (`test-mouse-latency-matrix.sh`); the histogram alone cannot show the latency cost.

## Validation
- `cargo test -- tx_batch tx_kick submit_local`: 19 passed — bucket-layout pin, snapshot propagation, Rust wire round-trip + pre-#16242 back-compat, and `submit_local_records_tx_batch_histogram` (end-to-end through a real submit; goes RED if `record_tx_commit` is removed).
- `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run TxKick|TxBatch`: ok.
- Layout pins updated for the +192B owner profile (2688->2880, offsets +192).

## Pending-main checks (cluster reserved by failover lane — no cluster mutation)
1. Deploy on the tcp cluster, drive `iperf3 -P32` per queue, read `tx_batch_hist`/`tx_kick_batch_hist` from binding status; report mean batch + full-batch share.
2. Mouse-latency matrix run as the latency baseline for any follow-up cap proposal.

## PR #16264 — userspace-xdp: add per-arm branch hit counters (#16241) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-22)

Branch: `fix/16241-xdp-branch-counters`

userspace-xdp: add per-arm branch hit counters (#16241)

Refs #16241

## Why

The narrowed #16241 acceptance requires, in order: (1) fallback-reason/branch hit counts for plain TCP hit-forwards, (2) a per-arm fail-closed analysis, and only then (3) removal of arms proven disposition-identical. The recoverable share of the measured 8.6% BPF self time is unproven without per-arm attribution, and the three-way validation found the original RSS-only slimming UNSOUND (most branches are fail-closed dispositions preventing the #304 kernel-forward-with-no-policy bypass).

## What

Instrumentation + analysis only. **No arm is removed**, because the analysis proves none is disposition-identical to another today. The perf claim is therefore structural and negative: zero branches removed.

- **New per-CPU map `userspace_branch_stats`** (27 slots, index order = dispatch order in `try_xdp_userspace`). A separate map, not new indices in `userspace_fallback_stats`: the degraded indices are a pinned operator ABI (Go `degradedPathReasonNames`, the Rust debug reader, the #8258 index-agreement test), and a hit-forward is not a degraded disposition.
- **Counting is TRACE-gated** inside the single outlined `incr_branch_stat` callee (the `record_trace_packed` #4113-F7 precedent): with tracing off, the hot path pays one flag test in one subprogram, not a map touch per arm. A TRACE-off control test proves dispositions are unchanged while zero branch arms count (and degraded counters still fire).
- **Redirect partitioning**: `session_hit_redirect` / `session_miss_redirect` / `session_miss_ifnat_redirect` count at their classifying arms; `redirect` counts only successes no earlier arm claimed. The four slots partition every successful XSK redirect, so the plain-TCP hit-forward rate reads directly off `session_hit_redirect`.
- **Surfaces**: Go `xdpBranchArmNames` + `readXDPBranchStatsLocked` → `ProcessStatus.XDPBranchCounters` (`xdp_branch_counters`); loader pinning + disposable-pin reconcile + ABI-check exclusion for the new map; Rust `XDP_BRANCH_ARM_NAMES` + `read_xdp_branch_stats` → `XDP_BRANCH:` debug dump.
- **Per-arm fail-closed analysis**: `docs/log/16241.md` — all 27 arms with disposition, fail-closed role, and why no two collapse. Packet classes named by the issue (local / WG / GRE / NAT-miss / early-filter) each have a row and a test cell.
- **Tests proving identical disposition per packet class**: `TestXDPBranchDispositionMatrix16241` runs the retained program via `BPF_PROG_TEST_RUN` for plain-TCP hit (REDIRECT and PASS_TO_KERNEL sessions), plain-TCP miss, local miss, NAT-miss, early-filter multicast, GRE inner-PASS, ARP, and L2 parse-fail — asserting action AND arm counter AND absent arms. Plus the WG steer pair (with/without WG_RX) and index-agreement tests on both sides (`TestXDPBranchArmNamesAgreeWithTheShim16241`, `TestXDPBranchArmsAreAllCounted16241`, Rust `xdp_branch_arm_names_agree_with_the_shim_16241`), all self-enrolling when an arm is added in the shim.

## Verifier cost (measured, structural — not a throughput claim)

Pinned build (nightly-2026-05-23, bpf-linker 0.10.2, `MAX_INTERFACES=65536`) via `cmd/shimverify` on this host (kernel 7.2.8): master object 815623 processed insns (18.44% headroom, PASS) → **862896 (13.71%)**, below the 15% #4555 floor. The object LOADS (not a kernel reject); the +47k is the verifier re-walking the one outlined counter callee under the dispatch's calling states. Because the floor is not met, the tracked object is installed with `XPF_SHIM_ALLOW_LOW_HEADROOM=1`; the gate verdict records `verdict: OVERRIDDEN, override_consumed: true`, and `TestShimGateVerdictIsMeasuredPass14851`'s exception pin is updated to exactly 862896 with a #16241 note (that test's comment had gone stale: #15854 had already retired the exception at 815623 PASS). Retiring the override needs the entry-path restructure deferred since #14954, deliberately not bundled into an instrumentation-only change.

## Validation

Local (this host):

- cargo/bpf pinned build green; shimverify LOADS at 862896 (override disclosed above).
- Privileged BPF cells (root): disposition matrix, WG steer pair, TRACE-gate control — PASS.
- Go: `TestXDPBranchArmNamesAgreeWithTheShim16241`, `TestXDPBranchArmsAreAllCounted16241`, `TestValidateUserspaceShimSpecSkipsDisposableBranchStatsPin16241`, `TestShimGateVerdictIsMeasuredPass14851`, `TestShimHeadroomOutlinesStayOutlined14851` (extended with `incr_branch_stat`), `TestUserspaceXDPShimObjectMatchesSourceManifest`, stack-margin — PASS.

## Pending-main checks (cluster RESERVED by the failover lane — not run here)

- Branch attribution under plain-TCP load: expect `session_hit_redirect` ≈ hit rate, `redirect`=0 for that class, `early_filter`/`wg_steer`/`gre_*`=0 without those features configured.

## PR #16265 — config: refuse jumbo MTU on userspace-bound interfaces at commit (#16244) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-22)

Branch: `fix/16244-mtu-propagation`

## Summary

Traced config mtu -> netdev propagation for XDP-attached interfaces (#16244):

- **Config**: `interfaces <if> mtu` / unit family mtu compile to `InterfaceConfig.MTU` / `InterfaceUnit.MTU`.
- **Netdev**: `planPhysDesired` (pkg/dataplane) merges zoned refs into one MTU per netdev; `mapZoneInterface` writes it via `LinkSetMTU` **before** `LinkSetUp` and before the deferred XDP attach (attach ifindexes are only queued in the same call). networkd also renders `MTUBytes`. So the MTU write already survives XDP attach in-order — propagation to the netdev was never the broken half.
- **AF_XDP**: the Rust helper binds without multi-buffer (`XDP_USE_SG`) support into fixed 4096-byte UMEM frames (`UMEM_FRAME_SIZE`, `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/mod.rs`). Frames above the 3566-byte budget (4096 − 512 headroom − Ethernet/VLAN) cannot reach a worker: copy mode drops them (`kernel_rx_dropped`), zero-copy may refuse the bind. The issue and the Wonder pass are explicit that jumbo-as-workaround is UNSOUND without the UMEM frame-size redesign.

This PR takes the acceptance's second arm — **named refusal at commit** — until that redesign lands:

- `validateUserspaceRxMTUStrict` hard-rejects on strict commit/commit-check any AF_XDP bind parent whose effective MTU exceeds 3566, naming the authored interface, resolved bind netdev when different, effective MTU, budget arithmetic, and remedy (lower to ≤3566 or unzone). The Opus fold replaces the initial per-reference predicate with `userspaceRxMTUBoundParents`: surviving zone membership comes from `InterfaceZoneMap`, rows resolve through `ResolveKernelIfName`, tagged rows redirect to the physical parent, and the lowest referenced untagged unit overrides the interface MTU. #9727 consumes the same effective-parent projection.
- Tolerant load/peer-sync paths downgrade to a warning (`lenientUserspaceRxMTU16244`, #1960 no-brick); the #9727 advisory is suppressed there, so the downgrade is that path's MTU signal.
- Unzoned, tunnel, and lifeline (fxp/em/fab/lo0) MTUs are untouched — jumbo stays legal for kernel-forwarded traffic.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestUserspaceMTU|TestJumboMTU|TestRxMTU|TestVlanUnitMTU|TestCompileTree|TestLenientCompileOpts'` — boundary 3566 accept / 3567 refuse, untagged override both directions, tagged-parent refusal, untagged-sibling acceptance, tagged RETH refusal on resolved member, unzoned+fxp0 accept, lenient and node-lenient warnings
- [x] `go test ./pkg/configstore/ -run TestCheckText.*16244` — day-0/commit-check gate refuses; at-budget and unzoned pass
- [x] `go test ./pkg/dataplane/ -run TestPlanPhysDesired.*16244` — plan carries 9000 to ordinary and tagged parents, 1500 when a referenced untagged sibling lowers the shared parent, and 9000 on the local member for a tagged RETH
- [ ] Full `pkg/config` / `pkg/dataplane` suites exceed the 300s job cap in the authoring environment; sampled broad subsets show only failures reproduced identically on clean `origin/master` (pre-existing #14139/#15034 drift, unrelated) — **pending main-agent full-suite run**
- [ ] Cluster is RESERVED by the failover lane — **no cluster deploy**; iperf at 9000-byte vs 1500-byte frames on the loss cluster is a **pending-main check** (acceptance's measurement arm; expected: 9000 now refuses at commit until the UMEM redesign, 1500 unchanged)

Refs #16244

## PR #16274 — userspace-dp: extract partial-publisher pipeline and stamp dedup (#16153) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-22)

Branch: `fix/16153-partial-publisher`

## Why

W2.4 narrowed survivor (validated-by:research, Codex C binding on P8):

- **P4:** `stampCaptureAuthorityWithRoutesMode` (builder.go) and `refreshCaptureAuthorityLocked` assigned the same four capture fields field-by-field and could drift.
- **P2-narrowed:** `PolicyRuleSnapshot.Action` / `DefaultPolicy` were stringly typed; the send gate checked counts only, so an empty/malformed/future action token shipped to the helper relying solely on the Rust reader.
- **P8-narrowed (canary-aware):** no standalone `binding_plan.go` move — `snapshotBindingPlanKey` et al. stay in `maps_sync.go` where `binding_plan_key_crossplane_8901_test.go`'s source-text canaries read them.

Publishers keep their prep, protocol/disarm gates, error wrapping, and their own dedup predicate: capture ANDs `publishedSnapshot != 0`, link-refresh ANDs `resampled == 0` — characterized, not unified. `syncSnapshotLocked` deliberately not extracted (distinct retained-publish shape, no clone twin).

- P2: typed `policyAction` vocabulary (`permit`/`deny`/`reject`, deliberately not unified with the filter `accept`/`discard` set) + `typedPolicyAction`; `validateSnapshotForSend` refuses unknown/empty rule actions and non-empty garbage defaults as known-unsent (`errSnapshotPolicyAction`, matched by `isKnownUnsentFailure` — no retry debt). `policyActionString` lowers through the typed tokens, deny fail-closed default. Rust enum remains the enforcement backstop, does not gate.
- #15955 hash leg reused, not re-fixed (coordination note in the issue).

## Validation

- Full `pkg/dataplane/userspace` run: only pre-existing failures, base-attributed on `974028945c` (lab socket-path length, WG degenerate-key and unit/vlan config gates, owner-key parity) — identical on clean `origin/master`.

Behavior preserved by construction (same dedup predicates, one hash per publish, ACK-then-retained-cache). The only new refusal is fail-closed at the Go send gate for hand-built/corrupt snapshots with invalid action tokens, matching the Rust #3365 refusal; no wire change. Perf: extraction removes duplicate hash/copy work, adds no marshal or lock hold (all helpers run under the existing `m.mu`).

## PR #16276 — config: add in-package per-channel test kit (#16139) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-22)

Branch: `fix/16139-config-test-kit`

Refs #16139

## Why
`pkg/config` had ~36 `must*` helpers; a scripted census (origin/master `9d098201cb`) found **73 pure hierarchical-parse clones** — single string arg, `*ConfigTree` return, only `NewParser(param).Parse()` + `len(errs)` guard + return — diverging in guard/message wording, plus per-file re-implementations of each compile channel. An external `configtest` package is rejected: 95%+ of this package's tests are in-package and cannot import it without a cycle.

## What
- New `pkg/config/helpers_test.go`: **one helper per compile channel, no bool lenient flag, no combined `MustCompile(opts...)`** (a lenient flag would let a test silently exercise the tolerant channel while claiming the strict one — `docs/engineering-style.md:50`):
  - `parseHierText` / `parseSetCommands` (parse-only, distinct instruments)
  - `compileHierStrict` / `compileHierLenient`, `compileSetStrict` / `compileSetLenient`, `compileTreeStrictKit` / `compileTreeLenientKit`, `compileTreeForNodeKit`
  - `configstore.CheckText` deliberately **not** wrapped (import cycle; tests needing the operator commit gate belong in `pkg/configstore` or `package config_test`) — naming a `CompileConfig` helper "check" would flatten that distinction.
- **Decl census / one clone family:** migrate all 73 pure clones — 554 in-file + 670 cross-file call sites (1224 total) — onto `parseHierText` and delete every clone. Helpers that wrap text, inject fixtures (e.g. `parseHier6454`), expand groups, panic instead of `Fatal`, or assert extra premises are **not** clones and stay untouched.
- Fix stale doc comments that named deleted helpers.
- New `pkg/config/helpers_equivalence_test.go`: permanent clone-equivalence pinned against **independent expected fixtures** (leaf key paths, Format round-trip, set-vs-hier Format equality, channels agree on a valid fixture) — a comparison against the deleted functions cannot compile, so none is attempted. `TestKitChannelsNotFlattened16139` pins a strict-vs-lenient divergence fixture (keyless cluster, #6611: strict rejects, lenient warns) proving **no channel flattening**.

## Validation
- `go vet ./pkg/config/` clean; `gofmt` clean on all changed files.
- `go test ./pkg/config/ -run TestKit` — all 5 equivalence tests pass.
- Spot-check `TestInactive_`/`TestDuplicatePolicyName`/`TestApplyGroupsExcept` passes.
- Full `pkg/config` suite exceeded the 300s local tool timeout without completing; **CI must confirm the full suite green** (acceptance check).

## Risk
Test-only change; no production code. Residual risk is a misclassified clone changing a test's parse channel — mitigated by the scripted purity census and the permanent independent-fixture equivalence tests.

`resolveNeighborsInner` (`pkg/daemon/daemon_neighbor.go`) re-issued `netlink.LinkByIndex` and a full `netlink.NeighList` dump **for every target**: `T` targets sharing one `(linkIndex, family)` — the normal case (many static-route next-hops / NAT addresses / `/32` address-book hosts behind one gateway) — re-dumped the identical neighbor table `T` times on every 15s pass, config apply, and HA takeover (issue H44-03, triple-validated, Low).

- **H41-02**: no `junos-host` deny path credited the global `policy_denied_packets` counter (`xpf_policy_denies_total` stayed 0 for every `to-zone junos-host` deny), and the deny RT_FLOW passed a default `NatDecision`, zeroing `nat_dst_ip`/`nat_dst_port` despite post-translation judging (#9529).

- `poll_descriptor/mod.rs`: capture the LocalMiss install result; on refusal count `note_admission_refused()`, recycle, `continue` (never Trusted). Sessionless-by-design LocalDelivery (non-SYN TCP, WG listener tuples) untouched. Stamp `fabric_ingress: packet_fabric_ingress` + #7096 `stamped_ingress_identity` on `local_metadata`.
- `host_inbound_policy.rs`: credit `counters.policy_denied_packets` once per deny/reject inside `junos_host_local_policy` (covers Stage-11, session-hit, session-miss; per-rule counter already credited by evaluation, not double-counted). `emit_junos_host_deny` takes the packet `NatDecision`.
- `flowless_verdict.rs`: flowless `junos-host` deny credits once; lo0 `Filtered` does not.
- Callers pass `decision.nat` (miss/hit), default for Stage-11/flowless (no translation).
- Tests: new `tests_host_inbound_15951.rs` (6 cells), flowless counter assertion, updated #10981 `nat_dst_*` assertion. `docs/log/15951.md`.

Scope notes: the enrichment's `nat_scope_ifindex`/`StaleDestinationNat` arm does not exist at this head (no such `SessionMetadata` field; #9563 declines LocalDelivery revalidation) — documented in `docs/log/15951.md`. H41-02 arm 3 (fabric ifindex in events) was NEEDS_VALIDATION and is unchanged. No `poll_descriptor/mod.rs` conflicts taken against open PRs beyond the confined call-site edits above.

## Validation

- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp 15951` — 6 passed (capacity-0 DNAT-to-local drop + `admission_refused == 1`, capacity control delivers+installs, miss/hit/reject `policy_denied_packets == 1`, DNAT deny event carries `nat_dst 10.0.61.1:8080` with wire tuple retained)
- `10981` — 3 passed; `9529` — 12 passed; `flowless` — 132 passed
- Full `--bin xpf-userspace-dp` suite: **7881 passed / 0 failed / 8 ignored**

## PR #16295 — eventengine: gate deferred replay on within match and fix sd-syslog NILVALUE envelope (#15945) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-22)

Branch: `impl-15945`

## Summary

Fixes both validated claims of #15945 (Refs-only):

- **H22-01 (High):** during the 30s cooldown, `evaluateEventMode` computed `withinMatches`, discarded it (`_ = matched`), and parked every event with `ThenCommands`; `drainDeferred` replayed it at cooldown expiry with no re-evaluation — so sub-threshold, over-ceiling, or already-latched events fired the remediation once without ever crossing.
- **H22-02 (Medium):** sd-syslog fallbacks emitted only two NILVALUE dashes (`RT_FLOW - - <body>`), placing the body in the RFC 5424 STRUCTURED-DATA slot where strict parsers misparse/drop it; `SCREEN_DROP`/`FILTER_LOG` had no structured handling.

## What

- `pkg/eventengine/evaluate.go`: `if !matched { continue }` before the defer branch — only a genuine crossing parks.
- `pkg/eventengine/engine.go`: `drainDeferred` re-evaluates `withinMatches` against the live policy/runtime, requires the parked semantic revision to still match, and only latches the authorizing generation. `staleReason` remains the commit-time backstop.
- `pkg/logging/format_rtflow.go`: third NILVALUE dash on both fallbacks (`RT_FLOW - - -`, `xpf - - -`); `FILTER_LOG` → `MSGID=FILTER_LOG` + NILVALUE SD + flat body as MSG (no Junos SD reference exists for filter logs — none invented); `SCREEN_DROP` → Junos screen SD arm cited from the Graylog Juniper SRX content pack (Junos OS 17.4+ sd-syslog: `RT_IDS - RT_SCREEN_TCP [junos@2636.1.1.1.2.40 attack-name=... ...]`), MSGID generalized to `RT_SCREEN_DROP` because Junos's per-category TCP/IP split cannot be derived from the wire record.
- Docs: `docs/config-schema.md` sd-syslog paragraph, `docs/log/15945.md`.

## PR #16298 — test: make session-sync idle baseline-relative (#16289) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16289-campaign`

Why: `ha_session_sync_idle_sample` required absolute `source sent == target received` for cumulative-since-daemon-start `Session create` counters. The daemons do not share a counter epoch (tcp-cluster evidence in #16289: sent=15, received=174, pending=0, static for the whole 30s window, later 74/233 — a constant offset of 159), so the pre-traffic session-sync precondition timed out forever on a fully caught-up pair, FAILed, and VOIDed every precondition-gated RG1 cell.

What:
- `test/incus/ha-assurance-lib.sh`: `ha_session_sync_idle_sample` now takes an explicit `(baseline_sent, baseline_received)` pair. Idle is `sent - baseline_sent == received - baseline_received` with `pending == 0`. The first sample of a wait only establishes the baseline (never idle by itself); a counter rewind since the baseline (daemon restart / epoch reset) is not idle and forces re-baselining instead of comparing across epochs; malformed or half-empty baselines are VOID (status 2). `drained` remains required/parseable, informational.
- `test/incus/test-failover.sh` (`ha_wait_for_session_sync_idle`) and `scripts/userspace-ha-failover-validation.sh` (`wait_for_session_sync_idle`): thread the baseline and re-baseline on every non-idle sample, so the existing 3-consecutive-idle rule proves "nothing sent since the baseline is unreceived" across consecutive samples.
- `test/incus/ha-assurance-selftest.sh`: offset-baseline fixtures (below).
- NOT changed: parsers, the 3-consecutive/30s policy, pending/drained requirements. A genuinely stuck sync (sends arriving unreceived, or pending nonzero) still never goes idle.

Validation:
- `bash test/incus/ha-assurance-selftest.sh` PASS, including new #16289 fixtures: static offset 15/174 pending=0 judged idle vs baseline; lockstep advance 74/233 idle; received stalled while sent grows not idle; pending=3 not idle; counter rewind not idle; malformed/half-empty baseline VOID; old 4-arg shape VOID.
- RED proof: reverting the helper to absolute equality fails the selftest on exactly the offset fixture (`expected 0, got 1 ... sent=15 ... received=174 ... pending=0`); restored and re-verified PASS.
- `bash -n` clean on all four scripts; shellcheck shows only pre-existing warnings.

Risk: live tcp-cluster `test-failover` precondition run not exercised in this lane (no destructive cluster); that remains the lab-verify item on #16289. Fail-closed intent preserved: unreceived sends or nonzero pending never reach idle.

Refs #16289
