## PR #16301 — screen: drop non-multiple-8 non-last fragments at any offset (#16030) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16030-teardrop-offset0`

Refs #16030

Why: `check_teardrop` gated both IPv4 and IPv6 arms on `frag_offset>0`, so a non-last first fragment (offset 0, MF/M=1) with a payload that is not a multiple of 8 (e.g. 4 or 12 bytes) was never dropped. RFC 791/RFC 8200 require every non-last fragment payload to be a multiple of 8; the tunnel reassembly path already enforces this (`gre_reassembly: info.more && payload.len()%8`). Conformance/screen-completeness gap (Low, A1-C9 from #15985).

What:
- Remove the `offset>0` gate in `check_teardrop` (`userspace-dp/src/screen/stateless.rs`) for both families; replace `payload < 8` with MF-gated `payload % 8 != 0`, which subsumes `<8` and also catches 12/20-byte non-last fragments at any offset. Zero/under-length payload arm (#3027) likewise runs at offset 0.
- Legal short LAST fragments (MF/M=0, 1-7 bytes, #9426) remain admitted because `%8` stays MF-gated; multiple-of-8 first fragments pass.
- Re-anchor two stale controls that asserted the bug: `teardrop_first_fragment_passes` (v4, 4B first frag) and `teardrop_v6_first_fragment_passes` now assert `Drop("teardrop")` and are renamed `*_illegal_payload_drops_16030`.
- `icmpv6_fragment_drops` fixture gets a legal `frag_data` so teardrop does not mask its icmp-fragment claim (teardrop precedes icmp-fragment in `check_fragment_and_route`).
- #14325 wording test now asserts teardrop fires on the pre-fix reconstructed shape while ping-of-death still does not.
- New #16030 sweeps: first-fragment 4/12/20B drops (v4+v6), non-first 12/20B drops, legal 8/16/24B first-fragment passes, short-last passes, zero-payload first-fragment drop.

Validation:
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp teardrop` — 26 passed (incl. new 16030 cells; fail-on-revert by construction: restoring the offset gate or reverting to `<8` reds them).
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp screen::` — 362 passed.
- `afxdp::` suite: 41 failures, spot-checked identical on unmodified `origin/master` (pre-existing: `pkt_len_fixture_drift_6883`, `arp_two_vlans_same_ip`, `keyed_shards_disperse` etc.) — not introduced by this change.

Risk: Low. Only newly dropped packets are non-last fragments with non-multiple-of-8 or zero payload — illegal per RFC, not producible by a conforming sender. Legal fragmented traffic (all non-last fragments 8-byte multiples, any-size last fragment) is unchanged. A middlebox emitting illegal fragments will now drop as `teardrop` where previously forwarded — intended screen behaviour, gated on `profile.teardrop`.

## PR #16302 — config: compiler/show parity fixes - interfaces, screens, backup-router, cluster resolution (#15944) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

## Why

#15944 bundles seven validated compiler/show parity claims (H4-01, H4-04, H13-03, H21-01, H21-02, H21-03, H23-02). This PR drives six claims fully; H4-04's userspace-MTU on-wire arm is explicitly parked (below), per the triage note.

### What changed, per claim

- **H4-01** — `pkg/config/compiler_interfaces.go`: inet owns only the legacy (IPv4) slots (first-wins), inet6 owns only the V6 slots and no longer mirrors into the legacy slots. `pkg/config/types_interfaces.go`: `Primary/PreferredAddressForFamily` family-check the legacy slot, so a v6 CIDR there never serves an IPv4 query. `pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface.go`: `planAddressReconcile` now also cycles a subnet's incumbent desired peer when the desired primary is not yet installed, so a fresh primary lands first instead of being appended as `IFA_F_SECONDARY`.
- **H4-04** — `pkg/dataplane/userspace/interfaces.go`: logical-only RETH unit MTU precedence is unit MTU → interface MTU → parent kernel MTU (was parent-only). `buildBridgeDomainModels` carries the IRB unit's MTU/primary/preferred/DHCP/DAD-disable; `buildFabricBondModels` carries the units' minimum MTU and per-family primary/preferred.
- **H13-03** — `pkg/config/compiler_security_screen_family_9421.go`: unbracketed packed family tails expand with open levels so siblings stay siblings (`tcp syn-flood alarm-threshold 100 attack-threshold 500;` compiles both thresholds, strict + lenient); bracketed tails keep the original chain walk and still strict-reject as the flat path does. Valueless `limit-session` direction observed and pinned: stays 0 with no BadNumeric (no Junos limit-session default asserted — inventing one would silently arm a session cap the operator never chose).
- **H21-01** — `pkg/config/compiler_system.go`: backup-router destinations accumulate across nodes (deduped, authored order; bare next-hop updates retain them; scalar stays in sync). `pkg/grpcapi/server_show_system.go`: renders every destination with a family-aware default (`::/0` for IPv6), matching the local CLI.
- **H21-02** — `cmd/cli/show_system.go`: remote license arm routes through the `license` ShowText RPC (shared `config.LicenseText`). Compiler arm probed at head (flat, packed-container, braced spellings) — already fixed, no compiler change, probe recorded in the commit.
- **H21-03** — `pkg/config/compiler_system.go`: NETCONF reader iterates every `netconf` sibling (`FindChildren`); parsed-text fixtures confirm sibling containers survive to the compiler, and the typed-flag warning fires off the corrected flag.
- **H23-02** — `resolveClusterInterfaceAddr` takes `cfg` and resolves via `cfg.ResolveKernelIfName` (daemon call sites pass the active/epoch config); `transportVRFBinding` resolves through the active config; the duplicate-identity watcher translates authored refs to the kernel device before lookup (`pkg/cluster`'s only config symbol is `config.LinuxIfName`, as in sibling files).

This PR touches different files in the same packages. H13-03 (screens) is in `compiler_security_screen_family_9421.go`, not `schema_security.go`. ## PR #16312 — userspace-dp: roll back cache probe on cached output drop (#15947) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/15947-single-claim-fast`

## Summary

Refs #15947 — single-claim residual only.

PR #15968 landed the validated arms of H26-02, H26-04, H27-03, H28-01,
H28-02, H29-01, H29-02, H29-04 arm 1, H30-01 and H30-03 arm 1. This PR
takes the one remaining single-claim residual, **H29-04 arm 2** as
narrowed by the research: on the flow-cache hit path the deferring probe
charged the session and locally completed the handshake *before* the
cached output-filter/policer verdicts, so a packet then dropped had
already been counted and had promoted the session — its HA Update was
merely withheld, never undone.

`SessionTable::rollback_dropped_probe_hit` now restores the exact
pre-probe `ProbeUndo` snapshots captured by `probe_hit_inner` for the
deferring arm, keyed by the producer's canonical stored key: accounting
target (including the reverse-only fallback), counters, observed
flags/ToS, both halves' handshake Booleans, and SYN-pressure index
membership; the withheld HA Update is discarded. Probe, emit and
rollback all resolve translated-alias packet identities to that
canonical key. A retransmitted completing ACK re-probes and, if
admitted, publishes exactly once.

Keepalive policy (fold 2): `last_seen_ns`/`expires_after_ns` are NOT
restored — the probe's throttled keepalive refresh stands on a dropped
packet, preserving the documented pre-fusion keepalive-before-drop
behaviour. A dropped packet proves liveness; it must not charge,
complete, or publish.

NOT touched (research NEEDS_VALIDATION, not single-claim): H29-01
NAT-leak/LocalDelivery arms, H26-02 arm 4 (clone perf), H29-02
diagnostics, H30-03 arm 2 (foreign host deny credit, vSRX semantics

## PR #16313 — userspace-dp: keep batched export window on last kicked command (#15950) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

`ExportOwnerRGSessions` commands co-resident in one worker drain had
their owner-RG sets unioned into a single export window.

That precondition is reachable: `apply_worker_commands` drains up to

window's queued command (S1) and its retry's command (S2) can both be
queued when the worker next drains. The coordinator BUSY gate cannot
prevent it — each kick was legitimate when made. Pre-fix, the handler
unioned both RG sets and both sequences; the adopted window exported

window's sequences, RG set, and kick epoch, discards pre-window
tombstones, and re-captures the kick epoch before recording its own —
matching the worker loop's existing single-window adopt
(`worker_export` overwritten with `purge_foreign`). Single-command
behaviour is byte-identical. The handler now returns whether it
superseded an earlier accept in the same drain.

Everything else in #15950 is already terminal: fixed by #15966
(H37-01, H37-02, H38-01 drain arm, H38-02, H38-03 arm 1, H38-04 parser
arm, H39-02 arm 1, H39-03 repairs arm — prewarm arm investigated and
confirmed NEEDS_VALIDATION, deliberately not folded untested —,

## PR #16317 — cluster: bound DHCP lease-chunk totalLeases before allocation (#16036) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16036-dhcp-totalleases`

## Summary

Refs #16036. `decodeDHCPLeaseChunkHeader` bounded the chunk count `total` to `[1, 1<<20]` but checked the lease count `totalLeases` only for `!= 0`, and `dhcpChunkState.addChunk` executed `make([]SyncLease, 0, totalLeases)` at assembly completion **before** the `len(complete) != totalLeases` refusal. One chunk header with `total=1, totalLeases=0xFFFFFFFF` requested ~4.29e9-record capacity (~672 GiB (721 GB decimal) virtual) before any check refused the set, and the assembly survived disconnect.

## Fix (fail-closed, all three legs from the issue's acceptance)

- `decodeDHCPLeaseChunkHeader`: `totalLeases` bounded to `[1, 1<<20]`, exactly like `total`. Out-of-bound headers are refused as malformed (counted via `MalformedRecordsDropped`, prior held set retained).
- `addChunk`: refuse `received > totalLeases` as soon as the accumulated count crosses the announced total, before any completion work; the generation is dropped.
- `addChunk` completion: size the concatenation by `a.received` (leases the parts have already proven) instead of the announced `totalLeases`, so no wire-controlled value ever sizes an allocation.

Wire format unchanged. A conforming sender never announces >1<<20 leases (chunked sets are bounded by the 64 MiB Kea read / 16 MiB frames), so no legitimate set is affected.

## Validation

New cells in `pkg/cluster/dhcp_chunk_totalleases_16036_test.go`:

- `TestDHCPChunkTotalLeasesBound16036` — exact fixture `0xFFFFFFFF` plus `0` and `(1<<20)+1` refused; boundary values `1` and `1<<20` admitted (positive control).
- `TestDHCPChunkForgedTotalLeasesNeverCommits16036` — the one-chunk forged frame driven through `handleMessage`: held set undisturbed, no pending assembly, counted malformed.
- `TestDHCPChunkReceivedOverTotalRefused16036` — two chunks carrying 2 leases against `totalLeases=1` (each header in-bound, so only the early refusal stops it): never commits, assembly dropped.
- `TestDHCPChunkCompletionAllocationBounded16036` — `TotalAlloc` measurement in the #8792 idiom at the admitted boundary `totalLeases=1<<20`: mutation-verified — reverting the guard allocated **176,161,392 bytes** vs the 1 MiB budget; with the fix ~nothing.

Full `pkg/cluster` suite passes (144s); existing #15160 chunk cells unchanged-green. Docs: `pkg/cluster/README.md` chunked-set bullet documents the bound.

Note on severity: per the issue, NV-1 (fatal under shipped GOMEMLIMIT/overcommit) remains the unrun host check and is **not** asserted here — the cells assert the host-independent invariant (refused before allocation, nothing commits), so the Low grade stands regardless.

## Risk

Fail-closed only: over-bound or over-total generations drop with the prior set retained (the existing #7175 posture). No sender, format, or commit-semantics change for conforming peers.

## PR #16318 — ipsec: render ascii 0x PSKs quoted, not raw hex (#15991) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix-15991-ascii-psk`

## Why

An `ascii-text` PSK spelled `0x61626364` lost its ASCII provenance in the
`pkg/ipsec` gateway-group secret fold (#15991, IKE-DEEP-2; stale-audit
continuation at 5fc385cc98): members became bare strings (hex values prefixed
with `0x`), and the lone-value emission treated any `0x`-prefixed string as a
hex key — rendering `secret = 0x61626364` unquoted, so strongSwan hex-decoded
the credential instead of using the literal ASCII string the operator
authored. The fold also collapsed an ASCII `0x<digits>` and a hexadecimal
`<digits>` member on one gateway into a single raw-hex element.

## What

- `pkg/ipsec/policy.go`: carry `pskValue{value, hex}` provenance through the
  fold and dedupe (replacing the bare-string / `"0x"+d` encoding), and make
  emission decide solely on the flag:
  - lone hex → `secret = 0x<hex>` (#15027 unchanged)
  - lone ASCII → quoted, including `0x`/`0X` values (`secret = "0x61626364"`)
  - grouped → comma-join each element by its provenance inside the existing
    single quoted string (byte-identical prior render; an ASCII `0x…` and a
    hex member with the same digits now survive as two distinct elements)
- New `pkg/ipsec/policy_psk_ascii_hex_15991_test.go`: lone ascii-0x vs hex
  control, policy-fallback ascii-0x, grouped ascii-0x+hex distinctness,
  grouped dedupe + plain member, non-hex `0xzzzz` quoted, and an end-to-end
  `ascii-text 0x61626364` compile→render cell mirroring #15027's hex leg.
- README + changelog + `docs/log/15991.md` updated; compiler/schema/gates
  unchanged (`PSKHex` already carried provenance to the renderer).

## Validation

- Probe at base `30638bcad3` (temporary test, removed): `PSK="0x61626364",
  PSKHex=false` rendered `secret = 0x61626364`, indistinguishable from the
  hex control — the reported defect.
- New tests GREEN with the fix, RED with `policy.go` stashed (4/5 direct
  cells + end-to-end; the grouped ascii-0x+plain cell is a control that
  passed pre-fix).
- Existing `TestPSKHexadecimal*15027` / `TestGatewayGroup*15024` unchanged
  GREEN; `go test ./pkg/ipsec/ -count=1` fully GREEN;
  `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestIPsecPSKHexadecimal15027'` GREEN;
  `go vet`/`gofmt` clean.

## Risk

Only lone ASCII values starting with `0x` change render (deliberately):
they now authenticate as the literal string and stop matching a peer that
had compensated by configuring the hex-decoded bytes. Hex, plain-ASCII,
grouped-plain, and malformed-hex skip renders are byte-identical. No
real-charon verification (no charon binary in this environment); the
swanctl render contract is pinned as in #15027.

## PR #16319 — nfqueue: verify reinject helper peer via SO_PEERCRED before any byte (#16052) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16052-reinject-peercred`

Why: `SocketReinjectSubmitter` dialed both helper unix sockets (submit and complete) with a bare `net.DialTimeout` and never checked `SO_PEERCRED`. A squatter listening on the socket path in a non-default (operator-selected, writable/sticky) socket dir received ANNOUNCE plus decrypted IPsec-inner payloads, and could return spoofed completions the client reported as success while every packet was dropped — blackhole with lying success (all completion paths are `VerdictDrop`, so no fail-open forwarding). Severity Medium: the default root-owned `/run/xpf` disallows squatting; the precondition is a non-default socket dir plus a local squatter. The #9171 census verified the Rust helper side, never the Go client's peer; #15950's server-side change does not fix this.

What:
- `dial` (the single choke point for both streams, `pkg/nfqueue/reinject_socket.go`) now verifies the peer via `SO_PEERCRED` immediately after connect, before any ANNOUNCE/payload/completion byte, closing and refusing the connection on failure.
- Only uid 0 or this process's own euid is accepted, mirroring `verifyUnixPeerIsPrivileged`/`peerCredTrustError` in `pkg/dataplane/userspace/socket_trust_9003.go` (#9003). In production both ends are root; the euid arm lets a non-root test binary drive the real path against a socket it binds itself.
- The decision (`reinjectPeerTrustError16052`) is split from the syscall shell (`readReinjectPeerCred16052`), which NEVER substitutes a zero `unix.Ucred` for a failed read — a zeroed credential has `Uid 0`, so swallowing the error would fail open. Refusals wrap the sentinel `errUntrustedReinjectPeer16052`.
- `peerVerify` / `reinjectGetsockoptUcred16052` seams let tests present a foreign credential on a real socket and force a credential-read failure (a non-root binary cannot manufacture a foreign-uid peer).
- `reinject_peercred_16052_test.go`: decision table, fail-closed shell cells, the decisive squatter regression, and a trusted-helper control. `docs/log/16052.md` records the change.

Validation:
- RED: the new test file alone fails to compile — `reinjectPeerTrustError16052`, `verifyReinjectPeer16052`, `errUntrustedReinjectPeer16052`, and `reinjectGetsockoptUcred16052` are undefined.
- Decisive regression: `TestReinjectSquatterSeesZeroBytes16052` stands up squatter listeners on both socket paths in a `/tmp`-style temp dir and drives ANNOUNCE, a decrypted-payload SUBMIT, and a completion drain through a client whose peer decision is foreign — every arm is refused with the sentinel, each squatter records exactly zero bytes on hangup, and no refused connection is retained.
- Mutant proof: deleting the verify call in `dial` (bare-dial mutant) turns exactly that squatter cell RED (announce accepted by the squatter) while the decision/read-failure cells stay GREEN.
- GREEN: `go test ./pkg/nfqueue/ -run 16052 -count=1 -v` 4/4 pass; dependent `-run 'Reinject|Announce'` suite passes; peercred cell passes under `-race`; `go vet ./pkg/nfqueue/` clean; `gofmt` clean on touched files. Pre-existing 9506/13234/14678 reinject suites exercise the same-uid path unchanged.

Risk: Verification runs once per lazy dial/reconnect, never per packet — no dataplane hot-path cost. Kernel-resolved `SO_PEERCRED` on the actual connection is race-free against path swapping, unlike path/mode checks. It authenticates uid only, matching the existing control/session/event socket posture (#9003/#9171); a root-compromised peer remains trusted. No live cluster mutated.

Refs #16052

## PR #16322 — dhcprelay: add per-sender fairness under aggregate rate limit (#16087) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16087-dhcp-relay-fairness`

## Why
#16087 (A10-17 fairness leg, split from #15988): the #5670 DHCP relay ingress limiter is one aggregate token bucket per interface, so a single sender sustaining >= `maximum-packet-rate` consumes every refill and legitimate DISCOVERs from other clients starve for the flood's duration. The eviction leg was refuted by all reviewers (pending capacity is rate-derived in `pending.go`) and is untouched. The Codex dissent is recorded honestly: chaddr/DUID are attacker-chosen, so per-sender fairness only stops a naive single-identity flooder — that limitation is documented in the README rather than hidden.

## What
- `fairLimiter` (relay.go) layered under the aggregate bucket on both relay paths (DHCPv4 chaddr key; DHCPv6 Client-ID DUID key, aggregate-only when no usable Client ID).
- Per sender: `ceil(rate/256)` pps sustained, burst floor 8 (a full DORA + retransmissions clears instantly); one identity can consume only ~1/256 of the aggregate.
- Aggregate bucket stays the pre-parse CPU/amplification bound; a fairness denial refunds its aggregate token so the flooder's drops cannot burn other senders' share.
- Table capped at 256 senders/interface, longest-idle (>=30s) recycling; identity rotation cannot evict established senders.
- Drops reuse `RequestsDroppedRateLimit` + warn-once log. No schema/counter/wire change.
- README documents the honest limit (multi-identity floods need switch DHCP-snooping/per-port controls); changelog + docs/log/16087.md.

## Validation
- Decisive check from the issue: `TestRunRelay_Fairness_SecondMACCompletesDORA` — 1-MAC flood (25 @ rate 5, frozen clock), second MAC's DISCOVER/REQUEST relayed and OFFER/ACK delivered. Plus `TestDHCPV6Fairness_SecondClientGetsShare` and `TestFairLimiter_*` (share, equal refill, bound, rotation, idle recycling).
- #5670 end-to-end tests updated to fairness-bound counts (single sender admits burst 8).
- Full `pkg/dhcprelay` suite passes except 3 pre-existing failures identical on clean origin/master (9406 x2, `TestInterfaceIPv4_Loopback` — env/fixture). Race run + `go vet` clean.
- RED-on-revert: removing either limiter layer raises single-sender admission in the 5670/fairness tests.

## Risk
A lone sender is capped at ~rate/256 sustained (1 pps at 100 pps default, burst 8) instead of the full aggregate — far above legitimate DHCP client behaviour; `maximum-packet-rate` raises every sender's share. Assignment verification was explicitly instructed, so tests were run in this worktree.

## PR #16324 — build: make cluster-deploy respects prebuilt deb (#16308) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16308-cluster-deploy-prebuilt-deb`

## Why

`make cluster-deploy` unconditionally rebuilt a stock deb via its `.PHONY deb` prerequisite, discarding a prebuilt high-version deb built with `make deb DEB_VERSION=99.0.x+…` (the #16219 downgrade-avoidance workflow). The rebuilt stock deb then won `cluster-setup.sh`'s `ls -t` selection and apt refused it as a downgrade (`Packages were downgraded and -y was used without --allow-downgrades`), so the documented entry point failed and the operator's `DEB_VERSION` bump was silently defeated. Agents worked around it by bypassing `make cluster-deploy` entirely.

Fixes #16308.

## What

- **Makefile**: replace the `deb` prerequisite of `cluster-deploy`, `loss-cluster-deploy`, and `cluster-deploy-and-gate` (`userspace-cluster-deploy` delegates to `cluster-deploy`) with an order-only `prepare-deb`:
  - explicit `DEB_VERSION` (command line/env, via `$(origin)`) → always build via `deb` (unchanged);
  - else a `dist-deb/xpf_*.deb` with filename version `>=` the stock version → **reused, no rebuild**, announced;
  - else (fresh tree / older-only) → build stock via `deb`.
  - Explicit `DEB_VERSION` is threaded to the scripts as `XPF_DEPLOY_DEB_VERSION` so the just-built deb deploys even beside a higher stale deb.
- **deploy-lib.sh**: new `deploy_deb_version` / `deploy_deb_newest` / `deploy_select_deb` — Debian version ordering via `dpkg --compare-versions`, never mtime; `XPF_DEPLOY_DEB_VERSION` / `XPF_DEPLOY_DEB_PATH` pins fail closed (die naming the pin).
- **cluster-setup.sh / test-rolling-upgrade.sh**: all `ls -t dist-deb` selections replaced with `deploy_select_deb`; deploy logs the selected deb + version.

## Validation (hermetic, no lab cluster)

- `bash test/incus/deploy-lib-selftest.sh` → **134 passed, 0 failed**, including 18 new #16308 cells: highest-version-beats-newest-mtime, empty-dir/stock-only, path+version pins (incl. missing-pin dies), and `make -n` decisions for reuse / fresh-build / older-only-rebuild / explicit-build + threading / `XPF_DEPLOY_FAST=1`.
- A real prebuilt `xpf_99.0.16308+601c5462a991.dirty_amd64.deb` (built via `make deb`, verified `dpkg-deb -f` → `99.0.16308+601c5462a991.dirty`) is reused by `make prepare-deb` with no rebuild; `deploy_select_deb` returns it.
- `shellcheck -S warning` clean on touched scripts; `git diff --check` clean.

## Risk

Selection is fail-closed on missing/unparseable pins; explicit-bump and FAST paths are unchanged; loss/tcp/udp env vars only threaded through. Live deploy acceptance remains lab-gated per the issue.

Refs #16219 (workflow preserved), #16290 (downstream manifest consequence).

## PR #16325 — configstore: preserve rollback history across active-rename crash window (#16064) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16064-rollback-meta-dual-binding`

Why: Config commit writes active.json first and publishes generation-bound rollback metadata only after rewriting every rollback slot. A power loss after the active rename but before that metadata publish left the sidecar binding the previous active identity, so boot tombstoned every generation-bound rollback slot even when all slot bytes still matched history. History was lost exactly when the just-committed config misbehaved.

What: Before WriteActive, plain and confirmed commits now durably publish a rollback preparation record (current committed entries plus next_active_hash and per-entry pending_hash with its own pending_timestamp/pending_comment). Boot certifies only that exact one-generation skew (including same-content commits) and admits matching slots at pre-shift positions (slot 1 = previous active hash, later slots = preceding committed entry, partially rewritten slots = prepared pending hash with pending attributes). A store recovered through the skew path re-arms preparation on every subsequent commit. Any other mismatch keeps the #10723 fail-closed tombstone behavior; completed commits clear the preparation fields. Adds fault-injection regression tests (real Commit path panicking at the slot writer after WriteActive, partial-rewrite gate test through the production loader, uncertified-rewrite guard, same-content certification, post-recovery re-arm). Updates docs/log/16064.md and debian/changelog.

Validation: go test ./pkg/configstore/ -run '16064' -count=1 green; neighboring -run '10723|10299|10825|10826|7176|3441|16064' green; full go test ./pkg/configstore/ -count=1 green (152.191s); go vet ./pkg/configstore/ clean; git diff --check clean.

Risk: Bounded to crash/skew recovery: relaxation is keyed to an exact recorded next-active hash and exact per-slot content hashes, so unrelated or corrupted history remains fail-closed. Successful commits pay one extra durable sidecar write before the active rename.

Refs #16064

## PR #16326 — dhcpserver: verify Kea lease-sync peer via SO_PEERCRED before any command (#16058) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16058-kea-peercred`

## Summary

Verify `SO_PEERCRED` on the Kea lease-sync control-socket dial (#16058), mirroring the reinject fix (#16052) and the helper-socket check (#9003).

## Why

The Kea lease-sync client dialed Kea's control socket by pathname (`defaultKeaDialer`: a bare unix dial) with no peer verification. A wrong/squatted server on that path was trusted as Kea: returned leases are sanitized, but sanitization cannot authenticate the wrong server, so fabricated lease data could be fed into HA lease sync — and lease-add/update commands would be delivered to the squatter on the seed path. The permissions arm of the claim is DUP A10-06 and out of scope; only the peer-verification arm is fixed here.

## What

- `pkg/dhcpserver/lease_sync.go`: `defaultKeaDialer` — the single production dial choke point for every Kea control-socket exchange (`lease{4,6}-get-all`, `lease{4,6}-add`/`-update`, `dhcp-disable`, display reads) — now verifies `SO_PEERCRED` immediately after connect, before any command byte is written, and closes/refuses on failure (`errUntrustedKeaPeer`). Trusted uids: the resolved Kea runtime user (`_kea`/`kea` via the #2450 lookup), root, or this daemon's own euid. The decision (`keaPeerTrustErrorAs`) is split from the syscall shell (`readKeaPeerUID`, `keaGetsockoptUcred` seam); a failed credential read never substitutes a zero Ucred (Uid 0 = root = trusted — the #9003 fail-open).
- `waitControlSocket` re-verifies when a custom dialer is in use, so a connectable squatter is never reported Kea-ready to the post-start seed.
- `pkg/dhcpserver/README.md` + `docs/log/16058.md` + `debian/changelog` updated.
- NOT changed: the `keaSocketDialer` test-seam contract (custom dialers are test doubles; `net.Pipe` cannot present credentials), the memfile fallback, sanitization, and all callers.

## Validation

- New `lease_sync_peercred_16058_test.go`: decision table (Kea/daemon/root admitted, foreign refused), no-Kea-user collapse, kernel-read positive control, fail-closed shell (non-AF_UNIX + forced `SO_PEERCRED` failure), readiness refusal.
- Decisive regression `TestSquatterRefusedAndSyncsZeroLeases16058`: squatter offering a fabricated lease, peer judged foreign via the `keaPeerVerify` seam for any test-binary uid, syncs 0 leases from it into an isolated memfile fixture (exactly its known 10.0.61.70 row returned) with 0 squatter commands recorded. Bare-dial mutant (removing the verify call) fails wanting exactly that fixture lease instead of the fabricated 10.0.61.99 row; restored GREEN.
- `go test ./pkg/dhcpserver/ -count=1`: only `TestKeaSubnetIDStableAcrossSpellingChange` fails — base-attributed (fails identically on unmodified `30638bcad3`). `pkg/cluster`, `pkg/daemon` lease-sync suites pass. `go vet`/`gofmt` clean.

## Risk

Verification runs on every dial, and the seed path dials once per command (`keaControl` per `lease-add`, plus one for a conflict `lease-update`), so verification IS per command there — one `getsockopt` per seeded lease on the async takeover seed, never per packet. A refused peer degrades to the existing memfile fallback / fail-open seed exactly as a down socket does, so serving cannot wedge. A root- or `_kea`-compromised peer is still trusted (uid is the authentication granularity), matching #9003/#16052. No live cluster was mutated.

Refs #16058

## PR #16332 — config: key session interface identity by unit device (#16065) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16065-ifindex-unit-name`

Refs #16065

## Why
Session display, clear-by-interface and flow-export keyed every unit on `{parent ifindex, VID = vlan-id else unit number}`:
- VLAN units were keyed by the parent netdev instead of their child device;
- two WireGuard units sharing one TUN (wg0.0/wg0.1, both VID 0) collided on one name, so `clear ... interface wg0.1` could delete wg0.0 sessions;
- daemon `buildIfNames` kept sorted first-wins, so flow-export sampling judged both units by the surviving sibling's name.

## What
- One shared derivation `config.SessionIfaceNames` (`pkg/config/session_iface_key_16065.go`): each unit resolves via `ResolveKernelIfName("<iface>.<unit>")` — its OWN kernel device (VLAN child, per-unit tunnel `gr-…u1`, shared WG TUN, RETH member) — with VID = wire `unit.VlanID` only, never the unit number.
- A key claimed by two DIFFERENT unit names is refused (omitted): consumers fall back to the zone arm / zone display / nameless flow-export semantics, never a sibling's name. Same-name claims (unit-0 collapse, RETH/member) keep the name.

## PR #16335 — ddns: add require-tsig opt-in and live unsigned-posture gauge (#15992) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/15992-require-tsig`

## Why

RFC2136 DDNS without TSIG trusted a forgeable rcode: a forged NOERROR recorded durable ownership of an unwritten name in state that survives restart, and a forged REFUSED/YXDOMAIN suppressed legitimate publishes — with only a once-per-process runtime warning. The posture needed to be continuously visible and optionally fail-closed, without breaking legitimate source-IP-ACL unsigned BIND (the default).

## What

- `require-tsig` valueless leaf on both DDNS surfaces (DHCP `dynamic-dns` and Surface A `system services dynamic-dns provider`): strict commit refuses `require-tsig` + non-loopback `update-server` + no `tsig-key` (DHCP: including a disabled family, which still withdraws persisted records at runtime — the backend refuses those unsigned withdrawals too, so supply a key for signed cleanup or remove `require-tsig`); tolerant load/peer-sync downgrades to a warning (no-brick).
- Runtime backstop in the RFC2136 backend: a `require-tsig` config that arrives without a key refuses the non-loopback UPDATE before sending, so no durable ownership is recorded on a forgeable verdict (the backend's `exchange` only carries RFC 2136 UPDATEs; SOA zone discovery is a separate query path). Loopback servers are exempt, matching the commit gate.
- Live gauges `xpf_dhcp_ddns_unsigned_nonloopback_active` / `xpf_ddns_surface_a_unsigned_nonloopback_active` stay at 1 for as long as the forgeable-rcode posture persists — including owned records still pending cleanup at an unsigned non-loopback endpoint after disable/removal, an in-progress cleanup pass (in-flight hold), a keyed-endpoint transition whose old records withdraw via the previous unsigned updater, and the post-restart window before the first reconcile (seeded at construction from persisted ownership + the boot config's cleanup endpoint) — refreshed every reconcile (not once per process).
- Spelling-gate registry: the three `require-tsig` rows registered as `flag (read, but value-less)`; flag ceiling 197 -> 200 with the reason recorded.

## Validation

- `pkg/config`: require-tsig strict-reject (both surfaces, plus disabled DHCP families), tolerant-warn, loopback/keyed/default controls pass; the runtime DELETE refusal is pinned alongside the publish refusal.
- `pkg/ddns`: full suite passes, including reconcile-driven gauge tests (`ReconcileScoped`/`Reconcile` -> `Stats`), cleanup-after-disable tests, an in-flight hold test (scrape while a cleanup UPDATE is blocked mid-pass), a keyed-transition test (old records withdraw via the previous unsigned updater), and a fresh-manager restart regression (persisted ownership + disabled unsigned endpoint reports 1 before any reconcile, keyed/loopback/record-free controls 0); mutation checks prove the loopback exemption, gauge wiring, in-flight hold, and previous-updater capture are load-bearing.
- `pkg/api`: gauge test passes through real manager reconcile -> `Stats` -> collector.
- Base-vs-worktree spelling-gate comparison on base `eea94248f5`: the members registry, coverage ratchet, and differential gate already drift on the pristine base (140 arrived / 6 departed / 8 reclassified leaves, none of them `require-tsig`); this change adds only its 3 rows and does not alter that pre-existing drift. Same for `pkg/api` `TestRESTRecycledIfindexIsNotReportedAsFact6960`, red on base and unchanged here.

## Risk

Default posture unchanged: unsigned source-IP-ACL publishing keeps working without `require-tsig`. The new gate is opt-in; loopback servers remain exempt on both the commit gate and the runtime backstop. The gauge may stay 1 while cleanup is genuinely pending at an unsigned non-loopback endpoint (including kept orphan ownership) — that is the intended alarm.

Refs #15992

## PR #16338 — harness: name refused deploy in attestation VOID reason (#16290) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16290-manifest-attestation`

Refs #16290

## Why

`cluster-setup.sh deploy` invalidates the executable-attestation manifest *before* deploying, but only writes the new manifest *after* the deploy body succeeds. When the rolling cut refuses (e.g. `xpfd upgrade --rolling` rejects replacing the live version dir because the same version tag was re-staged with different bytes — `refuse-before-PREFLIGHT`), `set -e` aborts before `deploy_write_manifest` runs, leaving **no** `dist-deb/xpf-deploy-manifest.json` at all. Every subsequent cluster gate then records VOID (`exe_check=UNAVAILABLE`, build under test unattributable) with no hint that a refused deploy is the cause — one refused re-stage silently poisons attestation for all later gates until the next fully successful deploy.

## What

Implements suggested fix (2) from the issue (explicit marker naming the refused deploy), preserving fail-closed semantics:

- **`test/incus/deploy-lib.sh`** — a `.failed` sidecar marker next to the manifest (`deploy_manifest_record_failure` / `deploy_manifest_failure_reason` / `deploy_manifest_clear_failure`) naming the deploy target, failed step, and reason. It carries no binary identity and `deploy_manifest_sha` never reads it. `deploy_manifest_invalidate` clears a stale marker; a successful `deploy_write_manifest` clears it.
- **`test/incus/cluster-setup.sh` `cmd_deploy`** — an EXIT-trap guard armed immediately after invalidation (guard state in globals, not locals, so the trap survives function return under `set -u`; `$?` captured as the trap's first action). Any `set -e` abort or `die` between invalidation and the manifest write records the marker with the failed step; the explicit `die` paths record their specific reason and disarm so the trap cannot overwrite it. On success the flag is cleared and the trap removed, so successful deploy paths behave exactly as before.
- **`test/incus/harness-result.sh`** — when `exe_check` (or the helper leg) is `UNAVAILABLE`, the VOID reason gains `; attestation unavailable because deploy <target> failed: <reason>`. Verdict and `exe_check` are unchanged (still VOID/UNAVAILABLE).

Fail-closed is preserved throughout: a deploy that cut some nodes leaves the marker, not a manifest claiming the old build; completed nodes re-attest only when the whole deploy succeeds.

## Validation

- `test/incus/deploy-lib-selftest.sh`: **147 passed, 0 failed**, including the hermetic invalidate→refused-cut→manifest-state sequence (deploy-A control; all-node refusal leaves no manifest, a marker naming the refusal, and no attestation; single-node refusal preserves the peer slot and names deploy 1; recovery deploy clears the marker; invalidation supersedes a stale marker; a reason-less marker fails closed) and the rewired `cmd_deploy` ordering check (invalidate → trap armed → deploy → write → disarm → rebaseline).
- `test/incus/harness-result-selftest.sh`: **260 passed, 1 failed** — the single failure (`#12140` cluster gate census) pre-exists on the base commit and is unrelated. The new case asserts a refused deploy VOIDs with a `void_reason` naming the refused deploy, not a bare `exe_check=UNAVAILABLE`.
- Mutation check: making `deploy_manifest_record_failure` a no-op turns the #16290 sequence checks RED.
- `bash -n` and `shellcheck -S warning` clean on all touched scripts.
- Not run: a live refused re-stage on the loss/tcp/udp clusters (no cluster available to this change). The acceptance sequence is covered hermetically with the real lib calls in `cmd_deploy`'s exact order.

## Risk

Low and harness-only. The marker is additive operator/ledger metadata: it never attests binaries, never revives stale provenance, and is cleared by the next invalidation or successful write. The EXIT trap exists only between invalidation and a successful manifest write.

## PR #16339 — vrrp: drop unknown-source priority-0/255 adverts once master learned (#16018) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16018-vrrp-unknown-source-z2b`

Refs #16018

## Why
xpf learned the legitimate master source per family (#10719) but only logged priority-0/255 adverts from other sources before applying them — a forged priority-0 armed the ~1ms backup takeover and a forged priority-255 demoted the master, even after the genuine master was learned and fresh. Separately (A7-03), native VRRP is consumed via AF_PACKET before netfilter input, so a zone host-inbound denial of `vrrp` never gated it and no commit-time signal said so.

## What
- `pkg/vrrp/instance_rx.go`: folds the #10719 counter/warning into `unknownSourceAdvert`, which also returns the drop decision. While the learned record is fresh (`observedMasterStaleLocked`), `handleBackupRx`/`handleMasterRx` return before any timer/state/record effect for a mismatched priority-0/255 source. Cold start, stale record, and the learned source itself keep RFC behaviour (genuine priority-0 still takes over in ~1ms); ordinary priorities 1–254 are ungated. Warning gains a `dropped` attribute.
- `pkg/config`: `validateHostInboundVRRPBypassWarnings`, WARN-only on every path (wired in `runTailGates`), names the AF_PACKET bypass per zoned interface carrying an explicit vrrp-group or active RETH-derived instance whose effective host-inbound protocols omit `vrrp`. Admitted/`all`/lifeline/no-VRRP stay silent; strict commit still succeeds.
- README trust-boundary section updated; the #10719 demotion cell now expects no demotion (known-source 255 demotion remains covered by its control test).

## Validation
- `go test ./pkg/vrrp/ -run '16018|10719'` — 12 tests PASS (incl. new backup-255, IPv6, cold-start, stale-master, genuine-resign cells).
- `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'VRRPBypass|HostInboundManagedRouting|TestHostInbound'` — PASS.
- Fail-on-revert: disabling the gate call reddens the 16018/10719 cells; removing the tailgate append reddens `TestVRRPBypassCompileWarnOnly16018`.
- Full `pkg/vrrp` run: only pre-existing base failure `TestRethOwnershipCollectorsUseTheSharedPredicate` (verified identical on clean base); same for `TestVRRPCrossGroupDifferentInterfacesCommits` in `pkg/config`.

## Risk
A genuine master that changes source IP while still fresh has its 0/255 adverts dropped until the learned record goes stale (one master-down horizon), after which elections resume. Spoofing the learned source itself remains the VRRPv3 protocol floor. The commit warning is advisory only and never rejects.

## PR #16341 — userspace-dp: verify snapshot interface/zone summary counts (#16056) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16056-snapshot-counts-z3b`

Refs #16056

## Why
The Rust snapshot apply handler checked `policy_count` against the built policies but never compared `summary.interface_count`/`zone_count` against the built `interfaces`/`zones` sections. A producer shape with `interface_count>0` but `interfaces=[]` passed all gates, built forwarding with zero bindings, unbound all workers, ACKed ok and persisted as baseline; `zones=[]` in a global-only config had the same joint-omission shape (zone-pair policies already fail preflight closed, so the surviving arm is availability-only, Low). Go also set the summary counts from the authored config maps before `quarantineCollidingZones`, so a naive Rust equality check would refuse legitimate quarantined snapshots.

## What
- Rust `apply` (after version + policy-count gates, before monotonicity/preflight/mutation): refuse `interface_count != len(interfaces) || zone_count != len(zones)`, and refuse an empty interfaces/zones install over a non-empty installed set even when both transmitted fields are zeroed (no full-clear signal exists for these sections, unlike policies' `clear_policies`). Refusals keep prior forwarding/snapshot, do not advance the reported generation, and count on `snapshot_policy_mismatch_total`.
- Go: full builder derives `InterfaceCount=len(built interfaces)`, `ZoneCount=len(built zones)` and reconciles all summary counts post-quarantine unconditionally; link-refresh and apply-time rebuild do the same; `prepareSnapshotForApply` re-syncs `InterfaceCount` after revalidation drops (incl. the config-less early-return path); `validateSnapshotForSend` refuses a section mismatch known-unsent (`errSnapshotPolicyMismatch`).
- Protocol v67 -> v68 both sides (Go `ProtocolVersion`, Rust `CONFIG_SNAPSHOT_PROTOCOL_VERSION`, shape/secure-tunnel pins; shape golden refreshed to the measured master digest `cf98a6a5` which already differed on clean `origin/master`).
- Existing Rust fixtures carrying zones/interfaces without summary counts now declare them; `TestSyncRetryRemarksUnlandedClear` keeps its interfaces through the clear retry (only policies legitimately empty).

## Validation
- `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run '16056|TestBuildSnapshotSummary|TestFullBuilderPopulatesEverySnapshotField|TestSnapshotShape|TestSnapshotProtocolVersion|TestSyncRetryRemarksUnlandedClear|TestValidateSnapshotForSend|TestCompileClearAll|TestBuilderInvariant'` — PASS, including new `TestBuildSnapshotSummaryCountsBuiltSections16056` (FAIL-ON-REVERT vs authored-map counts), `TestBuildSnapshotQuarantinedZoneCountReconciled16056` (z174/z214 collision), `TestValidateSnapshotForSendRefusesSectionMismatch16056`.
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- apply_snapshot_` — 35 passed; 1 failure `apply_snapshot_wires_day2_preserved_mtu_reconcile` fails identically on clean `origin/master` (pre-existing, unrelated D11/D14 join).
- Full Go package run: only pre-existing master failures (secure-tunnel PSK fixtures, SNAT parity liveness, retry-debt hash, GOTMPDIR socket-path artifacts), verified against clean master where applicable.

## Risk
A partial publish that empties all interfaces/zones is now refused at the helper; a genuine empty config still applies as a first install and full Compile builds re-derive counts from built sections. Mixed-version pairs refuse on the exact-equality gate until both sides reach v68. Decisive regression shape from the issue (over an installed snapshot, `zone_count=2/zones=[]` global-only and `interface_count=2/interfaces=[]`) is covered by `apply_snapshot_section_count_mismatch_is_refused_and_counted_16056` + the both-zeroed arm test, asserting prior bindings/snapshot intact.

## PR #16350 — nat: key PAT port allocation per RFC 6056 (#16011) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16011-rfc6056-pat`

Why: fresh PAT ports were handed out in ascending order from a shared monotonic cursor (pool claim), a shared round-robin counter (interface PAT walk and try_next_port), so an observer of one translated port — e.g. a colluding server that sees the remote tuple — could predict the next port, multiplying tuple-guessing attacks.

What:
- Pool PAT claims start at a keyed splitmix hash of the full flow tuple under a per-boot secret drawn once from the audited OS CSPRNG (`hot_hash_seed::os_random_seed_u64`, never zero), then probe forward over at most `range` distinct offsets, then fall through to the existing FIFO recycle ring. Monotonic cursor + its debug seam removed.
- Interface PAT walk and stateless `try_next_port` use the same keyed start (flow-keyed variant at the synthetic call sites).
- Deterministic CGNAT block allocation deliberately keeps its documented lowest-free-in-block contract (subscriber-derived reproducibility); recycle ring remains FIFO-queued, with a test-only recycled-phase seam for the #9327/#9392/#7174 cost fixtures.
- Tests that pinned sequential values adapted to keyed order (in-range/set/distinctness); new `tests_16011` pins secret-dependence, non-sequential spread, bounded next-port prediction (~random over 2000 trials), fail-closed exhaustion, sole-free-port probe, and concurrent uniqueness. Changelog entry added.

Validation: `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp nat::` — 736 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored (includes 5 new tests_16011 tests). Fail-on-revert: restoring sequential allocation makes `pat_fresh_ports_are_not_sequential_16011` and `pat_next_port_prediction_advantage_is_bounded_16011` fail.

Risk: new-flow translated ports change distribution (by design); persistent/deterministic/synced reservations and release paths untouched, so live sessions and HA imports keep exact tuples. Per-boot secret is node-local, never synced — synced sessions carry explicit tuples, so failover need not reproduce a peer's fresh-port choice. Probe worst case is O(range) bitmap CAS like the prior cursor probe, with an exact `occupied == range` fail-closed gate.

Refs #16011

## PR #16352 — nat: charge persistent leases per source (#16013) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16013-nat-per-source-fairness`

## Why
The pool allocator capped persistent leases only pool-globally (`max_tracked_flows`), while the per-source session quota is per (zone, src) per worker and never charged idle leases. One host churning source ports accumulated idle persistent leases (300s–24h retention) after its flows closed, retaining the whole lease table — and, on a single-address pool, its ports — while other sources were refused (#16013, A2-C2).

## What
- Count leases per `(src_ip, routing_scope)` at the single insert/remove seam for `persistent_by_source`, so every mint, import, carry and removal stays in step with no second counting convention.
- Refuse a NEW lease key at 4096 (mirrors the session-layer per-source default `DEFAULT_MAX_SESSIONS_PER_SOURCE`) after a bounded pressure-GC pass, on: local PAT, local address-only, HA-synced PAT, HA-synced address-only, idle-lease import, deterministic NAT64 BIB.
- Joining an existing lease is never refused by this gate; expiry/clear/GC/reseed release the charge through the same seam. Idle-lease per-source refusal reports through the existing `SkippedCapacity` outcome/counter.

## Validation
- New `nat::tests_persistent_per_source_16013` (6 tests): decisive churn cell (cap-many *closed* flows from one host → next new lease refused, second source still allocates), rejoin-not-charged, routing-scope separation, expiry releases charge, address-only charging, idle-import charging.
- Full `nat::` suite: 737 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo check --release --tests` clean.

## Risk
A single legitimate source needing >4096 distinct persistent leases (distinct source ports/protocols/scopes) in one pool is refused new leases until idle leases expire — the intended fairness bound, matching the existing per-source session ceiling. Spoofed-source churn on SAV-less LANs stays bounded by zone/session quotas (S2-01), not this allocator charge.

Closes #16013

## PR #16353 — userspace-dp: fail closed on tiny first-fragment unknown TCP flags (#16007) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16007-tiny-frag-flags`

Refs #16007

## Why
An 8-byte first fragment (declared L4 < 14 bytes) stamps `tcp_flags=0` in the shim (`first_fragment_l4`), so `syn-frag` cannot fire, SYN-flood/cookie logic keys on absent flags, and session admission reads the zero as a proven non-SYN — admitted under `no-syn-check` and exempt on LocalDelivery. The reassembled SYN arrives only in the offset-1 second fragment. Validated Medium (A1-C1 from #15985): default-config transit dies at the strict SYN check, but as `strict-syn-check`, not `syn-frag`, and the `no-syn-check` / LocalDelivery arms misclassify outright.

## What
Encode flags-UNKNOWN end to end and fail closed on it:
- **Shim** (`userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs`): `UserspaceDpMeta.tcp_flags_unknown` reuses the former `reserved` byte (96B ABI unchanged), folded out of `is_fragment && protocol==TCP && payload_offset==l4_offset` in the outlined meta store — the exact shape `first_fragment_l4` returns for declared L4 <14 — so no new `ParsedPacket` state for the verifier to carry.
- **Worker re-derivation** (`frame/inspect.rs`, `icmp.rs`): `frame_l4_flags_unknown` (verified L3 + IP-declared end + first-fragment walk) so slow-path/injected/replayed frames that never crossed the shim are covered; `meta_l4_flags_unknown` is the single consumer predicate (shim bit OR frame derivation).
- **Screen**: extractor fails closed with `TinyFirstFragmentFlagsUnknown` → reason `"syn-frag"` (per-reason index 13, existing `SCREEN_SYN_FRAG` counter) when a TCP first fragment's declared end (total_len/payload_len, never capture length) stops before L4+14; `check_tcp_flag_screens` drops unknown-flags first fragments as `syn-frag` defense-in-depth (never the false `tcp-no-flag` on tf==0).
- **Admission**: `strict_syn_check_drops_new_flow[_tunnel]` drop on unknown in every mode, including `no-syn-check` and the tunnel opt-out (a stamped SYN is not proven either).
- **LocalDelivery**: the poll-descriptor gate covers LocalDelivery only when flags are unknown — proven non-SYN LocalDelivery still reaches the local stack (peer RST/FIN for firewall-originated flows) — and LocalDelivery session caching declines on unknown (no helper-local session seeded off unseen flags).

Decisive regression (issue check): 8B first fragment + offset-1 second fragment drops in (a) default — `screen/tests_16007_tiny_frag.rs` (v4+v6) and live `stage_screen_check` drop with the legal second fragment passing as control; (b) `no-syn-check` — admission mode sweep; (c) LocalDelivery — unknown-only gate + cache-decline test.

## Validation
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 16007`: 7 passed.
- `screen::` suite: 368 passed, 1 failed — `screen::tests::extract_info_from_ipv4_frame` is a pre-existing header-only fixture (34-byte frame, total_len=20, MF set, no L4 bytes) whose shape is itself this issue's unknown-flags case; it now correctly fails closed. Left untouched rather than silently rewritten; happy to update it in a follow-up if preferred.
- `afxdp::` suite: 5928 passed / 42 failed; failure set byte-identical to the pristine-baseline run (same 42), plus one flaky `icmp_ratelimit` test that passes in isolation twice.
- Shim: candidate builds with the pinned toolchain, but this guest kernel rejects even a pristine-source rebuild at the 1M verifier cap (tracked .o measures 856646 insns / 14.34% = LOW-HEADROOM), so the tracked `userspace_xdp_bpfel.o` is NOT regenerated here. The worker-side frame re-derivation makes the fix effective without the new shim bit; the bit takes effect with the next successful shim rebuild.

## Risk
Legitimate TCP connections fragmented so the flags byte lands in the second fragment now drop as `syn-frag` instead of forwarding — the fail-closed posture the issue requires (indistinguishable from the attack shape). Proven-flags traffic, non-first fragments, and non-TCP fragments are unchanged. No ABI size change; no allocation on the hot path.

## PR #16354 — sessions: shed unreplied flows protocol-symmetrically under pressure (#16019) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16019`

Closes #16019.

## Why
Per-source session limits key on the claimed (spoofable) source, and pressure shedding only relieved a TCP initial-SYN newcomer by evicting handshake-incomplete TCP. Rotating spoofed-source UDP/ICMP singles each minted fresh quota and filled the session table; a legitimate second zone/host's new flows were starved with no relief path (S2-01 from #15985).

## What
- `can_admit_new_syn` → `can_admit_new_flow`: trigger is protocol-symmetric (TCP keeps its initial-SYN-only gate; non-TCP first packets qualify), same 90% watermark and hard cap.
- Victim predicate/index generalized from TCP openings (`pressure_shed_openings`) to never-replied local sessions (`pressure_shed_unreplied`): TCP handshake-incomplete, or non-TCP with zero reverse packets accounted (`SessionCounters::replied()` — the exact signal, immune to the `established` seeding divergence between app-timeout and no-app-timeout installs). Closing, peer-synced, transient-seed, fabric-ingress and reverse-companion entries are never victims.
- `update_session` maintains the index for all protocols; the shared-map shed fence (`is_pressure_shed_shared_unreplied`) accepts non-TCP victims (handshake state 0 by construction; incarnation still fenced by session_id/decision/metadata).
- Docs: session README admission section + changelog.

## Validation
- New `unreplied_pressure_16019_tests` (5 tests): rotating spoofed UDP fill cannot starve a second host; mixed ICMP/UDP fill with TCP-SYN and ICMP cross-protocol relief; replied UDP flow never shed; no-app-timeout UDP still sheddable; TCP non-SYN hard cap preserved. All pass.
- `session::` suite: 504 passed; only 2 failures, both verified identical on unmodified master (`session_decision_typed_snat_layout_11064`, `in_window_rst_valid_blind_rst_invalid_15753`) — pre-existing.
- `afxdp::tests_txn_flow_cache`: 56 passed (shared shed fence pins incl. non-TCP incarnation cases).

## Risk
At the 90% watermark, legitimate new-flow bursts can shed unreplied UDP/ICMP singles ahead of their idle timeout — intended (no reply seen; they reap soon anyway). Replied/established flows are never shed. Closing TCP flows are newly excluded from victims (strictly safer; they reap within seconds).

## PR #16355 — nat: revoke stored any-remote grants on permit tightening (#16017) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16017-persistent-nat-permit-revoke`

## Why (#16017, A2-C13)

`permits()` reads stored scopes; `SourceNatPoolAllocatorKey` = pool name + addresses + port range only, so `resolve_pool_allocators` reuses the previous allocator on a permit-only rebuild — leases + permissions carry across. Only revocation (`clear_persistent_leases`) fires from explicit coordinator clear, never on permit change; inbound hold disarms idle expiry while held. Mint an any-remote lease, rebuild same pool + tightened permit, probe `persistent_inbound_lookup_for_rule` from a non-target remote — **today: Permitted**.

## What

- Each bucket's `any_remote` grant records the **authorizing rule's permit epoch**: an allocator generation counter bumped on every allocator reuse in `resolve_pool_allocators` and shared by rules naming the pool. The epoch is threaded explicitly through `allocate_translation*`, `reserve_address_only_persistent*`, and `record_synced_persistent_permission_with_zones` to all mint/record sites; NAT64 BIBs pass 0 (no authorizing source-NAT rule).
- Permit-change sync **demotes every covered bucket** (`authorized_epoch := 0`) before any preserving `AnyRemoteHost` rule restamps it with the new epoch — stored grants, including imported grants, are revoked on tightening.
- **Stale-generation writers are fenced**: a writer whose epoch is older than a bucket's authorized epoch cannot restore `any_remote` (`record_with_zones` demotes the write); `permits()` honors only current-epoch authorization.
- **HA imports are demoted unless locally authorized**: generation validation proves record provenance, not local permit consent. Import APIs carry `permit_any_authorized` computed by the coordinator from live rules sharing the record's allocator/scope; `import_idle_lease_at_after_generation` defaults demoted, with `..._permit_any` as the authorized spelling (also used for NAT64 deterministic BIBs). Demoted imports still install and merge exact remotes; a later preserving sync restamps the wildcard.
- Exact target-host/target-host-port `remotes` stay permitted under every tighter mode.

Refs #9428: allocator key unchanged (permit is not pool-scoped; adding it would split one pool into two allocators and reintroduce duplicate `(addr,port)` mints).

## Test report

- **New** `nat::tests_persistent_permit_16017` (6 tests):
  - `persistent_permit_tightening_revokes_any_remote_grant_16017` — decisive check from the issue (tighten to `target-host-port`, non-target must be `Denied`).
  - `persistent_permit_tightening_to_target_host_revokes_any_remote_16017` — same for `target-host`.
  - `persistent_permit_unchanged_preserves_any_remote_grant_16017` — unchanged-permit preservation control.
  - `imported_any_remote_grant_is_revoked_on_tightening_16017` — imported grant revoked when the reusing generation tightens.
  - `stale_generation_writer_cannot_reauthorize_after_sync_16017` — old writer replays captured epoch after sync; inbound stays `Denied`.
  - `validated_import_after_tightening_stays_demoted_16017` — generation-validated wildcard import lands after tightening; lease installs, non-target stays `Denied`.
- **Existing**: full `nat::` suite **751 passed**; `idle_lease` filter **85 passed**; coordinator idle-lease tests **11 passed**.

## Risk

Fail-closed only: tightened/stale/unauthorized grants lose the wildcard until a current-epoch mint, preserving sync, or locally-authorized import re-grants. Exact remotes and lease installation unaffected; uncovered scopes untouched (#14322 preserved).

## PR #16358 — ha: anchor fabric rollout grace at persisted first keying (#16027) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16027-tokenless-grace`

Why:
The #11676 fabric rollout grace was anchored at the in-memory
no-key -> key transition in Manager.UpdateConfig. Every xpfd process
start satisfies that transition, so every restart of a long-keyed
node re-opened up to 5 minutes of tokenless read-only fabric RPCs
(GetSessions, interface monitor, safe ShowText) until the peer
authenticated — recurring read-only disclosure to on-segment hosts
with no operator action (A5-14, #16027). Key-touching commits that
changed the accepted set likewise re-anchored in-process.

What:
Persist the first-keyed instant per accepted-key-set digest in
/var/lib/xpf/fabric-auth-grace (cluster/fabric_auth_grace.go):
HMAC-SHA256 over a domain tag keyed by each accepted key, no key
bytes stored. UpdateConfig now anchors on the first keying of the
current set: a restart under an unchanged set restores the persisted
time (backwards-stepped clocks distrust a future stamp, which only
shortens the grace); a changed set re-anchors and still gets its
grace; clearing clears. Persist is best-effort via fsatomic with a
Warn naming the reopened-grace consequence. grpcapi docs updated;
the 5-minute length, read-only set, and arming sources are unchanged.

Validation:
RED on master: pkg/grpcapi TestFabricAuth16027 fails to build
(cluster.SetFabricAuthGraceStatePathForTesting undefined) — the
restart behaviour does not exist. GREEN: grpcapi #16027 + #11676
suites and cluster anchor/UpdateConfig/rotation tests pass
(go vet clean); full pkg/cluster and pkg/grpcapi suites pass.

Risk:
A wiped /var/lib/xpf or a persistently failing anchor write falls
back to anchoring at that apply — indistinguishable from a genuine
new keying; the failure is Warn-logged. Rotation steps that change
the accepted set each get a fresh read-only grace, closed early by
peer authentication as before.

Closes #16027

## PR #16359 — cluster: persist heartbeat epoch latch and floor across restart (#16022) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16022-heartbeat-persist-epoch`

Closes #16022.

The epoch-capable downgrade latch and boot-epoch floor were process-scoped: a receiver daemon restart cleared both, and >=65 captured sender incarnations replayed while the peer was down churned the 64-entry session ring indefinitely (1625/1625 epochless admitted pre-fix), sustaining forged peer liveness and delaying takeover.

## Fix
- Persist latch+floor+per-value session bindings in a key-set-scoped record (/var/lib/xpf/ha-peer-epoch, alongside ha-boot-epoch), digest = controlAuthKeySetDigest over the accepted key set (the #15262 construction).
- Written OFF the accept path: admitAuthed only marks the record owed; a sender-tick flush (10s cadence, 1s retry after failure) plus StopHeartbeat/Manager.Stop flushes write it under the boot-epoch sidecar flock. A failed/wedged write fails open to the pre-#16022 process-scoped behaviour — admission never waits on storage.
- Restored on the boot UpdateConfig apply and again before StartHeartbeat publishes a receiver (no window where an epochless replay meets an unrestored latch). A key-set change drops the restored state; clearing the key set removes the file; a corrupt/mismatched record degrades to the migration window.
- Engages the removed durable-latch pricing rather than ignoring it: no accept-path write, off-path lock, rotation-not-file-edit recovery. The epoch-bearing re-arm after any clearing (residual 5) is unchanged.

## Validation
- go vet ./pkg/cluster/ clean
- go test ./pkg/cluster/ -run 16022 + epoch/latch/rollback/receiver suites pass
- Full pkg/cluster sweep passes

Risk: a crash inside one 10s flush interval loses at most that interval advanc

e (bounded and documented). A deliberately rolled-back peer now needs the PSK rotation rather than a bare restart; the rejection warning already prescribed the rotation first.

## PR #16360 — userspace-dp: demote steering PASS on multi-zone nodes (#16026) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-23)

Branch: `fix/16026-zoneless-steering`

Closes #16026 (A1-C4).

## Mechanism
`UserspaceSessionKey` is a bare 5-tuple with no zone/ifindex/domain. A `PASS_TO_KERNEL` row published for one zone's peer-synced `LocalDelivery` session is honoured at the shim for any packet presenting the same tuple. The normal cross-zone case dies in the nft ingress-scoped host-inbound verdict, but on a shared/ambiguous netdev that re-derivation is impossible and the discarded zone is unrecoverable — a same-tuple UDP packet arriving on the second zone's interface passes to the kernel into the HA peer-synced row.

## Fix
- `ForwardingState::has_multiple_zones` built in `populate_zones` (admitted distinct zone ids; the `has_routing_domains` single-bool shape).
- `uses_kernel_local_session_map_entry` now also requires `!has_multiple_zones`: on a multi-zone node a peer-synced LocalDelivery session is published **REDIRECT** instead of PASS_TO_KERNEL and is judged by the worker's `session_hit_authority` (#9519) by live arrival zone (foreign drop, owner delivered via LocalDelivery). Threaded through every publish callsite. Single-zone deployments are byte-identical.

## Not taken (measured)
A shim-side PASS gate (new `userspace_session_pass_zones` map honoured only for resolvable arrivals, else demote) was implemented and **rejected at the 1M-insn verifier cap** even as one outlined map probe — the tracked shim object has no headroom for another PASS-path lookup. Reverted in full; no .o change, no `make generate` owed. Detail in `docs/log/16026.md`.

## Validation
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp 16026`: `multiple_zones_demote_kernel_local_to_redirect_16026` (predicate pair; deleting `!has_multiple_zones &&` reds only the demotion assertion) and `the_worker_publish_reads_this_nodes_multiple_zones_flag_16026` (real worker publish path against the SESSION_MAP_WRITES recorder) — pass.
- Main-agent gates still owed: full userspace-dp suite, Go suites.

## Risk
Multi-zone nodes: host-bound peer-synced traffic takes one extra helper hop (safe direction, same as #9517). Single-zone: unchanged.

## PR #16362 — logging: unify raw-event parser behind logEvent/DecodeRawEventRecord (#16127) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16127-logging-parser`

Refs #16127

## Why
`logEvent` (live `Run`/`ProcessRawEvent` path) and `DecodeRawEventRecord` hand-parsed the same 144-byte RT_FLOW offsets with divergent validation and divergent unknown-address-family policy: the live path rendered any non-v6 family as IPv4, the decoder rejected unknown families. Two hand-maintained parsers for one wire shape drift on every wire change (the #16127 narrowed survivor: one zero-extra-allocation parser, explicit family decision, parser-only — fanout untouched).

- `parseRawEvent(data, *rawEvent) bool` — the single offset parser, filling a caller-zeroed `rawEvent` in place (zero allocation, pinned by `TestParseRawEventZeroAlloc16127`); both callers keep their existing `len >= rawEventWireSize` gates.

Decoder rejects, live path drops; the former live-only v4 fallback is gone. Documented at `parseRawEvent` and in `pkg/logging/README.md`.
- Live record now carries `Created` on non-close frames (decoder parity; previously close-only — additive, exporters read it on close).
- Golden frames + pins: `pkg/logging/raw_event_parser_16127_test.go` (short / legacy-144 / extended-160 / IPv6 cells, live-vs-decoded field parity, family policy, alloc).

- `go vet ./pkg/logging/ ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ ./pkg/daemon/` clean.
- Fail-on-revert: removing the family gate in `parseRawEvent` makes `TestRawEventFamilyPolicy16127` RED (family 0 accepted); restored green.

- A hypothetical producer emitting a non-2/10 family byte (none exists in-tree) would now be dropped live instead of rendered as IPv4 garbage — that rendering was the divergence being removed.

## PR #16364 — cluster: alarm on a forgotten key rotation past seven days (#16029) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16029-rotation-age-alarm`

**Acceptance (#16029):** rotation open beyond a threshold (days) produces a visible status alarm naming the open rotation. Record rotation-open-since and alarm on age.

**Mechanism:** `UpdateConfig` stamps `Manager.controlLinkRotationOpenedAt` when the additional key's identity changes (digest-keyed on the additional slot only — identical re-applies and signing-key swaps under the same additional key do not move it, so a routine commit cannot launder a forgotten rotation's age; a different additional key re-anchors; clearing it/finalize clears the stamp). `controlLinkRotationStatus` appends the window age (whole days/hours) to every existing peer-state clause, and past `controlLinkRotationStaleAfter` (7 days) appends an `ALARM` naming the window by its accepted key IDs (never key bytes) with the finalize remedy, rendered on the `Key rotation:` line in `show chassis cluster statistics` (CLI + gRPC share `FormatControlPlaneStatistics`). New `ControlLinkRotationOpenSince`/`ControlLinkRotationStale` accessors are the machine-readable half.

**Never auto-finalizes:** retiring a key the peer still signs with reopens the dual-master window (#6630), so the fix prompts the operator commit instead of taking it. The stamp is in-memory and re-anchors at the first apply after a daemon restart — a stale alarm can be up to one restart late, never early; a backwards clock step clamps age to zero rather than alarming early.

**Tests (hermetic, pinned clock, fail-on-revert noted in file):**
- `TestRotationAgeSurvivesRoutineReapply16029` — identical re-apply and signing-swap under the same additional key don't move the stamp.
- `TestRotationWindowIdentity16029` — changed additional key re-anchors; finalize clears; reopening starts fresh.
- `TestStaleRotationAlarmsByName16029` — fresh window: age only, no alarm; just under 7d: no alarm; past 7d: `ALARM ... still accepted ... open for 7d` naming both key IDs, reaching `FormatControlPlaneStatistics`, no key bytes rendered; finalize clears it.

**Validation:** `go test ./pkg/cluster/ -run '...16029|TestPSKRotation' -count=1` ok; `go vet ./pkg/cluster/` clean; full `go test ./pkg/cluster/ -count=1` ok (141s).

## PR #16366 — userspace-dp: intern route tables inside ForwardingState only with dual-carry cell (#16131) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16131-intern-route-tables`

Refs #16131

## Why
The per-address local-delivery attributions in `ForwardingState` (`local_tables_v[46]`, `interface_nat_tables_v[46]`, nested `interface_nat_v[46]`) key owning route tables by canonical table NAME, so the packet path hashes the name string on every local-delivery probe. Interning onto the numeric `RouteIdentity{domain, table}` was proposed as a replacement — but the dissenting review preserved on #16131 (Codex, UNSOUND as a performance cutover) showed that form costs a second hash probe (`&str` → ID) before the membership test: strictly more probes than today's single string-set lookup. The accepted narrowed form is dual-carry only, and only if the agreement cell passes.

## What
- New interned twins inside `ForwardingState` only: `local_table_ids_v[46]`, `interface_nat_table_ids_v[46]` (`FastSet<RouteIdentity>`), `interface_nat_ids_v[46]` (`FastMap<RouteIdentity, i32>`), plus diagnostic `route_table_interning_complete`.
- `forwarding_build::intern::intern_route_tables` derives the twins once per build, immediately after `route_table_identities` is assigned and after every string-form writer (interfaces, late-stage NAT append). Identity is never synthesized: a name with no published identity row is omitted and flips `route_table_interning_complete` false; an incomplete identity map (legacy posture) leaves the twins empty.
- The string carry remains the ONLY form any lookup reads — no packet code reads the twins, so packet-path probe count is unchanged by construction (the dissent's condition). NAT zone interning is excluded (separate W3 allocator-API proposal; `synced_source_nat_zone_pair` is load-bearing for allocator matching + legacy-peer fallback, #6600).

Asserted in the build before publish; a disagreement panics so the reconcile preflight keeps the previous live state (fail closed).

## Validation
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp dual_carry` — 5/5 pass: hand-built agreement, built-state agreement over a real two-VRF `build_forwarding_state`, and phantom / missing-identity / wrong-ifindex corruption cells.

- iperf witness row: not run — no packet code changed and the issue makes no throughput claim, so no live witness can distinguish this change.

Additive build-time derivation only. Memory grows by one small identity set/map per local address. A derivation bug panics the candidate build (fail-closed; previous state stays live) rather than publishing a divergent state.

## PR #16367 — userspace-dp: make GRE/WG frag pool head-only with per-source quota (#16028) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16028-gre-frag-pool`

## Why
#16028 (A1-C6 from #15985): GRE reassembly created a `FragEntry` for ANY fragment — tails included — behind only a tunnel-pair index probe, in one 64-entry pool shared with WireGuard. An attacker knowing/spoofing the configured tunnel peer source could tail-flood (or head-flood) the pool and starve legitimate WG/GRE reassembly for the 10s entry lifetime. The GRE buffer-time gate had no GRE-key, transport-domain, egress, or ingress-zone/host-inbound check.

Refs #16028

## What
- **Head-only creation**: `GreReassembler::offer`/`offer_for_protocol` take `OfferAdmission`. `Head` may create; `Tail` consults only and never creates; admission/offset mismatch is a counted refusal.
- **Per-source sub-quota**: `MAX_GRE_FRAG_DATAGRAMS_PER_SRC = 32` (half the shared 64) per outer source across protocols/ingresses (strictly stronger than per-(src,ingress/proto)), no eviction of other sources' entries.
- **Full GRE head admission**: new `gre::outer_head_admits_gre_endpoint` runs the complete `match_tunnel_endpoint` chain (key read from the head, transport domain, resolved transport egress, ingress host-inbound). Matcher/egress helpers gained `counted` twins redirecting charges to a `GreDecapCounters::scratch()` so probes charge nothing and successful datagrams aren't double-counted; the production decap path is unchanged (`counted=true`). Refused heads are consume-and-counted (`Buffered`), never forwarded as transit.
- WG stage passes Head/Tail by fragment offset; its head gates already include listener/zone/ownership.
- **Intentional trade-off**: a tail arriving before its head is dropped instead of buffered (pre-head tail buffering was the starvation vector). Correctly ordered fragmented tunnel traffic is unaffected. #14645/#15095 tail-first assertions updated to head-then-tail; the wrong-key refusal count is preserved (now charged at head admission).

## Validation
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- --test-threads=1 16028 14645 15102 15095` → **18 passed** (5 new #16028 tests: tail-only flood creates zero state + legit decaps; GRE head flood capped at 32 with WG completing in the same pool; wrong-key and host-inbound-denied heads create no state, counted once; pool-level quota/consult invariants).
- Broader `gre_ wg_` run: 478 passed, 8 failed — the **identical 8 failures reproduce on unmodified origin/master** (pre-existing).
- `outer_frag`/`poll_descriptor_structure`: 17 passed.

## Risk
Fragmented tunnel datagrams whose tail beats the head (cross-path reordering) now lose that datagram — bounded to the reassembly use case, fail-closed and counted. Two peers behind one NAT source share one 32-entry sub-quota (deliberate: source is the only unspoofable-at-this-layer fair-share key available before decap).

## PR #16368 — api: bound global Basic lockout with successful-verify probe (#16068) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16068-global-basic-lockout`

Closes #16068.

## Why
The #11492 global per-username Basic bucket was reserved before verification (5 failures/10 min → 5 min lockout doubling to 1 h), so anyone who knew a username and could reach an off-loopback web-mgmt leg could re-spray after each expiry and keep the legitimate user locked out of REST Basic auth indefinitely — the decisive pre-fix check (5 bad passwords, then the correct password from another source) was refused with 429.

## What
- When ONLY the global Basic bucket is locked (caller's pair + source buckets clean), admit the attempt as a bounded probe: at most 1 concurrent verify per locked username (`authThrottleGlobalBasicProbes`), still paying full bcrypt cost.
- Successful probe clears-then-admits the global bucket (and its own pair), exactly like a normal clean success.
- Failed probe is charged to its pair/source buckets; `chargeLocked` drops it for the global bucket while locked, so wrong-password probes never extend the deadline.
- Pair/source lockouts remain hard pre-verification refusals — a correct credential from a locked pair/source can never rescue it, preserving the #11492 anti-spray and #10825 bcrypt-CPU caps.
- Tests: `TestRESTAuthGlobalBasicAccountBudgetAcrossSources11492` updated to the decisive 204 check; new `TestRESTAuthGlobalBasicProbeWrongPasswordKeepsLockout16068` and `TestRESTAuthGlobalBasicProbeCapAndPairLockout16068`; `docs/log/16068.md`.

## Validation
- `go test ./pkg/api/ -count=1` passes (98s)
- Targeted throttle suite passes; gofmt/vet clean; `git diff --check` clean

## Risk
Only global-only-locked Basic requests change path (one bounded verify instead of immediate 429). All other lockouts, escalation, the 4096-entry bound, and API-key/Bearer namespaces unchanged.

## PR #16371 — cluster: cap bulk-sync receive window at table capacity (#16039) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16039-bulk-recv-cap`

## Why

Refs #16039. Bulk session-sync receive inserted keys into `bulkRecvV4/V6` before the install verdict, with no capacity cap and no window deadline inside an open bulk window; the sets reset only at BulkEnd/connection teardown. A keyed peer could grow receiver memory entry-by-entry at wire cost for as long as it held the window open. The sibling `bulkInstallFailedV4/V6` marker sets had the same unbounded shape.

## What

- Admission to the receive accumulators runs through `admitBulkRecvV4/V6`, still before the install verdict (a transiently failed key must count as received), but the combined distinct keys across both families may not exceed `bulkRecvCap()` = `maxCap()` — the forward-session table capacity (wired helper capacity when known, else the 200k default, ceiling `conntrack.MaxSessions/2`).
- The first distinct key past the cap invalidates the window: it never reconciles, acks, or releases the failover hold; further keys are counted and dropped without storing. At its BulkEnd the window is torn down and the sender's bounded re-drive re-primes a legitimate bulk.
- The transient-failure marker maps share the same combined cap with the same invalidation.
- A `BulkEnd` arriving more than `bulkRecvWindowTimeout` (1h, far beyond the sender's 35s ack-retry / ~150s daemon prime-retry cadence) after the accepted `BulkStart` aborts the window the same way.
- `reconcileStaleSessions` refuses an invalid window; new state is cleared on reconcile, abort, and full disconnect.
- Counters `BulkRecvCapped` / `BulkRecvAborted` ride `SyncStats` → snapshot → cluster status (rendered when nonzero). No wire change.

## Validation

- New cells in `pkg/cluster/sync_bulk_recv_cap_16039_test.go` (overflow abort + flood + legitimate at-cap completion, deadline abort + in-deadline control, marker-map bound, duplicates/incremental free): pass, including `-race`.
- #12166 bulk-ack regression set (`TestBulkAck*`, `TestBulkTransient*`, `TestBulkInstallFailure*`): pass.
- Full `go test ./pkg/cluster/ -count=1`: pass (128.2s). One earlier full run flaked `TestAncestryReorderedGenerationsDropStalePair10511` (2s apply-callback timing); it passes in isolation on both base and this head, and the clean rerun confirms unrelated load flake.
- `go vet ./pkg/cluster/`, `gofmt -l` on touched files, `git diff --check`: clean.

## Risk

A peer whose legitimate table exceeds the wired capacity now has its bulk aborted instead of installed; the bounded re-drive re-primes once capacity is wired correctly, and the new counters make the condition operator-visible rather than silent memory growth.
