## PR #16372 — cluster: refresh peer liveness only on semantic accept with per-type payload caps (#16041) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16041-cluster-liveness`

Refs #16041

Why: In the sync read loop, missedHeartbeats=0 and the last-peer-receive stamp ran for any well-framed frame before handleMessage semantic accept, so junk frames from a keyed peer refreshed liveness and masked a dead peer's failover trigger. There were also no per-type payload caps beyond the global 16MiB bound.

What:
- handleMessage and every receive handler return semantic acceptance (applied, queued, or matched a live waiter/incarnation; stale/malformed/superseded/undecryptable/unknown rejected). receiveLoop refreshes liveness only on acceptance. Retired persistent-NAT types 38/39 deliberately count as accepted (old-peer liveness; ignored by migration design).
- syncPayloadCap (sync_payload_caps_16041.go) gives all 44 dispatched labels encoder-derived caps, enforced in receiveLoop from the header BEFORE payload allocation/read; over-cap counts OversizeFramesRefused (+Errors, rendered in cluster statistics when nonzero) and drops the connection. Unknown types keep only the global cap (forward-compatible, ignored, never liveness). Config and full-set/chunk types keep maxSyncPayload as their per-type cap (encoders chunk below it).
- Updated #16168 census mutations and #6650 source pin for the bool signatures; README + changelog.

Validation: New sync_liveness_caps_16041_test.go drives the real receiveLoop over net.Pipe: rejected frames (unknown type, truncated session, impossible clock, stale DHCP full-set, short acks/caps) do not refresh lastPeerRxMono/PeerHealthy while Barrier/Heartbeat controls do; over-cap headers refuse and drop without a body; cap census covers every dispatched type and conforming encoders fit. Tests pass including -race; full pkg/cluster suite passes (156s); go vet clean.

Risk: A peer whose only traffic is semantically rejected (e.g. duplicate stale-generation installs) no longer refreshes liveness and ages out — intended failover behaviour; heartbeat ACKs remain accepted so healthy peers are unaffected. Failover-ack detail is capped at 4KiB of peer error text (real errors are far below). Mixed-version: new receiver drops over-cap frames from any peer; conforming old senders never emit them.

## PR #16374 — sessions: require exact seq for RST teardown (#16040) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16040-rst-exact-seq`

sessions: require exact seq for RST teardown (#16040)

Why: #16040 (S2-03 leg2, split from #15985, Low residual). `tcp_closing_seq_verdict` returned Valid for any closing segment with `behind < wnd || seq == rcv_nxt`, so an in-window but non-exact RST stamped session teardown for any of ~window blind guesses. Leg1 (foreign/filter-dropped seq-note poisoning) was already fixed by #15947; this PR is leg2 only.

What:
- `tcp_closing_seq_verdict(key, seq, tcp_flags)` now requires exact seq when the RST bit is set (RFC 9293 §3.5.3 / RFC 5961 §3.2: a non-matching RST draws a challenge ACK, never a close). RST|FIN is driven by the RST bit.
- Fold (Opus): the exact target is the ENDPOINT's receive-next, not the firewall-observed send-end. `tcp_rcv_nxt` is the send-end (transmitted high-water, including downstream-lost bytes), so exact-vs-send-end dropped legitimate ACK-derived RSTs in downstream-loss recovery. New `tcp_peer_rcv_nxt`/`tcp_peer_rcv_nxt_seen` state on the sender-direction entry, recorded high-water from the companion direction's ACK field in the `note_tcp_seq_scaled` seam (SYN-ACK ack = ISN+1; bare SYN excluded). RST is Valid iff `seq == tcp_peer_rcv_nxt`; until an endpoint ACK is observed, the RST verdict is Unknown (admitted), never a send-end guess.
- FIN keeps in-window validity; the #15947 receiver (companion) advertised-window logic governs FIN only. `no-sequence-check` still bypasses the verdict. The poll slow-path caller passes `meta.tcp_flags`; the flow-cache fast path still never stamps close.
- Decisive tests: `rst_requires_exact_seq_16040` (full delivery: non-exact RST Invalid, exact Valid, FIN retained); `rst_exact_uses_endpoint_rcv_nxt_not_send_end_16040` (downstream loss 100 sent/50 ACKed: RST@1051 Valid, RST@1101 Invalid; target advances on retransmit-ACK, duplicate ACK does not rewind); updated `in_window_rst_valid_blind_rst_invalid_15753`, `scaled_window_and_receiver_window_verdict_15947`, `rst_seq_validation_in_window_vs_blind_15753`. Docs/changelog updated.

Validation: `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- rst_requires_exact_seq_16040 rst_exact_uses_endpoint in_window_rst_valid scaled_window_and_receiver rst_seq_validation seed_tcp_window_scale unilateral_wsopt` — 7/7 pass. Full `session::` module: 506 passed, 1 failed (`session_decision_typed_snat_layout_11064`, SessionDecision 116 vs pinned 112) — fails identically with the fold changes stashed, pre-existing on this head and unrelated. RED (first head): production change stashed with tests kept, the two updated tests fail on the pre-fix verdict. Unit level only; no live cluster run.

Risk: A legitimate RST desynced from the endpoint's ACK-tracked rcv_nxt is dropped instead of closing early; the session ages out on its normal timeout. Before any endpoint ACK is observed, RSTs are admitted (Unknown) as in the legacy no-state posture. FIN, no-sequence-check, and HA-imported (no local ACK state) paths are unchanged in posture.

Refs #16040

## PR #16376 — screen: judge ambiguous fabric arrivals under raw and claimed profiles (#16051) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16051-screen-profile-ambiguous`

## Why

Stage 10 (screens + SYN-cookie) runs before any forwarding resolution exists, so it resolved its screen profile from the raw fabric ingress zone alone. On an ambiguous (#15916) arrival — claimed zone withheld pending owner-RG promotion — that skipped the claimed zone's screen profile entirely: the packet was later promoted and admitted under a zone whose stateless screens never ran, and a returning cookie ACK was validated only under the raw zone. RN-04 from the #15985 cohort (validated Low, unanimous MATERIAL).

## What

- `screen_zone_candidates` returns `[raw ingress zone, withheld claimed zone]`, each gated on its own #12875 screen state.
- `stage_screen_check_with_ambiguous` / `stage_screen_syn_cookie_ack_on_session_miss_with_ambiguous` charge the FULL profile (flood/cookie state, counters, challenge, validated-client bypass, ACK validation) to the raw zone only — the peer that minted a cookie screened under it.
- The claimed zone contributes ONLY a stateless veto via new pure `ScreenState::stateless_screen_drop_for_zones` (LAND / TCP-flag / fragment / source-route; #7168 conservative default for an unresolved claimed reference; claimed `alarm-without-drop` = log-only). A claimed Drop recycles at stage 10 (flow + flowless branches) and vetoes even a Validated cookie ACK. It charges no flood sketch, mints no challenge, seeds no bypass — it can only subtract, never admit — so no claimed-zone state exists before owner proof and no premature SYN-ACK is possible (#15947 deferred-challenge final admission still governs replies).
- The #11332 pre-screen input-filter walk runs when either candidate has screen state.
- Non-ambiguous callers pass `ambiguous_zone=None` via the existing wrappers — byte-identical behavior.
- Docs: `docs/fabric-cross-chassis-fwd.md` #16051 section, `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/README.md`, `docs/log/16051.md`.

## Validation

- `ambiguous_claimed_zone_screen_drop_applies_16051` — decisive regression (issue's check): co-moved ambiguous `lan` stamp, SYN+FIN vs `lan`-only syn-fin profile → screen drop, no session, no forward, no SYN-ACK. Fail-on-revert: withholding `ambiguous_zone` at stage 10 makes the drop 0 and the session installs.
- `ambiguous_clean_syn_still_admitted_16051` — control: clean SYN still promoted/admitted (union adds drops only).
- `screen` suite: 402 passed. `tests_fabric_zone_stamp` / `poll_stages` suites match base: `arp_two_vlans_same_ip_distinct_logical_keys_2370` fails identically on unmodified master (verified via stash); `fabric_ingress_syn_ack_seeds_no_reverse_session_6478` passes in isolation (parallel-order flake, also present on base run).

## Risk

Rate-based claimed-zone screens (SYN/ICMP/UDP flood thresholds) still do not fire pre-promotion — bounded residual, documented in `docs/fabric-cross-chassis-fwd.md`: legitimate punts were already screened on the true ingress node (#4155), and a forged clone still receives exactly the promoted local-ingress adjudication (accepted #15916 shared-segment residual). No behavior change for non-ambiguous packets.

Deleting the wiring or the mint-side check reds the reject cells.

## PR #16378 — login: enforce argument-scoped command regexes on gRPC and REST (#16067) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16067-arg-scoped-commands`

Closes #16067

## Why
Canonical command strings carry no arguments, and both the gRPC and REST gates evaluated only the bare topic/path — so operator-authored argument-scoped regexes like `^ping 10\.99\.`, `^show route table secret-vrf` or `^show log .*` never matched remotely. The restriction the operator believes is enforced was silently inoperative (fail-open) on the remote surfaces.

## What
- **gRPC** (`pkg/grpcapi/authz_command_args_16067.go`): rebuild the full canonicalised command from the decoded request — every packed ShowText topic (route-table/protocol/prefix, log with count, screen statistics/ids-option, CoS name/type, firewall filter/effective, test-policy/routing/zone, applications, class-of-service, interfaces-queue, sessions-top), ShowText filters, Ping/Traceroute targets+options, GetSessions selectors (zone ID resolved via StableZoneIDOwnerForConfig), MatchPolicies selectors, ShowInterfacesDetail filter — and judge it with `EvaluateForms` alongside the argument-free charge. Reconstruction mirrors each handler's decoder; malformed packings/uncanonicalisable strings/unresolvable zones deny for restricted classes.
- **REST** (`pkg/api/authz_command_args_16067.go`): same reconstruction for show-text topics, diagnostics ping/traceroute bodies, session/match query selectors, interfaces/detail. REST show-text topics now resolve through the same longest-prefix rule as gRPC (previously plain map indexing denied every packed topic for restricted classes).
- **Advisories** (`pkg/config/login_command_surface_args_16067.go`): surfaces register argument-sample exemplars; the commit-time unenforceability advisory, per-alternative advisory and the once-per-class runtime warning now derive witnesses from the operator's pattern (literal spelling extending a registered command; unanchored literal segment occupying a proven argument slot) judged by the real compiled rules, so an argument-scoped pattern that fires remotely is no longer reported on-box-only. Witnesses are gated on registered samples, so fake/unproven surfaces keep the prior advisory (fake-surface #9340/#8189 tests unchanged and passing).
- Rewrote `TestArgumentLevelDenyIsOnBoxOnly7172` to assert the closed agreement; updated #11678 REST advisory test; docs (`docs/system-login.md`, `pkg/grpcapi/README.md`), gate/topic header prose, changelog.

## Validation
- `go test ./pkg/grpcapi/ -run 'TestArgument|TestUnenforceable|TestMalformedPacked'` — decisive cells: deny `^show route table secret-vrf$` denies `route-table:secret-vrf` and allows `public-vrf`; `^ping 10\.99\.`, `^show log .*`, screen/test-policy/test-routing/route-prefix/session-zone/match-policies/interfaces-filter shapes deny; allow-exception `^show log messages 100$` lifts `^show log$` for that spelling only; malformed packed topics deny.
- `go test ./pkg/api/ -run 'TestArgumentScoped|TestRESTArgumentScoped'` — REST twins of the above.
- `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestArgumentSamples|TestNoSamples|TestUnenforceable|TestCombinedDeny|TestWholeUnenforceable|TestPartialAdvisory'`.
- Main agent should run the full `pkg/grpcapi`, `pkg/api`, `pkg/config`, `pkg/cli` suites plus vet before merge (targeted runs above are green).

## Risk
Restricted classes may now be denied on requests whose arguments cannot be reconstructed (malformed packed topics, unresolvable zone IDs) where they previously passed on the bare path — fail-closed by design, matching the existing unmapped-command rule. Unrestricted classes are unaffected (the gate returns before reconstruction). Advisory witnesses only suppress warnings when a proven argument slot exists, never invent one.

## PR #16379 — nat: quarantine freed PAT ports on small pools (#16035) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16035-pat-quarantine`

Refs #16035

Why: free_recycle cleared the occupancy bit and FIFO-recycled the port immediately, so on a tiny/high-churn pool a delayed UDP reply reusing (translated_ip, port, remote) could land on a new owner of the same port. Large pools were already de-facto quarantined by FIFO-after-fresh-range reuse; TCP endpoints reject stray segments by sequence state.

What: stamp each recycle token with its monotonic free time and, for ranges <=256 ports, refuse to claim a token (via both the keyed probe and the recycled phase) until 60s after the free, retaining it with its original stamp. Production flow frees (release/rollback/unlink/allocation give-backs) thread now_ns into the stamp; lease-retention frees (expiry GC, persistent clear) stay unstamped because the lease already held the port for its full timeout. Retained tokens requeue without tripping the dedup bitset. Existing small-pool fixtures that pinned instant reuse now claim at post-quarantine times or use >256-port pools where they measured allocator mechanics, not reuse timing.

Validation: new tests_16035 cells (tiny-pool UDP quarantine + boundary reuse, TCP control, large-pool no-quarantine, recycled-phase token retention) pass; full nat:: suite 755 passed / 0 failed on rerun.

Risk: small pools under sustained churn can exhaust during the 60s window where they previously reused instantly - that refusal is the fix. Large pools, deterministic claim_in_block, and reserve paths are untouched.

## PR #16380 — nat: suppress fabric fallback NAT scope for ambiguous arrivals (#16045) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16045-nat-fabric-zone`

## Summary
For an ambiguous fabric arrival (#15916 — claimed zone withheld pending the owner-RG gate), pre-routing NAT resolved its scope from the LOCAL fabric/logical identity (fabric interface zone / config name / routing-instance) and could select a translation under that identity. The session-miss policy later promoted the claimed zone, so the translated action was keyed to a zone the policy never adjudicated (RN-01).

Fix direction per the validated refutation in #16045: suppress the fabric fallback identity only; never grant the claimed zone before owner proof.

- `PreroutingIngressScope` gains `ambiguous_provenance`; `prerouting_ingress_scope_ambiguous` resolves the same local identity stamped ambiguous (claimed zone and V2 peer scope ifindex never substituted). Flow-backed miss and flowless pre-routing paths both stamp it.
- NAT-layer ambiguous-provenance siblings (ordinary matchers untouched): pool DNAT -> Poisoned fail-closed (needs the winner's scope tier, so `DnatOutcome::Translate` now carries it), static DNAT withholds, NPTv6 -> Untranslatable, NAT64 -> MatchUnavailable; the persistent-NAT reader is skipped (ingress-keyed lease scope).
- UNSCOPED rules still fire (identity-independent), native owner-scope ingress unchanged, session-hit revalidation untouched.

## Decisive regression (co-moved owner fixture)
`*_16045` in `poll_descriptor/prerouting_scope_tests.rs`: fabric-scoped DNAT cannot fire prematurely; native `fabric`-zone ingress still translates; claimed-zone DNAT stays withheld; unscoped DNAT still translates; interface-scoped static, NAT64 and NPTv6 legs.

## Validation
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp 16045`: 7/7. RED-on-revert verified for the NAT64/NPTv6 legs (fail on clean master code). Note: in the poll harness the DNAT/static legs are broker-gated (session installs via the fabric-link binding end in MissingNeighbor), so the DNAT invariant is additionally pinned at the NAT-table tri-state; see `docs/log/16045.md`.
- `nat::` suite: 751 pass. Fabric zone-stamp suite: 66 pass.
- Three `prerouting` VLAN failures reproduce identically on clean master (pre-existing, unrelated).

## Risk
Fail-closed only: ambiguous arrivals with scope-constrained pre-routing NAT now drop/withhold instead of translating under the fallback identity. Unscoped and validated flows are byte-identical.

Closes #16045

## PR #16381 — userspace-dp: resolve PPTP data channel in claimed fabric domain (#16055) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/issue-16055`

## userspace-dp: resolve PPTP data channel in claimed fabric domain (#16055)

Fixes #16055 (RN-06).

### Why
The PPTP association table is domain-keyed, and associations are installed in the domain of the control flow that taught them — the domain stage 9b stamps from the claimed fabric identity (`ingress_zone_override.or(ambiguous_zone)`). The data-channel resolve instead derived its domain from the ingress interface plus the *validated* zone override only. On an ambiguous fabric arrival the two differ by construction: the claimed zone has no `zone_routing_domain` row, so stage 9b keys the flow in the per-zone quarantine band (`AMBIGUOUS_FABRIC_DOMAIN_BASE | zone`) while the resolve consulted the fabric link's own domain. The claimed tenant's association was missed, and a same-call-ID association in the wrong domain was claimed and idle-refreshed instead — the wrong-domain association refresh the issue names. (At the original evidence base the drift was narrower — override-only vs. the later ambiguous promotion in #15916 — but the invariant "resolve domain == install/re-key domain" is the same.)

### What
- New `pptp_resolve_routing_domain` helper in `poll_descriptor/mod.rs`: fabric arrivals resolve via the claimed zone (validated or ambiguous); a fabric arrival with **no** claimed zone fails closed to domain 0 instead of falling through to the fabric link's ifindex domain; the absent-stamp suspect arm stays domain 0; non-fabric arrivals keep the physical-ingress derivation unchanged.
- The descriptor-loop PPTP resolve calls the helper (replacing the ingress-only derivation).
- Decisive regression cells in `pptp_domain_16055_tests.rs`, plus `debian/changelog` and `docs/log/16055.md`.

### Validation
- `pptp_domain_16055`: **5 passed** (pinned toolchain, release, `--test-threads=1`) on head `92b897008f`.
- Decisive check from the issue: same endpoint pair + same call IDs installed in the claimed (quarantine) domain and in domain 0; a fabric-arrival packet resolves to the claimed domain's handle, keys there, and idle-refreshes **only** that association (the wrong-domain row expires on schedule). A control cell resolving in the pre-fix domain claims the wrong tenant, proving the fixture distinguishes the defect.
- Mutation: reverting the helper's fabric arm to the pre-fix expression reds the claimed-domain and refresh cells (verified).
- Broader `pptp` filter: 99 passed, 1 failed — `pptp_open_frame_carries_the_call_id_pair_13965` fails **identically on unmodified master** (verified via stash); pre-existing, unrelated.

### Risk
Fabric-arrival PPTP packets whose peer encoded no zone stamp now resolve in domain 0 rather than the fabric link's ifindex domain; such arrivals carry no tenant identity, and domain 0 is the same fail-closed answer the suspect arm already gives. Non-fabric and single-instance (`has_routing_domains = false`) paths are bit-identical to before.

## PR #16384 — sessions: validate handshake ack numbers at all completion gates (#16042) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16042-handshake-ack`

## Why
Refs #16042 (S2-05 from #15985). Handshake promotion/completion keyed on flags + `handshake_pending`/`is_reverse` only — no ack-number check. A wrong-ack SYN-ACK could promote a pair, and a wrong-ack completing segment could clear `handshake_pending` and move both halves onto the long established window without the peer ever answering correctly.

## What
ACK-number validation at **all** completion gates: a segment promotes/completes only when its parsed ack equals the companion direction's ISN + 1 (wrapping; a SYN consumes one sequence number).

- `SessionEntry.tcp_peer_isn` tracks each direction's SYN ISN — learned by `note_tcp_seq` on SYN/SYN-ACK, seeded onto both halves at install by `seed_tcp_isn` (companion resolved through `reverse_session_key`, so SNAT/DNAT/NAT64 alias pairs validate identically). The poll path seeds it at all five install sites next to the existing WSOPT seed.
- Gates gated: lookup SYN-ACK promotion, lookup completing-ACK (SYN-first and SYN-ACK-first), fused `probe_hit` (incl. deferring variant), flow-cache keepalive, deferred-Owner replay, and the `update_session`/`promote_synced_with_origin` twin. The ack is threaded via `SessionQuery`, `SessionUpdate`, `DeferredSyncedPromotion`, the resolve/promote plumbing, and the poll/flow-cache call sites that parse the frame (`pending_tcp_seq_note`, `extract_tcp_seq_ack_window`).
- **Unknown evidence fails open, never closed**: companion ISN unobserved (mid-stream pickup), HA import (imports carry no ISN — fail-closed there would strand failover sessions), or unparsed ack → flags-only, exactly as before, bounded by the opening window.
- Companion resolution uses the non-counting `revalidation_record` resolver so ordinary hits don't perturb the #7919 lookup-miss counters (two counter/alias regressions in the first cut, caught and fixed).

Partial prior edits on this branch were audited: the broken `note_tcp_seq_scaled` truncation was restored, and the seed/expected-ack helpers were rewritten to resolve through the canonical record.

## Tests
New `handshake_ack_16042_tests.rs` — 12 tests, all passing, fail-on-revert (dropping any gate's `ack_valid` conjunct turns its bad-ack test red):
- bad-ack SYN-ACK never promotes / correct-ack promotes-but-stays-pending (lookup)
- bad-ack completing ACK never completes, then correct ack completes (lookup)
- wraparound: server ISN `u32::MAX` expects ack 0
- SYN-ACK-first: reverse completing ACK validated
- cached-hit (`probe_hit` + deferring variant) and keepalive gates
- `update_session` and `promote_synced_with_origin` gates
- NAT SNAT alias companion validated
- HA import unknown-evidence fails open (arbitrary ack and unparsed ack both complete)
- deferred-Owner replay gate

Fixture fix: `tests_session_hit_authority_9519` ACK-bearing frames hardcoded ack=0; they now carry ack=2 (acking the fixture SYN seq=1). Suite 29/29.

Full-suite note: 83 failures on this branch, reproduced identically on the base head via stash (e.g. `session_decision_typed_snat_layout_11064`, `in_window_rst_valid_blind_rst_invalid_15753`, event-stream golden trailers) — pre-existing, untouched by this change.

## Risk
Only positively-wrong acks are newly refused, and they stay on the opening window. Mid-stream pickups, HA imports, and frame-less callers are byte-identical to before. Hot path: one companion probe on handshake-pending hits / install seeding only; established hits pay one Option check.

- Claimed-only parse errors Pass in both Err arms (no zone-0 event/counter); raw-present #2146 attribution unchanged.
- Replace the false-premise fabric test with poll-stage regressions:
  - `raw_audit_drop_does_not_suppress_enforcing_claimed_veto_16051` — raw lan syn-fin audit + claimed wan syn-fin enforce on SYN|FIN must recycle with the wan DENY event.
  - `claimed_only_cookie_ack_is_not_validated_16051` — a cookie minted under claimed wan is not validated when wan is only claimed (Pass, zero valid/invalid counters/events); the identical ACK under raw wan Validates (live-cookie control).
  - `claimed_only_parse_error_not_attributed_to_zone_zero_16051` — truncated frame with claimed-only profile Passes with zero drops/events.
- `docs/log/16051.md` fold addendum.

## Validation

- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp 16051`: **5/5 pass** at this head (re-verified after rebase onto latest master).
- Fail-on-revert, both actually exercised: restoring the raw-Drop suppression wrapper turns the raw-audit test RED; passing claimed in the raw slot turns the ACK role test RED.

Suite-parallel flakes `arp_two_vlans_same_ip_distinct_logical_keys_2370` / `co_moved_punt_admitted_when_all_data_rgs_local_15916` reproduce on unmodified base in parallel runs and pass in isolation.

## Risk

Raw-present behavior is unchanged. The claimed zone remains stateless-only; it can now only enforce its veto in the previously suppressed audit combination, which is the documented union semantics. No new cookie/flood state is charged to a claimed zone.

## PR #16387 — api: bind REST config-session token to minting principal (#16069) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16069-rest-session-bind`

## Why
The REST config-session token was validated by format only (`restConfigSessionID` checked the `rest-` prefix + 32 hex chars). The store holder was the bare token string and the principal was recorded only for journal attribution, so any equally-privileged insider who obtained another operator's 128-bit token could set, commit, confirm, or release (exit) that operator's candidate. The gRPC twin never had the hole because its holder is the kernel connection identity (`conn-*`). Validated severity Low: attribution/workflow integrity, not privilege gain — the second principal still needs `PermConfig` and commit-time adjudication runs for the committing class.

## What
- `POST /config/enter` records a server-derived binding key (source, UID, username, class/superuser) for the authorized principal alongside the token in a mutex-guarded `Server` map (`restSessions`, lazily allocated so `&Server{store: ...}` fixtures need no setup).
- `restConfigSessionID` (now a `Server` method) verifies on **every** holder-scoped follow-up — enter re-entry, exit, set, delete, activate, deactivate, load, rollback, annotate, commit, commit-confirmed, confirm — that the presenting principal matches the minting principal, denying with **403** before the store is called. A missing principal also fails closed with 403.
- Exit unbinds on successful release; a successful re-enter rebinds so a stale-lease reclaim takeover cannot strand the new holder or keep the old owner working.
- Sessions entered directly in the store (CLI/gRPC/internal/test fixtures) carry no REST binding and remain gated solely by the store holder check, matching the `conn-*` contract.
- Regression test `TestRESTConfigSessionBoundToPrincipal16069`: mints as principal A (credential `alice`, class `ops`), stages, then presents A's token as principal B (`bob`, same class) and requires 403 on set / re-enter / commit / exit with candidate and lock untouched and the commit callback never invoked, while A's own set/re-enter/commit/exit and a freshly minted token behave correctly. Pre-fix every B operation succeeded.
- Fixed `enterRESTConfigSession` test helper to install the authorized principal on fresh enters (the middleware does this in production).
- Changelog entry added.

## Validation
- `go vet ./pkg/api/` — clean.
- `go test ./pkg/api/ -run 'TestRESTConfigSessionBoundToPrincipal16069|TestRESTConfigSessionsAreMutuallyExcluded'` — PASS.
- Full `pkg/api` suite: 23 failures, all verified to fail identically on the unmodified base (`git stash` A/B) — NAT metrics commit-check zone fixtures, a doc-guard path check, and a mutation-guard body-read count. None in the config-session surface.

## Risk
Low. The binding lives only in the REST layer; CLI, gRPC, HA-sync, and internal store callers are untouched. A principal whose identity changes mid-session (credential rotation to a different identity) must re-enter — intended fail-closed behavior. In-memory bindings do not survive a daemon restart, after which tokens are unbound and the store holder check alone gates — the pre-fix posture, not a regression.

Closes #16069

## PR #16388 — config: warn that interactive-commands has no emitter (#16075) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16075-interactive-commands`

## Why

The `interactive-commands` syslog facility is accepted and rendered (mapped to local7 in `pkg/logging`), but no code emits a per-command record to it — there is no slog or syslog producer in CLI dispatch. An operator configuring Junos-style command audit via `interactive-commands` on a syslog host/file/user destination gets an empty file/collector bucket and false assurance that CLI activity is audited. Non-destructive verbs (clear/test/show) are also unjournalled. Validated Low (MGMT-08, unanimous MATERIAL) at master `c1b86e871b`.

## What

`ValidateConfig` (`pkg/config/compiler_validate_warn.go`) now emits one warning per distinct syslog destination (host, file, or user) that names the `interactive-commands` facility, stating that xpf emits no per-command record to the facility (local7), that the destination will receive no CLI audit records, and that the commit journal records commits/destructive actions with principal but does not journal non-destructive verbs.

The warning is warn-only (never a reject), matching the #7146 syslog archive advisory: a hard reject would fail the tolerant load / peer-sync path on a config an operator already has (the #1960 brick-on-upgrade shape). Because `runTailGates` folds `ValidateConfig` into `cfg.Warnings`, the warning reaches both the strict-commit surface (printed by `printConfigWarnings`) and the show/validate surface.

New tests in `pkg/config/syslog_interactive_commands_16075_test.go` pin warnings for file/host/user destinations, once-per-destination dedup when the facility appears in multiple selectors, and silence for other facilities and absent syslog.

NOT changed: no per-command emitter was implemented. A real audit producer would need principal/verb/result plumbing through both the in-process and remote CLI surfaces plus flood control — a feature, not this bounded fix; the issue's fix shape allows either, and the warning is the honest minimum. The commit journal already covers commits and destructive verbs with principal.

## Validation

- `go build ./...` — rc 0
- `go vet ./pkg/config/` — rc 0
- `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 'TestInteractiveCommands|TestSyslog' -count=1` — PASS (5 new cells green)
- Full `pkg/config` suite exceeds the 300s runner cap in this environment; the `TestValidate*` IPsec/NAT failures observed in a filtered run were reproduced identically on the stashed base at `a142c34` (pre-existing, base-attributed).

## Risk

Operators who already configured `interactive-commands` now see one extra commit warning per destination. No dataplane, apply, or rendering behavior changes.

## PR #16389 — config: neutralise shadowed class on api-auth credentials (#16074) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix-16074-api-auth-shadowed-class`

Closes #16074

## Why

The #14387 tolerant-load neutralisation rewrote `system login user` assignments naming a built-in shadowed by a custom class, but missed api-auth users/keys. Their classes (and the api-auth default that legacy `api-key` tokens inherit) kept the shadowed name, and the daemon (`daemon_run_servers.go`) wires them into the REST auth middleware, which resolves classes built-in-first — so under `class super-user { permissions view; }` an api-auth credential held built-in PermAll on tolerant load / peer sync while the authored narrowing never applied.

## What

Extend `neutraliseShadowedLoginAssignments14387` (same tolerant-only call site, gated on `lenientLoginClassShadowsBuiltin`):

- `APIAuthConfig.DefaultClass` naming a shadowed built-in → `unauthorized` (this neutralises legacy `api-key` tokens, which inherit the default at daemon wiring time).
- Every `APIAuthUser` / `APIAuthKey` whose effective class (explicit, or the authored default when empty) names a shadowed built-in → `unauthorized`. The authored default is captured before rewriting so an already-rewritten default cannot mask an explicit shadowed assignment, and no credential is double-warned.
- One warning per neutralised site, tagged #16074, in the #14387 wording shape. Unshadowed classes, the shadowing definition itself, and built-in-first precedence are unchanged. Strict commit still rejects the shadowing definition.

Docs: `docs/system-login.md` paragraph extended, `debian/changelog` entry, `docs/log/16074.md`.

- RED-on-revert: stashing the `compiler_system_login_gates.go` fix makes the decisive, explicit-class, and per-node tests fail with classes staying `super-user`.
- Full `go test ./pkg/config/` — one pre-existing failure (`TestZoneInterfaceDistinctUnitsAcrossZonesNotFlagged`, #15034 zone gate) that fails identically on unmodified `origin/master`; verified by stash.
- `gofmt` clean on touched files; `go vet ./pkg/config/` clean.

## Risk

Tolerant load / peer-sync only; strict commit behaviour unchanged. Unshadowed api-auth classes untouched; built-in-first precedence unchanged.

## PR #16390 — config: gate CommitCheck on the config-lock holder (#16070) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16070-holderless-commitcheck`

## Issue
Closes #16070 (A8-10 from #15987)

## Why
`CommitCheck` on both surfaces ran with no holder check: gRPC discarded its context (`_ context.Context`), REST ignored the request entirely (`_ *http.Request`), and `Store.CommitCheck` compiled the shared candidate under `RLock` with no holder parameter or admission limiter. Any PermConfig non-holder could obtain compile diagnostics about another session's staged candidate and trigger repeatable full compiles (CPU) at will.

## What
- **pkg/configstore**: `CommitCheckAs(sessionID)` verifies the config-lock holder via `ensureHolderLocked` under the read lock before any compile — a non-holder gets `ErrConfigLockedByOther` with no diagnostics leak and no compile cost. Every form takes the single-slot fail-fast `commitCheckSem` admission semaphore; a second concurrent check returns `ErrCommitCheckBusy` instead of queueing another full compile. `CommitCheck()` remains the internal/system form (`""` bypass, admission still bounded) for the in-process CLI and the event engine, which holds the lock itself.
- **pkg/grpcapi**: `CommitCheck` passes `connSessionID(ctx)` to `CommitCheckAs`; `configMutationStatus` maps `ErrCommitCheckBusy` → `codes.ResourceExhausted` (holder conflict stays `PermissionDenied`).
- **pkg/api**: `configCommitCheckHandler` requires the `X-Config-Session` header via `restConfigSessionID` (missing/malformed → 400 before the store, closing the `""` internal bypass), passes the holder identity to `CommitCheckAs`; `writeConfigMutationError` maps busy → 429, holder conflict → 409. Compile diagnostics (400) still reach the holder.
- The #9889 candidate-reading census guard now names `CommitCheckAs`.

## Validation
- New RED-on-revert pins: `pkg/configstore/commit_check_holder_16070_test.go` (non-holder/holder/internal + busy slot), `pkg/grpcapi/commit_check_holder_16070_test.go` (PermissionDenied / ResourceExhausted), `pkg/api/commit_check_holder_16070_test.go` (missing header 400, non-holder 409 with no leak, holder 200 + real ebpf diagnostic only for the holder).
- Full `pkg/grpcapi` (incl. #9889 census, #6515/#8484 advisory) and `pkg/api` suites pass; focused `pkg/configstore`/`pkg/cli`/`cmd/cli` suites pass; `-race` on the new admission paths passes; `go vet` clean.
- The pre-existing REST commit-check ebpf test now supplies a well-formed session header (its candidate is held by the internal no-holder enter, admitted via the documented no-holder bypass).

## Risk
Fail-closed only: non-holders lose diagnostics they should never have had, and a second concurrent commit-check gets a retryable busy error instead of a queued compile. Admitted callers' response shapes are unchanged.

## PR #16391 — daemon: re-resolve console login class on config change (#16071) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16071`

Closes #16071

## Why
`applyCLILoginClass` ran exactly once at daemon start, so the in-process console's user→class **assignment** went stale until restart — while class *definitions* were already re-read per command (`resolveClassPerms` reads `ActiveConfig()` every call) and remote surfaces resolve per-connection server-side. Revoking or changing a console user's class lagged until restart: the same revocation-lag class #9051 fixed for streams.

## What
- `pkg/daemon/cli_rbac.go`: new `consoleClassRefresher` — compares only the `system login` projection (`LoginConfig` pointer + `LoginDroppedByPacking`) against the seeded startup projection and re-runs the shared `applyCLILoginClass` resolution when it changes. Covers: re-class, user removal (→ `unauthorized`), first login stanza appearing, stanza removed (→ back to unset legacy mode), dropped-by-packing (fail-closed re-resolution). Unrelated applies are a no-op (no re-log spam).
- `pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go`: wires the refresher via `shell.SetRefreshUserClassFn(consoleClassRefresher(shell, d.store.ActiveConfig, osident.Current()))` right after the startup resolution.
- `pkg/cli`: `userClass` is now mutex-guarded; `UserClass()` is the sole read path (it can change while commands dispatch). `SetRefreshUserClassFn` + dispatch/completion-entry refresh hook (no-op when unwired, so standalone/test shells are unchanged).
- Canaries updated: `allowedSetUserClassCallers` gains `daemon::consoleClassRefresher` (required entry); the shared-resolver canary accepts the delegated shape (delegates to `applyCLILoginClass`, only direct write is the empty-class clear); the #6706 wiring test now pins exactly two `applyCLILoginClass` sites, both fed by `osident.Current()`.
- Docs: `docs/system-login.md` console section + `debian/changelog`.

## Validation
- New `TestConsoleClassRefresher16071` (7 rows: revoked / re-classed / first-stanza / stanza-removed / dropped-by-packing / unrelated-apply-no-op / no-login-never-set) + nil-active guard — passes, including under `-race`.
- Existing `TestApplyCLILoginClass*`, `TestConsoleLoginClassIsWiredToOsidentCurrent_6706`, `TestSetUserClassHasOneProductionCaller_6701`, `TestSetUserClassCallersResolveThroughTheSharedResolver_6701` pass; `go vet ./pkg/cli/ ./pkg/daemon/` clean.
- Full `go test -tags=unit ./pkg/cli/ ./pkg/daemon/`: remaining failures are pre-existing on `origin/master` (verified against a pristine base worktree; identical failure sets apart from timing).

## Risk
A console user revoked mid-session loses access on their next command (the intended behavior). Deployments with no `system login` stanza are byte-identical — the class is never set. Refresh cost is one projection comparison per dispatch; no per-command config walk.

## PR #16392 — config: warn on inert user root authentication (#16076) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16076-root-auth-warning`

Refs #16076

## Why
`system login user root { authentication … }` compiled silently but was inert: the daemon never applies root credentials from a `login user` stanza (applySystemLogin and the sudoers sweep skip root; root credentials come only from `system root-authentication` via applyRootAuth). docs/system-login.md called `user root authentication ssh-ed25519` 'an ordinary way to give root a key', so an operator could believe root was key-locked when it was not (false assurance / lockout class, Low).

## What
- `pkg/config/compiler_system.go`: emit a `cfg.Warnings` entry naming `system root-authentication` whenever `user root` carries an authored `authentication` child. Keyed on authored presence (not compiled values — the fold resets EncryptedPassword before reading children), so braced, flat-set, empty-auth, and sibling-block spellings all warn on both strict and tolerant compile paths. Warning-only; no compiled values or daemon behaviour change, and the stanza is deliberately NOT folded into RootAuthentication.
- `docs/system-login.md`: new 'Root credentials: use system root-authentication, not user root' section; corrected the uid-0 paragraph that called the inert spelling an ordinary way to give root a key. `user root class` remains honoured and does not warn.
- `pkg/config/compiler_root_auth_16076_test.go`: 7 positive cells (braced ssh/pw/empty auth, flat-set ssh/pw, auth beside class, sibling blocks) across strict+lenient, asserting the warning names root-authentication, says ignored, and that RootAuthentication stays nil; 5 quiet controls (root class-only, uid-only, no children, non-root auth, real root-authentication stanza).
- `debian/changelog`: entry.

## Validation
- `go test ./pkg/config/ -run 16076 -count=1` PASS (all subtests).
- RED-on-revert: stashing compiler_system.go makes all positive cells FAIL (no warning names root-authentication); controls stay quiet.
- Broader `-run 'Login|RootAuth'`: two failures (TestLoginPathPackedDoesNotOverReach_6706, TestGrantingSystemLoginDoesNotWarn_6972) reproduce identically on pristine origin/master — pre-existing, unrelated.

## Risk
Warning-only change. Previously silent commits now surface a warning at commit-check and on tolerant load/peer-sync. No change to compiled config values, daemon apply, sudo, or RBAC/class resolution.

Its corpus building, matrix cells, sorting, serialization, and compare/mismatch diagnostics are untouched; only `GOLDEN_4406_UPDATE=1` becomes `-update`.
- **Format package migrated first, atomically in the same change** (the flag-redeclaration hazard from the issue): `status_golden_test.go` deletes `var updateGolden = flag.Bool("update", ...)` while `status`/`cos`/`buffers` goldens switch to `testgolden.String(t, "testdata/<name>.golden", got)`. The non-golden #10500 subtract-lines byte test still reads the status baseline directly — it is not a compare-or-write tail.
- **Self-tests** `internal/testgolden/testgolden_test.go`: equal-compare passes; mismatch is fatal and names path, got, want, and `-update`; missing file is fatal and names path + `-update`; update mode writes exact headerless bytes into a nested path (proving `MkdirAll`).

Scope notes: `testgolden.JSON`/`.Lines`, `t.Name()` paths, a header line, and a `-update-golden` flag are all explicitly out (rejected in validation). Ratchet-txt readers in `pkg/config` are left alone — the issue scopes "format package first, then the 4406 tail", and those readers have split/compare semantics, not the string compare-or-write tail.

## Validation

- `go test ./internal/testgolden/` PASS; `go vet` clean on testgolden/format/config; `gofmt -l` clean.
- Format goldens PASS in compare mode: `TestFormatCoSInterfaceSummaryGolden`, `TestFormatStatusSummaryGolden`, `TestFormatSystemBuffersGolden`, plus `TestFormatStatusSummaryRejectReasonsAbsentByteCompare10500`.
- **Forced-regen-clean oracle (format leg):** `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/format/ -run Golden -update` leaves `git status` clean for all three `testdata/*.golden` files.
- **Corrupt-one-baseline goes red:** appending `CORRUPTED` to `cos_summary.golden` fails `TestFormatCoSInterfaceSummaryGolden` with got/want shown; baseline restored byte-exact.
- **No duplicate `-update` registration:** tree census — `flag.Bool("update", ...)` only in `internal/testgolden`; `updateGolden` symbol and `GOLDEN_4406_UPDATE` code gate gone.
- **4406 `-update` path:** writes the baseline; a second `-update` is byte-identical (idempotent regen).

## Risk

## PR #16407 — config: share three config-lifecycle helpers only (#16156) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `u16156-config-helpers`

Closes #16156.

## Why
The confirm-only branch (`IsConfirmPending() && !IsDirty()`) was triplicated across gRPC (`pkg/grpcapi/server_config.go`), REST (`pkg/api/config.go`) and local CLI (`pkg/cli/cli_config.go`); the REST commit-error classifier mirrored the gRPC `commitApplyStatus` by hand (#5742/#15281); and `cfg.Warnings` extraction was open-coded in three places. A fix on one surface could silently diverge on the others.

## What
Exactly three shared helpers in `pkg/configstore` (`commit_helpers_16156.go`), per the narrowed W2.5 form validated in #16156:

- `Store.ConfirmOnly()` — the pure confirm-only predicate (confirm-pending && candidate unchanged). Pure strengthening: both flags are now read under **one** store lock hold instead of two separate RLock holds, so a concurrent edit can no longer land between the reads and route a dirty candidate into the confirm-only branch (the #4000 silent-drop hazard). No authority is minted; each surface keeps its own `ConfirmCommitAs` call.
- `ClassifyCommitError(compiled, err)` — the structural (compiled, err) commit-error class (`Canceled` / `DeadlineExceeded` first, then committed-tail vs rejected, fail-safe to rejected). gRPC `commitApplyStatus` and REST `writeCommitError` now only map the shared class onto their own wire codes/envelopes; human-readable text is byte-identical.
- `WarningsOf(cfg)` — nil-safe defensive-copy extraction of `cfg.Warnings`, replacing grpcapi `configWarnings` (deleted) and both open-coded copies in pkg/api.

Explicitly **not** done (per the B-codex dissent adopted in #16156): no `configops.Service`, no three-surface `CommitGate(store, session) -> authority`. REST/gRPC still mint holder-epoch authority via `AuthorizeCommitAs` before the gate; the local CLI still commits authority-free with its possibly-empty internal session — that path is untouched.

## Acceptance (issue decisive check)
- 12-cell table: `TestConfirmOnly16156` pins confirm-pending × dirty at the store; per-surface cells (`TestRESTBareCommitConfirmOnly16156`, `TestGRPCBareCommitConfirmOnly16156`, existing CLI `TestBareCommitDuringConfirmWindow*_4000`) pin confirm-only vs fall-through commit per surface. CLI authority-free path is unchanged (predicate only).
- Classifier differential REST-vs-gRPC over the #5742 corpus: both surfaces now consume the single `ClassifyCommitError`; the existing `TestCommitErrorClassification_5742` (gRPC) and `TestRESTCommitErrorClassification_15281` (REST) corpora stay green, plus `TestClassifyCommitError16156` pins the shared classifier directly including context-beats-config precedence.
- Byte-identical operator output: no wire code, message, or printed text changes (classifier/warnings helpers only move the shared logic).

## Validation
- New: `TestConfirmOnly16156`, `TestClassifyCommitError16156`, `TestWarningsOf16156`, `TestRESTBareCommitConfirmOnly16156`, `TestRESTCommitResponseWarnings16156`, `TestGRPCBareCommitConfirmOnly16156` — all pass.
- Mutant-checked: dropping the dirty conjunct from `ConfirmOnly` reds the new cells.
- Existing suites green: 5742/15281 classifier, 4000 confirm-window (configstore + CLI), 6515/8484/9841 warnings transport. `go vet` clean on the four touched packages.
- Note: `Test9880_StrictCommitAcceptsValuedModifiers` (pkg/configstore) fails identically on clean `origin/master` — pre-existing, unrelated.

## Risk
Low. Pure refactor onto shared helpers; the only semantic delta is the atomic single-lock confirm predicate, which strictly narrows the #4000 race. Fail-safe preserved: unclassifiable commit errors still classify as rejected (400 / InvalidArgument), never committed/retryable.

## PR #16463 — userspace-dp: route activation-pending HA sets to the locked path (#16382) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `wt-16382`

Refs #16382. The #16217 fabric-adoption stack this was diagnosed alongside remains open/unmerged; this is the standalone #16382 lease-publication leg on current master.

Why: live D31 instrumentation at the adoption gate showed the servicing workers' cached RG1 triple stuck at (active=false, lease=Inactive) with the fresh forwarding_active_rgs set EMPTY for seconds after RG1 reported active in the status view. Root cause is in try_refresh_ha_leases: for a mixed watchdog set (siblings matching, one RG activation-pending stored-inactive/incoming-active) the pending RG was kept inactive but the whole set still stored with refreshed>0, so the activation was neither published by the locked path (no epoch bump, RefreshOwnerRGS, prewarm) nor servable later.

What: try_refresh_ha_leases now returns NeedsLock for the whole set whenever any RG is activation-pending (stored inactive, incoming active), regardless of sibling matches - exactly the routing the pure-activation case (refreshed==0) already had. Activations are therefore published only by Coordinator::update_ha_state with its transition side effects, and no later tick can launder a pending activation into a match-arm lease mint. Demotion arms unchanged: stored-active mismatch still mints only while the stored lease is valid, expired stored-active is never resurrected.

Validation: new mixed_set_activation_pending_needs_lock_16382 (mixed RG0/RG1/RG2 set routes NeedsLock twice, RG1 never mints; FAIL-ON-REVERT) and mixed_set_no_activation_still_served_16382 control; cargo test 16382 2/2, 9629 29/29. Live aged P4 acceptance NOT re-run for this standalone commit; it remains the #16217 lane's gate (the same fix plus Wire30 still failed live there, residual narrowed to the per-worker snapshot visibility race - this fix removes the fast-path laundering, it does not by itself claim the aged-failover cure).

Risk: watchdog sets containing a pending activation now take the control socket until the locked path lands the transition; steady-state matching sets stay on the session fast path (control test). This deliberately trades one throttled control round-trip for fail-closed activation publication.

## PR #16808 — build: add Stage-A test-only import loader for script tests (#16194) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `lk-16194-stage-a-loader`

## Summary

Stage-A only (#16194): one test-only `load_subject(name, path)` helper in `scripts/lib/load_subject.py` replaces the repeated `spec_from_file_location` scaffolding in script tests. NO packages, NO shims, NO Stage-B — production CLI files stay hyphenated files at their original paths, and `__file__`-derived roots do not move.

- **Helper** (`scripts/lib/load_subject.py`, 57 lines): creates the spec, registers the module in `sys.modules` **before** executing it (so `dataclasses` string-annotation resolution and self-imports work, and `sys.modules[name] is <returned module>`), removes that registration and restores any prior entry if execution raises (exception propagates unchanged), and raises `ImportError` on a missing/unloadable file instead of the old `FileNotFoundError`-from-exec / loader-`None` assert shapes.
- **Migration**: all 82 loader users migrated — `scripts/deploy` (27), `scripts/dist` (12), `scripts/image` (37 incl. two in-method loads), `scripts/test_*.py` (5), `test/incus/*_test.py` (11). The three files that hand-registered for dataclass subjects (`test_close_keyword_lint.py`, `test_cut_stall_analyze.py`, `test_skill_file_push_lint.py`) and the three registered `test/incus` files now get registration from the helper; every other subject gains the same guarantee before it can grow a dataclass. Zero `spec_from_file_location` call sites remain outside the helper.
- **Helper cells** (`scripts/lib/test_load_subject.py`, 9 cells): hyphenated load + identity, dataclass subject, self-import, exec-failure propagation + cleanup, prior-registration restore, missing-file `ImportError`, repeat-load replacement, fresh `-I` interpreter loading the real `close_keyword_lint` dataclass subject (per-file process isolation, as `run-selftests.sh` runs them), and original CLI invocation of a hyphenated subject by path in a subprocess.
- **Gate wiring**: `scripts/lib/test_*.py` added to `run-selftests.sh` §3, `selftest-census.sh` `PY_GLOBS` (+ its fixture in `selftest-census-selftest.sh`), and the #9669 main-guard scan — so the new test cannot accumulate unreached the way #7296/#15241 files did.
- Changelog entry. Net: 635 insertions / 581 deletions across 90 files (tracked test files alone: −168 lines net after the per-file 2-line bootstrap; the helper + its cells are new).

## Validation

- All 82 migrated test files executed: **80 pass**; the 2 failures are pre-existing and **identical on unmodified base `6235ac734e`** (verified in a detached base worktree): `scripts/dist/test_dist_resign_9920.py` (`test_all_cargo_recipes_use_pinned_toolchain`, 1 cell) and `test/incus/fairness_multi_sample_test.py` (3 harness-precheck cells). Neither touches a loader path.
- `scripts/lib/test_load_subject.py`: 9/9 pass. Confirmed the registration is load-bearing: loading `close_keyword_lint.py` without registration raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute '__dict__'`; with the helper it loads.
- `scripts/selftest-census.sh` passes (95 python files guarded, all tracked `scripts/*test*.py` covered); `test/incus/selftest-census-selftest.sh` 24/24; `test_selftest_main_guard_9669.py` and `test_selftest_lint_coverage_6499.py` pass; `git diff --check` clean; all touched files byte-compile.

Test-only, zero product risk. The proposed `genGuard` struct name was **not** used: it collides with the #9915 cap counters `genGuardMapCap`/`genGuardMapDefaultCap`/`genGuardSessionCap`, which keep their names. The domains are `sessionGenState` (field `genState`) and `peerSnapshotState` (field `peerSnaps`), pinned by an AST test that no cluster type is named `genGuard*`.

## What moved
- `sessionGenState`: `genCounter`, `genSentMu`+sender stamps/scoped/overflow, `sentGenGuardCap`/`recvGenGuardCap`/`genGuardSessionCap`/`genGuardMapCeilingOverride`/`testGenCapAfterCeilingRead`, sent+recv identity memos, `recvGenMu`+receiver maps/scoped/tombstone orders.
- `peerSnapshotState`: `peerIPsecSAs(Mu)`, `peerDHCPLeases{4,6}` + snapshots + `RecvAt` + `peerDHCPLeasesMu`, and the #6650 `peerSnapshotProtocol`/`peerSnapshotProtocolWriteMu`/`peerSnapshotProtocolGeneration` triple.
- Both are **value** fields (not pointers): ~98 bare `SessionSync{` literals never run a constructor, so a pointer would be nil there; a value field is zero-ready with no lazy-init branch and no allocation/copy change (maps still allocated by `initGenState`).

Added the lock-order graph on `SessionSync` in `sync.go`: every mutex, its guard domain, every nesting edge (`bulkSnapshotGenMu -> genSentMu -> recvGenMu`, `applyMu -> recvGenMu`, `mu -> peerSnapshotProtocolWriteMu/fenceAckMu`, full-set `*ApplyMu -> recvSeqMu -> peerDHCPLeasesMu`, leaf locks, atomics), pinned by `TestSessionSyncLockOrderGraphPinned16159` so it cannot rot silently.

## PR #16883 — frr: restore per-QNH RIP metrics via offset-lists (#12531) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/12531-campaign`

Why:
RIP received only its default metric for QNH-redistributed routes while OSPF got the configured per-next-hop metric. FRR 10.7.1 offers no working ripd route-map transport: daemon-scoped `vtysh -d ripd -f` silently applies nothing, integrated loads broadcast the set-metric action to other daemons, and ripd ignores route-map `set metric` for redistributed statics even when present (live-verified: map readback metric 7, RIP database and RIPv2 wire metric 1).

What:
Deliver the RIP QNH metric with ripd-native offset-lists inside the integrated `router rip` stanza: one offset-list (offset = metric-1, clamped to wire metric 16; metric 0 renders none) per QNH destination, selected by a generated `xpf-qnh-rip-*` access-list that permits exactly that destination. ACL definitions render beside the QNH prefix-lists, gated on a bare-static RIP export in the scope; policy-exported RIP keeps authored policy semantics. OSPF overlay, shared metric-free QNH map, and cleanup are unchanged. Deliberate scope cut: no next-hop/interface discrimination in RIP (offset-lists cannot express it; lowest metric per destination wins).

Validation:
- New `rip_qnh_metric_12531_test.go` (7 tests): RED before (undefined ACL helper), GREEN after; #12071-era RIP warning test updated to pin restored behavior.
- Targeted QNH/RIP/redistribute suites pass; full `pkg/frr` passes except 4 failures base-attributed on origin/master (TestBGPNoExportNeighborGetsDefaultExport15157, TestFamilylessIPv6NeighborWithoutPolicyIsV6Only11564, TestFRRLoadInet6OnlyNeighborIPv4Deactivation11374, TestFRRLoadBGPClasslessRIBSuppression11426); `go vet` clean.
- Live FRR 10.7.1 netns: integrated config carries offset-list + ACL, ospfd has no set-metric copy, OSPF LSA metric stays 20, RIPv2 wire carries metric 10 for the QNH prefix.

Risk:
RIP database still displays metric 1 (offset applies on egress); operators read the wire/peer view. Metrics above 16 advertise as unreachable in RIP. Destination-only keying collapses multiple backups of one prefix to the lowest metric in RIP.

Refs #12531

## PR #16887 — userspace-xdp: remove disposition-dead GRE inner lookups (#16241) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

userspace-xdp: remove disposition-dead GRE inner lookups (#16241)

Refs #16241
Refs #16695

## Why

PR #16264 delivered #16241's narrowed acceptance (per-arm branch hit
counters + fail-closed analysis) and proved no dispatch arm is
disposition-identical/removable. The three-way-validated residual
#16695 then found disposition-dead work *inside* the native-GRE arm:
on an inner session miss, `classify_native_gre_inner_ipv4`/`_ipv6` ran
up to five further hash lookups (DNAT exact+wildcard, interface-NAT,
local) returning `REDIRECT`-or-`0`. Both consumers act only on
`PASS_TO_KERNEL` (healthy arm plus local-outer gate; degraded twin via
`InnerSessionAction`), so `REDIRECT` and miss are indistinguishable —
the lookups could never change any disposition, only spend per-packet
work and verifier budget, while their comments described a steering
role that does not exist.

  directly; `dnat_lookup_v4`/`v6` and the unused `ingress_domain`
  plumbing are deleted. Comments rewritten to state the true contract:
  inner classification decides only the `PASS_TO_KERNEL` case; a miss
  stays on the helper path where the worker adjudicates the inner
  packet (including DNAT/local) itself.
- The `dnat_table`/`dnat_table_v6` map *declarations* are deliberately
  retained — the Go loader replaces them with the pinned
  dataplane-owned tables and validates their shape; deleting them
  would break shim loading, not remove dead code.
- Regenerated shim object + gate verdict + manifest.
- Tests: structural pin for the removal, retained-declaration pin, and
  BPF_PROG_TEST_RUN disposition cells (new file

## PR #16891 — vrrp: keep VID-0 priority-tagged native adverts (#16426) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16426-vrrp-vid0-priority-tag`

Refs #16426

## Why

`receiverAfPacket` dropped any frame whose `PACKET_AUXDATA` carried
`TP_STATUS_VLAN_VALID` on a non-VLAN netdev, without testing the VID
(#15049 regression). A priority-tagged peer advert (VID 0, PCP 6,
TCI `0xC000`) is stripped into skb metadata with `VLAN_VALID` set
exactly like a VLAN-100 advert, so the backup never heard the master,
its master-down timer expired, and both nodes held the VIP (dual
MASTER, ARP flapping). Linux treats VID 0 as native; only a non-zero
VID marks a frame as belonging to a VLAN sub-interface.

## What

- `pkg/vrrp/instance_receive.go`: gate the parent drop on a non-zero
  VID (`tagged && tci&0x0fff != 0`, masking PCP/DEI bits); update the
  `receiverAfPacket` contract comment.
- `pkg/vrrp/vlan_tag_present_15049_test.go`: add `hasAuxdata` to
  `vlanDelivery` and make `auxdataOOB` always encode `VLAN_VALID` so
  VID-0 deliveries are expressible (TCI 0 was previously conflated
  with "no auxdata"); new acceptance test
  `TestReceiverAfPacketParentKeepsVID0PriorityTaggedAdvert_16426`
  (PCP6/VID0 `0xC000` enqueues, TCI-0+VLAN_VALID enqueues, VLAN-100
  still drops) plus parser pins for VID-0 TCIs.
- `pkg/vrrp/README.md`, `docs/log/16426.md`: contract + action log.

NOT changed: the optional "only when the parent actually has tagged
VRRP siblings" refinement — the VID mask alone restores the #15049
contract and VID-N frames still drop unconditionally.

## Validation

- New test RED pre-fix (`parent received []` — both VID-0 adverts
  dropped), GREEN with fix.
- Targeted: `go test ./pkg/vrrp/ -run 'TestReceiverAfPacket|TestAfPacketAuxdata' -count=1` — 5 tests pass (incl. pre-existing #15049/#6560 cells); `go vet ./pkg/vrrp/` clean; gofmt clean.
- Full `go test ./pkg/vrrp/ -count=1`: one failure,
  `TestRethOwnershipCollectorsUseTheSharedPredicate/RethVIPsForRG`,
  verified pre-existing on clean `origin/master@ce4445ddcb` via stash
  check, unrelated to this change.

## Risk

Fail-open direction unchanged for VID-N (still drops) and for
missing/invalid auxdata. Kernel cmsg contents are synthesized from
the af_packet ABI, not captured from a NIC (same limit as the #15049
harness). Lab verification on a priority-tagging L2 path remains
outstanding.

## PR #16892 — userspace-dp: fix fixture pkt_len to full frame length and harden #6883 guard (#16444) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

## Diagnosis (assertion proven correct, fixtures wrong)
`pkt_len` is the length of the buffer the meta describes from offset 0 (`types/mod.rs` #8581 contract; shim `packet_len = data_end - data`; `logical_ingress.rs` #8581 invariant tests; `tx/cos_classify.rs:151 packet_bytes = meta.pkt_len`, `flow_cache.rs observed_bytes = u64::from(meta.pkt_len)`). So `frame.len() - 14` fixtures were 14 bytes short — the guard assertion was not weakened.

At base the guard was red only on `resolver_enqueue_tests.rs:228`, and blind to 12 listed sites plus more found in-tree: `txn_meta_v6`, `gre_to_self_outer_meta{,_v6}` (`- l3`, VLAN-aware 14/18), GRE frag overwrites, `poll_stages_tests` VLAN meta (`- l3`), and 40 `txn_meta_v4(.., (len - 14) as u16)` call sites (the helper stores its 3rd arg verbatim into `pkt_len`) — all fixed to stamp the full buffer length. GRE "deliberate L3 length" hypothesis checked and rejected: those metas have `l3_offset: 14/18` over full Ethernet frames.

## Guard hardening
Replaces the 3 literal sinks with a comment-stripped scan flagging any `pkt_len` field/assignment value or `txn_meta_v4` 3rd argument containing `-14`/`-l3`/`saturating_sub(14)`; non-`pkt_len` wire-length invariants (IPv4 total / IPv6 payload length, e.g. `tests_mss_inject_inspect.rs`) stay legal. Stale "nothing gates on pkt_len" header corrected.

## Validation
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp fixture_pkt_len_is_the_full_frame_length_6883`: **ok, 1 passed** on fixed tree (at base it printed 1 site: resolver_enqueue_tests.rs:228).
- Real-Rust mutations reintroducing `(frame_len - 14)`, `frame.len() as u16 - 14`, `(inner.len() - 14)`, and `txn_meta_v4(.., (len - 14))`: each **FAILED (red)**, restored tree green.
- Targeted modules (gre frag/pool/transit, embedded poll filter, poll stages, native GRE ECN, resolver enqueue, txn flow cache): 249 passed, 1 failed — `stage11_local_ike_passthrough_honors_ingress_input_filter_13637`, which **also fails alone at base** (pre-existing; along with 20 nat64/gre-local-delivery failures identical before/after).

## PR #16898 — feeds: restore legacy epoch sets without epoch_hash (#16427) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16427-restore-legacy-epoch`

Refs #16427

## Summary
`RestoreShrinkHighWater` required `digest == Hash` for durable records without `epoch_hash` (written before #15075). A legacy epoch whose count high-water had already rotated was therefore dropped on the first post-upgrade restart, and a wholesale same-count content swap of an enforced feed installed with no refusal — a regression versus the #14994 restore (R3-F05-07).

## Fix
For records without `EpochHash`, restore any canonical `Prefixes` set within the cap (the #14994 acceptance). The legacy `Prefixes` field was the epoch set and no epoch digest (and no MAC) was persisted to validate against, so the equality added no integrity and dropped exactly the rotated epochs. The restored set's own digest becomes the epoch hash, so the next snapshot persists it under `epoch_hash`. Records with a present `EpochHash` still must match it; non-canonical sets still drop fail-closed with the count epoch restored.

## Tests
- New `TestLegacyEpochWithoutEpochHashRestoresRotatedEpoch16427`: RED pre-fix (legacy record restored 0 epoch prefixes), GREEN post-fix (restores 100, identical set installs as control, disjoint equal-count swap refused and installs on exact ack).
- New `TestLegacyNonCanonicalEpochDropped16427`: pins the canonical bound for legacy records.
- Targeted `16427|15075|14994` run: 10/10 pass. Full `pkg/feeds` suite passes; `gofmt`/`go vet` clean.

## Risk
Scoped to the legacy restore leg. Corrupt-`EpochHash` fail-closed behaviour, thresholds, ack tuple, and true bootstrap are unchanged. The install-side epoch re-bootstrap for count-only records is #16651 (R3-A50-02), a separate fix site.

## PR #16899 — dhcp: reject non-granting REBIND replacement by omission (#16423) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16423-campaign`

Why:
The #14997 REBIND gate tested only teardown content (non-Success
status, valid-lifetime 0), so a non-granting on-link responder could
omit the held IA_NA address, offer a different live one, pass as a
pure extension, and have commitLease remove the held WAN address in
one packet (R3-F04-05). RFC 8415 18.2.10.1 leaves an omitted held
lease unchanged and adds only new leases; omission-plus-replacement
is neither, and the same shape abandoned every held IA_PD prefix.

What:
Extend v6ReplyTearsDownHeldBinding in pkg/dhcp/renew.go: for each
requested IA, read the held elements from the request echo and treat
a matched Reply IA that offers a live element but keeps none of the
held ones as teardown, reusing the DHCPv6TeardownRejects counter.
Silence on an IA and held-plus-new additions remain extensions.
Granting-server replacement, parse, reconcile, commitLease, the run
loop, and DHCPv4 are unchanged. Docs: pkg/dhcp/README.md bullet,
RenewalBindingStats comment, docs/log/16423.md.

Validation:
New TestV6RebindNonGrantingReplacementRejected16423 cells:
replace-IA_NA-only and replace-IA_PD-only rejected (counter 1),
granting replacement and held-plus-new/silent partner extensions
accepted. RED on revert of renew.go (both replacement cells
accepted, counter 0). Full go test ./pkg/dhcp/ -count=1 PASS;
go vet clean; gofmt and git diff --check clean.

Risk:
A failover partner that holds the binding but echoes no held element
is now ignored until it extends or the lease expires into Solicit,
the RFC 8415 18.2.10 posture already taken for NoBinding. The
deliberate #14600 handoff (an accepted extension becomes the next
RENEW binding) is unchanged and remains the documented limit.

## PR #16900 — daemon: restore prior faillock rules on SSH apply rollback (#16421) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16421-campaign`

Why:
The #14973 rollback stripped every managed pam_faillock block when a failed `applySSHConfig` had changed common-auth. On the upgrade transition that change merely rewrites the pre-#14973 legacy rules the host already had (no `even_deny_root`), so a failed first post-upgrade SSH apply (sshd -t, reload, drop-in write, or config render failure) left a non-appliance host with no SSH password lockout at all — less protection than before the apply, with nothing in the apply error mentioning the PAM state.

What:
`applySSHPAMFaillockChanged`/`setSSHPAMFaillock` now also return the exact pre-apply common-auth bytes alongside the changed flag. `applySSHConfig` captures them and its deferred rollback (`restoreSSHPAMFaillockOnRollback`, replacing `stripSSHPAMFaillockOnRollback`) restores the prior bytes verbatim — the same posture as `revertDropIn` for the sshd drop-in — falling back to the old strip only when no bytes were captured. A fresh install from stock therefore still ends at stock, and a legacy upgrade ends back at the original 3 legacy lines. NOT changed: install/upgrade rendering, the tamper refusal, the appliance skip, or the #15229 advisory-failure posture.

Validation:
- New `TestApplySSHConfigRollbackRestoresPriorFaillock16421` (6 subtests) RED pre-fix (all 4 legacy failure rows ended at bare stock with 0 faillock lines; stock-rollback and legacy-success controls passed), GREEN post-fix with byte-exact prior restore.
- Existing #14973 stock rollback tests, #11492 install/idempotence and #15229 tuned-block suites stay green (22 faillock-related tests); `TestApplySSHConfig` suite green; `go vet ./pkg/daemon/` and gofmt clean.

Risk:
A failed SSH apply now rewrites common-auth once more with the captured prior bytes instead of a strip render; if that restore write itself fails it is logged and joined into the apply error, never masking the original failure. Hosts with admin-installed faillock, appliance hosts, and unsupported PAM stacks are untouched. No wire/config-schema change.

## PR #16908 — userspace: ignore SIGHUP in helper (#16431) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16431-helper-sighup`

Refs #16431

## Why
#15084 made xpfd ignore SIGHUP, but the Rust helper kept the default disposition: xpfd's `signal.Notify` capture is a caught disposition that resets to SIG_DFL across exec, so `systemctl kill -s HUP xpfd` (delivered to every unit process) killed `xpf-userspace-dp`, failed transit closed, and forced a supervisor backoff respawn with rebuilt per-worker state.

## What
- `userspace-dp/src/server/lifecycle.rs`: install SIG_IGN for SIGHUP via `libc::signal` at the very top of `run()`, before workers/socket threads spawn; log posture at startup. SIG_IGN discards HUP in-kernel without touching `running`; deliberately NOT ctrlc's `termination` feature (would route HUP to graceful exit = still outage). SIGINT/ctrlc and shutdown-verb semantics unchanged; bare SIGTERM disposition unchanged (out of scope, Go sends shutdown verb first).
- `userspace-dp/tests/sighup_16431.rs`: blackbox cells spawning the real binary (`CARGO_BIN_EXE_xpf-userspace-dp`), real SIGHUP x3 with ping before/after, plus shutdown-verb exit-0.
- Changelog + `userspace-dp/src/server/README.md`.

## Validation
- `cargo test --test sighup_16431`: 2 passed.
- Mutant (removed `ignore_sighup()?` call): SIGHUP cell RED (child dies by Hangup); restored GREEN.
- Lifecycle unit filters: accept_step 9 passed, peer_uid 2 passed.
- Full bin suite (>9k tests) exceeded 300s window without observed failure; not run to completion.

## Risk
Low: one disposition set once at startup, fail-fast on SIG_ERR; no hot-path change. Helper ignores HUP even hand-run, matching xpfd's no-reload-on-HUP posture.

## PR #16918 — image: decouple ssh host-key regeneration from day-0 loader (#16445) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `feat/16445-ssh-hostkey-regen`

Refs #16445

## Why
A zeroize writes its pending marker at the day-0 stamp path (`/etc/xpf/.day0-config-applied`) before the seal leg erases `/etc/ssh/ssh_host_*` and rotates the machine-id. Any later leg failure or power loss left a boot where the stamp-gated `xpf-day0-config` unit — the only xpf `ssh-keygen -A` path — was condition-skipped, and Ubuntu's `ConditionFirstBoot` sshd-keygen was defeated by the fresh real machine-id. `sshd -t` then failed and the box was console-only.

## What
- New `xpf-ssh-hostkeys.service`: `ssh-keygen -A` `Before=ssh.service`, gated only on host-key absence (`ConditionPathExists=!/etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key`) — never on the day-0 stamp, first-boot, or machine-id.
- Staged + enabled by both `debian/rules` (dh_installsystemd, clean list, .gitignore) and `bake.py`; pinned in the #16198 systemd-unit canary on both shipping paths.
- Day-0 loader keeps its stamp gate (twin: still skipped under the pending marker) and no longer regenerates keys; dead `regen_ssh_host_keys` stubs removed from its harnesses. Seal comments/docs/changelog updated.

## Validation
- `test_ssh_hostkeys_regen_16445.py` 2/2: failed-reset fixture (pending marker present, keys absent, rotated machine-id) — real day-0 condition fails, real regen condition succeeds via `systemd-analyze condition`, real `ssh-keygen -A` creates keys, `sshd -t` passes with key / fails without; existing-key arm is skipped. Re-gating the unit on the stamp reds it (mutation-checked).
- `test_day0_machine_id_independence_10769.py` 3/3, `test_systemd_unit_canary_16198.py` 7/7, day-0 suites 16/16 + 16/16, `day0-configdb-guard-test.sh` all pass, targeted `go test ./pkg/factoryreset/` ok, `systemd-analyze verify` clean. No full selftest (campaign scope).

## Risk
`ssh-keygen -A` only creates missing key types and the unit is condition-skipped when any host key exists, so existing keys are never rotated; a partial set is completed — the desired per-instance identity.

## PR #16921 — factoryreset: refuse zeroize for busy provisioned accounts before wiping (#16443) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16443-zeroize-busy-account`

Refs #16443

## Why
`userdel -r` refuses a busy account (exit 8), and the operator's own SSH/CLI session runs under an xpf-provisioned account. The wipe erased SSH host keys, login keys, sudoers, networkd and the config DB before discovering the login leg could never succeed from that session; every retry failed identically, leaving a half-wiped box recoverable only from the console.

## What
- `checkProvisionedAccountsIdle` (`pgrep -u <uid>`) gates both `performWipeWithLogInventory` (before `beginZeroize` writes the pending marker) and `performWipe` (before any destructive leg): a busy provisioned account refuses the whole zeroize naming the account, every surface intact. Ownership uncertainty and probe failures also refuse (unknown, never idle).
- Inside `wipeLoginAccounts`, `terminateBusyProvisionedAccounts` closes the check-to-use window: terminates live processes scoped to the marker UID (`pkill -KILL -u`, never root/UID 0, never the wipe's own UID), re-verifies idle, and only then lets `userdel` fire; still-busy accounts keep markers for retry.
- New seams redirected in `RedirectWipePathsForTesting` (idle default); `setZeroizeLoginPaths` hermetic for them.
- Follow-on: the #16138 move left the #6584 termsafe tripwire's `server_diag_zeroize.go` exemption stale; repointed at `factoryreset/wipe.go`, declared the moved exec helper, scan now covers `../factoryreset`.

## Validation

- `go test ./pkg/factoryreset/ -count=1` green; cli termsafe tripwire green; daemon zeroize subset green; `go build ./...`, vet, gofmt clean
- Pre-existing unrelated grpcapi status-census failure (ShowConfig/GetSessionSummary) untouched

## Risk
Zeroize from a busy provisioned session now refuses instead of half-wiping (intended); operator ends sessions or uses console/root. Missing pgrep refuses rather than gambling. No dataplane impact.

Branch: `fix/16449-campaign`

Why: On the Ubuntu 26.04 base the grub-efi-amd64-signed / shim-signed postinst runs grub-install with NVRAM writes enabled, (re)creating the Ubuntu Boot#### entry at BootOrder[0]. The firmware then boots \EFI\ubuntu\shimx64.efi instead of an xpf slot, and xpf-uefi-slots preserved any non-xpf front as an operator choice forever, so the LANE-1 kernel arm refused with "BootOrder front is neither A/B slot" after the first routine bootloader security update.

What: `xpf-uefi-slots` records the BootOrder front it leaves in `/var/lib/xpf/uefi-bootorder-front`; when the current front is the distributor entry and the recorded front is an xpf slot, it re-asserts the recorded slot front non-destructively. A PXE front, or a distributor front with no recorded slot front, is preserved as an operator choice. Missing/garbled state never takes over. `bake.py` purges the state file at sysprep. The kernel arm gate is unchanged (no fail-open weakening).

Validation: RED on master script 6/9 new cells fail; GREEN `test_uefi_slots_6499` (29) + adjacent suites (94 total); `sh -n` + `shellcheck -S warning` clean. Baked-image VM probe remains lab-outstanding on the issue.

Risk: a hand-set Ubuntu front on a box whose recorded front is a slot is reverted once; documented in `docs/install-images.md`.

Refs #16449

## PR #16925 — cli: gate firewall live banner on applied marker after helper refusal (#16451) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16451-firewall-refused-live-banner`

Refs #16451

## Why
After an in-band helper refusal of a committed config's snapshot, both inputs of the #5067 liveness predicate (helper ack generation, last recorded apply generation) stay at the prior generation (7/7, armed), so `show firewall effective` certified the refused config as `dataplane-acknowledged (generation N)` and the RAW `show firewall` views paired the refused config's terms with the previous generation's counters.

## What
- `pkg/cli`: `firewallEffectiveLiveness` now additionally requires `store.ActiveApplied()` (via shared `firewallshow.Applied`) for `live`, with reason `active configuration not applied`. Both local RAW views print a previous-generation stale-counter WARNING when determined-but-not-live.
- `pkg/firewallshow`: shared `Applied` gate + `StaleCounterWarning` / `NotEnforcingWarning` texts so no surface copies the generation-only predicate.
- `pkg/grpcapi`: raw `firewall`/`firewall-filter:` topics print the stale-counter warning when helper status was obtained and the active config is unapplied; `firewall-effective*` topics print the NOT-enforcing/compiled-desired warning whenever unapplied (fail-closed even without helper status).
- Tests: refusal cell (7/7/armed unstamped → WARNING, never acknowledged; stamped twin → live banner) + RAW stale-counter cells (cli), four-surface gRPC cell; live fixtures stamped with `MarkActiveApplied()`.
- Docs: `docs/junos-cli-reference.md` generation-liveness section + `docs/log/16451.md`.

## Validation
- `go test ./pkg/cli/ -run 'TestShowEffectiveFirewallFilters|TestShowFirewallRawStaleCounters16451|TestCLIShowFirewallRawFields15173|TestShowEffectiveFirewallFilter' -count=1` PASS
- `go test ./pkg/grpcapi/ -run 'TestShowTextFirewall|TestShowFirewall' -count=1` PASS
- `go test ./pkg/firewallshow/ -count=1` PASS; `go vet` on the three packages clean
- Full `pkg/cli`/`pkg/grpcapi` suites carry pre-existing failures verified identical on clean `origin/master`.

## Risk
In-process surfaces rely on the daemon's in-memory `appliedDigest` (empty until first successful apply / boot apply stamp); before that stamp views warn — fail-closed, never a false live certification. No dataplane/enforcement change.
