## PR #16930 — image: ship only the default-ring hugepage pool and drop the deb sysctl (#16455) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16455-hugepages`

Refs #16455

## Why
`etc/sysctl.d/99-xpf-hugepages.conf` shipped `vm.nr_hugepages = 1440` (2.8 GiB) verbatim through the bake and the .deb's `/usr/lib/sysctl.d`, although the default `ring-entries 1024` needs 5 pages per binding (2560 frames x 4 KiB = 10 MiB, MAP_HUGETLB-rounded; 6 on virtio_net). The pool is applied at boot on every baked image — OOM kills on the 2 GiB Tier-1 validation VM, ~620 MiB free on the documented 4 GiB appliance before any service starts — and at package-install time on foreign hosts via systemd's `/usr/lib/sysctl.d` file trigger, contrary to debian/rules' 'next boot' claim and the #10733 unowned-host contract.

## What
- **Shipped default 1440 -> 90** in `etc/sysctl.d/99-xpf-hugepages.conf` (5 x 18 reference bindings at ring 1024 = 180 MiB); header rewritten (default formula, large-ring formula, bake/rig + manual provisioning, .deb installs nothing).
- **bake.py**: `hugepages_conf()` now refuses any shipped default other than exactly 90 (exact-equality gate over the preserved review-16260 systemd/kernel consumer-model parse — all ineffective spellings still die). New `--hugepages N` rig parameter: refuses N < 90 at arg parse and N < 1440 (reference large-ring pool) when rendering; renders by rewriting only the effective (last-surviving) assignment's value bytes and re-verifies the rendered effective value. Threaded through `virt_customize`/`main`.
- **debian/rules**: installs **no** sysctl.d payload, so `apt install` on an unmarked host leaves `/proc/sys/vm/nr_hugepages` unchanged.
- **validate.py**: scenario A asserts `HugePages_Total <= 90` and `MemAvailable >= 1 GiB` from one `/proc/meminfo` read in the 2 GiB gate VM (pure `_memory_floor_verdict`, unobserved readings fail).
- **Docs**: deploy-quickstart + userspace-dataplane-architecture rewritten (default pool shipped; large rings via `--hugepages` or /etc edit; .deb installs nothing). Changelog entry added.

## Tests
- `scripts/image/test_bake_hugepages_16243.py` re-based on 90 (18 cells): shipped-default equality, old 1440 default rejected at bake and at virt_customize, consumer-model spellings kept, override rendering (incl. shadowed-line and hex cases), `--hugepages` arg parsing, debian/rules sysctl-absence cells.
- New `scripts/image/test_validate_memory_floor_16455.py`: pre-fix meminfo fixtures (HugePages_Total 849 partial / 1440 full) fail, fixed 90-page fixture passes, unobserved readings fail, scenario-A wiring + bound cross-pinned against bake/conf.
- Full `scripts/image` unittest discover: **546 tests OK** (incl. updated reach-map count and main() namespace fixtures).
- `make -f debian/rules` dry-run: no sysctl install line; host `/proc/sys/vm/nr_hugepages` observed unchanged (20 before/after).

## Risk
A ring-entries 16384 appliance that relied on the old universal 1440 default now boots with the 90-page pool and takes the advisory-THP fallback (loud helper WARNING, measured 22.1->20.4 Gbps class at ring 16384) until the operator bakes `--hugepages 1440+` or edits `/etc/sysctl.d/99-xpf-hugepages.conf` per the rewritten docs. Correctness at any ring size never depended on the pool. No gate weakened: bake validation tightened from a >=1440 floor to exact-default equality; validate.py gains a new fail-closed assertion.

Residual: full `make deb` + real `apt install` in a VM not run (host is the shared control box); the .deb-side acceptance is pinned hermetically (rules payload absence + trigger mechanism documented from systemd's sysctl.d interest). Scenario A's live boot assertion runs with the next real bake/validate cycle.

## PR #16952 — userspace-dp: coerce tcp maximum window to wire range (#16482) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

## userspace-dp: coerce tcp maximum window to wire range (#16482)

Refs #16482

### Why
`security flow tcp-session maximum-window` (#15753) reached the Rust u32 wire field `tcp_maximum_window` via `buildFlowSnapshot` with a raw assignment — the one FlowSnapshot integer with no #1977 coercion. A value above u32::MAX arriving through a tolerant path (`Store.Load` of a hand-edited/foreign DB, `SyncApply` from a peer with a wider range; strict commit's `ValidateInteger(1024,1048576)` is only logged there) made serde reject the whole `apply_snapshot` decode, leaving the helper unconfigured.

### What
- `flow.go`: new `coerceWireTCPMaximumWindow` + `maxTCPMaximumWindow` (1048576); `buildFlowSnapshot` caps over-ceiling values to the schema ceiling with a `slog.Warn`. In-range values (65536) pass unchanged; non-positive stays on the existing `> 0` guard (0 = Rust default 65535).
- Capping to the schema ceiling rather than `math.MaxUint32`: a peer value such as 2^31 is already outside this node's operator range, and the ceiling keeps every emitted value also strict-commit-legal here.
- Tests: extend `TestBuildFlowSnapshotCoercesOutOfRange_1977`, add the field to the Layer A/B agreement table (`flow_numwidth_agreement_test.go`), add `TestTCPMaximumWindowCoerced16482` (cap + warn + u32-decodable wire JSON + 65536 unchanged + unset omitted).
- NOT changed: schema/compiler range, protocol version, Rust side.

### Validation
- Targeted (6/6 pass): `go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run 'TestBuildFlowSnapshotCoercesOutOfRange_1977|TestNumWidth_LayerAB_Agreement|TestTCPMaximumWindowCoerced16482|TestTCPFidelityKnobsReachWire15753|TestCoerceWireHelpers_1977|TestFullSnapshotMarshalsInRange_1977' -count=1`
- RED: reverting the one-line coercion makes both overflow tests fail (`TCPMaximumWindow = 5000000000, out of wire range`).

- `go vet ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/` clean; `gofmt` clean on changed files.

Branch: `fix/16484-nat64-reseed-scoped`

Refs #16484

## Why
Since #15678 several zone/RI-scoped NAT64 rule-sets can share one /96 with disjoint pools. The #6765 retained-address reseed, `prev_prefix_is_deterministic`, and `reuse_allocator` all selected the previous prefix by /96 bytes alone (first match), so a pool edit on any rule-set after the first reseeded from a sibling's allocator — carrying nothing, or suppressed outright when the first rule-set was deterministic — and the fresh allocator reissued live `(X,P)` tuples to other clients of that rule-set.

## What
- `Nat64Prefix` now carries the snapshot rule-set `name`.
- New `Nat64ScopeKey`: normalized zone/RI unions (singular folded in) plus parsed source-prefix constraint, normalized exactly as the build loop installs it.
- One selector `find_previous_prefix`: known name authoritative (renames neither steal nor keep ownership), nameless legacy falls back to bytes+scope, ambiguous legacy refuses to guess.
- `reuse_allocator`, `prev_prefix_is_deterministic`, and the reseed all go through it; installed prefix scope comes from the normalized key.
- Six `nat64_16484_*` regression cells; changelog + docs/log/16484.md.

## Validation
- `cargo test -- nat64_16484_` — 6 passed.
- Final targeted run: 9 passed (6 new + 15178 noop reuse, scoped zone match, two-zone union allocator).
- Broader `nat64_` filter: 358 passed / 16 failed; the 16 reproduce on unmodified origin/master (RFC 6056 per-boot PAT secret breaks exact-low-port assertions) — pre-existing, unrelated.

## Risk
Reload-path only; packet-path matching/revalidation untouched. Renamed rules behave like new rules (no carry-over). Duplicate names in a tolerated load fall back to first name match.

## PR #16957 — userspace-dp: carry retained deterministic NAT64 tuples on pool length change (#16481) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16481`

Refs #16481

## Why
A deterministic NAPT64 pool append/shrink changed `host_count`, so the NAT64 rebuild built a fresh allocator and (since #15178) skipped the #6765 reseed. Revalidation keeps retained subscribers' sessions because their (pool index, block) did not move, so the fresh allocator re-minted each subscriber's lowest block port — the port its oldest surviving session still holds — and a second flow to the same remote shared the live reverse tuple.

## What
- `PortAllocator::reseed_retained_deterministic_v6_from`: carries live deterministic flows whose tuple still satisfies `deterministic_v6_tuple_matches` under the NEW params into the fresh allocator, rebuilding each BIB lease with the new `DeterministicPortedIdentity::V6` (sibling flows join one lease, holder masks preserved); invalid tuples are counted, not carried.
- `Nat64State` wires it for det->det transitions; RR->RR keeps the generic #6765 carry and mode flips still start fresh (#15178).
- `ReseedOutcome` gains `reseeded_deterministic`/`skipped_deterministic_invalid`, classified in `needs_report`. Dead `prev_prefix_is_deterministic` removed.

## Validation
- `r3n05_det_pool_append_reissues_live_tuple`, `vn05_det_pool_shrink_reissues_live_tuple_and_tears_down_removed` pass (F2 differs from F1, F1 held, removed subscriber torn down).
- 3 allocator cells in `tests_det_reseed_16481.rs` pass (append/shrink carry, block-change control).
- #15178 cells, `tests_pool`, `tests_reseed` green (287 passed combined targeted run). The `nat64_`/`reseed` parallel batch shows 16 failures identical on pristine origin/master (pre-existing), unrelated.

## Risk
Commit-time work only, no per-packet cost. Sessions outside the new geometry are still torn down by revalidation as #15178 intended; round-robin and no-op re-applies unchanged. Idle BIB leases are not carried (no live session; tuple re-derives deterministically).

Changelog: `docs/log/16481.md`

## PR #16961 — config: recognize seconds-only legacy config archives (#16487) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-24)

Branch: `fix/16487-campaign`

Why:
Builds from 2026-02-14..06-28 wrote archives as `config-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.conf` (seconds only). `isXPFConfigArchiveSnapshot` accepted only the sequenced and nanosecond pre-sequence shapes, so those files were invisible: the #10825 Load purge skipped cleartext api-auth copies silently and `rotateArchives` never pruned them, so retention exceeded max-archives forever. Surviving pre-#4056 copies are also 0644 world-readable.

What:
- `isXPFConfigArchiveSnapshot` now accepts an exact seconds-only stamp when the name carries no dot; seconds-only names have no parseable seq, so rotation already sorts them oldest by lexical timestamp.
- The no-dot split plus explicit nine-digit fraction and stamp-length guards also stop `time.Parse`'s variable-length trailing fraction from recognizing foreign names such as `config-<stamp>.1.conf`.
- The Load purge sweep tightens any preserved recognized snapshot from 0644 to 0600 tighten-only before api-auth classification; chmod failure warns and retries on a later Load.
- NOT changed: `parseArchiveSeq`, `writeArchive` naming, factory-reset RemoveAll, foreign `config-*.conf` handling.

Validation:
- New `archive_seconds_only_16487_test.go` cells (recognizer accept/reject table, mixed-shape rotation, newest-seconds-only retention) plus the extended #10825 owned-archive fixture (cleartext seconds-only at 0644 purged; hashed seconds-only at 0644 survives byte-identical, tightened to 0600): 12 targeted tests pass.
- RED proof: neutralizing the seconds-only branch fails the recognizer, both rotation cells, and the purge fixture; neutralizing the chmod fails it with `mode = 0644, want 0600`.
- Full `pkg/configstore` suite: one pre-existing failure `TestThenFirstFromLineVerbsRefused12516`, reproduced on clean `origin/master` 8cfe1bc9c0 without this change.

Risk:
Only the explicitly opted-in api-auth archive root gains the chmod; custom destinations remain untouched. Foreign `config-*.conf` files stay unrecognized.

## PR #16965 — userspace-dp: stop refusing D11 admission on lock contention (#16495) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix-16495`

Refs #16495

## Why
D11 IPsec-inner admission refused admissible frames on lock contention at three sites left by #15151: router in-flight `try_lock` → `WORKER_QUEUE_FULL` (47, E23 counted with an empty queue), worker-set authority `try_lock` → `EVALUATOR_UNAVAILABLE` (52 → ADMIT_SHUTDOWN), tombstone `try_insert` → `LEASE_EPOCH` (50 → ADMIT_BAD_LEASE, attestation FAIL). Every refusal is a Go `VerdictDrop` of a permitted frame.

## What
Blocking `lock()` at all three sites (issue's accepted bounded-hold alternative): `authoritative_route` replaces `try_is_authoritative`/`try_route` (None only unpublished/empty); router in-flight lock (O(1) vs O(1) release); tombstone `try_insert`→`insert` (competing O(cap≤512) scans). E23 now moves only at genuine per-queue depth / per-flow in-flight bound; LEASE_EPOCH only duplicate/zero/at-cap. Per-queue BUSY (#15151 accepted risk), wire, Go, depths unchanged.

## Validation
`cargo test --bins ipsec_inner_queue::tests`: **32 passed**. 3 new deterministic ` *_16495` cells hold each competing lock from another thread across a spawned admit and require `Ok(0)` (inflight: E23 delta 0; tombstone: genuine duplicate still LEASE_EPOCH), each with positive control. Existing genuine-full/per-flow/BUSY controls green.

## Risk
Producer briefly blocks on bounded holds (no lock held across adjudication) instead of dropping. No lab production-rate measurement (matches finding evidence level).

## PR #16966 — build: shorten GOTMPDIR pin to /wtgt for sun_path bound (#16494) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16494-campaign`

Why:
The #14833 scratch pin exported `GOTMPDIR=/var/worktrees/.cache/go-tmp` (28 chars) to every make recipe. Go's `testing.TempDir` builds `<GOTMPDIR>/<name[:64]><random>/001/<sock>`, so a worst-case `control.sock` path is 120 octets — past the 107-octet AF_UNIX `sun_path` limit. `make test-go` / `test-race-dp` then showed 45+ false `bind: invalid argument` reds in helper control-socket, event-stream, HA-watchdog, reinject and gRPC teardown tests, indistinguishable from dataplane regressions. `scratch-pinning-selftest.sh` modelled a 71-byte path Go never produces (26-char test dir, no `/001`), so it stayed green while the gate was red.

What:
- `GOTMPDIR` defaults to `/wtgt` (5 chars; worst-case canary path 97 octets) in `Makefile`, `scripts/run-selftests.sh`, and the `test-memlock-guards` recipe. `TMPDIR`/`GOCACHE`/`CARGO_TARGET_DIR` pins under `/var/worktrees/.cache` are unchanged; an explicit caller `GOTMPDIR` still wins.
- The modelled-length check is replaced by an executed canary: `scripts/sunpath-canary` reproduces the real TempDir shape (64-byte name + 10-digit random stand-in + `/001/control.sock`) and binds it. `scratch-pinning-selftest.sh` requires it to pass under `/wtgt` and fail under a deliberately long root, so the check reds in both directions. If `/wtgt` cannot be created, the positive leg SKIPs loudly rather than falling back.
- `scripts/README.md`, `debian/changelog`, `docs/log/16494.md` updated. NOT changed: per-test `shortSockDir` helpers (still needed for deeper-than-`001` socket layouts) and the stale on-disk `/var/worktrees/.cache/go-tmp` directory (now unreferenced).

Validation:
- Canary: binds at 97 octets under `/wtgt`; fails at 120 under the old root and 116 under `/var/worktrees/.cache/gt` (proving no `/var/worktrees/.cache` path can fit).
- `sh scripts/scratch-pinning-selftest.sh`: green with new pins; RED on revert (restoring the 28-char pin fails naming all three GOTMPDIR/TMPDIR pins).
- Previously pinned-only failures pass under `/wtgt` and fail under the old root with the exact issue signatures: `pkg/nfqueue` TestReinjectSocketCompletionTimeoutResetsPartialFrame9506, `pkg/grpcapi` TestUngatedFallbackErasesDerivedHelperState10769, sampled `pkg/dataplane/userspace` event-stream/control/DumpFIB/HA-watchdog cells, and the two `pkg/daemon` event-stream race cells.
- `scripts/selftest-census.sh` still OK (62 self-tests invoked); `go vet`/`gofmt` clean on the canary.

Risk:
`/wtgt` must be creatable at the filesystem root; Makefile and selftest attempt `mkdir -p` and the selftest SKIPs loudly when they cannot, never silently falling back to a long root. Full `make test-go` pinned-vs-unpinned failure-set equivalence was not run (minutes under campaign load; packages carry unrelated pre-existing fixture rot) — targeted cells cover the pinned-only class.

Refs #16494

## PR #16967 — configstore: retire superseded api-auth migration staging (#16492) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16492-api-auth-staging`

Why: On the upgrade boot crossing #10826 with legacy cleartext api-auth and an unreadable confirm.json, #15273 defers the durable active rewrite and leaves `.configdb/api-auth-migration.json` staged (Old=H1, New=H2) with the pre-migration rollback-sidecar binding. The documented remedy for the resulting /health-503 lost-window alarm — a plain commit — or a routine HA `SyncApply` writes H3 and rebinds the sidecar to H3, but no promotion retired staging, so the next boot's staging-consistency gate matched neither staged side and returned `ErrConfigDBUnreadable`: xpfd refused to start on every later boot until an operator deleted a file no message named.

What: `apiAuthMigrationStagingSuperseded` (sidecar binds the on-disk active hash + device/inode/mtime exactly while naming neither staged hash) plus `retireSupersededAPIAuthMigrationStaging` in `rollback_metadata.go`. The retire hook runs after every durable promotion that rebinds or shifts the sidecar: plain commit and commit-confirmed (post-`saveRollbackFiles`), `SyncApply` (post shifted save; deferred with a pre-rename write failure), `PromoteRollback` and boot-recovery rollback (post-rebind), and the persist-retry heal. `Load` re-checks supersession before both staging-consistency gates so a retirement lost to a crash or failed delete self-heals, and the fatal error now names the staging file. NOT changed: the staged Old/New alias admission, per-slot staging checks, and the #15273 deferral itself — without a promotion, staging survives untouched.

Validation: new `api_auth_migration_superseded_16492_test.go` cells — arm A (deferred boot -> plain `Commit` -> boot2 clean, staging retired, api-auth hashed on disk), arm `SyncApply`, control B (no promotion still defers; staging + pre-migration active survive), control C (readable confirm converges on boot1, confirm + boot2 clean), negative control (tampered `active.json` vs stale sidecar stays `ErrConfigDBUnreadable`, now naming the staging file, staging preserved). Arms and the message assertion fail on base (staging stranded / fatal boot / unnamed file; verified via stash revert). Full `pkg/configstore` suite: 1 failure, `TestThenFirstFromLineVerbsRefused12516`, base-attributed on 5d0b11c11d (fails identically without this change). Neighboring #10826/#15273/#9887/#8566 migration tests pass; post-merge re-run of the new + #15273/#10825 cells green.

Risk: Supersession is exact (hash + identity), so any sidecar/disk disagreement stays fail-closed; a degraded sidecar write leaves staging for the next boot's Load-side check rather than retiring against an unverified ladder. No wire/schema changes; the only operator-visible deltas are the previously fatal boot now succeeding and the fatal message naming the repair file.

- Targeted: `cargo test --bins -- 16496 15268` → 5 passed (incl. existing `*_15268` deferred-replay cells); `cached_three_color_replay_latest_policer_dscp_wins_15793` green.

## PR #16970 — test: idle session sync when the gap shrinks (#16500) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16500-sync-idle-shrink`

Why:
The #16289 baseline-relative predicate in `ha_session_sync_idle_sample`
required `sent - baseline_sent == received - baseline_received`. Creates in
flight at the first sample then delivered (20/17 -> 20/20), or creates landing
between the two non-atomic CLI captures (20/22 -> 22/22), shrink the gap, so no
later sample ever reads idle. Both failover-gate precondition waits then time
out FAIL on a caught-up pair and VOID the downstream RG1 cells of
`make test-failover`. Lab-gate liveness only; no product effect.

What:
Idle is now `(sent - baseline_sent <= received - baseline_received) ||
(sent == received)` with `pending == 0` in the single shared helper
(`test/incus/ha-assurance-lib.sh`). The second clause covers the acceptance
sequence 20/22 -> 22/22 verbatim, where the delta gaps are 2 vs 0 (counters
unequal in deltas, equal absolutely); a growing gap (20/20 -> 25/20) stays not
idle either way. Both wait loops (`test-failover.sh`,
`scripts/userspace-ha-failover-validation.sh`) consume the helper verdict and
need no change: the sibling sources the same lib, and its baseline-keeping /
rewind-only re-baseline discipline is unchanged. NOT changed: verdicts 1/2/3,
pending/drained parsing, the 3-consecutive-sample policy, any daemon code.

Validation:
`bash test/incus/ha-assurance-selftest.sh` PASS, with new unit cells
(20/17->20/20 idle, 20/22->22/22 idle, 20/20->25/20 not idle, shrunk gap
pending=3 not idle) and new stateful loop cases for BOTH production wait loops
(shrinking gap PASS sample 4, received-ahead PASS sample 4, growing gap timeout
FAIL 8 calls). RED: equality-only revert fails on 20/17->20/20; inequality-only
(no counters-meet) fails on 20/22->22/22. `bash -n` + shellcheck clean.

Risk:
The counters-meet clause generalizes the issue's inequality on different-epoch
counters by treating absolute equality as caught up even if the baseline gap
was positive; pending==0 and the 3-consecutive-sample rule still guard it, and
a backlog never delivered remains indistinguishable from caught up under any
baseline scheme (pre-existing, noted on the issue). Live test-failover frequency
of the trigger is unmeasured; no cluster run was exercised.

## PR #16971 — userspace-dp: fail port terms closed on (0,0) in pre-screen walk (#16502) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16502-prescreen-port-zero`

Refs #16502

## Why
The #11332 pre-screen input-filter walk (`input_filter_would_deny_before_screen`) built its `TermMatchExtra` with only the flowless `ports_unknown` case, omitting the #9894 rule that a flow-backed `(0,0)` tuple is synthetic. On a tolerant-loaded `routing-instance` + `discard`/`reject` term whose port constraint literal 0 satisfies (e.g. `destination-port-except 80`), the pre-screen walk denied, every zone screen was skipped, and PBR enforcement — which fails port-constrained terms closed on `(0,0)` — forwarded the packet with no screen accounting.

## What
- Add one shared helper `filter::mark_ports_unknown_for_zero_flow`.
- Route through it: `input_filter_would_deny_before_screen`, `ingress_route_table_override_with_mode` (PBR enforcement), `revalidate_static_pbr_route_on_session_hit`, the per-packet session-hit PBR arm, `static_input_filter_deny_eval` (on top of its deliberate `TermMatchExtra::default()`), and `static_hit_log_for_action`.
- Widen `input_filter_would_deny_before_screen` to `pub(in crate::afxdp)` so the property cell can call it.
- Tests: vb13 arms A–D as `port_zero_syn_is_screened_despite_except_discard_pbr_term_16502` (arm B challenges on the second SYN; C counts discards; D screens port-80) plus `prescreen_deny_implies_enforcement_deny_16502` over 8 term shapes × 7 port pairs.
- `docs/log/16502.md`.

## Validation
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp 16502`: 2 passed.
- Mutation (pre-screen helper call neutralised): both new tests RED with the exact defect assertion.
- Neighbours `9894`/`11332`: 18 passed.
- Note: 3 `static_verdict_7212` tests fail identically on unmodified origin/master in a clean worktree (pre-existing, untouched by this change).

## Risk
`(0,0)` flows now fail port-constrained terms closed on the static deny/log walks too, matching PBR enforcement; real TCP/UDP flows never carry both ports zero. No allocation added (helper is `#[inline]`, by-value `Copy` extra).

## PR #16972 — userspace-dp: deliver D11 terminals for stale survivors and stop reaps (#16497) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16497-campaign`

## Why
#15149 residual (R3-B12-02): retiring a dead worker bumps the GLOBAL D11 worker-set generation, so descriptors queued on SURVIVING workers read stale in `drain_worker` and were dropped with no verdict; `stop_inner` likewise reaped every queue into `reaped_verdicts` but never delivered them. Both sets completed only by the 5 ms Go ack deadline (`pkg/nfqueue/pipeline.go`), with per-flow stall and ack-timeout mis-accounting; the undelivered list grew by the reaped count on every full stop. Fail-closed either way — the defect is the missing prompt Denied terminal.

## What
- `ipsec_inner_queue.rs`: the `drain_worker` stale branch records `Deny{stage:"d11_stale_generation", reason:STALE_GENERATION}` when `claim_stale` wins (exactly-once preserved), via a new `push_reaped_verdict` helper used by all three producers; a `reaped_count` atomic mirrors the Vec depth (`uncertain_count` precedent) so `has_pending_work` stays lock-free yet never hides an undelivered terminal.
- `worker/loop_body/mod.rs`: the worker loop takes reaped terminals after `drain_verdicts_into` and completes them on the same pass — a survivor is never swept, so this is the only delivery path for its stale descriptors.
- `coordinator/mod.rs`: `stop_inner` drains `take_reaped_terminal_verdicts` into `complete_ipsec_inner_verdict` right after its retire+join loops (slow path still installed; its ReinjectCore survives reconciles).
- NOT changed: the generation model, the `status.rs` dead-worker sweep, Go deadline behaviour.

## Validation
- Extended `dead_worker_sweep_retires_ipsec_inner_worker_15149` to run the survivor's drain: takes 0 (stale never adjudicated), records exactly one terminal, request 151492 completes `Denied`, both slabs reclaimed, zero leftovers. Pre-fix this drain completed nothing.
- New `stop_inner_delivers_reaped_ipsec_inner_verdicts_16497`: one queued request per worker, real `stop_inner(false)` → both complete `Denied`, `has_reaped_verdicts()` false, slabs reclaimed, second empty stop clean.
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 15149 16497 ipsec_inner`: **79 passed, 0 failed**.
- Coordinator suite (`afxdp::coordinator::`): 379 passed / 5 failed — all 5 (`apply_snapshot_wires_day2_preserved_mtu_reconcile`, `every_runtime_atomic_is_bound_or_knowingly_off_wire_6961`, `refresh_runtime_snapshot_publishes_a_coherent_view_pair`, `snapshot_duplicate_if_id_claimants_deny_through_adjudication_10540`, `snapshot_published_tunnel_rows_join_d11_10485`) reproduced identically on pristine `origin/master` `037049d500` in a detached base worktree: base-attributed, not caused by this change.

## Risk
A reaped entry recorded by a worker that dies before its next pass is still flushed by the dead-worker sweep or `stop_inner`; no new stranding path. Enforcement unchanged (Denied either way). Component level only, matching the finding's evidence; no Go pipeline/lab run.

Refs #16497

## PR #16973 — screen: cap per-source scan state at detection count (#16498) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16498-scan-cap`

Refs #16498

## Why
`ScanCore::check` fired port-scan/ip-sweep detection at the fixed `SCAN_DETECT_COUNT` (10) distinct destinations but kept inserting distinct destinations into a per-source heap `FxHashSet` up to `MAX_UNIQUE_PER_SOURCE` (1024). The window reset's `clear()` retained that bucket allocation and least-suspicious eviction preserved the fullest sets, so a spoofed-source new-flow flood could pin ~144 MiB (ip-sweep) + ~24 MiB (port-scan) of heap per worker per screened zone (~1 GiB at 6 workers with both screens on) — ~100x what detection requires — and paid hashing for destinations 11-1024 that carry no verdict information.

## What
- Recorded destinations now live in an inline `[Option<T>; SCAN_DETECT_COUNT]` buffer in `SrcEntry` (with `insert_unique`/`distinct_count`/`is_empty`/`reset_entries`): no per-source heap allocation, nothing retained across a window reset.
- `MAX_UNIQUE_PER_SOURCE` now equals `SCAN_DETECT_COUNT` (compile-time guard updated). A distinct destination past the count is not stored, counts once on the existing `skipped_pressure` signal (mirroring the old over-1024 path; a repeat of a recorded destination does not count), and the already-true verdict is still evaluated — no gate weakens, no fail-open.
- Eviction's least-suspicious ordering and cleanup's empty test read the capped count (<=10, semantics unchanged).
- scan.rs module doc + session README now publish the per-worker, per-zone bound: saturated records are 200 B (ip-sweep) / 64 B (port-scan), i.e. at most 4096 x (200 + 64) B = ~1.03 MiB per worker per zone for both screens' per-source records, plus the unchanged source-axis index overhead.

## Validation
- New `single_source_fanout_capped_at_detect_count_16498`: one source, 2000 distinct destinations in one window, both instantiations — fires exactly at the 10th, recorded count caps at 10 (RED on the pre-fix shape), inline bytes only, post-count pressure, repeat-not-pressure.
- New `per_source_state_capped_at_detect_count_16498`: cap equality, measured record sizes (200 B / 64 B), saturated 4096-source zone holds exactly sources x one fixed-size record.
- Existing bound cells (`per_source_unique_entries_bounded`, `memory_caps_bound_state_under_wide_window`) re-anchored to the new cap.
- `cargo test --bins screen::scan`: 34/34 green. Full `screen::` filter: 370/370 green.

## Risk
Verdict semantics unchanged. `skipped_pressure` now also counts distinct destinations past 10 (was: past 1024) — observability only, never a gate.

Residual: component level only, matching the finding's evidence; no appliance RSS/OOM measurement (the fix removes the attacker-driven heap axis rather than tuning it).

## PR #16974 — userspace-dp: cap WireGuard pad at inner budget (#16499) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16499-wg-pad-cap`

Why: TUN-origin WireGuard egress padded every record to a 16-byte multiple with no MTU cap. An operator `mtu` set by the standard underlay-minus-overhead formula (1420 on IPv6/1500, 1432 on IPv4 PPPoE 1492) made every full-size firewall-originated packet up to 15 bytes too big; each was silently dropped at `encap_mtu_drops` with no PTB.

What: Cap the §5.4.6 pad at the inner budget (`outer_mtu − overhead`), matching Linux `calculate_skb_padding` and wireguard-go `calculatePaddingSize`, on both encap sites (TUN-origin `wg_control` + transit `frame/wg.rs`) via `padded_len_capped` / `try_encap_capped`. Size models and `wg_inner_mtu` become the capped inverse; Go default wgN MTU drops the worst-pad subtraction and warns on an operator mtu above the default-underlay budget. Decap unchanged.

Validation: cargo `encap_and_send(1420-byte inner, v6 peer, outer 1500)` returns Sent with a 1452-byte record and decaps round-trip; probe rows (v6/1500→1420, v4/1492→1432, v4/1450→1390, v6/1450→1370) all fit exactly; Go `TestWgTunMTUForEndpoint` passes. Pre-existing failures on master noted in commit body.

Refs #16499

## PR #16977 — userspace-dp: dedup owed neighbor programs by key (#16508) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16508-campaign`

Why:
`record_owed` in `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/neighbor_program_limiter.rs` deduped owed bindings on `(key, mac)` via `bucket_owes`, contrary to its documented "update that key's existing owed entry" (#15770). One key advertising 4 distinct MACs inside one interval occupied every owed way of its bucket and evicted a victim key's owed kernel program; that neighbour's kernel entry then lagged until its next changed advert (host-path only; userspace map/transit unaffected). The `clear_owed` in `should_program`'s same-MAC branch was unreachable (`!owes_other` implies the MACs are equal), so a newer advert for the programmed binding never superseded an older owed change.

What:
- `record_owed`: first finds `desired_key == Some(key)` and overwrites its MAC and timestamp in place — at most one owed way per key. Free-way and oldest-eviction fallbacks unchanged; no programmed binding/timestamp touched, so the #5288 aggregate rate cap is preserved.
- `should_program`: owning-way exact-binding branch now calls new `clear_owed_superseded` (drops owed entries for the key whose MAC differs from the programmed one); the proven-present early return for a binding the owning way does not hold is now an explicit branch with unchanged behavior.
- Tests: strengthened `owed_binding_superseded_by_newer_mac_15247` with owed-occupancy assertions; new `one_key_flapping_macs_does_not_evict_victim_owed_16508` (4-MAC flap vs single-advert positive control via production `should_program`) and `programmed_mac_advert_supersedes_older_owed_change_16508`.
- `afxdp/README.md` owed semantics clarified; `docs/log/16508.md` added.

Validation:
- `cargo test --bins neighbor_program`: 16 passed (14 existing + 2 new).
- RED-verified: new/strengthened tests on pre-fix production logic fail with `<=1 owed way per key: left 4, right 1`, `newer MAC must supersede: left 2, right 1`, `stale owed MAC must be superseded: left 1, right 0`; other 13 limiter tests stay green pre-fix.
- `rustfmt --check` clean on the touched file.

Risk:
Confined to owed bookkeeping: a flapping key now retains only its newest owed MAC (intended supersede semantics); a victim's owed program survives a same-bucket 4-MAC flap. No gate weakened; rate bound untouched.

Refs #16508

## PR #16978 — userspace-dp: verify held MAC on refused probe instead of re-asserting it (#16505) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16505-neighbour-mac-move`

Refs #16505

## Why
On a genuine neighbour MAC move the kernel already holds the correct new MAC `G2` and probes it; the #15097 refused-probe re-assert REPLACE-overwrote that entry with the dead held MAC `G`, breaking host-originated traffic until a kernel FAILED cycle. The refused probe also erased key-only local-probe tokens.

## What
- `neighbor.rs`: refused-probe arm no longer re-asserts the held MAC into the kernel on the first refused probe. `refused_probe_action` (5s window, per-(key, held MAC), bounded 4096, fail-closed) drives `handle_refused_probe`: MAC-bound token + best-effort unicast verification solicitation; on window expiry the held binding is dropped via `remove_if_mac_matches` so fresh resolution adopts the new MAC. Seam renamed `parse_neighbor_msg_with_verify`/`RefusedProbeVerify`; old re-assert + rate limiter removed (no remaining callers).
- `sharded_neighbor.rs`: `clear_mac_bound_neighbor_probe` (preserves key-only tokens) + `remove_if_mac_matches`.

## Validation
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 16505 15097 10704 13660 13661 13898 mac_bound_probe_token`: **14 passed, 0 failed** — including new v4+v6 genuine-move cells (STALE(G2) → PROBE(G2) → REACHABLE(G2) with/without key-only token), verification-window cell, selective-clear cell, and the updated #15097 spoof cells (still keep G).
- Broader `neighbor` filter: 339 passed, 1 failed, 1 ignored. The failure (`seed_lifecycle_expires_on_app_window_not_default_10267`) fails identically on pristine origin/master 957f50f891; pre-existing, unrelated.

## Risk / residuals
- No fail-open weakening: differing-MAC updates still require solicited evidence or `NUD_PERMANENT`; the refused MAC never gains a token.
- Genuine move without a local probe converges after the 5s verification window + fresh resolution.
- Deferred lab item (per issue): two-netns integrated Rust-monitor genuine-move run showing `lost=0`; unit cells pin the dataplane half and the decision. [INFERENCE] Production solicitation uses the kernel ICMP-echo probe (kernel directs ARP/NS at its table MAC); the drop decision does not depend on the solicitation wire form.

## PR #16980 — userspace-dp: key egress DSCP rewrite only on the final class (#16506) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16506-campaign`

## Why

`resolve_cos_priority_class_lp_rewrite` chained filter class -> BA class -> clamped queue. When an input filter reclassifies with `then forwarding-class <fc>` and the egress DSCP rewrite-rule has no entry for `<fc>` (a partial "bleach best-effort only" rule), the packet was queued as `<fc>` but re-marked with the overridden BA class's code-point (queued EF, emitted DSCP 0), and the cached seed replayed that BA-derived marking on every flow-cache hit. This violates the documented #14663 contract that the filter class is the packet's FINAL forwarding class for egress DSCP rewriting. The same resolver's clamped-queue arm (Y28-05 cohort) bleached an unmaterialized BA class absent from the rule with the default queue's entry.

## What

- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tx/cos_classify_ba.rs`: the rewrite now keys ONLY on the packet's final class (filter class when present, else the BA class) — its `(class, loss-priority)` entry, then the queue entry only when the egress queue IS that class's own materialized queue. `resolve_cos_class_lp_rewrite` delegates to the shared resolver. A packet no classifier assigned any class to keeps the pre-#13968 queue-keyed behaviour (the selected queue is the classification result; pinned by #11386/#11808).
- Stale "then the BA class, then the clamped queue" comments in `tx/cos_classify.rs` updated; final-class-only contract recorded in `docs/cos-traffic-shaping.md`.
- NOT changed: the drain fallback (`uniform_fc_rewrite` already keys by the queue's own class, so it cannot resurrect the overridden class) and `cos_lp_reclassify` arming.

## Validation

- New cells in `cos_filter_fc_14663_tests.rs`: filter class absent from rule (fresh + cached seed `None`, two-packet hit seed DSCP 10 / hit DSCP 46 -> `None`, DSCP-46 twin, controls A/B, flowless), unmaterialized-filter variant (clamped default queue must not bleach), Y28-05 BA-only variant (fresh/seed/hit `None`, materialized-BE control).
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 16506 y28_05 14663 14636`: 10 passed. RED-verified by restoring the base resolver: all 3 new cells fail `left: Some(0) right: None`; restored green.
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- cos_`: 437 passed, 0 failed.
- Full `cargo test --bins`: 9451 passed / 80 failed vs 9449/79 on unmodified origin/master `957f50f891` (scratch worktree). Failure-set diff: the only fix-only failure is `v8_release_unused_v8_concurrent_preserves_ledger_invariant`, an unrelated shared-lease concurrency test that passes twice in isolation (flake under full-suite load); all other failures are pre-existing and identical.

## Risk

Packets whose assigned class (filter or BA) is absent from the egress rewrite-rule now leave unrewritten instead of inheriting another class's code-point — the documented #14663 contract. Component-level verification only, matching the issue's executed evidence; lab wire-marking verification under a partial rewrite-rule remains outstanding.

Refs #16506

Scratch-buffer lifecycle only; teardown semantics unchanged (every
teardown in a batch still receives the full trigger set).

## PR #16983 — userspace-dp: select NAT64 tunnel MSS with translated family (#16511) [MERGED] (merged 2026-10-25)

Branch: `fix/16511-nat64-tunnel-mss-family`

Refs #16511

## Why
The NAT64 builder selected the tunnel-egress TCP MSS clamp with the ingress `ForwardPacketMeta`, so a v4->v6 SYN-ACK into GRE/WG was budgeted as IPv4 and advertised an MSS 20 bytes above the IPv6 tunnel budget (1436 instead of 1416 on a 1500-byte transport), making full-size segments depend on ICMPv6 PTB. The v6->v4 direction was 20 bytes low (safe but wrong).

## What
- `frame/mod.rs`: compute `nat64_translated_meta` once in `build_nat64_forwarded_frames_with_commit_and_dynamic`, select the MSS with the emitted family, and reuse that meta for GRE/WG encapsulation.
- `tx/dispatch/slow_path.rs`: flip the family the same way for NAT64 (static-only site, kept consistent).
- Tests: `nat64_gre_mss_uses_translated_family_16511` (both directions through the real GRE builder: 1436 forward / 1416 reverse) and `nat64_wg_mss_uses_translated_family_16511` (selection-layer WG twin: 1385 v4 / 1365 v6).
- `docs/log/16511.md`.

## Validation
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 16511`: 2 passed
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 15948 14664 8896`: 23 passed
- `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp -- 16511 15948` (after mutation restore): 15 passed
- Mutation: reverting to ingress-meta selection fails the GRE cell (1416 vs expected 1436)

## Risk
Low — only SYN/SYN-ACK MSS selection for NAT64 tunnel egress changes; non-tunnel NAT64 keeps the all-tcp value (family-independent), unknown ingress families still fail closed in the inner builder. Residual: WG twin is pinned at the selection layer, not end-to-end through an established WG session.
